contents.versio: 018. I said to them, when I remembered this (the fear), I said, because of the horror, they said, I said: can’t I come tomorrow during the day instead? They said: no, you have to come with us now! They said: the chief is waiting for you! You have to come now quickly!

contents.textus: 019. Qayəm ono ste məlli omanno: "Ma zəd, mede ma zədtər mu mawto layto." ʕAl ruḥi məlli. Omanno: "Mede, mawto yo, zədtər mu mawto layt mede ḥreno."
contents.versio: 019. So I said (to myself): what is there more than death? There is nothing worse than death, I said to myself, something, it is death! More than death there is nothing else!

contents.textus: 020. Azzino, lwəšli ǧuli, azzi ʕam ap polis. Mḥeli ʕal u tarʕo du mudur, maṭina l su mudur, mḥeli ʕal u tarʕayḏe. Aṯi l qamuṯi omər: "O, tux." Hawxa yaʕni b fṣiḥuṯo hne, xəd d əmmat, maḥwele hno aʕmi.
contents.versio: 020. So I dressed up and left with the police. I knocked on the chiefs door; I arrived at the chief and knocked on his door. He came to me and said: oh, come on in! He said so in a happy manner so to say, he showed me (respect).

contents.textus: 021. Aṯi l qamuṯi, yatiwina, ǧġilina. Omər: "Komaḥwe, m iḏe d latwaylan ġalabe..." Hano, u mudur: "Komaḥwe, m iḏe latwaylan aḥna, ono w hat ġalabe asiruṯo, diyaloġ ʕam ḥḏoḏe, u medano hawi, səmlux." Omanno: "Komanno, e, baʕ, e. Kmaḥwe, m ayko koḏaʕno, hawxa ono sti mede."
contents.versio: 021. He stood up and welcomed me and we sat down and talked. He said: it seems that because we did not have much, the chief said: because we did not have much contact, dialog with each other, this matter occurred, what you did. I said: I believe so, yes, it seems so. I do not know really, something like this.

contents.textus: 022. Hiye zbəṭle, qayəm, yatiwina side, zbəṭle b mazbaṭa, kəmminala yaʕni, mazbaṭa, b ḥaq diḏi, yaʕni qay məlli u medano w qay ǧġənno medone hawxa. Zbəṭle b mazbaṭa b ḥaq diḏi. Mərle, mšayele, mšayele omər: "Hatu m ayko hatu?"
contents.versio: 022. He started, when we sat at his office, he started putting together a protocol about me, they call it mazbata, a protocol against me; why I said this and why I spoke in this way. So he started putting together a protocol about me and said, he asked, he asked and said: you, where are you from?

contents.textus: 023. Omanno: "Aḥna, u ʕamo..." Mšayele ʕal u ʕamo səryoyo, omər: "Hatu m ayko hatu?" Omanno: "Aḥna u ʕamo ʕatiqo d Beṯ Nahrin na, u ʕamo ʕatiqo d Məzopəṭamya. Noše ʕatəqtər minan layto harke. W aḥna, i dukṯayḏan harke yo."
contents.versio: 023. I said: we are the people, he asked about the Syriac people and said: where are you from? I said: we are the old people of Beth Nahrin, the old people of Mesopotamia. There are no other people older than us here. And our place is here.

contents.textus: 024. W ono, mə d məlli, hawxa ʕayəqle hiye, lo rḥəmle, qay yaʕni komanno, i dukṯayḏan harke yo w u hnayḏan harke yo.
contents.versio: 024. He was annoyed when I said that. He did not like it when I said that our place is here and our “origin” is here.

contents.textus: 025. Ḥəlli, koʕoyaqle, omanno: "Haka lə gmətyaqnat, tux, aḥna, kətlan ʕito, i ʕito, d koweno eba, hawila tralfo əšne, waxta d kowela tralfo əšne, d maʕməralle w d kətwa ʕamo səryoyo harke. W i ʕito das səryoye yo." Ono hawxa məllile. Omər: "Lo?" Omanno: "E, bele, tux, ḥzay!"
contents.versio: 025. When I noticed that he does not like what I am saying I said: if you do not believe me, come with me! We have a church, the church where I serve and where I live, it is two thousand years old, soon it will be two thousand years since it was build, which means that there was Syriac people here. And this church belongs to the Syriac people. Thus I said to him. He said: is that so? I said: yes, come with me and see for yourself!

contents.textus: 026. Axər mədle u nufusayḏi, yaʕni kṯule, zbəṭle b mazbaṭa. W mərwayli ġalabe medone tamo bi mazbaṭa. Mə d mšayele, məllile.
contents.versio: 026. So to continue, he took my identification card and wrote (my personal data) in the protocol. So, there I had said lots of things in the statement; whatever he asked I related for him.

contents.textus: 027. Fayəšno gabayye. Mə d hawyo i saʕa traḥṣar, mkamele i mazbaṭa, hano u mudur di yamniye. Omər: "Zux, ytaw tamo." Yaʕni hano kəmmile taḥt i ʕayno.
contents.versio: 027. I was held there. When it became midnight he was done with the protocol, the chief of security, he said: go over there and sit down. This is called “being watched”.

contents.textus: 028. Azzi, kalino tamo bayn ap polis hul, kalino gabayye hul ṣafro hawxa, yaʕ... qimo w hno baynoṯayye w aʕmayye.
contents.versio: 028. I went there and waited between the policemen. I waited until it became morning, awake between them and with them.

contents.textus: 029. Heš i saʕa hawyo ḥḏo du lalyo, omanno, kfotaḥno talafon lu bayto, gdomanno, gdomanno: "Kali raḥa no w layt mede, d lo saymutu, d lo howutu bi məṭṭala."
contents.versio: 029. When it was one o’clock in the morning I asked if I could phone home to tell, to tell that I am safe and that it is nothing and do not, you do not have to worry about me.

contents.textus: 030. Azzən mərre lu mudur, omər: "Ṭrowe." Omər: "Ṭro fotəḥ." Omər: "Uʕdo d lo gšəmʕo briṯo kula, an noše kulle, kulle kšəmʕi, kale u qašo zbiṭ w lo kəḏ... be mə ǧarile, ksaymi maraq."
contents.versio: 030. They went and asked the chief and he said: alright. He continued: let him make a call. He went on: if not, the whole world will immediately know about this, everyone will know that the priest is arrested and if they do not know.., what happened to him then they will get worry.

contents.textus: 031. Qayəm ftəḥle omər: "Marli i numara!" Məlli u numara du bayto, ftəḥle talafon lu bayto, larke gaban. Omər, ǧġənno ʕam u bayto b səryoyo, ǧġənno ʕam u bayto b səryoyo, ḥa mənne ṣxərle u talafon. Mədle m iḏi. Ṣxərle u talafon qumi, mərle: "Um... mə səmlux."
contents.versio: 031. So he (one of the policemen) dialed, he said: tell me the number! I told him the number home and he dialed the number home, home to us. He said, when I spoke to my wife in Syriac, I spoke to my wife in Syriac, one of them hanged up the phone on me! He snatched it from my hand! He hanged up the phone on me! He said: what have you done?

contents.textus: 032. Omanno: "Hat qay hawxa kosaymat?" Hawxa xəd qḥənno, qḥənno, ṭabi hno polis wayne, qḥənno, omanno: "Qay hawxa kosaymat?"
contents.versio: 032. I said: why do you do that for? I was goaded! Angry! But of course, they were policemen (and I could do not do much about it). So I was angry and said: why do you do this?

contents.textus: 033. Omər: "Hat b mən koməǧġolat?" Omanno: "Koməǧġanno b səryoyo. Mə kəmmat?" Komanno: "Kali raḥa no w layt mede ʕam u baytayḏi, ʕam i iqarṯayḏi." Omər, omər, qḥir, omər: "Hat aydarbo gməǧġolat səryoyo bu bayto? Mə šəkəl gməǧġolat səryoyo?"
contents.versio: 033. He said: in what language do you speak? I said: I speak in Syriac. And what do you say? I am telling them that I am ok and that they do not have to worry, I am calling home, my family. He said, he said, he got angry and said: why do you speak Syriac at home? How dare you speak Syriac at home?

contents.textus: 034. Omanno: "Baʕ b mən gməǧġanno?" Omanno: "Ono səryoyo no. Aṯutu mi ʕito, mbalxuli w alo səryoyo koməǧġolina bu bayto w b səryoyo komṣalina w səryoye na aḥna." Omanno: "U lešonayḏan hano yo!" Omanno: "Lešono ʕatiqo. ʕAtəqtər mine lešone layt, d mšiḥo."
contents.versio: 034. I said: well, in what language should I speak? I said: I am a Syriac person. You came and dragged me from the church and indeed we speak Syriac at home and in Syriac we pray, we are Syriacs. I said: this is our language! I continued: this is an old language; there are no older languages than this. It is the language of Jesus.

contents.textus: 035. Hiye qḥir ġalabe, omər: "Qay bu bayto gməǧġolat səryoyo w lə ǧġilat, lə gməǧġolat tərki?" Omanno: "Hawxa?" Omər: "E." Omanno, qḥənno, omanno: "Haka, haka ha sti", — omanno, — "šrolo gawro ṭawwo hat, izux, kale Dyarbakər u qunaydoġu kule koməǧġəl b kurmanǧi. Izux, lo ṭorat məǧġoli kurmanǧi!" ʕAyn hawxa məllile.
contents.versio: 035. He was very angry. He said: why do you speak Syr.., Syriac at home and did not speak, do not speak Turkish? I said: is that so? He said: yes! I said: I got angry and said: if you are, if you are, I said: a really tough guy, just look around you and see the whole of Diyarbakir, the whole of southeast (of Turkey) speaks Kurdish. Try to forbid them! Exactly these words I said to him!

contents.textus: 036. Hiye ste omər hedi, kali, law aḏəʕ, mə d omər. Kali, law aḏəʕ, mə d omər. Hedi ono sti omanno: "Hat komaḥwe, lo kəḏʕat." Qḥənno mine, omanno: "Lo kəḏʕat ʕam man, mə šəkəl ksaymat hno, maʕmala, hno yaʕni, e."
contents.versio: 036. Thus he too said, he was bewildered, he did not know what to say. He was silenced and did not know what to say. Then I went on and said: you obviously do not know, I was angry at him, I said: you do not know with who, how to handle, how to behave with (people), so to say, yes!

contents.textus: 037. Hedi hawxa kalina hul ṣafro gabayye. U mudur sti, u mudur sti hawi ṣafro, lo, edi bəṯr omər, omər: "Ftaḥ!" Omər: "Ftaḥ, məǧġal b tərki ʕam u bayto."
contents.versio: 037. Thus I was there until the morning! And also the chief, and the chief in the morning, no, after that the policeman said: make your call! Make your call but speak in Turkish with your family!

contents.textus: 038. Ftəḥle, ftəḥle u talafon disa, ǧġənno b tərki ʕam u bayto. Omanno, e omanno, omanno, omanno: "Uʕdo gməǧġanno ʕam i pirayḏi, b tərki lo... ġalabe mede hno, nuxroyo yo, lo kəḏʕoli ze, balki lo məǧġolo aʕmi ze", — omanno.
contents.versio: 038. He dialed the number, he dialed the number again and I spoke in Turkish with my family. I said, hm I said, I said, I said: now I will speak in Turkish with my wife it won’t be ... it is something very, how to say it, strange. She may not even recognize me and she may not talk to me either, I said.

contents.textus: 039. Omər: "Ftaḥ məǧġal, qana d... qana d əḏʕina aḥna sti, mə kəmmat, mə kosaymat, mən hno." Hedi ftəḥle, ǧġənno b tərki ʕam u bayto. Omanno: "Kali ṭawwo na, layt mede, lo saymutu məṭṭala w hawxa."
contents.versio: 039. He said: talk so that, so that we also know what you are saying and what you are doing, what hm.., at the end he dialed the number and I spoke in Turkish with my family. I said to them: I am good and there is nothing to worry about. Do not be concerned about me and so on.

contents.textus: 040. Hedi fayəšno hul ṣafro tamo. I saʕa hawyo ḥamməš u falga ṣafrayto, aṯi u mudur omər: "Qum!" Mərleli, omər: "Qum, papaz afandi, ṣafrayto." Omər: "Qum, hawat mašhur." Hawxa mərleli.
contents.versio: 040. After that I stayed there until the morning. At half past five in the morning, the chief came and said to me: get up! He said to me, he said: get up mister priest, when it was already morning! He said: get up! You have become famous. Thus he said to me.

contents.textus: 041. De, omanno: "Ṭraylux lo." Hawxa qḥənno, b qahar. Omər: "Qum izux, ṭro tre polis, ṭro məblilux lu bayto." Omanno: "Lo!" Hawxa qḥənno. Omanno: "Gəzzi ono." Omər: "Mə šəkəl gəzzux?" Omanno: "Gəzzi, aydarbo towe." Omər: "Lo, lo, ṭro məblilux."
contents.versio: 041. Yeh sure, let it go, I said in anger. I was irritated. He said: get up and let two policemen take you home. I said: no! I was annoyed! I said: I am able to go home myself! He said: how are you going to go by yourself? I said: I will find a way. He said: no, no, let them follow you home.

contents.textus: 042. Aṯən, mṭallalli lu bayto. Aṯina lu bayto, i saʕa hawyo ḥamməš, komqarawla laš šeṯ ṣafro. Aṯino omanno, gdomaxno čike. Lə ṭralle, d domaxno tamo. Omanno, gdomaxno čike. Daməxno əšmo, tarte saʕayat. I saʕa hawyo tmone, ḥəlli, əmmi: "Tux, disa u polis koqorelux. Aṯən annaqqa disa ap polis."
contents.versio: 042. They brought me home. We came home and it was five o’clock, closer to six in the morning. When I came home I thought of sleeping for a while. They did not let me sleep there! I thought of sleeping for a while. I slept for a while, about two hours. When it was eight o’clock they came and woke me up and said: come out, the policemen are here again they are asking about you. Now once again the policemen came to me.

contents.textus: 043. Mən yo? Əmmi: "Tux, annaqqa koqorelux hano, kəmminale u ṣawǧi, ǧumhuriyat, dawlat, güwanlək, maḥkamasi... du ṣawǧi, u rabo di hno, di maḥkama annaqqa. Hayo i masale yariwo." W omanno: "Ṭrowe."
contents.versio: 043. I said to the policemen: what is it now? They said: you have to come with us, this time you are asked for by the, we call it here the prose.., the prosecutor, the regional public prosecutor office, prose.., the prosecutor, the highest position of the, in court here. The problem got obviously bigger and ... I said: so be it then.

contents.textus: 044. Qayəm disa lwəšli ǧuli, azzi, d əzzi ʕam ap polis, ap polis əmmi: "Ma heš lo nafiqat larwal harke?" Omanno: "Lo, lo nafəqno." Omanno: "Qay?" Əmmi: "Kale at talafəzyone w ag gazetat w a hne d briṯo kula kalən qm u tarʕo, kəbʕi, d gərši ṣərto elux." Omanno: "Lə...", — omanno, —"ṭro gərši, ġamo layt." U polis omər: "Lo!" Lo maqbele. Lə ṭrele d gərši.
contents.versio: 044. So I left the policemen to go inside to get dressed and follow the policemen. The policemen asked me: have you not gone outside yet? I said: no, I have not gone out yet. I asked them: why do you ask? They said: well, the whole world’s television networks and newspapers and so are here, just outside your door; they want to photograph you. I said: hm, let them then photograph, I do not care! The policemen said: no! They did not accept that! They did not let the journalists take photos of me.

contents.textus: 045. Hedi i naqqayo hənnək kətwa ḥamšo polis wayne, səfil. Azzən tre mənne, maklalle u ʕamo w ag gazəǧatiye w at talafəzyone, makranne tamo b dukṯo. Ǧġile hawxa, maǧġələnne. Ono sti maʕraqalli, mahzammali tamo da, b dukṯo ḥreto da mofəqalli hul li ǧaʕda, mi ʕito.
contents.versio: 045. Then, there were five of them, the policemen, civil, three of them went out and gathered the crowd of people and the newspaper and television people in one comer; they spoke to them in order to draw their attention while the other dragged me with them, escaping from there. They took me somewhere else away from my church so that we came to the main road.

contents.textus: 046. Mərre, makralle ḥa taqsi maš šaʕuṯe, mərre, mərre: "Taqsi, klay!" Mərre: "Hano maḥkum yo." Mərre: "Hano maḥkum yo." Mərralle hawxa, qana d l obən, d l obən kallawat lu taqsi.
contents.versio: 046. They stopped a taxi, one of these yellow ones. They said: taxi driver stop! This man here, referring to me, is a condemned (criminal). They said to him: this one here is a convict. They told him this so that they will not have to pay him money for the ride.

contents.textus: 047. Mballalli li hno, mballalli lu maḥkama tamo. Azzino, yatuno, ap polis kanne aʕmi. U ṣawǧi, hano, d annaqqa, annaqqa kḥoyanno omər: "Me qime gdobat i ifada!"
contents.versio: 047. They took me to the, what is it called, they took me to the court there. I went there and sat down and the policemen still with me. The district attorney that was in charge, this time, said: you will give the statement while standing!

contents.textus: 048. Omanno b qaḥar omanno: "Aydarbo d əbʕat hawxa." Ono qḥərwayno. Fayəš ġalabe ʕaǧəzwayno w omanno, mən d howe, gdomanno, mən d oṯe qəm femi, gdomanno, law... hič haw ksamno tə hno.
contents.versio: 048. I answered irritated and said: as you wish so it will be! I was annoyed! I was very distressed and said to myself: whatever happens I do not care and whatever comes to my mind I will say it without thinking of the consequences.

contents.textus: 049. Qayəm koqore i ifada, d hiwoli ʕaṣriye kula, b lalyo, i ifadayo kula koqorela. Komər: "Haṯe hat hulux i ifadaṯe?" Omanno: "E, ono hiwoli." Omər: "Kito mede ḥreno, d maḥtat aʕla?" Omanno: "E." Omanno: "Kito mede ḥreno, d maḥənno aʕla."
contents.versio: 049. Thus he started reading up the whole statement that I gave in the evening, in the night. He reads up all that statement and says: have you given this statement? I said: yes, I gave it. He asked: do you have anything else to add to it? I answered: yes. There is something more to add to it!

contents.textus: 050. Annaqla i naqlayo kṯuwalle aʕli bag gazetat d Tərkiya harke "u xayən d baynoṯayna!" W kətwa u ṣlibo sti b iḏi, ḥzalle, balki ḥzallux bi hno. Mərre: "U xayən d baynoṯayna." Mən yo, qana d oṯe noše, d qoṭeli sti! Hul li daraǧayo.
contents.versio: 050. So at that time they had written about me in the newspapers, here in Turkey “the traitor among us” and there was also the cross in my hand, in my ... they had obviously seen it. You may also have seen in the ... “the traitor among us”! They made all this up so that someone will come and kill me! See all this was thought through!

contents.textus: 051. Maḥtalle "u xayən d baynoṯayna", yaʕni kulle ṭaye ne. Ono, ḥa ono bas ṣuroyo w qašo maqbeli... u sayfo, u qṭəl ʕamo dann armənoye w das səryoye. Məlli: "Me kule lebi komanno w kmaqbanno w hawi."
contents.versio: 051. They wrote “the traitor among us”! Do you understand? They are all Muslims and I am the only Christian and priest! I acknowledged the kil.., the massacre, the ethnical cleansing of the Armenian and the Syriac people. I said: I am saying that the massacre occurred and I admit it took place!

contents.textus: 052. Annaqqa žboyi d oṯe ḥa, d qoṭeli, hawxa səmme hno, maḥətte hno tamo. Annaqla qrele, qrele i hno, hano, ifada, qəryole, d hiwoli kula. Omər: "Kit mede ḥreno, d əmmat?" Omanno: "E." Omanno: "Tamo maḥətte aʕli, mərre eli "xayən tamo"!"
contents.versio: 052. Consequently, for the reason that someone will come and murder me, they made up all this, they presented the matter in this way. So he read up, he read up the statement, this distr.., he read up the whole statement that I had given. He asked: do you have something more to add? I answered: yes! I said: they are presenting me as a traitor there (in the newspapers)!

contents.textus: 053. Omanno: "Aḥna ʕamo səryoyo." Omanno: "Hani bann alfowat əšne", — omanno, — "kalan harke koʕayšina w ʕam Turkiya, ʕam i dawla me zawno, me dore yarixe kalan ʕam i dawla d Turkiya koʕayšina. W aḥna ʕamo ṭawwo ʕam i dawla.
contents.versio: 053. I said: we are Syriac people. I continued: we have been living here for thousands of years and also within the state of Turkey, since long time back, since long centuries back in time we are living side by side with the state. And we are good people to this state.

contents.textus: 054. Bass i dawla, i dawla d Turkiya lo kəḏʕo, l aḏiʕo i qimayḏan. D əmmina, l aḏiʕo bu i qimayḏan. D əmmina, l aḏiʕo bu qadrayḏan, d kətwayna hawxa ʕam ṭawwo, d kətwayna hno, d kətwaylan, d əmmina, kultur, d kətwaylan mede hno. L aḏiʕo i qimayḏan". Omanno: "Aḥna kosaymina ʕaskariye, kobina vargi, ko..., aḥna mə d, mə d kolozəm, kosaymina laf i dawla.
contents.versio: 054. But the state, the state of Turkey does not know our ... did not appreciate our significance, I mean the state did not know the value of us being fine people, being what is it called, that we had a culture, that we had something particu.., did not appreciate our value. I said: we serve in the military, we pay taxes, we ... whatever is asked from us, what is needed from us, we offer it to the state.

contents.textus: 055. Bas ono mərralli harke 'xayə...', kəmmili 'xayən'!" Omanno: "Kṯaw tamo: u ḥa, d mərleli 'xayən', xayən hiye yo." Hedi kṯule hawo sti tamo, maḥətle ʕal i hnayo w... hedi bəṯərke qayəm omər, aṯən tre polis, disa mṭallalli lu bayto. Hedi huwalli li maḥkama.
contents.versio: 055. But they are presenting me as a “traitor” here, they write that I am a “traitor”! I would like you to write down there that the one who is calling me a “traitor”, the traitor must be he himself! So actually the district attorney wrote down this too, he added it to my statement and ... Thereafter the district attorney ordered two policemen to bring me home again. After that I was sent to the district court proceedings.

contents.textus: 056. I maḥkama ṭləbbe eli šeṯ, me arbaʕ əšne hul šeṯ əšne ḥapəs. I daʕwa komalla tlaṯmo traḥṣar, tlaṯmo traḥṣar. D əmmina, u ḥa folaġ u ʕamo, d əmmina, folaġno ʕamo, xəd folaġno u ʕamo səryoyo, maqəmne mqabəl di dawla d Turkiya, mede hawxa.
contents.versio: 056. At court they pleaded for six, from four to six years in jail. The charge is known as three hundred twelve, 312! It means that when someone tries to split the people, as if I would divide the people, for example as if I would split the Syriac people and make them rise up against the state of Turkey, something like this.

contents.textus: 057. Tlaṯmo, i daʕwa kəmmila tlaṯmo traḥṣar. Ono me arbaʕ əšne hul šeṯ əşne huwwalli ḥapəs, xəd məlli, ṭləbballi yaʕni. E, hedi huwwalli li maḥkama.
contents.versio: 057. Three hundred, the case is known as three hundred twelve. They sentenced me to jail four to six years, they pleaded for this sentence, as I mentioned. So they sent me to district court proceedings.

contents.textus: 058. I maḥkama, kuḏʕutu, aṯən, mi maḥkama, aṯiwa ʕamo ġalabe me, mu Swed w me, me Almanya sti, aṯiwa w kətwa, w ʕamo, yaʕni kətwa, kətwa baynoṯayye mu parlamanto du Swed. Kətwa noše w kətwa hani zədqe nušoye, inṣan ḥaqlari, zədqe nušoye kəmminanne, awrəp..., d Awruppa aṯənwa hənnək sti.
contents.versio: 058. At the court hearings, as you know, lots of people came to the court; people came from Sweden and also from, from Germany came people and there were people, there were, there were between them some people from the parliament of Sweden and there were people from the human rights organizations, in Syriac we say Zddqe nusoye and from the Europ.., European Union also.

contents.textus: 059. W ḥatta i naqqayo lu ǧumhur bašqani d Almanya, hiye ste kṯuwwayle maktub aʕmayye eli, laǧani mšadarle: "Kṭəlbinalux šlomo w kṭəlbinalux hno..." — hawxa medone kṯuwwayle bu maktubayḏe.
contents.versio: 059. And at that time also the ambassador of Germany, he also had written a letter for me and sent it with the delegation. He sent me a letter saying that he sends me greetings and wishing me what is it called ... this kind of words he wrote in his letter.

contents.textus: 060. W aṯən larke aʕmi hul li maḥkama, hul li maḥkama qamayto w ġalabe haṯe maḥwela hno rabo, d əmmina, d əmmina, ḥaylo rabo. Turkiya zayiʕo, d əmmat. Aṯən hani kulle li maḥkama aʕmi, i naqqa d azzi li maḥkama.
contents.versio: 060. And they (the delegations) came with me all the way to the court, to the first court hearings. And this showed, of course a huge demonst..as you would say a huge support. It was obvious that Turkey was afraid then. All these came to the court hearings with me! When I attended the hearings.

contents.textus: 061. U ḥakəm məlle, qrele i ġazetayo di Hürriyat, d kətwa u ṣlibo b iḏi, omər: "Hat", — mšayele mini, w hənnək kulle ʕabiri li maḥkama, hani, d aṯən, kəpwalle arbʕi šaxṣat, ḥamši balki, omər omər, — "kale kqoreno, hat məllux am medonani kulle?" Mədle qrele i Hürriyet. Omanno: "E, hani kule ǧġilinanne, mirili." Maḥtile tamo, kṯiwile tamo.
contents.versio: 061. The judge started reading that article in the newspaper of Hurriyat, where I was photographed with a cross in my hand. He said: did you, he addressed the question to me while all the people that had come (from out of the country) had entered the court hall; these ones were almost forty, maybe fifty people, he said, he said: I will now read, have you made all these statements? He started then reading the article in Hurriyat. I said: yes, we talked about this, I said these things and the journalist put them there, he wrote them there (in the newspaper).

contents.textus: 062. Hedi bəṯr mi naqqayo mtaxarre i daʕwa, ḥzalle, d əmmina, aṯi ʕamo ġalabe m Awruppa, mtaxralle. W i naqqa dat tarte sti disa, disa, disa qrallalli li maḥkama. Disa a sniġrayḏi, yaʕni u mede, d lazəm, mərre, lo hnalle... w ono sti u mede, d lazəm, yaʕni lo daʕənno bi... bu mede, d məlli.
contents.versio: 062. Thus, after that they postponed the court hearings, after noticing that a large group of people came from Europe to attend the hearings, they postponed it. And also the second time, also, also they called me to the court hearings. Once again, my lawyers, I mean, they presented what had to be presented and they did not ... I also said what was needed to be said, I mean, I did not withdraw my statement, I did not deny what I said before.

contents.textus: 063. W hedi da tlaṯ si hawxa. Hedi bəṯr hiye hawiwa ġalabe mu ʕamayḏan, noše mšaylone, d əmmina, ġalabe mšayalle, d əmmina, maḥwalle ḥaylo rabo. U ʕamayḏan kule d Awruppa maḥwalle ḥaylo rabo, yaʕni, xud kuḏʕutu, balki b Almanya, kətwa balki ḥamšo-əšto alfo šaxṣat ṣayəm yawmo w səmme hno mqabəl d Turkiya.
contents.versio: 063. The third date for the court hearings, was like the two before it. This was all due to the crowds of our people who were engaged in this case. Many were engaged and showed immense courage. Everyone of our people in Europe showed immense courage. As you may know, in Germany there were maybe five, six thousand people that went on hunger strike for a day to express their opinion against Turkey.

contents.textus: 064. Hani kulle mṭanne, maḥwallan, maḥwallan li hno, lu... lu ḥakəm harke, kale hawxa yo i masale w u ʕamo kule bəṯr i masalaṯe yo w bəṯr u qašo yo w layto hno.
contents.versio: 064. All these facts were brought, were brought forward to the, to the judge here. See here, this is how the case is; the whole people are following up this case and supporting the priest and there is no way out.

contents.textus: 065. Hedi zayiʕo b hawxa lo... lə ḥkəmlali, hiye u... u..., xəd komanno, hiye, u qonṣoloṣ sti, u qonṣoloṣ d Ameriqa ste mšayewayle mini, d Amariqa, mšayewayle mini, omər: "Ma mḥallallux? Mərrallux mede?"
contents.versio: 065. So they were scared and that is why they did not sentence me. Another thing, fact may be that, that as I understood it, that also the consul, the consul of the United States had asked me, of the United States had asked me saying: did they torture you? Did they insult you?

contents.textus: 066. Omanno: "Lo mḥallalli, bass ʕal d məǧġol..., ʕal d koməǧġoliwayna səryoyo bu bayto, ḥa mənne mʕanatle hawxa aʕmi, qḥir. Mərle: "Qay koməǧġolat səryoyo bu bayto?" Mərwayli am medonani kulle lu qonṣoloṣ sti w hawxa.
contents.versio: 066. I said: no, they did not torture me but because I spok.., because I am speaking Syriac at home one of them was displeased with me. He was furious! He said to me: Why do you speak Syriac at home? All these aspects I had presented them to the consul also.

contents.textus: 067. W kətwa hiye mu ʕamayḏan sti, kətwa hən yaʕni zayʕiwa, d əmmina, d Ṣṭanbəl, am mardnoye, ġalabe, ġalabe zayʕiwa, mərre: "Dʕar eba." Mərre, mərre: "Dʕar, mdagal u mede, d məllux, mdagele bag gazetat, bat talafəzyone."
contents.versio: 067. And of course there were among our people those who were scared, for example those living in Istanbul, the Merdellis. They were very, very scared and asked me to deny what I stated. They said, they said: take it back and deny what you have said, deny it in the ne.., in the newspapers and on television.

contents.textus: 068. Ono məlli: "Lo, lo kəmdaganno, laybi mdaganno." W mərwayli, xəd məlli ba hne sti, bag gazetat sti awwəl, naqla d nafiqowa, ono məlli: "Ono kuhno no, lo kəmdaganno w lə kowe d mdaganno. U medano šrolo yo w hawxa yo." W hawxa tamo sti məlli, hawxa yo yaʕni, hič lo daʕənno eba w məlli.
contents.versio: 068. I said: no, I will not deny and cannot do that. And I had also said, as you know, in the newspapers, the first time this case appeared there, that I am a priest and do not lie and it does not suit me to lie. This whole matter is true and it happened and this is what I said there, in the newspapers and hence I will never take it back and deny it. Thus I said to them.

contents.textus: 069. W kətwa hən mu ʕamayḏan, ġalabe hnewalle, ġalabe kətwa hən, zayiʕiwa, d əmmina, d kətne zangin, d kətne hne. Kətwa ḥa mərle, omər, ftəḥleli talafon, omər: "Moqaḏluxlan, moqaḏluxlan." Hawxa mərle: "Moqaḏluxlan. Aydarbo gsaymət mede hawxa?"
contents.versio: 069. And there were some of our people that were very, that were very afraid, those who are wealthy, that are such. There was this one who said to me, he called me and said on the phone: you have burned us up, you have burned us up, these were his exact words, you have burned us up! How can you do something like this?

contents.textus: 070. Omanno: "Lo? Ma mə səmli, ma gmoqaḏlux?" Omər: "Lo kowe d əmmat medone mani!" Omanno: "Məlli w azzeyo." Omanno: "Məlli w azzeyo." U mede, d məlli, məlli w azzeyo. Haw kodoʕər, omanno.
contents.versio: 070. I said to him: is that so? What have I done to bum you up? He said: you cannot make this kind of announcement. I said: I have already said it and it is done; I said: I have already said it and it is done. What I have said, I said it and it is done and will not come back, thus I told him.

contents.textus: 071. E, omər, omər: "Gəmšadanno u talafəzyon gabux, mar, mdagal i masale, mar flan!" Omanno: "Laybi samno mede hawxa. U mede, d məlli, šrolo yo! Ono, u wuždanayḏi raḥat yo. Šrolo məlli w hawxa yo."
contents.versio: 071. Well, he said, he said: I will send the television (journalist) to you and you will say, you withdraw the whole matter and so. I said: I cannot do such a thing. What I stated is true! My conscience is calm and I just spoke the truth and that is all.

contents.textus: 072. W hedi hawxa, yaʕni ġalabe mu ʕamayḏan maḥwewalle hno mqabəl... bas yaʕni u ʕamayḏan kul gave komaškanne, yaʕni bi masalayo, ġalabe. Ġalabe tawdi l kulle, yaʕni d maḥwalle ḥaylo ġalabe rabo bi hnaṯṯe.
contents.versio: 072. And this way it was. Our people in general showed great, what is it called, against ... But I have to say that I always thank our people for their support to me in this case. I thank them all for the great courage they showed in this matter.

contents.textus: 073. W haṯe masale hawyowa ġalabe rabṯo asasan, yaʕni xəd məlli, xəd mərle, mərralle, bu talafəzyon sti haṯe latwa i masalayḏi w bas, d əmmina, i masala du ʕamo səryoyo kule, du ʕamayḏan du mšiḥoyo kule yo haṯe.
contents.versio: 073. This whole issue had taken on huge proportions from the beginning. As I mentioned, as I said, it was also broadcast on television; this was clearly not only my case but the case of all the Syriac people, our people, all Christians!

contents.textus: 074. Haṯe i naqqa, d qṭilənne, lo mərre: "Hani bas kquṭlina." Qṭəlle u ʕamo, ayna d maṭ..., u ʕamo mšiḥoyo kule qṭəlle. D qədriwa, gəmkamliwa kule.
contents.versio: 074. When the massacres started the murderers did not think that we will only slaughter these or those. They slaughtered whole groups people, anyone that came in their way, the whole Christian population. If the murderers had a chance they would have finished them totally.

contents.textus: 075. E, yaʕni haṯe balki, d əmmina, m Aloho wa. Balki i n aqqa d mšayele mini, ono, hən, hən mu ʕamo mərre: "Mdagal i masale." I naqqa d mšayele mini u ḥakəm, omər, omər, ono yaʕni hawxa, mṣawər qul ʕayni, omanno: "Aʕu", — omanno, — "aydarbo gdomanno, lawi u medano, yaʕni ono, lo maqbele u wuždanayḏi, lo hnele."
contents.versio: 075. Nevertheless, this may be, as we say, something divine. When the judge asked me; I still cannot believe how some of the people asked me to take back what I said, when the judge asked me and said, said ... I had a flashback, everything (the horror of the massacre that I heard about) came back to me again and I thought to myself: how can I say this never happened, my conscience did not accept it, it did not allow it.

contents.textus: 076. Omanno, haqqa qṭəlle ʕamo, haqqa qṭəlle, quṭliwa yaʕni kuhne, ḥasye, dayroye, hič lo marḥəmiwa appe, aydarbo gdomanno, lawi mede hawxa. Omanno, omanno: e, hawi, mə d kowe, ṭrowe omanno.
contents.versio: 076. I said to myself: so many many people they slaughtered, so much killing, they slaughtered priests, bishops, monks and did not show any kind of mercy towards them. How can I say that this never occurred? I said, I said: this took place for sure and I am not afraid of the consequences of what I am saying.

contents.textus: 077. Zədtər mu mawto? Omanno, u mede, d səmme, səmme eban, yaʕni hawxa məftakalli, u mede, d səmme, səmme, zədtər mawxa law kəppe saymi. Omanno: ṭrowe, ṭro saymi sti. Yaʕni hawi, hawi, šrolo yo.
contents.versio: 077. Gould the consequences be harder that death? What they did to us can never be undone again. Thus I thought: what they have done to us is already done and they cannot do more than tha. I thought: if they want to do more, so be it then. But what they already have done it is done. It happened and it is true.

contents.textus: 078. W hawxa yaʕni, xəd kuḏʕutu, šmiʕ yaʕni b briṯo kula. Ono mərwayli bag gazetat sti, omanno: "Gmašmaʕno qoli b briṯo kula w koṭəlbina u ḥaqqayḏan. Qay aḥna dlo suǧ w dlo sabab qṭəllallan, maḥətte, mṭalle sayfo aʕlayna." — ʕayn hawxa məftakarwayno ono yaʕni.
contents.versio: 078. And this is, as you may have heard, this case was known all over the world. I had also stated in the newspapers, that I will make my voice heard all over the world and we are, we are demanding our rights. Why were we without any reason or guilt massacred? Why did they put, bring a Sayfo over us. Exactly this way I was thinking at that time.

contents.textus: 079. Ġalabe noše sti, lə gbaʕno d omanno ann əšmonaṯṯe sti, d əmmina, d mərre: "Dʕar eba." Kətwa hən kuhne, kətwa hən ʕamo, kətwa hən mərre: "Kquṭlilux." Kətwa hən, d mərre, mərre: "Kquṭlilux, kṣuxri i ʕito."
contents.versio: 079. Many people, I do not wish to name names here, pleaded with me to withdraw what I said. Among them also priests, other people; they said: they will murder you! Some of them said, they said: they will kill you and close down the church.

contents.textus: 080. Ono məlli omanno: "Ṭro quṭlili, lanno ṭaw manək, d qṭili. Ṭro ṣuxri i ʕito. Haka ʕal foṯi d məṣxoro i ʕito, ṭro ṣuxrila. Ma i ʕito layba... qay ma hno yo gṣuxri i ʕito. E, hawxa yaʕni, hawxa yo."
contents.versio: 080. I answered and said: let them then kill me! Iam in no way better than all those that were massacred! Let them close down the church! If the church will be closed down because of me, let them then kill ... close it down! The church cannot ... it won’t be that easy to close down the church. So, this is it, this is how it is.

contents.textus: 081. E, tlaṯ kore yaʕni ḥkəmmalli bi maḥkama rabṯo d Dyarbakər, d Turkiya yaʕni. Tlaṯ kore, ʕal d məlli, qṭil u ʕamo səryoyo, aṯi sayfo aʕle w hawxa yaʕni.
contents.versio: 081. Three times I was examined in the highest court in Diyarbakir in Turkey. Three times just because I said that the Syriac people were massacred, a Sayfo was brought over them. That is all.

contents.textus: 001. B šrolo e, hiya i ṣbuṯo, ṣbuṯo rabṯo hawyowa b šrolo, hawyo aʕmi. Ono ste yaʕni naqqat kmiʕaǧabno, komanno: məš šəkəl xaləṣno mina.
contents.versio: 001. To be honest, the, well, what happened to me was a great issue, frankly. Sometimes I myself wonder and ask myself how I got away with it.

contents.textus: 002. Hiye, i naqqa d... i naqqa d ḥkəmno bat... komanno, tlaṯmo w ḥḏaḥṣar, i daʕwa d tlaṯmo w ḥḏaḥṣar. Harke b Turkiya, d əmmina, ḥa d foləġ u ʕamo, yaʕni d maqəmle ʕal i dawla.
contents.versio: 002. When, when I was put on trial, I believe it was three hundred and eleven, under Article three hundred and eleven. This means, here in Turkey, when someone divides the people, makes the people rise against the state.

contents.textus: 003. Maʕnata eli fləġli as səryoye, maqimili ʕal i dawla d Turkiya. Mu... mu... mu xṣuṣan... yaʕni mu medano ḥkəmno w tlaṯ kore, tlaṯ kore ḥkəmno bi maḥkama ʕelayto, yaʕni d kəmminala ʕelayto, i rabṯo tarke, d Diyarbakər, d Turkiya.
contents.versio: 003. This means that I have divided the Syriac people, made them rise against the state of Turkey. Becau.., becau.., for this matter I was put on trial three times. I was put on trial three times in the high court, what we call high court, the greatest one here, in Diyarbakir, in Turkey.

contents.textus: 004. W a tlaṯ kore sti halbat, xud kətyo iḏiʕo alxu, aṯi, aṯi noše folitiqore, noše, d əmmina, noše b darġe ʕeloye, du Swed, xəd qonṣoloṣe aṯi, dəṯxu hayo i wazərto barayto aṯyowa. Hayo d qṭilalle.
contents.versio: 004. And the three times, as it is, of course known for you, politicians came and as we say, people of high positions came, from Sweden, such as consular, your foreign minister came, the one that later was murdered.

contents.textus: 005. Tlaṯ kore aṯyo, aṯənwa xtani noše rabe, b darġe ʕeloye aṯənwa, aṯənwa li maḥkamayḏi w xaləṣno mina... kuḏʕat, hiye harke, harke mu... mi daʕwaṯe, tlaṯmo ḥḏaḥṣar, noše harke ste ḥkim, d əmmina b Turk... b gawe d Turkiya, d kətwayne, d əmmina, xud d uʕdo diḏan, u riš waziro diḏan. ʕAyni daʕwa ḥkim.
contents.versio: 005. She came three times; such people of high status came three times. They attended my hearings and I was saved. You know, also other people here were put on trial according to Article three hundred and eleven, Turks so to say, in Turkey, people that were, such as our own prime minister. He was put on trial for the same allegations.

contents.textus: 006. Hiye tre xabre, d latwayne diḏe, d ḥa, tre kaṯowe wayne, ḥkim w xile ḥapəs, daməx ḥapəs w hule zuze. Bas ono xaləṣno mina. Halbat haṯe, haṯe lo hawxa mede fšiqo hawyo. Paṯe halbat gmaškanno u ʕamayḏan kule, yaʕni u ʕamayḏan kule, d hawili mʕadrono w msaʕdono, d maqəmme, d əmmina, orifi li raġlo.
contents.versio: 006. It was because of a couple of words, that were not his own and that other people had written, he was sentenced to jail. He was put in jail and he had to pay money. But I was saved. But of course, this did not pass that effortlessly. For this I thank all our people, all our people that stood beside me and assisted me and that rallied the whole of Europe for this matter.

contents.textus: 007. Kit hən d səmme halxe, kit hən d ṣayimiwa, kətwa hən d ġalabe d səmwalle ḥṭufye laǧ..., ḥfiṭoṯo laǧani. Pawxa, pawxa, pawxa xaləṣno aṣaṣ. Maškanno u ʕamayḏan ġalabe w...
contents.versio: 007. Some people organized demonstrations, others did, for example some organized activities for my cause. Because of this, because of this, because of this I was saved. I thank our people very much and ...

contents.textus: 008. W halbat i masale masale rabṯo wa, xəd məlli. Maʕnata, maʕnata ono, i naqqa d ḥkəmno, d lo, d lo maḥətlali bu ḥapəs. Hiya ṭəlbowayli ḥapəs w kito, xud məlli, bu šəklayḏi d ḥkimi ġalabe noše harke sti, damixi ḥapəs, maʕnata maqbela yaʕni, i ṣbuṯo du sayfo, d hawi ʕal u ʕamayḏan.
contents.versio: 008. And of course, the problem was a great one, as I mentioned. It shows that, that when I was not sentenced and not sent to prison; the court was arguing for jail; and as I mentioned, there are quite many that had been sent to prison here, put in jail, which means that the issue of the genocide of our people is accepted.

contents.textus: 009. W b šrolo, yaʕni, yaʕni mu yawmo, yaʕni ono mu yawmo, d koḏaʕno ruḥi, koḏaʕno, d hawi, hawi u sayfano ʕal u ʕamayḏan. Bas malasaf kito mu ʕamayḏan, mu ʕamayḏan yaʕni kito d heš lo komaqbli, d hawi sayfo. Heš yaʕni, d kəmmi, lawi.
contents.versio: 009. And frankly since, as long as I remember I know that it happened, that there was a genocide of our people. But sadly there are some of our people, among our people, that still do not accept this fact. They still think that it did not happen.

contents.textus: 010. Ono gabi u ḥa, d lo maqbəl, hawi sayfo, maʕnata, maʕnata xayə... hani koməḥšowi, xəd, mə šəkəl d omannux, ḥa d omar xayən, latyo šafiro, elo mede hawxa. E, annaqla balki stene hənnək koṭəʕni, d əmmina, ġamo, d lowe mede. Ya gzayʕi. Ya... yaʕni ḥa kibe d oballe ḥaqq sti naqqawat.
contents.versio: 010. According to me, the one who does not accept the fact that it did really happen, he is a trai.., these may be seen as, how shall I explain it to you, if I say traitor it won’t be nice, but actually something similar. But on the other hand, they maybe are worried, that something bad will happen. Or they are anxious. Or ... but sometimes one may think that they are correct.

contents.textus: 011. Ama bas ḥa lə glozəm zoyəʕ. Haṯi i šrolo yo. Hano, hano u makṯab zabnayḏan yo, u tarixayḏan yo. Layban kufrina ebe ste. Aḥna, xəd mšiḥoye, haka qṭilina, ʕal foṯe d kətwayna mšiḥoye, ʕal foṯe d Mšiḥo, layban kufrina. Lo lazəm kufrina eba sti, fahimat?
contents.versio: 011. But one should not be afraid. This is the truth. This is our history, our past. We cannot deny it either. We as Christians, if we have been slaughtered because we were Christians, because of Christ, we cannot deny it. Nor should we ever deny it, do you understand?

contents.textus: 012. E, hawxa yo. Halbat bəṯr mi ṣbuṯayo d xaləṣno mina, maškərina Aloho, d xaləṣno mina dlo hno, dlo zə..., dlo tahlukat, dlo mede, dlo zəḥṯo. Hawi xaliṣina, maškərina Aloho.
contents.versio: 012. And so, after that I was saved from that trouble, I thank God that I have been saved without, what it is called, without, without any harm or any thing, and without dread. It happened that I have escaped and I thank God.

contents.textus: 013. Bəṯr mina hawi, howewa masalat, d əmmina. Kətwa, d əmmina, naqlawat ḥa, u ʕamo, d kətwa tarke, u waxtawo halbat, yaʕni uʕdo hani košapəʕ aʕla, balki taqriban traḥṣar əšne mede. I naqlayo ḥayriwa, kətwa b ʕayno lo ṭawto ebi. D əmmina, d ayriwa ebi harke ġalabe.
contents.versio: 013. After that happened, there used to happen various things to us. There were times, so to say, the people that were here, of course at that time, not now since almost twelve years have passed since then, at that time they used to look at me with mistrustfulness. They observed me a lot.

contents.textus: 014. Balki ḥzalxu, šamiʕutu, u ḥa, a ʕlayme d əzzənwa w duʕriwa, u ʕamo moḥənwa rapsat bat tarʕayḏan w ba... ba... w əmmiwaylan xabre. W kətwa, d əmmina, moḥənwa kefe sti me, me laʕlal, mu šuro di ʕito, moḥənwa kefe eban w tawriwa, d əmmina, ǧamat. W saymiwa ġalabe hno, həṣrono aʕlayna bam medonani, u waxtawo halbat. Uʕdo ṭawtər yo.
contents.versio: 014. You maybe have seen, heard, that some young men that passed the alley, back and forth, used to kick our doors, and that, and that, and they called us names. And there were some who used to throw stones from above, from the wall of the church. They used to throw stones on us and used to break, for example the windows. They used to cause us lots of harm, damage through these kinds of acts, at that time of course. Now it is better.

contents.textus: 015. Bəṯr kibi d omanno, ʕal hawxa sti, naqqa masala, kibi d obeno ṭofṣo, naqqa kətwo hən naʕime, ʕlayme, d əmmina, arbaḥṣar ḥamšaḥṣar əšne, w d rabtər sti, moḥənwa kefe.
contents.versio: 015. Concerning this I also can mention, I can give an example, once, once there were children, young men, let us say fourteen, fifteen year-olds, and also older, they repeatedly threw stones.

contents.textus: 016. Naqqa azzi, nafəqno, məlli l ḥa, omanno: "Qay gmoḥat kefe, yaʕni hawxa eban aḥna? Mə səmlan ebux?" Məlli la... lan nošayḏe hič lo hnalle ebi. Yaʕni hawxa lo ḥərre b... hič luwwalli foṯo, hawxa xəd ḥa d əmmi: hat ḥaqq hat. Kmaliqat d moḥən kefe ebux yaʕni.
contents.versio: 016. So once I went out and said to one of them: why are you throwing stones on us in this way? What have we done to you? I said to his family but they did not at all bother. They did not even look me in theeyes, so to say. They did not care, as if they wanted to say: it is correct behavior towards you. You deserve to be hit with stones.

contents.textus: 017. E, w naqqat sti disa ḥa, ḥa naʕimo moḥewo disa kef. Disa, disa azze, məlli la... yaʕni ḥoziwaynanne harke, ḥeḏorayna taqriban kuḏʕinanne, me zabno yarixo ono harke, azzi, məlli lu babo. U babo mərle: "Zux marke!" Hawxa, hawxa lo ṭawwo, b naxwaš, hawxa no, mərle: "Zux marke!" Xəd d əmmat yaʕni məqšaṭ, hawxa mede. Edi ṭreli mine halbat, hedi.
contents.versio: 017. Yes, and sometimes, also a child used to toss stones. Again, again I went and said to his, because we used to see them here, around us, we knew who they were, I have been here for a long time, so I went and sai.., told his father. His father said: go away! In such bad way, brutal, such as, he said: go away! As if he said: get the hell out of here! Or something similar. Thus, of course, I left him.

contents.textus: 018. B ḥa may yawme sti b ḥa yawmo sti kətwo ḥa disa m... ʕlaymo rab... yaʕni kəpwayle ḥamšaḥṣar əštaḥṣar əšne. Hawxa mazʕaqle bəṯri omər yaʕni: "Papaz papaz!" Yaʕni qašo qašo, hawxa mqašmalle aʕli.
contents.versio: 018. And also one day, one day there was also someone, an old, a young man, he was a fifteen, sixteen year-old. He shouted at med: papazpapaz, which means “vicar vicar”. Thus he made fun of me, so to say.

contents.textus: 019. Məlli: "D man hat?" Məlli: "Ma ayko yo u baytayḏux?" Azze mahzamle. Aḥ ḥawrone mərralli: "Zux, kale u baytayḏe harke." Azzi məlli omanno: "U abraṯxu hawxa komər." Ha... hanək sti, yaʕni xəd d əmmat, xəd d əmmat lo b ʕayno hno, yaʕni xəd lo ḥaruwe. Xəd d əmmat med... ṭawwo səmle ebux yaʕni hawxa.
contents.versio: 019. I asked: whose son are you? Where do you live? He rushed away. His friends said to me: he lives just here, go there! I went there and said: thus your son says to me. Also they, as if you would say, as if you would say, did not appreciate me, as if they did not care at all, as if you would say: whatever he did against you, you deserve it.

contents.textus: 020. Hawxa bu šəklano ha... howewo medone aʕmayna b šrolo. U ḥa yawmo sti kətwaylan d əmmina naqla hawxa ḏayfe, orḥe bi dərto yatiwayna. Ḥzelux i dərtayḏan. Bu qayṭo koyətwina tamo. Mḥalle kefe nafiqina, qəm ʕaṣriye. Nafiqina kalən, be man, kḥozina man komoḥe koḥozina qay komoḥən.
contents.versio: 020. So truthfully, in such way we were exposed to incidents. And also one day we had, so to say, guests, visitors and we were sitting in the courtyard. You have seen our courtyard. In summer we usually sit out there. It was early evening and they threw stones. We went out. We wanted to see who they were and why they were throwing stones.

contents.textus: 021. Ḥəllan kalən kəppe, kəppe balki ʕaṣro ḥamšaḥṣar ʕlayme, ḥaṭroṯe, skine masalat b iḏayye. Lo... yaʕni lo maǧrelan d mqadmina sti. Lə mqadamlan, d əmmina d nofəq mede mina. Kətwaylan ḏayfe sti, mʕaǧbi. Fayiši hawxa ʕəǧbo, kəmmi: "Aydarbo kowe hawxa medone?" Ḏayfe yatiwe.
contents.versio: 021. We saw immediately that they were almost, almost ten, fifteen young men armed with sticks, knives and such things. We did not, we did not even dare to approach them. We did not start to talk to them to inform ourselves about the reason. We had also guests sitting there and they were bewildered. They were astonished and wondered: how such things may occur, our sitting visitors.

contents.textus: 022. W xəd hawxa medone, hawxa, aḥna fayəš yaʕni yalifiwayna, xəd d əmmat, hawiwa normal elan. Yaʕni kul gave d əmmina gnəfqatwa gdəmmiwalux xabro. Gdəmmiwalux ‘papaz, papaz’, ’gawər gawər’, yaʕni. Gawər yaʕni maʕnayḏa lo komətyaqnat l Aloho, e hawxa.
contents.versio: 022. And this kind of incident, such, we got used to it, as if one would say, it became normality for us. Every now and then when I went out they would say something bad; they would, for example say, papaz papaz,gawdr gawdr. gawdr means that you do not believe in God, yes, so.

contents.textus: 023. Hawxa medone hawxa ġalabe əmmiwa bəṯrayna w b ḥa... w moḥənwa kefe eban w moḥənwa kefe ʕal mi... əh, ʕəl mi... ʕəl mu šuro di ʕito da eban. Xəd məlli tawriwa aǧ ǧamatayḏan, tawriwa medone. Saymiwa ḥəṣrono li ʕito w elan tavda. W bu tarʕo moḥənwa.
contents.versio: 023. They often used such utterances when one passed. And one, and they used to toss stones at me, and they also threw stones over the chur.., over the chur.., over the wall of the church towards us. As I mentioned, they used to damage our windows and other things. They caused the church and us together much destruction. And they also used to hit against the door.

contents.textus: 024. W kətwa d əmmina ġalabe maṭ ṭaye sti d harke aṣaṣ yaʕni bu šəršaṯṯe, həs mu sayfo d omanno, məštawtfe, mu sayfo, ġalabe mənne, yaʕni maǧ ǧəddaṯe w ma... mar rabaṯṯe, hawən, d əmmina u waxtawo hawən ṭaye žboyəd lo qəṭlənne.
contents.versio: 024. And also there were many of the Muslims here, originally, their origin still from the genocide, so to say victims of the genocide, many of them, of their grandfathers and of their elders, they converted to Islam to escape the slaughter.

contents.textus: 025. Annaqqa hani an... an naḏ... an nobġaṯṯe an navikaṯṯe, an nobġaṯṯe d əmmina, d uʕdo d kofayši, ġalabe mənne sti, kətwa hən mənne sti d əmmina məfṣoḥiwa bu medano. Ḥatta aṯi hən, d əmmina gabi, xəd d əmmat mtabrəkili yaʕni, d əmmi, d əmmi ṭawwo səmlux. D əmmi ṭawwo səmlux. Ma mə ksaymi ebux?
contents.versio: 025. So these ones, their grand, their grandchildren, their grandsons, their grandchildren, so to say, that are still in life now, many of them, some of them were happy for what happened. It went so far that some come to me and congratulated me, meaning well done. They said: well done. What can they do to you?

contents.textus: 026. Hani u šəršaṯṯe mšiḥoye ne. Kit harke ġalabe mənne. D əmmat ma qay lo kowən mšiḥoye? Lo kowən, xliṭi b ḥḏoḏe. D əmmina, kito ġalabe. Uʕdo kibux d əmmat bam mo ḥamši balki, haymen, u ḥa d mšaylat mene, u šəršayḏe mšiḥoyo yo. Yaʕni mu waxt du sayfo, yaʕni d lo məqtoli qana.
contents.versio: 026. And these are Christians by origin. There are many of them here. You may ask, why don’t they convert back to Christianity? They just cannot. They are mixed with each other. But there are lots of them. One can now say that maybe up to fifty per cent of, believe me, should you ask them, their origin is Christian. But they wanted to escape the slaughter during the genocide.

contents.textus: 027. W ġalabe komaḥkəlli masal, kibi d obenux ṣbuṯo ʕal hawxa, d omannux mede ʕal hawxa sti. Naqqa aṯi ḥa gabi. D əmmina, kəpwayle qaḏar əšti əšne wa hiye. Aṯi məllelli: ḥoli hattat.
contents.versio: 027. Many of them take me as an example. Let me give an example concerning this. I will tell you something in this matter also. Once came a man to me. He was about a sixty year-old. He came and said to me: you are my uncle.

contents.textus: 028. Omanno: məš šəkəl kowe? Omər: ḥoli hat. Aydarbo? Omər: emi mənxu yo. E, məš šəkəl? Omər, omər naqqa səmme d əmmina, i naqqayo əmmiwayla qafle, yaʕni saymiwanne qaflat an noše, yaʕni gərobaṭ, fahimat? Kofəhmat?
contents.versio: 028. I asked: how is that possible? He said: you are my uncle. But how? He answered: my mother is one of you. But how? He answered, he said: once they organized a caravan, at that time it was named caravan, which means a gathering of people, groups, do you get it? Do you understand?

contents.textus: 029. Omər: saymiwanne gərobaṭ w məbliwayne qəṭliwayne w duʕriwa. D əmmina, omər: emi ste naqqa mballe qafle; hano u ṭayo komaḥkeli, komər: emi baynoṯayye wa. Emi mənxu wa. Baynoṯayye wa. Hiya sti ḥḏo manək d mitawbəlowa lu qaṭlo wa. Məblənne omər: kətwa, kətwa ḥḏo pire baynoṯayye bat... ṭʕənto balki tmənyo yarḥe.
contents.versio: 029. They organized them in groups and took them away, slaughtered them and came back. So he said: also my mother, once they took a caravan; this Muslim man is telling me, my mother was in this caravan. She was one of you. She was in this caravan. She also was one of those who were taken to be slaughtered. They took them, he continued, and there was a woman amongst them that was pregnant, in her 8th month, maybe.

contents.textus: 030. Omər: a tranək d məblənne səmme mqarrasiyye, mǧadala hawxa ʕam ḥḏoḏe. Ḥa mərle: naʕimo yo w ḥa mərle: kaččəke yo, barṯo yo, ḥa mərle: abro yo. Hawxa səmme mqarrasi hul d l ayko, mi ḥarayto mədle i xanǧar čərre gawa, di... di pire, di pire mofaqle u naʕimo omər mərle: ḥzay be naʕimo yo kaččəke yo, yaʕni?
contents.versio: 030. He went on: the two soldiers that were guarding them started to argue, quarrel with each other. One of them said: it is a boy and the other one said: it is a girl, a daughter and one said: a son. Thus they quarreled a lot and at the end one of them seized a dagger and opened her belly, the, the woman’s belly, the woman’s belly and föok out the baby (foetus) and said: look here! Is it a boy or a girl?

contents.textus: 031. Yaʕni hawxa hul i daraǧayo aṭ ṭaye tarke komaḥkən. Yaʕni hano medano maḥkeleli u medano, u ṭayo, w xut tanṯe ġalabe masayəl koṯən yaʕni gməǧġoli aʕmi. Kit hani d kənne hawxa bu šəklano d əmmina ġalabe gruḥmilan. Kəmmi: hatu ṭawwe hatu; ṭaw minan hatu. Hənnək kəmmi yaʕni.
contents.versio: 031. So imagine, the Muslims here relate these kinds of horrifying stories. So this story was told to me by a Muslim and they also come to me and tell many other similar stories. There are also these kinds of people here, people that like us a lot. They say: you are good people. You are better than us. They utter such words.

contents.textus: 032. W bu šəklano kito ġalabe mənne d kənne, d əmmina xəd məlli bu šəršo mšiḥoye w u hawxa. W d əmmina kətwa ḥa sti i naqqa, i naqqa d nafəqno waxt, i naqqa d hawyo i masale, elo hənnək sti, d əmmina hənnək w hani a hno lə koṯən l ḥḏoḏe, i quṭnuṯo d Turkiya, lə koṯən. Lanne basime.
contents.versio: 032. And thus, there are many of them that are, as I said, Christians by origin and, yes. And moreover, there was another one, when, when I was released, when this issue arose, and not only them, but also, what are they called, they disagree with each other, the leaders in Turkey, they do not agree with each other. The relations between them are not good.

contents.textus: 033. Annaqqa hani d kənne minan, naqqa nafəqno, masal aṯi ḥa bu tarʕo aṯi nšəqle bayne ʕayni, hawxa msawyo. Ḥa zlam hawxa rabo wa bu ʕumro. Kibe šawʕi əšne taqriban yaʕni. Aṯi nšəqle bayne ʕayni omər: at tarte ʕayne hat. Omər: ṭawwo səmlux, yaʕni hawxa huleli moral.
contents.versio: 033. So these who belong to us, once I was on my way out, for instance, one of them came through the door and kissed my forehead, just like that; he was an elderly man. He was approximately seventy years old. He came forth and kissed my forehead and said: I am proud of you. He continued: you did the right thing, as if he was encouraging me.

contents.textus: 034. Omər: ṭawwo səmlux. Omər: mə ksaymi? Omər: ṭro oṯən mšayli mini, ono sti gdomanno d hawi sayfo w aḥna, w aḥna ab... ar rabayḏan, aq qamoyayḏan mšiḥoye wayne. Hul d hawo, hul u ṭayo hawxa d mərleli, w ġalabe. W heš kul d kḥozeli, kḥozeno naqqat, heš d kmaḥwe ʕalaqa basəmto ġalabe aʕmi, esore basime.
contents.versio: 034. He said: you did the right thing. He went on: what can they do to you? Let them come and ask me, I too will say that there had been a genocide, and we, and we, our forefath.., our ancestors, our forefathers were Christians. Even he, the Muslim man told me so, and many others. And every single time he sees me, I notice that he still shows good feelings towards me, good contact.

contents.textus: 035. Kito bu šəklano sti w kətwa hawxa sti. Annaqqa uʕdo i aġlab, bam mo, bam mo yaʕni təšʕi, kibux d əmmat, tmoni təšʕi mbadli d əmmina. Hənnək mbadli ʕam ḥḏoḏe w mbadli yaʕni aʕmayna, ʕam a mšiḥoye sti.
contents.versio: 035. So there are people of this kind, on the one hand, and there are also people that are the opposite, on the other. So now, the majority, one can say ninety percent, percent, or one may say eighty percent, ninety have changed. They have changed both between each other and towards us, towards the Christians also.

contents.textus: 036. Fayəš ab baladiyat d əmmina eli kətli esore aʕmayye. W ḥatta ono sti bi baladiye kito, kito kəmminale maǧlis dann arbʕi suhḏe ono sti bu maǧlisawo no. Yaʕni kmaydi i fəkrayḏi sti, i baladiye hul uʕdo. Uʕdo aṯilan baladiye ḥaṯo garak ʕayni hawxa d... d mhalxi bu šəklano.
contents.versio: 036. Nowadays, also in the municipalities I have contacts with them. And I furthermore, there is, there is, what we call council of the forty witnesses, I too am a member in that council. This means that the municipality takes my ideas into consideration, still until now. We have now a new council at the municipality but hopefully they will go on, continue the same way.

contents.textus: 037. Məd kowe medone kəmšawri eban, masala saymina hawxa ṭawwo yo saymina, ḥatta maqəmlan qoyəmto harke, yaʕni ʕal aʕ ʕame d ḏ̣limi harke, harke bi baladiye, ʕam ḥḏoḏe. ʕAl aʕ ʕame d ḏ̣limi, yaʕni d ḥzalle ʕasquṯo ġalabe harke. Lo kəmmi ftiḥo ʕal u sayfo.
contents.versio: 037. Whatever happens they consult us, for instance, is it better to act this way or is it better to, we have even raised a stele here, for the suppressed people here, the municipality here, together. It is for the sake of the people that have been suppressed, that have gone through lots of difficulties here. But it is not mentioned openly that it is for the genocide.

contents.textus: 038. Hənnək lo kəmmi hawxa. Bas kəmmi: ʕal aʕ ʕame d ḏ̣limi. Kṯuwe aʕla bu səryoyo, bu tərki, bu armnoyo, bu kərdi w bu... w b lešone hawxa kṯuwe ʕal i qoyəmtayo. W hul i daraǧayo yaʕni hawxa mḥalfi.
contents.versio: 038. Thus they do not say it openly. They only say: it is for the people that have been suppressed. It is written on it in Syriac, in Turkish, in Armenian, in Kurdish and in the languages such, it is written on the stele. Thus, so many things have changed.

contents.textus: 039. Aḥna, ono kətli d əmmina esore ġalabe ṭawwe aʕmayye. Halbat lo ba... bam mo mo mḥalfi, bam mo kibux d əmmat tmoni, d mḥaləf u ʕamo tarke. W w kətlan esore ṭawwe aʕmayye w xud hawxa masayəl d əmmina. Aḥna, aḥna, aḥna u ʕamo tarke, ḏiḏan as səryoye d əmmina heš, yaʕni heš hawxa hne ne ġalabe latte haž lo m... kito mənne mənne latte haž lo d hawi sayfo w lo lo.
contents.versio: 039. We, let us say I, have a very good relationship with them. But of course, they did not change one, one hundred percent. One may say that the people here have changed up to eighty percent. And, and we have good contact with them and so on. Bu we, we the people that are living here, our people, the Syriac people, they are still, they are still not aware of, some of them are not aware whether there has been a genocide or not.

contents.textus: 040. W latte, w lo kəbʕi maqəbli, kito hawxa šəklat sti baynoṯayna sti. Yaʕni aḥna glozam u ʕamo suryoyo kulan howina ʕayni bu fəkrano d... aḥna d hawi sayfo aʕlayna. Aḥna i naqqa d qṭilina lo hən minan qṭil w ṭralle hən. Əbʕi d quṭli kulle, u ʕamayḏan kule.
contents.versio: 040. And they do not have, they do not accept, yes, there are some that have these ideas also. We have to, I mean the Syriac people, all of us, have to have the same approach, that we were victims of the genocide. When we were slaughtered, they did not slaughter some of us and spare some of us. The aim was to kill everyone, every single one of our people.

contents.textus: 041. ʕAl hawxa kulan glozəm d howina bu... bu fəkrano ḥiṣe ʕam ḥḏoḏe, mḥayḏe ʕam ḥḏoḏe. W i ṣbuṯaṯe yaʕni xəd ḥzelux bi ṣbuṯayo diḏi, du sayfo d šmiʕo ġalabe, šmiʕo wa. Lazəm kul ḥa minan d mǧahəd yaʕni bu šəklano. D əmmət hawi, d hawi u medano aʕlayna, aḥna qṭilina. Liʔən... čunku i dukṯayḏan kula fayišo harke.
contents.versio: 041. That is why we all should be together, strong in this, in this approach, united together. And this matter, as you already have seen, through my dispute about the genocide, and that had created a great echo, that was heard, every single one of us should work hard the same way. I riiean that this has occurred, that this has happened to us, that we have been ethnically cleansed. Because our place of origin is here.

contents.textus: 042. D əmmina u ʕamayḏan d kətwaylan, aḥna kətlan makṯab zabno harke ʕatiqo. Kətlan d əmmina ʕamo ʕatiqo. Kətla kultur ʕatiqo. Kətlan lešono ʕatiqo, aʕtaq mene d layto harke bi dukṯaṯe. Əšma di dukṯaṯe sti aḥna, elan hulan yaʕni. Haṯe iḏəʕto yo yaʕni, əšma di ǧoġraf... di ǧoġrafiyaṯe kula, d əmmina d Beṯ Nahrin, w d gawa kule.
contents.versio: 042. Our people, that we had here, we had an old history here. We have ancient roots here. We have ancient culture here. We have an old language here, so old that there is no older language than it in this region. It is we who gave name to this region. This is fact, it’s geographical, the whole geographical term is Mesopotamia, and also what’s inside of it.

contents.textus: 043. Aḥna maḥətlan aʔ ʔəšmonani, hani. W iḏiʕo yo, i naqqa d əmmət əšma di dukṯo b səryoyo yo, bu... bu lešonayḏan yo. ʕAl hawxa aḥna, aḥna lazəm bu šəklano mətfakrina, bu šəklano ḥayṣina ḥḏoḏe, bu šəklano miḥayḏina, w b hawxa.
contents.versio: 043. It is we who gave these names. And this is evident, when you say the name of the region in Syriac, in, in, it is in our mother tongue. That’s why we, we have to think in this way, give each other strength in this matter, get united in this struggle and so on.

contents.textus: 044. W aḥna, aḥna, yaʕni haṯe bam mo mo yo. Layto, layto abadan hno eba d... d hawi sayfo aʕlayna. W ḥatta naqqa hawiwa harke, uʕdo mə d kowe zatan ono kəḏʕili d əmmina xd a sniġre xəttayna d kənne noše hne heš, ayna d ḥozəlli kəḏʕili kəmmi, i naqla d kowe masayəl d kəbʕina d əmmina, d... d kəbʕi məǧġanno aʕmayye bat talafəzyone aw b medone. Kuḏʕi. Komannanne.
contents.versio: 044. And for us this is something that is one hundred percent indisputable. There is no, there is no, not at all, that, that we were hot victims of the genocide. And even once it occurred here, actually, whatever happens now, since they know me, for instance, the lawyers, such as people that are, what is called, whoever meets me knows me, they say, when something particular arises, they want me to talk with them on television or something similar. They know. I talk to them.

contents.textus: 045. Kuḏʕi yaʕni i naqqa d kuḏʕi ono d mərwayli, yaʕni xəd hawino xəd d əmmat sambol d hawxa du sayfo. Naqqawat kəmmi, komanno: yawo kul gave lo qudrina, ḥa, ḥa ku..., kuhne harke b... mu ʕamayḏan gzoyəʕ, lo mi dawla. Annaqqa ṭray mu ʕamayḏan ḥa kozoyəʕ.
contents.versio: 045. They know, when they know what I have said, I mean I have become a symbol of this, the genocide. Sometimes they say, I say: God, one cannot every now and then, I, I, what is it called, am afraid of our own people and not of the state. So imagine, I am afraid of our own people.

contents.textus: 046. Ono d lo disa gdomanno. Yaʕni disa kibi məǧġanno, samno raportaže disa. Annaqqa mawxa kuḏʕili. Xəd hawino d əmmat sambol du sayfo yaʕni. Kulle kuḏ... iḏiʕo yo yaʕni lu ʕamayḏan sti w l ayna d... laq qaroyo, d əmmina laq qaroye, la sniġre, la... la... lan nahire du ʕamo, tarke sti w diḏan sti.
contents.versio: 046. If not, I am capable of saying it again. I mean I can speak of it again, give exposure again. So that’s why they know me. You may say that I have become like a symbol of the genocide. Everyone knows, it is known both for our people and for whoever, for the educated, so to speak, for the educated, for the lawyers, for the, for the, for the enlightened ones between the people, both Turks and our people.

contents.textus: 047. Hawxa, w towelux šuwole mede? Yaʕni b šrolo məqqa d omanno yaʕni gdəmmat balki kəhne ruḥe, hano yaʕni šəbhoro yo lo eli w bas; kuḏʕat ono mərralli əmmi: dʕar eba! Dʕar eba! Yaʕni u ʕamo tarke, diḏan, dʕar eba, gquṭlilux, čaykilux bu ḥapəs.
contents.versio: 047. So, do you have any questions? Honestly, no matter how much I tell you, you would maybe think: he is patting himself on the back, but this is a great deal, not only for me; you know, they told me: withdraw your statement! Take it back! I mean the people here, our people, take it back or they will kill you, they will throw you in prison.

contents.textus: 048. Omanno: lanno lo ṭaw mani d qṭili ʕal hawxa, lanno ṭaw me ḥa mənne. W ġalabe maḥətte b... qṭilənne w ba ḥbušye w ba hne. Ono sti ṭroweno tabaʕ tanək omanno. Yaʕni hawxa məftakalli. W bəṯərke mede šrolo wa.
contents.versio: 048. I answered: I am not in any way better than those who have been slaughtered so, I am not better than a single one of them. And they have put many in, they have killed them in prisons and in, what is it called? I said: let me also be one of those. I was thinking in this way. And furthermore, it was true.

contents.textus: 049. I naqqa d duʕrat b mede hano ebe makṯab zabno yo, yaʕni b qḏoli kfoyašwa, eli mede lo ṭawwo laǧani. Bəṯər kfoyašwa mede lo ṭawwo eli. Bas uʕdo d əmmina məlli, xəd məlli bu šawṭo, hawi ṭawwo eli, lu ʕamayḏan qamayto. Eli, ma ono xlo məllux ono, yaʕni lu ʕamo, lu sayfo hawi mede hno ṭawwo d əmmina.
contents.versio: 049. When someone withdraws a historical statement such as this, I mean it will forever remain my own responsibility and this I consider as something immoral for my own sake. It would have been something immoral for my own person. But now, what I have stated, as I mentioned earlier, it turned out much better for me, but above all for our people. Concerning me, I am just a simple person, but for the people, for the genocide it turned out to be something positive.

contents.textus: 050. D əmmina kibe waxt d oṯe d howe mede kibe d əmmi ma qay ḥa šab... b flan zabno, flan qašo, qašo Yusef mərle: hawi sayfo w kale ha.. lawi mede. Ḥa annaqqa koməftəḥ u tarʕo hedi xəd d əmmat.
contents.versio: 050. Imagine that it might come time and for some reason, someone would say: at a certain time, this or that person, that priest, priest Yusef stated that the genocide really occurred and behold, nothing happened to him. See, in this way the path for the truth opens little by little, as one may say.

contents.textus: 051. W ġalabe daʕwat, d əmmina bi daʕwaṯe d xaləṣno mina, harke b Turkiya, ġalabe daʕwat hawyo d əmmina zbəṭla d əmmina bahro, l daʕwat heš, yaʕni maḥkamat heš d ʕame heš, d noše heš yaʕni. Masala kəppe d əmmi qay, ma b flan daʕwa kale ḥkim bam maḥkamat.
contents.versio: 051. And there are many other lawsuits, for instance as this one and from which I have been saved, here in Turkey, and which drew interest, many other lawsuits, lawsuits are still at court, also about peoples, and individuals. They may for example say: but behold, in this certain lawsuit he had been in a court hearing.

contents.textus: 052. Ann avoqate kəppe d əmmi ḥkim flankas, flan qašo lo čəkke bu ḥapəs, masala. Haṯe d əmmat ṭəfṣo örnak yaʕni, kuyo yaʕni l ġalabe medone, gzubṭo bahro l medone heš, l daʕwat heš.
contents.versio: 052. The lawyers can for example say: a certain individual was heard in the court, a certain priest, but was not put in jail. This can be as an example, an example for many other issues; it sheds light on other issues, other cases.

contents.textus: 053. Yaʕni mərralli: dʕar! Məqqa d mərre sti ono lo maḥətli b hawni d doʕanno. Yaʕni ono bi maḥkama mətyaqan məftakarli omanno: haqqa aḥna, ono bi qriṯayḏi d əmmina tre yarḥe kamile mḥarabe b ʕIwardo.
contents.versio: 053. So they said to me: take back your statement! But not matter how much they asked me I did not even consider withdrawing my statement. Believe me, while I stood in the court, I thought for myself, how much we, just in my village, Iwardo, for example there three months of fighting.

contents.textus: 054. Yaʕni heš kofayši ag garme, ag garme d kofayši, kalən ba dkoṯanək. Heš kalən ab buġre du silaḥ bi ʕito, b Mar Ḥušabo, i ʕitayḏan. Heš hul l uʕdo kfayši. W i emo w bəṯərke ono, ono naʕimo i emo d babi ḥzewayla u sayfo. Naqqawat kmaḥwəlla bu talafəzyon sti. Maḥənwayla naqqawat.
contents.versio: 054. And there are still bones, the bones are still there, spread in those places. The bullets from the weapons are still in the church, in the church of St. Hushabo, our church. It is there until this day. And the mother of, and furthermore, I, when I was still little, the mother of my father had experienced the genocide. She is also shown on television sometimes. She was shown on television.

contents.textus: 055. Hiya ṭəʕnowa buġre, d əmmina mʕawnowa. Hiya ḥzela u sayfo kul gave maḥkyowaylan d əmmina. Maḥkyowa. W qrelan sti, lo hiya d maḥkyo, qrelan ba kṯowe w qrelan ma u waxtano. Bas hiya maḥkelalan ġalabe, aḥna naʕime. Heš čučkat koṯe l bolan d əmmina.
contents.versio: 055. She was distributing bullets, I mean she was helping. She survived the genocide and she used to tell us. She used to tell us. And not only what she told, but we also read, we read in the books and we read about that time. But she used to tell us while we were little. We remember that from the time we still were very little.

contents.textus: 056. Uʕdo mḥasyo halbat d... hani kibe šeṯ, šwaʕ əšne. W hiya maḥkyowaylan am medona d howənwa. W d əmmina ġalabe harke uʕdo, xəd məlli ġalabe kito harke ṣəbwoṯo, kšəmʕina maṭ ṭaye. Hənnək kəmmi, yaʕni hənnək.
contents.versio: 056. But now she has, of course, passed away, six, seven years ago. She used to tell us about the barbarism then. And as I mentioned many here now, there are many issues here, we hear about it from the Muslims. They tell us, they themselves.

contents.textus: 057. Aḥna kyətwina naqqawat ʕam i baladiye, di baladiye, u rayəs di baladiye, naqqa, lo məllilux koweno ono bu maǧlis ono sti, kyətwina mə d kowe ǧġaliyat hawxa, hiye komər: ono kṭolabno šəbqono mas səryoye.
contents.versio: 057. We gather from time to time at the municipality, at the municipality, the head of the municipality, so once, I told you that I too am a member in the council, we gather and when these kinds of issues are spoken of, he says: I ask the forgiveness of the Syriac people.

contents.textus: 058. Komər, komər: kṭolabno šəbqono mas səryoye d aḥna səmlan hawxa appe, səmme ab babonayḏan d əbʕiwa d quṭli as səryoye d əzzənne mi dukṯaṯe. W omər: as səryoye, hiye komar, as səryoye ġalabe ʕamo d əmmina b qalita wa. Ġalabe d əmmina b ṣənʕa yo.
contents.versio: 058. He says, he says: I ask the forgiveness of the Syriac people for what we have done to them, what our forefathers did, that they wanted to slaughter the Syriac people so they would vanish from this region. And he continued: the Syriac people, he is telling, the Syriac people were of high quality. They are, for example, very dexterous.

contents.textus: 059. Hawxa kmaḥke ǧare. Hiye komallan kul gave ... kurd ne. Hano kurd ne. Hani tarke kurmanǧ ne. W at tərk sti kəmmi: u ʕamo səryoyo, d əmmina, ʕamo d maḥətle, d markawle mdinoyuṯo u ʕamo ʕatiqo u ʕamo d kətle lišono ʕatiqo w d kətle makṯab zabno ʕatiqo, ak kurd sti w at tərk sti. Ma hano mede šrolo yo.
contents.versio: 059. Thus he tells. He tells us every now and then .., they are Kurds. This one here is Kurd. These here are Kurmanj. And alsp the Turks say that the Syriac people are the people who laid the fundament of civilization. It is the oldest people with the oldest language and that have ancient history. Both the Kurds and the Turks say such. Thus it is true.

contents.textus: 060. W hani d kul gave d əmmina d kənno aʕmayye d əmmina koṭəlbi kul gave, u reyəs yo, d laltaḥtər mine yo, w naqqawat a ḥrene sti, ar rabonaṯṯe kəmmi: ṭəl... aḥna kṭəlbina šəbqono mas səryoye ʕal d hawi mam masalatani d qṭililan.
contents.versio: 060. So every now and then, since I am with them, they ask every now and then, no matter if it is the chief or if it is his deputy, and sometimes also others from the elderly, say sor.., we ask the Syriac people for forgiveness for what happened, that we have slaughtered them.

contents.textus: 061. Xəd məllilux bu šawṭo maqəmlan qoyəmto yaʕni harke, b Dyarbakər. E yaʕni hul li daraǧayo aḥna kətlan uʕdo hne aʕmayye. Halbat kito d əmmina kito šəklat sti, bam mo ʕaṣro, ʕəri d lanne, kḥayri b ʕayno ḥreto. An noše kulle lappe yaʕni lə kowe d howən ṭawwe zaṭan.
contents.versio: 061. As I mentioned earlier, we have raised a stele here in Diyarbakir. So this means that our cooperation with them is that good now. But of course, there are different kinds of people also, about ten, twenty percent of them are not, they see us with different eyes. All people cannot, as a matter of fact, be good.

contents.textus: 062. E, hawxa. Kətwaylan aḥna noqušo. Lo meqəm tlaṯ əšne hawi məqq... ʕal, b Swičra hawiwa hno, b Swičra hawiwa ʕal a... ʕal a... ʕal am minarat da ǧweməʕ, lo maqblənne, rafarandəm səmwalle lo maqblənne b Swičra.
contents.versio: 062. Yes, so. We used to have a steeple. Was it not three years ago that a referendum, about, in Switzerland, there was, what is it called, in Switzerland there was about, about, about the mosque’s minarets, they did not accept them, they had a referendum and it was not accepted in Switzerland.

contents.textus: 063. Yaʕni mšayəlle mu ʕamo lo maqblənne. Annaqqa e, bay yawmanək wa aṯiwa tre, aṯiwa tloṯo, tloṯo dirak lu bayto, aḥna lawġul yat... e annaqla aḥna yatiwayna lawġul b šrolo šotiwayna qaḥwa. Ḥəlli, aṯi tloṯo mḥalle lu tarʕo.
contents.versio: 063. They asked the people and they did not accept them. So it was at that time when two men came, three men, three came directly home while we were sitting inside, so we were actually sitting inside having coffee. I heard that three men came and knocked on the door,

contents.textus: 064. Man yo u qašo tarke? Omanno: ono no. Mar mək kəbʕat, mək kəbʕutu? Omər, omər: kətxu noqušo harke? Omanno: e. Omər: hawo gdoratle! ʕAyn hawxa! Ono, ono hawino šaš hawxa mine yaʕni. Omanno: hano qay komər hawxa?
contents.versio: 064. Who is the vicar here? I answered: it is me. State your purpose, what do you want? He said, he said: do you have steeple here? I answered: yes. He said: you will tear it down! Just like that! I, I was confused because of that. I wondered why he is saying this.

contents.textus: 065. Omanno: qay? Omər: gdoratle! E, omanno: qay? ʕAl mən? Omər: b Swičra qay lo maqballe a... aǧ ǧwe... am manurat da ǧweməʕayḏan, qay lo maqblənne? Aḥna sti lə gmaqəblina. Gdoratle!
contents.versio: 065. I asked: why? He said: you will tear it down! I answered: but why? What is the reason? He answered: because in Switzerland, why did not they accept our mosque’s minarets, why did not they accept them? We do not accept it either. You will tear it down!

contents.textus: 066. Omanno: ma qay aḥna me Swičra aṯina? Omanno: aḥna ʕatiqe darke na yaʕni; ʕamo ʕatiqo; dukṯo ʕatəqto. Ma kibi dorene? Yaʕni laybi dorena. g... g... i dawla lə kmaqəblo! omər, omər: gdoratla! yawme d ʕrufto wa u yawmo d aṯən.
contents.versio: 066. I answered: but do you think that we come from Switzerland? I continued: we belong to this region since ancient times; we are ancient people; this is an ancient region; and this is an ancient church. Do you think that I can just tear it down? I cannot tear it down. It will, it will, the state will not allow that! He said, he said: you will tear it down! It was a Friday, the day when they came to me.

contents.textus: 067. Omər: elux muhla hul yawme d ʕrufto. Hat d lo doratla gḥozat omər. Yaʕni hawxa mərleli, mhadadleli! Bəṯər ono qreli lu polis. U polis ste azzeyo mḥay... mḥayṣele a tloṯo.
contents.versio: 067. He continued: you have until Friday to do so! And if you do not tear it down, you will see. Thus he said to me, he threatened me, so to say! After that I called upon the police. The Police left and caught, caught the three of them. Then, as a matter of fact, I, I had called upon, the police caught the three of them, but before the police had caught them, their families said, sent me a message.

contents.textus: 068. Əmmi: glozam dəʕrat xayifo bi daʕwayḏux ,d lo hat, disa mhadaddalli, hat gḥozat yaʕni! Dʕar eba xayifo! Əmmi, əmmi: d mičoki bu ḥapəs hat kuḏʕat! Hawxa yaʕni disa tah... hedodo.
contents.versio: 068. They said: you should immediately withdraw your claim, otherwise; they threatened me once again, otherwise you will see! Take it back at once! They said, they said: if they are to be put in prison you will see what will happen to you! So once again in such way they threa.., threatening.

contents.textus: 069. Edi ono, edi dəm... i naqla d azzi li maḥkama, azzi li maḥkama mšayele mini omər: hani mhadallalux? Yaʕni obəʕ d noḥəl ax xabre, yaʕni d be mərralli, xabre d qaṭlo mede nafəq me femayye lo. Hiye d omarre. Omanno: lo, bas mərralli: gdoratla. Qay b Swičra lə maqballe? Bi maḥkama.
contents.versio: 069. So I, so, when I was in court, when in court, I was asked: did these people threaten you? They wanted to hear extract the exact words, what they said to me, in case words of killing or so came out of their mouths or not. He wanted to tell them so. But I said: no, they just told me to tear it down. Why was this not accepted in Switzerland? This was in court.

contents.textus: 070. Qay lo maqballe i... a... am manurat da ǧweməʕ hat ste gdorat haṯe. Gdoratla! D əbʕat zux, zux maški d əbʕat l Awroppa, d əbʕat l Turkiya, d əbʕat lə gḏaʕno l ayko. Gdoratla! Yaʕni hul yawme... hul yawme d ʕrufto huwwalli muhla. Me yawme d ʕrufto hul yawme d ʕrufto.
contents.versio: 070. Because they did not accept the, the, the mosque’s minarets, you too will tear down this one. You will tear it down! And if you would like go, go and complain, and also to Europe, if you would like, and if you would like to Turkey, and if you would like, I don’t know where to. You will tear it down. So you have until Fri.., you have until Friday to do so. This means, from Friday to Friday.

contents.textus: 071. E, məlli lu ḥakəm, omanno, omanno: aḥna, omanno: lo yaʕni lanne, yaʕni lo kəmdaʕeno aʕlayye ʕal mede. Omər: qay? Omanno: hani yaʕni hawxa lə kšəbhi noše, hawxa ksaymi mede hawxa. Qay noše, noše azze li ǧamye, mḥarkənne ʕal hawxa mede.
contents.versio: 071. So I said to the judge, I said, I said: we, I said: no, they are not, I mean do not charge them for anything. He asked: why? I answered: well, these, they do not look like people that would commit such actions. Obviously some people, some people have been to the mosque and stirred them up to do so.

contents.textus: 072. Edi mšayele mənne. Ḥa omər: ono sti haw ... ono šteli, w ḥa omər: ono lə gḏaʕno ono mərralli bi ǧamye hawxa, w ḥa omər lə gḏaʕno mən. Edi lo ḥkimənne. Məd nafiqina aṯən ṭləbbe šəbqono mini, yaʕni xəd d əmmat, hanək, a tloṯanək.
contents.versio: 072. So he asked them. One of them said: I would never, I was drunk, and the second said: I do not know, while in the mosque they told me to do so, and the third one said I do not know what. So they were sentenced. When we came out of the court, they came forward and asked my forgiveness, so to say, those, those three men.

contents.textus: 073. Xəd səmli ṭawwuṯo aʕmayye, yaʕni xəd d əmmat fayiši mnakfe. Ṭləbbe šəbqono mini. Omanno: hatu aṯitu mhadad... əmmi: šəbqono latwaylan ḥaq aʕlux. Hawxa yaʕni masale, ṣbuṯo hawxa hawiwo aʕmi, e.
contents.versio: 073. Because I have done them a favor, they were ashamed, so to say. They asked my forgiveness. I said to them: you came and threatened me, what, what, what right did you have to come and threaten me? They answered: we are sorry; we did not have any right to do so to you. So, this was an example of an incident that affected me, yes.

contents.textus: 074. Adšato hawiwo ṣbuṯo ḥreto aʕmayna. D əbʕat d omannuxyo. ʕAl, ʕal u zʕurayḏi kibe d ḥṣar əšne. D əzzewa lu maktab. Fayəš mu hno, yaʕni ṭralle bu səd... ṭralle bu ṣənəf xəd kəmmina mu... mu dino yaʕni d lo... d lo samwa u dino di hno, di ṭayuṯo, yaʕni bu maktab, d lo doraswo ʕal u... ʕal i ṭayuṯo.
contents.versio: 074. This year we suffered from another problem. If you would like I will tell you about it. It is about, about my son. He is almost ten years old. He goes to school.
