contents.textus: 13. Ad+darbe komiṣakri me qume. Hánosti, ínaqla d̥komiṣakri ... u+səsyayḏe ʕăsīlwa.
contents.versio: 13. The roads disappear from before him. Then, when they disappear ... his horse was purebred.

contents.textus: 14. Azzé lәqriṯo, dəmmina, lәškafte, mede. U+tarʕayḏa ṣxīr mu+talgo. Koməḥyo qarʕa hawxaaa, kofətḥo u+tarʕo.
contents.versio: 14. He reached a village, let’s say, a cave, something. Its door was covered (lit. ‘shut’) with snow, she sticks out her head like so, she opens the door.

contents.textus: 15. Koqaymo ṗire, kofətḥo u+tarʕo. Ŭ koḥayro, kalé zlām rawixo, qafəl. Koṣuxro u+tarʕo qume.
contents.versio: 15. A woman gets up, opens the door. And she looks, here’s a man mounted (i.e., on horseback), he froze. She shuts the door in front of him.

contents.textus: 16. Koṣuxro u+tarʕo qume. Hánosi mə‿kosoyəm? Fāš, lišono layt ŭ mede layt, qafəl, kalé ʕal u+səsyo.
contents.versio: 16. She shuts the door before him. So this one, what does he do? He stayed (still), his tongue and thing aren’t there, he froze, here he is, on the horse.

contents.textus: 17. I+žənk̇esi, mә‿kosaymo? Kuzzá komarṯḥolux maye, dəmmina, bardәš dmaye. Ŭ kuṯyo kobayzo aʕle ŭ ʕal u+səsyo, di+qašʕa mafəlto u+səsyo.
contents.versio: 17. So what does the woman do? She goes and boils water, let’s say, a pot of water. And she comes back, she pours it on him and on the horse, so the frost lets go of the horse.

contents.textus: 18. Ŭ kuzzá komaḥtole nvine lawġul, ŭ koǧuġrole i+ṣopa ŭ k̬maydole maʕl u+səsyo, k̬maḥtole bi+nvine ŭ mičoko bəṯre, xud dəmmat, kәmšaḥnole.
contents.versio: 18. And she goes, puts down bedding for him inside, and she heats the stove for him, and takes him off the horse, puts him into the bedding and sneaks behind him, like you’d say, she warms him up.

contents.textus: 19. Hul d̥šaḥəlle, aṯi ruḥo ebe, axər, harke ŭ tamhok̇é. E, u+zlām ṭábiki, mәd̥‿šaḥəlle ŭ xile ŭ štele…
contents.versio: 19. Until it got warm for him, he revived (lit. ‘the spirit came into him’), finally, here and over there (i.e., some time passed). Yes, the man naturally, after it got warm for him, and he ate and drank…

contents.textus: 20. Me wắkidisi axər rāgle. Əmmo, ‘Aḥna, i+ʕadayḏan, qum ḥuf ŭ mašə́ġ ŭ bəṯr’. Košəmʕat? Hánosi, koḥayfole, i+žənk̇e ʕăsīlwa.
contents.versio: 20. Besides that, he finally got aroused. She says, ‘As for us, our tradition, up and bathe, and wash up, and afterwards’. Do you hear? So this one, she bathes him, the woman was well-bred (lit. ‘noble’).

contents.textus: 21. I+žənk̇e ʕăsīlwa. Ánnaqla meqəm latwa banyowat xud̥‿ani. Dəmmina, máṣrafwa ŭ i+qašʕa, u+quro, u+flān, axər.
contents.versio: 21. The woman was well-bred. Now then, earlier there were no bathrooms like these. Let’s say, there was a drain and ice, the cold, so and so, finally.

contents.textus: 22. Hánosi, koqaymo ḥayfo u+zlām, kočaykole bu+tāšt. Ŭ koḥayfole, košoləḥ aǧ+ǧulayḏe. Ínaqla d̥koḥayfole, koməḥyo tafk̇e lu+tāšt.
contents.versio: 22. Then she up and bathes the man, she sticks him into the basin. And she bathes him, he strips off his clothes. When she washes him, she gives a push to the basin.

contents.textus: 23. Koxōr tav u+talgawo hul larʕa di+baste. Kuzzé larʕa di+baste.
contents.versio: 23. It flows together with that snow to the bottom of the riverbed. It goes down to the bottom of the riverbed.

contents.textus: 24. Omər, ‘Way mə‿səmli bruḥi? Qafilo, mḥel... lu+səsyo ftə́ḥleli u+ta... šxwa mḥele bu+tarʕo, ŭ qafə́lwayno, hawyoli moro’.
contents.versio: 24. He says, ‘Woe is me, what have I done to myself? Freezing, it knocked… the horse opened for me the do… anyway, it knocked on the door, and I was frozen, she took responsibility for me.

contents.textus: 25. ‘Ŭ... (AA: Ḥə́flali, hnela), húlali muklo, maḥátlali nvine, ŭ mə‿səmli bruḥi?’
contents.versio: 25. And... (AA: She bathed me, she whatsited), she gave me food, put down bedding for me, and what have I done to myself?’

contents.textus: 26. Hánosi ánnaqla zalṭono ŭ i+kaffayo bayne qarʕe. Hīs komoḥe bruḥe, kosoləq.
contents.versio: 26. So this one, now then, he is naked, and that foam is around his head. So he, he gets out (lit. ‘beats in himself’, i.e., he makes an effort) and goes up.

contents.textus: 27. Kosoləq, dəmmina, lfalga di+kaše, raġle kuzzá bu+talgo.
contents.versio: 27. He goes up, let’s say, to the middle of the slope, his leg goes into the snow.

contents.textus: 28. Koḥoyər, kalá šk̇afte mliṯo ʕwone.
contents.versio: 28. He looks, here’s a cave full of sheep.

contents.textus: 29. Ŭ kīt ḥasti tamo, dəmmina, ḥa sofi ixtiyā́r b̰mo+əšne, kalé qmaʕ+ʕwonanək.
contents.versio: 29. And there is also a certain man there, let’s say, a venerable dervish of a hundred years, there among those sheep.

contents.textus: 30. Hánosi, híyesi komičək bi+šk̇aftayo, konoḥət támova, košoḥaḷḷe bayn aʕ+ʕwonanək hul ṣafro.
contents.versio: 30. Then he also sneaks into that cave, goes down there, he warms up among those sheep until morning.

contents.textus: 31. B̥ṣafro komaḷḷe lu+sofi, koḥozən ḥḏoḏe ṭábiki bi+šk̇afte, konohar aʕlayye. Komər, ‘Ḥāl ŭ i+masalayḏi haṯe b̥áṯeyo’.
contents.versio: 31. In the morning, he tells the old man, they see each other naturally in the cave, dawn breaks upon them. He says, ‘This is what has happened to me’ (lit. ‘my condition and problem is this one in this one’).

contents.textus: 32. Omar, ‘Mḥay bəṯri!’ Mḥele bəṯre ŭ azzənne. U+sofiyano, dəmmina, u+ixtiyarano kuzzé, kuzzé ŭ kuzzé, komoḥe ʕal u+tarʕo di+barṯo druḥe. Nafiqo i+barṯo du+sofi.
contents.versio: 32. He says, ‘Follow me!’ (lit. ‘strike after me!’). He followed him (lit. ‘struck after him’) and they went off. This old man, let’s say, this venerable one, he goes, goes, and goes, he knocks on his own daughter’s door. She turned out to be the old man’s daughter.

contents.textus: 33. Hánosi koʕubri. Maḥatla ʕayno aʕle, zbəṭla mŭkū́s̬‿diḏa mine. Zbəṭla mŭkū́s̬‿diḏa mine, mə́ḷḷela omər, ‘Kuḏʕat?’ Omər, ‘Mənyo?’
contents.versio: 33. Then they enter. She saw him (lit. ‘she set an eye on him’), she averted her gaze from him (lit. ‘she snatched her facial expression from him’). She averted her gaze from him. He told her, he says, ‘You know what?’ She says, ‘What is it?’

contents.textus: 34. Omər, ‘D̥hat zəbṭat u+mŭkusayḏax’, omər, ‘uʕdo g̊ˠqoṭaṇṇax’. Omər, ‘U+dayfàyḏanyo, ŭ lazəm howatle ġắlăbe moro’.
contents.versio: 34. He says, ‘If you avert your gaze from him’, he says, ‘I’ll kill you on the spot (lit. ‘now’)’. He says, ‘He’s our guest, and it’s very necessary for you to be his host’.

contents.textus: 35. Ŭ bəṯr qrele hak̇a qášowa, hak̇a malla, be mənwa, qrélele. Ŭ háyosti mbarxole aʕle, húlele i+barṯo druḥe.
contents.versio: 35. And then he called either a priest or a mullah, whatever it was, he called him. And that girl, he married her off to him, he gave him his own daughter.

contents.textus: 36. Ŭ me tamo hawən aṯto ŭ gawro tamo.
contents.versio: 36. And from that moment, they became husband and wife there.

contents.textus: 37. Ánnaqla hano Xaláf Aġawa, daʕәr. Dəmmina, me tamo azzənne lak̇+k̇owan daʕ+ʕarab, xud mə́ḷḷilux.
contents.versio: 37. Now then, this was Halaf Agha, he went back. Let’s say, from there they went to the tents of the Arabs, like I told you.

contents.textus: 38. Támosi ánnaqla, d̥kə́twayle aṯto ḥreto tamo bări, ŭ háyosti... ŭ daʕәr, azzənne, azzənne me tamo.
contents.versio: 38. There as well, now then, since he had another wife before, and that one too… and he returned, and they went away, they went away from there.

contents.textus: 39. Xaláf Aġá azzé, yatu bayne baxča. Ġắlăbe basímowa, u+qayso, taḥta, taḥt u+qayso di+baxčayo.
contents.versio: 39. Halaf Agha went, sat in a garden. It was very pleasant, the tree, under it, under the tree of that garden.

contents.textus: 40. Fāš tamo mədde. Omər, ḥəḷḷe, omər, ḥəḷḷe taḥt u+qaysawo, more di+baxčayo aṯi ltamo. Ŭ i+itawto dmora di+baxčayo, dlo taḥt ... i+qa+baxčayo, lo+yotawwa dlowewa taḥt u+qaysawo.
contents.versio: 40. He stayed there for a stretch. He says, he looked, he says, he looked under that tree, that garden’s owner came there. And the seat of that garden’s owner, if it weren’t under ... the whole of that garden, he wouldn’t sit (anywhere) unless it were under that tree.

contents.textus: 41. Hánosi maz+zuḥṯe, ínaqla d̥komaḥat ʕayno Xaláf Aġá ʕal u+zlām, kosoləq ʕal qarʕe du+qayso.
contents.versio: 41. So this one out of fear, when Halaf Agha sets eyes (lit. ‘an eye’) on the man, he climbs up to the top of the tree.

contents.textus: 42. Kosoləq ʕal qarʕe du+qayso ŭ háwose kuzzé koyotu taḥt u+qayso. Ínaqla dobaʕ̥ doməx, koḥṓr, ʕal u+qayso, kalé šaqṣ.
contents.versio: 42. He climbs up to the tree top, and that one goes to sit under the tree. When he wants to sleep, he looks, on top of the tree, there’s a man .

contents.textus: 43. Kalé šaqṣ. E, ba u+šaqṣano mə‿šəklyo? Omər, ‘Nḥat!’ Manḥatle.
contents.versio: 43. There’s a man. Yes, what sort is this man? He says, ‘Get down!’ He made him come down.

contents.textus: 44. Ŭ, ani, mbele, mofaqle mi+baxča, maḥatle bdarbo, ŭ ḥfəḷḷe, ḥfəḷḷe.
contents.versio: 44. And, like, he took him, expelled him from the garden, put him on the road, and he dug, he dug.

contents.textus: 45. Ŭ maḥatle, maḥatle u+zlām bi+hno... bgurto. Ṭməḷḷe u+zlām, fāš qarʕe du+zlām tăne.
contents.versio: 45. And he put him, he put the man in the whatsit, in a pit. He buried the man, only the man’s head stayed out.

contents.textus: 46. Fāš qarʕe du+zlām tăne. Kətle ṭažiye lmora di+baxča. Kətle ṭažiye lmora di+baxča.
contents.versio: 46. Only the man’s head stayed out. The garden’s owner has a greyhound. The garden’s owner has a greyhound.

contents.textus: 47. Gdoṯe, gdoṯe, kul+naqla gəmxapər, gəmxapər, doxele. Láwoste mḥe... kə́twayle, kə́twayle hno… kə́twayle sayfo.
contents.versio: 47. It would come, it would come, every time it digs, it digs to eat him. As for that one, he h[it]... he had, he had a whatsit… he had a sword.

contents.textus: 48. Ḥəḷḷe i+ṭažiye gduxlole. Aḏiʕat? Dmora di+baxča, háwosi šēx man daʕ+ʕàrabwa.
contents.versio: 48. He saw that the greyhound was going to eat him. You know? The garden owner’s [greyhound], so that one, he was one of these Arab sheikhs (lit. ‘a sheikh from these of the Arabs’).

contents.textus: 49. Qām mǧalǧaḷḷe ruḥe, oḏaʕ i+xanǧar qúmewa, qṭəʕle qarʕa di+ṭažiye, qṭilole. Aḏiʕat?
contents.versio: 49. He up and twisted himself back and forth, he knows the dagger was in front of him, he cut off the greyhound’s head, he killed it. You know?

contents.textus: 50. Edi bu+šəklano. Ŭ ínnaqla daṯi u+šēx daʕ+ʕàrabsi ltamo, kalá i+ṭažiyayḏe hawxa. Azzé u+šēx d̥qoṭal ánnaqla u+zlām.
contents.versio: 50. Then like this. And when the Sheikh of the Arabs also came there, here’s his greyhound like so. The sheikh went to kill the man then.

contents.textus: 51. He u+zlām támoyo. Qām u+zlām, qadər ʕal u+šex, qṭile. Qṭile, rawəx ʕal u+səsyayḏe, omər, ‘Growaxno ʕal u+səsyo ŭ mahzamno, ánnaqla’.
contents.versio: 51. The man is still there. The man up and overpowered the sheikh, he killed him. He killed him, mounted his horse, he says, ‘I’ll ride the horse and escape, then’.

contents.textus: 52. Səmle lo+səmle du+səsyawo, du+ḥaywanawo, d̥qoyəm əzzé ʕam u+zlām, lazzé.
contents.versio: 52. No matter what he did with that horse, with that animal, to up and go with the man, it wouldn’t go.

contents.textus: 53. Omər, ‘Ya mbarxo! Madāmki ono ksāmno lə+ksāmno...’ Hano Xaláf Aġá komaḷḷe lu+səsyo. Omər, ‘Madāmki komaṇṇo, ksāmno lə+ksāmno, lə+ksaymat ban diḏi, hat áykova dməblatli, aṣəl hattat’.
contents.versio: 53. He says, ‘Oh, blessed one! Since no matter what I do...’ This is Halaf Agha speaking to the horse. He says, ‘Since, I say, no matter what I do, you don’t do it my way (lit. ‘my call’), wherever you take me, you’re in charge’.

contents.textus: 54. (AA: U+səsyo áykova dmobele.) MuA: E. Hánosi, u+səsyo, korowəx aʕle, kuzzé, kuzzé, kuzzé, kokole. Ánnaqla u+ʕàrabsi, u+rabo daʕ+ʕarab kúlleyo.
contents.versio: 54. (AA: The horse, wherever it takes him). MuA: Right. Then, the horse, he rides it, he goes, he goes, he goes, it stops. Now then, so the Arab, he’s the leader of all the Arabs.

contents.textus: 55. Koḥayrat, i+k̇onayḏe, kīt, arbaʕ̥ṣar+stuwanyo, ḥəngi rábṯoyo. Kuzzé u+səsyo, kokole quma.
contents.versio: 55. You look, his tent, there it is, it’s fourteen poles, so large is it. The horse goes, it stops in front of it.

contents.textus: 56. Ŭ kolowəš aǧ+ǧule Xaláf Aġasi, du+ʕarab, du+rabo daʕ+ʕarab. Ǧġēr me ʕayne lə+kṭore… bʕayne druḥe.
contents.versio: 56. And so Halaf Agha wears the clothes, those of the Arab, of the leader of the Arabs. Apart from his eyes, he doesn’t let anything (show), with his own eyes.

contents.textus: 57. Hánosti, kosaymi, koqaymi, koqaymi, mә‿kosaymi?
contents.versio: 57. So this one, they are working, they get up, they get up, what do they do?

contents.textus: 58. Aʕ+ʕarab koṯən me hawī́r, mičoki taḥt i+k̇one, ŭ u+zlām maf+fehtiyat ṭməḷḷe qarʕe hawxa, kočākke bi+arʕo, noše loḏaʕle.
contents.versio: 58. The Arabs come from around (the area), they slip under the tent, and the man hid his head out of shame like so, he sticks (his eyes) to the ground, nobody recognizes him.

contents.textus: 59. Ŭ hə́nnəkste, bu+fəkraṯṯe u+šēx daʕ+ʕàrabyo.
contents.versio: 59. And as for them, in their minds, he’s the Sheikh of the Arabs.

contents.textus: 60. Kočṓk qarʕe bi+arʕo. E, ma mə‿ksaymi ánnaqla?
contents.versio: 60. He sticks his head to the ground. Right, what do they do, then?

contents.textus: 61. Koṯən, štaġaliye layt, ŭ koṯən ŭ kuzzə́n, hul d̥awi falge+dlalyo. Koqaymi hanək, aʕ+ʕarab, kuzzənne.
contents.versio: 61. They come, there isn’t any conversation, they come and go, until it became midnight. They get up, the Arabs, they go away.

contents.textus: 62. I+žənk̇e du+mērk̇o, du+ʕàrabi, koṯe... i+ṗirayḏe kuṯyo k̬yətwo qәm raġle du+šēx, ăma latyo u+šēx! U+šēx qṭíloyo. Lu+zlām qṭile, l Xaláf Aġá.
contents.versio: 62. The man’s wife, of the Arab, he comes… his wife comes to sit at the sheikh’s legs, but he’s not the sheikh! The sheikh is murdered. The man had killed him, Halaf Agha (had done it).

contents.textus: 63. Kəmmo, ‘Ḥaru bayto, u+rabo daʕ+ʕarab kúllehat, ŭ me ʕaṣriye, ʕal čik̇e d̥ṭažik̇e dәqṭilalle … ŭ kočaykat u+mŭkusayḏux bi+arʕo. Ma latyo ʕaybo?
contents.versio: 63. She says, ‘Goddamn it (lit. ‘the house is ruined’), you’re the leader of all the Arabs, but since the evening, over some runt (lit. ‘little bit’) of a greyhound pup that they killed … and you are sticking your gaze to the ground. Isn’t it a shame?’

contents.textus: 64. Ŭ aq+qa+ʕarabani diḏan koṯən bәgnune ŭ koduʕri bәgnune ŭ hawxa, latyo ʕaybo aʕlux?’
contents.versio: 64. ‘And all these Arabs of ours come and go furtively (lit. ‘in thievery’) and go back furtively, and so on, isn’t it a shame on you?’

contents.textus: 65. U+zlām koborəm, ani, hno di+ṗire. Komər, ‘M Aloho komətle... ž̥xwa minax komətle, m Aloho lə+k̬mətle’.
contents.versio: 65. And the man twists, like, the woman’s whatsit. He says, ‘It is hidden from God… of course, it is hidden from you, it isn’t hidden from God’.

contents.textus: 66. ‘Ăḷo, ono lanno u+zlamayḏax. Ono Xaláf Aġano, u+rabo di+barriye kúlano’.
contents.versio: 66. ‘By God, I am not your husband. I am Halaf Agha, the leader of this whole plain’.

contents.textus: 67. ‘Ŭ mətyaqnat, ḥzéleli bi+baxča druḥe. Ŭ eli, aṯi d̥qoṭeli, čə́kleli bdukṯo lu+qaṭlo’.
contents.versio: 67. ‘And believe me, he saw me in his own garden. And me, he came to kill me, he stuck me in a spot for killing’.

contents.textus: 68. ‘Ŭ i+ṭažiyayḏe aṯyo d̥ḥunqoli. I+xanǧar áʕmiwa, qṭiloli’.
contents.versio: 68. ‘And his greyhound came to grab my throat (lit. ‘to strangle me’). The dagger was with me, I killed it’.

contents.textus: 69. ‘Ŭ bəṯr híyesi maq+qaḥrat di+ṭažiye aṯi; qṭili híyesti’.
contents.versio: 69. ‘And then he also came full of rage for his greyhound; I killed him too’.

contents.textus: 70. ‘Ŭ rawəxno ʕal u+səsyayḏe, lwəšli aǧ+ǧulayḏe ŭ aṯino, mḥalaqli ruḥi lu+tōr ŭ baxtayḏax’.
contents.versio: 70. ‘And I mounted his horse, put on his clothes, and came (here), and I have thrown myself at your mercy’.

contents.textus: 71. ‘Ánnaqla aṣəl hattat. Kəbʕat maqṭeli ŭ kəbʕat... aṣəl hattat’. Əmmo, ‘Yār, d̥kəttat, əšmux nafiqo, Xaláf Aġahat.
contents.versio: 71. ‘Now then, you’re in charge. Whether you want me killed or whether you want ... you’re in charge’. She says, ‘Dear, if it’s you, you are famous (lit. ‘your name is outstanding’), you’re Halaf Agha!’

contents.textus: 72. ‘U+rabo di+barriye d̥ Xaláf Aġá d̥ Súriyahat, ŭ qṭilux u+zlamayḏi, nafiqat gawroṫə́r mu+zlamayḏi’.
contents.versio: 72. ‘You are the leader of the Syrian Halaf Agha Plain, and you have killed my husband, you’ve turned out to be manlier than my husband’.

contents.textus: 73. ‘Ono muʕdo pev lăǧanux’. (AA: ‘Yaʕni i+ṗirayḏux?’) E, əmmo, ‘Ono lăǧanux’.
contents.versio: 73. ‘I’m yours from now on’. (AA: ‘Like, your wife?’) Right, she says, ‘I’m yours’.

contents.textus: 74. Omər, ‘Madāmki háwxayo, e, áydarbo gmobaṇṇax?’
contents.versio: 74. He says, ‘Since it’s that way, right, how shall I take you away?’

contents.textus: 75. Əmmo, ‘Ono, bayn aʕ+ʕarab, u+ḥarb dbayn aʕ+ʕarab aʕli. Ono gəmḥarbono ʕam aʕ+ʕarab, ŭ məd nafiqina marke, u+aṯrayḏux aʕlux’. Omər, ‘Ónosi mәd̥‿čikno bi+barriyayḏi, zătan u+rabo di+barriye kúlano, zătan noše lo+komaḷḷi mede’.
contents.versio: 75. She says, ‘As for me, between the Arabs, the fighting that’s between the Arabs is on me. I shall fight with the Arabs, but when we get out of here, your place is on you’. He says, ‘Me too, when I get into my plain, of course I am the leader of the whole plain, of course nobody will say anything to me’.

contents.textus: 76. Hánosti koqaymo, kosaymi ruḥayye kār. Bar d̥ṣafro korawxi, kul+ḥa mənne ʕal səsyo, ŭ k̬moḥən bi+barriye.
contents.versio: 76. Then she gets up, they prepare themselves. Before morning, they ride out, each of them upon a horse, and they strike off for the plain.

contents.textus: 77. Hə́nnəksti koqaymi, koqaymi. kŽ̥xwara ŭ marak koqaymi ŭ komoḥən aʕla. Kəmmi, ‘Ăḷo, latwa u+šexayḏan, ŭ lano dәqṭile u+šexayḏan. Hano ḥrénowa. Ŭ malexu, kombele i+ṗirayḏe!’
contents.versio: 77. As for them (the Arabs), they get up, they get up. kEvery man for himselfk (lit. ‘for oneself and ourselves’), they up and set off after her. They say, ‘Gosh, it wasn’t our sheikh, but this one who killed our sheikh. This was another one. And go, he took his wife!’

contents.textus: 78. Ánnaqla, bann+alfowat konəfqi ʕarab, komḥalqi bəṯre.
contents.versio: 78. Now then, the Arabs come out in the thousands, they tossed themselves after him.

contents.textus: 79. I+žənk̇e kəmmo, ‘Kula aʕli’. Ŭ koqaymo mḥarbo aʕmayye ŭ komaxəlṣole mu+ʕafro druḥa, ŭ məd̥‿čiko bu+ʕafrayḏe… Ánnaqla, koqaymi, koqaymi me tamo, koqaymi, komaxlaṣla. Ŭ bu+šəklano.
contents.versio: 79. The woman says, ‘It’s all on me’. She up and fights with them and saves him from her own soil, and after she gets into his soil… Now then, they set off , they set off from there, they set off, he saves her. And so on.

contents.textus: 80. Ánnaqla, məḷḷe li+ǧămaʕayḏe, omər, әmmi, әmmi, omər, ‘Kuḏʕutu, ǧămaʕa?’ Әmmi, ‘Mənyo’?
contents.versio: 80. Now then, he said to his gang, he says, they say, they say, he says, ‘Guess what (lit. ‘do you know’), gang?’ They say, ‘What is it?’

contents.textus: 81. Omər, ‘Ono Xaláf Aġáwayno, mṭeli tarte, i+ʕasī̀l daṗ+ṗirayḏi háṯeyo’, ŭ hawyo i+ṗirayḏe. KṪə žməra sāġ!K (AA: KṪə saġṫə́r!K)
contents.versio: 81. He says, ‘I was Halaf Agha, I brought back two women, the nobler of my wives is this one’, and she became his wife. KMay you be well!’K (lit. ‘May you be healthy for my sake!’) (AA: K‘You too!’K (lit. ‘May you be healthier!’).

texts.textName: Murder in Kfarze, Ilyas’ summary of the story (Alyas d be Ġəzalo)

contents.textus: 001. Bə Kfarze kətwa… ʕoyašwa eba ṭáyeste w mšiḥóyeste. Kətwa ar+rabe də Kfarze dḥəkmiwa bu+zabnawo, bann+alfo w čaʕmo w čaʕ w ḥamši.
contents.versio: 001. In Kfarze there was… There lived in it both Muslims and Christians. There were the chieftains of Kfarze who ruled at that time, in 1959.

contents.textus: 002. I+naqlayo ar+rabone dəKfarze, ann+aġawin dəKfarze be Xátewayne. Haṯe ʕayla, ʕayla me di+qriṯoyo, maṭ+ṭaye. Hawi ʕam zabno dəžmə́nayiye bayn i+ʕaylaṯe w bayn ʕayla da+mšiḥoye.
contents.versio: 002. That moment the chieftains of Kfarze, the aghas of Kfarze were the Xate family. This is a family, a family from those of the village, from the Muslims. Over time hostility arose between this family and a family of Christians.

contents.textus: 003. Manyo i+ʕaylaṯe? I+ʕaylaṯe, kəmmila u+Šamʕən du+Išḳo. U+Šamʕən du+Išḳo, hánoste, kosōm qačaxčitiye bayn Túrkiya bayn Súriya. Yani, dəmmina, kuzzeyo, kəmbal silā́ḥ, kəmṭe silā́ḥ, w kəmṭe medone du+qačaġ, w kəmbal medone du+qačaġ, u+šuġlano kosōmle.
contents.versio: 003. Which one is that family? That family, they call it Šamʕən of Išḳo. The Šamʕən of Išḳo, this very one, he engages in smuggling between Turkey and Syria. Like, let us say, he goes, he’ll take some arms away, he’ll bring some arms back, and he’ll bring some contraband things back, and he’ll take away some contraband things, he does this sort of work for himself.

contents.textus: 004. Hani be Xáteste kosaymi u+gəlləhayḏe, be Xáteste košuġli ʕam i+dawle, ʕam i+dawle d Túrkiya. W mede dqudri … w mede dəbʕi kəppe saymi, qawyene ġắlăbe bi+dawle.
contents.versio: 004. These Xates complain about him, the Xate family also collaborate with the government, with the government of Turkey. And whatever they can... and whatever they want, they can do, they are very strong with the government.

contents.textus: 005. Hə́nnəkste kosaymi u+gəlləh du+Šamʕən, du+Šamʕən du+Išḳo, lašan dmazəbṭile dmaḥtile bu+ḥappəs. U+Šamʕən du+Ìšḳoste dínaqqa dəsəmme i+šəkwayḏe, mahzamle. Mahzamle lu+Šamʕən, azzeyo l Súriya.
contents.versio: 005. So they complain about Šamʕən, about Šamʕən of Išḳo to make them catch him to put him in jail. As for Šamʕən of Išḳo, when they made a complaint about him, he escaped. Šamʕən escaped, he went to Syria.

contents.textus: 006. Azzé l Súriya, yawmo, tre, tloṯo, yarḥo. Bi+ḥarayto omar, ‘Ksolaqno, gdoṯeno, yani, me Súriya lə Kfarze’.
contents.versio: 006. He went to Syria, a day, two, three, a month. Finally, he says, ‘I shall go up, I shall come back, like, from Syria to Kfarze’.

contents.textus: 007. Ḥa+lalyo aṯi, omar, ‘Ono w be Xate, kobaʕno doṯina ləḥḏoḏe. Áydarbo kəbʕina doṯina ləḥḏoḏe?’ Omar, ‘Ṭroṯe noše baynoṯayna mamṭelan ləḥḏoḏe, gdowina bəšlomo, yani, dlo+quṭlina ḥḏoḏe, dlo+saymina mede bəḥḏoḏe’
contents.versio: 007. One night he came back, he says, ‘The Xate family and I, I want us to come together. How will we come together?’ He says, ‘Let some people from among us come to bring us together, so that we shall be in peace, like, we shall not kill each other, so that we shall not do something to each other’.

contents.textus: 008. Mamṭənne ləḥḏoḏe lan+noše, w mamṭənne ləḥḏoḏe. U+Šamʕən fāš, hiye w hənnək, hawən ġắlăbe dōst ʕam ḥḏoḏe, yarḥo, tre, tloṯo, bu+šəklano. Kuzzé w oṯe l Súriya w kosolaq lə Kfárzeste. Qačaxčitiye kosṓm, šuġle háwoyo.
contents.versio: 008. The people brought them together, and they brought them together. Šamʕən stayed, he and they, they became very friendly between each other, a month, two, three, in this way. He comes and goes to Syria and he goes to Kfarze as well. He smuggles, that’s his job.

contents.textus: 009. Híyeste maḥatle bhawne, omar, ‘Kolozam aš+šaqṣatani sōmno mede appe. Məsōmno appe? Kobaʕno dqoṭálnanne’. Koṯe ánnaqqa blalyo, kul lalyo, dəmmina, koṯe me ʕIwárdoyo, aw koṯe me qəryawoṯe ḥréneyo. Qačaxčiyo.
contents.versio: 009. As for him, he set his mind to it, he says, ‘These people, it is necessary for me to do something to them. What shall I do to them? I want to kill them’. Now then, he comes at night, every night, let’s say, either he comes from ʕIwardo or he comes from other villages. He is a smuggler.

contents.textus: 010. Koṯe lgabayye li+ǧəvate, koṯe lgabayye li+ǧəvate. Ínaqqa dkoʕobar lawġul, koballe u+silāḥ alle, u+silaḥayḏe komaḥatle tamo. W kito čalkoyo treste aʕme, ḥawrone áʕmene. Hániste kosaymi qačaxčitiye ʕam ḥḏoḏe, kosaymi šuġlo.
contents.versio: 010. He comes by them to the assembly, he comes by them to the assembly. When he goes inside, he surrenders the weapon to them, he puts down his weapon there. And there is a Yezidi or two with him, he has allies with him. These ones smuggle together, they work.

contents.textus: 011. Kelə́n áʕmene, aṯən ltamo. Kul lalyo obewa u+silaḥayḏe alle. Ḥa mal+lalye omar, ‘U+silāḥayḏi lə+gbene’.
contents.versio: 011. Here they are with him, they came there. Every night he gave his weapon to them. One of the nights he says, ‘I won’t give up my weapon’.

contents.textus: 012. Aṯi, ʕabər lawġul, štalle i+čayaṯṯe axəlle u+muklaṯṯe. Bəṯr məd nafəq larwal, bəṯr məd nafəq larwal, hiye mətfakarle, səmle u+pilan dqoṭalle, u+lalyawo dqoṭalle. Nafəq larwal, hnele, yani, markawle u+silāḥ dqoṭal ḥa mənne, qoṭal u+babaṯṯe, u+rabo dkulle.
contents.versio: 012. He came, he went inside, they drank their tea, they ate their food. After he went outside, after he went outside, he thought, he made a plan to kill them, to kill them that night. He went outside, he whatsited, like, he equipped the weapon to kill one of them, to kill their father, the leader of them all.

contents.textus: 013. Dínaqqa dəhné lu+babaṯṯe, zbəṭle u+Šamʕən, zbəṭle u+Šamʕən. Lu+čalkoyo me bəṯre maḥatle u+silāḥ aʕle. Maḥatle u+silāḥ aʕle, qṭile. Aṯi u+àbroste, nafəq. U+abro nafəq me larwal ... žəxwá me larġul mu+bayto. Dínaqqa dnafəq, maḥatle silāḥ ʕal háwoste, qṭile háwoste.
contents.versio: 013. While he is whatsiting their father, the latter caught Šamʕən, the latter caught Šamʕən. The Yezidi shot his weapon at him from behind. He shot his weapon at him, he killed him. His son also came, he came out. His son came out from outside... of course, he came out from inside the house. When he went out, he shot the weapon at that one as well, he killed that one as well.

contents.textus: 014. Veǧa ǧġeni máṯeste, ǧġeni máṯeste, lu+Šamʕən kə́twayle problám ḥreno, kə́twayle problám ḥreno. Kə́twayle ḥurma mšiḥayto, gawírowa, gawírowa. I+ḥurmayḏe kətla ahl b Məḏyaḏ, harke. Kətla ahl b Məḏyaḏ, u+ahlano diḏa. Kətte ʕlaymo, hiya w ʕlaymo, hiya w ʕlaymano dəb Məḏyaḏ kəmmi korəḥmi ḥḏoḏe.
contents.versio: 014. Now then, apart from this, apart from this, Šamʕən had another problem, he had another problem. He had a Christian wife, he was married, he was married. His wife has family in Midyat, here. She has family in Midyat, this family of hers. They have a young man, she and this young man who is in Midyat, they say, they love each other.

contents.textus: 015. Hiya gawə́rtoyo. I+ḥurma du+Šamʕənano gawə́rtoyo ʕam u+Šamʕən. Bas hiye, u+Šamʕən, ʕal dkuzzeyo l Súriya w koṯe, lə+kfōš ġắlăbe bu+bayto. Híyaste konəfqo me Kfarze, kuṯyo l Məḏyaḏ.
contents.versio: 015. She is married. This Šamʕən’s wife is married to Šamʕən. But he, Šamʕən, since he comes and goes to Syria, he doesn’t stay at home a lot. As for her, she leaves Kfarze, she comes to Midyat.

contents.textus: 016. Kətla ahl b Məḏyaḏ, hiya w ʕlaymawo. U+Šamʕən košomaʕ dkətte ʕalaqat ʕam ḥḏoḏe. U+Šamʕən omar, ‘Madā́m i+ḥurmaṯe, an+noše komamṭi baḥəs diḏa, koməǧġoli bəṯra, ono kobaʕno dmarfeno i+ḥurmaṯe. Ono gmarfena, lə+gbaʕna’.
contents.versio: 016. She has family in Midyat, she and that young man. Šamʕən hears that they have relations with one another. Šamʕən says, ‘Since this woman, people are gossiping about her, they are talking behind her back, I want to let this woman go, I shall let her go, I don’t want her’.

contents.textus: 017. Komarfela. Bayn ele w li+ʕaylayo dbe hno, da+mšiḥoye, yani, hiye w u+ḥəmyono, hani kowən dəžmə́n ləḥḏoḏe. Marfele i+barṯaṯṯe, hawən dəžmə́n ləḥḏoḏe. Hániste kowən, xŭdəmmat, mərhṓv ʕamani be Xate.
contents.versio: 017. He lets her go. Between him and that family of the Whatsits, Christians, like, he and his father-in-law, these became an enemy to one another. He let their daughter go, they became an enemy to one another. These also became, as you say, kin with these Xates.

contents.textus: 018. Kowən ḥa, qarší du+Šamʕən, qarší du+Šamʕən, u+Šamʕən azzeyo, yani, dqo... u+lalyawo, dínaqqa dəqṭile aṭ+ṭaye, marfele kmo+silaḥat ʕal u+mšiḥòyoste. D̥qoṭele, lo+qadər dqoṭele. Yani hawiwa măsale bayn ele w la+mšiḥòyeste w bayn ele w aṭ+ṭàyeste, bu+šəklano.
contents.versio: 018. They unite against Šamʕən, against Šamʕən, Šamʕən went, like, to ki... that night, when he killed the Muslims, he released however many salvos against the Christian too. To kill him, he was unable to kill him. Like, it had become a problem both between him and the Christians and also between him and the Muslims, in this way.

contents.textus: 019. W bəṯr, bu+lalyawo bəṯr mədəqṭile aṭ+ṭayanək, azzeyo, mahzamle, azzeyo l ʕIwardo. Fāš u+lalyawo b ʕIwardo, me ʕIwardo azzeyo l Súriya, li+Qaməšlo, mi+Qaməšlo azzeyo l Lubnā́n w me Lubnā́n azzeyo l Awuṣtralya. Hūl uʕdo əšqaḏ təltaḏ ʕoyašwa b Awuṣtralya.
contents.versio: 019. And afterwards, on that night after he killed these Muslims, he went, he escaped, he went to ʕIwardo. He spent that night in ʕIwardo, from ʕIwardo he went to Syria, to Qamishli, from Qamishli he went to Lebanon, and from Lebanon he went to Australia. Until this last year or the year before he lived in Australia.

texts.textName: Murder in Kfarze, Interview with Numan

contents.textus: 001. Ilyas. Bări muʕdo b̥šato li+hno li+Fàrida mə́rwaylalan i+čiroḳe du+mḥasyo du+Šamʕən du+Išḳo. Áydarbo qṭile be Xate, u+Uso, i+măsale áydarbo hawyo? Maḥkéwaylalanyo, veǧa komaṇṇo məqqa dúgleyo, məqqa latyo dugle, čunku hiya ḥúrmayo, lo+kuḏʕo ġălabe medone. Veǧa u+Sargey omar, gdəmmina lu+ḥolo Nəʕman, hiye támowa, ḥzele kúlmede, koḏaʕ̬ kulmede, be mən ǧari, čunku hiye bu+waxtawo ʕláymowa, xortwa. Veǧa ánnaqqa … veǧa omaṇṇo ʕaǧaba bu+waxtawo i+măsale áydarbo hawyo? Mắsala dəmmina, u+Šamʕən qay qṭile dbe Xate? Qay əzzewa? Qay səmme bən xat, dəmmina, u+Šamʕən? W qay, dəmmina, marfele i+Maǧo? Qay bəṯr maqṭalle u+Yusef, mắsala u+Uso. Hani kulle qay hawxa ǧarən? Áydarbo barimo i+măsale, yani i+măsale áydarbo hawyo?
contents.versio: 001. I. A year ago, the whosit, Farideh, told us the story of the late Šamʕən Išḳo. How did he kill the Xates, Uso, how did the story go? She told it to us, now I am saying how much is falsehoods, how much isn’t falsehoods, because she is a woman, she doesn’t know a lot of things. Now Sargey says, let’s talk to Uncle Numan, he was there, he saw everything, he knows everything, what happened, because he was a youth, he was young. Now then … now I would like to say I wonder how the story went at that time? For example, let’s say, why did Šamʕən kill the Xates? Why would he come and go? Why did they send him below the line, let’s say, Šamʕən? And why, let’s say did he divorce Maǧo? Why did he later cause Yusef to be killed, that is Uso? All these things, how did they happen so? How did the story turn out, like, how did the story go?

contents.textus: 002. Nəʕman. k_Malḳavabûo_k, maló hat ṭaw mini kuḏʕat! U+Šamʕən du+Išḳo súriwa, əzzáwayle l Súriya. Ánnaqqa kə́twayle pa̝ləḳat d Súriya aʕme, kə́twayle pa̝ləḳat d Súriya aʕme. Qām aṯi li+qriṯo, aṯi li+qriṯo, madrile, mṣakrile. Mṣakarle ap+pa̝ləḳataṯṯe, mṣakrənne, w ha karixi harke w harke w harke. W noše lo+məḷḷe, ‘Kanné ap+pa̝ləḳat du+Šamʕən du+Išḳo’.
contents.versio: 002. N. Good grief, don’t you know it better than I!? Šamʕən Išḳo was Syrian, he would go to Syria. Now then, he had Syrian papers with him, he had Syrian papers with him. He up and came to the village, he came to the village, he dropped them, he lost them. He lost their papers, they lost them, and so they looked for them here and here and here. And nobody said, ‘Here are the papers of Šamʕən Išḳo’.

contents.textus: 003. N. Qām hánostene, li+Šəmme dbe Qačo ḥzila, ḥzila, hiwila l Osḳe dbe Xate. Ap+pa̝ləḳatayḏe hiwila l Osḳe dbe Xate. Hiwila l Osḳe dbe Xate ap+pa̝ləḳat. Osḳe dbe Xate məḷḷe lu+Šamʕən du+Išḳo, omar, ‘Šamʕən!’ Omar, ‘Mənyo?’ Omar, ‘Kalə́n ap+paləḳat, i+Šəmme dbe Qačo i+krivàyḏanyo, mṭila húlaline, kalənne, ap+pa̝ləḳatayḏux kalənne. Šamiʕat? Kobaʕno dṭorat mi… (i+krivaṯṯewa) i+Mačḳo dbe Mure, lo.
contents.versio: 003. N. This came up, Šəmme Qačo found them, she found them, she gave them to Oske Xate. His papers, she gave to Oske Xate. She gave Oske Xate the papers. Oske Xate said to Šamʕən Išḳo, he says, ‘Šamʕən!’ He says, ‘What is it?’ He says, ‘Here are the papers, Šəmme Qačo is our godmother, she brought them, she gave them to me, here they are, your papers are here. Do you hear? I want you to give up… (she was their godmother) on Mačko Mure, OK?’.

contents.textus: 004. I. Áydarbo ‘ṭorat mi+Mačḳo?’
contents.versio: 004. I. ‘Give up on Mačḳo’, how?

contents.textus: 005. N. Yawo, omar, ‘Ṭray mənne’, yani, ‘Qqoṭaṇṇe’, omar, ‘Qqoṭaṇṇo u+babayḏa, e’. Omar, ‘Qqoṭaṇṇa, qqoṭaṇṇanne’. U+Šamʕən du+Išḳo məḷḷe, ‘Qqoṭaṇṇanne’. Osḳe omar, ‘Ṭray mənne’. Omar, ‘Lo’. Talí, lo+maṣəṯle ʕal u+Šamʕən du+Išḳo. L Osḳe dbe Xate azzé, ap+pa̝ləḳatanək hiwile li+ḥkume. Hiwile li+ḥkume, l Osḳe hiwile li+ḥkume.
contents.versio: 005. N. For goodness’ sake, he says, ‘You give them up!’, meaning, ‘I shall kill him’, he says, ‘I shall kill her father, yes’. He says, ‘I shall kill her, I shall kill them’. Šamʕən Išḳo said, ‘I shall kill them’. Oske says, ‘You give them up!’ He says, ‘No’. Finally, he didn’t obey Šamʕən Išḳo. Oske Xate went, those papers he gave to the government. He gave them to the government, Oske gave them to the government.

contents.textus: 006. N. Qām hánostene, ʕaṣriye u+Šamʕən du+Išḳo azzé, omar, ‘Lawo, maslám ap+pa̝ləḳatayḏi!’ Ăḷa, səmme karabaləġ, lo ele qṭile, kəmdagli, lo ele qṭile, lu+čalkoyo qṭile. Lu+čalkoyo qṭile Osḳe, qṭile Osḳe. Ḥsayno azzé lu+Šamʕən du+Išḳo, azzele lu+Šamʕən du+Išḳo, lu+čalkoyo qṭile háwoste. Mḥele i+tfənge bi+tḥelayḏe w mgandaḷḷe háwoste, qṭile háwoste. Qṭile háwoste w mahzamme, azzehən. Əmmi, ‘Hə hə hə, lu+Šamʕən du+Išḳo qṭile be Xate’. Šamiʕat?
contents.versio: 006. N. This came up, in the evening Šamʕən Išḳo went, he says, ‘Boy, hand over my papers!’ By God, they made a hullabaloo, it was not he who killed him, they lie, it was not he who killed him, the Yezidi killed him. The Yezidi killed Oske, he killed Oske. Ḥsayno went to Šamʕən Išḳo, he went to Šamʕən Išḳo, the Yezidi killed that one too. He fired a rifle into his side and he rolled that one over as well, he killed that one as well. He killed that one as well and they escaped, they went away. They say, ‘Hey, hey, hey, Šamʕən Išḳo killed the Xate’. Do you hear?

contents.textus: 007. N. Qṭilənne, səmme u+hnaṯṯe, i+hnaṯṯe simalle hawxa. Qām hánostene, fayiši hawxa, lo? Səmme i+ʕazzaṯṯe w hnalle, karixi ʕal u+Šamʕən du+Išḳo dquṭlile. Səmme w lo+səmme lo+qadiri quṭlile, lo. Ma… azzeyo l Súriya, w azzé, me Súriya azzé l Awrupa, m Awrupa azzé l Awuṣtralya, Awuṣtralya, azzé l Awuṣtralya raḥuqo. Haw aṯi mənne quṭlənne!
contents.versio: 007. N. They killed them, they did their whatsit, their whatsit they did like so. This came up, they stayed like so, right? They made their wake and whatsited, they looked around for Šamʕən Išḳo to kill him. They tried and tried, they couldn’t kill him, right. Did ... he went to Syria, and he went away, from Syria he went to Europe, from Europe he went to Australia, Australia, he went far away to Australia. Another chance to kill them never came to them again.

contents.textus: 008. N. Qām hánostene, fayišo i+aṯto, i+Mačḳo fayišo hawxa. Ono obáʕwayna. Osḳe ... qalə́bwayno, ḥawre d Ósḳewayno bi+bar<bariye>, ḥawráyyewayno. Osḳe omar, ‘Dlo mōṯno kṭolábnuxyo’. Mi+səbbayo lemi lo+ṭrela ṭolabna. Kṭolábwayna, lemi lo+ṭrela. Emi əmmo, ‘Lukwe dṭəlballa’.
contents.versio: 008. This came up, his wife stayed, Mačko stayed like so. I wanted her. Oske ... I switched, I was Oske’s ally in the con… I was their ally. Oske says, ‘Unless I die, I will betroth her to you’. For that reason my mother did not allow me to betroth her. I would have betrothed her, my mother did not allow me. My mother says, ‘It’s not right that I betroth her’.

contents.textus: 009. I. W bəṯr məd u+Šamʕən azzeyo, dəmmina, azzéyo ltaḥt u+xat, me tamo azzéyo l Awuṣtralya, - áydarbo, bəṯr áydarbo barimo i+măsale?
contents.versio: 009. And after Šamʕən left, let’s say, he went below the line, from there he went to Australia, - how, afterwards how did the matter turn out?

contents.textus: 010. N. Lazzé l Awuṣtralya, qṭile w azzeyo, qṭile w azzeyo. Ánnaqqa ono obáʕwayna. Osḳe omar, ‘Dlo mōṯno kṭolábnuxyo’. Qām u+Šamʕən du+Išḳo lo+maqbele, emi əmmo, ‘Lukwe dṭəlballa’. Qām lu+Uso dbe Xətḳe, ṭlibole. Lu+Uso dbe Xətḳe, ṭlibole, fayišo tamo, hawila ḳačḳéstene, ḳačḳe, i+Gule. W bəṯr, ṣafre du+ṣàwmowa, lalye du+ʕeḏo, lo, qṭəlle bayn l Ḳamme w Ḳandaline tamo, qṭəlle tamo, azzewa lah+hažžəḳat našife. Azzé lah+hažžəḳat našife, qṭəlle tamo. Qṭəlle tamo, əmmi, ‘Hə, hə, hə, Ăḷo, qṭəlle u+Šamʕən dbe+Iško’. Azzano.
contents.versio: 010. N. He hadn’t gone to Australia, he killed him and he went away. Now then, I wanted her. Osḳe says, ‘Unless I die, I will betroth her to you’. Šamʕən Išḳo up and didn’t accept it, my mother says, ‘It is not right that I betroth her’. Uso Xətḳe up and betrothed her. Uso Xətḳe betrothed her, she stayed there, she also had a girl, a girl, Gule. And afterwards, one morning of the fast, Easter Eve, right, they killed him between Lḳamme and Ḳandaline, they killed him there, he had gone for dry brush. He went for dry brush, they killed him there. They killed him there, they say, ‘Hey, hey, hey, by God, they killed Šamʕən Išḳo’. They went away.

contents.textus: 011. I. Žxwa qṭəlle u+Uso?
contents.versio: 011. I. Of course, they killed Uso?

contents.textus: 012. N. U+Uso. Lu+Šamʕən du+Išḳo maqṭele, lu+Šamʕən du+Išḳo maqṭele u+Uso. Axər, marke w tamheniḳé nafəq hən ṭaye, əmmi, ‘Lo, lo, lo+lu+Šamʕən du+Išḳo qṭile. Hən zede qṭəlle’. Lo+nafəq u+qaṭəlayḏe du+Uso dbe Xətḳe, noše laḏəʕ manyo, šamiʕat, laḏiʕina manyo. W fāš mṣakro u+Uso, noše laḏəʕ lmaqqṭile, azzé me kise. Qām, i+măsalayḏan háwxawa du+Šamʕən du+Išḳo…
contents.versio: 012. N. Uso. Šamʕən Iško set up the killing, Šamʕən Iško set up Uso to be killed. Finally, here and there some Muslims came out, they say, ‘No, no, Šamʕən Iško did not kill him. Some other people killed him’. Uso Xətḳe’s killer did not emerge, nobody discovered who it is, you’ve heard, we have not discovered who it is. And Uso remained a mystery, nobody discovered who killed him, his case went cold. Then, our story, the one of Šamʕən Iško, was like so.

contents.textus: 013. I. Păki. Dínaqqa dəqṭile lu+Šamʕən a+tre, Ḥsayno w Osḳe dbe Xate, a+tre, komətyaqanno əšma di+ḥurma d Osḳe Láʕlewa.
contents.versio: 013. I. Alright. When Šamʕən killed the two, Ḥsayno and Osḳe Xate, the two, I believe that the name of Osḳe’s wife was Laʕle.

contents.textus: 014. N. Láʕlewa.
contents.versio: 014. N. It was Laʕle.

contents.textus: 015. I. Osḳe dbe Xate mən d Xátewa, yani, i+emo d Osḳe i+Xàtewa?
contents.versio: 015. I. Osḳe Xate was what to Xate, like, was Oske’s mother the Xate?

contents.textus: 016. N. I+emayḏe ṣuráytowa, Xátewa, i+Xàtewa, əšma Xátewa, ṣuráytowa. U+xwarz daṣ+ṣuròyewa. U+abro ánnaqqa… əmmíwayle l Osḳe, əmmíwa, K_ḳure Xate_K, i+emayḏe Xátewa, əšma Xato. Ha i+măsale du+Šamʕən du+Išḳo háwxayo, w bəṯr mahzamle, azzé l Australiya.
contents.versio: 016. N. His mother was Syriac, she was Xate, she was the Xate, her name was Xate, she was Syriac. He was the Syriacs’ nephew. The son, now then… they called Oske, they called him Xate’s son, his mother was Xate, her name was Xato. Therefore the story of Šamʕən Iško is like so, and after he escaped, he went to Australia.

contents.textus: 017. I: U+Šamʕən dínaqqa dəqṭile hanək, bəkmo ə́šnewa? Məqqa ʕláymowa, yani, kmo əšne xortwa?
contents.versio: 017. I. When Šamʕən killed those guys, how old was he? How young was he, like, how many years young was he?

contents.textus: 018. N: Yawo, lo, lo, latwa xort ġắlăbe, i+măsalayḏe, i+Mačḳo azzayo ʕam u+Yawsef du+abro du+ḥolayḏa l Məḏyaḏ, azzá aʕme l Məḏyaḏ, marke, aṯyo ʕaṣriye, aṯyo me Məḏyaḏ. Omar, ‘Mačḳo’, u+Šamʕən omar. ‘Mənyo?’ Omar, ‘Mačḳo, ləzzáx ʕam u+Yawsef. U+Yawsef latyo mʕadlo, ləzzáx aʕme. Taw, ləzzáx aʕme’. W háwxawaste, e, lo+komaṇṇux? Qām lo+səmla, lo+maṣəṯla aʕle, lo+maṣəṯla aʕle.
contents.versio: 018. N. For goodness’ sake, no, no, he was not very young, his story, Mačko went with the Yawsef, who is her cousin, to Midyat, she went with him to Midyat, from here, she came in the evening, she came from Midyat. He says, ‘Mačko’, Šamʕən says. ‘What is it?’ He says, ‘Mačko, don’t go with Yawsef. Yawsef is not decent, don’t go with him. Stay, don’t go with him’. It was like so, yes, am I not telling you? She up and didn’t do this, she didn’t listen to him, she didn’t listen to him.

contents.textus: 019. Qām i+Ṣarḳe mhalhela, mhalhela, əmmo, ‘U+abro du+Išo, u+abro du+Išo ko … kosōm hne … u+abro du+ḥolàyḏayo … kosōmlayo yār, kosōmla yār! Aḥna latna mu+šəklawo’. Səmla w axər maqəmla i+qyamto li+Ṣarḳe, Aloho mḥasela. Qām edi marfole. Omar, ‘Haw kobaʕna’, marfole. Omar, ‘Ḥayra, haw kobaʕna ono, emi w ḥóṯiyo’. Bəṯr məd məḷḷe, ‘Emi w ḥóṯiyo’, lo+fāšle mede aʕma, lo? Šamiʕat? Ánnaqqa ónostene di+raṣṭiye obáʕwayna. Emi əmmo, ‘Lukwe dʕəbro lu+baytayḏi’.
contents.versio: 019. Sarke up and cried out, she cried out, she says, ‘Išo’s son, Išo’s son is … is doing things, he is her cousin, he makes him out to be a lover to her, he makes her out to have a lover. We are not that type’. She did it, and finally Sarḳe raised a ruckus, God bless her. Then he up and left her alone. He says, ‘I don’t want her anymore’, he left her alone. He says, ‘Buddy, I don’t want her anymore, she is my mother and sister’. After he said, ‘She is my mother and sister’, he had nothing to do with her, right? Do you hear? Now then, in truth, I wanted her. My mother says, ‘It’s not right that she enters my house’.

contents.textus: 020. I. Yani, i+măsale dmarfole ʕal u+Yusefawo? Bas u+hno šaməʕno, d ʔu+Šamʕən obáʕwa dqoṭalwa u+Šàb̥ḳoste.
contents.versio: 020. I. Like, the story is he abandoned her because of that Yawsef? But I heard the whatsit, that Šamʕən had been wanting to kill Šabko as well.

contents.textus: 021. N. ʕAl u+Yawsawo. Qqoṭéwayle, ʕal … Osḳe lo ma<qbele>—mən komaṇṇo, ma lo+mə̀ḷḷilux, omaṇṇo, ‘Məḷḷe, “Qqoṭáṇṇanne!”’ Qoṭalwa hiye ak+kəf<lataṯṯe> … u+Ḥanna, u+Ṣa<lo> … Omarwa, ‘Qqoṭaṇṇo kulle!’ Osḳe omar, ‘A+krivinàyḏine, ṭray mənne’. Lo+maqbele, l Osḳe lo+maqbele dqoṭalle, e. Bəṯr əmmi, ‘Qquṭlina u+Šabo dbe Mure’, mədəqṭəlle Osḳe dbe Xate, əmmi, ‘Áḥnaste ktolina ḥayf, qquṭlina u+Šabo dbe Mure’.
contents.versio: 021. N. Because of that Yawsef. He would have killed him, because … Oske did not l<et>—what should I say, didn’t I tell you, I keep saying, ‘He said, “I shall kill them!”’ He would have killed <their> fam<ilies> ... Hanna, Sa<lo>…He said, ‘I shall kill them all!’ Oske says, ‘They are my godfathers, leave them alone’. He did not agree, Oske did not let kill them, yes. Afterwards they say, ‘We shall kill Šabo Mure’, after they killed Oske Xate, they say, ‘Now then, we shall take revenge, we shall kill Šabo Mure’.

contents.textus: 022. I. Man?
contents.versio: 022. I. Who?

contents.textus: 023. N. Be Xate.
contents.versio: 023. N. The Xates.

contents.textus: 024. I. Haḷḷa, Haḷḷa.
contents.versio: 024. By God, by God.

contents.textus: 025. N. E. U+Gallo dbe Mariḳa, Aloho mḥaṣele, omar, ‘Ṣabri!’ Omar, ‘Ha!’ Omar, ‘Ḥur, gdoṯən, gmaʕbri, gəmfatši gabayxu, i+škaftaṯxu gəmfatšila, kkurxi, gdəmmi, “Šabe Mure, K_lvərda-ya_K, Šabe Mure, hárkeyo”. Ḥur dlo+maʕbrat u+Šabe dbe Mure, lo+maʕbratle ltamo! Ha, kalkomaṇṇux, dʕobar ltamo qquṭlile, gdəmmi lu+Šamʕən du+Išḳo qṭile. Ṭro lo+ʕobar larġul. U+Šabo dbe Mure, ṭrofṓš larwal, fahimat? Latyo hawxa?’
contents.versio: 025. Yes. Gallo Marika, God bless him, says, ‘Ṣabri’. He says, ‘Here!’ He says, ‘Look, they will come, they will bring him in, they will search your place, they will search your cellar, they will go around, they will say, “Šabe Mure, he is here! Šabe Mure, he is here!” See that you don’t let Šabe Mure in, do not let him in there! Look, I am telling you, if he gets in there, they will kill him, they will say Šamʕən Išḳo killed him. Let him not get inside. Let Šabo Mure stay outside, understand? Isn’t it so?’

contents.textus: 026. N. ‘Ṭro lo+ʕobar larġul, ṭro hən zede ḥayri. Ṭro, ṭro u+Šabo… dbe Mure, ṭro lo+ʕobar larġul. Dʕobar larġul, qquṭlile, gdəmmi, ‘Lma qṭile? Lu+Šamʕən du+Iṣḳo qṭile!’ Šamiʕat?
contents.versio: 026. Let him not go inside, let some others look. Let, let Šabo … Mure, let him not go inside. If he goes inside, they will kill him, they will say, ‘Who killed him? Šamʕən Iṣko killed him!’ Do you hear?

contents.textus: 027. N. Qām l Ṣabriyo—ʕammi Ṣabriyo, Aloho mḥasele—omar, omar, ‘Yawo’, omar, ‘ṭro u+Šamʕən, u+Šàmʕənyo xero w dero hárkeyo’, omar, ‘u+Šabo dbe Mure ṭrofṓš larwal w izoxu. Man dkəzzé ṭrəzzeyo, noše ṭrokurxi larġul, man dkəzzé ṭrəzzeyo, dkəbʕutu ṭrokurxi lawġul, hăma u+Šabo dbe Mure lə+gmaqbaṇṇo dʕobar’. Lə+ṭrele dʕobar, ʕammi Ṣabriyo lə+ṭrele dʕobar.
contents.versio: 027. Ṣabriyo up and—Uncle Ṣabriyo, God bless him—says, he says, ‘For goodness’ sake’, he says, ‘let’s assume Šamʕən, either Šamʕən or whoever else is here’, he says, ‘so let Šabo Mure stay outside, and all of you go. Let whoever goes go, let people look around inside, let whoever goes go, if you want to let them go inside, except Šabo Mure, I shall not let him enter’. He did not let him enter, Uncle Ṣabriyo did not let him enter.

contents.textus: 028. I. Ínaqqayo ar+rabe di+qriṯo mánwayne?
contents.versio: 028. I. That time, who were the leaders of the village?

contents.textus: 029. N. Ar+rabe di+qriṯo be Smaílowayne, w be Ḥámḳewayne. W Osḳe dbe Xate qām barra dəṯṯe, qām barra dəṯṯe. Haymén šqile, šqile yani u+hnoste mənne.
contents.versio: 029. N. The leaders of the village were the Smailos and the Ḥamkes. And Oske Xate rose up against them, rose up against them. Really, he took, he took, like, the whatsit from them.

contents.textus: 030. I. I+rabuṯo?
contents.versio: 030. I. The leadership?

contents.textus: 031. N. Eeeš. Məkomaṇṇux. Bəṯr mədəqṭīl, disa fayiši hənnək. Osḳe dbe Xate, yani, yani, aṣ+ṣuroye w aṭ+ṭàyeste, aġlab maṭ+ṭàyestene, ḥawráyyewayne. ʕAm Osḳéwayne, e. Hawxa, áḥnaste ʕam … ónoste ʕam… ḥawre, ḥawre d Osḳéwayno, Aḷḷáh. Edi bəṯr disa daʕərno ʕam be Ḥam<ḳe>… ʕam be Smailo.
contents.versio: 031. N. Yesss. What I’m telling you. After he was killed, again they resumed. Osḳe Xate, like, like, Syriacs and Muslims, most of the Muslims too, were his allies. They were with Oṣke, yes. So, we too with … me too with, I was his ally, Oske’s ally, by God. Then, afterwards, I went back with the Ḥam… with the Smailos again.

contents.textus: 032. I. Kmo+abne kətle l Osḳe uʕdo ádyawma?
contents.versio: 032. I. How many sons does Osḳe have now, today?

contents.textus: 033. N. Lo, lo+fāšle abne. Nuriyo tăne fāš, ma lo+kuḏʕatle, ʕamər bayto!? E, hawo, u+ḥaǧiyawo fāš. Azzé lu+hno, hăma Ramazano kətle, mắsala, Tašǧínoyo w fāšle, w komaṇṇo, Oṣmano māṯ, noše lo+fāšle.
contents.versio: 033. N. No, he has no sons left. Only Nuriyo is left, don’t you know him, Lord have mercy!? Yes, that one, that hajji is left. He went to the whatsit, but he has Ramazan, that is, it’s Tašğino, and he has him left, and I am saying, Osman died, he has nobody left.

contents.textus: 034. I. Wăki i+măsale, i+măsale du+Šamʕən háwxawa. Bəṯr u+lalyo dəqṭile, u+lalyo dəqṭile, mən ǧari, yani, mən hawi? Bəṯr ax+xəbare, xud əmmina, nafəq me Kfarze, mahzamle, laykazzeyo mắsala?
contents.versio: 034. I. Then, the story, the story of Šamʕən was like so. After the night he killed him, the night he killed him, what happened, like, what was up? After the news, so to speak, he left Kfarze, he fled, where did he go, for example?

contents.textus: 035. N. Azzeyo l ʕIwardo. Azzeyo l ʕIwardo, e, mahzamle, azzé l ʕIwardo. Kali harke bi+qadəšto, kaliwa harke bi+qadəšto, hiye w u+čalkoyo.
contents.versio: 035. N. He went to ʕIwardo. He went to ʕIwardo, yes, he fled, he went to ʕIwardo. He stayed here in a sanctuary, he stayed here in the sanctuary, he and the Yezidi.

contents.textus: 036. N. Əmmi, ‘Zano, zánanne, k_čūya ʕIwarte_k’. Edi qām mahzamme, azzə́n l ʕIwardo. Azzə́n l ʕIwardo. Edi qām aṭ+ṭaye karixi aqqa dkoṯonani. Edi haw maǧralle dnuḥti lu+šalwo bi+Tqùzoda. Edi azzeyo. Qqoṭalwa hḗšstene, qquṭliwa hḗšstene, e. I+măsale háwxawa.
contents.versio: 036. N. They say, ‘Let’s go, let’s go to them, he went to ʕIwardo’. Then they up and fled, they went to ʕIwardo. They went to ʕIwardo. Then the Muslims up and looked around all these places, then they did not dare to go any further down to the gully through Tquzo. Then he went away. He would have killed even more, they would have killed even more, yes. The story was like so.

contents.textus: 037. I. Bəṯr me tamo naḥət taḥt u+xat, žxwa.
contents.versio: 037. I. Afterwards, from there he went under the line, of course.

contents.textus: 038. N. Naḥət taḥt u+xat, me taḥt u+xat…
contents.versio: 038. He went under the line, from under the line…

contents.textus: 039. I. Ema i+ḥurmayḏe… Látwayle bəṯr mi+Mačḳo niše heša?
contents.versio: 039. I. When did his wife… Didn’t he have even more wives after Mačḳo?

contents.textus: 040. N. Lo. Mṭele, i… əšma, ṭaʕino əšma. Lo, Ṣárayo komaṇṇo, ṭaʕino əšma. Mṭele hayo, hawila šawʕ … ḥamšo+abne, bi+Swičra … žxwa, b Awustraliya, e, kətla uʕdo ḥamšo+abne.
contents.versio: 040. N. No. He brought back… her name, I forgot her name. No, it is Ṣara I would say, I forgot her name. He brought back that one, she had sev… five sons, in Switzerland … in Australia of course, yes, now she has five sons.

contents.textus: 041. I. Yani hiye dínaqqa dkətwa harke u+Šamʕən, dəmmina, marfele i+Mačḳo?
contents.versio: 041. I. Like, he, when Šamʕən was here, so to speak, he abandoned Mačḳo?

contents.textus: 042. N. Marfole. Məḷḷe, omar, ‘Emi w ḥóṯiyo’.
contents.versio: 042. N. He abandoned her. He said, he says, ‘She is my mother and sister’.

contents.textus: 043. I. I+Mačḳo marfole, ḥḏo latle. Ánnaqqa áykoyo, ayko kofṓš?
contents.versio: 043. I. Mačḳo, he abandoned her, he doesn’t have a woman, now then, where is he, where does he end up?

contents.textus: 044. N. Azzé, mahzamle, komaṇṇux, mahzamle, azzé l Súriya.
contents.versio: 044. N. He went away, he fled, I am telling you, he fled, he went to Syria.

contents.textus: 045. I. Bas oṯewa, bas oṯewa, solaqwa.
contents.versio: 045. I. But he used to come back, but he used to come back, he used to come up.

contents.textus: 046. N. Solaqwa, əzzé w oṯewa, əzzé w oṯewa. Ánnaqqa aṭ+ṭaye də Kfarze əmmi, ‘Gəzzán ʕal u+šopayḏe’.
contents.versio: 046. N. He used to come up, he used to come and go, he used to come and go. Now then, the Muslims of Kfarze say, ‘Let’s go on his trail’.

contents.textus: 047. N. Qām mərre lu+Šamʕən du+Išḳo, ǝmmi, ‘Ḳurro, ṭrowelux h͜āž me ruḥux, gədquṭlilux ha, ṭrowelux hāž me ruḥux’.
contents.versio: 047. They up and said to Šamʕən Išḳo, they say ‘Boy, take care of yourself, they will kill you, yes, take care of yourself’.

contents.textus: 048. I. Mšadárwalle Malla ʕAli.
contents.versio: 048. I. They sent Mullah ʕAli.

contents.textus: 049. Malla ʕAli, haaa K_saḥát xwaš_K.
contents.versio: 049. Mullah Ali, aha, thank you.

contents.textus: 050. I. Dínaqqa, dínaqqa dlu+Uso dmərle, ‘Gmamṭeno i+Mačḳo’ … dəmmina lu+hno lo+mšadàrlele xabro, lo+mərle, ‘Qqoṭaṇṇux, ḥzay, dǝmṭatla’?
contents.versio: 050. I. When, when Uso said, ‘I shall bring back Mačko’ … so to speak, did whosit not send word to him, didn’t he say, ‘I shall kill you, see, if you bring her back’?

contents.textus: 051. N. Mə́ḷḷele…
contents.versio: 051. N. He said it to him…

contents.textus: 052. I. Mə́ḷḷele, latyo hawxa?
contents.versio: 052. I. He said it to him, isn’t it so?

contents.textus: 053. N. Mə́ḷḷele, mə́ḷḷele, omar, omar, ‘Komaṇṇux, lo+ṭəlbatla’. I+Səṫṫe əmmo, ‘Ḥur, dṭəlbatla gmaqəṭlallux, kal kəmaḷḷux, lo+dəmmat, lo+mə̀ḷḷuxli’.
contents.versio: 053. N. He told him, he told him, he says, he says, ‘I am telling you, do not betroth her’. Sǝṫṫe says, ‘Look, if you betroth her, I shall cause you to be killed, now I am telling you, don’t say I didn’t tell you’.

contents.textus: 054. N. ‘Lo+ṭəlbatla’. Omar, ‘Kṭolabna’. Li+Səṫṫe səmla w lo+səmla, lo+qadiro aʕle. Omar, ‘Ăḷa kṭolabna’. Qām ṭlibole, mədṭlibole, šato, tarte hawila i+Gule, i+ḳačḳayo hawila. Edi qṭǝlle, azzé lah+hažžəḳat, qṭəlle bu+ṭuro.
contents.versio: 054. N. ‘Do not betroth her’. He says, ‘I will betroth her’. Sǝṫṫe tried and tried, she did not prevail over him. He says, ‘By God, I shall betroth her’. He up and betrothed her, after he betrothed her, a year, two later she had Gule, she had that girl. Then they killed him, he went out for brushwood, they killed him in the hill country.

contents.textus: 055. I. Bele. Păki bəṯr mədəqṭile u+Šamʕən, qṭile a+tre dbe Xate, mən hawi bi+qriṯo, əmmi, aṯən ah+halaxxiye ʕal i+qriṯo w lu+gḏaʕno mən…
contents.versio: 055. I. Yes. Alright, after Šamʕən killed, killed two of the Xates, what happened in the village, they say, the Halaxxis came to the village and I dunno what…

contents.textus: 056. N. Həəəəə, ḥǧə́mwalle li+qriṯo, aṯənwa, ḥǧə́mwalle li+qriṯo, ma K_malḳavawo_K ma… laḏiʕat?
contents.versio: 056. N. Huh, they attacked the village, they came, they attacked the village, good grief, don’t you know?

contents.textus: 057. I. Ayna qəryawoṯe mắsala? Halaxxe w bas?
contents.versio: 057. I. Which villages, for example? Halaxxe and that’s it?

contents.textus: 058. N. Halaxxe, Halaxxe, Halaxxíwayne komaṇṇo, lu+gḏaʕno, lo, aš+šəṭraḳòyeste aṯənwa hən mənne, lo, lo…
contents.versio: 058. N. Halaxxe, Halaxxe, they were Halaxxis. I’m telling you, I dunno, no, the Šəṭraḳians also, some of them came, no, no…

contents.textus: 059. I. E, məssəmme bə Kfarze mắsala dəmmina?
contents.versio: 059. I. Yes, what did they do in Kfarze, as an example so to speak?

contents.textus: 060. N. Lo+səmme, hăma lbe Smailo, ḥayra, ḥayra, i+naqlayo, lbe Smailo tlalle iḏo.
contents.versio: 060. N.They did nothing, but the Smailos, buddy, buddy, that time, the Smailos helped out.

contents.textus: 061. I. Lə+tlalle iḏo?
contents.versio: 061. I. They didn’t help out?

contents.textus: 062. N. Bele. Əmmi, ‘Lo’. Qām Ǧamilo dbe Xate … I+Səṫṫe su+Šabe sámyowa, bu+baytawo du+Šabe samyówayne. I+Səṫṫe i+ḥoṯo du+Šàmʕənwa. Ḥǧə́mmalla, ḥǧə́mmalla, ono ḥawre dbe Xátewayno. Azzino, kalkó, kalkó zbiṭalle ʕal i+goro du+Šabe+samyo, zbiṭalle ʕal i+goro du+Šabe+samyo, zbəṭṭe i+Səṫṫe! U+talgo kə́pwayle hul mə́troste, kə́pwayle zəd me druʕo dtalgo. Tálgowa, ġắlăbe tálgowa. Qām támostene, Alyás, azzino maxəlṣoli, i+mḥasayto di+Səṫṫe, eli w lemi maxəlṣolan.
contents.versio: 062. N. Rather, they say, ‘No’. Then Ǧamilo Xate … Sǝṫṫe was at the blind Šabe’s, they were at that house of the blind Šabe. Sǝṫṫe was Šamʕən’s sister. They attacked her, they attacked her, I was an ally of the Xates. I went, look, look, they have captured her on the roof of the blind Šabe, they have captured her on the roof of the blind Šabe, they have captured Səṫṫe! There was a meter of snow, there was more than an arm’s length of snow. There was snow, a lot of snow. On the spot, Alyas, I up and went to rescue her, the late Sǝṫṫe, my mother and I rescued her.

contents.textus: 063. N. Omaṇṇo, ‘Zax sidan’, azzá sidan. U+Ǧamilo mḥéleli daḥfe, l Ǧamilo maqlábleli lu+talgo, hawo nafǝl bayn u+talgo, Ḥamadé Xate nafǝl bayn u+talgo, hanǝk nafili ltamo a+tre, w… i+Sǝṫṫe maxǝlṣolan, azzá gab i+Faho, fayišo gabayna. Maxǝlṣolan tamo, lo? Maxǝlṣolan, i+mḥasayto di+Sǝṫṫe.
contents.versio: 063. I say, ‘Go to our place’, she went to our place. Ǧamilo gave me a push, Ǧamilo toppled me into the snow, that one fell into the snow, Ḥamadé Xate fell into the snow, those two fell there, and… Sǝṫṫe, we rescued her, she went to Faho’s, she stayed with us. We rescued her there, right? We rescued her, the late Sǝtte.

contents.textus: 064. Edi qām azzano zbe Ǧǝǧo, ǝmmi, ǝmmi, ‘Nǝʕman, K_nayara_K’, Laʕle ǝmmo, ‘Nǝʕman, K_kríve máya, Nǝʕman, rə́ḥe máya_K’. U+ʕAzo dbe Mure, Aloho mḥasele, omar, ‘Kul bayto – tlaṯmo+noṭat. D̥ Šǝmoḳe – šeṯmo, dmǝǧġolo – malyún maṯe… alfo w maṯe’.
contents.versio: 064. Then we up and went to Ǧǝǧo’s house, they say, they say, ‘Nǝʕman, enemy’, Laʕle says, ‘Nǝʕman is our godfather, Nǝʕman is our soul’. ʕAzo Muro, God bless him, says, ‘Each house – three hundred liras. From Šemoke – six hundred, if she speaks up – one million… one thousand and two hundred’.

contents.textus: 065. N. Lu+ʕAzo dbe Mure w u+Gawriḳe di+Hədo, a+trani. I+Ṣa<briyo>… i+Hədo… ǝmmo, ‘Gawriye, ḳurem, čiko biḏoṯux i+qriṯo, marḥám, sǝm raḥme, ḳurem, sǝm raḥme, Gawriye, sǝm raḥme, lo+maṣiṯat ʕal u+ʕAzo’. Ánnaqqa qāmno ónoste šamǝʕno, šamǝʕno, omaṇṇo, ‘Ḳuro, Gawriye, mǝmăsáleyo kǝmmat? Kǝmmat, “Tlaṯmo+noṭat. D̥ Šǝmoke dmǝǧġolo, ktowǝn šeṯmo, dmǝǧġolo, ktowǝn alfo w maṯe.” Məštaġaliye komǝǧġolat? Kḥozeno u+gawrawo dǝzzé šoqal, ṭolab čarxi mi+Šǝmoḳe w me Ṣabriyo, šamiʕat?’
contents.versio: 065. ʕAzo Muro, Hədo’s Gawrike, these two. Ṣa<briyo>… Hədo says, ‘Gawriye, my boy, the village has slipped into your hands, be merciful, have mercy, my son, have mercy, Gawriye, have mercy, don’t listen to ʕAzo’. Now then I too up and heard, I heard, I say, ‘Boy, Gawriye, what is the story you are telling? You say, “Three hundred liras. If Šǝmoke were to speak up, it will be six hundred, if she speaks up (again), it will be a thousand and two hundred.” What tales are you telling? I would like to see the man who goes to take, to demand a nickel from Šǝmoke and from Sabriyo, do you hear?’

contents.textus: 066. N. Qām aḥna čikina, ono w u+ʕAzo dbe Mure čikina bi+qǝrrǝḳe dəḥḏoḏe tamo. U+ʕAzo dbe Mure omar, ‘Lawo, koṯat ʕul mənne?’ Omaṇṇo, ‘Lawo, koṯeno ʕul mənne, mǝqqa dǝmmat i+aṯto dʕámmiyo. Dǝḥḏóḏena. Mǝ kǝbʕatlux, ḳuro? Kalǝ́n tláṯmone, mǝdlux a+tlaṯmo noṭaṯxu, qay gdomar, “Dmǝǧġolo, ktowǝn šeṯmo, dmǝǧġolo, ktowǝn alfo w maṯe”?’
contents.versio: 066. N. We up and got at, ʕAzo Mure and I, we got at each other’s throats there. ʕAzo Mure says, ‘Boy, are you coming over to them?’, I say, ‘Boy, … no matter what you say, she is my uncle’s wife. We belong to each other. What do you want for yourself, boy? Here’s three hundred, take your three hundred liras for yourself. Why is he saying, “If she were to speak up, it will be six hundred, if she speaks up (again), it will be a thousand and two hundred”?’

contents.textus: 067. I. Veǧa šqǝlwalle mi+qriṯo kula?
contents.versio: 067. I. Now then, they took it from the whole village?

contents.textus: 068. N. Kula. Mi+qriṯo lkulle húwalle, kul ḥa tlaṯmo, e. Kula. Mi+qriṯo lkulle húwalle.
contents.versio: 068. N. All of it. From the village, everybody gave, each one three hundred, yes. All of it. From the village, everybody gave.

contents.textus: 069. I. E, balki kito faqire?
contents.versio: 069. I. Yes, perhaps there are some poor folks?

contents.textus: 070. N. Kǝtwa faqire, hən … šuqliwa … hǝn … lo, lo, lo, hən … lo+šuqliwa daf+faqire. Hani dkǝtwayne ḥawrayye ʕam dbe Smailo, dkǝ́twayne hawxa hno, šuqliwa.
contents.versio: 070. N. There were poor folks, some … they took … some … no, no, no, some ... they did not take from the poor. These who were allies with the Smailos, who were such a thing, they took (from them).

contents.textus: 071. I. W ak+kallawatani lman obǝ́nwanne?
contents.versio: 071. I. And these funds, to whom did they give them?

contents.textus: 072. N. L Laʕle, kulle l Laʕle obǝ́nwanne.
contents.versio: 072. N. To Laʕle, they gave all of them to Laʕle.

contents.textus: 073. I. Li+ḥurma du+qṭiloyo?
contents.versio: 073. I. To the wife of the murdered?

contents.textus: 074. N. E… Nuriyo, Nuriyo K_dǝl bráḥǝm_K wa.
contents.versio: 074. N. Yes… Nuriyo, Nuriyo was kindhearted.

contents.textus: 075. I. Hano u+Nuriyano?
contents.versio: 075. I. This very Nuriyo?

contents.textus: 076. N. Eš, eš, e, Səloye Xate hawxa. Səloye Xate omarwa, ‘Lawo, mǝkǝbʕútǝnxu, lawo, mǝkǝbʕútǝnxu, lḥa qṭile, kohnə́n i+qriṯo kula, mǝkǝbʕútǝnxu?’
contents.versio: 076. N. Sure, sure, yes, Səloye Xate as well. Səloye Xate said, ‘Boys, what do you yourselves want, boys, what do you yourselves want, one person killed him, they are whatsiting the whole village, what do you yourselves want?’

contents.textus: 077. N. Eee. K_Dǝl bráḥǝm_Kwa Səloye Xate, u+babo d Nadimo, e.
contents.versio: 077. N. Yesss. He was kindhearted, Səloye Xate, Nadimo’s father, yes.

contents.textus: 078. I. W bǝṯr a+kmo yawmanǝk hawxa, w fayito?
contents.versio: 078. I. And after these however many days like so, it passed?

contents.textus: 079. N. Fayito, e. E, Ăḷa, fayito hawxa. Alyás, ḥur domaṇṇux, Ăḷah, mede lo+fāš dlo+ḥzelan. Ma ánnaqqa kobaʕla…
contents.versio: 079. N. It passed, yes. Yes, by God, it passed like so. Ilyas, see that I am telling you, by God, there is nothing left that we did not see. Now then is it necessary…

contents.textus: 080. I. U+waxtawo…
contents.versio: 080. I. That time…

contents.textus: 081. N. U+waxtawo zaḥf pīswa. I+gnune w K_ad+dǝzziyat…_K
contents.versio: 081. N. This time was excessively bad. Thievery and thefts…

contents.textus: 082. I. Bǝṯr mǝdəqṭili, žxwa bnaqla ḥariwo.
contents.versio: 082. I. Once they had been killed, of course, it became ruined all at once.

contents.textus: 083. N. W bǝṯr bəḥḏo+naqqa ḥariwo, e.
contents.versio: 083. N. And afterwards, all at once it became ruined, yes.

contents.textus: 084. I. Me tamo bǝṯr bdalle a+kfarzoye dǝzzə́n marke l Awrupa.
contents.versio: 084. I. Thereupon Kfarzians started going from here to Europe.

contents.textus: 085. N. Kulle mǝd … mahzamme w mahzamme w mahzamme, w azzehǝn.
contents.versio: 085. N. All of them, after … they fled and they fled and they fled, and they went away.

contents.textus: 086. I. Mu+waxtawo bdalle.
contents.versio: 086. I. They started from that time.

contents.textus: 087. N. E, mǝkomaṇṇux, mu+waxtawo.
contents.versio: 087. N. Yes, that’s what I’m telling you, from that time.

contents.textus: 088. I. Bu+waxtawo nha komǝtyaqanno ínaqqayo iḏiʕéwayne ġắlăbe, dǝmmina, Osḳe w ann+abne, an+noše oṯənwa li+mʕaziye ġắlăbe.
contents.versio: 088. I. At that time, I believe, they were then likely very well-known, so to speak, Osḳe and his sons, people came to the wake a lot.

contents.textus: 089. N: Oṯǝnwa lgabe, yani komaṇṇux, šqile u+rišo, rišo yani, šqíwayle u+rišo, híyewa. Omar, l Ḥaddo mǝ́rwaylele, Ḥaddo mǝḷḷele l Osḳe dbe Xate, mǝḷḷele, omar, ‘Ose, Ose!’ Ḥaddo, ‘Ose, Ose, K_rúna, rúna, lə́nge xwa bǝkšéna lgorána xwa_K’. Omar, omar, ‘K_Azzé lə́nge xwa dəréžḳǝm_K’. Omar, ‘Gǝmḥalaqno...’ ‘Grāš raġlux lgorán druḥux!’. Omar, ‘Gmožadna hēš, hēš, hēš, gmožadna hēš!’ Yani hawxa lo+zōʕwa, lo?
contents.versio: 089. N. They were siding with him, that is, I’m telling you, he had taken control, like, control, he took control, it was he. He says, Ḥaddo said to him, Ḥaddo said to Oske Xate, he told him, he says, ‘Ose, Ose!’ Ḥaddo (in Kurdish), ‘Ose, Ose, take a seat, take a seat, stay in your lane’. He says, he says (in Kurdish), ‘But I am going to stretch my foot out!’ (Osḳe) says (in Turoyo), ‘I shall throw…’ (Ḥaddo, in Turoyo) ‘Stay in your lane!’ (Osḳe) says (in Turoyo), ‘I shall keep, keep, keep stretching it, I shall keep stretching it!’ Like, he was not so afraid, right?

contents.textus: 090. N. Edi l Ḥaddo bi+raḥa, Ḥaddo mə́ḷḷele, bi+raḥa omar, ‘Taw, lawo, taw!’ Lo+yotawwa, mdaʕewa ʕal i+ra… ʕal i+rišo… ʕal i+rabuṯo. W haymén šqilówaylestene. Qām qṭəlle.
contents.versio: 090. N. Then Ḥaddo calmly, Ḥaddo told him, he calmly says, ‘Take a seat, boy, take a seat’. He did not take a seat, he demanded lead… control… leadership. And really, he took it too… Then they killed him.

texts.textName: Murder in Kfarze, The Testimony of Farida

contents.textus: 001. Ilyas. Dəmmina, u+Šamʕən du+Išḳo.
contents.versio: 001. IL. Let’s talk, Šamʕən of Iško.

contents.textus: 002. Farida. E.
contents.versio: 002. FG. Yes.

contents.textus: 003. IL. I+măsalayḏe w d be Xate mənwa? Qay qṭile ann+abnaṯṯe? ʕAl mən hawyo i+măsalaṯe?
contents.versio: 003. IL. What was his problem and the Xates’? Why did he kill their members? What was this problem about?

contents.textus: 004. FG. E, ʕal mənwa? Əzzewa w oṯewa sətte, xud ann+aḥunònewayne. W gabáyyewa dayəm. U+ḥa lalyo…
contents.versio: 004. FG. Yes, what was it about? He used to come and go by them, they were like brothers. And he was always by their side. One night…

contents.textus: 005. IL. ʕAl mən hiye… bayn ele w alle i+măsale …
contents.versio: 005. IL. What about he… the problem between him and them…

contents.textus: 006. FG. Bayn ele w alle hawiwa, xŭdi+hno. Lə+mtaḥmalle ḥḏoḏe
contents.versio: 006. FG. It happened between him and them, like the whatsit. They did not bear each other.

contents.textus: 007. IL. Latwa i+măsale di+Maǧo?
contents.versio: 007. IL. Wasn’t it the Maǧo problem?

contents.textus: 008. FG. Lo, lo. Lo, latwa ʕal i+Maǧo. Qām Laʕle əmmo, ‘Hawli i+tfəngayḏux’. Omar, ‘Lə+gbènaxyo’. — ‘E, qay lə+gbàtliyo?’ Kul lalyo obéwaylayo. Lúlaleyo. Səmme w lo+səmme, liwole. Híyeste, kə́twayle ḥa+čalkoyo aʕme. Kə́twayle ḥa+čalkoyo aʕme. Mədde l Ḥsayno w lu+babo lu+silā̀ḥ miḏe. Mədde, brəmme biḏe dəḥḏoḏe. Mṣaʕáḷḷele lu+čalkoyo, omar, ‘Ma k_ṣabbav_k, lə+kḥayrat qquṭlili?’. Qām lu+čalkoyo, marfele ʕal a+tre, qṭilile w ṭrele. Ha i+măsalaṯṯe háyoyo.
contents.versio: 008. FG. No, no, it was not about Maǧo. Laʕle up and says, ‘Give me your rifle’. He says, ‘I shall not give it to you.’ ‘Yeah, why won’t you give it to me?’ He used to give it to her every night. She didn’t give it to him. They went back and forth, he didn’t give it. As for him, he had a Yezidi with him. He had a Yezidi with him. Ḥsayno and his father grabbed the weapon from his hand. They grabbed it, they twisted it in each other’s hands. He cursed at the Yezidi, he says, ‘Son of a bitch, don’t you see they are going to kill me?’ The Yezidi up and shot at the two, he killed them and left. So, that’s their story.

contents.textus: 009. IL. W i+măsale, qay? Kətwa dəžmənatiye baynoṯayye?
contents.versio: 009. IL. And the problem, why? Was there animosity between them?

contents.textus: 010. FG. E, hawyowa dəžmənatiye baynoṯayye hawxa.
contents.versio: 010. FG. Yes, the animosity between them had arisen like so.

contents.textus: 011. IL. Ono, u+mede dšaməʕno, dəmmina, maʕ+ʕatiqe, əmmiwa, dəmmina, li+šəmme dbe Qačo ḥzela u+kimlik.
contents.versio: 011. IL. As for me, what I heard, so to speak, from the elders, they said, so to speak, Šəmme of the Qačo family found his ID.

contents.textus: 012. FG. Lo, lo, latwa hayo. Hayo báriwa. Ăḷa, bə́ṯrwa. Bəṯr mu+qaṭlowa.
contents.versio: 012. FG. No, no, it was not that. That was earlier. God, it was later. It was after the murder.

contents.textus: 013. IL. Bəṯr mu+qaṭlowa?
contents.versio: 013. IL. It was after the murder?

contents.textus: 014. FG. E. E, bəṯr mu+qaṭlo ḥəzyola.
contents.versio: 014. FG. Yes, yes, she found it after the murder.

contents.textus: 015. IL. E, dəmmina, qay hawən, dəmmina, u+Šamʕən w be Xate, qay hawən dəžmə́n?
contents.versio: 015. IL. Yes, so to speak, why did they become, so to speak, Šamʕən and the Xates, why did they become enemies?

contents.textus: 016. FG. Hawənwa dəžmə́n dəḥḏode, lo+kəḏʕono ónoste.
contents.versio: 016. FG. They had become each other’s enemy, I also don’t know.

contents.textus: 017. IL. Latwa ʕal i+măsale di+Maǧo yani?
contents.versio: 017. IL. Wasn’t it about the Maǧo problem?

contents.textus: 018. FG. Lo, lo, latwa ʕal i+Maǧo.
contents.versio: 018. FG. No, no, it wasn’t about Maǧo.

contents.textus: 019. FG. Bi+ḥaraytaṯe əmmi, li+šəmme ḥzela u+dozdan, edi hula lbe Xate. Əmmo, ‘Kelé ḥzeli, ánnaqqa zoxu, ayko dkəbʕutu, ḥzāwle, qṭálŭle.’ Háwxawa i+măsalaṯṯe.
contents.versio: 019. FG. Finally, they said Šəmme found the purse, then she gave it to the Xates. She said, ‘Here it is, I found it, now go, wherever you want, find him, kill him!’ Their problem was like so.

contents.textus: 020. IL. Fahəmno.
contents.versio: 020. IL. I understand.

contents.textus: 021. FG. E, Ăḷo, háwxawa. Lo, qamayto i+Maǧo latwa bi+ḥolo, rabbane. Ḥatta mḥele bu+ḥəmyònoste, u+silā̀ḥ lo+qāṯ ebe.
contents.versio: 021. FG. Yes, God, it was like that. No, at first Maǧo had nothing to do with it, poor girl! He even shot at his father-in-law, the weapon didn’t hit him.

contents.textus: 022. IL. Bu+ḥəmyono? Ma u+ḥəmyono, áykowa?
contents.versio: 022. At his father-in-law? His father-in-law, where was he?

contents.textus: 023. FG. ʕAl qarʕe du+qubbūr, maṣəṯwa aʕlayye, qarʕa di+mḏara.
contents.versio: 023. FG. At the top of the turret, he overheard them, the top of the observatory.

contents.textus: 024. IL. Ma, be Xate áykowayne w be šabo ayko?
contents.versio: 024. IL. The Xates were where and the Šabos where?

contents.textus: 025. FG. E, b̥qarši dəḥḏoḏéwayne.
contents.versio: 025. FG. Yes, they were opposite each other.

contents.textus: 026. IL. Raḥúqewayne?
contents.versio: 026. IL. Were they far apart?

contents.textus: 027. FG. Lo! E, raḥúqewayne, e, bu+silā̀ḥ moḥewa ebe (Ăḷo ṭorelux). Hiye yasəq ʕal qarʕe du+qubbūr, maṣəṯwa ʕal u+qarabaləġ. Hiye dməḷḷe, be mənyo. Məd ḥəḷḷe, nafəq hiye, aṯi li… si+goro dbe … hno … d širinḳo. W marfele u+silā̀ḥ aʕle, hiye čəkle ruḥe taḥt u+qubbūr. Dlo mičəkwa taḥt u+qubbūr, qoṭalwa u+Šàbḳoste.
contents.versio: 027. FG. No! Yes, they were far apart, yes, he shot his gun at him (may God forgive you). He went up on top of the turret, he was listening to the hullabaloo. He thought, what is it? When he saw, he left, he came to… by the roof of the Whatsits … the Širinkos. And he shot his weapon at him, he sneaked himself under the turret. If he hadn’t sneaked under the turret, he would have killed Šabḳo as well.

contents.textus: 028. IL. W bəṯr, bəṯr mən hawi? Bəṯr mədəqṭili?
contents.versio: 028. IL. And afterwards, what happened after? After they were killed?

contents.textus: 029. FG. Bəṯr mədəqṭili, hedi qām marǧamme u+ʕamo. W bdalle…
contents.versio: 029. FG. After they were killed, then they up and fined the people. And they started…

contents.textus: 030. IL. Yani, hiye, ele məssəmle? Mahzamle, layko azzé?
contents.versio: 030. IL. Like, he, what did he do? Did he flee, where did he go?

contents.textus: 031. FG. Hiye mahzamle, azzé ltaḥt u+xat.
contents.versio: 031. FG. He fled, he went to ‘under-the-line’.

contents.textus: 032. IL. Taḥt u+xat layko? L Súriya?
contents.versio: 032. IL. ‘Under-the-line’ to where? To Syria?

contents.textus: 033. FG. E. Ma … ṭrele i+aṯto w an+naʕimàyḏeste, kə́twayle tre…tloṯo+naʕime.
contents.versio: 033. FG. Yes. He left his wife and children too, he had two … three children.

contents.textus: 034. IL. I+aṯto, an+naʕime … Ma lo i+aṯto i+Màǧowa?
contents.versio: 034. IL. His wife, the children … Wasn’t his wife Maǧo?

contents.textus: 035. FG. Lo i+Maǧo, lo i+Maǧo, kə́twayle ḥreto, məḏyayto. Mṭole.
contents.versio: 035. FG. Not Maǧo, not Maǧo, he had another one, a Midyatian. He married her.

contents.textus: 036. IL. Ma mṭéwayle hayo li+qriṯo?
contents.versio: 036. IL. Did he bring that one to the village?

contents.textus: 037. FG. E. Mṭole, tlaṯ+əšne, arbaʕ+əšne fayišo háyoste side. W bəṯr u+lalyo dəqṭilile, midile, blile l ʕIwardo. Laʕ+ʕiwarnòyestene tlalle i+aṯto hul ṣafro, w ṣafro qayimi, bari məd nohar, midalle blalle l ʕIwardo. I+ʕaskar mḥalaqla ʕal ʕIwardo. E, u+Skandar dbe Ḥanḳe u+mḥoyo dqāṯle, lo+qāṯ ltə ʔənsanat. Əmmi, ‘Xayifo… e, Ăḷa, ʕal i+măsale du+Šamʕən!’. Əmmi, ‘Ya vega gəmṭatla ya lowa, hárkeyo’. Omar, ‘Ăḷah, latyo harke. Blalle (mṭole, lo lə+mṭole), blole’.
contents.versio: 037. FG. Yes. He brought her, that one stayed three years, four years by his side. And after the night in which he killed them, he took them, he brought them to ʕIwardo. As for the ʕIwardians, they hid the woman until morning, and in the morning they got up before dawn, they took her, they brought her to ʕIwardo. The military pounced upon ʕIwardo. Yes, Skandar Ḥanke, the beating he got no people had ever got. They say, ‘Quickly ... yes, by God, on the matter of Šamʕən!’ They say, ‘Whether you’re going to bring her out now or not, she’s here.’ He says, ‘By God, she is not here. They took her away (he brought her, he did not not bring her), he took her away.’

contents.textus: 038. IL. Bele.
contents.versio: 038. IL. Yes.

contents.textus: 039. FG. E. Hedi blole, w bu+lalyayḏa manḥtole li+Qàməšlo.
contents.versio: 039. FG. Yes. Then he took her, and on that very night he brought her down to Qamishli.

contents.textus: 040. IL. E, bəṯr mi+Qàməšlo?
contents.versio: 040. IL. Yes, after Qamishli?

contents.textus: 041. FG. E, bəṯr mi+Qaməšlo.
contents.versio: 041. FG. Yes, after Qamishli…

contents.textus: 042. IL. Azzewa maḷa ʕÁliste bəṯre dqoṭele?
contents.versio: 042. IL. Mullah ʕAli also went after him to kill him?

contents.textus: 043. FG. E. Karixi aʕle ġắlăbe, e, karixi aʕle ġắlăbe, lo+mḥayṣalle.
contents.versio: 043. FG. Yes. They looked for him a lot, yes, they looked for him a lot, they didn’t catch him.

contents.textus: 044. IL. W me tamo layko azzewa?
contents.versio: 044. IL. And from there, where did he go?

contents.textus: 045. FG. Edí azzé lad+dawal.
contents.versio: 045. FG. Then he went abroad.

contents.textus: 046. IL. Komaṇṇo, herhaldá me tamo, əmmiwa, azzewa l Lubnā́n.
contents.versio: 046. IL. I would say, anyway, from there, they said, he went to Lebanon.

contents.textus: 047. FG. E, žxwá, azzewa támoda, lad+dăwāl, lo+kəḏʕono.
contents.versio: 047. FG. Yes, of course, he went over there, abroad, I don’t know.

contents.textus: 048. IL. W me Lubnā́n, əmmiwa, azzé l Awuṣtralya.
contents.versio: 048. IL. And from Lebanon, they said, he went to Australia.

contents.textus: 049. FG. E, azzewa, azzé. Ánnaqqa ma mede sə́mwalle! U+lalyo dəqṭilile ṣaḥwo čīḳwa, bəṯr mḥalaqle lu+admo, w lu+talgo bam+marziwe.
contents.versio: 049. FG. Yes, he did go, he went. Now then, what a thing they did! The night he killed them it was perfectly clear, afterwards the blood and the snow lept into the downspouts.

contents.textus: 050. IL. Əmmiwa, i+šatayo ġắlăbe aṯiwa talgo.
contents.versio: 050. IL. They said, that year a lot of snow fell.

contents.textus: 051. FG. E, ma talgo! Semoqo!
contents.versio: 051. FG. Yes, what a snowfall! Red!

contents.textus: 052. IL. Talgo semoqo?
contents.versio: 052. IL. Red snow?

contents.textus: 053. FG. E, Ăḷa.
contents.versio: 053. FG.Yes, by God!

contents.textus: 054. IL. Ma talgo semoqo kito?
contents.versio: 054. IL. Is there red snow?
055. FG. Yes, yes.

contents.textus: 056. IL. Yani latyo talgo semoqo. Balki ʕafro aṯi, dəmmina, xud u+tōz ʕam u+talgo.
contents.versio: 056. IL. Like, there isn’t red snow. Probably dust came, let’s say, like powder with the snow.

contents.textus: 057. FG. E, žəxwá, ʕafro, hawxa hawiwa xud u+ʕafro aʕle, əmmi, ‘Semoqo!’
contents.versio: 057. FG. Yes, of course, dust, so it became dustlike upon it, they say, ‘Red!’

contents.textus: 058. IL. Yani, xud əmmat, aṯi ʕafro, tōz, u+tōz aṯi ʕam u+talgo, hawi semoqo yani. Latyo dəmmat, talgo semoqo lo+koṯe, yani.
contents.versio: 058. IL. Like, as you say, along came dust, powder, the powder came with the snow, it became red, like. There isn’t what you say, red snow doesn’t fall, like.

contents.textus: 059. FG. E. Yani, saməqwa mu+admaṯṯe, w mu+hnàṯṯeste, aġlaba əmmiwa, semóqoyo.
contents.versio: 059. FG. Yes. Like, it got red from their blood, and also from their whatsit, mostly they said, ‘It is red’.

contents.textus: 060. IL. W bəṯr rǧəmme i+qriṯo?
contents.versio: 060. IL. And afterwards, did they stone the village?

contents.textus: 061. FG. E, bavó, lah+Halaxiye, lab+Bahwariye.
contents.versio: 061. FG. Yes my dear, Halaxiye and Bahwariye.

contents.textus: 062. IL. E, əmmi u+mede, dsə́mwalle b̥ Kfarze, ban+noše, bas+suryoye.
contents.versio: 062. IL. Yes, they say the thing that they did in Kfarze, to the people, to the Christians.

contents.textus: 063. FG. Ma mede sə́mwalle ínaqqayo. Aḥna zbe emi, lə+mqadàmwalle.
contents.versio: 063. FG. What a thing they did that time! We were at my mother’s, they did not attack it.

contents.textus: 064. IL. Qay?
contents.versio: 064. IL. Why?

contents.textus: 065. FG. Babi sōmwa i+kafḳaṯṯe, be maʕna. Kafḳe, saymiwa kafḳe du+muklo.
contents.versio: 065. FG. My father prepared their foam, innocently. Foam, they made foam for eating.

contents.textus: 066. IL. Kafḳe mənyo?
contents.versio: 066. IL. What is foam?

contents.textus: 067. FG. Kəmmila kafḳe, lo+kəḏʕono.
contents.versio: 067. FG. They call it foam, I don’t know.

contents.textus: 068. IL. Áydarbo kosaymi i+kafḳe du+muklo?
contents.versio: 068. IL. How do they prepare foam for eating?

contents.textus: 069. FG. Saymíwayla hiye w u+mḥasyo du+Malke dbe Afremḳo, a+tre.
contents.versio: 069. FG. They made it, he and the late Malke Afremko, those two.

contents.textus: 070. IL. Ha, yani hani dsaymiwa, balki u+muklàṯṯewa.
contents.versio: 070. IL. Ah, like, these were those who made it, it was probably their food.

contents.textus: 071. FG. E, žəxwá, u+muklaṯṯe. Ánnaqqa, kafḳe, mayo saymiwa aġlaba.
contents.versio: 071. FG. Yes, of course, their food. Now then, foam, they mostly made this kind of thing.

contents.textus: 072. IL. Fahəmno. Hani saymə́nwanne muklo lani doṯənwa li+mʕaziye, komaḥwe.
contents.versio: 072. IL. I understand. These made them food, for these who came to the wake, it appears.

contents.textus: 073. FG. E, e. La+mʕazičiye.
contents.versio: 073. FG. Yes, yes. For the wake guests.

contents.textus: 074. IL. Yani, xud əmmat, hani aščiye, ah+hostawinaṯṯe, dsaymə́nwanne muklo, dobə́nwanne muklo lani dəgdoṯən li+mʕaziye.
contents.versio: 074. IL. Like, as you say, these are cooks, their experts, who prepared food for them, who gave food to those who would come to the wake.

contents.textus: 075. FG. E, e! Aṯən a+mʕazičiye ġắlăbe... Elo Laʕle lo+maqbela lo+doṯən lbabi, w lo lbe… lu+babo di+Faho, w be mxalati Malke, lo+gəšše panək. Wăki a+ḥrene kulle, simə́nwanne barabát.
contents.versio: 075. FG. Yes, yes! Many wake guests came… But Laʕle did not agree that they should come either to my father or to the family of…. to Faho’s father, and cousin Malke’s family, they did not touch those ones. But all the others, they ruined them.

contents.textus: 076. IL. Yani rǧimənne , áydarbo?
contents.versio: 076. IL. Like, they fined them, how?
077. FG. Yes.

contents.textus: 078. IL. W mắsala məqqa šqəlle kallawat mənne?
contents.versio: 078. IL. Question, how much money did they take from them?

contents.textus: 079. FG. Məqqa dəbʕat.
contents.versio: 079. FG. However much you want.

contents.textus: 080. IL. Yani, dəmmina, šqəlle alfo, tralfo…
contents.versio: 080. IL. Like, let’s say, they took a thousand, two thousand…

contents.textus: 081. FG. E, Ăḷa, tlóṯostene, šuqliwa mənne.
contents.versio: 081. FG. Yes, by God! Even three, they took from them.

contents.textus: 082. IL. Ma rǧəmwalle i+qriṯo kula?
contents.versio: 082. IL. They fined the whole village?

contents.textus: 083. FG. E. Bayto lo+ṭrewalle. Kəmmallux, a+tloṯò+bote w bas. Be šəmoḳe, w babi, w u+mḥasyo du+babo du+Nihat. Hani tăne lo+rǧimənne, wăki … kulle.
contents.versio: 083. FG. Yes. They didn’t spare a house. I tell you, three houses and that’s it. The šəmokes, my father, and Nihat’s late father. These alone, they did not fine them. But … all of them.

contents.textus: 084. IL. W əmmi, sə́mwalle ġắlăbe medone pisitiyat bi+ḥoṯo du+šamʕən.
contents.versio: 084. IL. And they say they did many nasty things to šamʕən’s sister.
