contents.textus: 085. FG. Ah, u+mede dsəmme, hayo, hayo lə+kmitaḥke, məlfono.
contents.versio: 085. FG. Ah, what they did, that thing, that thing is left unspoken, teacher.

contents.textus: 086. IL. Áydarbo i+naqlayo suryoyo nošo lo+məǧġəlwa?
contents.versio: 086. IL. Why at that time did no Syriac person speak up?

contents.textus: 087. FG. Ma maǧrənwa?!
contents.versio: 087. FG. Did they dare?!

contents.textus: 088. IL. Yawo, hăma mən towe ṭrowe!
contents.versio: 088. IL. For goodness’ sake, then whatever happens, let it happen!

contents.textus: 089. FG. Lo+maǧrənwa, aḥuno. Qṭíwayle tre+šaqṣat mənne, Ăḷa lo+maǧrənwa fətḥi femayye. E, l Ăḷa, li+mḥasayto di+emo di+Faho … li+ḥmoṯo … mḥalaqla ruḥa ʕal i+mḥasayto di+Səṫṫe, ínaqqa dəmzalṭnalle w hnalle. Ma bʕebra w ʕaǧeba qṭilalle!? Ṗaṗuḳe, híyaste w i+Maǧo, di+ḥòṯoste.
contents.versio: 089. FG. They did not dare, brother. He killed two of their people. By God, they did not dare to open their mouths. Yes, by God, the late mother of Faho … the mother in law … she threw herself upon the late Səṫṫe, when they stripped her and whatsited her. Did they not beat her something awful!? Wretched, she and Maǧo as well, both her and her sister Maǧo.

contents.textus: 090. IL. E. Ma alle məsūč!? Ma látwalle zlamat!?
contents.versio: 090. IL. Yes. What is their fault!? Did they not have husbands!?

contents.textus: 091. FG. Ma a+zlamataṯṯe nəfqiwa!?
contents.versio: 091. FG. Did their husbands go out!?

contents.textus: 092. IL. Hawxa, mənyo hawxa? Áydarbo u+zlām dlo+hne ruḥe ʕal i+ḥurmayḏe?
contents.versio: 092. IL. So, why is it like so? How does the husband not whatsit himself for his wife?

contents.textus: 093. FG. Ăḷa, lo+maǧralle nəfqi me larġul. Lo+maǧralle nəfqi me larġul.
contents.versio: 093. FG. By God, they did not dare to come out from inside. They did not dare to come out from inside.

contents.textus: 094. IL. Haymén wăki látwayne ṭawwe. Towənwa ṭawwe, lo+kṭorənwa, áydarbo kṭorən yani? Yani i+ḥurmayḏe, mən tuyo ṭruyo, áydarbo kṭore?!
contents.versio: 094. IL. Surely then they were not good people. Had they been good, they would not have allowed it, how would they allow it, like? Like, his wife, let whatever happens happen, how would he allow it?!

contents.textus: 095. FG. Lo+maǧrənwa. Lo+maǧrənwa, məlfono, lo+maǧrənwa. Ġắlăbe hawyowa briṯo nuro, e, lo, oṯənwa daq+qəryawoṯe kúlleste, aḥuno, kulle ḥawráyyewayne, hak. Hənnək aṯənwa lu ... oṯənwa lu+māl du+ʕamo, dəblile.
contents.versio: 095. FG. They did not dare. They did not dare, professor, they did not dare. It became very dangerous, yes, no, they also came from all the villages, brother, they were all allies, see. They came for... they came for the people’s property, to take it away.

contents.textus: 096. IL. Aq+qəryawoṯani dḥeḏoráyyeste kulle ḥawráyyewayne?
contents.versio: 096. IL. These villages around them, were all of them their allies?

contents.textus: 097. FG. E! Hwalle ḥawrayye, ṭayúṯowa.
contents.versio: 097. FG. Yes! They were their allies, it was Islam.

contents.textus: 098. IL. Yani bi+zoriye saymiwa, xud əmmat, bi+zoriye?
contents.versio: 098. IL. Like, they did it violently, as you say, violently?

contents.textus: 099. FG. E, Ăḷa, bi+zoriye. Aḷáh, ha maliwa qmu+tarʕo dbe Wurro w hul qmu+tarʕo dbe ... di+anišḳe du+ṭyoro, dəmmina, du+čiqalayḏan, u+ḥa qmu+ḥa, noše lo+maǧrewa nofaq lfeme du+tarʕo. Me larġul lo+nəfqíwayna, Ăḷa!
contents.versio: 099. FG. Yes, by God, violently. By God, it filled up here in front of the Wurros’ door as far as the door of the family… as the corner of the garden, let’s say, of our Čiqal, one after the other, nobody dared to pass the doorframe. We did not come out from inside, by God!

contents.textus: 100. IL. Hawxa kətwa zorayiye?
contents.versio: 100. IL. Was there such violence?

contents.textus: 101. FG. Eeee. E, qṭiwayle, uʕdo quṭlat tre+ṭaye…
contents.versio: 101. FG. Yesss. Yes, he killed, now if you kill two Muslims…

contents.textus: 102. IL. Háwxayo. Məqqa dəmmat, háwxayo. Latyo mede…
contents.versio: 102. IL. It is so. However much you say, it is so. This is not something …

contents.textus: 103. FG. Ma mede, mede sə́mwalle?!
contents.versio: 103. FG. What a thing, a thing they did?!

contents.textus: 104. IL. U+noše lo+qayəm qarši dəṯṯe?
contents.versio: 104. IL. Did people not stand against them?

contents.textus: 105. FG. Lo! Ma, ma maǧrewa!?
contents.versio: 105. FG. No! Did they dare?!

contents.textus: 106. IL. Ma bu+zabnawo Xuri ʕAzī́z latwa bi+qriṯo?
contents.versio: 106. IL. At that time was Xuri ʕAziz not in the village?

contents.textus: 107. FG. Lo, kəmmono.
contents.versio: 107. FG. No, I would say.

contents.textus: 108. IL. Azzewa Xuri ʕAzī́z, latwa harke?
contents.versio: 108. IL. Xuri ʕAziz was gone, wasn’t he here?

contents.textus: 109. FG. E, u+Xuri latwa harke. Kamíwayle arbʕi+yawme lu+barḥmayḏi ... hēš lo+kamiliwa ann+arbʕiyayḏe … Kóhnowa. Lo, u+Xuri latwa harke.
contents.versio: 109. FG. Yes, Xuri wasn’t here. The forty days had been completed for my brother in-law … his forty days had not yet been completed… He was a priest. No, Xuri wasn’t here.

contents.textus: 110. IL. Háqqayo yani, i+măsalaṯe háwxayo …
contents.versio: 110. IL. It is that much, like, the matter is like so…

contents.textus: 111. FG. Háwxawa, háwxawa. E, blalyo həǧmiwa li+Maǧo w li+Səṫṫe.
contents.versio: 111. FG. It was like so, it was like so. Yes, at night they attacked Maǧo and Sətte.

contents.textus: 112. IL. Blalyo?
contents.versio: 112. IL. At night?

contents.textus: 113. FG. E, Ăḷa, blalyo əzzə́nwayla, moḥǝ́nwanne.
contents.versio: 113. FG. Yes, by God, at night they went to her, they battered them.

contents.textus: 114. IL. Ma kowe mede hawxa yani?
contents.versio: 114. IL. Is such a thing possible, like?

contents.textus: 115. FG. Kəmmono, Ăḷa.
contents.versio: 115. FG. I would say, by God.

contents.textus: 116. IL. Áydarbo a+zlamaṯṯe ṭorənwa?
contents.versio: 116. IL. How did their husbands permit it?

contents.textus: 117. FG. W at+tarte bnaʕime, qṭəlle an+naʕimaṯṯe bgawayye.
contents.versio: 117. FG. And the two women were with children, they killed their children within them.

contents.textus: 118. IL. Áydarbo u+ʕamo ṭore, yani, áydarbo ṭore u+medano…
contents.versio: 118. IL. How do people permit it, like, how do they permit this thing ...

contents.textus: 119. FG. E, ba, oho, ma maǧrənwa!?
contents.versio: 119. FG. Yes, would, oh, would they dare!?

contents.textus: 120. IL. E, hăma ṭro məqṭoliwa hǝ́nnəkste, ṭro lo+ṭorənwa.
contents.versio: 120. IL. Yes, then let them be killed as well, they ought not to have permitted it.

contents.textus: 121. FG. Lo, ma lápwalle.
contents.versio: 121. FG. No, they couldn’t.

contents.textus: 122. IL. Yani…
contents.versio: 122. IL. Like…

contents.textus: 123. FG. Ăḷa, u+mede dsəmme appe …, na bixwîna, na bibîna.
contents.versio: 123. FG. By God, the thing they did to them... some things are better left unsaid.

contents.textus: 124. IL. Lo, yani, latwa mede šafiro u+hnano.
contents.versio: 124. IL. No, this whatsit was not a good thing.

contents.textus: 125. FG. Ma latwa, ma, aḥuno, kə́pwalle? Lápwalle, lápwalle.
contents.versio: 125. FG. Wasn’t it, could they, brother? They couldn’t, they couldn’t.

contents.textus: 126. IL. Ínaqlayo komaḥwe be hno, be Xate, ġắlăbe xúrtwayne.
contents.versio: 126. IL. That time, it seems, the Whatsits, the Xates, were very powerful.

contents.textus: 127. FG. E, ba xúrtwayne!? Dlo howənwa hawxa…
contents.versio: 127. FG. Yes, weren’t they powerful!? If they were not so...

contents.textus: 128. IL. Ma ínaqqayo be ḥamḳe w be Smaílo latwa?
contents.versio: 128. IL. That time, the Hamḳes and the Smailos were not?

contents.textus: 129. FG. Lo…
contents.versio: 129. FG. No…

contents.textus: 130. IL. Dəmekki latwa mede biḏayye?
contents.versio: 130. IL. In that case, didn’t they control something?

contents.textus: 131. FG. Lo, tə́mede latwa biḏayye.
contents.versio: 131. FG. No, they did’t control anything.

contents.textus: 132. IL. Kúlmede biḏe dbe Xátewa.
contents.versio: 132. IL. Everything is under the control of the Xates.

contents.textus: 133. FG. E, latwa mede biḏe tanək. Edi məd hanək azzehən w mfarḳo, w hno hežnú hani hawən də bandiye, be Smaílo w be ḥamḳe.
contents.versio: 133. FG. Yes, those ones did not control anything. Then, after those ones went away and it settled down, from then on they became two parties, the Smailos and the Hamkes.

contents.textus: 001. Dawәd lebe dməryo, Dawәd lebe dməryo, Dawәd lebe dməryo málkowa, e, Ăḷa … hno. Ánnaqqa kə́twayle arbʕi+niše.
contents.versio: 001. God’s favourite David (lit. ‘David, the Lord’s heart’), God’s favourite David, God’s favourite David was a king, right, Gosh ... whatsit. Now then, he had forty wives.

contents.textus: 002. Ŭ Urí u+xwarzàyḏewa. Uriyo u+xwarzàyḏewa.
contents.versio: 002. And Uri was his nephew (i.e., his sister’s son).  It’s Uri, he was his nephew.

contents.textus: 003.Ha i+qriṯaṯe duʕdo aṯutu, i+qriṯayo d Uriyo. Daṯutu hawxa áʕlada daṯutu larke, i+qriṯo kəmmina Xrabé Huriya, i+qriṯo d Uriyo. Əšma uʕdo Xrabé Huríyayo, d Úriwa, u+xwarz dmalko Dawәd lebe dməryo, u+xwarzàyḏewa.
contents.versio: 003. That there village through which you have now come, this village is Uri’s. The one via which you so came when you came here, the village we call Xerabê Hurîya, it’s Uri’s village. Now its name is Xerabê Hurîya, it was Uri’s, God’s favourite King David’s nephew, he was his nephew.

contents.textus: 004. Kə́twayle ṗire bәḥḏo+ʕayno, ŭ l Dawәd lebe dməryo kə́twayle arbʕi, arbʕi.
contents.versio: 004. He had a one-eyed wife, and God’s favourite David had forty, forty.

contents.textus: 005. Ŭ azzə́n lu+ḥarb l Galyé Košana, harke kəmmi Galyé Košana. Azzé lu+ḥarb, lan+năyā̀r. Ŭ ánnaqqa koqoṭal, i+ʕaskărayḏe koquṭlo, noše laybe ʕal Uri. Koquṭli.
contents.versio: 005. And they went to war, to Koshana Ravine, here they call it Koshana Ravine. He went to war against the enemy. And now then he kills, his army kills, nobody can prevail against Uri. They kill.

contents.textus: 006. U+màlkoste saləq li+goro (latyo domar ḥa haqqa, elo kəmmutu). E, ga kalkó i+ṗire ḥayfo, i+barṯo … i+ṗire d Uri koḥayfo, bәḥḏo+ʕàynowa. Marfele ʕayne eba. Marfele ʕayne eba.
contents.versio: 006. As for the king, he went up to the roof (no one ought to say so much, but you’re asking). Right, over here his wife is bathing, the daughter ... the wife of Uriah is bathing, she was one-eyed. He cast his eyes on her. He cast his eyes on her.

contents.textus: 007. Mtarasle, omar, ‘Tux lu+bayto’. Omar, ‘Tux lu+bayto’. Mtarássalle,  ǝmmi, ‘Tux lu+bayto’.
contents.versio: 007. He sent for him, he says, ‘Come home’. He says, ‘Come home’. They sent for him, they say, ‘Come home’.

contents.textus: 008. Aṯi lu+bayto. Hule sōz ʕam aḥ+ḥaw<ronayḏe> … mdayšanne lu+baxyo, əmmi, ‘G̊ʶquṭlilan?’ Omar, ‘Sōzyo, lǝ+gnoḥatno mʕal i+səsto’. KSozá meré bareK ŭ meqəm ǝmmiwa ‘sōz’ xălā́ṣ. Lo+ḥoraw u+sōz. Azzeyo, omar, ‘Sōz, lə+gnoḥatno mʕal i+səsto’.
contents.versio: 008. He was coming home. He made a promise to his fri<ends> … they started crying, they say, ‘Will they kill us?’ He says, ‘It’s a promise, I won’t get off the horse’. KThe word of the people of yesteryearK and formerly they used to say ‘a promise’, that’s it. He doesn’t spoil the promise. He went, he says, ‘It’s a promise, I won’t get off the horse’.

contents.textus: 009. Hedik̇a, lo+naḥət mʕal i+səsto. ‘Mənyo, mǝn hnoyo?’ əmmi, ‘Sǝmlan i+beriyayḏux, nḥat flān korǝḥmínalux’. ‘Lo’, omar, ‘Huli sōz ʕam aḥ+ḥawronayḏi, lə+gnoḥatno’.
contents.versio: 009. Then, he didn’t get off the horse. ‘What is this? What’s the whatsit?’, they say, ‘we missed you, come down, etc, we love you!’ ‘No’, he says, ‘I made a promise to my friends, I won’t get off’.

contents.textus: 010. Hedik̇a sə́mlale beʕe bi+nuqro kəmmina, ŭ ṣədla ha hawxa ʕam gab i+səsto.
contents.versio: 010. Then, she (i.e., his wife) made him some eggs in a frying pan, as we say, and she held it like so (i.e., for him to eat) at the horse’s side.

contents.textus: 011. Xile. Omar, ‘Ko, mašqeno u+sayfayḏux, mašqeno u+sayfayḏux, i+rəmḥayḏux mašqena’. Hedik̇a azzé gab qənaġčiye, mbasmaḷḷe i+k̇alane ŭ i+šəlfk̇e bәḥḏoḏe.
contents.versio: 011. He ate. (Someone) says, ‘Come on, I’ll sharpen your sword, I’ll sharpen your sword, your spear, I’ll sharpen it’. Then he went to a quartermaster’s office, he nailed the sheath and the blade together.

contents.textus: 012. Ánnaqqa aṯi, lo+ḥǝḷḷe eba, maḥatle qәm ḥaṣe. Ŭ xile ab+beʕayḏe, ŭ ṭləble xaṭər mənne, ŭ ‘Ḥay Aḷḷah!’ Azzé l Galyé Košana.
contents.versio: 012. Now then, he came back, he didn’t look at it, and he put it on his back. And he ate his eggs, took his leave from them, and ‘Goodbye!’ He went to Koshana Ravine.

contents.textus: 013. Azzé bayn aḥ+ḥawronayḏe, mzaraṭle, hule qirat, ‘Tlawu iḏo, kaṯino’. Komōd lu… lu+sayfayḏe, koḥoyar kalé mbasmro.
contents.versio: 013. He went to his friends, he swaggered, he gave them courage, ‘Keep fighting (lit. ‘hold up the hand’), I have come!’ He reaches for … for his sword, he sees, hey, it’s nailed in.

contents.textus: 014. Komar, ‘Waaay, way aʕli, ʕal i+ḥṭiṯayḏi. Ono ḥoli hawxa səmle‿bi. Ánnaqqa šān ma‿kʶqoṭanno aqqasani, šān ma‿ksōmno u+ḥarb?’
contents.versio: 014. He says, ‘Woooe, woe is me, for my sins. Me, it’s my uncle who did so to me. Now then, for whom am I killing all these people (lit. ‘these however many’), for whom I am waging the war?’

contents.textus: 015. Naqqa+ḥreto i+ġirayḏe lә+mtaḥmela ḥəngi. An+naʕime dəšše ʕal rafšo dgamlo, šləḥle i+polk̇e di+gamlo, qṭile hul dəmmat bas bi+polk̇e di+gamlo. Qṭile bi+polk̇e di+gamlo, i+ḥarayto omar, ‘Bas’, ha səmle hawxa.
contents.versio: 015. Once more, he couldn’t stand (lit. ‘his passion wouldn’t bear’) so much. The servants (lit. ‘children’) had trampled on the scapula of a camel, he stripped off the camel’s shoulder blade, he killed until you cry ‘uncle’ (lit. ‘until you say “Enough!”’) with the camel’s shoulder blade. He killed with the camel’s shoulder blade, finally he says ‘Enough!’, he did just like so.

contents.textus: 016. Omar, ‘Sōzyo ʕam Aloho lo+gmaxǝṇṇo admo mǝnxu. Toxu qṭáluli!’ Qām qṭǝlle. Aṯən qṭəlle, k̇ăzā́b šawútiwayne. Qṭəlle, kalé u+qawrayḏe b Galyé Košana.
contents.versio: 016. He says, ‘It’s a promise to God, I won’t shed any (more) blood from you. Come kill me!’ They up and killed him. They came and killed him, they felt sorry for him (lit. ‘they were burned guts’). They killed him, his grave is over there in Koshana Ravine.

contents.textus: 017. E, ánnaqqa aṯi u+malaxo, mə́ḷḷele l Dawәd̥. Omar, ‘Dawәd̥, lebe dməryo!’ Omar, ‘Mənyo?’ Omar, ‘Uʕdo d̥ḥa howele arbʕi+riše dәʕwone, lowalle k̇emayiye, u+ǧiranayḏe howele ḥḏo bḥa+bezo. Mətḥasad li+ʕwonayo d̥kətyo b̥ḥa+bezo. Ḥaq diḏe mənyo?’
contents.versio: 017. Right, now then, the angel came, he spoke to David. He said, ‘God’s favourite David!’  He says, ‘What is it?’ He says, ‘Now, if someone has forty head of sheep, they don’t have any faults, his neighbor has a single one with one teat. He is envious of that sheep, who’s with one teat. What is his just deserts?’

contents.textus: 018. Omar, ‘Ḥaq diḏe rúġzoyo!’ Omar, ‘Ḥur ʕul me qarʕux!’  Naqqa ag+gulok̇at di+nuro hawxa konuḥti mi+šmayo. Aḏəʕ, omar, ‘Ya mōr, ḥaṭino’. Kali u+ruġzo.
contents.versio: 018. He says, ‘Wrath is his just deserts!’ He says, ‘Look above your head!’. At once balls of fire accordingly come down from the sky. He understood, he says, ‘Oh Lord, I have sinned’. The wrath ceased.

contents.textus: 019. Omar, ‘G̥ḥəfrat arbʕi+darġe taḥt i+arʕo ŭ gmolat aʕlayye qaṭmo, qaṣmono, ŭ kul+yawmo gmašiġat ḥa mənne bad+damʕe dʕaynux’.
contents.versio: 019. He says, ‘You’ll dig forty steps underground and fill them up with ashes, cinders, and each day you’ll wash one of them with the tears of your eyes’.

contents.textus: 020. Naḥət, ftəḥle arbʕi+darġe taḥt i+arʕo ŭ mlele ʕal ann+arbʕi qaṣmono. Ŭ kul+yawmo mašəġwa ḥa mənne bad+damʕe, bad+damʕayḏe dboxewa ʕal a+ḥṭohayḏe.
contents.versio: 020. He went down, he exposed (lit. ‘opened’) forty steps underground and filled the forty up with cinders. And each day he would wash one of them with tears, with his tears that he would cry for his sins.

contents.textus: 021. Omar, ‘Ánnaqqa zux ʕal u+qawro d Urí dәmfaḥelux, šmiṭoyo’ (be áykowa lo+kuḏʕono). Əzzewa hul Galyé Košana, azzé ʕal u+qawrayḏe, boxewa. Tarte+kore azzé, lə+mtanele. Da+tlaṯ+kore azzeyo, omar, ‘Kobaʕno sămaḥa minux’.
contents.versio: 021. He says, ‘Now then, go onto Uriah’s grave for him to forgive you, barefoot’ (wherever it was, I don’t know). He would go to Koshana Ravine, he went onto his grave, he would cry. Two times he went, he didn’t answer. On the third time he went, he says, ‘I want forgiveness from you’.

contents.textus: 022. Aṯi qolo mu+qawro, omar, ‘Mšiḥo msamaḥ’. Háwoste lo+kәmsamàḥwayle.
contents.versio: 022. A voice came from the grave, it says, ‘It is Christ who forgives’. As for that one, he wasn’t forgiving him.

contents.textus: 023. Omar ḥzele bu+ḥəlmo, hak̇a dahərí, ḥzele tre+malaxe mqatalle, mḥalaqqe a+tre+malaxe li+gihano. Zayәʕ̥. Omar, omar, ‘Ḥolo, Mšiḥo msamaḥlux!’
contents.versio: 023. He says he saw (either) in the dream, or a vision, he saw two angels had fought, they threw the two angels into Hell. He became afraid. He says, he says, ‘Uncle, may Christ forgive you!’

contents.textus: 024. Háwoste, háwoste ḥzeli, hawxa mə́rralli. Haṯe yani…hawxa mə́rralli. Hawxa šamiʕalla, balki … hawxa šamiʕono.
contents.versio: 024. As for that one, as for that one I saw it, they told me so. This, like… they told me so. I heard it so, maybe … I heard so.

contents.textus: 001. Yáwseβwa, Yáwseβwa, čəkke bu+gubo. Yáwseβwa hawo. U+abro d Yáḥqubwa, kəḏʕutu?
contents.versio: 001. It was Joseph, it was Joseph, [whom] they threw into a cistern. That one was Joseph. He was Jacob’s son, do you know?

contents.textus: 002. U+abro d Yáḥqubwa, kə́twayle traḥṣar+aḥunone. Hənnək ʕəṣro dṗírewayne, w tre – Benyamən w Yawsef - dəḥḏówayne.
contents.versio: 002. He was Jacob’s son, he had twelve brothers. Ten of them were from a wife, and two – Benjamin and Joseph – were from another one.

contents.textus: 003. E, ánnaqqa məḷḷe, ‘Ḥzeli ḥulmo, traḥṣar+kəkwe kosuġdi lkəkwo’. Ann+aḥunone makuwe gawo mine, əmmi, ‘Hawo hatat?’
contents.versio: 003. Yes, once he said, ‘I had a dream, twelve stars are bowing down to a star’. The brothers grew jealous of him, they say, ‘Are you that one?’

contents.textus: 004. (Yani ṭowo lo+kəḏʕàllaste, elo bele hani kmo+kore kəmmi lquli.)
contents.versio: 004. (Like, I still don’t know it well, even though they indeed told it these however many times in my presence.)

contents.textus: 005. Hediḳa mbele ʕrayto dann+aḥunone.
contents.versio: 005. Then, he brought his brothers’ lunch.

contents.textus: 006. Maḥatte bu+gubo, maḥatte bu+gubo, azzeyo w mədde i+qeməstayḏe, mədde i+qeməstayḏe, mgamblalle bayn u…bayn u+admo, bayn u+hno, nḥərre ṣafuro.
contents.versio: 006. They threw him into a pit, they threw him into a pit, and then they took his shirt, they took his shirt, they smeared it in… in blood, in the whatsit, they slaughtered a kid.

contents.textus: 007. Məṛṛe, ‘Lu+dewo xile’. Məḷḷa, ‘Ašə́r reḥe ddewo lo+koṯe mine. Dúgleyo’.
contents.versio: 007. They said, ‘A wolf ate him’. She said, ‘Really, the scent of a wolf isn’t coming from it. It is a lie’.

contents.textus: 008. Mrastaq u+karwan aʕle. Mrastaq karwan, bazərgā́n, aʕle. Mofaqqe mu+gubo w mballe li+walaye d Məṣər, mzabanne. (Šamiʕútəlla?) Mzabanne.
contents.versio: 008. The caravan came upon him. A caravan, a merchant and his entourage, came upon him. They took him out of the pit and brought him to the city of Cairo, they sold him. (Have you heard of it?) They sold him.

contents.textus: 009. Azzé qmiḏe+du+malko xud u+greʕo. I+ṗire du+malko maḥatla niqe bəqḏole.
contents.versio: 009. He went into the possession of the king as a servant. The king’s wife slandered him.

contents.textus: 010. Məḷḷe, ‘Ašə́r, lo+konoṭaṇṇo’. Elo məḷḷe w azzé, čəkle bu+ḥappəs. Čəkle bu+ḥappəs tloṯo+yawme.
contents.versio: 010. [The king] said, ‘Really, I wouldn’t expect it’. But she said it and he went, he stuck him in prison. He put him in prison for three days.

contents.textus: 011. Omar, omar, omar, ‘Lo+ṭoʕatli’. Ma+tloṯo+yawme hawi tlaṯ+šnaye. ʕAl domar ‘lo+ṭoʕatli’, hawi tlaṯ+šnaye. Hawi tlaṯ+šnaye bu+gubo… bu+ḥappəs.
contents.versio: 011. He says, he says, he says, ‘Don’t forget me’. From three days it became three years. Because he said ‘don’t forget me’, it became three years. It became three years in the pit… in prison.

contents.textus: 012. Naqqa ḥa omar, ‘Ḥzeli ḥəlmo’. Omar, ‘Ḥzeli ḥəlmo w kaleyo baṣro ʕal qarʕi, kəmzabanne’. Omar, ‘Ašə́r, ṣafro gəm…qquṭlilux’.
contents.versio: 012. Someone once says, ‘I had a dream’. He says, ‘I had a dream, and there’s meat on my head, I am selling it’. He says, ‘Really, tomorrow they will put … they will kill you’.

contents.textus: 013. Ḥa omar, ‘Ḥzeli laḥmo ʕal qarʕi’ Hawo bi+loqàntawa’. Mballe ʕal u+šuġlayḏe.
contents.versio: 013. Someone said, ‘I saw bread on my head’. That one used to be in a restaurant. They took him back at his job.

contents.textus: 014. Azzé… hawi… yani ṭowo lo+kəḏʕono. Dísane lu+malko məḷḷe, ‘Ḥzeli ḥəlmo’. Məṛṛe, ‘Ăḷa, kīt ḥa bu+ḥappəs košoraḥ aḥ+ḥəlmone’. ‘Ha, Yáwseβyo’.
contents.versio: 014. He went… it happened… like, I don’t know it well. Once more the king said, ‘I had a dream’. They said, ‘By God, there is someone in prison who interprets dreams’. ‘Aha, it is Joseph’.

contents.textus: 015. Azzé, mṭalle. Omar, ‘Kito… ḥzeli šwaḥ+šəble, šəblo zaʕīf xila šwaḥ+šəble dḥeṭe taqine.
contents.versio: 015. He went, they brought him. He says, ‘There is…I saw seven ears of grain, a thin ear ate seven thick ears.

contents.textus: 016. Ḥzeli tərto zaʕīf, xila šwaḥ+tawroṯe taqine’. Omar, ‘Ašə́r gdoṯe šwaḥ+šnaye’.
contents.versio: 016. I saw a thin cow, she ate seven fat cows’. He says, ‘Really, there will come seven years’.

contents.textus: 017. Edi bdele … Huwe a+qliḏe di+hno biḏe, bdele baʕ+ʕanebər, mlele aʕ+ʕanebər d Məṣər kulle ḥeṭe.
contents.versio: 017. Then he began … they put the keys to the whatsit into his hand, he started with the granaries, he filled all the granaries of Egypt with wheat.

contents.textus: 018. Mlalle ḥeṭe, w aṯi šato hno, w sə́mmalle məqqa dsəmme lu+malko, lo, lo+sawəʕ. Məqqa dsə́mmalle laḥmo, lo+sawəʕ, məqqa dsə́mmalle laḥmo, lo+sawəʕ. Sə́mmalle qursḳe dqaṭmo, xile háwoste w lo+sawəʕ.
contents.versio: 018. He filled them with wheat, and a whatsit year came, and they made for the king however much they made for him, no, he didn’t get full. However much bread they made for him, he didn’t get full, however much bread they made for him, he didn’t get full. They made him an ash cake, he ate that one too and he didn’t get full.

contents.textus: 019. Omar, ‘Minux fənyo, aʕlux kulyo’, mḥalaqle bu+šabòḳoda, mḥalaqle. Omar, ‘Minux fənyo aʕlux kulyo’.
contents.versio: 019. Someone says, ‘What goes around, comes around’, he tossed him out the window, he tossed him out. He says, ‘What goes around, comes around’.

contents.textus: 020. Aṯyo i+šato di+ġala, w ánnaqqa ele ftəḥle aʕ+ʕanebər, hule laf+faqire, ha-ha, ha-ha, ha-ha, hule laf+faqire.
contents.versio: 020. The year of the famine came, and at that point he opened the granaries, he gave it to the poor, here, here, and here, he gave it to the poor.

contents.textus: 021. Kalé yawmo ʕal i+goro, ḥzele ann+aḥunone baliqi. Ḥzele, ann+aḥunone baliqi. Məḷḷe laṗ+ṗirat, məḷḷe, ‘Sumu muklo, kalkaṯi karwan, faqire, duxli’.
contents.versio: 021. This one day on the rooftop, he saw, his brothers had appeared. He saw, his brothers had appeared. He said to the women, he said, ‘Make food, a caravan is coming, poor ones, to eat’.

contents.textus: 022. Aṯən, blile lu+muklo, muklile w maštəlle.
contents.versio: 022. They came, he brought them to the food, he gave them food and drink.

contents.textus: 023. W hiye hiye koḏaʕʕe, hənnək lo+kuḏʕile. Hənnək maḥatte bu+gubo w hiye hawi malko.
contents.versio: 023. And he, he does recognize them, but they do not recognize him. They had put him in the pit but he became a king.

contents.textus: 024. Hēs̠te kəmmi, ‘K_Xudiyé ṣabré_K (bi+kurmanǧi) K_malaḳé Məṣré_K’. Kəmmi, ‘U+nošo dhowele ṣabr, ktowe u+malko d Mawṣal’.
contents.versio: 024. They still say, ‘The possessor of patience (in Kurmanji) is King of Egypt’. They say, ‘The one who has patience becomes King of Mosul’.

contents.textus: 025. Edi xəḷḷe w štalle, w mlele aṭ+ṭaʕnaṯṯeste, lo+ṣədle kallawat.
contents.versio: 025. Then they ate and drank, and he also filled their loads, he would not take any money.

contents.textus: 026. Omar, ‘Ma áydarbo hatu?’ Flān behvān. ‘E, kətlan aḥu … babo samyo, w kətlan aḥuno, əšme Benyámenyo’.
contents.versio: 026. He says, ‘How are you?’ So on and so forth. ‘Yes, we have a blind bro … father, and we have a brother, his name is Benyamin’.

contents.textus: 027. Omar, ‘Lázəmyo dəmṭutu u+aḥunàwoste. Ánnaqqa doṯutu, mṭéwulle. Dlo+mṭùtəlle, lo+kobènanxu muklo’.
contents.versio: 027. He said, ‘You must bring that brother as well. When you come, bring him. If you do not bring him, I won’t give you any food’.

contents.textus: 028. Hawo u+aḥunàyḏewa ánnaqqa. Əmmi, ‘Ăḷo lə+gbelan, baban lə+gbelan’. Omar, ‘Lazəm. Dləmṭútəlle, komaṇṇo litux!’
contents.versio: 028. That one was then his brother. They say, ‘By God, he won’t give him to us, our father won’t give him to us’. He said, ‘It is necessary. If you don’t bring him, I say, don’t come!’

contents.textus: 029. Azzehən, azzehən. E, tām u+muklaṯṯe. Səmme lo+səmme, əmmi, ‘Ašə́r lo+kəzzano’. “Ašə́r’, komar, “dlo+mṭutu aḥunayxu…”’
contents.versio: 029. They left, they left. Yes, their food finished. They tried and tried, they say, ‘Really, we won’t go. “Really”, he says, “if you don’t bring your brother…”’

contents.textus: 030. Omar, ‘Haa haay! Zrəʕxu, mṣakarxu Yawsef, kəbʕutu mṣakrutu Benyámənste. Ăḷa lə+gbenànxuyo’. Hul dhawən šapərzá.
contents.versio: 030. He says, ‘Aha! You dropped, you lost Joseph, you want to lose Benjamin too. By God, I shall not give him to you’. Until they became miserable.

contents.textus: 031. A+bnoṯemmi, ‘Yabo, ma gmamṯat kəfla ʕal šaqṣ? Hăma háwweyo!’ Qām mṭele, mṭele.
contents.versio: 031. The daughters say, ‘Dad, will you cause a family to die for someone? Then give him to them!’ He up and brought him, he brought him.

contents.textus: 032. Disa hawi waxt d, doṯən, saləq li+goro, nqəḥle. Nqəḥle. Aṯi reḥe du…reḥe du+aḥuno.
contents.versio: 032. Once again it became the time when they come, he went up to the roof, he sniffed. He sniffed. Along came the scent of… the scent of his brother.

contents.textus: 033. Aṯi ánnaqqa, ṣə́dlalle qadr w maʕrifa. W húlalle muklo, mlele aṭ+ṭaʕnaṯṯe zād.
contents.versio: 033. At that point he came, he paid them all due respect. And he gave them food, he filled their loads with grain.

contents.textus: 034. W u+kosayḏe du+semo maḥatle bu+xurǧo du+aḥuno.
contents.versio: 034. And he put his silver cup into his brother’s saddle bag.

contents.textus: 035. W gyotaw gabe w hnele. W hənnək lo+kuḏʕile. Hediḳa əmmi dəbʕi qaymi maṭəʕni.
contents.versio: 035. And he sits next to him and whatsited. And they do not recognize him. Then they say they want to start loading.

contents.textus: 036. Omar, ‘Ăḷo, u+kosayḏan lə+gmaḥwe! Kraxu harke w tamhó, kraxu!’ Kuzzə́n məfqile mi…mu+koso (ele maḥátwayle d Benyamen) ‘Ha, gnulux u+kosayḏi! Ašə́r mǧázyohat, lə+gbenux, lo+koṭoreno dəmblilux’.
contents.versio: 036. He says, ‘By God, our cup isn’t showing up! Search over here and over there, search!’ They go take it from the saddle bag…. (he had put it in Benjamin’s). ‘Aha, you stole my cup! Really, you ought to be punished, I won’t give you up, I won’t let them take you’.

contents.textus: 037. Ánnaqqa kofətli w duʕri ḥeḏr i+walaye w saymi … əmmi, ‘Ăḷo, lo+kəzzano, baban qqoṭelan’.
contents.versio: 037. At that point they make a circle around the city and return and they do … they say, ‘By God, we shall not go, our father will kill us’.

contents.textus: 038. I+ḥarayto edi maḏəʕle ruḥe appe, omar, ‘Ono Yáwsef̬no. Kalá i+čaffiyayḏi, mbālla, hāwla lbabi. Gmoḥela bʕayne dməftoḥi. W toxu hatu, mṭewu babi, aḥwoṯi, w toxu mṭāwlan, toxu larke’. Edi azzehən.
contents.versio: 038. Finally, Joseph then revealed himself to them, he says, ‘I am Joseph. Here is my headdress, take it, give it to my father. He will touch it to his eyes so they open. And you come back, bring my father, my sisters, and come bring them to us, come here’. Then they went away.

contents.textus: 039. Kul tre+xabre gdomarwa la+bnoṯe, ‘De zox nqaḥu, be koṯe reḥe d Benyamen, lo?’ Əmmiwa, ‘Ăḷa yabo gdəmmina xabro, lo lo+məqḥorat’. ‘Mənyo?’ Omar, ‘Reḥe d Benyamen lo+koṯe, le reḥe d Yawsef koṯe’. Eli+čaffiyayḏe məṭyówalle.
contents.versio: 039. Every other second, he kept saying to his daughters, ‘Come on, go smell whether it smells of Benjamin, no?’ They kept saying, ‘By God, Dad, we shall say something, but don’t get angry’. ‘What is it?’ They say, ‘It doesn’t smell of Benjamin, but it does smell of Joseph’. For they had brought back his headdress.

contents.textus: 040. Mṣaʕárwalle, omarwa, ‘Áydarbo? Hani arbʕi+šnaye Yawsef mṣakar, reḥe koṯe? W Benyamen hani arbʕi+yawme’.
contents.versio: 040. He was scolding them, saying, ‘How? These forty years Joseph has been lost, it smells of him? And Benjamin, these forty days’.

contents.textus: 041. Bi+ḥarayto edi aṯi, edi húwalle bəšra w mḥalle i…i+čafyayo bʕayne, ftiḥi. W edi maṭʕanne w azzehən hə́nnəkəstene.
contents.versio: 041. Finally, he then came, then they brought him the good news and they put that headdress on his eyes, they opened. And then they packed up and went, they too.

contents.textus: 042. Ánnaqqa áydarbo ktowe? Azzə́n li+qamaytayḏe, mxamalle manduriye (manduriye, kefo, ha hawxa, ha hawxa ḥləmto, ha hawxa mandrí<w>ayna meqəm ann+igore. Naqqa dlatwa čimanto mandríwayna ann+igore eba).
contents.versio: 042. Now then, how does it go? They went to meet him, they dressed up a roller (a roller, a stone, like so, so thick, like so we formerly used to level roofs. When there was no cement we used to level roofs with it).

contents.textus: 043. Mxamalle manduriye hawxa w maḥattalle bi+qamaytayḏe. Maḥatte i+ṣərto d Yawsef aʕla.
contents.versio: 043. They dressed up a roller like so and set it out to meet him. They put Joseph’s picture on it.

contents.textus: 044. Qbiḏole qəm ṣadre, i+kefayo. Kəmmi faširo hul dbaxi. Nafəq henuḳa me bəṯr u+šuro, məḷḷe, ‘Yabo, kalí’.
contents.versio: 044. He clasped it to his breast, that stone. They say it melted until he cried. At that moment he came out from behind the wall, he said, ‘Dad, here I am’.

contents.textus: 045. Hawxa háyostene. Hawxa šamiʕalla, balki kiba ġálteste. Hawxa šamiʕono iqṣa d Yawsef. Ánnaqqa he kəmmi, ‘K_Xudiyé ṣabré malaḳé Məṣré_K’. šqile ṣabər. Hawxa.
contents.versio: 045. Such is that one as well. I heard it like so, maybe it also has mistakes. I heard the story of Joseph like so. Now then, they still say, ‘The possessor of patience is King of Egypt’. He demonstrated patience. Like so.

contents.textus: 1. Dəlo ŭ Falak̇o aḥunónewayne. Dəlo ŭ Falak̇o aḥunónewayne, ŭ i+qriṯo kula əmmíwayla Be Dərra.
contents.versio: 1. Dilo and Falako were brothers. Dilo and Falako were brothers, and they used to call the whole village the Dirra family.

contents.textus: 2. Hanək, noše lo+qudriwa ʕal a+tranək.
contents.versio: 2. Those ones, no one could prevail over those two.

contents.textus: 3. A+tre … gabórewayne.
contents.versio: 3. Both of them … were strongmen.

contents.textus: 4. Gabórewayne, lo+qudriwa, i+qriṯo kula lo+qudrowa aʕlayye.
contents.versio: 4. They were strongmen, they couldn’t, the whole village couldn’t prevail over them.

contents.textus: 5. ‘Məs‿saymina, məd‿dəmmina?’ Ḥa sowo, dəmmina xoṯi, dəmmina, sowo, omar, ‘Lapxu aʕlayye, hul dlobútənne barṯo me dəṯxu.
contents.versio: 5. ‘What’ll we do, what’ll we say?’ An old man, let’s say like me, let’s say, an old one, says, ‘You can’t beat them (lit. ‘can’t be over them’), unless you give them a daughter of yours.

contents.textus: 6. I+barṯo hak̇a qadiro aʕlayye ... naxxa lo+kowe’. (Xud Šəmšun Gaboro, məḷḷə́lxuyo hayo.)
contents.versio: 6. The daughter, if she were to prevail over them ... otherwise, it won’t happen’. (Like the story of the hero Samson, I told you that one.)

contents.textus: 7. Qām, məs‿saymi? Mərre lk̇ačk̇e me diḏan … dəṯṯe, d̥kətwa šafərto. Malwáššalla ǧule xúššək̇at. Əmmi, ‘Zax ŭ itax ḥeḏorayye, mbasamme, ŭ ṣaʕár elan, balki ṭəlbilax’.
contents.versio: 7. Then, what do they do? They told one of our girls … theirs, who was pretty. They dressed her in beautiful clothes. They say, ‘Come and go (lit. ‘go and come’) around them, please them, and insult us, maybe they’ll accept you’.

contents.textus: 8. Veǧa lwəšla ǧule xúššək̇at, ŭ azzá ŭ aṯyo ḥeḏorayye.
contents.versio: 8. Then she put on beautiful clothes, and she came and went around them.

contents.textus: 9. Mṣaʕáḷḷalle ŭ mqatela mm... mqatlowa ʕam ab+be babayḏa, əmmowa, ‘Gunah də́ṯxuyo’.
contents.versio: 9. She insulted them and she fought with… she would fight with her father’s family, she would say, ‘This is your fault’.

contents.textus: 10. Ŭ əzzawa ŭ əṯyowa, ‘Ḥaylayxún Ăḷo! B̥xēr aṯutu!’ Səmla ŭ maḥatla ruḥa ǧəlá šəl aʕmayye. ‘Mənyo, mən loyo?’
contents.versio: 10. And she would come and go, ‘May God give you strength! Welcome!’ She clung to them like a wet shirt (lit. ‘she made and put herself wet clothing-wise with them’, i.e., to trick them into trusting her). ‘What is it (lit. ‘what is it, what isn’t it)?’

contents.textus: 11. U+Falak̇o oḏaʕwa, u+ràbowa. U+Dəlo naʕímowa, ǧehəlwa. Marfele ʕayne eba.
contents.versio: 11. Falak̇o would know, he was the older one. Dilo was the younger one, he was ignorant. He set his eye on her.

contents.textus: 12. Omar, ‘Ašə́r gəmbaraxna. Gmohaṇṇa’ — ‘Yămā́n, daxī́l! I+barṯo dan+nayaryo’. Səәәmle, lo+səmle, omar, ‘Lo! Gəmbaraxna’.
contents.versio: 12. He says, ‘Really, I’ll bless (i.e., marry) her. I’ll marry her (i.e., in the Muslim fashion)’. — ‘Mercy, help! She’s the enemies’ daughter’. Whatever he did (lit. ‘he did, he didn’t do’), he says, ‘No! I’ll marry her’.

contents.textus: 13. ‘Kәmṣaʕro lab+be babe ŭ kohno... korəḥmolan’.
contents.versio: 13. ‘She insults her father’s family and she whatsits… she likes us’.

contents.textus: 14. Qām, məṭyole, mhirole. Ánnaqqa maḥatla ruḥa bi+qeməstaṯṯe. Kə́twalle tart‿aḥwòṯeste.
contents.versio: 14. Then, he brought her back, he married her. Now then, she put herself in their guise (lit. ‘shirt’). They also had two sisters.

contents.textus: 15. Ŭ ánnaqqa g̊ḥayfalle ŭ mašiġalle ŭ saymalle muklone basime ŭ...
contents.versio: 15. And now then, she would bathe them, do the washing for them, cook delicious meals for them, and...

contents.textus: 16. Axər komnad̥fo lawġul, ŭ axər b̥xabrayye. ‘Ḥaylayxún Ăḷo, b̥xer aṯutu’. Hoool dәmġaflila, ḥašša, hul dhawyo ... (hátuste xud aḥunoni) ... hawyo b̥ṭaʕno. Hawyo b̥ṭaʕno, ṭʕino.
contents.versio: 16. Finally, she is cleaning inside, and finally by their word (i.e., she does). ‘God is your strength, welcome!’ Until she made them inattentive, pardon, until she became… (you are like my brothers)… she became pregnant. She became pregnant, she was pregnant.

contents.textus: 17. Məd d̥ṭʕino, hedik̇a yawmo kočəmzo ruḥa, kuyo bemáʕd. Komar, ‘Qay, mə‿ḥăwā́l díḏaxyo?’ Kəmmo, ‘Aḥunux ǧġīl aʕmi’. ‘Əəəəmmm’. ‘Aḥunux ǧġīl aʕmi’.
contents.versio: 17. After she was pregnant, then, one day, she contorts herself, she becomes ill-tempered. He says, ‘Why, what’s your situation?’ She says, ‘Your brother spoke with me (i.e., he made an advance)’. ‘Hmm...’ ‘Your brother spoke with me’.

contents.textus: 18. Ánnaqqa mən gdomar? Azzé, omar, ‘Aḥuno, ašə́r koḏaʕno, dúgleyo, elo hawxa mə́ḷḷali’. Omar, ‘Haaa, qay lo+mə̀ḷḷilux? Qay lo+mə̀ḷḷilux, i+barṯo dan+nayaryo!’ Omar, ‘Aḥuno, ġamo layt’. Omar, ‘Ḥarā́m aʕli u+ʕafrano!’
contents.versio: 18. Now then, what will he say? He went, he says, ‘Brother, surely I know that it’s a lie, but she told me so’. He says, ‘See, so didn’t I tell you? So didn’t I tell you, she’s the enemies’ daughter’. He says, ‘Brother, no problem’. He says, ‘This place is off-limits to me (lit. ‘this soil is forbidden to me’)’.

contents.textus: 19. ‘Səmli lo+səmli, lo+səmlux bdiḏi. U+ʕafran‿aʕli howe ḥarā́m. Gəzzí lʔaṯro dnoše loḏaʕ lo manno, lo u+abro dmanno’.
contents.versio: 19. ‘Whatever I did, you didn’t do it according to me. This place’ll be off-limits to me (lit. ‘may this soil be forbidden to me’)! I’ll go to a place where people know neither who I am, nor whose son I am’.

contents.textus: 20. Hedik̇a rawəx ʕal u+səsyayḏe ŭ mədle lu+sayfayḏe. Tlele qŭ́naġ ŭ maḥatle ḥa, tlele qŭ́naġ ŭ maḥatle ḥa, tlele qŭ́naġ ŭ maḥatle ḥa.
contents.versio: 20. Then he mounted his horse and took his sword. He folded a camp and pitched one, he folded a camp and pitched one, he folded a camp and pitched one.

contents.textus: 21. Raḥəq, azzéee lʔaṯro dnoše loḏaʕle. Noše loḏaʕle.
contents.versio: 21. He went far, he went to a place where people didn’t know him. Nobody knew him.

contents.textus: 22. Azzeyo gab u+aġa di+qriṯo. ‘B̥k̇ēr dmə‿koṯat?’ Omar, ‘D̥oweno sayəs laʕ+ʕalok̇at. B̥k̇ēr dmede ḥreno lo+koṯeno’.
contents.versio: 22. He went to the village’s agha. ‘What are you good at (lit. ‘of what do you come in handy’)?’ He says, ‘Let me be a turkey wrangler. I am not good at anything else (lit. ‘of any other thing, I don’t come in handy’)’.

contents.textus: 23. Noše lo+koḏaʕle, manyo, u+abro dmanyo. ‘D̥oweno sayəs laʕ+ʕalok̇at’. Mbalwa aʕ+ʕalok̇at du+aġa, la+ṭyork̇at d̥ḥeḏər i+qriṯo.
contents.versio: 23. Nobody knows him, who he is, whose son he is. ‘Let me become a turkey wrangler’. He would take the agha’s turkeys to the gardens around the village.

contents.textus: 24. Marʕéwalle, mṭéwalle. Ǧule qṭiʕe lowašwa. Bayn aš+šak̇alat yotawwa. Lo+xile ġamo, lə+ṭrele dnoše mašək.
contents.versio: 24. He would tend them, bring them back. He would wear torn clothes. He would sit among the shoes (i.e., in the outermost part of the room, near the door). He didn’t care (lit. ‘he didn’t eat grief’), he didn’t allow anyone to take note.

contents.textus: 25. Yawmo, nafəl hăwar ʕal i+qriṯo. Mballe u+sawā̀l di+qriṯo, mballe u+ṭarš di+qriṯo, mballe lan+nayā̀r.
contents.versio: 25. One day, an alarm arose (lit. ‘fell’) in the village. They took away the village livestock, they took away the village cattle, the enemy took it away.

contents.textus: 26. Ánnaqqa kosolaq lu+šuro, forax raġloṯe hawxa, ‘ʕAlo ʕalaykən, ʕalo ʕalaykən, ʕalo ʕalaykən’. U+admano koqolaʕ.
contents.versio: 26. Now then, he’s scaling the wall and scratching his feet like so, ‘Gobble be with you, Gobble be with you, Gobble be with you!’ This blood is flowing out.

contents.textus: 27. Ḥa xoṯi, dəmmono, sowo, kalé ʕal u+k̇opalayḏe komalax, komar, ‘Kazzí, be mə‿hawi, məl‿lawi’. Noše lo+fāš bi+qriṯo, azzehən lu+hăwar.
contents.versio: 27. Someone like me, I’d say, an old person, here he is, walking with his walking stick, he says, ‘I am going to see what’s going on (lit. ‘what happened and what didn’t’)’. There was no one left in the village, they went to the alarm.

contents.textus: 28. Koḥoyar ebe, ga kalkó... hăma forax raġle bu+šuro du+ḥarbo, komar, ‘ʕAlo ʕalaykən, ʕalo ʕalaykən, ʕalo ʕalaykən’. U+admo koqolaʕ braġloṯe.
contents.versio: 28. He looks at him, look, here he is, he just rubs his feet against the wall of the ruin, he says, ‘Gobble be with you, Gobble be with you, Gobble be with you!’ The blood is flowing on his legs.

contents.textus: 29. Omar, hawxa me ʕaql diḏe, omar, ‘Kīt ŭ layt, hano u+Falak̇o d̥kə́mmiyo’.
contents.versio: 29. He says, so on his own account (lit. ‘out of his own mind’), he says, ‘One way or another (lit. ‘there is and there isn’t’), this is one they call Falako’.

contents.textus: 30. Omar, ‘Falak̇o!’ Mabramle foṯe. Omar, ‘Lə+mball‿u+talā̀n?’
contents.versio: 30. He says, ‘Falako!’ He turned his face. He says, ‘Didn’t they take the rustled cattle?’

contents.textus: 31. Məd məḷḷe hawxa, mḥalaqle, ‘Ŭ áykoda, lo?’ Xud əmbli u+talā̀n ŭ əzzé, u+hawā̀r hárkeda, hiye barəm hawxa.
contents.versio: 31. After he said so, he pounced, ‘And to where, no?’ Like they’re taking the rustled cattle and going away, the alarm is towards here, he turned like so (i.e., as a shortcut).

contents.textus: 32. Rawəx ʕal u+səsyayḏe ŭ mədle li+rəmḥayḏe ŭ azzé li+qamayto dan+nayā̀r.
contents.versio: 32. He mounted his horse, took his spear, and went to meet the enemy.

contents.textus: 33. Qṭile ḥa harke, ŭ mahzamle ḥa harke, ŭ qṭile ḥa harke, ŭ drele ḥa harke, ŭ ḥa harke mahzamle. Madʕaḷḷe u+talā̀n mʕal riša di+qriṯo, madʕaḷḷe u+talā̀n. ‘Lman madʕaḷḷe, lman madʕaḷḷe? Hooo, ašə́r Falák̇oyo. Falak̇o madʕaḷḷe!’
contents.versio: 33. He killed one here, and one escaped here, and he killed one here, he dropped one here, and one here escaped. He brought back the rustled cattle from up on top of the village, he brought the cattle back. ‘Who brought it back, who brought it back? Oh, surely it’s Falako! Falak̇o brought it back!’

contents.textus: 34. Hedik̇a mṭalle, henuk̇a aḏiʕile. ‘Qay lo+mawḏaʕlux ruḥux?’
contents.versio: 34. Then they brought him, suddenly they recognized him. ‘Why didn’t you reveal yourself?’

contents.textus: 35. Mṭalle lu+ḥəmmā̀m, masḥalle, malwáššalle ǧule naḏife, madmaxxe bayn aǧ+ǧule, ŭ ṣə́ddalle qadr haqqa. Ŭ ṣafro edi u+šulṭono di+walaye maḥatle qmi+dukkano.
contents.versio: 35. They brought him to the bath, washed him, they clothed him in clean clothes, bedded him in the clothes, and paid him so much respect. And then in the morning, the city’s sultan put him in front of the shop.

contents.textus: 36. Maḥatle qmi+dukkano, húlele i+dukkano. Maḥatle bu+tarʕo di+dukkano, koxal ŭ šote, naḏifo, ṯniḥoyo.
contents.versio: 36. He put him in front of the shop, he gave him the shop. He put him at the door of the shop, he eats and drinks, clean, rested.

contents.textus: 37. Hak̇a əšmo, hak̇a ġắlăbe, edi lo+kuḏʕono, i+duglo pīsyo. ʕAl u+mamro d̥kəmmi, aṯile qaṣəd me tamo, bəṯr mine qṭəlle u+aḥuno.
contents.versio: 37. Whether it was a little or a lot, I don’t know anymore, the fable is bad. According to what they say, a message came from there: after him (i.e., after he left), they killed his brother.

contents.textus: 38. Qṭəlle lan+nayā̀r u+aḥuno, i+ṗire azzá, mhiralle ʕal ruḥayye. L Ăḷo húlela abro, i+ruḥo du+babo. Háwoste b̥saloġa hawi xōrt.
contents.versio: 38. The enemies killed his brother, his wife left, they married her to themselves. And God had given her a son, the image (lit. ‘spirit’) of his father. As for that one, he became a young man according to a report.

contents.textus: 39. Azzeyo ḥa bi+dawsayḏe ŭ bu+šopayḏe, harke ŭ tamhó, harke ŭ tamhó, harke ŭ tamhó. Azzé gabe.
contents.versio: 39. A certain man had gone on his footsteps and his trail, here and over there, here and over there, here and over there. He went to him.

contents.textus: 40. Omar, ‘Falak̇o!’ Omar, ‘Mənyo?’ Omar, ‘Ašə́r qṭəlle Dəlo’. ‘Ma məs‿sōmno?’
contents.versio: 40. He says, ‘Falako!’ He says, ‘What is it?’ He says, ‘They really killed Dilo’. ‘What should I do?’

contents.textus: 41. Qām hedik̇a rawəx ʕal u+səsyayḏe. Tlele qŭ́naġ waxt̚, tlele qŭ́naġ waxt̚, tlele qŭ́naġ ŭ maḥatle ḥa. Aṯi ŭ aṯi ŭ aṯi blalyo, ga kanné at+tarte ḥwoṯe bi+ʕutma.
contents.versio: 41. Then he up and mounted his horse. He pulled up stakes (lit. ‘a sojourn’) for a while, he pulled up stakes for a while, he pulled up stakes and pitched one. He came, and came, and came at night, look, here are his two sisters in the dark.

contents.textus: 42. Omar, ‘Mḥawu ʕal u+tarʕo!’ Ak+kazabaṯṯe marʕalle. Omar, ‘Aḥunáyxuno, ftāḥli u+tarʕo!’
contents.versio: 42. He says, ‘Knock on the door!’ Their knees (lit. ‘livers’) trembled. He says, ‘I’m your brother, open the door for me!’

contents.textus: 43. Ftəḥḥe u+tarʕo, omar, ‘Qay bi+ʕutma hatu?’ Əmmi, ‘Lə+gmaǧrina, k̇ak̇o. Hăma dmaqiṯina i+nuro, koṯənlan’.
contents.versio: 43. They opened the door, he says, ‘Why are you in the dark?’ They say, ‘We wouldn’t dare, big brother. As soon as we light the fire, they come for us’.

contents.textus: 44. Ánnaqqa, ʕal d̥kətwa i+barṯaṯṯe dan+nayā̀r, hawxa səmla.
contents.versio: 44. Now then, since she was the enemies’ daughter, she had done so.

contents.textus: 45. Lo+maǧralle muhrə́nneste. Fayiši at+tarte esī́r lawġul.
contents.versio: 45. They also didn’t dare marry them either. The two stayed imprisoned indoors.

contents.textus: 46. ‘Lo ko... lə+gmaǧrina, k̇ak̇o. Qṭəlle aḥunux. G̊ʶquṭli hatste!’
contents.versio: 46. ‘We don’t… wouldn’t dare, big brother. They killed your brother. They’re going to kill again, you too!’

contents.textus: 47. Omar, ‘Adlequ i+nuraṯxu, be mə‿komáṇṇanxu?!’ Meqəm qayse, hažžək̇at, nuro saymiwa, ǧuġriwa, ṣopat ŭ medone latwa.
contents.versio: 47. He says, ‘Light your fire, aren’t I telling you?!’ Before it was twigs, brush, they would make a fire, they would burn them, there weren’t any ovens or such things.

contents.textus: 48. Ăḷa, maqəṯṯe i+nuro. Əmmi, ‘La+klabṯoṯanək maqəṯṯe i+nuro, zóxunne’. Aṯən, ‘Klabṯoṯe maqəṯxu i+nuro?’ Omar, ‘Toxu, toxu! Ăḷa gmazraqno b̥feme d̥babayxu! Hul dnohar aʕli ŭ aʕlayxu’.
contents.versio: 48. Gosh, they lit the fire. They say, ‘Those bitches lit the fire, go to them’. They came, ‘You bitches, did you light the fire?’ He says, ‘Come, come! Gosh, I’ll hit you so hard your dad’ll feel it (lit. ‘I’ll piss in your father’s mouth’)! Up until (the sun) rises on me and you!’

contents.textus: 49. Marʕalle, azzə́n, əmmi, ‘Ăḷa, kalkaṯi lu+bayto’. Kanné bi+ḥəmto.
contents.versio: 49. They trembled, they went, they say, ‘Gosh, he’s already come home’. There they are, in a frenzy (lit. ‘fever’).

contents.textus: 50. Kanné bi+ḥəmto. Hedik̇a ṣafro azzé lu+maydā̀n, səmle lăġam.
contents.versio: 50. There they are, in a frenzy. Then, in the morning, he went to the square, he made a channel.

contents.textus: 51. Lăġam, kəmmina, xud‿əmmina, xud i+ǧuwe dmeqəm saymiwa lag+gubone.
contents.versio: 51. A channel, we call it, like we’d say, like the ditch that they made before for the cisterns.

contents.textus: 52. Lăġam d̥səmle mu+qawro du+aḥuno hul lu+maydā̀n d̥kosaymi u+ḥarb, u+šarr.
contents.versio: 52. A channel that he made from his brother’s grave up to the square where they make war, fight.

contents.textus: 53. Gədnuḥti, gdomar, ‘Nḥatu!’ Naḥiti, qoṭal, qoṭal, qoṭal. Gəzzé ʕal u+qawrayḏe, gdomar, a‘Dəlo, baaas, mo baaas?’a
contents.versio: 53. They’ll go down, he’ll say, ‘Get down!’ They went down, he kills, he kills, he kills. He’ll go to his grave, he’ll say, a‘Dilo, is it enough or not?’a

contents.textus: 54. Ŭ gəzzé, qoṭal, ŭ qoṭal, ŭ qoṭal. Əmmi, ‘U+abro daḥunux i+ruḥo du+bàboyo’.
contents.versio: 54. He’ll go, he kills, and kills, and kills. They say, ‘Your brother’s son is the image (lit. ‘spirit’) of his father’.

contents.textus: 55. Aḏəʕle. Kəmṭe i+ḏarbo aʕle, lə+kʶqoṭele.
contents.versio: 55. He recognized him. He has a chance to hit (lit. ‘he brings down the blow at him’), he doesn’t kill him.

contents.textus: 56. Koqoṭal ŭ qoṭal, u+admo koqolaʕ ʕal u+qawro. Qoṭal, ŭ qoṭal, ŭ qoṭal. Gdoṯe ʕal u+qawro, gboxe, gdomar, a‘Dəlo, ma baaas, mo baaas?’a
contents.versio: 56. He kills and kills, and the blood flows upon the grave. He kills, and kills, and kills. He’ll come to the grave, he’ll cry, he’ll say, a‘Dilo, is it enough or not?’a

contents.textus: 57. Ŭ gəzzé disa lu+šarrayḏe. Bu+mqamawo hul dəmṣafəlle.
contents.versio: 57. And he would go again to his fight. In this manner, until he wiped them out.

contents.textus: 58. Mṭewa i+ḏarbo ʕal u+brazi, lo+qoṭewayle, naqqa lu+brazi mṭele i+ḏarbo aʕle, omar, ‘ʕÁmmuxno’. ‘Áydarbo ʕámmihat?’ Omar, ‘ʕÁmmuxno’.
contents.versio: 58. He would get chances to hit his nephew (lit. ‘he would bring down a blow at his nephew’), he wouldn’t kill him, once the nephew had a chance to kill him, he says, ‘I’m your uncle’. ‘How are you my uncle?’ He says, ‘I’m your uncle’.

contents.textus: 59. ‘Mayko... qay ʕámmihat?’ Omar, ‘Hat izúx šāl emux’.
contents.versio: 59. ‘Where are (you from) ... why are you my uncle?’ He says, ‘Go ask your mother yourself’.

contents.textus: 60. Hedik̇a azzé lu+bayto. Omar, ‘Yade’. Əmmo, ‘Mənyo?’ Omar, ‘Šaḥalli bardəš dmaye, ġắlăbe ʕaǧəzno bu+ḥarbano’.
contents.versio: 60. Then he went home. He says, ‘Mummy’. She says, ‘What is it?’ He says, ‘Heat for me a pot of water, I am very tired of this battle’.

contents.textus: 61. Ăḷa, ʕaǧəz. Azzá mšaḥállale maye, əmmo, ‘Tux, lawo, tux, košaḥini’. Omar, ‘Ṭro ṭowo šuḥni’.
contents.versio: 61. Gosh, he was upset. She went and heated the water for him, she says, ‘Come, young man, come, it has heated up’. He says, ‘Let it be heated well’.

contents.textus: 62. Omar, ‘Ṭro rəṯḥi’. Hawi palăpál dəṯṯe, azzé mədle li+buqto dak̇+k̇aziyayḏa.
contents.versio: 62. He says, ‘Let it boil’. Its blub blub blub happened, he went to grab her by the hair (lit. ‘the bundle of her locks’).

contents.textus: 63. Omar, ‘Mar, be manyo babi!’ ‘Yade, babux flān behv...’ Omar, ‘Ono komaṇṇax, mar, be manyo babi!’
contents.versio: 63. He says, ‘Tell me, who’s my father!’ ‘My boy (lit. ‘mummy’), you father is so-and-s...’ He says, ‘I’m telling you, tell me who’s my father!’

contents.textus: 64. Edi məḷḷa əmmo, ‘Ḥāl ŭ măsale hawxa’. Mədle, čəkle qarʕa bayn am+maye. Muqḏole ŭ azzé maṭi lu+ʕammo. KHun žə mə ra sāġ.K
contents.versio: 64. Then she said, she says, ‘The situation (lit. ‘state and matter’) is like so’. He grabbed her, he stuck her head in the water. He burnt her and then went to meet his uncle. KYou be well for me!K

contents.textus: 1.	Nisane: Ánnaqqa, dəmmono ‘Diṫə́n Hăzár’.
contents.versio: 1.	Now then, let me tell the ‘Seeing Nightingale’.

contents.textus: 2.	Ilyas: Amár háyoste.
contents.versio: 2.	Tell that one too.

contents.textus: 3.	N. Diṫə́n Hăzárstene, háwoste šulṭónowa, rábowa, háwoste naʕime látwayle.
contents.versio: 3.	So, Seeing Nightingale, so, that one was a Sultan, he was great, so, that one had no children.

contents.textus: 4.	Azzé, karəx ʕal d̥ḥozele ṗire, azzé, kal kīt tlaṯ+aḥwoṯe bdukṯo.
contents.versio: 4.	He went, he went around to find a wife, he went, hey, there were three sisters in a place.

contents.textus: 5.	‘Mə‿kəbʕutu?’ Omar, ‘Kobaʕno ṗire’. Əmmi, ‘Hăma, a+tlaṯayna aḥwóṯena’. Omar, ‘Mən koqoḏe ab̥xu?’
contents.versio: 5.	‘What does Your Majesty want?’ He said, ‘I want a wife.’ ‘Well, the three of us are sisters.’ He said, ‘What do you do?’ (lit. ‘what passes with you’)

contents.textus: 6.	Əmmo ḥḏo mənne, əmmo, ‘Saymono marše qas di+umma dә Mḥammad dyətwo aʕla lə+g̊taymo’. Omar, ‘Hayo eli komanfʕo!’
contents.versio: 6.	One of them says, she says, ‘I’ll make a carpet that won’t run out even if the whole community of Muhammad sits on it’. He said, ‘That is useful for me!’

contents.textus: 7.	Ŭ ḥḏo mənne əmmo, ‘Layšono; saymono laḥmo məqqa duxli mine i+ummaṯe d Mḥammad lə+g̊taymo. Omar, ‘Tamā́m, háyoste eli komanfʕo!’
contents.versio: 7.	And one of them said, ‘I knead; I’ll make bread that won’t run out no matter how much this community of Muhammad eats from it.’ He said, ‘Ok, that is also useful for me!’

contents.textus: 8.	Ŭ i+naʕəmto, ‘Mə‿g̊saymat?’ Əmmo, ‘Kul+šato, g̊d̥oweli k̇urrǝk̇o ŭ k̇ačk̇e, Kguhár zerín’.K Omar, ‘Tamā́m’.
contents.versio: 8.	And the little one, ‘What’ll you do?’ She said, ‘Every year, I will have a son and a daughter, Kgolden earrings.K ‘He said, ‘Fine.’

contents.textus: 9.	Mbele a+tlaṯ, mbele a+tlaṯ, ba laṯi mənne, at+tarte rabe, xud i+măsale!? Laṯi mənne saymi ṫə+mede. Mḥalqile li+băṭàlĭye, ŭ kalá háyostene, xud d̥kəmmi, hátuste xud aḥunoni, b̥ṭaʕno, b̥ṭaʕno. L Aloho húlela tre+naʕime, Kguhár zerín,K hawila tre+naʕime, Kguhár zerín.K
contents.versio: 9.	He took the three (of them), he took the three (of them), couldn’t they do (lit. ‘didn’t it come from them), the two elder (sisters), like they said (lit. ‘like the matter’)!? They weren’t able to do (lit. ‘it didn’t come from them’) anything. He tossed them aside (lit. ‘to their uselessness’), and here’s that one, like they’d say, you’re like my siblings, she is burdened, she is burdened (with a child). God gave her two children, Kgolden earrings,K she had two children, Kgolden earrings.K

contents.textus: 10.	Ann+aḥwoṯe kəmmi, ‘Mən g̊saymina?’ Ăḷa, haw ko... lo+komaku riše minan, k̬roḥam—hiya. (1:18)
contents.versio: 10.	The sisters say, ‘What shall we do? Gosh, no longer does he… he doesn’t trouble himself with us, he’s in love—it’s her.’

contents.textus: 11.	Hedik̇a azzehən, maḥatte kul+ḥa kapk̇e d̥šakar b̥femayye, blənne maḥtənne b̥qəšto, b̥qəbbala ʕul mu+baḥar, maḥtənne b̥qəbbala manək.
contents.versio: 11.	Then they went, each of them put a piece of sugar into their mouths, they brought them, they put them in an arch, in a nook above the sea.

contents.textus: 12.	Mṭalle tre+ǧewǝrk̇at d̥kalbe li+dərto. Koṯe, hiye koṯe: komisalṗxi aǧ+ǧewərk̇at. ‘Hak hak, hani ǧewə́rk̇atne? Mən, ǧewə́rk̇atne!?’ ‘Aǧ+ǧewərk̇at di+aṯtàyḏuxne’.
contents.versio: 12.	They brought two puppies to the courtyard. He comes, he’s the one who comes: the puppies are climbing up. ‘Wow, wow! Are these puppies? What, there are puppies!?’ ‘They are your wife’s pups.’

contents.textus: 13.	Hedik̇a kǝmʕalaqla bu+tarʕo, komaḥat dǝquqo mi+xaṣra dlarwal, ŭ ḥa mi+xaṣra dlawġul. Ayna dʕobar, moḥela dǝquqo, ŭ ayna dnofaq, moḥela dǝquqo. Mʕalqalle.
contents.versio: 13.	Then he hangs her from the gate, he puts a mallet on the outer side, and one on the inner side. Whoever enters, a mallet strikes her, and whoever exits, a mallet strikes her. They hung her up.

contents.textus: 14.	Ŭ an+naʕimestene, u+baqoro komṭele i+baqrayḏe ʕal feme du+čām, komašte aq+qanyonayḏe. Naqqa koṯe mərča mərč. Maḥátwalle kul+ḥa kapk̇e d̥šakar b̥femayye. Koṯe mərča mərč. Kuzze, koḥṓr tre+naʕime.
contents.versio: 14.	And as for the children, the cowherd would bring his cattle to the mouth of the brook, to water his livestock. One time, the sound of lip-smacking comes. They had put a piece of sugar in each of their mouths. The sound of lip-smacking comes. He goes, he sees the two children.

contents.textus: 15.	Ánnaqqa u+baqòroste naʕime látwayle, hăma midile qəm ṣadre ŭ mṭǝlle, ṭrele maq+qanyone mṭǝlle hiwile li+ṗirayḏe. (2:14)
contents.versio: 15.	Now then, the shepherd also had no children, so then he took them to his chest and brought them back, he left the cattle behind, he brought them back, he gave them to his wife.

contents.textus: 16.	‘žənk̇e, žənk̇e! Mədlax naʕime! Ṗăṗu, naʕime, l Aloho lúlelan?’ Omar, ‘žənk̇e, ḥzalli ʕal u+băḥar, mḥálqene, sə́mlanne‿mmore’.
contents.versio: 16.	‘Woman, woman! Take some children for yourself! Congrats, children, hasn’t God provided for us?’ He says, ‘Woman, I found them, by the sea, they are castaways, take care of them for us.’

contents.textus: 17.	Simənne‿bmore, ŭ hawən rabe, ŭ hawən xōrtat.
contents.versio: 17.	They took care of them, and they got big, they became youths.

contents.textus: 18.	(I+žənnək̇e, răbane, ayna dnofaq komoḥela dǝquqo, ŭ ayna d̥koʕobar komoḥela dǝquqo.)
contents.versio: 18.	(As for the woman, poor woman, whoever exits, a mallet strikes her, and whoever enters, a mallet strikes her.)

contents.textus: 19.	Hawən rabe, dəmmina, xwani diḏan d̥kuzzən lu+maktab. Azzə́n mḥalle lnaʕimk̇o d̥ṗire, mḥalle lnaʕimk̇o d̥ṗire, azzá i+ṗìrestene, kawla bu+naʕimayḏa, məḷḷa, ‘Mayṯutu, noše lo+koḏaʕ manyo babayxu, yatume qarʕe daq+qalme, be lu+baqoro mṭélalxu maʕl u+baḥar?’
contents.versio: 19.	They got big, let’s say, like ours when they go to school. They went to beat a woman’s son, they beat up a woman’s son, so the woman went, she got upset for her son, she said, ‘May you die, people don’t know who your father is, you orphans (with) heads (full) of lice, didn’t the shepherd bring you back from over by the sea?’

contents.textus: 20.	E, aṯən, mšalṭi, mšalaṭ bi+žənk̇e, bi+žənk̇e d̥təlyówayle ŭ maḥtówayle, bi+aṯto du+baqoro, ‘Mar be manyo babi! E, flān latno, əlláh lanna dəṯxu!’
contents.versio: 20.	Yes, they came, they rushed, he rushed at the woman, at the woman who was raising him and accommodating him, at the shepherd’s wife, ‘Say who my father is! Yes, I’m not so-and-so, by God, we aren’t yours!’

contents.textus: 21.	Əmmo, ‘ḥayra, mənxu kowe xāf, m Aloho lo+kowe xāf. Ăḷa, ḥāl ŭ măsale, lu+baqoro ḥzélalxu bi+pečak̇e, he hatu naʕime, mḥaláqqanxu, be mənne mḥaláqqanxu, komṭélalxu, aḥna kosaymínanxu bmore, naʕime latlan, sə́mlanxu bmore’.
contents.versio: 21.	She says, ‘My dear, it is hidden from you, but it isn’t hidden from God. By God, the fact of the matter is (lit. ‘the state and the matter’), the shepherd found you in swaddling clothes, you were still small, they threw you away, however they threw you away, he had brought you back, we took care of you, we don’t have any children, we took care of you.’

contents.textus: 22.	‘E’, omar, ‘Tawdi ġắlăbe, ʕomar baytayxu, e, Ăḷa lo+g̊fayšina gabayxu’.
contents.versio: 22.	‘Yes,’ he says, ‘Thanks a lot, God bless you (lit. ‘may He build your house’), right, by God we shan’t stay with you (any longer).’

contents.textus: 23.	Ánnaqa kul d̥ḥayfi, konofaq tre+dinore bam+mayaṯṯe, azzéyo… kul d̥ḥayfi konofaq tre+dinore bam+mayaṯṯe. (3:40)
contents.versio: 23.	Now then, every time they bathe, two dinars appear in their (bath-)water, so it goes… every time they bathe, two dinars appear in their (bath-)water.

contents.textus: 24.	Hawən zangī́n, maʕmarre, raḥuqo mi+qriṯo … ǧăre b Bequsyone ḥzelux, b Bequsyone? Ánnaqqa, i+xaṣra d̥falge+dyawmo, kəmmi u+ḥammi di+ʕito. Ánnaqqa, u+ḥammi di+ʕito diyāryo. Kəmmina ‘u+gubo du+diyā̀r’. Ǧăre b Bequsyone hawxa maḥkíwayna, ḥoṯi əmmówaylan. Xud dmaʕmaḷḷe, dǝmmina ‘bayto bu+gubo du+diyā̀r’.
contents.versio: 24.	They became rich, they built it, far from the village. Haven’t you ever seen it in Bequsyone, in Bequsyone? Now then, the southern (lit. ‘noon’) side is called ‘the glebe’ (lit. ‘the church’s plot’). Now then, the glebe is a hill. We call it ‘the hill pit’. Sometimes, in Bequsyone, we would tell it like this: my sister would say it to us. Just like the one they built, which we call ‘a house in the hill pit’.

contents.textus: 25.	E, maʕmaḷḷe. I+ḥoṯo kuzzeyo ... kuzzé hiye lu+nečīr, i+ḥoṯo kuyo lawġul. Až+žənk̇at šamiʕi, až+žǝnk̇at šamiʕi, ann+aḥwoṯe di+žǝnk̇e. Šamiʕi, mtarasse ḥḏo sehrabande, mǝrre, ‘Zax, be lə+g̊saymat ʕalā́ǧ mine’. (4:25)
contents.versio: 25.	Yes, they built. The sister goes … he goes hunting, as for the sister, she stays inside. The women heard, the women heard, the woman’s sisters. They heard, they sent a certain witch, they said, ‘Go, won’t you put the fix on him?’

contents.textus: 26.	Ŭ ele məḷḷe li+ḥoṯo, omar, ‘Mad‿doṯe lu+tarʕo, lo+kowe d̥fətḥatle’. Kosoxar u+tarʕo du+quṣro quma, hiye gǝzzé lu+nečīr, hiya kosaymo, mḥayḏro, mašiġo, ŭ mkafro, kəmṭe muklo, ŭ kosaymo.
contents.versio: 26.	And he told the sister, he says, ‘No matter who comes to the door, it isn’t right for you to open it.’ He closes the castle door in front of her, he goes hunting, she works, she tidies up, she washes, and she cleans, he brings food, and she works.

contents.textus: 27.	Aṯyo ḥḏo sehrabande kəmmila. ‘Yade qurbane, ftaḥli u+tarʕo’. Kəmmo, ‘Ábadan, ábadan ono tarʕo lnoše lə+g̊fətḥono’. ‘Ḥúltaxno, i+ḥulto du+zlamàyḏaxno, ḥultáyxuno, yade qurbane, kuṯyono mu+ḥaǧ, baṭə́ltono, ftaḥli u+tarʕo!’ Kosaymo ŭ lo+saymo, i+k̇ačk̇e lə+g̊fətḥo u+tarʕo.
contents.versio: 27.	Then along came a certain witch, they call her. ‘My daughter (lit. ‘mommy’), please, open the door for me’. She said, ‘I’ll never ever open the door for anyone’. ‘I am your auntie, I am your husband’s aunt, I am your auntie, my daughter, please, I am coming back from the Hajj, I am wiped out, open the door for me!’ No matter what she does (lit. ‘she does and she doesn’t’), the girl wouldn’t open the door.

contents.textus: 28.	Koṯe u+k̇urrə̀k̇ mu+nečīr, koṯe u+k̇urrə̀k̇ mu+nečīr. Komalla, ḥəlto mə‿kosaymat harke? Əmmo, ‘Yade qurbane, ha aṯyono mu+ḥaǧ, ḥultáyxuno. Me ṣafro kalí harke, kosaymono lə+ksaymono, ḥoṯux lə+g̊fətḥoli u+tarʕo’. Omar, ‘Ftaḥla, ftaḥ u+tarʕo, ftaḥ’. ʕAbiri a+tre, maḥšamme, ŭ disa damixi, fayišo u+lalyawo gabayye, ṣafro disa hiye azzé lu+nečirayḏe. (5:26)
contents.versio: 28.	The boy comes back from hunting, the boy comes back from hunting. He said to her, ‘Auntie, what are you doing here?’ She said, ‘My dear son (lit. ‘mother’), I’ve just come from the Hajj, I am your aunt. Since dawn, here I’ve been, no matter what I do, your sister won’t open the door for me’. He says, ‘Open it for her, open the door, open it!’ They both entered, they had dinner, and they still went to sleep, she spent that night with them, in the morning again he went on his hunt.

contents.textus: 29.	Kəmmo, kəmmo ‘kHaw bana, kačam,k mede noquṣo layt aʕlax, d̥owewa kdare+raqosak harke, məqqa ṭáwwowa. Tane, lo+koṯelax ṣabr’.
contents.versio: 29.	She said, ‘kIf only, my daughter,k you were lacking nothing, if there were a kDancer’s Stickk here, how nice it would be! Alone, you’ll get bored’.

contents.textus: 30.	Koṯe u+aḥuno, ŭ azzá mraṣtqo. Koṯe u+aḥuno. Bemáʕd, kalá bemáʕd. ‘Ha k̇ak̇e mənyo?’ Kəmmo, ‘Ba ono tane bu+quṣrano, ṣabr lo+koṯeli, kəmmi kīt dare+raqosa, gzomárwayli, gəhnéwayli, gdoṯéwayli ṣabbər’. Omar, ‘Ăḷa, mqawmo aʕli!’
contents.versio: 30.	The brother comes, and she goes straight away. The brother comes. Irritable, here she is, irritable! ‘Hey, sister, what is it?’ She said, ‘Aren’t I alone in this castle, I’m bored, they say there is a kDancer’s Stick,k it would have sung for me, it would have whatsited me, I wouldn’t have been bored’. He says, ‘Gosh, she is on the warpath against me (lit. “she is rising up against me”)!’ (6:00)

contents.textus: 31.	Azzé ŭ azzé ŭ azzé ŭ azzé - šmaʕ ǧăre mito, toxu! - azzéyo, laqi ləzlā́m xətyā́r, b̥falge du+darbo, komar, ‘Kul ḥa…’, ono, muʕa, ‘Šlomo aʕlux, ʕammo, mə‿kosaymat?’ Omar, ‘U+darbano kRiyá Čun ŭ Nahatə́nek yo, ayna dəzzé lə+gdoʕar. U+darbano du+xēryo, ŭ ḥaq diḏi dinóroyo’. Kobele u+dinorayḏe, komar, ‘Ăḷa, gəzzí bu+darbano, d kRiyá Čun ŭ Nahatə́ne.k ‘Yămā́n, daxī́l’, flān … Omar, ‘Aʕli máwṣyoyo, gəzzino hárkeda’.
contents.versio: 31.	He went, and went, and went, and went—listen sometimes, you spy, (addressing one of the three children), come!—he encountered an old man, in the middle of the road, he says, ‘Everyone who,’ I, um, ‘Greetings, uncle, how are you doing?’ He says, ‘This road is the kRoad of Going-and-Not-Coming-Back,k whoever goes won’t come back. This road is the good one (lit. ‘the one of goodness’), and my price is a dinar’. He gave him his dinar, he says, ‘Gosh, I’ll go on this road, of the kRoad of Going-and-Not-Coming-Back.k ‘Please, I beg you,’ and so forth… He says, ‘It’s incumbent (lit. ‘prescribed’) upon me, I’ll go this way.’ (6:40)

contents.textus: 32.	Azzé, hedik̇a mqalazle ʕal i+žənk̇e, mbele u+qayso, mṭele, mṭele aṯi. Gnule mina, mṭele. Be mən šəkl mṭele … damə́xtowa ... be mǝn mṭele … ŭ aṯi ŭ daʕǝr. Omar, ‘Ašə́r noše lo+daʕǝr mu+darbano, kodaʕirat!’ Aṯi, maḥatle bu+quṣro.
contents.versio: 32.	He went, then he stalked the woman (i.e., Seeing Nightingale, the owner of the Dancer’s Stick), he took the stick, he brought it back, he brought it back, he came back. He stole it from her, he brought it back. However, he brought it back… she was asleep … however he brought it back… and he came back and returned. He says, ‘Really, nobody has returned from this way, (but) you’ve returned!’ He came back, he put it in the castle.

contents.textus: 33.	Ánnaqqa kuzzayo tre tloṯo+yawme, disa mtarsalle. Mərre, ‘Zax, be mə‿ǧarile?’
contents.versio: 33.	Now then, two or three days go by, they sent her once again. They said, ‘Go, what has happened to him?’

contents.textus: 34.	Kuzzayo, ga kalkó i+taliye du+qayso, kozomar bu+šabok̇o, ŭ kalá i+k̇ačk̇e yatuto fṣiḥayto. ‘Hah mṭele, yade, mṭele!’ ‘Ftaḥla u+tarʕo!’ Ftə́ḥlala u+tarʕo. ‘Ánnaqqa, d̥owéwalxu, ánnaqa, kAva+Ḥayate,k ŭ kSeva+Xalate,k mənxu noqúṣoyo’. (7:30)
contents.versio: 34.	She went, look, there’s the end of the stick, it’s singing in the window, and there’s the girl, seated, happy. ‘Oh, he brought it, mommy, he brought it!’ ‘Open the door for her!’ She opened the door for her. ‘Now then, if only you had, now then, the kWater of Lifek and the kAkhlat Apple,k it’s what you’re lacking.’

contents.textus: 35.	Azzá disa bu+darbawo. Disa aṯyo, maġballa ruḥa, əmmo, ‘Mamṭí háwoste!’ Hedik̇a azzé disa bu+darbawo; disa lu+zlamawo hawxa mə́ḷḷele, húlele dinoro. Omar, ‘Abro, bas izúx hárkeda; noše lə+gdoʕar mu+darbano’. Omar, ‘Ăḷa gəzzí!’ Disa húlele u+dinorayḏe, ŭ azzé ... Be b̚mə‿šəkl, gnule háwoste. Mṭele, mṭele, disa aṯi. kSeva+Xalatek ŭ kAva+Ḥayatek kalá bi+šušaye dam+maye, ŭ kSeva+Xalatek kalé b̥fema di+šarbo. Hawxa qaḏi; háwoste mṭele.
contents.versio: 35.	Once again, she went back on that way. She came back once more, she made herself angry, and said, ‘Bring that one as well!’ Then, he went on that way once more; again, that man told him so, he gave him a dinar. He says, ‘Son, just go that way; nobody returns from this way.’ He says, ‘By God, I’ll go!’ Once again, he gave him his dinar, and he went… by whatever means, he stole that one too. He brought it back, he brought it back, he came back again. The kAkhlat Apple,k and the kWater of Life,k here it is, in the water bottle, and the kAkhlat Apple,k here it is, in the mouth of the carafe. It ended up like so; he brought that one back, too.

contents.textus: 36.	Qădark̇e aṯyo i+žənk̇e ḥreto disa. (08: 15) Disa aṯyo i+žənk̇e, aṯyo, go ho komṭele háwoste. Əmmo, 'Ánnaqqa b Aloho, hano di+raṣṭiye lo+kuḏʕono’. Axər, mtarasla lmede ḥreno, ṭaʕyalle, lo+kuḏʕono mənwa.
contents.versio: 36.	A little while later, the other woman (i.e., the witch) came once more. The woman came once more, she came, look, here he’s brought that one, too. She says, ‘Now then, by God, this one I really don’t know’. Finally, she sent him for something else, I forgot it, I don’t know what it was. (8:30)

contents.textus: 37.	Hedik̇a i+žǝnk̇e… i+k̇ačk̇este mašəkla, Diṫə́n Hăzár mašəkla d̥koməgnu u+medayḏa. Lo+damixo. Hedik̇a azzé mqalazle mqalazle mqalazle aʕla, húlale rawṭo, səmla kefo kəmto. Səmla kefo kəmto, ŭ u+səsyayḏe. (8:53)
contents.versio: 37.	Then the woman… the girl also noticed, Seeing Nightingale noticed that her stuff (lit. ‘her thing’) is getting stolen. (So) she didn’t go to sleep. Then he went, he stalked, he stalked, he stalked her, (but) she used a wand on him (lit. ‘she gave him a wand’), she made him a black stone. She made him a black stone, and his horse too.

contents.textus: 38.	Laṯi u+aḥuno, laṯi, i+arʕo haw ṣədla. Ṗaší ḥoṯo ŭ aḥunúṯoyo. Kətyo Gule kuḏʕo, u+aḥuno məqqa ḥályoyo. Ko, i+ḥoṯo korǝḥmo u+aḥuno. Kohnó, ánnaqa azzá bu+šoṗayḏe. Komǝḥyo ʕal ṣadra, i+k̇ačk̇e ánnaqqa mǝḥyo ʕal ṣadra, guršo ṣaʕra, mǝḥyo ʕal ṣadra, məḥyo ʕal barkoṯa.
contents.versio: 38.	The brother didn’t come back, he didn’t come back, she searched frantically for him (lit. ‘she didn’t touch the ground anymore’). After all, it is sister-and-brotherhood. Maybe Gule knows, brothers are so sweet. Look, sisters love brothers. She whatsits, now then, she went on his trail. She beats her chest, the girl, now then, she beats her chest, she pulls her hair, she beats her chest, she beats her knees.

contents.textus: 39.	Azzá bu+šoṗawo, azzá, maṭyo lu+zlamawo, disa drela šlomo. Omar, ‘Qəṣṭo ma ləḏʕatwa, noše lo+kodoʕar mu+darbano’. Əmmo, ‘Azzé, fāš’, ŭ azzayo. Omar, ‘Kuḏʕat mə‿gdomannax?’ Əmmo, ‘Mə‿gdəmmat?’ (09: 26)
contents.versio: 39.	She went on that trail, she went, she encountered that man, once more she greeted him, he says, ‘Shameful girl (lit. “shaven [girl]”), didn’t you know? Nobody returns from this road!’ She says, ‘He went, he survived’, and she went. He says, ‘Do you know what I’m going to tell you?’ She says, ‘What are you going to say?’

contents.textus: 40.	Omar, ‘Zax, malla, mar, “Diṫə́n Hăzár, mālxărabe! Aḥna saymíwayna heviye dmərhovaṫiye, dəbraxwăṫiye minax, qaymat saymat aḥuni kefo kəmto!” Lawla dmadəʕr‿aʕlax, ha, dmadəʕr‿aʕlax, hiyastene g̊d̥uyo, [g̊d̥uyat] hatste kefo kəmto. “Diṫə́n Hăzár, mālxărabe! Aḥna saymíwayna heviye dmərhovaṫiye dəbraxwăṫiye minax, qaymat saymat aḥuni kefo kəmto! Diṫə́n Hăzár, mālxărabe! Aḥna saymíwayna heviye dmərhovaṫiye, dəbraxwăṫiye minax, qaymat saymat aḥuni kefo kəmto!”. Lawla darbo măfar madəʕr‿aʕlax’. (09: 52)
contents.versio: 40.	He says, ‘Go, say to her, say, “Seeing Nightingale, you wretch! We were hoping for a kinship, for fraternalism with you, you up and make my brother a black stone!” Don’t give her (the opportunity) to respond to you, she too will become… you too will become a black stone. “Seeing Nightingale, you wretch! We were hoping for a kinship, for fraternalism with you, you up and make my brother a black stone! Seeing Nightingale, you wretch! We were hoping for a kinship, for fraternalism with you, you up and make my brother a black stone!”, don’t give her a way out to respond to you’.

contents.textus: 41.	Azzá hawxa məḷḷa, ‘Diṫə́n Hăzár, mālxărabe, aḥna saymíwayna heviye dmərhovaṫiye dəbraxwăṫiye minax, sǝmlax aḥuni kefo kəmto. Diṫə́n Hăzár, mālxărabe, aḥna saymíwayna heviye dmərhovaṫiye dəbraxwăṫiye minax, ksaymat aḥuni kefo kəmto’. Məḷḷa ŭ məḷḷa ŭ məḷḷa ʕal ḥḏoḏe. (10: 08)
contents.versio: 41.	She went to say so, ‘Seeing Nightingale, you wretch! We were hoping for a kinship, for fraternalism with you, you made my brother a black stone! Seeing Nightingale, you wretch! We were hoping for a kinship, for fraternalism with you, you make my brother a black stone!’ She said, and said, and said it all together.

contents.textus: 42.	Əmmo, ‘Ko nfaq! Be aḥunax manyo?’ Əmmo, ‘Ha hánoyo’. Mḥela u+rawṭo aʕle, hawi nošo, ŭ mḥela ʕal u+səsyayḏe, hawi nošo. U+surăhayḏa kule qarʕe da+zlàmatwa, mḥela ʕal kulle əmmo, ‘Qumu zoxu lab+botaṯxu’. Kulle qayimi xud i+bayluk di+ʕaskar, mbarbzi ʕal ab+botaṯṯe. (10:35)
contents.versio: 42.	She says, ‘Get right out! Who is your brother?’ She said, ‘It’s this one here’. She struck him with the wand, he became human, and she struck on his horse, it became a living being (lit. ‘a human’). Her fence was entirely men’s skulls, she struck all of them, she said, ‘Get up, go back to your homes!’ All of them got up like a military platoon, they scattered to their homes.

contents.textus: 43.	Hedik̇a híyaste rawixo ŭ aṯyo aʕmayye, rawixo aṯyo aʕmayye. Rawixo ʕal u+səsyo ŭ hiye ʕal u+səsyo; rawixo bəṯre, ŭ i+k̇ačk̇e mḥela ʕam gabayye. Aṯyo maʕ+ʕəšqat, aṯyo bi+qamayto drela šlomo ʕal u+zlām. Omar, ‘Mən səmlax?’ Əmmo, ‘Mṭelan híyaste ʕam ruḥan’. Ŭ aṯila… bʕəšq ŭ kēf (10.44). Aṯyo lu+bayto bi+qamayto, aṯyo li+qamayto. Mhirole, hawyóleyo ṗire ŭ híyaste ... hno.
contents.versio: 43.	Then she (i.e., Seeing Nightingale) also rode and came back with them, she rode and came back with them. She rode on the horse, and he was on the horse; she rode behind him, and the girl struck ahead alongside them. She came joyfully, she came first and greeted the man. He said, ‘What have you done?’ She said, ‘We also brought her with us.’ She became… she came gladly (lit. ‘with passion and pleasure’). She came home first, she came as the first one. He married her, she became a wife for him, and she also … whatsits.

contents.textus: 44.	‘Mənyo ŭ lo mənyo?’ I+žənk̇e kuzzá kəmmo, ‘Ăḷa komṭela i+sehrabande! Kuzzá komṭela híyaste, mṭela híyaste, hawyóleyo ṗire. Ba áydarbo lo áydarbo? Məs‿saymina məl‿lo+saymina?’ (11.10) Əmmi, ‘Ăḷa g̊saymina ʕazima, gəmsammínale, g̊saymina ʕazima gəmsammínale’. Ánnaqa səmme ʕazima ŭ ánnaqa qralle lag+gundi kulle.
contents.versio: 44.	‘What’s going on (lit., what is it and isn’t it)?’ The woman goes and says, ‘By God, she has brought the witch! She goes and brings her back too, she has become his wife (lit. a wife for him). How about it (lit. how, how not)? What should we do (lit. what should and shouldn’t we do)?’ They say, ‘By God, let’s have a get-together, we’ll poison him, we’ll have a get-together, we’ll poison him.’ Then they had a get-together, and then they invited all the villagers.

contents.textus: 45.	(Ŭ i+k̇ačk̇e, i+žənk̇e răbane kalá mʕalaqto; ayna dnofaq, ayna dnofaq komoḥela dequqo, ŭ ayna dʕobar komoḥela dequqo).
contents.versio: 45.	(And the girl, the poor woman, here she is hanged; whoever exits, a mallet strikes her, and whoever enters, a mallet strikes her.)

contents.textus: 46.	Ŭ azzehǝn ... azzayo, li+žənk̇e mbela i+qaṭǝn ʕam ruḥa. Aḏiʕo gəmsammila, mbela i+qaṭən ʕam ruḥa. Naqqa əmmo—rmalle kulle ŭ rmalle álleste—əmmo, ‘Aḥna, dl‿i+qaṭənayḏan bi+qamayto uxlo, aḥna lo+kuxlina’. I+žənk̇e šahrăzawa. (Ánnaqa maḥatte ... ánnaqa čāx̬ dlu+k̇urrək̇o mḥele dequqo, li+emo əmmo, ‘Yaaay, i+ḏarbo du+abrayḏi məqqa basə́mtoyo’.) Hawən hne hawxa, qayəm hedi hedik̇a maḥatte u+muklo qmi+qaṭən. Naqqa i+qaṭən xila naqqa mfarfṭo, i+qaṭən mfarfṭo mayiṯo. Mayiṯo.
contents.versio: 46.	And they went… she (i.e., Seeing Nightingale) went, the woman took a (queen) cat with her. She knew that they were going to poison her, she took a cat with her. Now then, she says—they had put everything out and even put it out for them—she says, ‘As for us, unless our cat eats first, we won’t eat’. The woman was experienced. (Now then, they put… now then, the time that the boy struck the mallet, his mother said, ‘Oooh! How sweet is the stroke of my son!’) Things being what they were (lit. ‘they became so’), they up and surreptitiously put the food before the cat. As soon as the cat ate, she gasped, the cat gasped, she died. She died.

contents.textus: 47.	‘Həǝǝ’, əmmo, ‘Koḥozat? Koḥozat áydarbo msamámmallan? Ha koḥozat? Kətlux hāž?’ Əmmo, ‘Ya ḥakəm! Haṯe i+piràyḏuxyo. Ono i+kalàyḏuxno, ŭ haṯe i+barṯo ŭ u+abràyḏuxne, ŭ kul d̥ḥayfi konofaq tre+dinore taḥtayye. U+mamrayḏa nafəq, hedik̇a a+ḥrene laṯi mənne; lo+nafəq u+mamraṯṯe. Makuwwe gawayye, mʕalqalle. Kəmmo, “I+ḏarbo du+abrayḏi məqqa basə́mtowa”, mḥélela u+dequqo’. (13:00)
contents.versio: 47.	‘Huh,’ she (i.e., Seeing Nightingale) says, ‘See? See how they poisoned us? Now do you see? Are you aware?’ She said, ‘Oh, ruler! This is your wife. I am your daughter-in-law, and this one is your daughter, and your son, and every time they wash, two dinars appear beneath them. What she said happened, then nothing came from the others; what they said didn’t happen. They got jealous (lit. ‘they harmed their guts’), they hung her up. She (i.e., the mother) says, “How sweet is the stroke of my son!”, he had struck her with the mallet’.

contents.textus: 48.	‘Lo+kowe!’ Əmmo, ‘Ăḷa, kalkó mḥawyo. Ḥur! Mtarasse aq+qa+hnani, aš+šarṭani, maḥtila qumi, ŭ mṣakarla, ŭ l Aloho lo+hnele. Kaṯyono ónoste, hawyono i+kalaṯxu, ŭ koḥozat msamamme ha li+qaṭən, i+qaṭən mayiṯo’. Omar, ‘Barbezu, barbezu, barbezu i+daʕwo kula!’ Mbarbzi.
contents.versio: 48.	‘It can’t be!’ She says, ‘By God, this is how it seems. Look! They sent so many of these whatsits, these conditions, she put them on me, and she failed, and God didn’t whatsit (i.e., permit it’). I have come too, I became your daughter-in-law, and you see they poisoned this here cat, the cat died’. He said, ‘Scram, scram, scram, the whole wedding party!’ They scrammed.

contents.textus: 49.	‘Heee! Miḥasyo i+emo ŭ u+babo d̥awo dǝmṭe quflo, ya ṭarfe, ya ftile, ya qayse’. Ŭ səmle ǧeziye hawxa xwani d̥similan šan aʕ+ʕeze. Hedik̇a mədle lat+tarte, mḥalqile aʕlayye, muqḏile, ŭ manḥatle i+ḥreto.
contents.versio: 49.	‘Hear ye, please bring (lit. ‘that one who brings, may his mother and father be blessed’) an armful of leaves, blades of grass, or sticks!’ Then he made a heap, just like one of those we made for goats. Then he took the two women (i.e., the wicked sisters), tossed them on top of them (i.e., the heap), set fire to them, and brought down the other woman (i.e., the mother).

contents.textus: 50.	I+žənk̇e, i+kalayḏa taxtūrwa. Hedik̇a grəšla dawqe du+laḥmo šk̇avá ʕal ag+garme di+ḥmoṯo, maniḥola. Ŭ moqaḏle at+tarte ḥrene, ŭ mhəlle i+ḥreto. Disa hawyo i+ṗirayḏe, ŭ ag+K‘guhár zerín’K hawən i+barṯo u+abrayḏe, Ŭ Diṫə́n Hăzár hawyo i+kalayḏe.
contents.versio: 50.	As for the woman, her sister-in-law was a physician. Then she pulled apart pieces of unleavened bread over the bones of her mother-in-law, she cured her. So, he burned up the two other women and married the other one. She became his wife again, the Kgolden earrings’K became his (legal) daughter and son, and Seeing Nightingale became his daughter-in-law.

contents.textus: 51.	Hun žmǝra sāġ.
contents.versio: 51.	You be well for my sake!

contents.textus: 001. Əmmi, u+waziro ... ŭ waziro ŭ šǝlṭono, ŭ waziro, ŭ azzehən, maḏəffe bbayto, maḏəffe bbayto, bayto ʕiqo, čučk̇at, ḥḏo+ṗire, maḏəffe.
contents.versio: 001. They say, the vizier… both a vizier and a sultan, and a vizier, and they went, they became guests in a house, they became guests in a house, a narrow house, kids, one woman, they became guests.

contents.textus: 002. I+ṗire nafilo qəm ḥāl druḥa, ŭ hənnək fayiši bi+dərto, ŭ i+žənk̇e ʕabiro lawġul. L Aloho hule i+dargəštayḏa.
contents.versio: 002. The woman went into labour (lit. ‘she fell before her own condition’), and they stayed in the courtyard, and the woman went inside. God gave her a cradle (i.e., a child).

contents.textus: 003. Konofaq xort bǧule ḥewore me gaba. Kəmmi, ‘K̇uro, mə‿saymatwa tamo? E, i+ṗirayo qəm ḥāl diḏa, mək‿konəfqat me lawġul?!’ Omar, ‘Ono maláxono, kṯuli, “I+barṯo du+šulṭono g̊tuyo năṣī́b du+zʕurano”.’
contents.versio: 003. A boy dressed in white leaves from her side. They say, ‘Boy! What were you doing there? Yeah, that woman is in labour (lit. ‘is before her condition’), why are you leaving from inside?’’ He says, ‘I am an angel, I have written, “The sultan’s daughter will be the soulmate of this boy”’.

contents.textus: 004. Ánnaqqa i+kalo du+wazìrowa ... ánnaqqa, ánnaqqa. Səmla rabbane… əmmo naqla ... səmla fəršə́k̇, baṭilo, damixo.
contents.versio: 004. Now then, the vizier’s bride was… now then, now then. The poor one did… then she says … she gave milk for the first time (lit. ‘she made colostrum’), she got tired, she slept.

contents.textus: 005. Komaydile, maḥtile bayne ... maḥátwayla bayn ap+pačk̇ayḏa, rabbane. Mbeeela dəmmina, əmmíwayna aḥna b Bequsyone kGuharrá ʕAvdál,k dəmmina uʕdo harke dǝmmina kZyaratá Maṣí.k
contents.versio: 005. They take him, they put him in… She had put him in swaddling clothes, the poor one.  He took him, let’s say, what we in Bequsyone used to call kʕAvdal Slope,k let’s say here now, let’s say kFish Graveyard.k

contents.textus: 006. Marḥaqla  mi+qriṯo, maḥatla bayn… maḥatle bayn davik̇e ŭ aṯi, mrastqi azzəhən, mǝḷḷe, ‘Hay dabibat gdoxele’.
contents.versio: 006. She (i.e., he, the sultan) removed him from the village, she put him within... he put him within a thicket and came back, they set off directly, he said, ‘Certainly wild beasts will eat him’.

contents.textus: 007. I+žənk̇e, ṗaṗuk̇e, koqaymo maḥiso, lo+pečak̇e w lo+mede. Ánnaqqa meqəm əmmíwayna aǧ+ǧənnat kəmblənne. Maḥtíwayna šalfe, maḥtíwayna skine, maḥtíwayna medone, əmmíwayna aǧ+ǧənnat kuxlǝnne, kəmblənne.
contents.versio: 007. The woman, poor thing, starts to wake up, there’s no (babe in) swaddling clothes or anything. Now then, earlier we used to say that djinns take them. We used to put flick knives, we used to put knives, we used to put things, we used to say that djinns eat them, take them away.

contents.textus: 008. Hiya rabbane baxyo šab̥ṯo, məḷḷa, ‘Laǧ+ǧənnat mballe ŭ azzé’. Šab̥ṯo baxyo aʕle, azzé. Kuzzé hak̇a yarḥo hak̇a tre. Ánnaqqa u+zlamayḏa baqóroyo, kuzzé qm aq+qanyone.
contents.versio: 008. She, the poor one cried a week, she said, ‘The djinns took him and he’s gone.’ She cried a week over him, he’s gone. Either a month or two goes by. Now then, her husband is a cowherd, he goes with (lit. ‘in front of’) the cattle.
