contents.textus: 7. Əmmo, ‘Ma ínaqqa dəmqatlina, b̰mə‿gmoḥatli?’ Omar, ‘Bi+ḥaṭro di+baqoruṯo’. Əmmo, ‘Oow, qay kibi tēr d̥ḥaṭro’.
contents.versio: 7. She says, ‘When we fight, with what are you going to beat me?’ He says, ‘With my cowherd’s prod’. She says, ‘Oh, at most I can take one prod’.

contents.textus: 8. Azzá, ṭrele mina. Azzá, azzá, azzá, maṭyo lu+ruʕyo.
contents.versio: 8. She went, he left her. She went, she went, she went, she met a shepherd.

contents.textus: 9. Omar, ‘Keze qwərto, lay gəzzáx?’ Əmmo, K‘K̇úla+bávē+kḗzē’. K
contents.versio: 9. He says, ‘You silly beetle, where are you going?’ She says, K‘To hell with “you beetle”!’ K

contents.textus: 10. ‘Qay?’—‘Maḷḷi, “Naze, názeliya, du+čarčaf yaroqo, du+ṣʕuno semoqo!” ’
contents.versio: 10. ‘Why?’ —‘Tell me, “Darling, delightful one! She of the green veil, she of the red shoes!”’

contents.textus: 11. Omar, ‘Naze, názeliya, du+čarčaf yaroqo, du+ṣʕuno semoqo, lay gəzzáx?’
contents.versio: 11. He says, ‘Darling, delightful one, she of the green veil, she of the red shoes, where are you going?’

contents.textus: 12. Əmmo, ‘Gəzzí kokurxalli ʕal ḥa’. Omar, ‘Tax! Ono ŭ hat saymina ḥḏoḏe!’
contents.versio: 12. She says, ‘I am going to look around about a man’. He says, ‘Come! You and I should marry each other’.

contents.textus: 13. Əmmo, ‘Ínaqqa dəmqatlina, bmə gmoḥatli?’ Omar, ‘Bi+ḥaṭro di+ruʕyuṯo’. Əmmo, ‘Oow, qay kibi tēr dəḥḏo. Ăḷă, lo+ksaymallux’.
contents.versio: 13. She says, ‘When we fight, with what are you going to beat me?’ He says, ‘With my shepherd’s prod’. She says, ‘Oh, at most I can take it once. By God, I shall not marry you’.

contents.textus: 14. Azzá maṭyo lu+daworo. Malaxla, malaxla, maṭyo lu+daworo.
contents.versio: 14. She went, she met a ploughman.

contents.textus: 15. ‘Keze qwərto, lay gəzzáx?’ Əmmo, K‘K̇úla+bávē+kḗzē’. K
contents.versio: 15. ‘You silly beetle, where are you going?’ She says, K‘To hell with “you beetle”!’ K

contents.textus: 16. ‘Ba məd‿domaṇṇo?’—‘Mar, “Naze, názeliya, du+ṣʕuno semoqo, du+čarčaf yaroqo” ’.
contents.versio: 16. ‘What shall I call you?’ —‘Say, “Darling, delightful one, she of the red shoes, she of the green veil” ’.

contents.textus: 17. Omar, ‘Naze, názeliya, du+čarčaf yaroqo, du+ṣʕuno semoqo, lay gəzzáx?’
contents.versio: 17. He says, ‘Darling, delightful one, she of the green veil, she of the red shoes, where are you going?’

contents.textus: 18. Əmmo, ‘Gəzzí kurxalli ʕal ḥa, saymalli ḥa’. Omar, ‘Tax! Ono ŭ hat’. Əmmo, ‘Ma ínaqqa dəmqatlina, bmə‿gmoḥatli?’ Omar, ‘Bu+masoso’. Əmmo, ‘Qay kibi tēr d̥ḥa’.
contents.versio: 18. She says, ‘I am going to look around about a man, to marry a man’.He says, ‘Come, you and I!’ She says, ‘When we fight, with what are you going to beat me?’ He says, ‘With a goad’. She says, ‘At most I can take it once’.

contents.textus: 19. Azzá, azzá, malaxla, malaxla, malaxla, maṭyo lu+ʕebugro.
contents.versio: 19. She went, she went, she went on, she went on, she went on, she met a mouse.

contents.textus: 20. Omar, ‘Keze qwərto, lay gəzzáx?’ Əmmo, K‘K̇úla+bávē+kḗzē’. K
contents.versio: 20. He says, ‘You silly beetle, where are you going?’ She says, K‘To hell with “you beetle”!’ K

contents.textus: 21. ‘Mən domaṇṇax?’—‘Mar, “Naze, názeliya, du+ṣʕuno semoqo, du+čarčaf yaroqo, lay gəzzáx?” ’
contents.versio: 21. ‘What shall I call you?’ —‘Say, “Darling, delightful one, she of the red shoes, she of the green veil, where are you going?” ’

contents.textus: 22. Omar, ‘Naze, názeliya, du+čarčaf yaroqo, du+ṣʕuno semoqo, lay gəzzáx?’
contents.versio: 22. He says, ‘Darling, delightful one, she of the green veil, she of the red shoes, where are you going?’

contents.textus: 23. Əmmo, ‘Gəzzí saymalli ḥa’. Omar, ‘Tax! Ono ŭ hat saymina ḥḏoḏe’. Əmmo, ‘Ínaqqa dəmqatlina, bmə gmoḥatli?’ Omar, ‘Bi+dūv̥k̇ayḏi’. Əmmo, ‘Ṭrowe, i+dūv̥k̇ayḏux lo+gmakiwoli’.
contents.versio: 23. She says, ‘I am going to marry a man’. He says, ‘Come, you and I should marry each other!’ She says, ‘When we fight, with what are you going to beat me?’ He says, ‘With my tail’. She says, ‘OK, your tail will not harm me’.

contents.textus: 24. Azzehən lu+bayto, azzehən lu+bayto … E, čirók̇eyo, kuḏʕat, dúgleyo, dúgleyo.
contents.versio: 24. They went home, they went home … Yes, this is a fable, you know, it is not true, it is not true.

contents.textus: 25. Azzé, omar, ‘Haṯe i+koro da+ṭlàwḥeyo, ŭ haṯe du+bə̀rġəlyo, ŭ haṯe du+gàrsoyo, haṯe …’ Madile ʕal ak̇+k̇elik̇at du+bayto. Hawxa kəmmi, čirók̇atne. Mahnalle, ŭ azzé hiye lu+ṭuro.
contents.versio: 25. He went, he says, ‘This is a hopper of barley, and this one is for bulgur, and this one is for cracked wheat, and this one …’. He showed her about the daily routine (lit. ‘he showed her about the moments’). They tell it like so, these are fables. They whatsited, and he went out to the hill country.

contents.textus: 26. Azzá dmaḥto, ddəryo ṭlawḥe bi+bardəš. Nafilo li+koro, azzá be sar ŭ bərhān.
contents.versio: 26. She went to put, to pour some lentils into a pot. She fell into the hopper; she disappeared without a trace (lit. ‘without head or clue’).

contents.textus: 27. Koṯe, ‘Naze! Naze! Naze!’—Naze layt.
contents.versio: 27. He comes, ‘Darling! Darling! Darling!’ —There is no darling.

contents.textus: 28. Hedik̇a mgavazle bayn u+qaṭmo di+tfayo ŭ azzeyo, azzeyo li+dawmo. Əmmo, K‘Hak məšk̇ó, čə́ma ṫə sar bəxwalī́-yī?’ K Omar,
contents.versio: 28. Then he rolled around in fireplace ashes and he went, he went to a tree. She (i.e., the tree) says, K‘Gee, Mouse, why are you ashen-faced? (lit. ‘why are you head-ashen?’)’ K He (i.e., the mouse) says,

contents.textus: 29. K‘Hoo, Mə́šk̇o ʕAvdurraḥmā́no, sar bəxwalī́-ya! Náze Nazadáne káṫa kuwárk̇a nīsk̇á-da; čū bē sar ŭ bē bərhā́n!’K
contents.versio: 29. K‘Well, Abdurrahman Mouse, his face is ashen (lit. ‘the head is ashen’)! Baby Darling fell down into the lentil hopper; she is gone without a trace!’ K

contents.textus: 30. Nṣəfla ruḥa mad+dawme, palle lə+ṭrela bruḥa. Aṯyo i+qəžžək̇e aʕla, K‘Hak Dáro, čə́ma ṫə pal wašándī?’ K Əmmo,
contents.versio: 30. She shook the leaves off herself (lit. ‘she shook herself off the trees’); she did not leave a leaf upon herself. A crow came upon her, K‘Gee, Tree! Why so leaf a-shaken, you?’ K She (i.e., the tree) says,

contents.textus: 31. K‘Hoo Dáro, pal wašándī, ŭ Mə́šk̇o ʕAvdurraḥmā́no, sar bəxwalī́-ya; Náze Nazadáne káṫa kuwárk̇a nīsk̇á-da, čū bē sar ŭ bē bərhā́ne!’ K
contents.versio: 31. K‘Oh, Tree, leaf a-shaken, and Abdurrahman Mouse, his face is ashen; Baby Darling fell down into the lentil hopper; she is gone without a trace!’ K

contents.textus: 32. Qām hiya grəšla i+dūv̥k̇ayḏa, azzayo ʕal am+maye … əmmo … d̥šətyo. Əmmo, K‘Qəžžə́k̇ē, čə́ma dūv kəšándī?’ K Əmmo,
contents.versio: 32. She up and plucked off her tail, she went to the waters … she says … to drink. She (i.e., they, the waters) says, K‘Crow, why so tail a-plucked?’ K She says,

contents.textus: 33. K‘Qəžžək̇e, dūv kəšándī, Dáro, pal wašándī; Mə́šk̇o ŭ ʕAvdurraḥmā́no, sar bəxwalī́-ya; Náze Nazadáne káṫa kuwárk̇a nīsk̇á-da, čū bē sar ŭ bē bərhā́ne!’ K
contents.versio: 33. K‘Crow, tail a-plucked, Tree, leaf a-shaken; Abdurrahman Mouse, his face is ashen; Baby Darling fell down into the lentil hopper; she is gone without a trace!’ K

contents.textus: 34. Híyastene azzá lam+maye, hawyo fatle admo, ŭ ḥa maye. Azzeyo u+tayso, u+ʕarbo kəmmutu, d̥šote. K‘Avá-ma, čə́ma bə-xwī́n-a?’ K Əmmo,
contents.versio: 34. She also went into the water, one ripple became blood, and another water. A six-toother goat went—you call it a four-toother goat—in order to drink. K‘Why is our water bloody?’ K She (i.e., they, the waters) says,

contents.textus: 35. K‘(Avá-ma) bə-xwī́na, ŭ Qəžžə́k̇ē, dūv kəšándī; Dáro, pal wašándī, ŭ Mə́šk̇o ʕAvdurraḥmā́no, sar bəxwalī́-ya, ŭ Náze Nazadáne káṫa kuwárk̇a nīsk̇á-da, čū bē sar ŭ bē bərhā́ne!’ K
contents.versio: 35. K‘(Our waters) are bloody, and Crow, tail a-plucked, and Tree, leaf a-shaken, and Abdurrahman Mouse, his face is ashen, and Baby Darling fell down into the lentil hopper; she is gone without a trace!’ K

contents.textus: 36. Qəṣle daqne, azzeyo. Ŭ am+maye nafili ʕal u+daḥno. K‘Čə́ma avá-ma bə-xwī́n-a?’ K Əmmo,
contents.versio: 36. He sheared off his beard, he went away. And the waters fell upon the millet. K‘Why is our water bloody?’ K She (i.e., they, the waters) says,

contents.textus: 37. K‘Avá-ma bəxwī́n-a, ŭ Nəhrī́yo, rəh qusándī, ŭ Qəžžə́k̇ē, dūv kəšándī, ŭ Dáro, pal wašándī, ŭ Mə́šk̇o ʕAvdurraḥmā́no, sar bəxwalī́-ya, ŭ Náze ŭ Nazadáne káṫa kuwárk̇a nīsk̇á-da, čū bē sar ŭ bē bərhā́ne!’ K
contents.versio: 37. K‘Our waters are bloody, and Goat, beard a-shorn, and Crow, tail a-plucked, and Tree, leaf a-shaken, and Abdurrahman Mouse, his face is ashen, and Baby Darling fell down into the lentil hopper; she is gone without a trace!’ K

contents.textus: 38. Ṭwele qarʕe, ṭwele qarʕe. Azzé u+daworo ddowar, K‘Čə́ma gárəso ṫə sar nuxwī́nī?’ K
contents.versio: 38. He bowed down his head, he bowed down his head. The farmer went to plough. K‘Why, Millet, are you head droopy?’ K (The millet says,)

contents.textus: 39. K‘Gárəso, sar nuxwī́n-a, ŭ avá-ma bəxwī́n-a, ŭ Nəhrī́yo, rəh qusándī, ŭ Qəžžə́k̇ē, dūv kəšándī, ŭ Dáro, pal wašándī, ŭ Mə́šk̇o ʕAvdurraḥmā́no, sar bə-xwalī́-ya; Náze ŭ Nazadáne káṫa kuwárk̇a nīsk̇á-da; čū bē sar ŭ bē bərhā́n!’ K
contents.versio: 39. K‘Millet, his head is droopy, and our water is bloody, and Goat, beard a-shorn, and Crow, tail a-plucked, and Tree, leaf a-shaken, and Abdurrahman Mouse, his face is ashen; Baby Darling fell down into the lentil hopper; she is gone without a trace!’ K

contents.textus: 40. Ḥăša, maḥatle u+masoso b̥ṭize. Aṯyo i+barṯo, mṭélale qroṭən. Ga kalé, K‘Yā́bo, čə́ma ṫə qun məsā́sī?’, K əmmo.
contents.versio: 40. Excuse me, he stuck the goad up his arse. Along came his daughter, she brought him breakfast. Lo and behold, K‘Daddy, why are you arse a-goaded?’ K She (i.e., he, the father) says,

contents.textus: 41. K‘Yā́bo, qun b̰-məsā́s-a; gárəsē-ma, sar nuxwī́n-a, ŭ avá-ma bəxwī́n-a, ŭ Nəhrī́yē-ma, rəh qusándī, ŭ Qəžžə́k̇ē, dūv kəšándī, ŭ Dáro, pal wašándī; Mə́šk̇o ŭ ʕAvdurraḥmā́no, sar bəxwalī́-ya; Náze Nazadáne káṫa kuwárk̇a nīsk̇á-da, čū bē sar ŭ bē bərhā́n!’ K
contents.versio: 41. K‘Daddy, his arse is a-goaded; our millet, his head is droopy, and our waters are bloody, and our goat, beard a-shorn, and Crow, tail a-plucked, and Tree, leaf a-shaken; Abdurrahman Mouse, his face is ashen Baby Darling, she fell down into the lentil hopper; she is gone without a trace!’ K

contents.textus: 42. Maqlabla u+ṣeniye du+qaṭiro ʕal qarʕe druḥa, azzá lu+bayto. Əmmo, K‘Hak, k̇áčam, čə́ma ṫə sar bəmáṣṭī’. K Əmmo,
contents.versio: 42. She flipped a plate of yogurt over her own head, she went home. She says, K‘Gee, my daughter, why are you yogurty-headed?’ K She (i.e., the daughter) says,

contents.textus: 43. K‘Yádē, k̇áča-ṫa, sar bə-máṣṭ-a, ŭ zlā́mē-ṫa, qun b̰-məsas-a; gárəsē-ma, sar nuxwī́n-a, ŭ avá-ma bəxwī́n-a, ŭ Nəhrī́yo, rəh qusándī, ŭ Qəžžə́k̇ē, dūv kəšándī, ŭ Dáro, pal wašándī, ŭ Mə́šk̇o ʕAvdurraḥmā́no, sar bə-xwalī́-ya, ŭ Náze Nazadáne káṫa kuwárk̇a nīsk̇á-da; čū bē sar ŭ bē bərhā́n!’ K
contents.versio: 43. K‘Mommy, your daughter, her head is yogurty, and your husband, his arse is a-goaded; our millet, its head is droopy, and our water is bloody, and Goat, beard a-shorn, and Crow, tail a-plucked, and Tree, leaf a-shaken, and Abdurrahman Mouse, his face is ashen, and Baby Darling fell down into the lentil hopper; she is gone without a trace!’ K

contents.textus: 44. Háyoste yatiwo ʕal u+dawqo semoqo. Aṯyo … yatiwo … i+ǧiranaṯṯe li+nuro. K‘Hak, čə́ma ṫə qun bəsélī?’ K Əmmo,
contents.versio: 44. That one also sat down on a red-hot griddle. Along came … she sat down … their neighbour for some fire. K‘Gee, why are you arse a-griddled?’ K She (i.e., the mother) says,

contents.textus: 45. K‘Hoo, az qun bə-sél-əm, ŭ k̇áča-m, sar bə-máṣṭ-a, ŭ zlā́mē-m, qun b̰-məsā́s-a; gárəse-ma, sar nuxwī́n-a, ŭ avá-ma bə-xwī́n-a, ŭ Nəhrī́yo, rəh qusándī, ŭ Qəžžə́k̇ē, dūv kəšándī, ŭ Dáro, pal wašándī, ŭ Məšk̇o ʕAvdurraḥmā́no, sar bə-xwalī́-ya, ŭ Náze Nazadáne káṫa kuwárk̇a nīsk̇á-da; čū bē sar ŭ bē bərhā́n!’ K
contents.versio: 45. K‘Oh, I am ass a-griddled, and my daughter, her head is yogurty, and my husband, his arse is a-goaded; our millet, its head is droopy, and our water is bloody, and Goat, beard a-shorn, and Crow, tail a-plucked, and Tree, leaf a-shaken, and Abdurrahman Mouse, his face is ashen, and Baby Darling fell down into the lentil hopper; she is gone without a trace!’ K

contents.textus: 46. Háyoste moqaḏla ruḥa … lo+kuḏʕono. Basyo, haw kuḏʕono.
contents.versio: 46. That one set herself on fire … I don’t know. This is enough, I don’t know any more.

contents.textus: 1. Kaleyo Mar Duməṭ, hawi qadišo, u+abro du+šulṭònowa.
contents.versio: 1. There is St. Dometius, he became a saint, he was the sultan’s son.

contents.textus: 2. Qṭəlle ann+armnoye kulle. D ʔArzrum, qṭəlle ann+armnoye kulle. Lu+aġaṯṯe qṭilile, lo+kuḏʕono əšme mənyo.
contents.versio: 2. They killed all the Armenians. Of Erzurum, they killed all the Armenians. Their agha killed them, I don’t know what his name is.

contents.textus: 3. Də Ṣṭambəl ... ṣəlṭán Ḥamíd̥̚ qṭile də Ṣṭambəl ann+armnoye kulle.
contents.versio: 3. Of Istanbul ... Sultan Hamid killed all the Armenians of Istanbul.

contents.textus: 4. ṣəlṭán Ḥamíd̥̚ hawo, kuḏʕono əšme. Də Dyarbákərste lo+kuḏʕono əšme. Mbele šwaʕmo+zlamat armnoye ʕal u+pər dә Dyarbakər, nḥərre aš+šawʕo … šwaʕmo.
contents.versio: 4. That Sultan Hamid, I know his name. As for the one of Diyarbakır, I don’t know his name. He brought seven hundred Armenian men to the Diyarbakır bridge and slaughtered the seven … seven hundred.

contents.textus: 5. Ŭ daʕiri ʕal i+qriṯo, ay+yasire, an+naʕime, ax+xətyàr d̥xoṯi, qṭilənne.
contents.versio: 5. And they returned to the village, (i.e.,) the prisoners, children, elderly people like me, they killed them.

contents.textus: 6. Ŭ aǧ+ǧehəl, ak̇+k̇ačk̇at, hak̇a bgawre, ŭ hak̇a ṭlibe, mnayšne, ŭ hak̇a k̇aččək̇at, mhirənne bu+zōr, mhirənne.
contents.versio: 6. And the youth, the girls, whether married, or pledged, betrothed, or (just) girls, they married them (i.e., in the Muslim way) by force, they married them.

contents.textus: 7. U+abro du+šulṭono dә Dyarbakər qorewa bə Ṣṭambəl. Qorewa bə Ṣṭambəl Maktab̥, ṭălăbá, ṭălăbá du+maktab̥.
contents.versio: 7. The Sultan of Diyarbakır’s son was studying in Istanbul. He was studying at ‘Istanbul School’, a student, a school student.

contents.textus: 8. Yawmo ṣəlṭán Ḥamíd̥̚ komar, ‘Šaməʕno d̥fāš ḥappoṯe d̥ṣuroye bә Dyarbakər. Lázəmyo dməqšoʕi!’
contents.versio: 8. One day Sultan Hamid says, ‘I heard that some bits of Christians remained in Diyarbakır. They must be wiped out!’

contents.textus: 9. U+abro du+šulṭono dә Diyarbakər mqadamle, məḷḷe, ‘Ya ṣəlṭán, ono koḏaʕno, ono u+abro du+šulṭono dә Diyarbákərno. Koḏaʕno am+maġarat daṣ+ṣuroye áykone. U+ḥa d̥fā́šәste, dobatli ʕaskar, g̊ˠqoṭanne.
contents.versio: 9. The Sultan of Diyarbakır’s son approached him, he said, ‘Sultan, I know, I’m the Sultan of Diyarbakır’s son. I know where the caves of the Christians are. If even one remains, if you give me soldiers, I’ll kill him.

contents.textus: 10. E, ánnaqqa ṣə́dlele qadr omar, ‘Ṣafro, betfā́q, mbal aṭ+ṭằlăba du+maktab̥ kulle ʕam ruḥux ŭ ḥa lo+ṭorat!’
contents.versio: 10. Yes, now then, he honored him (lit. ‘he caught him honor’), he says, ‘Tomorrow morning, if nothing happens (lit. ‘without accident’, i.e., uneventfully), take all the students of the school with you and don’t spare anyone!’

contents.textus: 11. Qayəm, ŭ lə+ṭrele dəzze lutel, ŭ húlele ḥšamto basəmto.
contents.versio: 11. He got up, and he didn’t let him go to a hotel, and he gave him a nice dinner.

contents.textus: 12. Húlele ḥšamto basəmto ŭ madmaxle gab ruḥe, bi+oda … boda+ḥreto. Húlele oda naḏəfto.
contents.versio: 12. He served him a nice dinner and let him sleep by him, in the room … in another room. He gave him a clean room.

contents.textus: 13. Ŭ damixi. Damixi, aṯi malaxo Gabriʔél mi+šmayo.
contents.versio: 13. And they fell asleep. They fell asleep, the angel Gabriel came from heaven.

contents.textus: 14. Naḥət ʕal ṣadre. Omar, ‘U+ḥa d̥fāš me qmu+sayfo dbabux, quṭlaṭle? At+tarte+ʕaynayḏux gmofáqnanne’.
contents.versio: 14. He came down upon his chest. He says, ‘The one who survived your father's sword (lit. “from before’), you’ll kill him? I’ll put out both your eyes!’

contents.textus: 15. Səmle lo+səmle, omar, ‘Əlláh gmofaqno ʕaynux’. Ŭ lúlele darbo dmofaq ʕayne, ḥəngi mlaʕe ebe, omar, ‘ʕAyni lo+məfqatte. U+mede d̥kəbʕat, səm ebi!’
contents.versio: 15. No matter what he did, he says, ‘By God, I’ll put out your eyes!’ But he didn’t give him a way to put out his eyes, he begs him so much, he says, ‘My eyes, do not put them out. Whatever (else) you want, do to me!’

contents.textus: 16. Hăma brəmle u+garmo du+maġàz, dʕarquwe. Brəmle hawxa, ŭ ha, u+garmano du+maġàz, dʕarquwe, ha hano brəmle, hawxa səmle.
contents.versio: 16. Then he twisted the heel bone, of his heel. He twisted like so, and voila, that heel bone, of his heel, he twisted this here one, he did so.

contents.textus: 17. Nafəl k̇arăk̇ā́r aʕle, ŭ saləq li+šmayo. Omar, ‘U+ḥa d̥fāš me qmu+sayfo dbabux, quṭlaṭle?’
contents.versio: 17. He started screaming (lit. ‘a screaming and shouting fell upon him’), and he went up to heaven. He says, ‘The one who remained from your father's sword, are you going to kill him?

contents.textus: 18. ‘K̇ār ŭ k̇ār ŭ āy ŭ āy ŭ āy’. Qolo bi+arʕo, ḥa bi+šmayo.
contents.versio: 18. ‘Argh and argh and aye and aye and aye’, a sound on earth, one in heaven (i.e., he screamed so loud it could be heard in heaven).

contents.textus: 19. Ánnaqqa, e, mə‿g̊soyam? Konofaq, harke lə+ksōm idara. Nafəq lu+ṣalòn, kuzzé ŭ oṯe, lә+ksōm idara.
contents.versio: 19. Now then, right, what’ll he do? He goes out, he can’t manage here. He went out to the hallway, he comes and goes, he can’t manage.

contents.textus: 20. Azzeyo, nafəq lu+balqòn, lə+ksōm idara. K̇ār ŭ k̇ar, hul nafəq ṣəlṭán Ḥamíd̥, maḥəsle ʕal qole.
contents.versio: 20. He went, he went out to the balcony, he can’t manage. Argh and argh, until Sultan Hamid came out, he woke up from his noise.

contents.textus: 21. ‘He, abro, mə‿xēryo?’ Omar, ‘Ḥāl ŭ măsale. Ašə́r aṯili malaxo Gabriʔél’.
contents.versio: 21. ‘Oh, son, what’s up?’ He says, ‘This and that. Really, the angel Gabriel came to me!’

contents.textus: 22. Mə́ḷḷeli, ‘Ay+yasire d̥fayiši me qmu+sayfo dbabux, ʕaynux ʕal d̥quṭlatte, qušʕátteyo? At+tarte+ʕaynayḏux gmaṭə́ṇṇanne!’
contents.versio: 22. ‘He told me, “The prisoners who remained from (lit. ‘from before’) your father’s sword, do you have your eye on killing them, eradicating them? I shall knock out both your eyes!”’

contents.textus: 23. Lə+ṭreli maṭər ʕayni, ašə́r grəšle u+garmo du+maġàz, qṭíleli, idara lə+ksōmno.
contents.versio: 23. ‘I did not let him knock out my eyes, really, he pulled the heel bone, he killed me, I can’t manage’.

contents.textus: 24. ṣəlṭán Ḥamíd̥ madʕaḷḷe aʕle, məḷḷe, ‘Čara latlux! Lo ono kə́tlilux čara ŭ lo at+taxetər kətlux čara. Lázəmyo dəzzúx qəm ʕito daṣ+ṣuroye, quṭʕat tawbe. Zux, mḥalqat ruḥux ltor ŭ baxt dʕito mdaṣ+ṣuroye. Hăk̇a nāḥlux … naxwa ašə́r čara latlux. Taxetər, čara layt’.
contents.versio: 24. Sultan Hamid replied to him, he said, ‘There’s no cure! Neither can I help you, nor can the doctors. It is necessary for you to go to a Christian church and make (lit. ‘cut’) penance. Go, you’ll throw yourself to the mercy (lit. ‘protection and honor’) of one of the Christian churches (lit. ‘a church from one of the Christians’). If you get well … (great), otherwise, surely nothing can help you (lit. ‘there’s no cure for you’). Doctors, there’s no cure’.

contents.textus: 25. Qām azzeyo, zangīnwa. Mbele kallawat ġắlăbe ŭ səmle muklo, ʕazima li+ʕito d Urfa.
contents.versio: 25. He up and went, he was rich. He brought a lot of money and made a meal, a banquet for the church of Urfa.

contents.textus: 26. Mḥalaqle ruḥe ltōr ŭ baxt di+ʕito d Urfa, ŭ səmle muklone basime, ŭ mʕazamle i+walaye kula, ŭ daməx bgawa di+ʕito du+qadišo, ŭ húlele kallawat ġắlăbe lu+qadišo.
contents.versio: 26. He threw himself to the mercy (lit. ‘protection and honor’) of the church of Urfa, and made nice dishes, invited the whole city, slept inside the church of that saint, and gave a lot of money to the saint.

contents.textus: 27. I+brusk̇e nayiḥo, i+brusk̇e nayiḥo. Eló balé ṣắqaṭyo, ṣắqaṭyo, komaʕraǧ bәḥḏo+raġlo.
contents.versio: 27. The pain got better, the pain got better. But he is lame, he is lame, he is limping on one leg.

contents.textus: 28. Məḷḷe, ‘Bəṯr dǧarili hawxa, ono haw kosōmno aġatiye, ṣəlṭaniye! Ono g̊d̥oweno dayroyo, ʕabodo, g̊ˠqoreno, g̊d̥oweno mšiḥoyo’.
contents.versio: 28. He said, ‘After this happened to me, I’ll no longer act as agha, sultan (lit. ‘do aghahood, sultanhood’)! I’ll become a monk, a worshipper, I’ll study, I’ll become a Christian’.

contents.textus: 29. Məthaymalle bә Mšiḥo ŭ hawi dayroyo, hawi ʕabodo. Hawi qadišo. Kalayo uʕdo i+ʕito d Zāz, ʕal ə́šmeyo, Mar Duməṭ.
contents.versio: 29. He came to believe in Christ and he became a monk, a worshipper. He became a saint. Now there’s the church in Zaz, it’s in his name, St Dometius.

contents.textus: 30. Mar Duməṭ kalayo b Zāz. Hayo ʕal ə́šmeyo. Háyostene ... khūnk … d̥owutu šani sāġ, háwoste kamilo, hawxa.
contents.versio: 30. St Dometius, here it is in Zaz. That one’s in his name. That one too… you … you be well for me, that one is finished, like so.

contents.textus: 001. Kətwa, latwa, ṭaw̃ m Aloho latwa. Maru, ‘latwa’, mar ‘latwa’!
contents.versio: 001. There was and there wasn’t, there was none better than God. Say ‘there wasn’t’, say ‘there wasn’t’!

contents.textus: 002. Kətwa abro tăne b Walaṭé Məġurbiye. Əšme Mămoye Alá wa.
contents.versio: 002. There was an only son in the City of the West. His name was Mămo Ala.

contents.textus: 003. W Sǝtyá Zīn, i+barṯo du+malko dəGzírowa. I+barṯo du+malko dəGzírowa. A+treste...
contents.versio: 003. And Lady Zin was the King of Gziro’s daughter, she was the King of Gziro’s daughter. Both of them also...

contents.textus: 004. Kə́twayle l Mamó avayiye ʕal u+baḥar.
contents.versio: 004. Mămo had a house by the sea.

contents.textus: 005. (Ǧare bi+zmarto kəmmila. Ánnaqqa, kəmmutu, ‘Suryoyo maḷḷan’. E, ono… ǧare u+babo dan+naʕime omárwayla bi+zmarto.)
contents.versio: 005. (Sometimes they say it as the song. Now then, you say, ‘Tell us in Ṭuroyo’. Yes, I … sometimes the kids’ father would say it in a song).

contents.textus: 006. Ánnaqqa hawxa rḥímewayne, a+tre+tằnewayne, rḥímewayne. Rḥímewayne.
contents.versio: 006. Now then, they were so beloved, the two were only children, they were beloved. They were beloved.

contents.textus: 007. E, hawxa, laǧ+ǧənnat ṭʕənne. (Hawxa kəmmi, ono lo+kəḏʕono hawxa. I+təšʕiṯo háwxayo.) Laǧ+ǧənnat ṭʕənne i+ǧana… u+taxt d Sətyá Zīn, məblalle l Məġurbiye, Walaté Məġurbiye.
contents.versio: 007. Yes, so, jinns bore it… (They say so, I myself don’t know how. The story is like so.) The jinns bore the dea… Lady Zin’s bed, they brought it to the West, to the Western Country.

contents.textus: 008. Maḥatte u+taxtayḏa bi+oda d Mămoye Alá. Maḥtalle bi+oda d Mămoye Alá, maḥtalle bi+oda d Mămoye Alá.
contents.versio: 008. They put her bed in Mămo Ala’s room. They put her in Mămo Ala’s room, they put her in Mămo Ala’s room.

contents.textus: 009. Maḥəsla. Kaleyo zlām bi+odayḏa damixo! Hiya lo+kəḏʕo, kəmmo, ‘Man hat, u+abro dman hat kodəmxat bi+odayḏi? Nfaq mi+odayḏi!’
contents.versio: 009. She woke up. Here’s a man asleep in her room! She does not know, she says, ‘Who are you, whose son are you, sleeping in my room? Get out of my room!’

contents.textus: 010. Komar, ‘I+odàyḏiyo, latyo diḏax. Dīḏyo.’ Kəmmo, ‘Dīḏyo! Qum w nfaq mi+oda! Komar, ‘Ḳačḳo, dīḏyo!’ Komar, ‘Haḳa díḏaxyo, qray laǧ+ǧeriyayḏax.’
contents.versio: 010. He says, ‘It’s my room, it isn’t yours! It’s mine.’ She says, ‘It’s mine! Get up and get out of the room!’ He says, ‘Girl, it’s mine!’ He says, ‘If it’s yours, call your maidservants!’

contents.textus: 011. Koquryo laǧ+ǧeriyayḏa, kəmmo, ‘Faṭəm, ʕAyšo, ʕAyšo, Faṭəm, Faṭəm!’ k_Ba xwedé b̥ke!_k Faṭəm, ʕAyšo kăné bəGziro!
contents.versio: 011. She calls her maidservants, she says, ‘Fatima, Aisha, Aisha, Fatima, Fatima!’ Ha, that’ll happen! Fatima, Aisha, they are over here, in Gziro!

contents.textus: 012. W hiye kalé omar, ‘Ánnaqqa dawryo qoreno lan+naʕ … lag+greʕayḏi! Aḥmad, Aḥmad, Maḥmud, Maḥmud!’ Əmmi, ‘K_Ləbbe mire ma?_K’ Əmmi, ‘Mənyo u+ʕmirayḏan, u+hnayḏan?’
contents.versio: 012. And here he is saying, ‘Now it is time to call my boy… my servants! Ahmad, Ahmad, Mahmud, Mahmud!’ They say, ‘Oh dear, our prince?’ They say, ‘What is it, our prince, our whatsit?’

contents.textus: 013. Omar, ‘Ha ánnaqqa!’ Aḏiʕo. Aḏiʕo. Axər, səmane ǧəvate, pṣiḥi bəḥḏoḏe. W ǧġili ləḥḏoḏe, huwe sōz ʕam ḥḏoḏe dmiḥawli tavda w mḥalaffe aʕ+ʕisaqyotàṯṯeste.
contents.versio: 013. He says, ‘Now then, voilà!’ She understood, she understood. Finally, they broke the ice, they warmed up to one another. And they spoke to one another, they gave a promise to one another to move in together, and they exchanged their rings as well.

contents.textus: 014. L Mamó hule i+ʕisaqṯo l Sətyá Zīn. W l Sətyá Zīn hula i+ʕisaqṯo l Mămoye Alá. W čiki kul ḥa ʕal at+taxtaṯṯe, damixi.
contents.versio: 014. Mămo gave his ring to Lady Zin. And Lady Zin gave her ring to Mămo Ala. And each sneaked off to their beds, they fell asleep.

contents.textus: 015. Damixi. Áydarbo damixi, disa laǧ+ǧǝnnat ṭʕənne Sətyá Zīn, məblalle ləGziro.
contents.versio: 015. They fell asleep. As soon as they fell asleep, the jinns once again bore Lady Zin away, they took her to Gziro.

contents.textus: 016. Komaḥəs Mămoye Alá, koḥoyar, komar, ‘Málava, Ăḷo! Omárwayno u+ḥəlmano dahǝriyo ga šayṭaniyo’.
contents.versio: 016. Mămo Ala wakes up, he looks, he says, ‘Holy Moly, by God! I would say this dream is so straightforward it is plainly diabolical’.

contents.textus: 017. Kuzzé mašġiḏe w foṯe, koḥōr, ga kalá i+ʕisaqṯo d Sətyá Zīn ʕal ṣawʕe. Kalá i+ʕisaqṯo d Sətyá Zīn ʕal ṣawʕe.
contents.versio: 017. He went to wash his hands and face, he looks, there’s Lady Zin’s ring on his finger! There’s Lady Zin’s ring on his finger!

contents.textus: 018. E, koməqḥər, kosōm mṭala. Hiye kalé bi+Məġurbiye, w hiya kalá bəGziro qŏnáġ dšawʕo yarḥe, šwaʕ̬+šnaye. E, kosōm mṭala.
contents.versio: 018. Yes, he gets angry, he worries. Here he is in the West, and here she is in Gziro, a sojourn of seven months, seven years. Yes, he worries.

contents.textus: 019. W ánnaqqa ḥa tắneyoste. Koman … U+babo komanbahle ga komanqaṣle, komanqaṣle, kozăʕī́f w komanqaṣ, kosōm mṭala, hawxa kowe punə́ži.
contents.versio: 019. And now then, he is also the only one. He notic… His father notices him, look, he has faded away, he has faded away, he is growing thin and fading away, he is preoccupied, he is becoming so pensive.

contents.textus: 020. Omar, ‘Mămo, lawo, qayyo? Lhǝn mḥélelux?’ ‘Lo.’ ‘Ṭrele lebux?’ ‘Lo.’ ‘Mqatalle aʕmux?’ ‘Lo.’ ‘E qay bemaʕd hat?’
contents.versio: 020. He says, ‘Mămo, my boy, what’s up? Has someone beaten you?’ ‘No.’ ‘Offended you?’ ‘No.’ ‘Fought with you?’ ‘No.’ ‘So why are you listless?’

contents.textus: 021. Omar, ‘Yabo, dlo+mṭatli Sətyá Zīn, idara lə+ksōmno. Kosōmno mṭala d Sətyá Zīn, kobaʕno Sətyá Zīn.’
contents.versio: 021. He says, ‘Dad, if you don’t bring me Lady Zin, I can’t manage. I am preoccupied with Lady Zin, I want Lady Zin!’

contents.textus: 022. Omar, ‘Lawo, kale u+quṣrayḏux bayne falge+du+baḥar i+arʕayḏe ḳahrabánatyo u+qṭorayḏe marmaryo aš+šəbbaḳayḏe dsémone w hat ḥa tắnehat.
contents.versio: 022. He said: ‘My boy, Here’s your castle within the sea’s midst its ground is amber stones its ceiling is marble its windows are silver and you are the only one.

contents.textus: 023. Ono w emux hawina xətyár, kobaʕno dlo+ṭorat minan. Maltamno u+ahlayḏi kuuule, ksōmno daʕwo, w kulle lətmi. I+ḥḏo dǝbʕatla, huyo barṯo, huyo nxirayt<o>, ṭləb̥to, w huyo bgawro, gəmṭénuxyo.’ Omar, ‘De səm!’
contents.versio: 023. Your mother and I have become oldsters, I want you not to leave us. Let me gather my entire family, I’ll make a wedding feast, and all will gather. The one whom you want, be she a virgin, be she engaged, betrothed, and be she married, I shall bring you her.’ He says, ‘Come on, do it!’

contents.textus: 024. Səmle daʕwo tloṯo+yawme w tloṯo+lalye bi+dahole, bi+zərnaye, bu+muklo w bu+štoyo. W karəx tloṯo+yawme Mămó bayn i+daww… bayn i+govande. Lo, lə+ḥzele ḥḏo xudSətyá Zīn.
contents.versio: 024. He held a feast for three days and three nights with a dhol drum, a zurna horn, with food, and with drink. And Mămo went around for three days in the feas … in the line dance. No, he did not see anyone like Lady Zīn.

contents.textus: 025. Omar, ‘Yabo, ṭro mibarbzi. Maqbeli minux, ṭro mibarbzi kul ḥa lab+botaṯṯe. Ono lo+kobaʕno’. Mbarbzi, w bak+ḳeliḳat w bas+saʕat komanqaṣ.
contents.versio: 025. He said, ‘Dad, let them disperse! I am grateful to you, let every one of them disperse to their homes. I don’t want it.’ They dispersed, and moment by moment and hour by hour he grows thinner.

contents.textus: 026. E, áydarbo ktowe? Omar, ‘Ăḷé gəzzino.’ Rawəx ʕal u+səsyayḏe, azzeyo. Səmle lo+səmle lu+babo, lə+ṭrele … lo+kali. Azzé mə́ḷḷela li+ṗirayḏe, omar, ‘Ḳačḳo, Ăḷo u+abrayḏax kəmrastaq ʕal … ʕal Gziro. Izáx! Haḳa madʕaḷḷax … Nawxa Ăḷḷa azzeyo’.
contents.versio: 026. Yes, how does it go? He says, ‘By God, I shall go.’ He rode on his horse, he went away. No matter what his father did, he did not let … he did not stay. He went to tell his wife, he says ‘Girl, by God your son is heading to … to Gziro. Go! If you bring him back … Otherwise, by God, he is gone.’

contents.textus: 027. Azzá, ‘Lawo, ono w babux hawina xətyár, masulan. U+quṣrano lo+ṭoratle lan+noše! Walaṭé Məġurbiye basímoyo. Kalé bayne falge+du+baḥar ʕamiro u+quṣrayḏux. I+arʕayḏe ḳahrabánatyo. U+qṭorayḏe marmaryo. Aš+šəbbaḳayḏe dsémone. Lo, lo+ṭorat minan!’
contents.versio: 027. She went, ‘My boy, Your father and I have become oldsters, we have aged. Do not leave this castle to the people! The City of the West is pleasant. Here’s your castle built within the sea’s midst. Its ground is amber stones. Its ceiling is marble. Its windows are silver. No, do not leave us!’

contents.textus: 028. Səmle lo+səmle, omar, ‘Laybi.’ I+emo əmmo, əmmo, ‘Madā́m hat baslux minan, áḥnaste baslan minux. U+oġrayḏux lowe du+xēr’. W azzé.
contents.versio: 028. No matter what he did, he said: ‘I can’t’. The mother says, she says, ‘If you have had enough of us, then we also have had enough of you. May your fortune not be a good one!’ And he went.

contents.textus: 029. Azzé w azzé w azzé. Tlele qŭ́naġ w maḥatle ḥa, tlele qŭ́naġ w maḥatle ḥa, tlele qŭ́naġ w maḥatle ḥa. Azzéee w maṭi ləGziro.
contents.versio: 029. He went, and he went, and he went. He folded a camp and pitched one, he folded a camp and pitched one, he folded a camp and pitched one. He went and reached Gziro.

contents.textus: 030. Maṭi ləGziro. Kalayo Sətyá Zīn w aǧ+ǧeriyayḏa kulle ʕali+ʕayno, dkoqusri aǧ+ǧule, mašiġi aǧ+ǧule.
contents.versio: 030. He reached Gziro. Here’s Lady Zin and her maids, all of them at the spring, who are fulling clothes, washing clothes.

contents.textus: 031. Kané tamo, omar, ‘Ḳačḳát mṭēwli zarḳe dmaye šoteno. Mṭēwli zarḳe dmaye dšoteno’.
contents.versio: 031. There they are, he says, ‘Girls, bring me a bowl of water to drink, bring me a bowl of water to drink!’

contents.textus: 032. Li+barṯo d Băkoye ʕAwán mbélale zarḳe dmaye, li+barṯo d Băkoye ʕAwán mbélale zarḳe dmaye. Omar, ‘Lə+kšoteno dlo i+xatunayḏax bəxwá ǝmṭo. Dlo i+xatunayḏax bəxwá ǝmṭo, lə+kšoteno’. Əmmo, ‘Man haaat, u+abro dayna kalbo hat <di+barṯayḏi, di+ǧeri…> di+xatunayḏi əmṭolux maye?’
contents.versio: 032. Băko Awan’s daughter brought him a bowl of water, Băko Awan’s daughter brought him a bowl of water. He says, ‘I shall not drink unless your mistress herself brings it. Unless your mistress herself brings it, I shall not drink.’ She says, ‘Who are you, the son of which bitch are you, that <my daughter, my maidserv …> that my mistress should bring you water?!’

contents.textus: 033. Ba Mămoye Alá lə+ḥzele xabre hawxa. Hediḳa madʕaḷḷe qarʕa di+səsto, madʕaḷḷe qarʕa di+səsto, ddoʕar laxalf.
contents.versio: 033. Mămo Ala had not seen such things, right? He quietly turned his mare’s head, he turned his mare’s head to turn back.

contents.textus: 034. Li … li … Sətyá Zīn əmmo, ‘Hooo kīt w layt, hawo Mămoye Alayo! Izáx, basám lebe, adʕere.’
contents.versio: 034. She … she … Lady Zin says, ‘Oh, one way or another, that is Mămo Ala! Go soothe his heart, bring him back!’

contents.textus: 035. Azzá li+qamaytayḏe i+barṯo d Băkoye ʕAwán, šahr w šahrbazwa. ‘Ya, Mămoye Alá laḏiʕallux, mdageli’, ḥaša, ‘xili əḥre w ḥaṭyono. Šəbqono, kəbʕono duʕrat. Laḏiʕallux.’ Madʕaḷḷa.
contents.versio: 035. Băko Awan’s daughter went to meet him, she was a witch. ‘Oh Mămo Ala, I did not recognize you, I misspoke’, excuse me, ‘I ate shit and sinned. I am sorry, I want you to return. I did not recognize you’. She brought him back.

contents.textus: 036. Madʕaḷḷa, azzé baynaṯṯe hoool ʕaṣriye. ʕAṣriye azzeyo gab u+šəlṭono. Lo+maǧrele əzzé gabayye, azzé gab u+šəlṭono.
contents.versio: 036. She brought him back, he went along with them until evening. In the evening he went by the governor. He didn’t dare to go by them, (so) he went by the governor.

contents.textus: 037. U+šəlṭónoste omar, ‘De ṣafro gdomaṇṇo lu+ʕmiro. Zano nəfqina lu+sayrangə̀h. Rawxina ʕal as+səsyayḏan, əzzán lu+čolano w saymina sayrangə́h, marfina bəhn diḏan. W edi izúx gab Sətyá Zīn, disa gməǧġolutu.’
contents.versio: 037. The governor says, ‘In the morning, let me speak to the ruler. Let’s go out to the promenade. We shall ride our horses, go to this plain and do a promenade, we shall take our rest. And then go by Lady Zina, you will talk again’.

contents.textus: 038. Azzeyo … nafiqi, rawixi ʕal as+səsyaṯṯe w azzehən lu+čōl. W mballe, mṭalle as+səsyaṯṯe, rahiṭi w axər səmme kēf.
contents.versio: 038. He went … they went out, they rode their horses and went to the plain. They took and brought back their horses, they ran, and in the end they enjoyed themselves.

contents.textus: 039. L Băkoye ʕAwán mə́ḷḷele lu+ʕmiro dəGziro, omar, ‘Qay lo+kəḏʕat hawxa mənyo?’ Omar, ‘Mənyo?’ Omar, ‘Ašə́r kaleyo, kaleyo Mămoye Alá gab Sətyá Zīn.’ ‘Haaa, mawxa!’
contents.versio: 039. Bako Awan told the ruler of Gziro, he says, ‘How don’t you know what is so?’ He says, ‘What is it?’ He says, ‘Mamo Ala is by Lady Zin’. ‘Ahhh, so that’s it!’

contents.textus: 040. Aṯi, aṯi, kalá bi+odaḳayḏe. Lo+qadər dqoyam, čiko taḥt u+kurkəd Mămoye Alá. Čiko taḥt u+kurk d̚ Mămoye Alá, ba aṯi u+ʕmiro dəGziro. W lo+qām mequme, lo+qadər qōm mequme, lo+qadər qōm mequme.
contents.versio: 040. He came, he came, and here she is in his room. He couldn’t get up, she had sneaked under Mamo Ala’s fur coat, she had sneaked under Mamo Ala’s fur coat, the ruler of Gziro came, right? He did not get up in front of him, he could not get up in front of him, he could not get up in front of him.

contents.textus: 041. Maṭi u+xabro lu+waziro, maṭi u+xabro lu+waziro. Omar, ‘Zax!’ Mə́ḷḷale li+ṗirayḏe. Omar, ‘Hat ʕraq! W ono gmōdno lu+sayfo, gdoṯeno bəṯrax. Haḳa ínaqqa ... mar, ‘Aaaʕaw, hăwara, ʕmiro! Aṯi dqoṭeli, u+waziro qqoṭeli!’ Haḳa ínaqqayo qoyam doṯe lafelax, edi Sətyá Zīn (kə́twayla šaboḳo haqqa bayn li+oda du+babo w li+odayḏa) gəzzá li+odayḏa.’
contents.versio: 041. Word reached the vizier, word reached the vizier. He says, ‘Go!’ His wife told him. He says, ‘Hey you, run away! And I will take the sword, I shall come after you. If then … say, ‘Waaah, help, ruler! He came to kill me, the vizier will kill me!’ If then he gets up to come to your side, then Lady Zin (she had a window yea large between her father’s room and her room) will go to her room.’

contents.textus: 042. Azzá i+žənḳe, ʕariqo, ʕariqo, rahiṭo lu+tarʕo du+ʕmiro. Əmmo, ‘Hăwara, ʕmiro, lu+waziro qṭíleli.’ Qām li+qamaytayḏa. Sətyá Zīn ǝmmo čəp, mḥalaqla ruḥa bu+šaboḳo li+odaḳayḏa.
contents.versio: 042. The wife went, she fled, she fled, she ran to the ruler’s door. She says, ‘Help, ruler, the vizier has attacked me.’ He got up to meet her. Lady Zin goes ‘Hup!’, she tossed herself through the window into her room.

contents.textus: 043. Mḥalaqla ruḥa li+odaḳayḏa. Henuḳa qām Mămoye Alá, azzé li+qamayto du+ʕmiro, ba lo+maqbele. Lo+maqbele.
contents.versio: 043. She tossed herself into her room. At that moment Mamo Ala got up, he went to meet the ruler, he would not receive him, right? He would not receive him.

contents.textus: 044. Hawxa bəhno mašəkle, mašəkle. Azzé, mḥalaqle a+tre li+biro. Mḥalaqqe Mămoye Alá w Sətyá Zīn, a+tre li+biro…
contents.versio: 044. So he realized it, he realized. He went, he tossed them both into the well. They tossed Mamo Ala and Lady Zin, both of them, into the well…

contents.textus: 045. (I+biro kalá bu+darbo dəGziro, dkuzzə́n an+nošayḏan, əzzənwa mbliwa, mbliwa dibəs lu+zebono, medone, abišoṯe, dibəs. Kalá bdarbayye. Hawən tre+šətlat drǝḥanat, tre+šətlat drǝḥanat hawxa. W Băkoye ʕAwán marfele ruḥe bayn la+tre, hawi, hawi ʕulto, kubo, hawi kubo.)
contents.versio: 045. (The well is over here on the way to Gziro, where our people would go, they went to take, to take grape syrup for sale, stuff, raisins, grape syrup. It’s over here on their way. They became two shoots of basil, two shoots of basil like so. And Bako Awan insinuated himself between the two, he became, he became a thorn bush, a spiny plant, he became a spiny plant.)

contents.textus: 046. … hol dmašəkle lu+waziro. Azzé mə́ḷḷalle, mašəkle d … kǝnne bi+hno, azzé qrélalle. Əmmi, ‘Haw towe ʕal ʕəmran, bayïqina, bayïqina, ktowina harke, bayïqina.’ Băkoye ʕAwanste mḥalaqle ruḥe, hawi kubo w yaʕi.
contents.versio: 046. … until the vizier realized it. He went to tell them, he realized that … here they are in the whatsit, he went to call them. They say, ‘It no longer makes sense at our age, we became decrepit, we became decrepit, we shall be here, we became decrepit.’ Bako Awan also tossed himself, he became a spiny plant and sprouted up.

contents.textus: 047. Aḥunoni imalle, əmmi, ‘Azzáno, kalá disa … kalá šətlo drǝḥane harke, w ḥḏo harke, w bu+falgaṯṯe kīt ʕulto.’
contents.versio: 047. My brothers swore, they say, ‘We went, here it is again … here’s a sprout of basil right here, and one here, and in the middle there’s a thorn bush.’

contents.textus: 048. Ono lə+ḥzeli, hawxa kəmmi, ono hawxa šamiʕono. Balki šamiʕūtla bdəkoṯe hēš, ono hawxa šamiʕono. Ánnaqqa bi+kurmanǧi kəmmila, komərxila. Ánnaqqa hatu kəmmutu, ‘Səryoyo máḷḷanyo.’ Hawxa, hawxa šamiʕono.
contents.versio: 048. As for me, I haven’t seen it, they say so, I heard so. Perhaps you heard it in other places, as for me, I heard it like so. Now then, they say it in Kurmanji, they prolong it. Now then, you say, ‘Tell it to us in Ṭuroyo’. So, I heard it like so.

contents.textus: 1. Mar Barṣawmo, riše dabile, yatúmowa.
contents.versio: 1. St Barṣawmo, the chief of the mourners, was an orphan.

contents.textus: 2. U+babo māṯ, i+emo šqila ḥreno, ŭ mbela ʕam ruḥa. Ḥəfla ŭ mašəġla, hawi tlaṯ+šnaye.
contents.versio: 2. His father died, his mother married another man, and she took him with her. She washed and rinsed him, he turned three years old.

contents.textus: 3. Azzé, qrele ŭ kṯule, qrele ŭ kṯule.
contents.versio: 3. He went away, he read and wrote, he read and wrote.

contents.textus: 4. Saləq yawmo li+goro, behn diḏe ʕayəq.
contents.versio: 4. One day, he climbed up to the roof, he was bored (lit. ‘his breath became tight’).

contents.textus: 5. Šaməʕ̥ qole dar+ruʕye. Kəmmina d̥koṯən kəmṭən aḥ+ḥayewən mu+ṭuro. Ar+ruʕye, kəmmina, komarʕәn aʕ+ʕeze bu+ṭuro, kuḏʕat, kofǝhmat?
contents.versio: 5. He heard shepherds’ voices. (That’s what) we call those who come and bring their animals from the hill country. Shepherds, we say, they pasture goats in the hill country, you know, you understand?

contents.textus: 6. Aṯən, azzé, omar, ‘Kazzí gabayye dməštaʕeno tre+xabre aʕmayye, behn diḏi rowaḥ’.
contents.versio: 6. They came, he went, he says, ‘I’m about to go to them to play a little bit (lit. ‘two words’) with them, to relax (lit. ‘to expand my breath’).

contents.textus: 7. Ak+kalbe dar+ruʕye ḥzalle, he lar+ruʕye lə+ḥzalle, ak+kalbe ḥzalle, azzéhəlle.
contents.versio: 7. The shepherds’ dogs saw him, the shepherds haven’t seen him yet, the dogs saw him, they went to him.

contents.textus: 8. Azzéhəlle, mədde, ŭ xəḷḷe, ŭ nkətte, ŭ mgavlačče.
contents.versio: 8. They went to him, grabbed him, ate him, bit him, and squished him.

contents.textus: 9. Xaləṣ karwan bu+qawlawo bi+qriṯayo. Əmmi, ‘ʕáǧaba hano arnuwe ṣǝdle, hano taʕle ṣǝdle u+qa…ak+kalbani hawxa kosaymi’.
contents.versio: 9. A caravan was passing on that stint by that village. They say, ‘I wonder, did this one catch hares (i.e., did these ones catch a hare), did this one catch foxes (i.e., did these ones catch a fox), and so many… these dogs are doing so?’

contents.textus: 10. K̬madiqi ʕul mu+syoġo, bi+arʕo kḥayri ga kalé zʕuro bayn al+lappat dak+kalbe, kalé zʕuro bayn al+lappat dak+kalbe.
contents.versio: 10. They glance over the fence, they look at the ground, hey, there’s a boy in the dogs’ paws, there’s a boy in the dogs’ paws.

contents.textus: 11. Azzehən. Aḥ+ḥaṭroṯaṯṯe, žxwa, ḥaṭro d̥qayse kowe aʕmayye d̥koqulʕi a+ḥmore, kətwa ḥaṭroṯe aʕmayye, mlalle qəm ṣadrayye kefe.
contents.versio: 11. They went. Their staves, of course, there’s a wooden staff with them to drive donkeys, they had staves with them, they have gathered armfuls of stones.

contents.textus: 12. Ŭ azzə́n, maḥatte ʕal ak+kalbanək, maḥtǝnne. Maḥatte, maḥatte, maḥatte aʕlayye, šqəlle u+zʕuro mənne.
contents.versio: 12. And they went, they fell upon those dogs, they put them down. They fell, fell, fell upon them, they took the boy away from them.

contents.textus: 13. Šqəlle u+zʕuro mənne. Koḥayri, mətwile, lo admo, lo naparušk̇e, lo aǧ+ǧulayḏe qṭiʕi, lo mede, xud ruḥe.
contents.versio: 13. They took the boy away from them. They take a look, they sit him up, neither blood, nor a scratch, nor his clothes torn, nor anything at all, like himself (i.e., like he was before).

contents.textus: 14. Əmmi, ‘Komt̬ʰaymnina b Aloho’. Ḥa mənne, ‘Hano u+ṭowo d Alóhoyo, dak+kalbani hawxa səmme ebe ŭ lo+ǧarile mede’.
contents.versio: 14. They say, ‘We believe in God’. One of them, ‘This is God’s blessed, that these dogs did so to him and nothing happened to him’.

contents.textus: 15. U+ḥreno komar, ‘Komt̬ʰaymanno, b Aloho, d̥kətyo hano qadišo rabo, dak+kalbe hawxa səmme u+ʕaǧobano ebe, lo aǧ+ǧulayḏe qṭiʕe, ŭ lo ǧarūd̥k̇e, lə+nkətte, lo admo xār mine. Hano ṭowo d Alóhoyo’.
contents.versio: 15. Another one says, ‘I believe, by God, that he is a great saint, that the dogs did this strange thing to him like so, neither are his clothes torn, nor (is there) a small wound, nor did they bite him, nor did his blood shed. This is God’s blessed’.

contents.textus: 16. Ŭ azzehən, azzehən, aṯi híyeste lu+bayto, aṯi lu+bayto, lo+bmede. Malaxle, omar, ‘Gəzzí li+barriye, ʕobadno šan Aloho’.
contents.versio: 16. And they went away, they went away, but he came home, he came home, in no time at all (lit. ‘not by anything’). He walked, he says, ‘I shall go to the wilderness and worship on God’s behalf’.

contents.textus: 17. Malaxle, azzé li+barriye. Laqi lnahro dmaye, nahro kobe pelat, maye semoqe. Kozayəʕ̥, mdayšalle lu+baxyo, yatu, mdayšalle lu+baxyo. Lo+maǧrele moḥe bayn am+mayanək, naʕímowa.
contents.versio: 17. He walked, he went to the wilderness. He encountered a river, the river has waves, reddish water. He had become scared, he started crying, he sat down, he started crying. He didn’t dare plunge into that water, he was a child.

contents.textus: 18. Mdayšalle lu+baxyo. L Aloho mtarasle malaxo, məḷḷe, ‘Zux, šāl be i+niyayḏe mənyo’.
contents.versio: 18. He started crying. God sent an angel to him, he said, ‘Go and ask him what his intention is’.

contents.textus: 19. U+malaxo naḥət xud i+stune mi+šmayo, mḥele ruḥe bŭwā́r di+ṭalane. Səmle ruḥe nošo, ŭ azzé gabe bu+šəklayḏe.
contents.versio: 19. The angel went down like a pillar from the sky, and he threw himself in front of a thicket. He made himself a human, and he went to him in his likeness.

contents.textus: 20. Komar, ‘Šlomo aʕlux, abro! Mə‿kosaymat harke, brazi, abro?’ Komar, ‘B̥šayno, bәšlomo, ʕammo, b̥xēr aṯət, may‿koṯat?’ Omar, ‘Ma mə‿kosaymat harke?’
contents.versio: 20. He says, ‘Peace upon you, my son! What are you doing here, nephew, son?’ He says, ‘Hello, welcome, uncle, peace be upon you, where are you coming from?’ He says, ‘What are you doing here?’

contents.textus: 21. Mdayšalle lu+baxyo, omar, ‘Ono zʕuro, yatúmono, babi māṯ, emi šqila ḥreno ŭ mbélali ʕam ruḥa. Uʕdo kobaʕno əzzino, ṣoyamno, mṣaleno šan Aloho’.
contents.versio: 21. He started crying, he says, ‘I am a child, an orphan, my father has died, my mother took another one and took me with her. Now I want to go, to fast, to pray on God’s behalf’.

contents.textus: 22. Omar, ‘Yaʕni gdobat ṣōz, ddoʕat ŭ mṣalat šan Aloho?’ Omar, ‘Ṣōzyo. Hul d̥kətli ʕəmro, ono mṣaleno ŭ mṣaleno, ṣoyamno šan Aloho’.
contents.versio: 22. He says, ‘Like, do you give me your word that you will bless and pray on God’s behalf?’ He says, ‘It’s a promise. As long as I have life, I shall keep praying and praying, fasting on God’s behalf’.

contents.textus: 23. Omar, ‘D‿itúx bəṯri’. Azzé bəṯre, mbele. Omar, ‘Naʕímohat, dǝzzúx li+barriye, gməšḥoṭat. Izúx, gəmbannux ldayro’.
contents.versio: 23. He says, ‘Come on, come after me’. He went after him, he took him. He says, ‘You are a child, if you go to the wilderness, you’ll get dehydrated. Go, I’ll take you to a monastery’.

contents.textus: 24. Azzé, mbele ldayro, kal kīt dayroye ŭ məlfone ŭ rīšdayroyo, ʕam i+ʕaṣriye, ʕam u+noqušo dʕaṣriye. Drele šlomo. ‘B̥šayno, bәšlomo, ʕammo. Xēryo?’
contents.versio: 24. He went, he brought him to a monastery, here there are monks and teachers and an abbot, in the evening, with the evening bell (i.e., at 6 pm). He extended greetings. ‘You’re welcome, (come) in peace, uncle. How are you (lit. ‘is it good’)?’

contents.textus: 25. Omar, ‘Ašə́r, u+zʕurano yatúmoyo. Ŭ māṯ u+babo, ŭ li+emo šqila ḥreno, kubʕo, kubʕo… Kobaʕ̥ d̥koṯaw ŭ qore, yolaf dәmṣale šan Aloho’.
contents.versio: 25. He says, ‘Really, this boy is an orphan. And his father died, and his mother married another man, she wants, she wants... He wants to read and write, to learn to pray for God’s sake’.

contents.textus: 26. Ḥǝrre ga zʕuro xušk̇o, hawxa lavhati ŭ saxi. Omar, ‘ʕAla ʕayne, ʕammo, ʕala ʕayne!’
contents.versio: 26. They looked, here’s a beautiful young man, so good-looking and complaisant. He says, ‘At your service (lit. ‘upon eyes’), uncle, at your service!’

contents.textus: 27. Lǝḏʕiwa d̥kətyo malaxo. Omar, omar, ‘Kazzí bxa<ṭәr dәṯxu>, fayšutu bәšlomo!’ Əmmi, ‘ʕAmmo, ʕaṣríyeyo, gəzzúx layko? Fuš ádlalyo gaban’. Omar, ‘Ašə́r, gəzzino. Lo+ḥaruli’. Saləq. Nafəq i+darga ŭ hawi xud̥ stune, saləq li+šmayo u+malaxo.
contents.versio: 27. They did not know that he was an angel. He says, he says, ‘I am going by <your leave>, goodbye!’ They say, ‘Uncle, it is evening, where are you going? Stay with us tonight’. He says, ‘Really, I’ll go. It doesn’t bother me’. He went up. He went through the gate and became like a pillar, the angel went up to heaven.

contents.textus: 28. Fāš u+zʕuro gabayye. Ánnaqqa meqəm ṣopat mani latwa. Sōmwa i+nuraṯṯe, konašwa u+qaṭmaṯṯe, ŭ mṭéwalle maye, sōmwa k̇elik̇at ʕal iḏayye, qorewa ŭ koṯáwwaste.
contents.versio: 28. The boy stayed with them. Now then, back then there were none of these stoves (lit. ‘stoves from these’). He would do their fires, sweep their ashes, and bring water to them, do chores at their command (lit. ‘their hands’), he would also read and write.

contents.textus: 29. Qrele, kṯule, hawi šamošo. Mi+šamošuṯo hawi dayroyo. Mu+dayroyo hawi rīš̬dayroyo. Hawi rīšdayroyo. Arbʕi+dayroye nafəl taḥt iḏe.
contents.versio: 29. He read, he wrote, he became a deacon. From deaconship, he became a monk. From the monk, he became an abbot. He became an abbot. Forty monks fell under his control (lit. ‘hand’).

contents.textus: 30. Ánnaqqa u+ʕamo xd‿i+măsale duʕdo nafəlwa baḥ+ḥṭohe, nafəlwa baḥ+ḥtohe. Əzzewa kul+lalyo lәqriṯo, korazwa aʕlayye, mofaqwa ... madʕárwalle mšiḥoye.
contents.versio: 30. Now then, people, just like today’s situation, they had fallen into sin (lit. ‘the sins’), they had fallen into sin. He would go every night to a village, he would preach to them, he would cast out… he would turn them back into Christians.

contents.textus: 31. Yawmo mḥele b̥qarʕe d̥ṭuro. Kətwa qriṯo b̥qarʕe d̥ṭuro, mḥele bi+kaše. Naqqa aṣ+ṣalme, aʕ+ʕasekər daṣ+ṣalme šridi, əmmi, ‘Kaṯi Barṣawmo, kmazər aṣ+ṣalmayḏan’. Ŭ šridi ʕam gabe, ŭ mčanqalle ad+dargat dlo+ʕəbri ... dlo+ʕobar li+walaye.
contents.versio: 31. One day, he struck off for a mountaintop. There was a village on a mountaintop, he struck off for the slope. At once, the idols, the idols’ soldiers followed, they say, ‘Barsawmo has come, he harms our idols!’ And they followed by his side, and bolted the gates so they don’t enter … he doesn’t enter the city.

contents.textus: 32. Omar, ‘Darban raḥúqoyo, kobaʕno mənxu d̥fətḥutu ad+dargat. Aḥna šafóʕena ŭ silaḥe latlan ŭ lə+k̬maze<nna>…’ Əmmi, ‘Dlo+mazirat aḥna ŭ aṣ+ṣalmayḏan’. Omar, ‘Ašə́r, lə+gmazərno lo hatu ŭ lo aṣ+ṣalmaṯxu, ono zlām ʕabódono, kobaʕno d̥fətḥutu ad+dargat, šafóʕena, gəzzano’.
contents.versio: 32. He says, ‘Our way is distant, I want you to open the gates. We are passers-by and we don’t have any weapons with us and we won’t har<m>...’ They say, ‘If you don’t harm us and our idols’. He says, ‘Really, I won’t harm either you or your idols, I’m a man of worship, I want you to open the gates, we are passers-by, we shall go’.

contents.textus: 33. Hedik̇a ftəḥḥe ad+dargat, azzé hul fəlga di+walaye, komalxi ʕam gabe. Omar, ‘Uʕdo, məǧġalno xabro du+šayno. Mə‿kəmmutu?’ Əmmi, ‘Dməǧġolat, dlo+mazirat aṣ+ṣalmayḏan, məǧġál!’
contents.versio: 33. Then they opened the gates, he went as far as the center of the city, they are walking at his side. He says, ‘Now, I’ll say something peaceful (lit. ‘a word of peace’). What do you say?’ They say, ‘If you speak, if you don’t harm our idols, speak!’

contents.textus: 34. Omar, ‘ʕÁǧaba, uʕdo ʕal mə‿kowutu idara b̥qarʕe du+ṭurano našifo? ʕAl mə‿kowutu idara?’
contents.versio: 34. He says, ‘I wonder, on what do you manage on this dry mountaintop? On what do you manage?’

contents.textus: 35. Əmmi, ‘Ašə́r, ġắlăbe hawina šapərzá. Hani arbaʕ+əšnaye maṭro laṯilan, ŭ an+nahrat raḥúqene. Kuzzano baṫ+ṫanak̇e, bas+sablat, ba+ḥmore, kəmṭina maye. Ġắlăbe hawina šapərzá’.
contents.versio: 35. They say, ‘Really, we became very miserable. Rain hasn’t come these four years, and the rivers are far away. We go with canisters, with panniers, with donkeys, we bring water. We became very miserable’.

contents.textus: 36. Omar, ‘Uʕdo ṭolabno mu+alohayḏi doṯe maṭro aʕlayxu. Lo+kәmt̬haymnutu ebe?’ Əmmi, ‘Bele’. Ġắlăbe aṯile ʕәšq.
contents.versio: 36. He says, ‘Now I’ll ask my God for rain to fall (lit. ‘come’) upon you. Don’t you believe in him?’ They say, ‘Indeed’. He became very happy (lit. ‘a great happiness came to him’).

contents.textus: 37. Hiye ŭ ann+arbʕi dayroyayḏe čiki b̥ḥarbo, mṣalalle ŭ brəkke ŭ ṭləbbe, ‘Ya u+morayḏan, dhat marḥmat ʕal i+walayaṯe, balki mhaymni’.
contents.versio: 37. He and his forty monks sneaked into the ruins, they prayed, kneeled down, and petitioned, ‘O, our lord, if you have mercy upon this city, perhaps they will believe’.

contents.textus: 38. ‘Ma i+saʕaye ba məqqa?’ Omar, ‘I+saʕaye bat+tarte ŭ falge’. Hedik̇a hawyo tarte du+lalyo, pežən lawi. Ánnaqqa ḥəngi d Mar Barṣawmo brəkle, mṣalele, baṭəl, marfele hawxa, gnele hawxa ʕal i+anišk̇ayḏe. Ḥəlle, ḥzele kәkwo bi+šmayo. Omar, ‘Xud̥ koḥozeno u+kәkwano bi+šmayo, Alóhoste koḥozeli mžido’.
contents.versio: 38. ‘What time is it (lit., ‘how much the hour?’, i.e., when will it rain?)’. He says, ‘At half past two’. Then, it became two at night, and there wasn’t any trace. Now then, so much did St Barsawmo pray, kneel, he became tired, he let up like so, he leaned like so on his elbow. He looked, he saw a star in the sky. He says, ‘Just as I see this star in the sky, God also sees me stretched out’.

contents.textus: 39. Arbaʕ ŭ ḥamši+šnaye səmle ʕəmro, lә+mžīd ŭ lo+daməx. Maḥatwa qariše dab+baṣmore ʕal ḥaṣe dlo+domax ŭ mḥalaqwa u+ḥawlo lkaṯpoṯe, fōšwa qimo dayəm qəm Mšiḥo.
contents.versio: 39. He was forty-five years old (lit. ‘forty-five years he did life’), he hadn’t stretched out or lain down. He would put straps of nails on his back so he wouldn’t lie down, and he would toss a rope onto his shoulders, he would always stay upright before Christ.

contents.textus: 40. Omar, ‘Ăḷ... Mšiḥo…xud̥ ḥzeli u+kәkwawo, lә Mšíḥoste ḥzéleli mžido’.
contents.versio: 40. He says, ‘By Go... Christ… just as I saw that star, Christ also saw me stretched out’.

contents.textus: 41. Qayəm, dʕele, ṭləble. Hawi saʕaye ḥḏo, ḥḏo ŭ falge, tarte. Əmmi, ‘Haaa, Barṣawmo mdaglono! Koyo u+maṭro dl Aloho mṭelelan? U+alohayḏux, koyo?’
contents.versio: 41. He stood up, he prayed, he petitioned. It turned one o’clock, one and a half, two o’clock. They say, ‘Aha! Barsawmo the deceiver! Where is the rain that God has brought us? Your God, where is he?’

contents.textus: 42. Naqqa qayimo i+hawa taḥtayto baq+qudrat d Aloho. Ŭ aṯən aʕ+ʕaywe xd‿aq+qatore, ŭ hawən aṭ+ṭavat ŭ mḥele lu+maṭro.
contents.versio: 42. At once the east wind (lit. ‘lower wind’) rose through God’s powers. And clouds like boulders were coming, and thunderstorms were appearing, and the rain hit.

contents.textus: 43. Bat+tarte ŭ falge dmərre, mḥele lu+maṭro, arbʕo+yawme ŭ arbʕo+lalye. Malən ag+gubone, malən ab+bašqoqone, malən hne.
contents.versio: 43. At half past two, as they said, rain struck, four days and four nights. The cisterns filled up, the alleys filled up, some whatsits filled up.

contents.textus: 44. Kəmmi, ‘Barṣawmo, marle lu+alohayḏux dәmbaṭal u+maṭrano’. Omar, ‘Ašə́r dlo+tawrutu aṣ+ṣalmaṯxu, suġḏútəlle, ṭoreno dmaḥrawxu’. Azzə́n twərre.
contents.versio: 44. They say, ‘Barsawmo, tell your God to stop this rain’. He says, ‘Really, if you do not break your idols, worship him, I’ll let him destroy you’. They went, they broke them.

contents.textus: 45. Maṭi u+xabro lu+qašo, lu+qašaṯṯe… Kə́twayle tarte+bnoṯe, ġắlăbe roḥámwalle, u+qašaṯṯe.
contents.versio: 45. The news reached the priest, their priest… He had two daughters, he loved them very much, their priest.

contents.textus: 46. Nafiqi li+qamaytayḏe, əmmi, ‘Barṣawmo, mǝ‿kubʕat? Manqaṣlux i+ʕaskar dbabayna’. Omar, ‘Klawu bdukṯayxu’.
contents.versio: 46. They went out to meet him, they say, ‘Barsawmo, what do you want? You have reduced our father’s army!’ He says, ‘Stand still in place (lit. ‘on your place’)’.

contents.textus: 47. Zriʕi bayn li+arʕo ŭ li+šmayo. Fayiši hawxa, haykle. Lappe lo+məǧġoli, lo+qaymi, lo…haw… Fayiši hawxa haykle.
contents.versio: 47. They froze between the earth and heaven. They remained so, statues. They can neither talk, nor get up, nor … anymore. They remained so, statues.

contents.textus: 48. Maṭi u+xabro lu+qašo, u+qašo ġắlăbe roḥamwa a+bnoṯe. Aṯi, mžīd qəm raġle d Mar Barṣawmo. Maḥatle u+ʕafro draġle d Mar Barṣawmo ʕal qarʕe druḥe ŭ sġəḏle l Mar Barṣawmo, omar, ‘Kobaʕno d̥šorat a+bnoṯayḏi’. Omar, ‘Məšrewu!’ Naqqa šarən.
contents.versio: 48. The news reached the priest, the priest loved his daughters very much. He came, stretched out before the feet of St Barsawmo. He put the dirt of St Barsawmo’s feet on his head, and he bowed down to St Barsawmo, he says, ‘I want you to release my daughters’. He says, ‘Be released!’ At once they got released.

contents.textus: 49. Ŭ azzə́n, edi twərre aṣ+ṣalmaṯṯe ŭ mət̬haymanne, mət̬haymanne bә Mšiḥo ŭ hawən səryoye. kŬ hun žә mə ra sāġ.k
contents.versio: 49. And they went, then they broke their idols and believed, they believed in Christ and became Christians. kAnd you be well for me!k

contents.textus: 001. Əmmi, kətwa Ndaṯalo b Ḥəmməṣ.
contents.versio: 001. They say there was a Theotokos [church] in Homs.

contents.textus: 002. Ánnaqqa ašə́r lo+kəḏʕono əšme, məḷḷe, mə́ḷḷali, lo+kəḏʕono əšme. U+šulṭono d Ḥəmməṣ mšiḥóyowa. Me gab ruḥe kul šato, kul šato, kul šato sōmwa u+šahrayḏa. Me gab ruḥe.
contents.versio: 002. Now then, really, I do not know his name, he said… she told it to me. I do not know his name, the Sultan of Homs was a Christian. On his own every year, every year, every year he would do her feast day. On his own.

contents.textus: 003. Zowanwa nune laḥ+ḥasye ŭ lad+dayroye. Ŭ zowanwa baṣro lan+noše. Saymiwa u+šahro, yani saymiwa u+šahrayḏa. Mšahríwayle.
contents.versio: 003. He would buy fish for the bishops and monks. And he would buy meat for the people. They would do the feast day, like, they would do her feast day. They would celebrate it.

contents.textus: 004. Lo xd‿uʕdo, raqḏo, zmoro, ŭ medone. Qole di+ʕito, qroyo da+kṯowe, ŭ ṣluṯo, ŭ kraza, ŭ qole daš+šamoše, ŭ hawxa.
contents.versio: 004. Not like now, dancing, singing, and such things. Church hymns, reading the books, worship, sermons, deacons’ singing, and such.

contents.textus: 005. Qole di+ʕito əmmiwa. Saymiwa u+šahrayḏa; dayroye, ḥasye, qaše, ʕulmoye oṯənwa.
contents.versio: 005. They would sing church hymns. They would do her feast day; monks, bishops, priests, and laypeople would come.

contents.textus: 006. Azzé lu+šulṭono, mə́ḷḷele, la+greʕe məḷḷe, ‘Zoxu lu+baḥar, gab aṣ+ṣayode, amṭewu nune lad+dayroye ŭ laḥ+ḥasye, lo+kuxli baṣro’.
contents.versio: 006. The sultan went, he told him, he tells the servants, ‘Go to the sea, by the fishermen, bring fish for the monks and bishops, they don’t eat meat’.

contents.textus: 007. Ḥa abro kə́twayle. Ḥa abro kə́twayle, rḥímowa. Rḥímowa. Dəmmina, xd‿uʕdo, xd̥ano diḏan, duʕdo aṯi larke.
contents.versio: 007. He had one son. He had one son, he was beloved. He was beloved. Let’s say, like now, like our boy who just came here.

contents.textus: 008. Azzé aʕmayye. Azzé aʕmayye, tqəlle an+nunaṯṯe, mṭənne… gab aṣ+ṣayode, feme du+baḥar. Səmme, lo+səmme, u+zʕuro laṯi.
contents.versio: 008. He went with them. He went with them, they weighed their fish, they brought them… by the fishermen, the seashore. No matter what they did (lit. ‘they did, they didn’t’), the boy didn’t come back.

contents.textus: 009. E, rḥímowa. Lə+ṭralle lebe. Lə+ṭralle lebe, laṯi. Áydarbo g̊d̥owe?
contents.versio: 009. Yes, he was beloved. They didn’t upset him (lit. ‘they didn’t leave his heart’). They didn’t upset him, (but) he didn’t come back. What happens next (lit. ‘how will it be’)?

contents.textus: 010. Aṯi, aṯi, omar, ‘Koyo u+naʕimo?’ Omar, ‘Ašə́r, səmli lo+səmli, laṯi, kalé komfaraǧ ʕal aṣ+ṣayode’.
contents.versio: 010. He came, he came, he says, ‘Where is the child?’ He says, ‘Really, no matter what I did (lit. ‘I did, I didn’t do’), he didn’t come back, here he is, looking at the fishers’.

contents.textus: 011. Áydarbo… aṯən me gabe, mḥalaqle ruḥe lgamiye xliṯo. Laš+šalqat du+baḥar mṭalle i+gamiye li+ḳaviye du+baž. Mḥalaqle ruḥe li+gamiye xliṯo.
contents.versio: 011. How ... they left him, he tossed himself into an empty boat. The sea waves brought the boat to the shore (lit. ‘to the edge of the dry land’). He tossed himself into the empty boat.

contents.textus: 012. Ŭ laš+šalqat mballe, mballe… ṭār, ṭār mi+gamiye, čīk bu+baḥar.
contents.versio: 012. And the waves took him away, they took him away… he flew off, he flew off the boat, he plunged into the sea.

contents.textus: 013. Omar, ‘Ay yade!’ Aṣ+ṣayode ḥərre. Balki kə́pwalle məfqíleste, lo+makuwe rišayye.
contents.versio: 013. He says, ‘Oh, mummy!’ The fishermen saw. Perhaps they could have taken him out, but they didn’t bother (lit. ‘they didn’t sicken their heads’).

contents.textus: 014. Axər u+zʕuro azzeyo. Koṯe i … kuzzé ʕaṣriye ... gdəṯyo i+emo. Ḥa tắneyo, rḥímoyo, ‘Koyo u+zʕuro, koyo u+naʕimo?’ ‘E, kalé bayn an+naʕime’. Lə+gmaqəḷḷa.
contents.versio: 014. In the end, the boy went off. Along comes his [mother] … he goes in the evening… his mother will come. He is the only [child], he is beloved, ‘Where’s the boy, where’s the child?’  ‘Yes, here he is, among the kids’. He wouldn’t admit it to her.

contents.textus: 015. E, azzé hiye. Azzé hiye ʕam i+ʕaṣriye, komar, komar, ‘U+zʕurawo, u+zʕurawo harke, harke áykoyo?’ Kəmmi, ‘Ha qay díḏuxwa?’ Kəmmi, ‘Ăḷo d̥owe rišux basimo, ašə́r mḥalaqle ruḥe lu+baḥar, ḥnīq. Ləḏʕíwayna díḏuxyo. Ašə́r áḥnaste lo+makulan rišan’.
contents.versio: 015. Yes, he went. He went in the evening, he says, he says, ‘That boy, that boy here, here, where is he?’ They say, ‘Oh, why, was he yours?’ They say, ‘May God rest his soul (lit. ‘may your head be pleasant’), really, he threw himself into the sea, he drowned. We did not know he was yours. Really, we didn’t bother (lit. ‘we didn’t sicken our heads’).’

contents.textus: 016. Daʕər. Lo+maqəḷḷe, du+šahro di+Ndaṯalo lo+boṭal. Lo+maqəḷḷe, gdəṯyo i+emo, gdəmmo, ‘E, koyo u+zʕurawo? Naʕímoyo! Koyo? Kafínoyo, ṣáhyoyo!’
contents.versio: 016. He came back. He didn’t admit it, so the Feast Day of the Theotokos wouldn’t stop. He didn’t admit it, the mother will come, she will say, ‘Right, where is that boy? He’s a child! Where is he? He’s hungry, he’s thirsty!’

contents.textus: 017. Komar, ‘Kalé bayn an+naʕime koməštaʕe, mə ḥarulax mine?’ Kotole qole aʕla.
contents.versio: 017. He says, ‘Here he is, playing among the kids, what is troubling you about him?’ He raised his voice at her.

contents.textus: 018. Ha, tre+xabre disa gdəṯyo. ‘E, u+naʕimawo koyo?‘ E, komar, ‘Kalé bayn an+naʕimani, bayn an+nošani koməštaʕe, mə kəbʕat mine?‘ Səmla lo+səmla, lo+komàqərste. Lo lela ŭ lo lnoše.
contents.versio: 018. Here, a few moments later (lit. ‘two words’) she will come again, ‘Right, that child, where is he?’ ‘Yes’, he says, ‘Here he is, among those children, he is playing among those people, what do you want from him?’ No matter what she did (lit. ‘she did, she didn’t), he wouldn’t admit it as well. Neither to her nor to anyone else.

contents.textus: 019. Axər, e, da waxt di+šànṯoyo, lályoyo. Komar, ‘Gdomax bayn an+naʕime, lo+ḥarulax!’ Kul dəṯyo, lo+komaḷḷa mede.
contents.versio: 019. In the end, yes, it is bedtime, it is night. He says, ‘He’ll sleep among the children, don’t let it trouble you!’ Whenever she comes, he wouldn’t tell her anything.

contents.textus: 020. Ṣafro disa aṯyo. Mṣalalle bgawa di+ʕito, mqarawwe, səmme u+šahraṯṯe, maqraṭṭe. Ŭ ko… kul… kul+naqqa dəṯyo, gdomar, ‘Kalé bayn an+nošani, lo+ḥarulax!’
contents.versio: 020. In the morning, she came again. They prayed inside the church, they held Mass, they did their feast day, they had breakfast. And every… whenever she comes, he would say, ‘Here he is with those people, don’t let it trouble you!’

contents.textus: 021. Hul dәmrastqi azzehən. Mrastqi azzehən, nafiqi mi+walaye d̥ Ḥəmməṣ. Azzehən, azzá, mə́ḷḷale əmmo, ‘Gəzzé ʕam qaflat, gmiṣakar!’ Omar, ‘Ḥurma, me aṯməl čik bu+baḥar, ḥnīq. Kəbʕat, xŭd‿kəbʕat, ánnaqqa bxay!’
contents.versio: 021. Until they went straightaway. They went straightaway, they left the city of Homs. They went, she went, she said to him, she says, ‘He’ll go with the crowd (lit. ‘groups’), he’ll get lost!’ He says, ‘Woman, since yesterday he has plunged into the sea, he has drowned. If you wish, as you wish, then cry!’

contents.textus: 022. Ánnaqqa k̬məḥyo ʕal barka, k̬məḥyo ʕal ṣadra, k̬məḥyo ʕal qarʕa. ‘Way, u+naʕimayḏi. Way u+ṣabrayḏi! Way u+rḥimayḏi! Ono ŭ babux masulan. U+bahro dʕaynan, i+quwa dbarkoṯan’.
contents.versio: 022. Then she beats on her knees, she beats on her breast, she beats on her head. ‘Woe, my baby! Woe, my hope! Woe, my beloved! Your father and I have become old. The light of our eyes, the strength of our knees!’

contents.textus: 023. Ŭ kobuxyo. Kobuxyo baxyo mayiro. Aḥ+ḥaroye daš+šahroye kəmmi, ‘Málava, uʕdo meqəm nafiqina mi+walaye, mede latwa. U+baxyo mayirano, hano məb‿baxyo mayíroyo?’
contents.versio: 023. And she cries. She cries bitterly (lit. ‘a bitter cry’). The last few celebrants say, ‘Good grief, now before we left the city, there wasn’t anything. This bitter cry, what bitter cry is this?’

contents.textus: 024. Koduʕri ʕal ḥḏoḏe, mšayli, ‘Mənyo, lo mənyo?’ Kəmmi, ‘Ašə́r, u+abro du+šulṭono me aṯməl čīk bu+baḥar, ḥnīq ŭ lo+maqəḷḷe’.
contents.versio: 024. They turn to one another, they ask, ‘Whatever could it be? (lit. ‘what is it, what isn’t it?’).’ They say, ‘Really, since yesterday the sultan’s son has plunged into the sea, he has drowned, and he didn’t admit it’.

contents.textus: 025. As+sobahkàr koṯən, kəmḥalqi ruḥayye lu+baḥar, koduʕri. Mḥalqi ruḥayye lu+baḥar. Ga, u+zʕuro ínaqqa domar ‘ay’, i+Ndaṯalo nqīr‿ebe. Nqīr‿ebe, mədla ŭ ṭʕəḷḷa.
contents.versio: 025. The swimmers come, they toss themselves into the sea, they return. They toss themselves into the sea. Look, the boy, when he says ‘oh!’, the Theotokos swooped down onto him, she swooped down onto him, she grabbed him and carried him off.

contents.textus: 026. Ṭʕəḷḷa. Məqqa dʔaṯi dăbibat ... am+malaxe kanné ḥeḏora. Məqqa dʔaṯi dăbibat, ddawṣile ya uxlile, gnəfḥi appe, gmayṯi.
contents.versio: 026. She carried him. Whenever creatures came... the angels, they’re there around her. Whenever creatures came, to bite him or to eat him, they would blow on them, they would die.

contents.textus: 027. Hul dʔaṯən as+sobahkàr, mofaqqe. Dʔaṯən as+sobahkàr, hənnək lo+kḥozəlla, hiya koḥəzyalle, hula biḏayye.
contents.versio: 027. Until the swimmers came, they took him out. When the swimmers came, they don’t see her, she sees them, she put (lit. ‘gave’) him into their hands.

contents.textus: 028. Hula biḏayye. Nafəq, koməfqile mu+baḥar, ga aǧ+ǧulàyḏeste lo+tarən. Kəmmi, ‘Ya šəbḥo l Ăḷo! Hano mə măsáleyo me aṯməl?’
contents.versio: 028. She put (lit. ‘gave’) him into their hands. He came out, they take him out of the sea, look, even his clothes didn’t get wet. They say, ‘Praise be to God! What’s the story (lit. ‘what story is this’) since yesterday?’

contents.textus: 029. Komar, ‘Di‿tawu’, ŭ mə́ḷḷaste əmmo, ‘Šāl b̥kēf dbabux, šāl b̥kēf dbabux ŭ daḥ+ḥasye ŭ daq+qaše ŭ day… dayroye ŭ di+ǧamaʕa kula, d̥kosaymi u+ša͜hrayḏi. Š͜͜͜āl b̥kēf dəṯṯe, ŭ gdobono ḥaq dbabux. Bi+briṯaṯe lə+g̊ṭәryono mede ǧorelux ŭ bi+briṯàyoste gdoballe ḥaq diḏe bi+ʕulbe mʕaramto. Ŭ izux, Aloho aʕmux’.
contents.versio: 029. He says, ‘Now sit down!’ and she also said, she says, ‘Send my regards to your father (lit. ‘ask about your father’s wellbeing’), send my regards to your father, to the bishops, the priests, the monks, and the whole community, who did my feast day. Send my regards to them, and I’ll give your father his due. In this world, I won’t let anything happen to you and in that world too I’ll give him his due in full measure. So go, may God be with you’.

contents.textus: 030. Aṯi, ánnaqqa koməfqile, kəmmi, ‘ʕAǧobo hano, me aṯməl kalux bu+baḥar! Lə+ḥniqat ŭ lo+tarat!’
contents.versio: 030. He came, then they take him out, they say, ‘This is a miracle, since yesterday you’ve been there in the sea! You didn’t drown and you didn’t get wet!’

contents.textus: 031. Komar, ‘Di‿tawu domáṇṇanxu’. Ánnaqqa komaḥkille. Komar, ‘Ónoste, səmme lo+səmme lag+greʕe, lazzí aʕmayye. Aṯyo i+gamiye xliṯo li+ḳaviye du+baž, mḥalaqli ruḥi ela ŭ laš+šalqat mbállalli.
contents.versio: 031. He says, ‘Now sit down so I can tell you’. Then they tell him [sic]. He says, ‘As for me, no matter what the servants did (lit. ‘they did and they didn’t’), I didn’t go with them. An empty boat came to the shore (lit. ‘to the edge of the dry land’), I tossed myself into it and the waves carried me away.

contents.textus: 032. Mbállalli, ŭ naqqa ṭayərno mi+gamiye, čīkno bu+baḥar. Omaṇṇo, ‘Ay yade!’, naqqa i+Ndaṯalo aṯyo, lqə́flali, ṭʕə́ḷḷali. Ṭʕə́llali, ŭ aṯən ad+dăbibat duxlili.
contents.versio: 032. They carried me away, and all of a sudden (lit. ‘at once’) I flew from the boat, I plunged into the sea. I say, “Hey, mummy!” at once the Theotokos came, she snatched me, she carried me. She carried me, and creatures came to eat me.

contents.textus: 033. Nəfḥiwa am+malaxe kulle ḥeḏora, ač+čangaṯṯe nuro, ŭ nəfḥiwa appe, quṭlə́nwanne ŭ mamṯə́nwanne. Lə+ṭrela ašyáh‿əmqadamli.
contents.versio: 033. All the angels were blowing around her, their wings fire, and they were blowing on them, they were killing them and putting them to death. She didn’t let anything approach me.

contents.textus: 034. Ŭ fāšno aʕma hul dʔaṯutu. Aṯən as+sobahkàr, məḷḷa, ‘Šayal b̥kef di+ǧamaʕa, du+šahro kule, ŭ dad+dayroye, daq+qaše, daḥ+ḥasye. ŭ šāl b̥kef dbabux. Gdoballe bi+ʕulbe mʕaramto, harke gnəṭrono bi+briṯaṯe, gnəṭranxu, gnəṭrallux dlo mede lo+ǧorelux, ŭ bi+briṯàyoste gdobono ḥaq lbabux bi+ʕulbe mʕaramto’.
contents.versio: 034. And I stayed with her until you came. The swimmers came, she said, “Send my regards to the community (lit. ‘ask about the community’s wellbeing’), all those of the feast day, and to the monks, the priests, the bishops, and send my regards to your father. I will give to him in full measure, here I’ll protect here in this world, I’ll protect you (pl.), I’ll protect you (sg.) lest anything happen to you, and also in that world I’ll give your father his portion in full measure”’.

contents.textus: 035. Ŭ naqqa+ḥreto dísane azzə́n aš+šahroye mbarbzi. Ŭ d̥owutu šani sāġ, hánoste kamilo. Basə́mtowa?
contents.versio: 035. And again once more the celebrants went off (lit. ‘they went, they scattered’). And you be well for me, this one too is finished. Was it nice?

contents.textus: 1. Kətwaaa, latwa, rab̰‿m Aloho latwa, ḥaq! Mar ‘ḥaq’!
contents.versio: 1. There was and there wasn’t, greater than God, there wasn’t. True! Say ‘true’!

contents.textus: 2. E. Əmmi, kətwa ṗire, dəmmina, xoṯi. Azzá lu+tanuro, tanuro d̥saymo u+laḥmo.
contents.versio: 2. Yes. They say, there was once a woman, say, like me. She went to the oven, an oven to make bread.

contents.textus: 3. Səmla, lo+səmla, u+tanurayḏa lo+qāṯ, lo+daləq, dǧuġrole.
contents.versio: 3. No matter what she did, her tannoor did not catch fire, did not ignite, for her to kindle it.

contents.textus: 4. Kətwa safruno ʕal u+sawgo, ʕal u+syoġo. Mə́ḷḷale, mə́ḷḷela, ‘Ṗire, u+tanurayḏax lə+gdolaq. Tax, kit kubo braġli, šlaḥe ŭ maḥát bu+tanuro, gdolaq!’
contents.versio: 4. There was a bird on the fence, on the hedge. She said to him, he said to her, ‘Lady, your oven won’t ignite! Come, there is a thorn in my foot, take it out and put it in the oven, it’ll ignite!’

contents.textus: 5. Azzá li+ṗire, šləḥla u+kubo me raġle du+safruno, maḥatla bu+tanuro, nfəḥla, omar ‘gurp’, daləq!
contents.versio: 5. The woman went, she tore the thorn out of the bird’s foot, put it in the oven, blew on it, it went ‘gurp’ (lit. ‘it said gurp’), it ignited!

contents.textus: 6. Daləq, ǧġəḷḷa, səmla u+la(ḥmo)... ǧġəḷḷa u+tanurayḏa, azzá mṭela u+layšo, səmla u+laḥmo.
contents.versio: 6. It ignited, she kindled it, she made the brea(d)... she kindled her oven, she went and brought dough, she made bread.

contents.textus: 7. Əmmo, ‘Ma lo+kuxlat?’ Omar, ‘Lanno kafino’. (E, safrúnoyo, hayo ḥəkkáyeyo, šrolo dugle, dúgleyo, ḥəkkáyeyo).
contents.versio: 7. She says, ‘Why don’t you eat?’ He says, ‘I am not hungry’. (Yes, it’s a bird, this one is a story, truthfully fables, it’s fables, it’s a story).

contents.textus: 8. Məḷḷe, ‘Lo+koxanno, sawíʕono’. Mədla lu+taštayḏa du+laḥmo dmaḥto ʕal kaṯpa dəzzá lu+bayto. Komar, ‘Heeey! Marke ŭ laaayko?’ ‘Mənyo?’ Omar, ‘Hawli u+kubayḏi!’
contents.versio: 8. He said, ‘I’m not eating, I am full’. She took her basin of bread to put it on her shoulder to go home. He says, ‘Hey! Where are you going? (lit., ‘from here and to where?’)’ ‘What is it?’ He says, ‘Give me my thorn!’

contents.textus: 9. Əmmo, ‘Hak u+kubayḏux, ha gdoballux kubo’. Omar, ‘U+kubayḏi bәnafs kobaʕne.’ ‘E, u+kubayḏux moqaḏli!’ Omar, ‘Lo, dlowe ya u+kubayḏi ya šwaʕ̥+ṭalme dlaḥmo ŭ qursk̇e’.
contents.versio: 9. She said, ‘Oh, your thorn, here, I’ll give you a thorn’. He says, ‘I want the very same thorn’. ‘Well, your thorn, I burned it!’ He says, ‘No, either my thorn or seven loaves of bread and a bun’.

contents.textus: 10. Flān behvā́n, səmla lo+səmla, čara lo+səmla mine. Húlale šwaʕ̥+ṭalme ŭ qursk̇e.
contents.versio: 10. So-and-so, no matter what she did, there was no way to deal with him. She gave him seven loaves and a bun.

contents.textus: 11. Mʕalqile b̥kaṯpe, azzé, azzé, azzé, azzé, azzé, laqi lar+ruʕye. (Ar+ruʕye, d̥komarʕən. Xud uʕdo, d̥kətne aʕ+ʕezayḏan ʕal i+ʕayno).
contents.versio: 11. The bird hung them on its shoulder, he went, went, went, went, went, and encountered shepherds. (Shepherds, who herd. Like now, when our goats are at the spring).

contents.textus: 12. Komarʕən aʕ+ʕeze, ko… ko rabbana, kofərxi darke ŭ bʕure, ġálawa, be mә... bayn u+ḥalwo duxli.
contents.versio: 12. They were herding their goats, poor things, they were crumbling cow pies and goat droppings, it was a famine, into… into milk to eat.

contents.textus: 13. Komar, ‘Hanək mənne?’ Kəmmi, ‘Aḥna, háwxayo, layto laḥmo duxlina’. ‘Buzu, buzu, buzu, mašiġu u+lăganaṯxu, kalé u+laḥmo aʕmi’.
contents.versio: 13. He says, ‘What is that?’ They say, ‘We, it’s like this, there isn’t any bread for us to eat’. ‘Toss it out, toss it out, toss it out, wash your bowl, there’s bread with me’.

contents.textus: 14. Kobayzi u+ḥalwawo, a+bʕure, ŭ ad+darkanək, mašiġi u+lăganaṯṯe ṭowo.
contents.versio: 14. They toss out the milk, the goat droppings, and those cow pies, they wash their bowl well.

contents.textus: 15. Ŭ komaḥti, kəmṭe u+laḥmo, šwaʕ̥+ṭalme ŭ qursk̇e. Frəxxe ŭ ḥluwwe disa nof+ḥreno d̥ḥalwo maʕ+ʕeze, húwanne.
contents.versio: 15. And they put it down, he brings the bread, seven loaves and a bun. They crumbled it and again milked another round of milk from the goats, they gave it to them.

contents.textus: 16. Xəlle. Xəlle, əmmi, ‘Tux xul!’ Omar, ‘Sawíʕono’. Omar, ‘Sawíʕono’.
contents.versio: 16. They ate. They ate, they say, ‘Come eat!’ He says, ‘I am full’. He says, ‘I am full’.

contents.textus: 17. Mәd hawi waxt du+rəstoqo dәmrastqi aʕ+ʕezaṯṯe, əzzə́n lu+ṭuro, komar, ‘Hee! Marke ŭ layko?’ ‘Mənyo?’ ‘Háwәli u+laḥmayḏi!’
contents.versio: 17. When the time came to head off, to direct their goats, they went to the hill country, he says, ‘Hey! Where are you going? (lit., ‘from here and to where?’)’ ‘What is it?’ ‘Give me my bread!’

contents.textus: 18. ‘May gdobínalux u+laḥmayḏux? Ha… gduxlíwayna ad+darke, a+bʕurayḏan. Ma mə‿ḥarúwaylux minan? Húluxlanyo, xilan, ŭ azzé’. Omar, ‘Loo! U+laḥmayḏi ya šwaʕ+ʕwone ŭ barxk̇e’.
contents.versio: 18. ‘From where shall we give you back your bread? Ha… we would have eaten the cow pies, the goat droppings. Why would you have troubled yourself with us? You gave it to us, we ate it, and it’s gone’. He said, ‘Noo! Either my bread or seven sheep and a little lamb’.

contents.textus: 19. ‘Šwaʕ+ʕwone ŭ bárxk̇e mayko gəmṭina?’ Səmme lo+səmme, čara lo+səmme mine. (E, ḥəkkáyeyo). Húwalle šwaʕ+ʕwone ŭ bárxk̇e.
contents.versio: 19. ‘From where shall we bring seven sheep and a little lamb?’ No matter what they did, there was no way to deal with him. (Yes, it is a story). They gave him seven sheep and a little lamb.

contents.textus: 20. Húwalle šwaʕ+ʕwone ŭ bárxk̇e.
contents.versio: 20. They gave him seven sheep and a little lamb.

contents.textus: 21. Húwalle šwaʕ+ʕwone ŭ bárxk̇e. Mḥalle qum ruḥe, azzé. Azzé, azzé, azzé, azzé lәqriṯo.
contents.versio: 21. They gave him seven sheep and a lamb. He drove them in front of himself, he went. He went, went, went, went to a village.

contents.textus: 22. (Kəmmina, haṯe qríṯoyo, Məḏyaḏ waláyeyo). Azzé lәqriṯo, kalkoruqḏi ŭ zəmri. Məštúṯoyo, komḥawli kalo. (Kuḏʕat, i+kalo mənyo?).
contents.versio: 22. (Let’s say, this is a village, Midyat is a city). He came to a village, here they are, dancing and singing. It’s a wedding, they are moving the bride. (Do you know what ‘bride’ is?)

contents.textus: 23. Komḥawli kalo, saymi məštuṯo. Konəḥri əmṭən ʕebugre, baqqat, xačxaǧok̇at, marmarok̇at, gəmgəmok̇at, komaḥti bi+ṣəfriye.
contents.versio: 23. They are moving the bride, they are doing the wedding. They are slaughtering, bringing mice, frogs, agamas, house geckos, fat-tailed geckos, they are putting them on the tray.

contents.textus: 24. ‘Pak, pak! Hani mə́nnani? Buzu, buzu, buzu, mašiġu i+ṣufriyaṯxu ṭowo! Kann‿aʕ+ʕwone, nḥaru ʕwone.’
contents.versio: 24. ‘Ooh, ooh! What are these? Toss it out, toss it out, toss it out, wash your tray well! Here are the sheep, slaughter sheep!’

contents.textus: 25. Hedik̇a koqaymi bayzi a+gmara-šmarayo, bayzila. Mašiġi bu+ṣafono ŭ bu+darmono i+bard̥šaṯṯe ṭowo.
contents.versio: 25. So they up and toss out that filth-shmilth, they poured it out. They washed their pot well with soap and detergent.

contents.textus: 26. Ŭ maḥti… k̬nuḥri aʕ+ʕwone, ksaymi ánnaqqa baṣro daʕ+ʕwone čətəlxáyr. Kuxli ŭ šotən, mkayfi, ruqḏi, zəmri.
contents.versio: 26. And they put … they slaughter the sheep, then they make the meat of the sheep a feast. They are eating, drinking, enjoying themselves, dancing, singing.

contents.textus: 27. Hawi ʕaṣriye. ‘Heeey! Marke ŭ layko?’ ‘Mənyo?’ Omar, ‘Háwәli aʕ+ʕwonayḏi!’ ‘Aʕ+ʕwone mayko!? Nḥirilan!’
contents.versio: 27. The evening came. ‘Heyy! Where are you going? (lit., ‘from here and to where?’)’ ‘What is it?’ He says, ‘Give me back my sheep!’ ‘The sheep, from where!? We slaughtered them!’

contents.textus: 28. Omar, ‘Lo, ắbadan! Aʕ+ʕwonayḏi, vega! Ya aʕ+ʕwonayḏi ya i+kalo!’
contents.versio: 28. He says, ‘No, for sure! My sheep, right now! Either my sheep or the bride!’

contents.textus: 29. Marke ŭ layko, səmme lo+səmme, lo+qadiri aʕlayye. Húwalle i+kalo.
contents.versio: 29. Back and forth (lit. ‘from here and to where?’), no matter what they did, they couldn’t prevail upon them (i.e., him). They gave him the bride.

contents.textus: 30. Húwalle i+kalo, maḥtole b̥xúrǧək̇e, b̥čalṭa, ŭ mʕalqole b̥kaṯpe. Ḥəṭle i+hno, mḥalqole b̥kaṯpe. Azzé, azzé, azzé, maṭi ldaworo.
contents.versio: 30. They gave him the bride, he put her in a saddlebag, in a handbag, and hung it on his shoulder. He tied the whatsit, threw it on his shoulder. He went, he went, he went, he encountered a ploughman.

contents.textus: 31. Kalkodowar baq+qanyone (kuḏʕat, u+dworo mənyo? Zərʕi zād, kodawri baq+qanyone).
contents.versio: 31. Here he is, plowing with cattle. (Do you know what ploughing is? They plant crops, they plough with cattle).

contents.textus: 32. Omar, ‘Ma maye, daworo, maye layt gabux?’ Omar, ‘Bele bele, kito gurno ha bi+…šurawhòk̇ene, bu+xarbawhòk̇ene.
contents.versio: 32. He says, ‘Water, ploughman, don’t you have water with you?’ He says, ‘Of course, of course, there is a trough over by that there wall, in those there ruins’.

contents.textus: 33. Omar, ‘Ḥur, kalá i+xurǧk̇ayḏi harke dlo+gayšat eba! I+čalṭayḏi kalá harke dlo+gayšat eba.’ Omar, ‘Lo, lo!’
contents.versio: 33. He says, ‘Look, there’s my saddlebag here, so don’t touch it! My handbag, here it is, so don’t touch it!’ He says, ‘No, no!’

contents.textus: 34. Azzeyo hiye lu+gurno d̥šote. Koṯe u+daworo, ḥōr, ga k̇ačk̇e bi...
contents.versio: 34. He went to the trough to drink. The ploughman comes, he sees, there’s a girl in the...

contents.textus: 35. Omar, ‘Zax itáw tamhók̇ene’. Azzá yatiwo bəṯre šuro. Kə́twayle, ḥăša, klabṯo.
contents.versio: 35. He says, ‘Go sit over there’. She went, she sat behind a wall. He had, excuse me, a bitch.

contents.textus: 36. Maḥtole bi+xurǧk̇e, ḥiṭole ŭ aṯi ko...kodowar. Mḥele i+xurǧk̇e b̥kaṯpe, azzeyo komalax.
