contents.versio: 36. He put her in the saddlebag, sewed her up, and came back to plough (lit. ‘ploughing’). He (the bird) threw the bag on his shoulder, he went away (lit. ‘walking’).

contents.textus: 37. Kowe nūṣnū́ṣ di+klabṯo bi+xurǧk̇e. Komar, ḥăša, komar, ‘Hak̇a mazruqe mazráq, hak̇a əḥre ḥray, Ăḷo, lə+g̊fotaḥno qumax’.
contents.versio: 37. There’s a bitch’s whining in the bag. He says, excuse me, he says, ‘If you pee, if you poop, by God, I shall not open it up for you (lit. ‘in front of you’)’.

contents.textus: 38. Azzá azzá azzá azzá lbayto, azzé lәqriṯo, lbayto. Maḏəfle, omar, ‘Sumu dukṯi bi+k̇adine. Elo məqqa doreno hắwar, lo+maqi<rutu>, loṯuṯu lafeli, ha!’
contents.versio: 38. She went, went, went, went to a house, he went to a village, to a house. He lodged there, he says, ‘Make my spot in the barn. But however much I cry for help, don’t div<ulge> (it), don’t come to me, see!’

contents.textus: 39. Azzeyo, ftəḥle. Frəsse dukṯe bi+k̇adine ŭ azzé, ftəḥle fema di+xurǧk̇e, i+klabṯo yarixole.
contents.versio: 39. He went, he opened it. They spread out his spot in the barn, and he went, he opened the mouth of the saddlebag, the bitch struck out at him.

contents.textus: 40. ‘Hắwara, hắwara, hắwara! Lawo, hắwara, Khắwarak… hắwaraka diya,K latyo u+hăwarano, hăwár ḥrénoyo!’ Lo+makuwwe rišayye, məḷḷe.
contents.versio: 40. ‘Help, help, help! Boy, help, Ka “help”… it is a different “help”,K it’s not this “help”, it’s another “help”!’ They didn’t bother (lit. ‘trouble their heads’), he said it.

contents.textus: 41. De de de disa čikole bi+xurǧk̇e ŭ ḥiṭole. Ṣafro qām omar, ‘Qay laṯutu lafeli?’ Əmmi, ‘Baʕ məḷḷux “Lo... li... litoxu lafeli!”’
contents.versio: 41. Bit by bit, he sneaked her into the saddlebag once more and sewed it up. In the morning, he up and says, ‘Why didn’t you come to me?’ They say, ‘Didn’t you say, “Don’t… don’t… don’t come to me!”?’

contents.textus: 42. Azzé, azzé, azzé, azzé, laqi lruʕyo ʕal am+maye, ač+čaxani. Ruʕyo ʕal am+maye, omar, ‘Waa ruʕyo!’ Omar, ‘Hoo!’
contents.versio: 42. He went, went, went, went, he met a shepherd by the water, the appropriate times. A shepherd by the water, he says, ‘Hey, shepherd!’ He called back (lit. ‘he said hoo!’).

contents.textus: 43. Omar, ‘Ma lə+gbatli u+mašruqawo, gdobenux klabṯo?’ Omar, ‘Bele, ašə́r komilaʕeno, i+klabṯo gəmḥamyo aʕ+ʕezayḏi mad+dewe’.
contents.versio: 43. He says, ‘Won’t you give me that flute, I’ll give you a bitch?’ He says, ‘Yes, I’m longing for it, the bitch will defend my goats from the wolves’.

contents.textus: 44. Hedik̇a ftəḥle i+hno, lu+ruʕyo húlela laḥmo, ŭ mblole gab ruḥe ŭ húlele u+mašruqo.
contents.versio: 44. Then he opened the whatsit, the shepherd gave her bread, and he took her to his place and gave him the flute.

contents.textus: 45. Húlele u+mašruqo d̥kozomar (kuḏʕat u+mašruqo mənyo? Kozomar ha hawxa ebe, konofaḥ).
contents.versio: 45. He gave him the flute he plays (do you know what ‘the flute’ is? He plays it like so, he blows).

contents.textus: 46. Saləq ʕal qarʕe d̥qatoro rabo, omar, ‘Liruliiir!’ Omar, ‘Huli u+kubo bәšwaʕ̥+ṭalme ŭ qursk̇eee!’
contents.versio: 46. He got up on top of a big boulder, he says, ‘Liruliiir!’ He says, ‘I gave a thorn for seven loaves of bread and a bun!’

contents.textus: 47. A+šwaʕ̥+ṭalme ŭ qursk̇e hiwi<li> b... a+šwaʕ̥+ṭalme ŭ qursk̇e hiwili bәšwaʕ+ʕwone ŭ barxk̇eee.
contents.versio: 47. The seven loaves of bread and a bun, I ga<ve> them for… the seven loaves of bread and a bun, I gave them for seven sheep and a lamb.

contents.textus: 48. A+šwaʕ+ʕwone ŭ barxk̇at hiwili b̥kalo. I+kalo hiwoli bәklabṯo.
contents.versio: 48. The seven sheep and lambs, I gave them for a bride. The bride, I gave her for a bitch.

contents.textus: 49. I+klabṯo hiwoli b̚mašruqo. Noše layto dmoǧaq qarʕi’.
contents.versio: 49. The bitch, I gave her for a flute. There isn’t anybody who can beat me (lit. ‘smash my head’).

contents.textus: 50. Lu+ruʕyo mḥelele kefo, mǧəqle qarʕe, azzé, mədle lu+mašruqayḏe, azzé lu+bayto. KHun žmәra sāġ,K kamilo!
contents.versio: 50. The shepherd struck a stone at him, he smashed his head, he went, he took his flute, and went home. KAnd you be well,K it’s finished!

contents.textus: 001. Dəmmaḷḷa? E, kətwa, latwa, rab̰m Ăḷo latwa, ḥaq!
contents.versio: 001. Shall I tell it? Yes, there was, there wasn’t, there wasn’t anybody greater than God, truth!

contents.textus: 002. Kətwa pire xoṯi, sawto. W kə́twayla qaṭən w taʕlo.
contents.versio: 002. There was a woman like me, old. And she had a cat and a fox.

contents.textus: 003. Əmmo, ‘Gəzzino li+ʕito. Luxluṯu u+ḥalwayḏi, haaa!’
contents.versio: 003. She says, ‘I shall go to church. Do not drink my milk, ever!’

contents.textus: 004. Əmmi, ‘Lo, lo’. Əmmo, ‘Gəmṭanxu ṭawʕo’. ‘Ṭrowe’.
contents.versio: 004. They say, ‘No, no’. She says, ‘I shall bring you a prosphoron’. ‘OK’.

contents.textus: 005. (Kuḏʕutu, ‘ṭawʕo’ mənyo? Kosaymi aṭ+ṭawʕe hawxa bi+ʕito, kowe u+qurbono, u+faġro mine, i+brukṯo mine. Obe... kowən hən zəyude kobənne lan+naʕime).
contents.versio: 005. (Do you know what a ‘prosphoron’ is? They make ‘prosphora’ at church like so, there is the Eucharist, the host from it, the antidoron from it. He gives… if there are any extra, they give them to children.)

contents.textus: 006. E, azzá li+ʕito, u+taʕlo nafəl ʕal u+ḥalwo, ‘lap, lap, lap, lap’, xile u+ḥalwo.
contents.versio: 006. Yes, she went to church, the fox fell upon the milk, ‘lap lap lap lap’, he drank the milk.

contents.textus: 007. Azzé li+qamayto di+qašto lu+tarʕo di+ʕito, omar, ‘Qašto, qašto!’
contents.versio: 007. He went to face the old lady at the door of the church, he says, ‘Old lady, Old lady!’

contents.textus: 008. Əmmo, ‘Mənyo?’ Omar, ‘Lo+xili u+ḥalwayḏax, hawli u+ṭawʕayḏi!’ Húlale u+ṭawʕo, kuṯyo lu+bayto, ga lo ḥalwo, lo mede, lo ḥalwo w lo mede. Veǧa...
contents.versio: 008. She says, ‘What is it?’ He says, ‘I have not drunk your milk, give me my prosphoron!’ She gave him the prosphoron, she comes home, there’s no milk, no nothing, neither milk nor nothing. Then...

contents.textus: 009. ‘Qwiro taʕlo, qay xilux u+ḥalwayḏi?’ Omar, ‘Li+qaṭən xila!’
contents.versio: 009. ‘Silly fox, why have you drunk my milk?’ He says, ‘The cat has drunk it!’

contents.textus: 010. ‘Qaṭən, qay xilax u+ḥalwayḏi?’ Əmmo, ‘Ăḷah yade, lo eli xili, lu+taʕlo xile’.
contents.versio: 010. ‘Cat, why have you drunk my milk?’ She says, ‘By God, mummy, I have not drunk it, the fox has drunk it’.

contents.textus: 011. Əmmo, ‘De zux gab be ḥolux, mṭi u+ḥewuṭo, gmasəḥyallux’.
contents.versio: 011. She says, ‘Get going to your uncle’s, bring back a laundry paddle, I’ll give you a wash’.

contents.textus: 012. Azzé gab ab+be ḥole, mṭele u+ḥewuṭo, masḥela, mḥela ʕal i+duvayḏe, qṭiʕola.
contents.versio: 012. He went to his uncle’s, he brought back the laundry paddle, she gave him a wash, she beat upon his tail, she cut it off.

contents.textus: 013. Qṭəʕla i+duvayḏe. Azzé bayn aḥ+ḥawrone, kəmmi, K_‘Qúṫṫo qúṫṫo bəré-da, šunəḳ dare qúneda. Hára brəyá mála xále-da!’_K
contents.versio: 013. She cut off his tail. He went to his friends, they say, ‘Tailless, tailless on the road, a laundry paddle at the ass. Hit the road to Uncle’s house!’

contents.textus: 014. K_‘Qúṫṫo qúṫṫo bəré-da, šúnəḳ dáre qúne-da. Hára brəyá mála xále-da!’_K
contents.versio: 014. ‘Tailless, tailless on the road, a laundry paddle at the ass. Hit the road to Uncle’s house!’

contents.textus: 015. Koṯe, komar, ‘Qašto, qašto, hawli i+duvayḏi. Kuzzí bayn aḥ+ḥawrone. Kəmmi, K_“Qúṫṫo qúṫṫo bəré-da, šúnəḳ dáre qúne-da. Hára brəyá mála xále-da!”_K’
contents.versio: 015. He comes back, he says, ‘Old Lady, Old Lady, give me back my tail. I am going to my friends. They say, “Tailless, tailless on the road, a laundry paddle at the ass. Hit the road to Uncle’s house!”’.

contents.textus: 016. Əmmo, ‘Zux, mṭi u+ḥalwayḏi!’ Azzé gab aʕ+ʕeze ṭuroye, dkəmmina.
contents.versio: 016. She says, ‘Go bring me my milk!’ He went by some hill country goats, as we say.

contents.textus: 017. Omar, ‘ʕEze, ʕeze, hāwli ḥalwo, ḥalwo dobeno lqašti, qašti doboli i+duvayḏi, elo kuzzí bayn aḥ+ḥawrone, kəmmi, “Qúṫṫo qúṫṫo bəré-da, šúnəḳ dáre qúne-da. Hára brəyá mála xále-da!”’. Əmmi, ‘Zux mṭilan ṭarfe’.
contents.versio: 017. He says, ‘Goats, goats, give me some milk, for me to give my old lady the milk, for my old lady to give me my tail back, since I go to my friends, they say, “Tailless, tailless on the road, a laundry paddle at the ass. Hit the road to Uncle’s house!”’. They say, ‘Go bring us some leaves’.

contents.textus: 018. Azzeyo, məḷḷe laḥ+ḥadode, omar, ‘Ḥadode, ḥadode, hāwli maglo, i+maglo – əzzí qoṭaʕno ṭarfe, aṭ+ṭarfe obénanne laʕ+ʕeze, aʕ+ʕeze obəlli ḥalwo, ḥalwo obene li+qaštayḏi. Elo – doboli i+duvayḏi –kuzzí bayn aḥ+ḥawrone, kəmmi, “Qúṫṫo qúṫṫo bəré-da, šúnəḳ dáre qúne-da. Hára brəyá mála xále-da!”’.
contents.versio: 018. He went, he said to some blacksmiths, he says, ‘Blacksmiths, blacksmiths, give me a sickle, the sickle – I may go cut some leaves, the leaves – I may give them to the goats, the goats – they may give me some milk, some milk – I may give it to my old lady. Since – for her to give me my tail back – I go to my friends, they say, “Tailless, tailless on the road, a laundry paddle at the ass. Hit the road to Uncle’s house!”’.

contents.textus: 019. Əmmi, ‘Izúx mṭilan sʕore… zux mṭilan beʕe’.
contents.versio: 019. They say, ‘Go bring us some barley... go bring us some eggs’.

contents.textus: 020. Azzé omar, ‘Gyoṯe, gyoṯe, hāwli beʕe, ab+beʕe dobénanne laḥ+ḥadode, aḥ+ḥadode dobəlli maglo, i+maglo dobena lqašti, qašti doboli i+duvayḏi, dobəlli ḥalwo, ḥalwo dobeno lqašti, qašti doboli i+duvayḏi. Kuzzí bayn aḥ+ḥawrone, kəmmi, “Qúṫṫo qúṫṫo bəré-da, šúnəḳ dáre qúne-da. Hára brəyá mála xále-da!”’
contents.versio: 020. He went, he says, ‘Hens, hens, give me some eggs, the eggs – to give them to the blacksmiths, the blacksmiths – to give me a sickle, the sickle – to give to my old lady, my old lady – to give me my tail back, [the goats] – to give me milk, the milk – to give to my old lady, my old lady – to give me my tail back. I go to my friends, they say, “Tailless, tailless on the road, a laundry paddle at the ass. Hit the road to Uncle’s house!”’.

contents.textus: 021. Əmmi, ‘Izúx mṭilan sʕore, e, izúx mṭilan sʕore’. Azzeyo gab aḥ+ḥaṣode, lu+ṭuro.
contents.versio: 021. They say, ‘Go bring us some barley, yes, go bring us some barley’. He went to the harvesters, to the hill country.

contents.textus: 022. Omar, ‘Ḥaṣode, ḥaṣode, hāwli quflo dəsʕore. As+sʕore dobénanne lag+gyoṯe, ag+gyoṯe dobəlli beʕe, ab+beʕe dobénanne laḥ+ḥadode, aḥ+ḥadode dobəlli maglo, i+maglo dobena… dqoṭaʕno ṭarfe laʕ+ʕeze, aʕ+ʕeze dobəlli ḥalwo, ḥalwo dobene lqašti. Elo kummili, “Qúṫṫo qúṫṫo bəré-da, šúnəḳ dáre qúne-da. Hára brəyá mála xále-da! ”’
contents.versio: 022. He says, ‘Harvesters, harvesters, give me an armful of barley. The barley – to give to the hens, the hens – to give me some eggs, the eggs – to give to the blacksmiths, the blacksmiths – to give me a sickle, the sickle – to give it … to cut some leaves for the goats, the goats – to give me some milk, the milk – to give it to my old lady. Since they tell me, “Tailless, tailless on the road, a laundry paddle at the ass. Hit the road to Uncle’s house!”’

contents.textus: 023. Əmmi, ‘Zux, mṭilan maye’. Azzeyo, <mḥalle>. Kə́twayle gawdo (əmmíwayna ‘gawdo’, meqəm əmmíwayna ‘gawdo du+săwāl’, saymíwaynale mṭíwayna maye la+freze ebe).
contents.versio: 023. They say, ‘Go, bring us some water.’ He went, he struck out. He had a skin, (we called it ‘a skin’, formerly we called it ‘a cattle skin’, we made it, we brought water to the stubble fields in it).

contents.textus: 024. Azzé, mbele u+gawdo qmi+ʕayno, məlyole, mətyole, maḥtole gabayye. Omar, ‘De ánnaqqa hāwli!’ Əmmi, ‘Ašə́r, lə+gbinalux’. ‘Áydarbo lə+gbutli?’
contents.versio: 024. He went, he took the skin to the spring, he filled it, he brought it back, he put it by them. He says, ‘Now then give it to me!’ They say, ‘Certainly, we shall not give it to you’. ‘How come you will not give it to me?’

contents.textus: 025. ‘Ašə́r lə+gbinalux’. Omar, ‘Ya Mar Sisi, ṭaʕno dbasmo me kisi! Doṯe ʕalʕolo, moḥe ʕal aḥ+ḥaṣode, ʕal as+semolo, ʕal a+gdiše, kulle. Ṭoreli quflo taḥte qatoro’.
contents.versio: 025. ‘Certainly, we shall not give it to you’. He says, ‘Oh Mar Sisi, a load of frankincense from my bag! May a whirlwind come, beat down the harvesters, the sheaves, the stacks, everything. May it leave me an armful under a boulder’.

contents.textus: 026. Ánnaqqa qām u+ʕalʕolo, qām u+ʕalʕolo, mḥele aʕlayye, mbele aḥ+ḥaṣode w as+semolo, a+gdiše, ṭrélele quflo taḥte qatoro.
contents.versio: 026. Then a tornado arose, a tornado arose, it beat them down, it carried away the harvesters and the sheaves, the stacks, it left him an armful beneath a boulder.

contents.textus: 027. Ăḷo, mṭele a+sʕorayḏe, hiwile la+gyoṯe, a+gyoṯe húwalle beʕe, ab+beʕe húwalle. Məblile laḥ+ḥadode, aḥ+ḥadode maglo – i+maglo – hule, hiwalle.
contents.versio: 027. God, he took his barley, he gave it to the hens, the hens gave him some eggs, they gave him the eggs. He brought them to the blacksmiths, the blacksmiths a sickle – the sickle – gave, they gave it.

contents.textus: 028. Azzé, qṭəʕle ṭarfe, aṭ+ṭarfe hiwile laʕ+ʕeze, aʕ+ʕeze húwalle ṣəṭlo dḥalwo, u+ḥalwo. Azzé, hule li+qašto, i+qašto húlale i+duvayḏe.
contents.versio: 028. He went, he cut off some leaves, he gave the leaves to the goats, the goats gave him a bucket of milk, the milk. He went, he gave it to the old lady, the old lady gave him back his tail.

contents.textus: 029. Mʕalaqla zraʕle, zage, ḳaspəḳat, medone xərxərḳat, maqəṯla bi+duvayḏe w ḥəṭla bi+duvayḏe, azzé.
contents.versio: 029. She hung buttons, bells, ornaments, clapping things, she attached them to his tail and she sewed them onto his tail, he left.

contents.textus: 030. Veǧa kuzzé, maʕ+ʕəšqat kohōz hawxa ruḥe, kəmmi ‘xəng xəng xəng xəng’. Kuzzə́n aḥ+ḥawronayḏe li+qamaytayḏe.
contents.versio: 030. Then he is leaving, he is quivering with joy like so, they go ‘jingle, jingle, jingle, jingle’. His friends come out to face him.

contents.textus: 031. ‘Qwiro taʕlo, mayko lux ax+xəng hnani?’ Məḷḷe, ‘Bramšəl mḥalaqli ruḥi li+rawmo, galiḏo aʕli, hawxa hawən xərxərḳat bi+duvayḏi’.
contents.versio: 031. ‘Silly fox, where did you get these jingle-whatsits?’ He said, ‘Last light I threw myself into the pond, it froze on me, so clappers appeared on my tail’.

contents.textus: 032. Azzə́n, mḥalaqqe ruḥayye li+rawmo. Hən twiro raġlayye. Hən twiro druʕayye. Hən biṭo ʕaynayye, hən hawən ḳul w ḳam.
contents.versio: 032. They went, they threw themselves into the pond. Some, their legs broke. Some, their arms broke. Some, their eyes burst. Some, became sick and diseased.

contents.textus: 033. Əmmi, ‘Qay hawxa səmlux eban?’ Omar, ‘Ma qay əmmútwayli u+“qúṫṫo qúṫṫo bəré-da”? Ónoste tleli ḥayf diḏi aʕlayxu’.
contents.versio: 033. They say, ‘Why have you done so to us?’ He says, ‘Why did you say to me “tailless, tailless on the road”? I took my revenge on you as well’.

contents.textus: 034. Azzehən lu+karmo du+qašo. Azzə́n lu+karmo du+qašo. Omar, ‘Waa!’ Saləq lu+šuro, omar, ‘Waa, ʕammi, qašo! Marfi i+fadono, mṭi i+mašo. Lat+taʕle, lat+taʕəlyoṯe xəḷḷe u+karmayḏux! Waaa! ʕAmmi qašo! Marfi i+fadono, mṭi i+mašo. Lat+taʕle, lat+taʕəlyoṯe xəḷḷe u+karmayḏux. Waaa! ʕAmmi qašo! Marfi i+fadono, mṭi i+mašo. Lat+taʕle, lat+taʕəlyoṯe xəḷḷe u+karmayḏux.’
contents.versio: 034. They went to the priest’s vineyard. They went to the priest’s vineyard. He says, ‘Hey!’ He climbed the wall, he says, ‘Hey, Uncle, Priest! Unyoke the team, bring the drawbar. The foxes, the vixens ate your vineyard! Hey, Uncle, Priest! Unyoke the team, bring the drawbar. The foxes, the vixens ate your vineyard! Hey, Uncle, Priest! Unyoke the team, bring the drawbar. The foxes, the vixens ate your vineyard!’

contents.textus: 035. Saliqo i+pire du+qašo, ‘Mənyo? Mənyo? Taʕlo qwiro, məkəmmat?’ Omar, ‘Lat+taʕle, lat+taʕəlyoṯe mṣafalle u+karmaṯxu!’
contents.versio: 035. The priest’s wife climbed up, ‘What is it? What is it? Silly fox, what are you saying?’ He says, ‘The foxes have cleaned out your vineyard!’

contents.textus: 036. Azzeyo lu+qašo, marfele i+fadono. Mṭele i+mašo, falət bəṯrayye, ṣədle ḥḏo mənne.
contents.versio: 036. The priest went, he unyoked the team. He brought the drawbar, he ran after them, he caught one of them.

contents.textus: 037. Əmmo, ‘ʕAmmi qašo! Uxliwa aḥ+ḥalye, obə́nwayli aḥ+ḥamuṣe’. Marfyole, əmmo, ‘Hay ḥreli ʕal daqnux, ono uxlówayno aḥ+ḥalye, obówaynanne aḥ+ḥamuṣe’.
contents.versio: 037. She says, ‘Uncle, Priest! They ate the sweet ones, they gave the sour ones to me’. He let her go, she says, ‘Screw you and your beard, I was the one eating the sweet ones, I gave them the sour ones’.

contents.textus: 038. Falət, ṣədle ḥreto, ṣədle ḥreto. Háyostene hawxa məḷḷa.
contents.versio: 038. He ran, he caught another one, he caught another one. That one also said so.

contents.textus: 039. Ánnaqqa xaliṣo, fāš u+taʕlo. Kalé rawiʕo bayn i+dawmo. Naqqa kefo əmmo ‘šaláp’, qayiṯo ebe.
contents.versio: 039. Then she escaped, the fox remained. He was lying within a thicket. At once a stone goes ‘slap’, it landed on him.

contents.textus: 040. Omar, ‘Ašə́r hawo, l Mar Sisi mḥéleli i+kefayo. Fāš u+ṭaʕno du+basmo b̥kisi, bəqḏoli’.
contents.versio: 040. He says, ‘Surely it was this Mar Sisi who threw this stone at me. The load of frankincense is still in my bag, my neck’s in the noose’.

contents.textus: 041. Ăḷa azzé mžīd qəm ǧaʕ… ǧaʕda, darbo.
contents.versio: 041. By God, he went, he stretched out on a high… on a highway, on a road.

contents.textus: 042. Naqqa aṯi lilalili, qola di+havale, naqqa aṯi kalo, aṯi kalo. Komalxi. ‘Ha! Kalé taʕlo, kalé taʕlo!’
contents.versio: 042. Suddenly a ululation came, the sound of ‘O friend’, at once a bride came, a bride came. They are walking. ‘Hey, there’s a fox, there’s a fox!’

contents.textus: 043. Lo+ʕarəq, lo+mahzamle. Faliti bəṯre, ṣədde.
contents.versio: 043. He did not get away, he did not escape. They ran after him, they caught him.

contents.textus: 044. Ṣədde, moṣarre, bəṯr i... ga ko… konoqaḥ, ga reḥe du+basmo koṯe, kal kito xurǧo dbasmo taḥt i+kalo, ʕal i+səsto.
contents.versio: 044. They caught him, they tied him up behind the bri... here he ... he sniffs, here comes the smell of frankincense, there’s a saddlebag of frankincense here under the bride, on the horse.

contents.textus: 045. Ăḷa kole. Hə́nnestene, kanné. Komaḷḷa li+kalo, komar, ‘Ašə́r dlo+nuḥtat, gdomaṇṇo, mpašelax’.
contents.versio: 045. By God, he waits. As for them, here they are. He tells the bride, he says, ‘For sure, if you do not get down, I shall say that you passed gas’.

contents.textus: 046. ‘Wawayle, ánnaqqa mahətkono!’ Qām kəmmo li … kəmmalle kəmmo, ‘Anḥētli!’
contents.versio: 046. ‘Woe is me, then I would have disgraced myself!’ She up and says to … she says to them, she says, ‘Take me down!’

contents.textus: 047. ‘E, qay manḥtínalax?’ Əmmo, ‘ʕAǧizono, manḥētli, gmalxono’(i+rabbane, mi+nəkfuṯo druḥa, maḥat niqa bəqḏola).
contents.versio: 047. ‘Yes, why should we take you down?’ She says, ‘I am sick and tired of it, take me down, I shall walk’ (the poor thing, for the sake of her own shame, he casts aspersions on her).

contents.textus: 048. Qām naḥito, komalxi hawxa. Komaləz komoḥe i+duvayḏe b̥ṭiza di+səsto, ‘ha ha ha’. Komalax, malax. W ha məd raḥəq, mḥele i+duvayḏe b̥ṭiza di+səsto, tlela.
contents.versio: 048. She up and came down, they walk like so. He quickly strikes his tail upon the mare’s ass, ‘ha ha ha’. He runs away. So after he become a little distant, he hit the mare’s ass with his tail, she took him away.

contents.textus: 049. Mbele u+basmo, i+səsto lu+tarʕo d Mar Sisi, maqlable u+ṭaʕno du+basmo lu+tarʕo d Mar Sisi, w madʕaḷḷe i+səsto, məṣrole bdawmo ḥreto. W hun žmərra saġ, háyoste...
contents.versio: 049. He took the frankincense, the horse to the entrance of Mar Sisi, he turned the load of frankincense over to the entrance of Mar Sisi, and he returned the mare, he tied her to another tree. And you be well, so this is it.

contents.textus: 1. Lo+šamiʕono hayo. Šamiʕono i... Šəmšə́m gaboro, hayo šamiʕalla. Balki háwoyo. Šəmšə́m balki háyoyo.
contents.versio: 1. I haven’t heard this one (i.e., Aḥiqar). I have heard the (story of) the hero Samson, that one I did hear. Maybe it’s that one. Samson, maybe it’s that one.

contents.textus: 2. Šəmšə́m gaboro gabórowa. Noše lo+qodarwa aʕle, ḥokamwa ʕal i+qriṯo kula, noše lápwayle, xašuno. Ŭ hiye, əšme Šəmšə́m gabóroyo.
contents.versio: 2. The hero Samson was a hero. Nobody could prevail over him, he ruled over the whole village, nobody could overcome him, (he was) tall. And he, his name is the hero Samson.

contents.textus: 3. Bu+yawmo lḥasyo Benyamen Aktaš bu+talavәziṑn ŭ dayroyo Samyel miralle. Miralle, әmmi, ánnaqqa... miralle...
contents.versio: 3. One day (lit. ‘on the day’), Bishop Benyamin Aktash on television and monk Samuel retold it. They told it, they say, now then... they told it...

contents.textus: 4. Əmmi, Šəmšə́m gaboro, kəmmallux, gabórowa ŭ ġắlăbe ḥokamwa, ḥokamwa. E, áydarbo ḥokam? Áydarbo, lo áydarbo, məš‿šəkl?
contents.versio: 4. They say, the hero Samson, I tell you, he was a hero and he would rule a long time (lit. ‘a lot’), he would rule. Yes, he would rule how? No matter how (lit. ‘how, not how’), what kind?

contents.textus: 5. Ánnaqqa hanək ag+gundiyayḏe dlo+qudriwa aʕle, mərre, ‘Gdobínale k̇ắčәk̇e. Malawšínala ǧule xŭššәk̇at, ṭrosaymo ruḥa ebe dmohaḷḷa. Dlo i+k̇ačk̇e saymo ʕalā́ǧ mine, aḥna layban aʕle’.
contents.versio: 5. Now then, those villagers of his that could not prevail over him, they said, ‘Let’s give him a girl. Let’s dress her in beautiful clothes, let her do herself up for him so that he’ll marry her. If this girl won’t put the fix on him, we can’t prevail over him ourselves’.

contents.textus: 6. Edi hak̇a hayo, hak̇a lo, lo+kuḏʕono, ánnaqqa əmmi i+k̇ačk̇e əšma Dalílawa. Əšma Dalílawa, lawšowa ǧule šafire.
contents.versio: 6. Then whether that one or not, I don’t know, now then, they say the girl, her name was Dalila. Her name was Dalila, she wore beautiful clothes.

contents.textus: 7. Ŭ səmla ruḥa ebe, ŭ híyaste šafə́rtowa. Әmmi, səmla ruḥa ebe, nafəl lebe eba, mḥawal aʕma, mhirole.
contents.versio: 7. And she did herself up for him, and she too was beautiful. They say, when she did herself up for him, he (lit. ‘his heart’) fell for her, he moved in with her, he married her.

contents.textus: 8. Mhirole, mhirole. Ba ánnaqqa kəmmole, kəmmo, ‘I+gaboruṯayḏux bmənyo? Gabórohat, i+gaboruṯayḏux bmənyo?’ Komər, ‘E, məḥ‿ḥarulax mini?’
contents.versio: 8. He married her, he married her. Now then, doesn’t she tell him, she says, ‘Your strength, where (lit. ‘in what’s’) is it? You are a hero, where’s your strength? He says, ‘Right, what bothered you (lit. ‘ruined you’) about me?

contents.textus: 9. Gdəmmo, ‘Bi+maknəšto’, gəzzá məqḏo i+maknəšto. Gdəmmo, ‘Bәflā́n médeyo’, g̊saymo zyono.
contents.versio: 9. She’ll (i.e., he’ll) say, ‘In the broom’, she will go burn the broom. She’ll (i.e., he’ll) say, ‘It is in such-and-such a thing’, she’ll do some damage.

contents.textus: 10. Kohné šato ŭ tarte ŭ tlaṯ, kofəlto bəṯre. Kəmmo, kəmmo, ‘Maḷḷi, be i+gaboruṯayḏux bmənyo?’ Ġắlăbe kəmbasmóleste.
contents.versio: 10. He whatsits a year and two and three, she pursues him. She says, she says, ‘Tell me, where’s (lit. ‘in what’s’) your strength?’ She pleases him a lot too.

contents.textus: 11. (Lə+g̊šətyono, lə+g̊šətyono). Ŭ ġắlăbe kəmbasmole ŭ saymo ruḥa ebe ŭ ṣaydole maʕrifa ŭ omar, ‘Ḥurma, i+gaboruṯayḏi b̥ṣáʕriyo, b̥sawki, b̥ṣaʕri’.
contents.versio: 11. (I will not drink it, I will not drink it). And she pleases him a lot, she does herself up for him and she does him every honor (lit. ‘she catches for him recognition’), and he says, ‘Woman, my strength is in my hair, in my hairdo, in my hair’.

contents.textus: 12. ‘Mu+yawmo dhawino lo+qəṣli. Ono, ṣaʕri, u+k̇očak̇ d Alóhoyo. Lo+qəṣli ṣaʕri’. Yarәx ak̇+k̇aziyayḏe, ha háwxawayne, nəḥtiwa harke.
contents.versio: 12. ‘From the day that I was born, I haven’t cut it. As for me, my hair, it’s God’s spur. I haven’t cut my hair’. His locks grew long, they were just like so, they went down to here.

contents.textus: 13. Hedik̇a qā‿maštela, maštela hak̇a wiski, hak̇a be məš‿šəkl, maštela ŭ maštela. Ánnaqqa komaḥwowa i+ǧәzok̇ayḏa biḏa ŭ u+qudaḥ biḏe, biḏa.
contents.versio: 13. Then she up and made him drink, she made him drink either whiskey or whatever else, she made him drink and drink. Now then, it (i.e., the television program) would show her jezve in her hand and the glass in his hand, in her hand.

contents.textus: 14. Ŭ kobole, komaštole obole, maštole obole hul dhawi behə́š, hawi behə́š, mədla lu+šalfo, ánnaqqa ṣərta maḥwewa hawxa.
contents.versio: 14. And she gives it to him, she makes him drink, gives to him, she makes him drink, gives to him, until he became unconscious, he became unconscious, she took the knife, now then, her picture showed it like so.

contents.textus: 15. Ṣə́rtaste maḥwewa, mḥela u+šalfo ʕal ak̇+k̇azikayḏe, kulle qṭiʕila. Mḥela u+šalfo ʕal ak̇+k̇azikayḏe, qṭiʕila, ŭ azzayo, mašrat hawxa mʕalela i+parda.
contents.versio: 15. So her picture showed it, she took the knife to his locks, she cut them all off. She took the knife to his locks, she cut them off, and she went, and so believe it or not, she raised the curtain.

contents.textus: 16. Maḥwowa, maḥwela hawxa, mʕalela i+parda ŭ səmla lam+morayḏa hawxa. Ánnaqqa mballe aq+qayse, palq, palq, palq, palq! Komoḥe bruḥe, laybe qōm. I+gaboruṯayḏe azzá, mofaqqe at+tarte+ʕaynayḏe, mofaqqe at+tarte+ʕaynayḏe, ŭ maḥatte aʕleee, mqaṣqaṣṣe.
contents.versio: 16. It would show, it depicts her like so, she raised the curtain and she signaled (lit. ‘did’) to her bosses like so. Now then, they took sticks, bam, bam, bam, bam! He forces himself (lit. ‘he beats himself up’), he cannot get up. His strength went away, they put out both his eyes, they put out both his eyes, and they fell upon him, they tore him to bits.

contents.textus: 17. Moṣarre, mḥalaqqe zənǧər, u+zənǧər b̥xwa maḥwewa. Zənǧər mani a+ḥlime. Ḥa larke ŭ larke, mballe lu+ḥaps.
contents.versio: 17. They bound him, they chained him, it would show the chain itself. One of those thick chains. One over here and one over here, they took him to the prison.

contents.textus: 18. Mballe lu+ḥappəs, fāš be məqqa bu+ḥappəs hul dyarəx ṣaʕre. Lə+mballe bīr d̥qayṣile, ṣaʕre disa yarəx xud meqəm.
contents.versio: 18. They took him to the prison, he stayed for however long in prison until his hair grew out. It did not occur to them to cut his hair, his hair grew out again like before.

contents.textus: 19. Ŭ mofaqqe, ínaqqa dmofaqqe mu+ḥappəs, omar, әmmi... Səmme ánnaqqa ʕazima, səmme ʕazima bu+hayklo, latimi kulle lәḥḏoḏe. Mtarasle u+xwarzayḏe, mtarasle u+xwarzayḏe, omar, ‘Zux be man ŭ manne bu+hayklo?’
contents.versio: 19. And they brought him out, when they brought him out of the prison, he says, they say... They made, now then, a banquet, they made a banquet in the nave, all of them gathered together. He sent his nephew, he sent his nephew, he said, ‘Go, who and who are in the nave?’

contents.textus: 20. Azzeyo omar, ‘Ḥolo!’ Omar, ‘Ha!’ ‘Flānkás ŭ behvānkás ŭ fəltankás’ hanәk dәmʕan<atte>… dhawxa səmme ebe, kulle kanné bu+hayklo.
contents.versio: 20. He went, he says, ‘Uncle!’ He says, ‘Here!’ ‘Such-and-such, and so-and-so, and what’s-his-name’ those who were ang<ry> … who had done so to him, they’re all there in the nave.

contents.textus: 21. Kanné kulle bu+hayklo. Omar, ‘De mbali! Smaxli li+stune du+hayklo ŭ dʕar!’
contents.versio: 21. They’re all there in the nave. He says, ‘Take me! Prop me against the pillar of the nave and go back!’

contents.textus: 22. Azzé mbele. Hooo, komqašməri aʕle, ʕayne kanné biṭe, iḏoṯe kanné mәṣre, ŭ zənǧər harke ŭ harke, ha hawxa kanné iḏe mәṣre bu+zənǧər.
contents.versio: 22. He went to take him. Oooh, they mock at him, his eyes, there they are, burst, his hands, there they are bound, and a chain, here and here, just like so, there are his hands, tied with the chain.

contents.textus: 23. Ŭ azzé mbele, sməxle ḥaṣe li+stune du+hayklo ha hawxa, ŭ u+zʕuro nafəq.
contents.versio: 23. He went to take him, he propped his back against the pillar of the nave just like so, and the boy left.

contents.textus: 24. Ŭ ánnaqqa hənnək koguḥki mqašməri aʕle, koguḥki aʕle. Hăma səmle hawxa, naqqa omar ‘mrrrrr’ u+hayklo. Qṭile kulle ŭ qṭile rúḥeste. Hawxa šamiʕono.
contents.versio: 24. And now then, they laugh to mock at him, they laugh at him. So he did like so, at once the nave goes ‘timber’. He killed everyone and killed himself too. I heard it like so.

contents.textus: 1. Dəmmono? Əmmi, kətwa, latwa, rab̰‿m Aloho latwa. Ḥaq!
contents.versio: 1. Should I say (something)? Maybe it happened, maybe it didn’t (lit. ‘it was and it wasn’t’), there wasn’t anyone greater than God. Truth!

contents.textus: 2. Əmmi kətwa ʕezo. Kə́twayla tre+ṣafure, Šángali ŭ Pángali. Əṯyowa mamṣówalle, ŭ əzzənwa... Əzzawa li+marʕa.
contents.versio: 2. They say there was a goat. She had two kids, Shangali and Pangali. She would go and milk them, and they would go… She would go to pasture.

contents.textus: 3. Əzzawa li+marʕa. Aṯyo, hak̇a əšmo, ŭ hak̇a ġắlăbe, aṯyo, ‘Šángali, Pángali, maʕ!’ Pežən dәṯṯe lo+koṯe.
contents.versio: 3. She would go to pasture. (One time) she came back, either a little bit or a lot (later), she came back, ‘Shangali, Pangali, baa!’ There’s no sound from them (lit.‘their sound doesn’t come’).

contents.textus: 4. Aṯi u+dewo lu+tarʕo. Aṯi meqəm dəṯyowa i+hno. Aṯi u+dewo lu+tarʕo, ‘Šángali, Pángali maʕ!’ Kəmmi, ‘Lattat eman!’ ‘Šángali, Pángali, maʕ!’ Əmmi, ‘Lattat eman!’
contents.versio: 4. A wolf had come to the door. He had come before the whatsit came back. The wolf came to the door, ‘Shangali, Pangali, baa!’ They say, ‘You are not our mother!’ ‘Shangali, Pangali, baa!’ They say, ‘You are not our mother!’

contents.textus: 5. Omar, ‘Emáyxuno’. Ḥḏo məḷḷa li+ḥreto, ‘Ḥayra, latyo eman!’ ‘Šángali, Pángali, maʕ!’ Əmmi, ‘Lo, qolux lə+kšobah ldeman’.
contents.versio: 5. He says, ‘I’m your mother’. One said to the other, ‘Buddy, it’s not our mother!’ ‘Shangali, Pangali, baa!’ They say, ‘No, your voice doesn’t resemble our mother’s’.

contents.textus: 6. ‘Šángali, Pángali, maʕ!’ Lo+səmme bәḥḏoḏe, ḥḏo əmmo, ‘Latyo eman!’ Ŭ ḥḏo əmmo, ‘Émanyo’.
contents.versio: 6. ‘Shangali, Pangali, baa!’ They didn’t agree (lit. ‘didn’t make with one another’), one says, ‘It’s not our mother!’ And one says, ‘It’s our mother’.

contents.textus: 7. Ftəḥḥe u+tarʕo, xile at+tarte. Xile at+tarte, aṯyo i+emo mu+ṭuro, ‘Šángali, Pángali, maʕ! Šángali, Pángali, maʕ! Šángali, Pángali, maʕ!’ Layt.
contents.versio: 7. They opened the door, he ate both. He ate both, the mother came back from the hill country, ‘Shangali, Pangali, baa! Shangali, Pangali, baa! Shangali, Pangali, baa!’ Nothing.

contents.textus: 8. Nafiqo, kīt ṗire xətyā́r, xoṯi, qәm šuro manək, әmmo, ‘Ṗire! Lə+ḥzelax Šángali ŭ Pángali?’
contents.versio: 8. She went out, there’s an old woman, like me, in front of one of those walls, she says, ‘Woman! Haven’t you seen Shangali and Pangali?’

contents.textus: 9. Əmmo, ‘Lo+ḥzeli, d̥owe lu+dewo xilile, d̥owe lu+dewo xilile’. Qrela lu+dewo. Əmmo, ‘Dewo, xilux aṣ+ṣafurayḏi!’ Omar, ‘Bi+arʕo lo eli xilili!’
contents.versio: 9. She says, ‘I didn’t see them, maybe the wolf ate them, maybe the wolf ate them’. She called the wolf. She says, ‘Wolf, you ate my kids!’ He says, ‘On the earth (I swear), it wasn’t me who ate them!’

contents.textus: 10. Əmmo, ‘Mar di+raṣṭiye!’ Omar, ‘Bi+šmayo lo eli xilili!’ Əmmo, ‘Kәmmallux, elux xililux! Izúx, aʕwád ʕaršux! Ŭ gəzzí ónoste gab aḥ+ḥadode, maʕūdono qarni. Ŭ gnuḥtina lu+maydàn’.
contents.versio: 10. She says, ‘Speak truthfully (lit. ‘of truth’)!’ He says, ‘On the heavens, it wasn’t me who ate them!’ She says, ‘I’m telling you, it was you who ate them! Go, sharpen your teeth! And I’ll go to the blacksmiths, me too, I’ll sharpen my horn. And we’ll go down to the square’.

contents.textus: 11. E, mašrat, bu+televiz… bu+radyayḏan omarwa, oṯewa gumăgū́m dәṯṯe b̥qole du+radyo. Kə́twaylan radyo wáxtak̇e, hawxa.
contents.versio: 11. Right, believe it or not, on the televi… on our radio it would say, their boom-boom would come in the sound of the radio. We had a radio at that time, like so.

contents.textus: 12. Azzayo, ela lṭəšla qarna ŭ azzé híyeste gab u+taʕlo. Mәḷḷe, ‘Taʕlo, lṭaš ʕarši d̥qoṭanno i+ʕezo+koviye. Ono ŭ hat gduxlina u+baṣrayḏa’.
contents.versio: 12. She went, she sharpened her horn, and he too went to a fox. He said, ‘Fox, sharpen my tooth so that I’ll kill the wild goat. You and I’ll eat her meat’.

contents.textus: 13. Əmmo, ‘Hoo!’ Omar lṭəšše xәruǧәnák̇ xәrxәronák̇. Kefo du+zaluṭo kəmmina. Mbele, mṭele ʕal ʕarše, ŭ azzehәn lәḥḏoḏe, lu+maydàn.
contents.versio: 13. She (i.e., he) says, ‘Oh!’ It says, they sharpened up a hullabaloo. Sharpening stone, we call it. He moved it back and forth (lit. he took it, he brought it back) on his teeth, and they went to one another, to the square.

contents.textus: 14. Gurm ŭ gurm ŭ gurm ŭ gurm. Maḥatte ʕal ḥḏoḏe. Maḥatte ʕal ḥḏoḏe, i+ḥarayto mḥela qarna bgawe, mofaqla at+tarte+ṣafәryoṯayḏa me gawe.
contents.versio: 14. Boom, boom, boom, boom. They set at each other(’s throats). They set at each other(’s throats), finally she struck her horn into his belly, she took her two kids out of his belly.

contents.textus: 15. E, ḥəkkáyeyo. Əmmo, ‘Qay azzoxu?’ Əmmo, ‘Ăḷo səmli, lo+səmli, haṯe məḷḷa, “Ḥayra, latyo eman”. Əmmo, “Émanyo”. Ŭ ftəḥlan’.
contents.versio: 15. Right, it’s a fable. She says, ‘Why did you go?’ She says, ‘Gosh, no matter what I did (lit. ‘I did and I didn’t do’), this one said, “Buddy, it’s not our mother”. She says, “It’s our mother”. And we opened it’.

contents.textus: 16. ‘Ḥuuur, edi, bas ŭ fətḥutu u+tarʕo, ha!’ Əmmi, ‘Lo, yade, lo, haw kofətḥínale’.
contents.versio: 16. ‘Looook, then, enough opening the door (lit. ‘enough and you open the door’), see!’ They say, ‘No, mommy, no, we shan’t open it any longer’.

contents.textus: 17. Háyoste, d̥owutu šanan sāġ, háyәste xalā́ṣ. Hawxa kuḏʕono, balki lanne kúlleste, hamma hawxa kuḏʕono.
contents.versio: 17. That’s it, be well for us, that one’s also over. I know it like so, maybe they aren’t all there too, but I know it like so.

contents.textus: 001. Kətwa latwa, rab m Aloho latwa. ḥaq! ḥaq! Mar ‘ḥaq’!
contents.versio: 001. It was, it wasn’t, greater than God there wasn’t. Truth! Truth! Say ‘truth’!

contents.textus: 002. Kətwa Stērká Zerá. Rḥə́mtowa, kə́twayla šawʕo-aḥunone. Kofəhmat? Kə́twayla šawʕo-aḥunone, hiya tắnewa.
contents.versio: 002. Once upon a time there was Sterka Zera. She was beloved, she had seven brothers. Do you understand? She had seven brothers, she was the only sister.

contents.textus: 003. I-emo ġắlăbe rəḥmówayla. Rəḥmówayla, ánnaqqa, xud uʕdo dəmmina, ḥa dan-naʕimani.
contents.versio: 003. Her mother loved her very much. Well, she loved her in the way one loves one of these children, so to speak.

contents.textus: 004. Dəzzehən lu-ṭuro ... (Maḥtíwayna áḥnaste, əzzáwayna. Əzzáwayna, maltmíwayna hažžəkat, əmmíwayna hažžəkat, qayse našife. Fərsíwayna u-ḥawlo ha hawxa, maḥtíwayna ʕal u-ḥawlo, maqimíwayna u-ḥawlo, maḥtíwayna bəqḏolan w márkeda maydíwayna lu-ḥawlo mḥalqíwayna larke w larke, w ṭuʕníwayna aqqayse ha hawxa: pəštiyat, pəštiyat).
contents.versio: 004. When they were going to go to the hill country ... (We used to put... we also used to go. We went to collect twigs, we called them hažžǝkat, dry brush. We spread a rope like that, we put them upon the rope, we lifted the rope, we placed them on our nape. And from here we grabbed the rope, we threw it hither and hither, and in this way we carried brush: bundles, bundles.)

contents.textus: 005. Ánnaqqa azzehən an-naʕime, aḥ-ḥawronayḏa lap-pəštiyat, əmmo, ‘Yadé, ónoste gəzzí!’ — ‘Yadé, ləzzáx, naʕə́mtohat, kṭorəllax bu-ṭuro.’ Əmmo, ‘Lo, yadé, yadé, miḥase babax, yadé, gəzzí aʕmayye.’
contents.versio: 005. Now then, as the children, her companions went out for bundles, she said, ‘Mommy, I shall go too’. — ‘Mommy, don’t go, you are little, they will leave you in the hill country’. She said, ‘No mommy, mommy, blessed be your father, mommy, I shall go with them.’

contents.textus: 006. Əmmo, ‘De zax aʕmayye, mbal u-ḥawlayḏax, elo xayifo səm i-pəštiyayḏax, qăna dlo-fayšat mənne, haa dlo-ṭorəllax bu-ṭuro.’ (ġắlăbe rḥə́mtowa, hiya tắnewa, kə́twayla šawʕo-aḥunone.) Əmmo, ‘Hehe’.
contents.versio: 006. She said, ‘Come on, go with them, take your rope, then make your bundle quickly, so that you do not stay without them, whoah! so that they do not leave you in the hill country.’ (She was very much beloved, she was the only one, she had seven brothers.) She said, ‘OK, OK’.

contents.textus: 007. Azzá lu-ṭuro, səmla i-pəštiyayḏa. Əmmo, ‘Toxu, səmli i-pəštiyayḏi.’ Əmmi, ‘Aḥna he lo-səmlan diḏan. De dmax dmax, dmax hul d-saymina diḏan.’ Əmmo, ‘Lo-kṭorutu mini?’ Əmmi, ‘Lo, áydarbo kṭorina minax?!’
contents.versio: 007. She went to the hill country, she made her bundle. She said, ‘Go back! I have made my bundle.’ They said, ‘We haven’t yet made ours. Come on, rest, rest, rest until we have made ours.’ She said, ‘Aren’t you going to leave me?’ They said, ‘No, how could we leave you?!’

contents.textus: 008. (Ánnaqqa maḥtíwayna ǧəllə́k hawxa qəm ḥaṣan, dap-pəžkat daq-qayse lo-mičokiwa bḥaṣan.)
contents.versio: 008. (Now then, we used to place a piece of cloth under our back like that so that splinters would not get into our back.)

contents.textus: 009. Maḥto aǧ-ǧulayḏa, maḥatla qəm riša, răbăné, ṭawiʕo. ṭawiʕo, ṭəryalle tamo bu-ṭuro.
contents.versio: 009. She puts her clothing, she put it under her head, poor girl, she fell asleep. She fell asleep, they left her there in the hill country.

contents.textus: 010. Aḥ-ḥawronayḏa ṭʕənne ap-pəštiyat, aṯən lu-bayto, fayišo hiya bu-ṭuro. Fayišo bu-ṭuro, komaḥiso falge-dlalyo: k_răša hayve_k, ʕutma, falge-dlalyo.
contents.versio: 010. Her companions loaded the bundles upon themselves, they went home, but she remained behind. She remained behind, she wakes up in the middle of the night, a moonless night, darkness.

contents.textus: 011. Ánnaqqa ‘waaa yadé!’ U-ʕavd komar, ‘Mənyo, yadé, mənyo?’
contents.versio: 011. And then, in the middle of the night, ‘Mommy!’ And a monster answers, ‘What is it, Mommy, what is it?’

contents.textus: 012. Kəmmo, ‘Lattat emi, emi i-qeməstayḏa kə́mtowa’. Azzé, mḥele ruḥe bayn u-qaṭmo, bayn u-šiḥoro, makəmle i-qeməstayḏe. Omar, ‘Tax, yadé, tax, i-qeməstáyḏiste kə́mtoyo.’
contents.versio: 012. She said, ‘You are not my mother, my mother’s dress was black!’ He went to blend himself with ashes, soot, he blackened his clothing. He said, ‘Come, mommy, come! My dress is black too.’

contents.textus: 013. Əmmo, ‘Waaa yadé, lattat emi, waaa yadé!’ — ‘Mənyo, yadé, mənyo?’ Əmmo, ‘I-qeməstayḏa ḥewártoyo, ḥewártowa demi.’ Omar, ‘ónoste!’ Azzé xləṭle ruḥe bu-talgo, məḷḷe, ‘ónoste, iqeməstayḏi ḥewártoyo.’
contents.versio: 013. She said, ‘Mommy!’ ‘You are not my mother! Mommy!’ — ‘What is it, Mommy, what is it?’ She said, ‘Her dress is white. My mother’s was white.’ The monster said, ‘Me too!’ He went to blend himself with snow, he said, ‘Me too, my dress is white.’

contents.textus: 014. Azzá əmmo, ‘Waaa yadé!’ Omar, ‘Mənyo, yadé, mənyo?’ Əmmo, ‘I-qeməsto demi semáqtowa.’ Azze, xləṭle ruḥe bu-ṭino-semoqo, omar, ‘Həʔəhə i-qeməstáyḏiste semáqtoyo.’
contents.versio: 014. She went calling, ‘Mommy!’ He said, ‘What is it, Mommy, what is it?’ She said, ‘My mother’s dress was red.’ He went to blend himself with red mud, he said, ‘Hah hah! My dress is also red.’

contents.textus: 015. E, azzé w azzé, maṭən ləḥḏoḏe, maṭən ləḥḏoḏe. Azzé šuro w šuro, u-ʕavdste aṯi laff ela, midole, mḥalqole ʕal katfe, məblole mḥalqole lzarzamiye, maḥṣele u-tarʕo quma, w kalá hiya tăne bi-zarzamiye fayišo, fayišo.
contents.versio: 015. Yes, he went and went, they met each other, they met each other: sidling along the wall, the monster came towards her, grabbed her, tossed her over his shoulder, took her away, threw her into an underground chamber. He shut the door in front of her, and, hey, she stayed, she stayed alone in the underground chamber.

contents.textus: 016. Ánnaqqa azzé lu-bayto. — ‘Koyo Stērká Zerá?’ Əmmi, ‘Lo-ḥəzyolan.’ Mṣakro Stērká Zerá. Məblole, fayišo be kmo-šnaye, l Aloho húlela tre-naʕəmkat.
contents.versio: 016. And then they went home. ‘Where is Sterka Zera?’ They said, ‘We have not seen her.’ Sterka Zera got lost. He took her away. She stayed however many years. God gave her two boys.

contents.textus: 017. Naqqa aṯi u-aḥuno ʕal ḥaṣa di-zarzamiye.
contents.versio: 017. Once, her brother came to the surface of the underground chamber.

contents.textus: 018. Kə́twayla xud i-lampaṯe: naqwo bu-qṭoro di-škafte.
contents.versio: 018. It had something like this lamp: a hole in the ceiling of the cave.

contents.textus: 019. Omar, ‘Hačke!’ Əmmo, ‘Looo ruʕyo, ruʕyo dbe bábihat’. (B Kurmanǧí gdəmmono hano?) k_‘Az Stērká Zērá ma Xwəha ḥaft brá ma Diyá ʕIsá w Musá ma Gərtīkē ʕavd w hərčá ma_k.’
contents.versio: 019. He said, ‘Hačke!’ She said, ‘Hey, shepherd! You are the shepherd of my father’s house!’ (Shall I now say this in Kurmanji?) k_‘I am Sterka Zera! I am the sister of seven brothers! I am the mother of Isa and Musa! I am the prisoner of monsters and bears!’_k

contents.textus: 020. Latyo hawxa? Eh véǧane, ánnaqqa ‘howā́ḥ čale!’ I-ʕezayḏa i-čale, mḥalaqla aḥ-ḥəmre dəqḏola lqarna di-ʕezo.
contents.versio: 020. Isn’t it? Now then, ‘Howaḥ, goat!’ As for her goat, the goat, she threw her neck beads upon the goat’s horn.

contents.textus: 021. Kuzzá i-ʕezo gab u-ruʕyo, ‘Hak hani aḥ-ḥəmre d Stērká Zerane!’
contents.versio: 021. The goat goes to the shepherd and, ‘Oh, these beads belong to Sterka Zera!’

contents.textus: 022. Kuzzé lu-bayto, lə-gmaḥšam. Ksōm..., lə-gmaḥšam. ‘Qay, yadé, qay lə-gmaḥašmat?’ — iemayḏe — ‘Lhən mḥélelŭx, ṭrele lebux? Qay lə-gmaḥašmat?’
contents.versio: 022. He goes home, he does not have dinner. He does… ‘Why, mommy, why won’t you have dinner?’ — his mother — ‘Has somebody beaten you, offended you? Why won’t you have dinner?’

contents.textus: 023. Komar, ‘Yadé, ha kanné aḥ-ḥəmre d Stērkā́ Zerá.’ Hiye koboxe w i-emo kobuxyo.
contents.versio: 023. He said, ‘Mommy, here are Sterka Zera’s beads!’ He cries, and his mother cries.

contents.textus: 024. ‘Kooo răbăné Stērka Zerá, kətyo lad-dăbibat xilalle. Məǧ-ǧarila?’
contents.versio: 024. ‘Oh Sterka Zera, poor creature, maybe wild beasts ate her. What has happened to her?’

contents.textus: 025. Qām naqqa ḥreto, əmmo, ‘De zux disa bu-šopawo.’ Azzé disa bi-dŭkṯo du-yawmo-qamoyo. Dísane omar, ‘Howā́ḥ howā́ḥ!’
contents.versio: 025. Now, once more, she said, ‘Come on, go back on that trail again!’ He went once more to the place of the day before. He said once more, ‘Howaḥ, howaḥ!’

contents.textus: 026. Əmmo, ‘Looo šəvanó’, əmmo, ‘Looo ruʕyo, ruʕyo dbe bábihat W ono Stērká Zerano I-emo d ʕIsá w Musano I-asərto daʕ-ʕavdat, dah-hurčatno.’
contents.versio: 026. She said, ‘Hey, herdsman!’, she said, ‘Hey, shepherd! You are the shepherd of my father’s house, and I am Sterka Zera, I am the mother of Isa and Musa! I am the prisoner of monsters and bears!’

contents.textus: 027. ‘Howā́ḥ, Xəzēnke!’ Azzá i-ʕezoste, mḥalaqla ag-gŭharayḏa lqarna.
contents.versio: 027. ‘Howaḥ, Xǝzenke!’ The goat went, she threw her earrings on its horns.

contents.textus: 028. Azzé omar, ‘Ha kanné ag-gŭharayḏa!’
contents.versio: 028. He went and said, ‘Oh! Here are her earrings!’

contents.textus: 029. Azzeyo omar, ‘Ma marke w layko?’ Əmmo, ‘Marke lgabux’. — ‘Mənyo?’ — tfīq eba — ‘Mən măsắleyo?’ Əmmo, ‘Ha kal koḥozat, hǎka dəmṭutu aʕ-ʕašfe w am-maḏ̣răbat, w am-maqrasyoṯe, nuqwutu u-naqwano, dkətyo hawxa čike rabo w guršūtli — naxwa čara layto.’
contents.versio: 029. He went and said, ‘How far is it from here to wherever (you are)?’ She said, ‘From here to your side’. ‘What is it?’ — he ran into her — ‘what is the problem?’ She said, ‘Hey, you see, if you bring hoes and hammers and chisels, and make this hole, which has to be a bit large like so, and pull me out ... otherwise there is no way.’

contents.textus: 030. W azzehən azzé məḷḷe, ‘Yadé, kalá Stērká Zerá sāġ bflān škafte, lu-ʕavd ṣidole.’
contents.versio: 030. And they went, he went and said, ‘Mommy, now, Sterka Zera is alive in a certain cave, the monster trapped her.’

contents.textus: 031. Qām qralle lag-gundi, laǧ-ǧirane, kulle maltamme aḥ-ḥawle, mballe aʕ-ʕašfe, w am-maḏ̣rǎbat, am-maqrasyoṯe, twəṛṛe u-qṭoro, marwaḥḥe haqqa w mballe aḥ-ḥawle.
contents.versio: 031. They started calling the villagers, the neighbours, all of them collected ropes, they brought hoes, hammers and chisels, they broke open the roof, they made it that wide, and brought ropes.

contents.textus: 032. (Əmmíwayna ḥawle ḥayṣíwayna aṭ-ṭaʕne da-ḥmore ǧare appe. Ḥawle yarixe kowən, ḥamšaḥsar-kore ha hawxa.)
contents.versio: 032. (We used to say ropes, once we used to tie the donkey loads with them. They are long ropes, fifteen times that long.)

contents.textus: 033. Mballe ḥawle ġắlăbe w məṣrənne bǝḥḏoḏe w manḥtənne li-škafte, w mḥalaqla li-nawqayḏa, grišola.
contents.versio: 033. They brought many ropes and tied them together, and dropped them down into the cave, and she tied it to her waist, she pulled her out.

contents.textus: 034. An-naʕime əmmi, ‘Yadé, gəzzáx layko?’ Əmmo, ‘Gəzzí gab be ḥolayxu.’ — ‘Yadé gəzzáx layko?’ — ‘Gəzzí gab be ḥolayxu.’
contents.versio: 034. The children said, ‘Mommy, where are you going?’ She said, ‘I am going to your uncle’s house.’ — ‘Mommy, where are you going?’ — ‘I am going to your uncle’s house.’

contents.textus: 035. Aṯən, grišalle w məblalle.
contents.versio: 035. They came, they pulled her out and took her away.

contents.textus: 036. Aṯi ʕaṣriye u-ʕavd, omar, ‘k_Šəm bəm bəm bəm bəm, bēhna ġarb w ġarība žə va dara tē_k.’
contents.versio: 036. The monster came in the evening, and he said, ‘k_Šǝm bǝm bǝm bǝm bǝm, a smell of something western and foreign is coming out of this place_k.’

contents.textus: 037. Kofotaḥ i-škafte, ga noše layto. Komar, ‘ʕIsa, emux azzá layko?’ Komar, ‘Azzá gab be ḥoli.’
contents.versio: 037. He opens the cave, and aha! There is nobody! He said, ‘Isa, your mother – where has she gone?’ He said, ‘She has gone to my uncle’s house.’

contents.textus: 038. Komar ‘rəm’ moḥe qarʕe bu-šuro, qoṭele.
contents.versio: 038. He makes a thwack, he beats his head against the wall, he kills him.

contents.textus: 039. Komar, ‘Musa, ma emux azzá layko?’ Komar, ‘Azzá gab be ḥoli.’
contents.versio: 039. He said, ‘Musa, where has your mother gone?’ He said, ‘She has gone to my uncle’s house.’

contents.textus: 040. Komoḥe ... raġle táwoste ... moḥele bu-šuro qoṭele.
contents.versio: 040. He strikes ... the foot of the other one ... he strikes him against the wall, he kills him.

contents.textus: 041. k_W hun žə mə ra sāġ!_k
contents.versio: 041. k_You be well for me!_k

contents.textus: 001. Gdəmmanxu di+tərto+Zarè, di+tərto+Zarè, di+tərto+Zarè. Pire w zlā́mwayne, pire w zlā́mwayne. L Ălo húlela k̇aččək̇e, hawyo čik̇e bāš. Mayiṯo, i+pire mayiṯo.
contents.versio: 001. I shall tell you about Tawny the Cow, Tawny the Cow, Tawny the Cow. They were husband and wife, husband and wife. God gave her a daughter, she grew up a bit. She died, the woman died.

contents.textus: 002. U+zlām azzé mṭélele ḥreto, mṭélele ḥreto. Ánnaqqa i+k̇ačk̇e hawyo bāš. I+k̇ačk̇e yatəmto, di+emayḏa mayiṯo, hawyo bāš.
contents.versio: 002. The man went and brought back another one, brought back another one. Now then, the girl became older. The orphan girl whose mother died became older.

contents.textus: 003. Azzayo (əzzawa qm i+tərto, kə́twalle tərto+zaré), azzá qm i+tərto+zarè. Əmblówayla i+žənbavayḏa, i+pire du+babayḏa, maḥtówayla darke w bʕure. Sarwo w zawlo maḥtówayla məḥləf u+laḥmo, məḥləf ann+abišoṯe!
contents.versio: 003. She went (she used to go with the cow, they had a cow, Tawny), she went with Tawny the Cow. Her stepmother, her father’s wife, used to bring for her, to put cow pies and goat droppings out for her. Manure and dung she would put out for her instead of bread, instead of raisins!

contents.textus: 004. Ánnaqqa uxlowa, i+tərto aṯyo fəlge+dyawmo, waxt di+ʕrayto. I+tərto aṯyo, ga kal kuxlo. Kəmmo, ‘Hak hak hak, mək kuxlat? Mək kuxlat?!’ Əmmo, ‘I+žənbavayḏi komaḥtóline’.
contents.versio: 004. Now then, she was eating, the cow came, at midday, lunchtime. The cow came, she is now eating here. She says, ‘Oh, oh, oh, what are you eating?! What are you eating?!’ She says, ‘My stepmother puts these out for me’.

contents.textus: 005. Əmmo, ‘Bəz, bəz, bəz! Búzene, ḥaléqene, mašə́ġ iḏax w femax’. Azzá, bizila, mašəġla iḏa w foṯa, fema w aṯyo. Əmmo, ‘Məṣ mi+qarnaṯe’. Məṣla mi+qarnayo, xila … əmmo … laḥmo w baṣro w bərġəl. ‘W maṯe štay maye qayire!’
contents.versio: 005. She says, ‘Throw it away, throw it away, throw it away! Throw these away! Toss them out! Wash your hand and your mouth!’ She went, threw them away, washed her hand and her face, her mouth, and came back. She says, ‘Suck on this horn!’ She sucked on that horn, she ate … say, bread, meat, and bulgur. ‘And from this one drink cool water!’

contents.textus: 006. Məṭyowa maṯe duxlowa laḥmo w bərġəl w baṣro, w maṯe šətyowa maye qayire.
contents.versio: 006. She produced from this one so she would eat bread, bulgur, and meat, and from this one she would drink fresh water.

contents.textus: 007. Ánnaqqa i+pire, kul dmaḥtówayla bi+ṫurk̇e, bayzówayle. Məd nəfqowa mi+qriṯo, bayzówayle. Mǝd aṯyowa falge+dyawmo, ǝṯyowa i+tərto, obówayla, mayṣowa me qarna. Harke muklo w harke maye.
contents.versio: 007. Now then, the woman, everything she put into the shoulder bag, she threw it away. Whenever she left the village she would throw it away. When she came at midday, the cow would come, she would give her something, she would suck on her horn. Here is food and here is water.

contents.textus: 008. Hawxa hul dhíyaste hawila k̇ačk̇e. Hawyo rabṯo, hawyo hawxa, bəlṭə́k̇. Híyaste hawyo rabṯo. Əmmo, ‘Yadé, yadé, gəzzino ʕam i+k̇ačk̇e yatəmto qm i+tərto?’
contents.versio: 008. And so forth until she had a daughter. She became older, she became like so, a toddler. She also became older. She says, ‘Mummy, mummy, shall I go with the cow together the orphan girl?’

contents.textus: 009. Əmmo, ‘Lo yadé, lo lo lo … U+ṭuro, kīt kube, kīt kurfe, kīt ʕiqarwe. Ləzzáx, naxwašyo u+ṭuro, ḥémoyo’.
contents.versio: 009. She says, ‘No mummy! No, no, no … The hill country, there are thorns, there are snakes, there are scorpions. Don’t go, the hill country is bad, it is hot’.

contents.textus: 010. Əmmo, ‘Yadé, miḥase babax, yadé, gəzzino’.
contents.versio: 010. She says, ‘Mummy, please, mummy, I am going!’

contents.textus: 011. Səmla lo+səmla, lo+qadiro ʕal i+barṯo, w lo+ṭrela leba. Azzá, azzá. Mlela i+ṫurk̇e di+yatəmto disa sarwo w mlela di+barṯo laḥmo dḥeṭe, w abišoṯe w ḥalile w medone.
contents.versio: 011. Whatever she did, she could not prevail upon her daughter, and she did not break her heart. She went, she went. She filled the shoulder bag of the orphan girl with dung once again, and her daughter’s she filled with white bread, and raisins, and fruit roll-ups, and other things.

contents.textus: 012. Azzə́n lu+ṭuro. Lo+maǧrela ánnaqqa i+kačk̇e yatəmto bayzole. Mʕalaqqe, azzə́n falge+dyawmo duxli.
contents.versio: 012. They went to the hill country. This time, the orphan girl did not dare to throw it away. They hung them up and at midday they went to eat.

contents.textus: 013. Əmmo, ‘K̇ačk̇e, bəz! U+sarwawo buze, xul aʕmi’. Əmmo, ‘Lo. Lemax hawxa maḥatla elax w ono maḥatla eli hawxa. Ono duxlono hawxa, hat xul diḏax. Lo+kuxlono aʕmax’.
contents.versio: 013. She says, ‘Girl, throw it away! This dung, throw it away, eat with me’. She replied, ‘No, your mother has put such things out for you, and as for me she has put such things out. I shall eat like so and you eat yours. I will not eat with you’.

contents.textus: 014. Aṯyo i+tərto+zarè, ánnaqqa dobola, dobola muklo li+k̇ačk̇e yatəmto. Koḥayro, kalá i+k̇ačk̇e di+žənk̇e, di+žənbave ḥaḏərto. Əmmo, ‘Hə hə’. Mahzamla, kəmmina, ʕariqo, azzá bu+ṭùroda.
contents.versio: 014. Tawny the cow came to give her food, to give food to the orphan girl. She looks, here is the woman’s daughter, the stepmother’s is there. She says, ‘Uh-oh’. She ran away, we say she fled, she went towards the hill country.

contents.textus: 015. Azzá bu+ṭùroda. Ánnaqqa kəmmola i+k̇ačk̇e yatəmto, kəmmo, ‘Ṫaʕá Zaré, ṫaʕá Zaré, ṫaʕa Zaré, yade qurbane!’
contents.versio: 015. She went towards the hill country. Now then, the orphan girl says to her, she says, ‘Come on Tawny, come on Tawny, come on Tawny, mummy, please!’

contents.textus: 016. W i+ḥreto, dkətla emo, kəmmo, ‘Ṫaʕá Zaré, ṫaʕá Zaré, waylá gurāxwaré’.
contents.versio: 016. The other girl, the one who had a mother, says, ‘Come on Tawny, come on Tawny, for shame, you wolf-eaten (cow)!

contents.textus: 017. (Kīt, aḥna kəmmina, dewo bu+ṭurayḏan, koxal u+săwā́l. E, xud ak+kàlbeyo, elo dewo bárriyo bu+ṭuro, koxal u+săwā́l).
contents.versio: 017. (There are, we like to say, wolves in our hill country, they eat livestock. Yes, it is like dogs, but the wolf is wild in the hill country, it eats livestock.)

contents.textus: 018. ‘Ṫaʕá Zaré, ṫaʕá Zaré, waylá guraxware’. W i+yatəmto kəmmo, ‘Ṫaʕá Zaré, ṫaʕá Zaré, ṫaʕá Zaré, yade qurbane’. Yani kəmmo, ‘Qurbanax itáx’.
contents.versio: 018. ‘Come on Tawny, come on Tawny, for shame, you wolf-eaten (cow)!’ And the orphan girl says, ‘Come on Tawny, come on Tawny, come on Tawny, mummy please!’ That is, she says, ‘Please, come!’

contents.textus: 019. I+tərto ʕariqo. Kul dkoḥəzyo i+žənk̇e... di+žənk̇e, ʕariqo.
contents.versio: 019. The cow fled. Whenever she sees the woman … the one of the woman, she fled.

contents.textus: 020. Ṣahən. Ṣahən, qralle lar+ruʕye. Qrela i+yatəmto lar+ruʕye, əmmo, ‘Waaa ruʕye!’, dkuzzə́n marʕən aʕ+ʕeze bu+ṭuro.
contents.versio: 020. They became thirsty. They became thirsty, they called out for shepherds. The orphan girl called out for shepherds, she says, ‘Hey shepherds!’, the ones who go herd goats in the hill country.

contents.textus: 021. Əmmi, ‘Ho ho!’ Əmmo, ‘Miḥasyo emayxu w babayxu! Maye layto šətyono? Ṣíṯono, maye xwani? Əmmi, ‘Miḥasyo emax w bábaxste! Kito, kito, itáx!’
contents.versio: 021. They say, ‘Here, here!’ She says, ‘May your mothers and fathers be blessed! Isn’t there any water for me to drink? I am thirsty, some water like this?’ They say, ‘May your mother and father also be blessed! There is, there is, come!’

contents.textus: 022. Azzə́n, maḥwallalla maye zalile, xušk̇at, ḥewore, štela. Hawi u+ṣahro harke, u+yawmo harke.
contents.versio: 022. They went, they showed her pure, beautiful, clear water, she drank it. Here (on her forehead) the moon appeared, and here (on her chin) the sun.

contents.textus: 023. W i+k̇ačk̇e kəmmo, ‘Waaa!’ Aṯyo. ‘Qay hawxa?’ Əmmo, ‘Ăla qreli lar+ruʕye, húwalli maye hawxa’.
contents.versio: 023. And the daughter says, ‘Hey!’ She came. ‘Why like that?’ She says, ‘By God, I called out for shepherds, they gave me such a water’.

contents.textus: 024. Əmmo, ‘Waaa, ruʕye!’ Əmmi, ‘Ho ho!’ Əmmo, ‘Daləq emo w babo, ma maye layt gabayxu?’ Əmmi, ‘Dəlqi emax w bábaxste, bele, bele, tax!’
contents.versio: 024. She says, ‘Hey shepherds!’ They say, ‘Here, here!’ She says, ‘Blast your mother and father, isn’t there any water with you?’ They say, ‘Blast your father and mother as well, yes, yes, come!’

contents.textus: 025. Azzehən, húwalla maye bemrés, kome, húwalla. He-he, ǧare ǝmmíwayna hawxa. Uʕdo, lo+kəmmalla lan+naʕime, lo+šamiʕi. Kəmmono ʕáyboyo. Hawi … i+čənk̇e du+ḥmoro harke w aš+šeke harke.
contents.versio: 025. They went, they gave her unclean, black water, they gave it to her. Heh heh, sometimes we used to tell it like so. Now then, I don’t tell it to children, they haven’t heard it. I say it’s a disgrace. There appeared … a donkey pee pee here and balls here.

contents.textus: 026. Kuzzá lu+bayto, koguḥxi ‘pak pak’. I+emo kəmmo, ‘Qay hawxa?’ Əmmo, ‘Ḥāl w măsale, i+tərto ʕariqo. Hiya məḷḷa, ‘Miḥasyo emayxu w babayxu’. Húwalla maye xušk̇at, hawi u+ṣahro harke, u+yawmo harke. W ono əmmono, ‘Daləq emo w babe’. Hawi hawxa.
contents.versio: 026. She went home, they laugh, ‘Ooh, ooh!’ Her mother says, ‘Why like that?’ She says, ‘The thing is, the cow fled. She said, ‘May your mother and father be blessed!’ They gave her beautiful water, here appeared the moon, here the sun. And I say, ‘Blast your mother and father!’ It became like so.

contents.textus: 027. Ánnaqqa i+žənk̇e əmmo, ‘I+tərto+Zaré gnuḥralla. Ábadan gnuḥrono i+tərto+Zaré’.
contents.versio: 027. Now then, the woman says, ‘Tawny the Cow, I shall slaughter her. For sure I shall slaughter Tawny the Cow!’

contents.textus: 028. Ánnaqqa azzə́n ṣafro, azzá i+yatəmto lu+ṭuro. I+tərto məḷḷala, əmmo, ‘I+žənbaváyḏax gnəḥroli’. Əmmo, ‘Ma məs saymono?’
contents.versio: 028. Now then, they went in the morning, the orphan girl went to the hill country. The cow told her, she says, ‘Your stepmother is going to slaughter me’. She says, ‘What shall I do?’

contents.textus: 029. Edi əmmo, ‘Məs saymono?’ Əmmo, ‘Marre, “U+baṣro di+tərto Zaré howe aʕli ḥarā́m, ḥarā́m, ḥarā́m!” Luxlat u+baṣrayḏi! Məqqa dəmḥalqi garmo, mude! Məqqa dəmḥalqi garmo, mude! Məqqa dəmḥalqi garmo, mude!’ Əmmo, ‘Ṭrowe’.
contents.versio: 029. Then she says, ‘What shall I do?’ She says, ‘Tell them, “The meat of Tawny the Cow ought to be forbidden, forbidden, forbidden to me!” Do not eat my meat! However much bone they throw away, take it. However much bone they throw away, take it. However much bone they throw away, take it’ She said, ‘It’ll do’.

contents.textus: 030. Ánnaqqa nḥəḷḷa i+tərto, mabašlola. Kul lalyo ksaymowa bardəš dbaṣro. Hiya, u+zlamayḏa w i+barṯo uxliwa.
contents.versio: 030. Now then, she slaughtered the cow, she cooked her. Every night she made a pot of meat. She, her husband, and her daughter ate it.

contents.textus: 031. Omarwa, ‘Lawo, tax xul!’ Əmmowa, ‘U+baṣro di+tərto+Zaré howe aʕli ḥarā́m, ḥarā́m, ḥarā́m!’ W buxyowa. Lo+xila.
contents.versio: 031. He would say, ‘Girl, come eat!’ She would say, ‘The meat of Tawny the Cow ought to be forbidden, forbidden, forbidden to me!’ And she would cry. She did not eat.

contents.textus: 032. Lo+xila hul dkaməl u+baṣro. Kaməl u+baṣro, maltamla ag+garme. Kul dəmḥalqíwayle, təlyówayle. Kul dəhno, təlyówayle. Kul dəhno, təlyówayle.
contents.versio: 032. She did not eat until the meat was finished. The meat was finished, she collected the bones. Every thing they threw out, she put it away. Every thing, she put it away. Every thing, she put it away.

contents.textus: 033. Mǝd kaməl u+baṣro, əmmo, ‘Ṭlab u+galdo me babax!’
contents.versio: 033. After the meat was finished, she says, ‘Request the hide from your father!’

contents.textus: 034. Əmmo, ‘Yabo, yabo, hawli u+galdawo!’ Omar, ‘Lawo, ksōmne…’
contents.versio: 034. She says, ‘Dad, Dad, give me that hide!’ He says, ‘Girl, I shall make it…’

contents.textus: 035. (Meqəm ono ḥzeli, aḥna bəxwá lwəšlan, ag+galde daq+qanyone saymíwaynanne čwerəx. Lastik̇at latwa, šak̇alat latwa. Saymíwayna ag+galde daq+qanyone čwerəx … saymíwayna.)
contents.versio: 035. (Earlier, I saw, we wore them ourselves, cattle hides – we used to make them into footwear. There were no galoshes, no manufactured footwear. We used to make cattle hides into footwear, we made them.)

contents.textus: 036. ‘Yabo, miḥase…’ ‘Lawo, ksōmniyo čarəx, flān’. — ‘Yabo, miḥase babux, hăma lo xili u+baṣrayḏa, kəbʕono dobatli u+galdò. Kobaʕno dobatli u+galdò’. Qām húlela u+galdò, lebe yaqəḏ aʕla. Húlela u+galdò.
contents.versio: 036. ‘Father, please…’ ‘Girl, I am going to make it into footwear for myself, something’. ‘Father, please, since I have not eaten her meat, I want you to give me her hide. I want you to give me her hide’. He up and gave her the hide, his heart bled for her. He gave her the hide.

contents.textus: 037. Maḥatla ag+garmanək kulle bu+galdò, maltamla w azzayo. Ḥfəḷḷa i+qalto ha haqqa. (I+qalto, dkobayzina u+sarwo).
contents.versio: 037. She put all those bones into the hide, she collected it and went. She dug up a dunghill so much. (A dunghill, on which we throw manure).

contents.textus: 038. Ha haqqa ḥfəḷḷa w maḥatla u+galdawo bayn u+sarwo, ṭməḷḷa w ṭməḷḷa. Əmmo, ‘Hul dšabṯo ʕəṣro+yawme, izáx, ktowe kule dahwo’.
contents.versio: 038. She dug up so much and she put that hide among the manure, she buried it and buried it. She says, ‘After a week, ten days, come! It will become all gold’.

contents.textus: 039. Azzayo, maḥatla bayn i+qalto, fāš ʕəṣro+yawme. Kuzzá, koməfqo, u+galdo hawílayo qeməsto šafərto, šafərto, šafərto! Dəmmono, xwaṯe diḏi.
contents.versio: 039. She went, she put it within the dunghill, it stayed ten days. She goes, she takes it out, the hide turned into a beautiful, beautiful, beautiful shirt! That is to say, like this one of mine.

contents.textus: 040. W u+dahwo hawi šayre harke, hawi guharat harke w harke, hawi gardaniye harke, hawi ḥiyaṣa ʕal ḥaṣa, hawi xalxule braġla, hawi kul šəkəl dahwo. Dinore bəqḏola! W aṯyo, mṭela, tlela, tlela.
contents.versio: 040. And the gold became bracelets here, it became earrings here and here, it became a necklace here, it became a belt on her waist, it became anklets on her legs, it became all kinds of gold. Dinars on her neck! And she came back, she brought it, she hid it, she hid it.

contents.textus: 041. Hawi məštuṯo bi+qriṯo, hawi məštuṯo bi+qriṯo.
contents.versio: 041. A wedding party happened in the village, a wedding party happened in the village.

contents.textus: 042. Li+žənk̇e maḥatla tre+lagane, ḥa harke, ḥa harke. Əmmo, ‘Kazzán ono w i+barṯayḏi li+ məštuṯo. Doṯina, ga hano latyo malyo damʕe w hano latyo malyo šume, quṭlallax’.
contents.versio: 042. The stepmother put out two basins, one here and one here. She says, ‘My daughter and I are going to the wedding party. When we come back, if this one is not filled with tears and that one with snot, I shall kill you’.

contents.textus: 043. Maḥatla, azzá, nafiqo, hiya azzá li+məštuṯo. Aṯyo i+qaṭǝn.
contents.versio: 043. She put (them) out, she went, she went to the wedding party. A cat came along.

contents.textus: 044. Əmmo, ‘Răbane, may gməlyat hano damʕe w hano šume? Zax mṭilax galún dmaye raqiqe, xušk̇at, ḥat harke. W ḥat ləpk̇e dmalḥo baynaṯṯe, ktowən šume’.
contents.versio: 044. The cat said, ‘Poor thing, whence will you fill this one with tears and this one with snot? Go bring yourself a pin of fine, beautiful water, put it here. Put a fingertip of salt in it, it will become snot’.

contents.textus: 045. ‘W am+maye… a+hno … ḥa … bhən … galún maye bemrés ḥat harke, ktowən šume’. Ăla azzá, hawxa səmla’.
contents.versio: 045. ‘And the water… the whatsits… one … in some … a pin of unclean water put here, it will become snot’. By God she went and did like so’.

contents.textus: 046. ‘W izáx hátstene bayn i+daʕwo’.
contents.versio: 046. ‘And you too go to the wedding’.

contents.textus: 047. Azzá, mṭela galún dmaye raqiqe, maḥatla harke, xušk̇at, w maḥatla ləpk̇e dmalḥo baynaṯṯe, w maḥatla galún dmaye bemrés harke towən šume.
contents.versio: 047. She went, she brought a pin of clear water, placed it here, beautiful, and put a fingertip of salt into it, and she placed a pin of unclean water here to become snot.

contents.textus: 048. W azzá, mašəġla iḏa w foṯa, lwəšla aǧ+ǧule xušk̇anǝk, w u+dahwawo maḥatla ʕal ruḥa w barimo hawxa dlo+ḥozən u+šopayḏa.
contents.versio: 048. And she went, she washed her hands and her face, she put on those beautiful clothes, and that gold she put on herself, and she weaved around like so, so that they don’t see her trail.

contents.textus: 049. W azzá, čik̇o bayn i+govande w raqiḏo. Raqiḏo hoool falga+dsaʕa meqəm dbəṭlo i+ məštuṯo. Me d… Meqəm falga+dsaʕa dbəṭlo i+məštuṯo, nafiqo.
contents.versio: 049. And she went, she slipped into the dance circle and danced. She danced until half an hour before the wedding party would end. After … Half an hour before the wedding party would end she left.

contents.textus: 050. Nafiqo, barimo disa hawxa w aṯyo bəgnune, čik̇o lawġul, šləḥla aǧ+ǧulanək, tlalla. W lwəšla a+qṭiʕe w yatiwo qm al+laganayḏa, kobuxyo.
contents.versio: 050. She left, she weaved around once more like so, she came back secretly, she slipped inside, she took off her clothes, she put them away. And she put on tatters and sat down in front of her basins, she is crying.

contents.textus: 051. Aṯyo i+žənk̇e, aṯyo i+žənbave, kəmmo, ‘Ălo, k̇ačk̇e, kətwa ḥḏo xoṯax. E, ba məǧ ǧule xušk̇at kətwa aʕla, w məǧ ǧule šafire kətwa aʕla! W raqiḏo tēr … haw … w naqqa talyo. Be i+k̇ačk̇ayo máykowa?’ E hawxa, – tre, tloṯo+yawme hawxa.
contents.versio: 051. The woman came back, the stepmother came back, she says, ‘By God, girl, there was someone like you. Yes, what beautiful clothes were upon her, and what nice clothes were upon her! And she danced her limit … no more … and at once she took off. That girl, where was she from?’ Yes, like so, two-three days like so.

contents.textus: 052. Qām zʕuro dəmmina xoṯux, hedik̇a azzé, mḥalaqle bəṯr i+k̇ačk̇e. ‘Hedi, be i+k̇ačk̇aṯe máykoyo, may kuṯyo, lay gəzzá?’
contents.versio: 052. A boy, say like you, up and went carefully, he threw himself after the girl. ‘Wait, where is this girl from, where does she come from, where is she going?’

contents.textus: 053. Obaʕwayla, barəm bəṯra w bəṯra hul dčik̇o bu+bayto, čik̇o bu+bayto. Məḷḷe li+emo w lu+babo, omar, ‘Kobaʕno dəzzoxu ṭəlbūtli i+k̇ačk̇e yatəmto’.
contents.versio: 053. He wanted her, he weaved after her and after her until she slipped into her house, slipped into her house. He told his mother and his father, he says, ‘I want you to go request for me the orphan girl’.

contents.textus: 054. E, azzéhəlla lu+ṭlobo. Kuḏʕat ánnaqqa, áydarboyo? Kofəhmat? E, ṭlobo, yani kṭəlbi i+k̇ačk̇e lu+k̇urrək̇.
contents.versio: 054. They went to her for the request. Now then, do you know how it is? Do you understand? Yes, a request, that is they request the girl for the boy.

contents.textus: 055. E ánnaqqa i+emo, u+babo azzə́n, ṭliballe. Azzə́n dṭəlbila, kəmmo, ‘Lo, lo+kuṯyo b̥k̇er dmede. Kalá dayəm bu+ṭuro. Toxu, ṭlabu diḏi!’
contents.versio: 055. Yes, now his mother, his father went, they requested her. They went to request her. She says, ‘No! She is good for nothing. Look, she is always in the hill country. Come, request mine!’

contents.textus: 056. Kəmmi, ‘Aḥna kəbʕina i+k̇ačk̇e yatəmto’. Axər ṭliballe, simalle he, ṭliballe, mnayšnalle. Haka əšmo, haka ġălabe, aṯən dəmḥawlila.
contents.versio: 056. They say, ‘We want the orphan girl’. Finally they requested her, they made an agreement, they requested her, they engaged her. Whether a little or a lot, they came to move her (to their house).

contents.textus: 057. Aṯən dəmḥawlila … hedik̇a dmaḥtila… Meqəm maḥtiwayna fuṭa ʕal qarʕayna, aḥna ak+kaloṯe. Maḥtiwa fuṭa ʕal qarʕayna, ha hawxa. Uʕdo balki bu+aṯraṯxu, be áykoyo... ḥayṭiwayna dəsmale šaʕəṯto dabrisam, ha hawxa maḥtiwayna, ṭəmriwayna foṯan.
contents.versio: 057. They came to move her … then to put her… Earlier we used to put a head covering on our heads, we brides. They put a head covering upon our head, like so. Now probably in your country, wherever it is… they used to sew a yellow scarf out of silk, we used to put them on like so, we covered our face.

contents.textus: 058. Veǧa maḥtalle hawxa … ṭmərre … maḥtalle bi… hawxa dṭumri foṯa, e. Hedik̇a azzá, mədla li+k̇ačk̇e yatəmto, dkətwa u+yawmo w u+ṣahro. Maḥtola bu+tanuro.
contents.versio: 058. Then they put it like so, they covered it. They put it on… like so in order to cover her face, yes. She went stealthily, she took the orphan girl, who was Sun-and-Moon. She put her into the oven.

contents.textus: 059. Bu+tanuro kosaymi u+laḥmo, maḥti nuro bu+tanuro, ǧuġrile w saymi u+laḥmo. Azzá maḥtola bu+tanuro, maḥatla diḏa taḥt i+fuṭa, taḥt i+dəsmale.
contents.versio: 059. They make bread in the oven, they put a fire in the oven, they start it and make bread. She went, she put her in the oven, she put her own under the head covering, under the scarf.

contents.textus: 060. E, ánnaqqa kosolaq u+diko, kosolaq u+diko ʕal u+tanuro, komar, ‘Qaqluqī́ž! Kalé u+yawmo w u+ṣahro bu+tanuro, w kalé u+helək̇ w u+gunək̇ taḥt i+fuṭa. Qaqluqī́ž! Kalé u+yawmo w u+ṣahro bu+tanuro, w u+helək̇ w u+gunək̇ kalé taḥt u+maḥfū̀r, kalé taḥt i+dəsmale’.
contents.versio: 060. Now a rooster jumped up, a rooster jumped up on the oven, he says, ‘Cock-a-doodle-doo! Sun-and-Moon is here in the oven, and Nut-and-Ball is here under the head covering. Cock-a-doodle-doo! Sun-and-Moon is here in the oven, and Nut-and-Ball is here under the veil, here under the scarf!’

contents.textus: 061. Kəmmo, ‘Kəšša ḥiko!’ Komažḏo bəṯre, kofəlto bəṯre, komahzam, ʕoraq, naqqa+ḥreto koṯe ʕal u+tanuro.
contents.versio: 061. She says, ‘Shoo scrap!’ She pursues him, she chases after him, he runs away, he flees, once again he comes back on the oven.

contents.textus: 062. ‘Qaqluqī́ž! Kalé u+yawmo w u+ṣahro bu+tanuro, w kalə́n a+ḥrene, u+helək̇ w u+gunək̇ kanné taḥt i+fuṭa!’
contents.versio: 062. ‘Cock-a-doodle-doo! Sun-and-Moon is here in the oven, and here are the others, Nut-and-Ball, here they are under the head covering!’

contents.textus: 063. Kuzzə́n am+more di+kalo, kuzzə́n, koḥayri, kalayo taḥt u… kalá bu+tanuro. Hedik̇a midalle, mǝṭyalle, maḥtalle taḥt i+fuṭa w mədde layo di+žənk̇e w maḥtalle bu+tanuro.
contents.versio: 063. The bride’s parents come, they come, they see, here she is under… here in the oven. They stealthfully took her, they brought her, they put her under the head covering, and they took that of the woman and put her into the oven.

contents.textus: 064. I+žə̀nk̇este ánnaqqa bʕəšq kəmmo, ‘Hnoli!’ Kuzzá əṯyo bʕəšq, mədla dawqo dnuro, azzá, marfela ʕal i… bu+tanuro, dǧuġro, saymo u+laḥmo.
contents.versio: 064. As for the woman, now she says with glee, ‘I whatsited her!’ She goes and comes with glee, she took a flaming griddle, she went, she put it upon… into the oven to start it, to make bread.

contents.textus: 065. Kəmmo, ‘Yade ónono, yade ónono!’ Əmmo, ‘Klay, klay, klay!’ Hiya məḷḷa i+yatə̀mtoyo. Ǧġəḷḷa w dwəqla u+laḥmo, səmla u+laḥmo, mṭela.
contents.versio: 065. She says, ‘Mommy, it’s me! Mommy, it’s me!’ She says, ‘Wait, wait, wait!’ She thought it was the orphan girl! She started it and stuck the bread, she made bread and brought it out.

contents.textus: 066. W marwaxxe i+kalo. ‘Hedi, hedi nəšqono i+kalaṯxu, hedi nəšqono i+kalo’. Kəzzá, koḥayro, ga i+k̇ačk̇e yatəmto!
contents.versio: 066. They sat the bride (atop a horse). ‘Wait, wait, let me kiss your bride, wait, let me kiss the bride!’ She goes, she sees, here’s the orphan girl!

contents.textus: 067. Komoqaḏla druḥa! Ánnaqqa koməḥyo ʕal ṣadra, buxyo, buxyo, buxyo, məḥyo ʕal ṣadra, guršo saw… ṣaʕra w məḥyo ʕal ṣadra, kobuxyo.
contents.versio: 067. She has just burnt her own! Now she beats her breast, she cries, she cries, she cries, she beats her breast, she pulls her hair out and beats her breast, she cries.

contents.textus: 068. U+merək̇ kodoʕar, me bəṯrayye u+zlām kodoʕar, me bəṯr me… du+xēl di+kalo, ga kal kobəxyo, ‘Qay kobuxyat?’
contents.versio: 068. Her husband comes back, her husband comes back after them, after the … bridal procession. Look, here she is crying. ‘Why are you crying?’

contents.textus: 069. Kəmmo, ‘Ălo, moqaḏli i+barṯayḏi’. Komar, ‘Lo, ḥayf diḏax. Ma əbʕatwa dmuqḏat i+barṯayḏi! E, nafilo diḏax bdukṯa’.
contents.versio: 069. She says: ‘By God, I have burned my daughter!” He says: ‘No, your just deserts. Did you want to burn my daughter? Yes, yours fell into her place’.

contents.textus: 070. E, hawxa. W hun žə mə ra sāġ
contents.versio: 070. Yes, like so. You be well for me!

contents.textus: 001. Kətwa, latwa, rab̰m Ăḷo latwa, ḥaq! Aloho bi+šmàyoyo, kuḏʕat? Ḥaq! Lázəmyo dəmmina ‘ḥaq’!
contents.versio: 001. There was and there wasn’t, there was none greater than God, truth! God is in Heaven, do you know? Truth! It is necessary to say ‘truth!’

contents.textus: 002. Əmmi, kətwa dísane zʕuro parišā́n. Bayto kə́twayle zʕuro parišā́n, hawxa yani latwa haqqa b̥ḳerhati, žīr.
contents.versio: 002. They say, there was also ‘an unfortunate youth’. A family had an unfortunate youth, so like, he was not so gifted, clever.

contents.textus: 003. Əzzewa qmaṣ+ṣafure, əzzewa qmaṣ+ṣafure. Aṣ+ṣafurayḏe məxloṭiwa baʕ+ʕeze dar+ruʕye. Moḥə́nwayle.
contents.versio: 003. He would go out before the kids, he would go out before the kids. His kids would mingle with the shepherds’ goats. They would beat him.

contents.textus: 004. W marfewa ba+zyone bayn az+zadone, bayn ak+karme, moḥə́nwayle (Kofəhmutu, kuḏʕutu?).
contents.versio: 004. He would harmfully graze them within the fields of grain, within the vineyards, they would beat him (Do you understand? Do you know?).

contents.textus: 005. E, áydarbo ktowe? Yawmo kalkombal hawxa bi+ḳaviye di+qriṯo, čiḳe hawxa xdu+šaḥuno, barbaróšḳ kəmmina.
contents.versio: 005. Yes, how does it go? One day here he is, taking them to the edge of the village, a little bit like a kind of warm area, we call it a sunny side.

contents.textus: 006. Kalkosōmle, maltam kefe, sōmle xaniḳo (Aḥna, an+naʕime, hawxa maltmíwayna ǧare, naʕime, kefe, saymíwayna xaniḳo əmmíwayna, saymina bayto).
contents.versio: 006. Here he is, making for himself, gathering stones, making himself a little shelter. (We, the children, we sometimes as children gathered stones like so, we made what we called a little shelter, we made a house).

contents.textus: 007. Kosōm xaniḳo, naqqa aṯyo kurfo xuššḳé balaḳé. Əmmo, ‘Fiiiis’, fayarto šafiʕo ʕam gabe.
contents.versio: 007. He is making a little shelter, then along came a beauuutiful pied snake. She makes a slithering sound, she glided by his side.

contents.textus: 008. Mədle lak+kefayḏa, lak+kefe du+xaniḳayḏe, dmoḥe mina. Koḥōr kaṯyo ḥḏo+sawto, ḳalandore bēmrés. Kalkofəlto bəṯra duxlola. Kalkofəlto bəṯra duxlola.
contents.versio: 008. He took its stones, the stones of his little shelter, to throw at her. He sees an old, aged, dirty one has come. Here she is, pursuing her to eat her. Here she is, pursuing her to eat her.

contents.textus: 009. Naqqa hăma daʕər ʕalayo, i+pīsḳe, ʕal i+sawtayo dkəbʕo uxlola. Bak+kefe du+xaniḳayḏe, rap w rap w rap w rap w rap. Mḥele aʕla, qṭilole, qṭilole.
contents.versio: 009. Then at once he turned towards that one, the bad one, towards that old one who wanted to eat her. With the stones of his little house, bam-bam-bam-bam-bam. He struck her, he killed her, he killed her.

contents.textus: 010. Naqqa i+kurfò+xušḳè madʕaḷḷa foṯa, koqṭilole. Əmmo, ‘Ḳurḳó, qṭilux i+kurfayo?’ Omar, ‘E’.
contents.versio: 010. At once the beautiful snake turned around, here he is, having killed her. She says, ‘Boy, have you killed this snake?’ He says, ‘Yes’.

contents.textus: 011. Əmmo, ‘Tux, ono i+barṯo du+šēx dak+kurfeno. Itúx, gəmblallux gab babi, gdobelux dəšno’. Omar, ‘Hooo gdawṣūtəli!’ Əmmo, ‘Lo, sōzyo. Áydarbo gdawṣallux? Qṭilux i+nayarayḏi, gduxlówayli’.
contents.versio: 011. She says, ‘Come, I am the daughter of the chief of the snakes. Come, I’ll take you to my father’s, he’ll give you a bounty’. He said, ‘Ooh, (all of) you will bite me!’ She says, ‘No, it’s a promise! How could I bite you? You killed my enemy, she would have eaten me’.

contents.textus: 012. Azzehən. Azzə́n li+mʕarṯo dak+kurfe, ga ho ho ho ho! Konafəl nalanal aʕlayye, ‘W hano nóšoyo’, aṯəlle. Əmmo, ‘Klawu bdukṯayxu, hăma dmoḥutu mede, mqadmutu lu+zʕurano, kṭəryono babi šolaḥ qarʕe dkulxu!’
contents.versio: 012. He went along. They went into the snakes’ cave, oh, oh, oh, oh, look! Here they are, a moaning having fallen on them, ‘And this is a man’, they came to him. She says, ‘Stay in your place, if you beat something, if you approach this youth, I’ll have my father cut the heads off all of you!’

contents.textus: 013. Kalən, as+sowe kalən, ač+čučḳat … Hawxa, əmmo, ‘Kəmmanxu, klawu bdukṯayxu’.
contents.versio: 013. They stopped, the elders stopped, but the little ones... So, she says, ‘I am telling you, stay in your places’.

contents.textus: 014. Kalən bdukṯayye. Azzá məblila… mbela gab u+babo. Əmmo, ‘Yabo, flān kurfo gduxlówayli, lu+zʕurano qṭilole. Kobaʕle dəšno minux’.
contents.versio: 014. They stayed in their places. She went taking them… she took him over by her father. She says, ‘Dad, a certain snake would have eaten me, this boy killed her. He wants a bounty from you for himself’.

contents.textus: 015. Omar, ‘Lawo, ma məkubʕat?’ Omar, ‘Ašə́r zʕuro parišānno. Aṣ+ṣafurayḏi koqulbi la+zyone, kuzzə́n bayn aʕ+ʕeze dar+ruʕye, komoḥəlli. Hăma dsaymatli čara me medone hawxa … ġamo layt, kobaʕno’.
contents.versio: 015. He says, ‘Boy, what do you want?’ He says, ‘I am really an unfortunate boy. My kids harmfully overrun, they go among the goats of the shepherds, they beat me. Well, you could relieve me from such things … if it’s not a problem, I want it.

contents.textus: 016. Húlele rawṭo. (Rawṭo kuḏʕat mənyo? Ḥaṭro ha haqqa. Hawxa dkomoḥən lu+săwā̀l).
contents.versio: 016. He gave him a rod. Do you know what a rod is? A staff so long. For them to beat cattle like so.

contents.textus: 017. Omar, ‘Mədlux lu+rawṭano. Mar, ‘bəždəm!’, grawʕi… gyətwi. Dəmmat ‘bardəm!’, groʕən duxli gelo.
contents.versio: 017. He says, ‘Take this rod. Say, “Lat me bind ye”, they will lie down… they will sit down. If you say “Lat me lowse ye”, they will go grazing to eat grass’.

contents.textus: 018. E, omar, ‘Ăḷa, lo ṭaw mano. Ġắlăbe tawdi! Ăḷa gəmbanne’.
contents.versio: 018. Yes, he says, ‘By God, nothing is better than this. Thanks a lot! By God, I shall take it’.

contents.textus: 019. Mbele w azzá i+barṯo dak... du+šēx dak+kurfe aʕme, mofaqla, marḥaqla mak+kùrfeste dlo+dawṣile. W aṯi, maṭi laṣ+ṣafurayḏe.
contents.versio: 019. He took it, and the daughter of the sna… the chief of the snakes went with him, she brought him out, she also took him away from the snakes, lest they bite him. And he came back, he came to his kids.

contents.textus: 020. Veǧa domar, ‘bəždəm!’, grawʕi, domar, ‘bardəm!’ gdəmmi, ‘maʕ-maʕ-maʕ’ groʕən.
contents.versio: 020. Now then, if he says ‘Lat me bind ye’, they lie down, if he says ‘Lat me lowse ye’, they go, ‘maa-maa-maa’, they graze.

contents.textus: 021. Bu+mqamawo hul ʕaṣriye komar, dlo ṭoʕe, hăma komar ‘bəždəm’ w ‘bardəm’, ‘bəždəm’ w ‘bardəm’.
contents.versio: 021. In this way until evening, he says so he won’t forget, he always says, ‘Lat me bind ye’ and ‘Lat me lowse ye’, ‘Lat me bind ye’ and ‘Lat me lowse ye’.

contents.textus: 022. Ha ʕaṣriye, dísane aṯən aʕ+ʕeze lu+bayto. Mṭele aṣ+ṣafure qmu+tarʕo. I+emo əmmo, ‘U+qwirawo disa mṭele aṣ+ṣafure, kxolaṭṭe baʕ+ʕeze!’
contents.versio: 022. So it’s evening, the goats once again came home. He brought the kids in front of the gate. His mother says, ‘That silly one brought the kids back again, he is mixing them up with the goats!’

contents.textus: 023. Me hediḳa, lə+kṭore noše šəmʕi, omar, ‘bəždəm’. Rawiʕi kulle qmu+tarʕo.
contents.versio: 023. Deftly, not allowing people to hear, he says, ‘Lat me bind ye’. All of them lay down in front of the gate.

contents.textus: 024. Hak! Ăḷo, kalkó... kalkó… rawiʕi. Rawiʕi. Mədəḥluwwe aʕ+ʕezaṯṯe, ḥluwwe ḥalwo mənne, rawiʕi.
contents.versio: 024. Ooh! By God, here they are, here they are, having lain down. They have lain down. After they milked their goats, they milked them, they lay down.

contents.textus: 025. Me hediḳa omar ‘bardəm’. Naqqa čiki taḥt ann+emoṯe, čiki taḥt ann+emoṯe, komayṣi u+ḥalwaṯṯe.
