contents.versio: 025. Deftly he says, ‘Lat me lowse ye’. Then they sneaked under their mothers, they sneaked under their mothers, they are sucking their milk.

contents.textus: 026. W məd məṣṣe, disa frišənne, maḥtənne bi+kozḳe bašqa. Omar ‘bəždəm’, disa rawiʕi kulle bi+kozḳe.
contents.versio: 026. After they sucked, they separated them again, they put them in another pen. He says, ‘Lat me bind ye’, they all lay down in the pen again.

contents.textus: 027. Bu+mqamawo haḳa šato w tarte w tlāṯ, hawi rabo, azzé qmaʕ+ʕèzeste, hawxa.
contents.versio: 027. In that way, be it a year, and two, and three, he grew up, he went before the goats too, like so.

contents.textus: 028. Hawile u+rawṭawo (dayəm bíḏeyo, w lə+kṭore nóšeste dmašək w doḏaʕ) hawíleyo dălḗl.
contents.versio: 028. It happened that the rod (it is always in his hand, and he doesn’t let anyone else know and realize it) became a reminder for him.

contents.textus: 029. Yawmo, haḳa ġalabe, haḳa... hawi xort, dəmmina, xoṯayxu, ʕlaymo! Yawmo hawi məštuṯo disa bəqriṯo.
contents.versio: 029. One day, whether many or… he became mature, let’s say, like both of you, a young man! One day a wedding banquet happened in some village, again.

contents.textus: 030. Hawi məštuṯo bəqriṯo. Mə́ḷḷele lu+babo, omar, ‘Baba!’ Omar, ‘Mənyo?’ Omar, ‘Ádyawma məštúṯoyo. Kobaʕno dəzzúx qmaʕ+ʕeze me darbi.’
contents.versio: 030. A wedding banquet happened in some village. He said to his father, he says, ‘Dad!’ He says, ‘What is it?’ He says, ‘Today there is a wedding banquet. I want you to go before the goats in my place’.

contents.textus: 031. Omar, ‘ʕAl aʕ+ʕayne, abri. Dayəm kalúx qmaʕ+ʕeze, ádyawma gəzzí məḥlofux’. Omar, ‘Ónoste gəmfaraž̊no ʕal i+məštuṯo’.
contents.versio: 031. He says, ‘At your service, my son. Here you are, always in front of the goats, today I shall go instead of you’. He says, ‘And I shall take a look at the wedding banquet’.

contents.textus: 032. Azzé u+babo qmaʕ+ʕeze, qmaʕ+ʕeze, w hiye azzé bayn i+məštuṯo, w kalé u+rawṭḳayḏe aʕme, lə+kṭore noše mašək.
contents.versio: 032. The father went before the goats, before the goats, and he went to the wedding banquet, and here is his little rod with him, he doesn’t let anyone know.

contents.textus: 033. Ăḷo mora di+daʕwo səmme i+daʕwaṯe, nḥərre u+săwā̀l, aḳ+ḳabaniyat kosaymi bab+baredəš u+baṣro, aṗ+ṗirat konuqli maye. W axər dáʕwoyo, zəmri, ruqḏi, mhalhli.
contents.versio: 033. By God, the wedding hosts prepared that wedding feast, they slaughtered livestock, the homemakers are cooking meat in kettles, the women are fetching water. And finally, it’s the wedding feast, they are singing, dancing, and ululating.

contents.textus: 034. Məd aṯyo i+kalo... azzə́n li+kalo, məṭyalle, aṯyo lu+tarʕo di+dərto, gmanḥtila maʕl i+səsto, gmanḥtila maʕl i+səsto.
contents.versio: 034. Once the bride has come… they went for the bride, they brought her, she came to the courtyard gate, they are taking her down from the horse, they are taking her down from the horse.

contents.textus: 035. W aṗ+ṗirat, kanné am+maġrafyoṯe biḏayye, komxalṭi ab+baredəš. W u+ḥaṯno, kalé ʕal i+goro, w u+qariwo, kalá i+šarbo biḏe dmoḥela bi+arʕo, dtowaḷḷa.
contents.versio: 035. And the women, here are the ladles in their hands, they are stirring the kettles. And the groom, here he is on the roof, and the best man, here is the flask in his hand to throw on the ground, to smash it.

contents.textus: 036. Naqqa me hediḳa komar ‘bəždəm’. Kulle fayiši. I+kalo fayišo, raġlo mdiḏa ʕal kaṯpe du+zlām, ḥḏo ʕal i+səsto. A+gḏone fayiši, a+mxole fayiši ʕal kaṯpe daṗ+ṗirat, am+maġrafyoṯe fayiši biḏe daḳ+ḳabaniyat. W aṗ+ṗirat, dgəmhalhli, femayye fāš ftiḥo. I+šarbo fayišo biḏe du+qariwo.
contents.versio: 036. Then he says under his breath, ‘Lat me bind ye’. Everyone froze. The bride froze, a leg of hers was on the man’s shoulder, one on the horse. Jugs froze, pitchers froze upon the women’s shoulders, ladles froze in the homemakers’ hands. And the women that were ululating, their mouth froze open. The flask froze in the best man’s hand.

contents.textus: 037. Omar, ‘Bas haṯe măsáleyo w hano mən... áydarboyo?’ Flān behvā́n. ‘E, áydarbo ktowe? Mənyo lo+mənyo? Qay i+kalaṯe latyo năṣī́b du+zʕurano? Ayna dšore i+măsalaṯe, ṭruyo i+kalo ele’.
contents.versio: 037. He says, ‘But this is a problem and what’s this... how come?’ And so on. ‘Yes, how could it be? What could it be? Is this bride not that boy’s soulmate? Whoever solves this problem, let the bride be his’.

contents.textus: 038. B̥qawl komqadamle, b̥qawl, b̥qarā́r, gab u+qašo, gab u+aġà, gab ar+rabone di+qriṯo. Huwwe sōz, əmmi, ‘Ayna dšore i+masalaṯe, gdobínale i+kalo!’
contents.versio: 038. With a pledge, he approached the priest, the chief, the village elders, with a pledge, with a proposal. They made a promise, they say, ‘Whoever solves this problem, we shall give him the bride!’

contents.textus: 039. Omar ‘bardəm’, me hediḳa omar ‘bardəm’. Naqqa aṗ+ṗirat əmmi ‘Li-li-li-li!’ A+gḏone nafili me kaṯpe daṗ+ṗirat, twiri. I+šarbo nafilo me kaṯpe du+qariwo, twīr… miḏe du+qariwo, twīr. W i+kalo nafilo me ʕal qa... maʕl u+səsyo, me ʕal kaṯpe du+zlām, twīr qarʕa.
contents.versio: 039. He says ‘Lat me lowse ye’, he says ‘Lat me lowse ye’ under his breath. Then the women say, ‘Li-li-li-li!’. The jugs fell from the women’s shoulders, they broke. The flask fell from the shoulder of the best man, it broke... from the hand of the best man, it broke. And the bride fell from the hea… from the horse, from the man’s shoulder, her head broke.

contents.textus: 040. Axər hawi mede hno… hawi xēr. ‘Mənyo, lo+mənyo? E, latwa naṣíb du+zlamano’. Hediḳa mḥele bi+qamaytayye, məblole lu+bayto.
contents.versio: 040. Finally, a whatsit thing happened … it became good. ‘What could it be? Yes, she was not that man’s soulmate.’ After that, he struck off ahead of them, he took her home.

contents.textus: 041. Məblole lu+bayto, koṯe ʕaṣriye u+babo. Ga, kalá məštuṯo gabe! Komṭélele ḥḏo. K_Xerá xudé_K! E, háyostene… K_ṫə žməra saġ_K, háyostene tayimo.
contents.versio: 041. He took her home, his father comes in the evening. Look, here’s a wedding party at his place! He has brought back a woman. God is good! Yes, that one… Be well for me, that one is finished.

contents.textus: 001. Kətwa Aḥmád Aġá, Alyás, w Oṣmán Aġá. Oṣmán Aġá u+aḥùnowa.
contents.versio: 001. There was Ahmad Agha, Ilyas, and Osman Agha. Osman Agha was his brother.

contents.textus: 002. Aḥmád Aġá təǧǧārwa, kə́twayle săwā́l ġắlăbe. K̇očar, xəd u+k̇očar, kə́twayle săwā́l ġắlăbe. W u+aḥunayḏe faqírowa, Oṣmán faqírowa.
contents.versio: 002. Ahmad Agha was a merchant, he had abundant livestock. A nomad, like a nomad, he had abundant livestock. And his brother was poor, Osman was poor.

contents.textus: 003. U+ʕulmo mqaḥamwa ʕal Oṣmán zəd me Aḥmád Aġá. Oṣmán Aġá faqírowa, hăma gáwrowa, u+ʕulmo əzzáwayle affele.
contents.versio: 003. The whole world bonded with Osman more than with Ahmad Agha. Osman Agha was poor but brave, and the world beat a path to his door.

contents.textus: 004. E, Aḥmád Aġá məqḥərwa, məqḥərwa. Məs sōm hano? Omar, ‘Lə+qqoḏe hawxa ʕam u+aḥunano diḏi. Haymén šqile u+rišo mini. Áydarbo howeli šawʕo+abne, w ele lowele abro, w hawxa u+ʕulmo kuzzə́n gabe’.
contents.versio: 004. Yes, Ahmad Agha was upset, he was upset. What’s this guy to do? He says, ‘It is not working with that brother of mine. He surely took first place from me. How is it that I have seven sons and he has no son, and even so the whole world goes to his side’.

contents.textus: 005. ‘W ḥəzbe lo+ṭrèleli, w ḥăsáb haw ṭréleli, w šqile u+rišo mini w híyeyo.’ Qam, omar, omar, ‘Dlo+maqṭanne, čara layto’.
contents.versio: 005. ‘And he did not leave any merit for me, he no longer left any value for me, and he took first place from me, and it’s him’. He up and says, he says, ‘Unless I have him killed, there is no solution’.

contents.textus: 006. Hánostene mək kosōm? Kobele kmo qamariye lḥa, w komaqṭele, komaqṭele. I+àṯtostene lḥal ḥrénoyo, ṭʕə́ntoyo i+aṯto. Qṭile u+aḥuno druḥe. I+aṯto d Oṣmán əmmo, əmmo, ‘Hăwara! Áydarbo qoṭal u+aḥuno druḥe!?’
contents.versio: 006. As for this one, what does he do? He gives however many coins to a certain man, and he had him killed, he had him killed. As for his wife, she is in a family way, his wife is pregnant. He killed his own brother. The wife of Osman says, ‘Help! How come he kills his own brother!?’

contents.textus: 007. Hiye koyome, komar, ‘Lo eli maqṭeli!’ W hiya kəmmo, ‘Elux maqṭelux!’ W hiye koyome, komar, ‘Lo!’ Qaḏila at+təšʕo+yarḥe li+aṯto, hawile abro, maḥatla əšme du+babo aʕle, Oṣmán.
contents.versio: 007. He swears, he says, ‘No, it was not I who had him killed!’ And she says, ‘It was you who had him killed!’ And he swears, he says, ‘No!’ After nine months had passed for the wife, a son was born to him. She gave him his father’s name, Osman.

contents.textus: 008. Oṣmánstene naʕímoyo, hawi əšmo birawā́r (čirókeyo), hawi əšmo birawā́r u+zʕuro. Li+emo mə́ḷḷale, əmmo, ‘Oṣmán!’ Omar, ‘Ha, yade!’ Əmmo, ‘K̇urem, lʕammux maqṭele babux, maqṭele babux žboy diḏi, hăma ono lo+kuzzì aʕme. Žboy diḏi maqṭele babux’. Omar, ‘Yade, áydarbo qqoṭal u+aḥuno druḥe?’
contents.versio: 008. As for Osman, he is a child, he became a little more mature (it’s a story), the boy became a little more mature. His mother told him, she says, ‘Osman!’ He says, ‘Here, Mummy!’ She says: ‘K_My boy_K, your uncle had your father killed, he had your father killed on account of me, but I am not going with him. On account of me, he had your father killed’. He says, ‘Mummy, how come he kills his own brother!?’

contents.textus: 009. Əmmo, ‘Ono kəmmaḷḷux’. E, Oṣmánstene (čirok̇e, mắsale di+čiròk̇eyo) hawi rabo, səmle ḥəkkəm dəšwaḥṣar tmonaḥṣar+əšne, čīk bann+əšne, aṯi b̥k̇ēr du+silā̀ḥ, w qə́mṯestene kiba ha haqqask̇e, hurək̇yo, hurək̇yo, hăma gáwroyo, ʕal u+babo aṯi gawro.
contents.versio: 009. She says, ‘I am telling you’. Yes, as for Osman (a story, it’s a story thing), he became big, he became 17-18 years old, he became of age, he became good with weapons, and as for his stature, it was yea high, he is tiny, he is tiny, but he is brave, he became brave after his father.

contents.textus: 010. Hánostene, Aḥmád Aġá, kətle šawʕo+abne w barṯo. Səṫṫiye i+bàrṯoyo, w aš+šawʕo+abne ḥrene kətle. Aš+šawʕo lo+ṭowən baṣmoro. Ḥa mənne omar, ‘Yabo!’ Omar, ‘Ha’. Omar, ‘Yabo, mtaláf u+săwalàno, basyo! Gmaḥtat ruḥux ʕal u+săwalàno.’ Omar, ‘Ooo k̇urem, Ăla lo+kəmzabanne, u+săwāl lo+kəmzabanne.’ K̇óčaryo. Hánostene lo+ksōm bdu+abro naʕimo.
contents.versio: 010. As for this one, Ahmad Agha, he had seven sons and a daughter. Səṫṫiye is his daughter, and otherwise he has seven sons. Those seven aren’t worth a plug nickel. One of them says, ‘Dad!’ He says: ‘Here’. He says, ‘Dad, sell off this livestock, enough already! You are putting yourself out because of this livestock’. He says, ‘Ooo, my boy, by God I won’t sell them. The livestock, I won’t sell them’. He is a nomad. As for this one, he doesn’t do according to his little son.

contents.textus: 011. Məḷḷele lu+abro naʕimo, omar, ‘K̇urem’. Omar, ‘Ha’. Omar, ‘Lawo, qaymina marke! Haw fāš čeriye harke, lo+fāš marʕa harke. Gəblina u+săwalayḏan lu+zozan, qlaʕən.
contents.versio: 011. He said to his little son, he says, ‘My son!’. He says, ‘Here’. He says, ‘Boy, let’s get out of here! Here, no more pasture is left, there is no pasturage left here. We will take our livestock for the summer pasturage. Drive them’.

contents.textus: 012. Azzehən lu+zozan li+qăza d Rəzgán Aġá. Rəzgán Aġá čalk̇óyoyo, čalk̇óyene. Čīk bu+ḥədudaṯṯe, ḥəḷḷe kalá baxča, baxča basəmto, tēr di+marʕayḏe.
contents.versio: 012. They went for the summer pasturage to the district of Rəzgan Agha. Rəzgan Agha is a Yezidi, they are Yezidis. He slipped past their boundaries, he saw, here’s a field, a pleasant field, enough for his pasturage.

contents.textus: 013. Aḥmád Aġá məḷḷe lann+abne, lann+əšto abne. (U+naʕimo laṯi aʕmayye.) Məḷḷe lann+əšto naʕimayḏe, omar, omar, ‘K̇urem’. Omar, ‘Ha’. Omar, ‘Maḥtínanne bi+baxčaṯe’. ‘E’, omar, ‘Yabo, i+baxčaṯe ma i+baxčaṯe bexwadiyo?! Latyo dlo+more, Yabo?! Doṯəllan, ktawri ʕarz diḏan, ktawrilan, balki qquṭli hən mínanstene, yabo.’
contents.versio: 013. Ahmad Agha said to his sons, to his six sons. (The little one didn’t come with them.) He said to his six kids, he says, ‘My sons’. They say, ‘Here’. He says, ‘Let’s put them in this field’. They say, ‘Dad, this field, is this field ownerless?! Doesn’t it have an owner, Dad? If they come to us, they will cut us down to size, they will cut us, perhaps they will kill some of us too, Dad’.

contents.textus: 014. Omar, ‘Haymén gmaḥanno i+k̇onayḏi ha harke, bayn i+baxča basəmtaṯe. Gmaḥanno u+săwalayḏi harke, gmarʕene harke’. Maḥatle i+k̇onayḏe tamo, w marʕele u+săwalayḏe. Hánostene, Oṣmán du+braziyayḏe, məḷḷela li+emo, omar, ‘Yade’. Əmmo, ‘Ha’. Omar, ‘ʕAmmi azzé lu+zozan, ónostene gəzzí bəṯre w bəṯre’.
contents.versio: 014. He says, ‘I will surely put my tent right here, within that pleasant field. I will put my livestock here, I will pasture it here’. He put his tent there and pastured his livestock. As for this one, Osman his nephew, he said to his mother, he says, ‘Mummy’. She says, ‘Here’. He says, ‘My uncle went for the summer pasturage, I will also go wherever he goes.

contents.textus: 015. ‘Qayyo k̇urem?’ Omar, ‘Yade, b̥k̇ēr dgawruṯo lukṯe. Tloyo diḏo, ləktole iḏo, lo hiye w lo+ann+əšto abne. Šawʕo+abne kətle. U+gawro u+naʕímoyo. Laṯi, ann+əšto ḥrene ḥfar w ṭmar, lukṯən b̥k̇ēr. W koḏaʕno ʕammi ktowaḷḷan. Haymén gəzzino ónoste, ónoste gəzzino.
contents.versio: 015. ‘Why is it, my son?’ He says, ‘Mummy, he is no good at heroics. Raising a fist, he will not raise a fist, neither he nor his six sons. He has seven sons. The hero is the little one. He did not come, the other six: dig (a grave) and bury, they are good for nothing. And I know that my uncle hurts them. Surely I will go too, I too will go.

contents.textus: 016. Əmmo, ‘Lawo, dsaymat bdiḏi, taw! Lo+kəzzano’. Omar, ‘Haymén gəzzino, qəm!’ Maqəmle i+emo druḥe, maḥatle i+k̇onayḏe buwā́r di+k̇one du+ʕammo, d Aḥmád Aġá. Maḥatle i+k̇onayḏe buwā́r di+k̇one du+ʕammo.
contents.versio: 016. She says, ‘Boy, if you are going to do it my way, stay! We are not going’. He says, ‘I shall surely go, get up! He made his own mother get up, he pitched his tent facing the tent of his uncle, of Ahmad Agha. He pitched his tent facing the tent of his uncle.

contents.textus: 017. Aḥmád Aġá komar, ‘Hawo, mányawo maḥatle i+k̇onayḏe tamo?’ Azzé u+abrayḏe u+rabo, ḥəḷḷe, kalé u+abro du+ʕammo. Omar, ‘Yabo’. Omar, ‘Ha’. Omar, ‘Oṣmanyo, Oṣmán aṯi, Oṣmanyo.’ Omar, ‘E, təmā́m, Oṣmán, Oṣmán’.
contents.versio: 017. Ahmad Agha says: ‘That one, who is that one who pitched his tent over there?’ His eldest son went, looked, here’s his uncle’s son. He says, ‘Dad’. He says, ‘Here’. He says, ‘It’s Osman, Osman has come, it’s Osman’. He says, ‘Yes, fine, Osman, Osman’.

contents.textus: 018. E, kəzzehən qm u+săwalaṯṯe. Rəzgán Aġástene koṯe me támoda, kalé rawixo ʕal i+səstayḏe, w koṯe, koḥōr, kalé, haylooo lu+săwal, kalé bi+baxčayḏe. Omar, ‘Hano manyo? Abre dmányano, dmaḥatle bi+k̇onayḏi dlo+šewər, dlo+mšawaḷḷe ebi. W maḥatle bi+baxčayḏi, w maḥatle i+k̇one b̥falga di+baxčayḏi, komarfe u+săwal bi+baxčayḏi, w bi+ḥəmyayḏi … Manyano?
contents.versio: 018. Yes, they go with their livestock. As for Rəzgan Agha, he comes from over there, here he is, riding on his mare, and he comes, he sees. Here’s so much livestock, here in his field! He says, ‘Who is this? Whose son is this, who set up in my field without asking, without asking me. And he set up in my field, and he pitched his tent in the middle of my field, he releases his livestock in my field and in my heights… Who is this?’

contents.textus: 019. Mšāʕle tre, mšāʕle tre, azzehən. Omar, ‘Man hatu, man hatu?’ Omar, ‘Aḥna, e’, omar, ‘Aḥna ann+abne d Aḥmad Aġana. Aṯina áḥnastene … ḥeḏər Gziro … me ḥeḏər Gziro aṯina, maḥatlan ak̇+k̇onayḏan harke, w haymén u+săwalayḏan … Mu+kafno mahzamlan, aṯina larke, səmlan qəṣd d Aloho w dəṯxu, dmaḥtina. Maḥatli i+k̇onaṯe harke, w haymén gdomarwayno, gəmšālwayno, gdomarwayno, “Gəzzino gabayye” … Kalkó hat aṯat, Aġá, Rəzgán Aġá! Kalkaṯina, haymén kalán qumux kalye, u+mede dəmmat, ahla w sahla.
contents.versio: 019. He sent out two, he sent out two, they went. He says, ‘Who are you, who are you?’ He says, ‘We, yes, we are the sons of Ahmad Agha. As for us, we came … around Gziro … we came from around Gziro, we pitched our tents here, and surely our livestock… We have escaped from hunger, we made it to God and to you, to set up. I pitched that tent here, and surely I would have said, I would have asked, I would have said, ‘I am going by them’ … Here you have come, Agha, Rəzgan Agha! We have just come, surely here we are standing before you, and whatever you say, be my guest’.

contents.textus: 020. Omar hawxa, omar, ‘E’. Omar, ‘Təmā́m, haṯe … mən k̇áčk̇eyo? Omar, ‘Haymén i+k̇ačk̇àyḏiyo’. ‘Hútoyo, lo?’ Omar, ‘Lo’. Omar, ‘Liwoli, hăma mdagalto dḥayo.’ Omar, ‘Yawo háwliyo’.
contents.versio: 020. He says like so, he says, ‘Yes’. He says, ‘Fine, this one … who is the girl?’ He says, ‘Surely, it’s my daughter’. ‘She is taken, no?’ He says, ‘No’. He says, ‘I have not given her up, but she is betrothed to someone’. He says, ‘For goodness’ sake, give her to me!’

contents.textus: 021. Omar, ‘Ba lo, ḥayra, may koḏaʕno? Kalkó dḥozina … mdaglolan, ánnaqqa dḥozina. Kətlan aḥuno … kətlan tre … šawʕo+aḥunònena, əšto minan aṯi, w ḥa minan fāš bu+bayto. W layban dlo+maḥunayna u+ḥrènostene dəmdaglínala. D̥ḥozina. Ăloho ráboyo!
contents.versio: 021. He says, ‘Well, buddy, how would I know? Here, let’s go see… we have betrothed her. Now then, let’s see. We have a brother … we have two… we are seven brothers, seven of us came, and one of us stayed at home. Save with our other brother we are unable to betrothe her. Let’s see, hopefully.

contents.textus: 022. ‘Hawxa…’ Omar, ‘E’. ‘Ləgbútula?’ Omar, ‘Lo’. Ḥa mənne, Aḥmád Aġá, omar, ‘Ləgbena’. ‘Ləgbatla – ləgbatla.’ Rəzgán Aġá qām azzeyo mšāʕle ʕaṣro+zlamat. Omar, ‘Zoxu mṭawu Aḥmád Aġá, w moṣērle w mṭáwule’.
contents.versio: 022. ‘So that’s how it is’… He says, ‘Yes’. ‘You won’t give her up?’ He says, ‘No’. One of them, Ahmad Agha, says, ‘I won’t give her up’. ‘You won’t give her up – you won’t give her up’. Rəzgan Agha up and went, he sent ten men. He says, ‘Go bring Ahmad Agha, bind him and bring him’.

contents.textus: 023. Aṯən ʕaṣro+zlamat bu+silāḥ, w aṯənle l Aḥmád Aġá. Mədde l Aḥmád Aġá, moṣarre w dəblile, dəblile. Oṣmán Aġá koḥṓr, ‘K̇uro, qay hawxa kosaymutu?’ Əmmi, ‘L Rəzgán Aġá məḷḷe, ‘Mṭawule!’ Omar, ‘Marféwule, marféwule!’ Lo+marfalle. Qṭile tmanyo mənne, w lətre mahzamme. L Oṣmán Aġá, l Oṣmán qṭile tmanyo, lətre mahzamme.
contents.versio: 023. Ten men came forth with weapons, and they came to Ahmad Agha. They seized Ahmad Agha, bound him to take him away, to take him away. Osman Agha looks, ‘Boys, why are you doing this?’ They say, ‘Rəzgan Agha said, ‘Bring him!’ He says, ‘Let him go, let him go!’ They didn’t let him go. He killed eight of them, and two escaped. Osman Agha, Osman Agha killed eight, and two escaped.

contents.textus: 024. Mahzamme a+trànəkstene. Ḥa mənne, šləḥle … mḥele u+sayfo ʕal feme, šləḥle nḥire w feme w tavda. W lu+ḥreno mahzamle, mahzamme w azzehən.
contents.versio: 024. As for those two, they escaped. One of them, he cut off … he struck his sword against his face, he cut off his nose and his mouth altogether. And the other one escaped, they escaped and got away.

contents.textus: 025. ‘K̇uro, qay hawxa?’ Omar, ‘Haymén kətwa ḥa, kəpwayle haqqask̇e. W aṯi w qṭile tmanyo aḥ+ḥawronayḏi. W haymén a+tretàynaste mahzamlan. Ónostene, mḥele u+hno … ʕal qarʕi, nḥiri w femi tavda, šliḥile’, wooo wooo diḏe hawxa.
contents.versio: 025. ‘Boys, why like so?’ He says, ‘Surely, there was one, he was yea high. He came and killed eight of my friends. And surely, the two of us, we escaped. As for me, he struck the whatsit … against my head, my nose and my mouth altogether, he cut them off’, his murmuring like so.

contents.textus: 026. ‘Hawxa?!’ Omar, ‘E’. Səmle əšti+zlamat kār. Omar, ‘Lukwe dləzóxule! Izoxu, qṭalu hawo d … zoxu qṭálule. Zux, lawo, aʕmayye, maḥwə́lleyo’. Omar, ‘Haaawheník̇eyo, háááwk̇eyo’. Hawi šāš ḥəngi zāʕ mine, kozōʕ mine, ‘Haaawhenik̇eyo’. ‘Hawxa … Hánoyo?’ Əmmi, ‘E’.
contents.versio: 026. ‘So that’s how it is?!’ He says, ‘Yes’. He prepared sixty men. He says, ‘You cannot but go to him! Go, kill that one … go kill him. Go, boy, with them, show him to them’. He says, ‘He’s oh - oh - oh - ver yonder, oh - oh - oh - ver yon’. He became confounded, since he was so scared of him, he is scared of him. ‘‘He’s oh - oh - oh - ver yonder’. ‘So … is this him?’ They say, ‘Yes’. ‘This is him?’ They say, ‘Yes’.

contents.textus: 027. Hǧə́mmalle, hǧə́mmalle, qṭile ann+əšti, qṭile ann+əšti. Rəzgán Aġá koḥōr mi+mḏara, koḥōr, noše lə+kḥoze. ‘K̇uro, háykoda, háykoda azzə́n? Hayko …’ flān behvān … ‘Háykoda azzə́n hani?’ Əmmi, ‘Haymén qṭile ann+əšti’.
contents.versio: 027. They attacked him, they attacked him, he killed these sixty, he killed these sixty. Rəzgan Agha looks from the observatory, he doesn’t see anybody. ‘Boys, whereabouts, whereabouts have they gone? Where…’, and so on and so forth… ‘Whereabouts have these ones gone?’ They say, ‘Surely, he has killed the sixty’.

contents.textus: 028. ‘Hawxa?’ Əmmi, ‘E’. Omar, ‘Bavo lə+qqoḏe hawxa’. Hule xabro li+ʕašərto, Alyas, hule xabro li+ʕašərto. Maltamle tloṯalfo+šaqṣat mi+ʕašərtayḏe l Rəzgán Aġá w mšayʕile l Oṣmán l Aḥmád Aġá.
contents.versio: 028. ‘So, that’s how it is?’ They say, ‘Yes’. He says, ‘Daddy-o, it isn’t working out like so’. He sent word to the tribe, Ilyas, he sent word to the tribe. Rəzgan Agha gathered three thousand men from his tribe, and he sent them after Osman <and> Ahmad Agha.

contents.textus: 029. Aḥmád Aġá hiye šilo ləktole, w ann+àbneste šilo ləkwən, w hǧə́mmalle l Oṣmán Aġá, Oṣmán.
contents.versio: 029. Ahmad Agha shows fear, and his sons also become afraid, and they attacked Osman Agha, Osman.

contents.textus: 030. ‘K̇uro, haynayo?’ Əmmi, ‘Hánoyo.’ Əmmi, ‘Mala+bave+Rəzgán Aġá be, ho moṯ Rəzgán Aġá, hiye w babawo diḏe. Maltámlelan tloṯalfo+šaqṣat ha ʕalano! Kibe xud diko!
contents.versio: 030. ‘Boys, which one is he?’ They say, ‘This one’. They say, ‘Let it be on the house of Rəzgan Agha, let Rəzgan Agha die, he and that father of his. He gathered us, three thousand persons here against this one. He is the size of a rooster’

contents.textus: 031. W rawəx ʕal i+səstayḏe, omar, ‘Yade’. Əmmo, ‘Ha’. Omar, ‘Kal kazzínanne’. Əmmo, ‘Oṣmán, k̇urem, taw, nḥat, k̇urem, nḥat mi+səsto’. Omar, ‘Haymén gəzzínanne, yade’.
contents.versio: 031. And he mounted upon his mare, he says, ‘Mummy’. She says, ‘Here’. He says, ‘I am just going to go to them’. She says, ‘Osman, my boy, sit down, get down, my boy, get down from the mare’. He says, ‘I will surely go to them, Mummy’.

contents.textus: 032. Azzeyo, qṭile alfo w ḥamməšmo mənne. Ann+alfo w ḥamməšmo ḥrene mahzamme, kul ḥa bdúkṯoda azzé. Mṭarqile, kul ḥa bdúkṯoda azzeyo. Qṭile alfo w ḥamməšmo mənne, alfo ḥamməšmo mahzamme, xud dmoḥat lappe dḥəmṣe bi+arʕo, kul ḥḏo bdúkṯoda dəzzayo. Hániste kul ḥa bdúkṯoda azzeyo, mahzamme, mahzamme.
contents.versio: 032. He went, he killed one thousand and five hundred of them. Another one thousand and five hundred fled, each one went towards some place. He dispersed them, each one went towards some place. He killed one thousand and five hundred of them, one thousand and five hundred fled, as if you cast a handful of chickpeas against the ground, so each pea goes towards some place. As for these ones, each one went towards some place, they fled, they fled.

contents.textus: 033. Maxlaṣṣe hən mənne, azzehən se Rəzgán Aġá.’ Omar, ‘Lawo, haymén, qṭile alfo w ḥamməšmo minan, kalkó áḥnaste mahzamlan, aṯina’. ‘Hawxaaa?!’ Omar, ‘E’. Omar, ‘Haymén, hano, dlowe bəbebaxtiye mtalafno hano, hano … lukwe hawxa ʕamano’.
contents.versio: 033. Some of them escaped, they went to Rəzgan Agha’s. He says, ‘Boy, surely, he killed one thousand and five hundred of us, as for us here, we fled, we have come’. ‘So, that’s how it is?!’ He says, ‘Yes’. He says, ‘Surely, this one, unless I destroy this one in a disgraceful way, - this one, otherwise it will not work with him’.

contents.textus: 034. Rəzgán Aġá mšāʕle šaqṣ, ḥa šaqṣ. Omar, ‘Zux amaḷḷe l Aḥmad Aġá, amár, ‘Rəzgán Aġá məḷḷe, ‘Kobaʕno, ono ʕabəṇṇo ba+qṭiloyayḏi kulle, ʕabəṇṇo b̥kulle, kobaʕno hăma dʔoṯeno lalyo gabux ḥozenux’
contents.versio: 034. Rəzgan Agha sent a person, one person. He says, ‘Go tell Ahmad Agha, say, “Rəzgan Agha said, ‘I want, I have gotten over all those of mine who were killed, I have gotten over all of them, I only want to come by you some night to see you’”’.

contents.textus: 035. Hawxa omar, ‘E’. Aṯi, aṯi, ‘Salām ʕalayk!’ ‘ʕAlaykumu ssalām. Ha, lawo, məx xēryo?’ ‘Aḥmád Aġá!’ omar. ‘Aḥmád Aġá’ omar, ‘Ha!’ Omar, ‘Ḥayra, haymén mšaʕleli l Rəzgán Aġá, məḷḷe, ‘Kobaʕno doṯeno ḥozenanne; ʕabəṇṇo ba+qṭiloye dəqṭəlle kúllestene, ʕabəṇṇo. Ṭrowən xaṭər d Aḥmad Aġá, w kobaʕno doṯeno gabe w hamma doxanni fako dmuklo gabe, w hiye doṯe gabi, doxele fako dmuklo gabi’.
contents.versio: 035. He says like so, ‘Yes’. He came, he came, ‘Greetings to you!’ ‘To you too. Here, boy, what’s up?’ ‘Ahmad Agha!’ he says. Ahmad Agha says, ‘Here’. He says, ‘Buddy, Rəzgan Agha has surely sent me, he said, ‘I want to come see them, I have gotten over all the ones whom they killed too, I have gotten over it. Let it be out of respect for Ahmad Agha, and I want to come by him and only eat a bit of food with him, and if he comes by me, let him eat a bit of food with me’.

contents.textus: 036. Omar, ‘Yabo, ṭrowe! Ahla w sahla, ṭroṯe!’ Hánostene kodoʕar, u+zlamawo koṯe, komar, ‘Rəzgán Aġá!’ Komar, ‘Ha’. Komar, ‘Məḷḷe, ‘Ṭroṯe, sarbastyo, ṭroṯe!’ ‘Hawxa?’ Omar, ‘E’. Omar, ‘De qumu, qumu qădar mo šaqṣaṭ mənxu, ṭroṯe aʕmi qădar mo w gəzzano’.
contents.versio: 036. He says, ‘Daddy-o, it’ll do! Welcome, let him come!’ As for this one, he returns, that man comes back, he says, ‘Rəzgan Agha!’ He says, ‘Here’. He says, ‘He said, “Let him come, it is safe, let him come!”’ ‘So that’s how it is?’ He says, ‘Yes’. He says, ‘Come on, get up, get up, about one hundred persons out of you, let about a hundred come with me and we shall go’.

contents.textus: 037. Malaxxe, aṯən, səmme ruḥaye kār, mədde lu+silaḥaṯṯe w aṯən. W kalé Oṣmánstene bi+k̇onak̇ayḏe, w aṯən li+k̇one d Aḥmád Aġá am+mo, aṯən li+k̇one d Aḥmád Aġá.
contents.versio: 037. They took off, they came, they prepared themselves, they took their weapons and came. And here’s Osman as well in his tent, and the hundred came to the tent of Ahmad Agha, they came to the tent of Ahmad Agha.

contents.textus: 038. Aḥmád Aġá nḥə́ḷḷalle barxat, sə́mlalle muklo bu+qadər w bi+maʕrifa, zbə́ṭlalle xaṭər, w məḷḷele l Rəzgán Aġá, omar, ‘Rəzgán Aġá, hăma kalí ono gweto w hat šalfo, kalí qumux kalyo’. Omar, ‘Kul mede xaṭər diḏux’. Omar, ‘Təmā́m! ʕOmar baytux, miḥasyo emux w babux’. Omar, ‘Təmā́m’.
contents.versio: 038. Ahmad Agha slaughtered some lambs for them, he prepared food for them with honour and acknowledgement, he showed deference to them, and he said to Rəzgan Agha, he says, ‘Rəzgan Agha, here I am, like a lamb to the slaughter, here I am standing before you’. He says, ‘Anything, out of respect for you’. He says, ‘Fine! Thank you, bless your mother and father’. He says, ‘Fine’.

contents.textus: 039. Hánistene komaḥəšmi, u+muklaṯṯe kuxlile, w komar, ‘De ánnaqqa, kəbʕina doṯat, dəzzán gabayna, ánnaqqa hat doṯat gabayna, mʕazmínalux.
contents.versio: 039. So they dine, they eat their food, and he says, ‘Come on, now then, we want you to come, that we go by us, now then, that you come by us, we invite you.

contents.textus: 040. Omar, ‘Ahla w sahla’. Məḷḷe laš+šawʕo abnayḏe, omar, ‘Lawo, sumu ruḥayxu kār, ádlalyo gəzzano se Rəzgán Aġá li+ʕazima, lu+muklo. Itoxu, malexu, zano!’ U+naʕimo omar, ‘Yabo, lo+kəzzano!’ Omar, ‘Qəm!’ Komar, ‘Lo+kəzzano, yabo, lo+kəzzano’ u+naʕimo. Omar, ‘Haymén gəzzano.’
contents.versio: 040. He says, ‘Welcome’. He says to his seven sons, he says, ‘Boys, prepare yourselves, this night we shall go by Rəzgan Agha’s for a get-together, for dining. Go, move, let’s go!’ The little one says, ‘Dad, let’s not go!’ He says, ‘Get up!’ He says, ‘Let’s not go, Dad, let’s not go’, the little one. He says, ‘Surely, we shall go’.

contents.textus: 041. Ann+əšto ḥrene əmmi, ‘Ăla gəzzano!’ Hano … Səmme ruḥayye kār lann+əšto w l Aḥmad Aġá, w rawixi ʕal as+səsyaṯte. Oṣmán Aġá fatəl b̥qamuṯayye, aṯi lqamuṯayye. Omar, ‘ʕAmmo’. Omar, ‘Ha’. Omar, ‘ʕAmmo, səm bdiḏi, ləzzúx, dʕar. Komaṇṇux ləzzúx dʕar’. Omar, ‘Haymén gəzzino. Rəzgán Aġá məḷḷe, “Toxu li+ʕazima!” Gəzzano li+ʕazima, gduxlina u+muklayḏe w gdoṯina”’. ‘Hawxa…’ Omar, ‘E’. Omar, ‘Izoxu’.
contents.versio: 041. The other six say, ‘By God, we will go!’ This one… The six and Ahmad Agha prepared themselves, and they mounted their horses. Osman Agha circled around before them, he came before them. He says, ‘Uncle’. He says, ‘Here’. He says, ‘Uncle, do it my way, don’t go, come back. I tell you, don’t go, come back’. He says, ‘Surely, we will go’. Rəzgan Agha said, ‘Go to the get-together’. We will go to the get-together, we will eat his food, and we will come back’. ‘So that’s how it is’. He says, ‘Yes’. He says: ‘Go ahead’.

contents.textus: 042. Malaxxe marke ltamhenik̇é. Oṣmán Aġá dísane qrélele, omar, ‘ʕAmmo, klay!’ Omar, ‘Mənyo?’ Omar, ‘ʕAmmo, klay gdoṯeno ónostene’.
contents.versio: 042. They took off from here over yonder. Osman Agha called him again, he says, ‘Uncle, wait a bit!’ He says, ‘What is it?’ He says, ‘Uncle, wait a bit, I too will come’.

contents.textus: 043. Omar, ‘Lawo, layt dukṯo’. Omar, ‘Layt dukṯo?’ Omar, ‘Ḥayra, ḥētli bǧambiye du+xurǧo w ḥetu kéfostene bŭwár diḏi w gdoṯeno, growaxno, gmičəkno bu+xurǧo. Ḥētli bǧambe du+xurǧo, w i+ǧambe ḥrétostene, w ḥetu kefo bŭwár diḏi w gdoṯeno’. Omar, ‘Hat kuḏʕat.’
contents.versio: 043. He says, ‘Boy, there isn’t any room’. He says, ‘There isn’t any room?’ He says, ‘Buddy, put me on one side of the saddlebags and put a stone as well opposite me, and I will come along, I will ride, I will sneak myself inside the saddlebags. Put me on one side of the saddlebags, and as for the other side, put a stone opposite me, and I will come along’. He says, ‘You know best’.

contents.textus: 044. I+emo koquryole, kəmmo, ‘Osmán, k̇urem, ləzzúx!’ Omar, ‘Yade, haymén gəzzino. Koḏaʕno, yade, mə ksaymi bʕammi. Haymén qquṭli híyeste w aš+šawʕo+àbnestene. Qṭili tmanyo mənne, qṭili əšti mənne, qṭili alfo w ḥaməšmo mənne. Áydarbo, áydarbo lə+qquṭlile? Ksaymi bebaxtiye aʕle, qquṭlile. Ăla gəzzino’.
contents.versio: 044. The mother calls for him, she says, ‘Osman, my boy, don’t go!’ He says, ‘Mummy, surely I will go. I know, Mummy, what they will do to my uncle. Surely they will kill him and his seven sons as well. I killed eight of them, I killed sixty of them, I killed one thousand and five hundred of them. Why, why wouldn’t they kill him? They will act disgracefully against him, they will kill him. By God, I will go’.

contents.textus: 045. Hánostene komalax, koṯe, komičək bu+xurǧo, w komaḥti kéfoste bŭwár bi+xaṣra ḥreto du+xurǧo. Komalxi, kəzzehən. Malaxxe, azzehən se Rəzgán Aġá. Kalə́n yatiwe. Rəzgán Aġá bi+oda. ‘Sălamu ʕalayk!’ - ‘ʕAlaykŭmu ssălām!’ Qām me qumayye, qayimi me qumayye, ‘Ahla w sahla Aḥmád Aġá, ahla w sahla Aḥmád! Tux, tux, itúx, toxu, šfaʕu, šfaʕu’.
contents.versio: 045. As for this one, he takes off, he comes, he slips into the saddlebags, and they also put a stone opposite, on the other side of the the saddlebags. They take off, they go. They took off, they went to Rəzgan Agha’s. Here, they are sitting. Rəzgan Agha, in the room. ‘Greetings to you!’ ‘To you too!’ He stood up in front of them, they stood up in front of them, ‘Welcome, Ahmad Agha, welcome, Ahmad! Come, come, come, come, go ahead, go ahead’.

contents.textus: 046. Šafiʕi. Maḥatte u+xurǧo tamo, w maḥtənne tamo, w ʕabiri bu+ṣṭuwawo w maḥatte u+muklo, grəšše u+muklo qumayye. Qām hánostene … Xəlle u+muklaṯṯe, u+štoyaṯṯe. Hawi ḥəkəm dfalge dlalyo. Rəzgán Aġá omar, ‘Aḥmád Aġá!’ Omar, ‘Ha’. Omar, ‘Ma, lawo, ma lawo, manhat? Abre dmanhat, lawo, daṯat maḥatlux bi+baxčayḏi? W, lawo, maḥatlux i+k̇onayḏux b̥falga di+baxčayḏi, bi+marʕayḏi, marʕolux. Abre dmanhat, lawo?’
contents.versio: 046. They went ahead. They put down the saddlebags there, and they put them there, and entered that corridor, and they put the food, they pulled the food out before them. As for this one, he up and … They ate their food, their drinks. It was almost midnight. Rəzgan Agha says, ‘Ahmad Agha!’ He says, ‘Here’. He says, ‘What, boy, who are you? Who do you think you are, boy, that you came and set up in my field? And, boy, you pitched your tent in the middle of my field, in my pasturage, you grazed it. Who do you think you are, boy?’

contents.textus: 047. ‘Qumu’, mərle la+greʕayḏe, Rəzgán Aġá mərle la+greʕe. Omar, ‘Qumu oṣērne, moṣeru aš+šawʕo, ann+əšto abne w hiye, w masléqune ʕal i+goro, mḥaléqune maʕl i+goro, qṭalune kulle.
contents.versio: 047. ‘Get up’, he said to his servants, Rəzgan Agha said to his servants. He says, ‘Get up, bind them, bind those seven ones, his six sons and him, and bring them up on the roof, toss them from the roof, kill them all’.

contents.textus: 048. Aḥmád Aġá omar, ‘Ma lo Rəzgán Aġá haṯe bebaxtíyeyo ksaymat aʕlan, quṭlatlan?!’ Omar, ‘Ăla ḥa mənxu sāġ lə+kṭoreno! Lawo, ma áydarbo kṭoʕeno dəqṭile … dəqṭəlxu tmanyo, qṭilux əšti, w qṭilux alfo w ḥamməšmo. Lawo, áydarbo kṭorenuxyo, k̇učək̇ abre du k̇učək̇.
contents.versio: 048. Ahmad Agha says, ‘Isn’t this a disgrace that you are doing to us, Rəzgan Agha, to kill us?!’ He says, ‘By God, not a single one of you shall I leave alive! Boy, how could I forget that he killed… that you killed eight, that you killed sixty, that you killed one thousand five hundred? Boy, how could I permit it to you, whelp, son of a whelp’.

contents.textus: 049. Oṣmán Aġá komaṣəṯ aʕlayye. Midənne, moṣarre ann+əšto abne w hiye, moṣarre aš+šawʕo, məṣrənne w məfqənne. W Oṣmán Aġá nafəq mu+hno, mu+xurǧo, nafəq mu+xurǧo, šalp w šalp w šalp, qṭile harke ḥa, harke ḥa, ḥa harke. ‘K̇uro’ … hawo dsəmme brindā́r, ‘K̇u-k̇u-k̇u-k̇u-k̇uro, ha hano, ha hano, hano, hano!’ Qṭile háwostene … ǧġīl… qṭile háwostene, w noše lo+ṭrele. Mṣafile tamo, l Oṣmán Aġá mṣafile.
contents.versio: 049. Osman Agha is listening to them. They seized them, they bound the six sons and him, they bound the seven, they bound them and brought them out. And Osman Agha went out of the whatsit, out of the saddlebags, he went out of the saddlebags, slash and slash and slash, he killed one here, one here, here one. ‘Boy!’ That one, whom they injured, ‘B-b-b-boy, this one here, this one here, this one, this one!’ He killed that one too. He spoke, he killed that one too, and he left no one. He wiped them out there, Osman Agha wiped them out.

contents.textus: 050. Rəzgán Aġá mahzamle. ‘Koyo Rəzgán Aġá?’ Oṣmán Aġá komar, ‘Hayko dúkṯoyo?’ Əmmi, ‘Ăla mahzamle’. Omar, ‘Ăla lo+qoṭanno hatu … hatu …’ Əmmi, ‘Aḥna kalán taslīm’. Maʕlalle hawxa iḏoṯayye, lo? ‘Aḥna taslīm.’
contents.versio: 050. Rəzgan Agha escaped. ‘Where is Rəzgan Agha?’ Osman Agha says, ‘Where is his place?’ They say, ‘By God, he has escaped’. He says, ‘By God, I shall not kill you… you …’ They say, ‘Here we are, a surrender’. They raised their hands like so, no? ‘As for us, a surrender’.

contents.textus: 051. Qām mšayele ʕal Rəzgán Aġá, ‘Rəzgán Aġá hayko dúkṯoyo w hayko dúkṯoyo w lo+hàykoyo?’ Ḥəḷḷe l Oṣmán Aġá, omar, ‘Koṯe ḥəs marke.’ Koʕobar. ‘Ftaḥ i+odaṯe!’ Ftəḥḥe i+oda. Kalkalé čīk bayn at+tarte niše, čīk bayn at+tarte niše. W ʕabər, omar, ‘Hawxa!? Ánnaqqa, mənyo hawxa? Nfaq, Rəzgán Aġá, me tamo!’
contents.versio: 051. He up and asked about Rəzgan Agha, ‘Rəzgan Agha, where is his place, where is his place, and where isn’t it?’ Osman Agha looked around, he says, ‘A sound is coming from here’. He enters. ‘Open this room!’ They opened the room. Here he is, he has just sneaked between the two wives, he sneaked between the two wives. And he entered, he says, ‘So that’s how it is!? Now then, what’s up? Rəzgan Agha, get out of there!’

contents.textus: 052. Nafəq aṯi hǧəmle lraġloṯe d Oṣman Aġá, nšəqle raġloṯe, nšəqle iḏoṯe, nšəqle foṯe, omar, ‘Kobaʕno dlo+quṭlatli, lo+ṭorat an+nišayḏi bu+ʕulmo’.
contents.versio: 052. He got out, he flung himself at the feet of Oṣman Aġá, he kissed his feet, he kissed his hands, he kissed his face, he says, ‘I want you not to kill me, do not abandon my wives to the world!’

contents.textus: 053. Omar, ‘Lawo, bəṯər dməḷḷux u+xabrano lə+qqoṭannux w lə+kṭoreno an+nišayḏux lu+ʕulmo. Ġamo layto, elo naqqa ḥreto bebaxtiye hawxa lo+saymat ʕal noše, naqqa ḥreto lo+saymat bebaxtiye hawxa ʕal noše. Ġamo layto, lawo, ma … ánnaqqa lə+qqoṭannux’. Lə+qṭile. Omar, ‘Zoxu šrawu!’ Maslaqle, saləq. Omar, ‘Šrawu Aḥmád Aġá w ann+abne!’ Šrənne. Məṣrewayne, šrənne.
contents.versio: 053. He says, ‘Boy, after you said this thing, I shall not kill you, and I shall not abandon your wives to the world. No worries, but do not act so disgracefully to people again, never again act so disgracefully to people. No worries, boy, now then I shall not kill you!’ He did not kill him. He says, ‘Go release him!’ He picked him up, he stood up. He says, ‘Release Ahmad Agha and his sons!’ They released them. They were bound, they released them.

contents.textus: 054. Yatiwi, yatiwi. L Rəzgán Aġá qrele lan+naʕime, li+ḥurmayḏe, omar, ‘Mṭaylan muklo ḥreno, ṭruxli’. Oṣmán Aġá omar, ‘Latna ak+kafinayḏux, lo+kuxlina, lo+kuxlina, xilan uʕdo’, maḥšamme.
contents.versio: 054. They sat down, they sat down. Rəzgan Agha called his children, his wife, he says, ‘Bring us another meal, let them eat’. Osman Agha says, ‘We are not your starven, we shall not eat, we shall not eat, we have eaten now’, [i.e.] they had dinner.

contents.textus: 055. Omar, ‘Lə+ḥzélilux hat bayn u+muklo, hat lə+ḥzélilux bayn u+muklo, nəhá kafínohat.’ Omar, ‘Luxanno, lukxanno u+muklayḏux. Kal kazzano … kal kazzino. ʕAmmo, hatu qaymutu, lo?’ Omar, ‘Qaymina.’ Omar, ‘Lo, lo, hatu fušu’. Omar, ‘Ono kal kazzí’. Məḷḷe lu+ʕammo, l Aḥmad Aġá, omar, ‘Lə+qqaymutu?’ Omar, ‘Lo, lo, hăma kfayšina a+tre xabrani w qaymina áḥnastene.’ Omar, ‘Kal kazzino, wăki ono kal kazzí’.
contents.versio: 055. He says, ‘While dining, I didn’t see you, I didn’t see you while dining, now you are hungry’. He says, ‘I shouldn’t eat, I shall not eat your food. Now we are going… now I am going. Uncle, you should get up, no?’ He says, ‘Let’s get up’. He says, ‘No, no, you stay’. He says, ‘Now I am going’. He said to his uncle, to Ahmad Agha, he says, ‘Aren’t you getting up?’ He says, ‘No, no, but we shall stay for two shakes of a lamb’s tail and we too shall get up’. He says, ‘Now I am going, in that case I am going’.

contents.textus: 056. Azzeyo Oṣmán Aġá, fatəl ʕal u+tarʕo, tlele ruḥe b̥qurčḳe, tlele ruḥe, maḥatle ruḥe b̥qurčḳe. Rəzgán Aġá omar, ‘Koyo hawo? Háykoda azzé?’ Əmmi, ‘Hawo azzé lu+bayto’. Omar, ‘Qūməne, qumu, oṣērne, moṣērne’. Məḷḷe l Aḥmad Aġá w lann+abne, omar, ‘Moṣērne’, omar, ‘Moṣeru disa, moṣeru w qṭálune!’ Omar, ‘D K_ǧəh da_K qṭálune’.
contents.versio: 056. Osman Agha went, he circled around the door, he hid himself in a corner, he hid himself, he put himself in a corner. Rezgan Agha says, ‘Where is that one? Whither has he gone?’ They say, ‘That one went home’. He says, ‘Get on them, get up, bind them, bind them’. He said it about Ahmad Agha and his sons, he says, ‘Bind them’, he says, ‘Bind twice over, bind and kill them’. He says, ‘Kill them on the spot!’

contents.textus: 057. E, Oṣmán košomaʕ, kalé bəṯr i+qurčk̇e, bəṯr u+šuro košomaʕ. Moṣarre disa aš+šawʕo, məṣrənne w mədde, ánnaqqa məsqənne dəmḥalqənne me ʕal i+goro, quṭlənne.
contents.versio: 057. Yes, Osman hears, here he is, behind the corner, behind the wall, he hears. They bound the seven again, they bound them and seized, now then, they brought them up to throw them from the roof to kill them.

contents.textus: 058. Omar, ‘Ma lawo hayko gəmṭeno Oṣmán Aġá, lawo, hayko gəmṭene?’ Mə́ḷḷele l Rəzgán Aġá, omar, ‘Lawo, bebaxt … ma ayko … Aḷḷá bebaxtiye səmlux dísane. Ma Oṣmán Aġá azzeyo? Ma hayko gəzzí əmṭeno Oṣmán Aġá?’
contents.versio: 058. He says, ‘Boy, whence shall I bring back Osman Agha, boy, whence shall I bring him back?’ He said to Rəzgan Agha, he says, ‘Boy, dishonourable… where… by God, you acted dishonourably again. Is Osman Agha gone? Where shall I go to bring back Osman Agha?’

contents.textus: 059. Oṣmán Aġá omar, ‘Kalino! Kalí!’ Nafəq mi+qurčke. Nafəq, omar, ‘Hə’, mḥele u+hno ʕal qarʕe d Rəzgán Aġá, qṭile. Qṭile Rəzgán Aġá. W hánostene, qām Aḥmád Aġá čīk bu+kawnayḏe xud meqəm. W qayimi blalyo, səmme ruḥayye kār, w rawixi ʕal aḥ+ḥayewənaṯṯe, w aṯən lu+bayto.
contents.versio: 059. Osman Agha says, ‘Here I am! Here I am!’ He went out from the corner. He went out, he swipes, he struck the whatsit upon the head of Rəzgan Agha, he killed him. He killed Rəzgan Agha. And as for this one, Ahmad Agha, he slipped back into his former glory. And they got up in the night, prepared themselves, mounted their beasts, and went home.

contents.textus: 060. Aṯən lu+bayto. Oṣmán Aġá omar, ‘Yade!’ Omar, ‘Ha’ Omar, ‘Aḷḷá, mṣafili. Hawxa səmme bʕammi, moṣarre aš+šawʕo w lawən šilo, lo+tlalle iḏo, yade, w Aḷḷá qṭili Rəzgán Aġástene w qṭili kulle, mṣafili’.
contents.versio: 060. They went home. Osman Agha says, ‘Mummy’. She says, ‘Here’. He says, ‘By God, I wiped them out. They had done such and such to my uncle, they had bound the seven, and they became afraid, they didn’t raise a fist, Mummy, and, by God, I killed Rəzgan Aghá too and killed them all, I wiped them out’.

contents.textus: 061. Əmmo, ‘Lawo, ono mə mə́ḷḷilux, hat mə səmlux? Ono mə́ḷḷilux, “Taw, ləzzúx!” Azzúx, hawat dəžmə́n, ánnaqqa hawat dəžmə́n d Rəzgán Aġá, dač+čalkoye. Ač+čalkoye, noše lə+gmaxlaṣ mənne. Səmlux ruḥux …’
contents.versio: 061. She says, ‘Boy, what did I tell you, what have you done? I told you, ‘Stay, don’t go!’ You went, you became an enemy, now then you have become an enemy of Rezgan Agha, of the Yezidis. The Yezidis, nobody will ever escape from them. You made yourself…’

contents.textus: 062. Omar, ‘Yade, haqqa w haqqa ḥrénoste howən, lə+qqudri aʕli. Bu+ḥaylo d Aloho’, omar, ‘u+ḥaylo d Aloho áʕmiyo, lə+qqudri aʕli’.
contents.versio: 062. He says, ‘Mummy, had they been that much and even twice that much, they wouldn’t have overpowered me. By the power of God’, he says, ‘the power of God is with me, they wouldn’t have overpowered me’.

contents.textus: 063. Fāš hawxa Oṣmán Aġá. Kalé taḥt i+k̇onayḏe məždo, možadle ruḥe, kalé taḥt i+k̇onayḏe yatiwo. Aḥmád Aġástene kaleyo u+bəllurayḏe, dan+naʕimayḏe bər-bər du+bəllūr bayn aʕ+ʕwone w bayn aʕ+ʕeze, bayn i+baxča d Rəzgán Aġá.
contents.versio: 063. Osman Agha remained like so. Here he is, stretched out under his tent, he stretched himself out, here he is, sitting under his tent. As for Ahmad Agha, here’s his flute, his children’s flute piping, among the sheep and goats, within the field of Rezgan Agha.

contents.textus: 064. Hánostene … Koḥayri u+ahl d Rəzgán Aġá, koḥayri, koḥayri, koṯən me támoda, láḏiʕi dəqṭəlle Rəzgán Aġá. Hənnək, b̥ḥəšbonayye, Rəzgán Aġá lə+qṭəlle, sāġyo. Koṯən me támoda… ‘K̇uro hano mən?’ U+ahl d Rəzgán Aġá čalkóyene, mšayalle harke w harke w harke. Əmmi, ‘Qṭəlle ġắlabe mənne, w Rəzgán Aġá kalé bu+bàytoyo. W maḥatte bi+k̇onayḏe.
contents.versio: 064. As for this one… The family of Rəzgan Agha looks, they look, they look, they come from over there, they didn’t know that they had killed Rəzgan Agha. They, in their minds, they had not killed Rəzgan Agha, he is alive. They come from over there, ‘Boy, what is this?’ The family of Rəzgan Agha are Yezidis, they asked around. They say, ‘They have killed many of them, and here’s Rəzgan Agha, at home. And they have set up in his tent’.

contents.textus: 065. Koṯe nof ḥreno me támoda, qădā́r ḥəkəm dalfo dalfo w maṯe šaqṣat, koṯe me támoda. Əmmi, ‘Bavo, lḥa qṭile tmanyo w qṭile əšti, w qṭile alfo w ḥamməšmo. Hawxa šamiʕina, w i+măsale háwxayo. Qay maḥatte bi+k̇one d Rəzgán Aġá? Kal kazzán se Rəzgán Aġá, lə+koṭorínanneyo’.
contents.versio: 065. Another group comes from over there, as many as almost a thousand, a thousand and two hundred people, it comes from over there. They say, ‘Daddy-o, someone has killed eight, and killed sixty, and killed one thousand and five hundred. We have heard so, and such is the problem. Why did they set up in the tent of Rəzgan Agha? Let’s get going to Rəzgan Agha’s, we shall not leave it to them’.

contents.textus: 066. Hánəkstene ann+alfo šaqṣaṭ, hánəkstene koṯən se Rəzgán Aġá. Kəmšayli, Rəzgán Aġá layt. At+tarte+nišaṯṯe kalə́n tamo xud tarte+yatumoṯk̇at. ‘K̇ače hayko dúkṯoyo?’ Əmmi, ‘Ho, Ăḷa, qṭəlle Rəzgán Aġá w qṭəlle an+naʕimayḏe. Lo+fāš. Fayišina at+tarte+pirak̇at. Ăḷa lḥa hawxa káryowa məḷḷe, ‘At+tarte+pirak̇at lə+qqoṭannanne, xətyar, tarte+pirák̇atne, lə+qqoṭanno ap+pirak̇at.’ An+naʕimáyḏeste qṭilənne, w Rəzgán Aġáste qṭəlle, haymén azzehən’.
contents.versio: 066. As for those thousand people, they also come to Rəzgan Agha’s. They inquire, there is no Rəzgan Agha. Two of his wives, here they are like two little orphan girls. ‘Girls, where is his place?’ They say, ‘Hey, by God, they have killed Rəzgan Agha and have killed his children. He did not survive. We two little women have survived. By God, someone yea short said, ‘I shall not kill the two little women, oldsters, they are two little women, I shall not kill the little women’. As for his children, he killed them, and he killed Rəzgan Agha as well, surely they have gone away’.

contents.textus: 067. ‘Hawxaaa!?’ Əmmi, ‘E!’ ‘Kmo šáqṣaṭwayne?’ Omar, ‘Ḥawa, kətwa … šawʕo+zlamátwayne, aš+šawʕanək a+zlamat lo+tolənwa iḏo. Lano, lḥa naʕimk̇o, kəpwayle haqqaske, lawo qṭile kulle.’ ‘Hawxa?’ Əmmi, ‘E! Iyyu kal kazzanne!’ Azzéhənle.
contents.versio: 067. ‘So that’s how it is!?’ They say, ‘Yes!’ ‘How many people were they?’ They say, ‘It was one, there was… they were seven men, those seven men didn’t lift a finger. This one, someone tiny, he was yea tall, that one killed all of them’. ‘So that’s how it is!?’ They say, ‘Yes! Come on, let’s get going to them!’ They went to him.

contents.textus: 068. Aḥmád Aġá koḥōr, ‘Man hatu?’ Əmmi, ‘Aḥmad Aġá, kaṯina gabux’. ‘Mən xēryo aṯutu doṯutu gabi?’ Əmmi, ‘Aṯina … gdoṯina … gabux. Šamiʕina dʔaṯat me ḥeḏər Gziro, aṯat lu+zozan larke, aṯat mṭelux u+săwalayḏux, aṯat larke maḥatlux bi+k̇one d Rəzgán Aġá, w haymén aṯina áḥnastene, ḥozina kəmmi zlām gawro w hawxa hno hat, w mard hat, w hawxa hat, w hawxa hat, gawro hat, hawxa hat. Aṯina gabux.
contents.versio: 068. Ahmad Agha looks, ‘Who are you?’ They say, ‘Ahmad Agha, we have come by you’. ‘For what good have you come by me?’ They say, ‘We came, we are coming… by you. We heard that you had come from around Gziro, you came here, to the pasture, you came, you brought your livestock, you came here, you set up in the tent of Rəzgan Agha, and, surely we also came, we see they say you are a brave man and so whatsit, and you are generous, and you are like so, and you are like so, you are brave, you are like so. We came to you’.

contents.textus: 069. Aṯən. ‘Tawu!’ Yatiwi, yatiwi. U+abraṯṯe u+naʕimo kalé bu+baytoyo, w a+ḥrene azzə́n qm u+săwalaṯṯe, qm u+săwā̀l. K̇óčarne! Oṣmán Aġaste kalé bi+k̇onayḏe məždo, yatiwo. Kalé u+səsyayḏe b̥feme du+tarʕo di+k̇onayḏe məṣro, w kalá i+emostène košayfo ḥaṣe d Oṣmán Aġá, w raġloṯe košayfalle, koḥayko qarʕe.
contents.versio: 069. They came. ‘Sit down!’ They sat down, they sat down. Their little son, here he is in the house, and the others went after their livestock, after the livestock. They are nomads! As for Osman Agha, here he is, stretched out in his tent, sitting. Here is his horse, tied up at the door frame of his tent, and here too is his mother, stroking Osman Agha’s back, and his feet, she is stroking them, she is scratching his head.

contents.textus: 070. Kəmmo, ‘K̇urem, dmaxlux saʕaye!’ Komar, ‘Yade, baṭilat, bas šayfat qarʕi w ḥaṣi w raġli’. Əmmo, ‘Bele, k̇urem, baṭilat, ġamo layto’. Hánostene … Hedik̇a koyətwi, w komaydi li+k̇ačk̇e d Aḥmád Aġá. Lḥa mənne midole w marŭxole ʕal u+səsyo w yaḷḷa! Ntišole, lḥa mənne.
contents.versio: 070. She says, ‘My boy, have yourself a nap for an hour!’ He says, ‘Mummy, you have gotten tired, enough stroking my head, my back, and my feet’. She says, ‘Yes, my boy, you have gotten tired, no worries’. As for this one … While they are sitting, they take the daughter of Ahmad Agha. One of them took her and mounted her on the horse, and off they go! He kidnapped her, one of them.

contents.textus: 071. U+aḥunayḏa Aḥmád Aġá layt … lə+ktole iḏo, w i+Səṫṫiye <d>i+barṯo kodəryo lu+hawā̀r. E, u+aḥuno omar, ‘Ma alfo+šaqṣaṭ, ma may kibi aʕlayye?! Ónoste laybi aʕlayye.’ Qām hule xabro l Oṣmán Aġá, məḷḷe, ‘Oṣmán!’ Omar, ‘Ha’. Omar, ‘Haymén mballe, mballe ḥoṯi’. Aḥmád Aġá omar, ‘Aḷḷa məblalle. Me qm i+tḥelayḏi blalle.
contents.versio: 071. Her father Ahmad Agha is not … he doesn’t lift a finger, and Səṫṫiye, his daughter, sounds the alarm. Yes, her father says, ‘A thousand people, how can I overcome them?! As for me, I cannot overcome them’. He up and said to Osman Agha, he said, ‘Osman!’ He says, ‘Here’. He says, ‘Surely, they have taken my sister’. Ahmad Agha says, ‘By God, they have taken her. They have taken her from right by my side’.

contents.textus: 072. ‘Bas háykoda azzə́n, lo haykoda azzə́n?’ Əmmi, ‘Aḷḷa, azzé hárkeda’. Ḥəḷḷe l Oṣmán Aġá, kalá! Qaṭəʕ lqamuṯayye, xud mắsala dəzzé marke, mičək b̥qamuṯayye. Ḥəḷḷe, kalá, maruxole! Bəṯra … hắwar hắwar diḏa … bəṯra. ‘Oṣmán, k̇ak̇o! Abre dʕammo! K̇ak̇o, Oṣmán! Hayko gdoṯat w hayko gdoṯat maxəlṣatli? W mbeleli bi+zoriye lano!’
contents.versio: 072. ‘But which way have they gone, which way haven’t they gone?’ They say, ‘By God, he went that way’. Osman Agha looked, here she is! He cut ahead of them, so for example he goes from here, he slips ahead of them. He looked, here she is, he made her ride! On her trail… her scream, her scream… on her trail. ‘Osman, brother! My cousin! Brother, Osman! Whence will you come and whence will you come to save me? This one took me by force’.

contents.textus: 073. Koḥōr kalé Oṣmán Aġá b̥qamuṯe. ‘Ha kalé Oṣmán Aġá, hánoyo!’ Omar, ‘Tlay, ḥaláq, nḥat nḥat nḥat.’ Midole, mḥalqole, w mahzamle, mahzamle.
contents.versio: 073. He looks, here’s Osman Agha in front of him. ‘Here, here’s Osman Agha, he is this one!’ He says, ‘Take off, cast away, get down, get down, get down’. He seized her, tossed her away, and fled, he fled.

contents.textus: 074. L Oṣmán Aġá … omar, ‘Taw harke, Səṫṫiye’. Mḥalaqle bəṯre, čīk larġul, čīk larġul, maxlaṣle mal+lăpaṭayḏe, čīk larġul. Oṣmán Aġá karəx w lo karəx, harke w harke w harke … Lo ḥzele, lo ḥzele. Tlele ruḥe.
contents.versio: 074. Osman Agha … he says, ‘Sit down, Sittiye’. He cast off after him, he slipped inside, he slipped inside, he escaped from his clutches, he slipped inside. Osman Agha went around and around, here and there and everywhere. He did not see him, he did not see him. He had hidden himself.

contents.textus: 075. Daʕər Oṣmán Aġá, daʕər, laqi lanək, lann+alfanək dkətwayne, daʕər aʕlayye. Daʕər aʕlayye, qṭile mo mənne, ač+čaʕmo ḥrene mahzamme, kul ḥa bdúkṯoda azzeyo, mahzamme.
contents.versio: 075. Osman Agha returned, he returned, he met those, those thousand that were there, he returned to them. He returned to them, he killed a hundred of them, the other nine hundred fled, each one went towards some place, they fled.

contents.textus: 076. Aṯi Oṣmán Aġá, ṯi lu+bayto, mṭele Səṫṫiye w aṯi. Məḷḷele lu+ʕammo, omar, ‘ʕAmmo’. Omar, ‘Ha!’ Omar, ‘ʕAmmo, qum, basyo. Qəm, zano, ʕammo, ldukṯayna! Basyo, marʕelan i+marʕàṯṯestene, w qṭilílanstene, w basyo! W haymén kə́pwayli əmṭeno at+tarte+nišàyḏestene, omaṇṇo náməsyo, lə+ksōmno, i+benamusiyaṯe lə+ksōmna. W yabo, qəm marke, gəzzán ldukṯayna’.
contents.versio: 076. Osman Agha came back, he came home, he brought Sittiye and came back. He said to his uncle, he says, ‘Uncle’. He says, ‘Here!’ He says, ‘Uncle, get up, that’s enough. Get up, let’s go, uncle, back to our place! That’s enough, we have grazed even their pastures, and have also killed them, and that’s enough. And I surely could have brought his two wives, I say it’s right, I won’t do it, this dishonour, I won’t do it. And, Daddy, get up from here, let’s go back to our place’.

contents.textus: 077. Omar, ‘K̇urem, hat kuḏʕat’, omar, ‘Lawo, hat kuḏʕat’. Maṭʕanne ak̇+k̇onaṯṯe, Alyas, maṭʕanne ak̇+k̇onaṯṯe w malaxxe, aṯən mu+zozan, aṯən lu+bayto. Əmmi, ‘Aḷḷá Aḥmad Aġá kal kaṯi lu+bayto, aṯi daʕər li+qriṯo, Aḥmad Aġá daʕər li+qriṯo’. Yatiwi, yatiwi bu+bayto.
contents.versio: 077. He says, ‘My son, you know best’, he says, ‘Boy, you know best’. They loaded up their tents, Ilyas, they loaded up their tents and went away, they came back from the pasturage, they came home. They say, ‘By God, Ahmad Agha has just come back home, he came back to the village, Ahmad Agha returned to the village’. They settled down, they settled down at home.

contents.textus: 078. Oṣmán Aġástene, u+baytayḏe xud t̬owe tamho, mqabəl du+bayto du+ʕàmmoyo. Ḥa yawmo aš+šawʕo+abnayḏe koqaymile l Oṣmán Aġá, koqaymile l Oṣmán Aġá ʕal mắsale di+ḥoṯaṯṯe.
contents.versio: 078. As for Osman Agha, his house, as if it were over there, opposite the house of his uncle. One day his seven sons rise up against Osman Agha, they rise up against Osman Agha on account of their sister.

contents.textus: 079. Omar, ‘Lawo, azzúx mṭelux ḥoṯi … lu+naʕimo … mṭelux ḥoṯi, lawo, hat w hiya tăne. ‘K̇uro’, omar, ‘Lawo, ḥoṯux, mṭoli šqiloli mu+zlām, w u+zlām mahzamle. Qoṭalwayno, háwostene mahzamle. Lawo, ma ono … , ḥoṯux ḥóṯuxyo, təmā́m, ḥóṯuxyo, hăma i+barṯo dʕámmiyòstene. Maxəlṣoli, mṭoli.
contents.versio: 079. He says, ‘Boy, you went to bring my sister…’, the little one, ‘You brought my sister, boy, only you and her’. ‘Boy’, he says, ‘Boy, your sister, I brought her, I seized her from a man, and the man escaped. I would have killed him, but that one escaped. My boy, did I …? your sister is your sister, fine, she is your sister, but she is also my cousin. I saved her, I brought her back’.

contents.textus: 080. Hǧə́malle, hǧə́malle. Aḥmád Aġá baxi, nafəl k̇urén b Aḥmád Aġá. Omar, ‘D̥qaymutu qarši d ʔOṣmán Aġá, qoṭaṇṇo ruḥi’. Mədle lu+šalfo, omar, ‘Hăma, dməǧġolutu mine, kčōrno gawe druḥi, qoṭaṇṇo ruḥi’. Kalən, kalən, fayiši hawxa, fayiši hawxa w komarʕən u+săwalaṯṯe. W Oṣmán Aġástene kalé bi+k̇onayḏe yatíwoyo.
contents.versio: 080. They attacked him, they attacked him. Ahmad Agha cried, Ahmad Agha started yelping. He says, ‘If you rise up against Osman Agha, I shall kill myself’. He seized a dagger, he says, ‘Well, if you speak against him, I shall rip up my own belly, I shall kill myself’. They ceased, they ceased, they stayed like so, they stayed like so, and they graze their livestock. And as for Osman Agha, here he is in his tent, he is sitting.

contents.textus: 081. Ḥa yawmo Aḥmád Aġá koloqe li+emayḏe, li+emo d Oṣmán Aġá. Aḥmád Aġá koloqela, komar, ‘Lay gəzzáx, Ḥazno?’ Əšma Ḥáznowa. ‘Lay gəzzax, Ḥazno?’ Əmmo, ‘Haymén gəzzino hárkeda, k̇ak̇o. Qay, mək kəbʕat?’ Omar, ‘dsaymat bdiḏi, gmohaṇṇax, gmohaṇṇax’.
contents.versio: 081. One day Ahmad Agha meets his mother, the mother of Osman Agha. Ahmad Agha meets her, he says, ‘Where are you going, Hazno?’ Her name was Hazno. ‘Where are you going, Hazno?’ She says, ‘For sure, I am going over here, brother. Why, what do you want?’ He says, ‘If you do my bidding, I shall marry you, I shall marry you’.

contents.textus: 082. Əmmo, ‘Hawxa?’ Omar, ‘E’. Əmmo, ‘Aḥmado, Aḥmado, Aḥmado! Qṭilux aḥuno druḥux. Kuḏʕono dəqṭilux aḥuno druḥux aʕli. Hat babi w aḥuni hat. Áydarbo ksaymallux, lukwe dsaymallux.
contents.versio: 082. She says, ‘So that’s how it is?’ He says, ‘Yes’. She says, ‘Ahmad, Ahmad, Ahmad! You killed your own brother. I know that you killed your own brother on account of me. You are a father and a brother to me. How could I marry you, it is not for me to marry you’.

contents.textus: 083. ‘Hawxa?’ Omar, ‘E’. Omar, ‘Haymén dlo+saymatli gqoṭanno u+abrayḏax’. Əmmo, ‘Qṭale! Ăḷah ləksaymallux, w Ăḷah gabux lo+damixono!’ ‘Hawxa?’ omar. ‘E’. ‘Təmā́m’.
contents.versio: 083. ‘So that’s how it is?’ She says, ‘Yes’. He says, ‘Surely, if you do not marry me, I shall kill your son’. She says, ‘Kill him! By God, I shall not marry you, by God, I shall not sleep with you!’ ‘So that’s how it is?’ he says. ‘Yes’. ‘Fine’.

contents.textus: 084. Aṯi lu+bayto, aṯi lu+bayto, məḷḷalle laš+šawʕo abnayḏe, ‘Maḥanno ere+d Oṣmán Aġá b̥ṭize+dkulxu, b̥ṭize+daš+šawʕotayxu, maḥanno ere dṭorūṭəleyo’.
contents.versio: 084. He came back home, he came back home, he said to his seven sons, ‘I shall put the penis of Osman Agha in all of your assholes, in you seven’s assholes, I shall put his penis if you permit him this’.

contents.textus: 085. Ánnaqqa ḥzawu mətfakeru, ǧamaʕa, məs səmle l Oṣmán, w l Aḥmád Aġá mək kosōm bu+rabbàn d Oṣmán. Qām səmle aš+šawʕo+abnayḏe kār dəzzənle l Oṣmán dquṭlile.
contents.versio: 085. Now see, think, everybody, what Osman has done, and what Ahmad Agha is doing to poor Osman. He up and prepared his seven sons to go to Osman to kill him.

contents.textus: 086. Hedik̇a Oṣmán komaḷḷa li+emo, komar, ‘Yade’. Komar, ‘Ha’. Komar, ‘Hawli u+silaḥayḏi’, komar, ‘Kal kaṯili. Haymén qquṭlili doṯe mənne.
contents.versio: 086. Now then, Osman says to his mother, he says, ‘Mummy!’ She says,‘Here!’ He says, ‘Give me my weapons’, he says, ‘He is coming for me right now. Surely they will kill me if they have the chance’.

contents.textus: 087. Čiko i+emaṯṯe, čiko b̥qamuṯayye, čiko b̥qamuṯayye, əmmo, ‘Lawo, dʕaru!’ Əmmo, ‘Lawo, ḥa abro kətli. Rkadu, ṭrawu mine, lo+quṭlūtle. Aš+šawʕotayxu koṯūtle bu+silaḥ hawxa, ṭrawu mu+abrayḏi, ḥayra, qqaymina marke, gəzzano.
contents.versio: 087. His mother sneaked, she sneaked in front of them, she sneaked in front of them, she says, ‘Boys, come back!’ She says, ‘Boys, I have only one son. Calm down, spare him, do not kill him. The seven of you have come to him armed like so, spare my son, buddies, we will set out from here, we will go’.

contents.textus: 088. ‘Gəzzoxu marke?’ Omar, ‘E’. U+naʕimo omar, ‘D … dəzzoxu, gduʕrina, dləzzoxu lukwe dlo+quṭlinale’.
contents.versio: 088. ‘You will go away from here?’ He says, ‘Yes’. The little one says, ‘If … if you go, we will retreat, if you don’t go, it is not appropriate not to kill him’.

contents.textus: 089. Omar, ‘Gəzzano!’ I+emo, ‘Gəzzano!’ I+emo d Oṣmán əmmo, ‘Gəzzano!’ Qām daʕiri. ‘Qay daʕirutu?’ Omar, ‘Yabo, gəzzé Oṣmán Aġá, hiye w i+emo, qqaymi marke gəzzehən’. ‘Gəzzehən? E, ṭrəzzə́n’.
contents.versio: 089. He says, ‘Let’s go!’ His mother, ‘Let’s go!’ The mother of Osman says, ‘Let’s go!’ They up and returned. ‘Why have you returned?’ He says, ‘Dad, Osman Agha is going, he and his mother. They are up and going from here’. ‘They are going? Yes, let them go’.

contents.textus: 090. Azzehən. Oṣmán Aġá qām me qumayye, qām me qumayye. (Ḥayra, yarə́xtoyo, ma heš əzzí bəṯra?) Qām me qumayye. Oṣmán Aġá azzé, azzé, Oṣmán Aġá azzeyo, xud măsala dəmmina marke, dəzzeyo l Məḏyaḏ, mayele ruḥe me tamo.
contents.versio: 090. They went. Osman Agha set out from their presence, he set out from their presence. (Buddy, it’s long, shall I still go ahead?) He set out from their presence. Osman Agha went, he went, Osman Agha went, so for example we might say, as if he were to go to Midyat from here, he turned himself away from there.

contents.textus: 091. Hánostene Aḥmád Aġá omar, ‘Ǧamaʕa!’ Omar, ‘Ha!’ Omar, ‘Lawo, Ăḷa u+săwalayḏi kafínoyo. W haymén dukṯo lo+fāšli dmarʕeno u+săwalayḏi, w kobaʕli zād, w kobaʕno dšoqalni zād lu+săwalayḏi, w čeriye noqúṣṭoyo, i+čeriyayḏi noquṣṭoyo, u+săwalayḏi manqaṣle’.
contents.versio: 091. This Ahmad Agha says, ‘Hey, group!’ It says, ‘Here!’ He says, ‘Boys, by God, my livestock is hungry. And surely, there is no place left for me to graze my livestock, and I need grain, I need to get grain for my livestock, and the pasture is insufficient, my pasture is insufficient, my livestock has become lean’.

contents.textus: 092. ‘Lay gəzzoxu?’ Əmmi, ‘Gəzzano lə Gziro’. <Aḥmád Aġá> … azzehən lə Gziro lu+zād, dəmṭənne zād šan u+săwalaṯṯe. Hánostene, ḥa mač+čalkoye, kəmḥalaq bəṯre, bəṯre Aḥmád Aġá. ‘Háykoda azzé lo+háykoda azzé?’ Əmmi, ‘Haymén azzé lu+bayto, lə Gziro.’
contents.versio: 092. ‘Where are you going?’ They say, ‘We are going to Gziro’. Ahmad Agha … they went to Gziro for grain, to bring grain for their livestock. This one, one of the Yezidis, runs after him, after Ahmad Agha. ‘Did he go this way or that way?’ They say, ‘Surely he went home, to Gziro.’

contents.textus: 093. Ḥa čalkoyo, u+abro du+ʕammo d Rəzgán Aġá, u+abro du+ʕammayḏe, mḥalaqle bu+šopayḏe, aṯi. ‘Koyo Aḥmád Aġá?’ Əmmi, ‘Latyo bu+bayto, azzé lə Gziro lu+zād’. An+naʕimayḏe…
contents.versio: 093. One Yezidi, the nephew of Rəzgan Agha, the son of his paternal uncle, followed his trail, he came along. ‘Where is Ahmad Agha?’ They say, ‘He isn’t at home, he went to Gziro for grain’. The children…

contents.textus: 094. ‘Hano xud manyo u+xətyarano? Əmmi, ‘U+babáṯṯeyo, Aḥmád Aġayo, u+babáṯteyo, haṯe i+barṯoyo’. Məḷḷela li+barṯo, omar, ‘Qum!’ Midole, w moṣaḷḷe Aḥmád Aġá tamo, moṣaḷḷe, lu+abro du+ʕammo d Rəzgán Aġá, moṣaḷḷe Aḥmád Aġá, w mədle li+barṯo Səṫṫiye, w yaḷḷa ntišole, ntišole, blole, blole. Hăwár hăwár d Aḥmád Aġá, w hăwár di+k̇ačk̇e, noše layt, hăwár, layt noše, layt. Blole, blole.
contents.versio: 094. ‘This one, like, who is this old man?’ They say, ‘He is their father, he is Ahmad Agha, he is their father, this one is his daughter’. He said to the daughter, he says, ‘Get up!’ He seized her, and he tied Ahmad Agha up there, he tied him up, Rəzgan Agha’s nephew, he tied Ahmad Agha up and seized his daughter Səṫṫiye, and, come on, he snatched her, he snatched her, he took her away, he took her away. Ahmad Agha’s alarm, alarm, and the girl’s alarm. There isn’t anyone, alarm, nobody is there, nobody. He took her away, he took her away.

contents.textus: 095. Hawi qəm ʕaṣriye, aṯən aš+šawʕo+aḥunonayḏa, aṯən me Gziro, mṭalle u+zadaṯṯe, w aṯən lu+bayto, koḥayri, ‘Qay hawxa?’ U+babo marəmle ʕayne mu+baxyo. ‘Kalé məṣro, w koyo ḥoṯayna?’
contents.versio: 095. It became close to evening, her seven brothers came, they came from Gziro, they brought their grain and came home, they look, ‘Why is this so?’ Her father had inflamed his eyes from crying. ‘Here he is tied up, and where is our sister?’

contents.textus: 096. Omar, ‘Ăḷa ḥoṯayxu lḥa blole w azzé’. ‘Laḏiʕatle?’ Omar, ‘May koḏaʕne, lawo, manyo?’ ‘Véǧare məs saymina?
contents.versio: 096. He says, ‘By God, someone took your sister and went away’. ‘Don’t you know him?’ He says, ‘How would I know, boys, who he is?’ ‘What should we do this time?’

contents.textus: 097. U+naʕimo omar, ‘Lawo, tawu, tawu ḥozina.’ Yatiwi aš+šawʕo ʕam ḥḏoḏe, ḥa mənne omar, ‘Ḥayra dsaymutu bdiḏi, dšəmʕutu xabri, bəṯər məd azzayo ṭrawu mina.’
contents.versio: 097. The little one says, ‘Boys, sit down, sit down, let’s see’. The seven sat down together, one of them says, ‘Buddy, if you were to do it my way, if you were to follow my advice, since she is gone, leave her be’.

contents.textus: 098. U+ḥreno komar, ‘Ṭrawu mina.’ U+naʕimo omar, ‘Ho ho ho.’ Omar, ‘Baḥ+ḥaye d Alohayḏux koyomeno, hul dləzzino əmṭeno i+ḥoṯayo diḏi, lukwe, u+baytano aʕli ḥarā́m.
contents.versio: 098. The other one says, ‘Leave her be’. The little one says, ‘Ooh, Ooh, Ooh!’. He says, ‘I swear upon the life of your God, lest I go bring that sister of mine back, it’s not possible, this house is off limits to me’.

contents.textus: 099. ‘Šrawu šráwule!’ Šralle, azzeyo rawixo ʕal u+səsyayḏe, azzé mṭele Oṣmán Aġá, mṭele l Oṣmán Aġá. Mḥalaqqe ʕal u+šopayḏa. ‘Ha harke, ha harke, ha harke’. Azzé tre+yawme bi+ḥolo, bi+ḥolo, azzé tloṯo+yawme bi+ḥolo, marke mšayele, harke, harke, harke.
contents.versio: 099. ‘Release, release him!’ They released him, he went riding upon his horse, he went to fetch Osman Agha, he fetched Osman Agha. They followed her trail. ‘Here it is, here it is, here it is’. Two days passed in the meantime, in the meantime, three days passed in the meantime, he would ask here and there.

contents.textus: 100. Əmmi, ‘Haymén kalá bəflā́n+baytò’. Azzə́n lu+baytawo, azzə́n lu+baytayo. Koḥayri kalá Səṫṫiye, kalá Səṫṫiye. Grəšla, koguršo b̥ṣaʕra, w xed i+ǧənne qarʕa, w kobuxyo. Hăwár, hăwár diḏa, ‘Ma hayko gəmṭono Oṣmán Aġá u+abro dʕammi, hayko gəmṭalle?
contents.versio: 100. They say, ‘She is surely here, in such and such a house’. They went to that house, they went to that house. They look, here’s Səṫṫiye, here’s Səṫṫiye. She has pulled, she is pulling on her hair, and her head is like a djinni, and she is crying. Her outcry, her outcry, ‘Whence shall I summon Osman Agha, my cousin? Whence shall I summon him?’

contents.textus: 101. Omar, ‘Kalkaṯino, kalkaṯino!’ ʕAbər Oṣmán Aġá, hǧəmle larġul, hǧəmle, koḥṓr, k̇ačé! ‘Kone?’ Əmmo, ‘Kalə́n bi+odayo’. ‘Mqadámmalax, lo?’ Əmmo, ‘Lo, ema ṭreli dəmqadmili! B̥femi lo u+muklaṯṯe šteli, lo am+mayaṯṯe, w lo+ṭreli dəmqadmili.
contents.versio: 101. He says, ‘I am coming, I am coming’. Osman Agha entered, he rushed inside, he rushed, he looks, the girl! ‘Where are they?’ She says, ‘Here they are, in that room’. ‘Did they attack you, no?’ She says, ‘No, when would I let them attack me? In my mouth, neither <did I eat> their food, nor did I drink their water, and I did not let them attack me’.

contents.textus: 102. ‘Kone?’ Əmmi, ‘Kalə́n bi+odayo!’ Azzalle, azzalle, qšəʕle qarʕe dkulle tamo, qṭile kulle, qṭile kulle w mədle li+Səṫṫiye w mṭole, mṭole, aṯi. Aḥmád Aġá komar, ‘Hə, Oṣmank̇o! Mə səmlux, qṭíluxli gawre, mə sə́mluxli’. Komarle ánnaqqa lu+braziyayḏe, Aḥmád Aġá, ‘Mə sə́mluxli? Qṭilux gawre!’ ‘K̇urro,’ omar, ‘ʕAmmo, mṭeli, qṭilílistene w mṭeli i+Səṫṫiye, mṭoli’. ‘Koyo i+Səṫṫiye?’
contents.versio: 102. ‘Where are they?’ They say, ‘There they are, in that room!’ He went to them, he went to them, he cut off the heads of everyone there, he killed everyone, he killed everyone and took Səṫṫiye and brought her back, he brought her back, he came back. Ahmad Agha says, ‘Hey, Osman! What have you done? You have killed men for me! What have you done for me?’. Now then, Ahmad Agha says to his nephew, ‘What have you done for me? You have killed men!’ ‘Boy,’ he says, ‘Uncle, I have brought her back, I have killed them for my own sake and I have also brought back Səṫṫiye, I have brought her back’. ‘Where is Səṫṫiye?’

contents.textus: 103. Omar, ‘Kaláyo’. Koḥōr, ḥəngi hawi sáwwəssi. Moṣarre, hawi sáwwəssi. Aḥmád Aġá loḏaʕwa, haw oḏaʕwa li+barṯo druḥe, loḏaʕwa li+Səṫṫiye. Qām tamo hedik̇a lu+aḥunayḏa u+naʕimo hule Səṫṫiye l Oṣmán Aġá. W tə sāġ.
contents.versio: 103. He says. ‘Here she is’. He looks... since he became crazy. They tied him up, he became crazy. Ahmad Agha did not recognize, he no longer recognized his own daughter, he did not recognize Səṫṫiye. So, then, her brother, the little one, he up and gave Səṫṫiye to Osman Agha. The end.

contents.textus: 104. Hánostene, mḥawlole l Oṣmán Aġá, qrele laz+zuṭoye. W mṭele u+săwāl lu+aḥunayḏa u+naʕimo, mṭele u+săwāl w nḥərre.
contents.versio: 104. This one, Osman Agha, married her, he summoned minstrels. And her brother, the little one, brought livestock, he brought livestock and they slaughtered it.

contents.textus: 105. L Oṣmán Aġá mšaʕle bəṯre i+ʕašərto, w aṯən u+ʕulmo (əzzí bəṯra?), qrele li+ʕašərto w aṯən w nḥərre u+săwāl d Aḥmád Aġá. Lu+aḥunayḏa mə́ḷḷela Səṫṫiye, omar, ‘Səṫṫiye, u+săwāl u+baṣro du+săwāl di+daʕwayḏax kule aʕli’. Nḥərre mo+riše dsăwā́l, huwe nḥərre u+săwālaṯte huwe lu+ʕulmo, qrele lu+ʕašərto, lu+ʕulmo.
contents.versio: 105. Osman Agha sent for his tribe, and people came (shall I go ahead?), he summoned his tribe, they came and they slaughtered Ahmad Agha’s livestock. Her brother said to Səṫṫiye, he says, ‘Səṫṫiye, the livestock, the meat of the livestock for your marriage is entirely on me’. They slaughtered one hundred head of livestock, they gave, they slaughtered their livestock, they gave it to the people. He had summoned the tribe, the people.

contents.textus: 106. Oṣmán Aġá hawxa, u+Oṣmán Aġá ṭlibole, mḥawlole. Omar, ‘Yade!’ Omar, ‘Ha’. Omar, ‘Yade, ánnaqqa mə sōmno? Haymén harke tə+šuġlo layto, tə+ʕamlo layto, yade. D̥saymat bdiḏi, hăma áḥnastene qqaymina gəzzalan, ldukṯo. Lo+săwā̀l kətli, w lo+mede kətli. W kalán! I+nxiraytàyḏistene, i+ḥurmàyḏiste mṭoli. D̥saymat b̥diḏi, yade, qqaymina marke’. Əmmo, ‘Qəm, k̇urem, qəm, basyo.’
contents.versio: 106. Osman Agha, like so, Osman Agha betrothed her, he married her. He says, ‘Mummy!’ She says, ‘Here’. He says, ‘Mummy, what shall I do now? Surely, there is no work here, there is no job, mummy. If you do it my way, we shall up and go off on our own to somewhere. I have no livestock, and I have nothing. And here we are! My fiancée, my wife, I brought her back. If you do it my way, we shall set out from here’. She says, ‘Get up, my boy, get up, it’s enough’.

contents.textus: 107. U+aḥunayḏa d Səṫṫiye omar, ‘Yade!’ Əmmo, ‘Ha’. Omar, ‘Yade, dəzzino, – ba ʕammi xətyárk̇oyo, w hawi be həš, w kətle əšto+abne ḥrene, ann+əšto+abne ḥrénestene axrabṭə́r mínene, tə+iḏo ləktolən, – yade, dəzzino, haymén quṭlənne. Gəbli u+qa săwalano u+qa ṭarš w talanano, kule gəblile. Qṭili ġắlăbe mu+ʕulmo, yade. D̥šəmʕat xabri, dsaymat bdiḏi, lo+kəzzano’.
contents.versio: 107. Səṫṫiye’s brother says, ‘Mummy!’ She says, ‘Here’. He says, ‘Mummy, were I to go, – well, my uncle is a little old man, and he has become witless, and he has another six sons, the six sons are worse than me, they are good for nothing, – mummy, were I to go, surely they would kill them. They will take this livestock, the whole shebang, this cattle and property, the whole shebang, they will take all of it. I have killed many of their people, mummy. If you listen to what I say, if you do it my way, we shall not go’.

contents.textus: 108. Əmmo, ‘K̇urem, dsaymat bdiḏi, qəm! K̇urem, qṭilux ann+abne du+ʕulmo, gdoṯəllux qquṭlilux’. W kobuxyo.
contents.versio: 108. She says, ‘My boy, if you do it my way, set off! My boy, you have killed everyone’s sons, they will come kill you’. And she cries.

contents.textus: 109. Omar, ‘Yade, kobaʕno, yade, dṭorat mini. Koḏaʕno qquṭli ʕammi, w Ăḷah, qquṭli aš+šawʕo+abnàyḏestene. D̥šəmʕat xabri, yade … žboyi dxaṭər … čikno b baxt du+qawro dbábistene w dbábaxstene, kobaʕno dṭorat mini, dlo+məṯnəḥ lebe du+ʕulmo. Koḏaʕno b Aloho qquṭli ʕámmistene w qquṭli [ann+aḥunone] ann+abnestene. Hăma lə+qqōmno.
contents.versio: 109. He says, ‘Mummy, I want you, mummy, to leave me be. I know that they will kill my uncle and, by God, they will kill his seven sons as well. If you listen to what I say, mummy… for my sake… I swear on my father’s grave and your father’s grave as well, I want you to leave me be, since the people’s hearts will not stay. I know, by God, they will also kill my uncle and kill [his brothers] his sons as well. So be it, I won’t set off.

contents.textus: 110. I+Səṫṫiye əmmo, ‘Ăḷah dsaymat bdiḏi, Oṣmán Aġá, dsaymat bdiḏi, qqaymina!’ U+xabrayḏa latyo pīs, u+xabro dəḥmoṯi latyo pīs. ‘Qṭilux u+ʕulmo, qṭilux tmanyo bdukṯo, qṭilux ʕaṣro bdukṯo, qṭilux əšti bdukṯo, qṭilux alfo w ḥamməšmo bdukṯo, qṭilux mo bdukṯo. Ma áydarbo kṭorə́lluxyo? D̥saymat bdiḏi, Oṣmán Aġá, qqaymina.’ Omar, ‘Ăḷah lə+qqōmno, lə+kṭoreno maḥunax w me babax, lə+qqōmno’.
contents.versio: 110. Səṫṫiye says, ‘By God, if you do it my way, Osman Agha, if you do it my way, let’s set off!’ Her words were not wrong, my mother-in-law’s words were not wrong. ‘You have killed people, you killed eight in one place, you killed ten in another place, you killed sixty in another place, you killed one thousand and five hundred in another place, and you killed one hundred in yet another place. How will they let it be for you? If you do it my way, Osman Agha, let’s set off’. He says, ‘By God, I shall not set off, I shall not abandon your brother and your father, I shall not set off’.

contents.textus: 111. Hawxa koməǧġoli, əmmi, ‘U+ahl d Rəzgán Aġá kalkaṯi lə Gziro’. Ánnaqqa ḥzay mu+Zozan hǧəmme lə Gziro, Alyas, hǧəmme lə Gziro, hǧəmanne, k̇uró, mənyo hawxa, mənyo hawxa? Əmmi, ‘Hooo, qṭəlle haqqa minan, šaqṣaṭ haqqa minan.’
contents.versio: 111. Like so they communicated, they say, ‘Rezgan Agha’s family has just come to Gziro’. Now then, look, they attacked Gziro from Zozan, Ilyas, they attacked Gziro, they attacked them, boy, what is this, what is this? They say, ‘Ooh, they killed so many of them, so many people among them’.

contents.textus: 112. W čīk Oṣmán Aġá baynoṯayye, čīk Oṣmán Aġá baynoṯayye, w qṭile mənne hul dəmmat, ‘Lo+bas?’, qṭile mənne. Oṣmán Aġáste hawi brindár, miḏe i+čappe qāṯle ḏarbo, bi+iḏo čappe hawi brindár.
contents.versio: 112. And Osman Agha slipped into their midst, Osman Agha slipped into their midst and kept killing them until you would say, ‘Is it not enough?’, he kept killing them. Osman Agha also became wounded, a blow struck him on his left hand, he was wounded in his left hand.

contents.textus: 113. Qāṯle ḏarbo mi+iḏo čappe, hawi brindár mi+iḏo čappe, w čīk, bi+iḏo ráṣṭeyo, čīk baynoṯayye, čīk baynoṯayye. Hano u+aḥunayḏa, u+aḥuno di+Səṫṫiye u+naʕimo, mi+xaṣrayo komoḥe w hawo mayo komoḥe. Oṣman məḷḷe lu+barḥme, omar, ‘Haymén ono bəḥḏo+iḏòno’. Šamiʕi u+ahl d Rəzgán Aġá, əmmi, ‘Haymén səmlan brindár, hahá wenik̇eyo, dəqṭile u+qa+ḥesəl ʕamano.
contents.versio: 113. A blow struck him on his left hand, he was wounded on his left hand, and he slipped, this time with his right hand, he slipped into their midst, he slipped into their midst. This brother of hers, Səṫṫiye’s little brother, he is fighting from that side, and that one is fighting from the other side. Osman said to his brother-in-law, he says, ‘Surely I am one-handed’. Rezgan Agha’s family heard, they say, ‘Surely we have wounded him, that one is over there, who killed a raucous mob, the whole shebang.

contents.textus: 114. Qām hánostene u+aḥunay̥ḏa, u+aḥuno di+Səṫṫiye, čīk baynoṯayye, w Oṣmán Aġaste mi+xaṣrayo, bəḥḏo+iḏoyo u+rabā̀n, mi+xaṣrayo de de de, čiki baynoṯayye, koquṭli hahá mənne. Ḥərre naqəṣ u+ʕulmo, noše lo+fāš, noše lo+fāš.
contents.versio: 114. As for this one, her brother, Səṫṫiye’s brother, he up and slipped into their midst, and Osman Agha also from that side, that poor thing was one-handed, from that side doo doo doo, they slipped into their midst, they are killing every last one of them. They looked, people were lacking, nobody remained, nobody remained.

contents.textus: 115. Osmán Aġá omar, ‘Aḥuno!’ Omar, ‘Ha’. Omar, ‘D̥saymat bdiḏi, zan lu+bayto, ko druʕi azzayo, i+čappe, brindarno’. Omar, ‘Hayde!’ Aṯən lu+bayto, mdarmanle druʕe, w moṣarre druʕe, čīk bi+šamṯo, čīk bi+šamṯo, Alyas. Ḥərre komoḥən bat+tarʕe, bu+tarʕo, k̇uro, manyawo dkomoḥe bu+tarʕo, mannanək?’
contents.versio: 115. Osman Agha says, ‘Brother!’ He says, ‘Here’. He says, ‘If you do it my way, let’s go home, look, my forearm is gone, the left one, I am wounded’. He says, ‘Let’s go!’ They went home, treated his forearm, they bound his forearm, he slipped into sleep, he slipped into sleep, Ilyas. They looked, they are beating on the doors, on the door, boy, who is that one who is beating on the door, who are they?’

contents.textus: 116. Əmmi, ‘Hooo, Ăḷah kalkó hǧəmme lu+tarʕo, w Ăḷah kəppe <appe> … Aloho koḏaʕ məqqa šáqṣaṭne, kalkaṯən bəṯr u+tarʕo, kalkaṯən bəṯr u+tarʕo, w haymén qquṭlilux, hawxa? Omar, ‘E’. Məḷḷela li+emo, omar ‘Yade!’ Omar ‘Ha’. Omar, ‘Qəm səmli čike dqaḥwa, səmli qadaḥ dqaḥwa, yade.’ Səmlale li+emo qadaḥ dqaḥwa, štele u+qadaḥ di+qaḥwayḏe.
contents.versio: 116. They say, ‘Oh, God, they just attacked the door, and by God, they are … God knows how many people they are, they just came behind the door, they just came behind the door, surely they are going to kill you, right?’ He says, ‘Yes’. He said to his mother, he says, ‘Mummy!’ She says, ‘Here’. He says, ‘Go ahead, make me a spot of coffee, make me a cup of coffee, mummy’. His mother made him a cup of coffee, he drank his cup of coffee.

contents.textus: 117. ‘Lawo’, əmmo, ‘Ləzzúx, qquṭlilux, ləzzúx!’ Omar, ‘Ăḷah gəzzí’. Mḥalaqle ftəḥle … štele i+qaḥwayḏe, w mḥalaqle ftəḥle u+tarʕo w hǧəmlanne, qṭile harke w harke w harke, hul maṭi xabro li+Səṫṫiye, hula xabro lu+aḥuno, əmmo, ‘Tux!’
contents.versio: 117. ‘Boy’, she says, ‘Don’t go, they are going to kill you, don’t go!’. He says, ‘By God, I shall go’. He tossed it, he opened … he drank his coffee, he tossed it, he opened the door, and attacked them, he killed here, and here, and here, until word reached Səṫṫiye, she brought word to her brother, she says, ‘Come!’

contents.textus: 118. Qay ínaqqa dazzalle, Səṫṫiye azzale, hǧəmla lsu+aḥuno, məḷḷa lu+aḥuno, əmmo, ‘Kalkaṯən l Oṣmán Aġá, Oṣmán Aġá kalkazzalle.’
contents.versio: 118. Why, when he went against them, Səṫṫiye went to him, she rushed to the side of her brother, she said to her brother, she says, ‘They have just come to Osman Agha, Osman Agha has just gone to them.

contents.textus: 119. Qām u+aḥunáyḏaste mi+xaṣrayo, w Oṣmán Aġá mi+xaṣrayo, w mṣafalle hánəkstene, qṭəlle hánəkstene, qṭilənne, hánəkstene ṣafən, lo+fāš noše. Aṯən lu+bayto, aṯən lu+bayto.
contents.versio: 119. Her brother also started from that side, and Osman Agha from that side, and those ones they cleansed, those ones they killed, they killed them, those ones were cleansed, no one remained. They came home, they came home.

contents.textus: 120. Aḥmád Aġá omar, ‘Ha, k̇urem, mə səmxu?! Hăma dquṭlutu noše!’ U+abrayḏe u+naʕimo omar, ‘Dawla d Ăḷo dqarʕe dann+əšto+abnayḏux, dqawratte ann+əšto, qawratte ádlalyo!’ Omar, ‘Qay k̇urem?’ Omar, ‘Ann+əšto lo+ṭowən baṣmoro, aš+šawʕotayna howina greʕe d Óṣman’.
contents.versio: 120. Ahmad Agha says, ‘Oh, boys, what have you done?! Well, you killed people!’ His little son says, ‘God bless your six sons, you should bury the six of them, bury them tonight!’ He says, ‘Why, my boy?’ He says, ‘The six aren’t worth a plug nickel, the seven of us should become Osman’s servants’.

contents.textus: 121. Omar, ‘Lawo, qay kəmmat hawxa?’ Aḥmád Aġá koqōmle lu+abro+naʕimo. Omar, ‘Ono komaṇṇux aš+šawʕotayna howina greʕe d Óṣman, w hulíleste i+Səṫṫìyeste, blole. Yabo, šamiʕat’. Omar, ‘Šaməʕno, šaməʕno dəblole, ġamo layt, ʕal u+xēr, šaməʕno dəblole’.
contents.versio: 121. He says, ‘Boy, why do you say so?’ Ahmad Agha stands up to his small son. He says, ‘I’m telling you that the seven of us should become Osman’s servants, and I also gave him Səṫṫíye as well, he took her. Daddy, you heard it’. He says, ‘I heard, I heard that he took her, don’t worry, it’s for the best, I heard that he took her’.

contents.textus: 122. W tə saġ.
contents.versio: 122. And the end.

contents.textus: 001. K̇uró, omaṇṇux, ḥur, kətwa zlām, dʕele lu+Alohayḏe, dʕele lu+Alohayḏe dhowele abro. Hawile abro, hawile abro, hawi bāš, hawi bəlṭə́k, hawi ... səmle ḥəkəm dšwaḥṣar+tmonaḥṣar+əšne.
contents.versio: 001. Boy, I shall tell you, look, there once was a man, he petitioned his God, he petitioned his God to give him a son. He had a son, he had a son, he grew up, he became a young man, became ... he reached roughly 17-18 years.

contents.textus: 002. Omar, ‘Lawo, gəmṭenux ḥḏo’. Omar, ‘Baba, hat kuḏʕat, hat kuḏʕat. Wăki mṭay, hat kuḏʕat, sarbast+hat.
contents.versio: 002. He says, ‘Boy, I will bring you someone’. He says, ‘Daddy, you know best, you know best. In this case, bring her, you know best, feel free’.

contents.textus: 003. Ánnaqqa imane layt, lə+gyome, lə+gmar lo+Ăḷah, lo+flān lo+behvān. Lə+ktowar u+xabro du+babayḏe.
