contents.versio: 003. Now then, there are no oaths, he doesn’t swear, he does not say either by God, or by so-and-so. He does not break his father’s word.

contents.textus: 004. U+babayḏe omar, ‘Təmā́m, oġləm, kṭolabnux ḥḏo’. Omar, ‘Ṭlab!’ ‘Dman ṭolabno?...’ Omar, ‘Oġləm, kətle lu+baqòro, u+baqòro, kətle ḥḏo+barṯo. I+barṯayḏe šafə́rtoyo w ṭáwtoyo, híyaste lgorā́n díḏuxyo, lo+kəmdaglo w lo+koyəmyo, lgorā́n diḏuxyo’.
contents.versio: 004. His father says, ‘Okay, my son, I shall engage someone for you’. He says, ‘Engage away!’ ‘Whom shall I engage?’ He says, ‘My son, the cowherd has, the cowherd has one daughter. His daughter is beautiful and good, she is also your type, she neither lies nor swears, she is your type’.

contents.textus: 005. Omar, ‘Təmā́m’. Maḥatle u+nišanayḏe, naḥətle u+maloxo, naḥətle u+maloxo. Omar, ‘Dəmṭatlux ḥḏo’, omar, ‘Gmayṯat. Dlə+mṭat ḥḏo ktowat Yašamíš, lə+gmayṯat xayifo’. Omar, ‘Təmā́m’.
contents.versio: 005. He says, ‘Fine’. He put on his ring, an angel came down to him, an angel came down to him. He says, ‘If you bring someone back for yourself’, he says, ‘You will die. If you don’t bring back someone, you will be long-lived, you won’t die immediately’. He says, ‘Fine’.

contents.textus: 006. I+k̇ačk̇estene ʕayni xoṯe, w azzé u+maloxo si ... li+k̇ačk̇e. Məḷḷela li+k̇ačk̇e, omar, ‘D̥saymat ḥa, gmayṯat, w dlo+saymat, ktowat yašamíš’. Əmmo, ‘Təmā́m, təmā́m’.
contents.versio: 006. And the angel came by … to the girl as well, just like him. He said to her, to the girl, he says, ‘If you marry someone you will die, and if you don’t marry you will be long-lived’. She says, ‘Fine, fine’.

contents.textus: 007. Hawxa madəmme, madəmme hawxa: qām maḥatte u+nišanaṯṯe mḥawlalle, mḥawlalle, aṯən lu+bayto, səmme daʕwo w nḥərre săwā́l, w səmme baṣro w rezo w bərġəl. Sə́mmanne muklo, qralle lu+ʕulmo, u+muklo koxal u+ʕulmo.
contents.versio: 007. They proceeded like so, they proceeded like so: they up and put their rings on, they married her off, they married her off, they came home, they made a wedding party and slaughtered livestock, and made meat, rice, and bulgur. They made food for them, they summoned people, people ate food.

contents.textus: 008. Hánostene ... kito ruʕyo, faqíroyo. Kətle ḥḏo+qeməsto, ele w li+aṯto, w kətle arbʕo+naʕime, kətle arbʕo+naʕime, w kətle ... I+aṯto konəfqo kolawšo u+fistanayḏa, w hiye dkonofaq konofaq, kolowaš u+fistā̀n, latle ... faqíroyo ... latle mede.
contents.versio: 008. As for this one... there is a shepherd, he is poor. He has one robe, he and his wife, and he has four children, he has four children, and he has... The wife goes out, she wears <it as> her gown, and he, when he goes out, he goes out, he wears the gown, he has not… he is poor… he has nothing.

contents.textus: 009. Ḥa+fistānyo. Da+tre, ḥa+fistānyo. Hánostene ... Qām li+ḥurmayḏe məḷḷa lu+merk̇o, əmmo, ‘Mērk̇o!’ Omar, ‘Ha’. Əmmo, ‘Mērk̇o, de hăma zux, mbal i+ṣəṭlo, mṭaylan əšmo dbaṣro mi+daʕwo. Kalá ṭəršk̇é, u+baṣro zaḥfyo. W zux, mṭaylan baṣro!’
contents.versio: 009. This is the only gown. For the two of them, it is the only gown. As for this one… His wife up and said to her husband, she says, ‘Husband!’ He says, ‘Here’. She says, ‘Husband, prithee go now, take the bucket, bring us a little bit of meat from the wedding. There’s stew, meat is plentiful. And go, bring us meat!

contents.textus: 010. Omar, ‘Təmā́m. Hawli i+ṣəṭlo’. Lwəšle u+fistā̀n. Fayišo hiya zalṭoniṯo i+rabane, w ele lwəšle u+fistā̀n, lwəšle u+fistān, azzeyo. Ḥəḷḷe lu+k̇ùrrək̇o, kalkaṯi, e, u+k̇ùrrək̇o ḥaṯnoyo, kalkaṯi u+ruʕyo.
contents.versio: 010. He says, ‘Fine, give me the bucket’. He put on the gown. She is the one who remained naked, the poor thing, and he is the one who put on the gown, he put on the gown, he went away. He saw the boy, he had just come, yes, the boy is the bridegroom, the shepherd had just come.

contents.textus: 011. Omar, ‘Ba!’ Omar, ‘Ha! Ha, oġləm’. Omar, ‘Mlay i+ṣəṭlayḏe <baṣ...> bərġəl w baṣro. Mlaya bərġəl w baṣro, w ṭroṯe u+ruʕyawo, ṭroṯe larke’.
contents.versio: 011. He says, ‘Daddy!’ He says, ‘Here, here, my son’. He says, ‘Fill the bucket with mea… burgul and meat. Fill it with burgul and meat, and let that shepherd come, let him come here’.

contents.textus: 012. U+ruʕyo saləq, saləq lmalʕal, azzé, mbele li+odayḏe, ftəḥle u+baġōl, malwašlele badle mdiḏe. Malwašlele qundraye ḥaṯto, lwəšlele gomlak, badle, tām səmle xud ruḥe lu+ḥaṯno.
contents.versio: 012. The shepherd went up, he went upwards, he went, he took him to his room, he opened the trunk, he made him wear a suit of his. He made him wear a new pair of shoes, he dressed him in a shirt, a suit, the bridegroom made him completely like himself.

contents.textus: 013. Hánostene u+ruʕyo koṯe lu+bayto, kəmṭe i+ṣəṭlayḏe, koṯe lu+bayto. Koḥayro, komoḥe bu+tarʕo, i+aṯto koḥayro hawxa bu+tarʕo, kito bu+tarʕo naqwo, kibe haqqa. Qrawa bəqḏole, w i+badlayḏe aʕle w komoḥe bu+tarʕo, koḥayro. Əmmo, ‘Ṣabbā́v, abre du+ṣabbavawo, zux me qmu+tarʕayḏi! Hay, k̇učək̇ abre du+k̇učək̇, lə+gminakfat ʕal+babe druḥux, koṯat, koṯat, komoḥat bu+tarʕayḏi.
contents.versio: 013. This shepherd comes home, he brings his bucket, he comes home. He looks, he knocks on the door, the wife looks through the door like so, there is a hole in the door, it is yea large. There is a necktie around his neck and his suit is on him and he knocks on the door, she looks. She says, ‘Bitch, son of a bitch, get away from my door! Hey, whelp, son of a whelp, aren’t you ashamed of your own father, coming, coming, knocking on my door!’

contents.textus: 014. ‘K̇ačé’, omar, ‘Lə+mṣaʕrat, k̇ačé, pəṫe, ónono, lə+mṣaʕrat, u+zlamàyḏaxno. Əmmo, ‘U+zlām’, bdela ebe baṣ+ṣuʕre.
contents.versio: 014. ‘Girl,’ he says. ‘Girl, don’t rant and rave, girl, honey, it’s me, don’t rant and rave, I am your husband’. She says, ‘That man!’, she started ranting and raving at him.

contents.textus: 015. Mṣaʕaḷḷale, qayimole. ‘K̇ačé’ omar, ‘Lə+mṣaʕrat, ónono, húleli badle lu+ḥaṯno, húleli badle, xud druḥe sə́mleli ḥaṯno. Húleli badle me druḥe’.
contents.versio: 015. She ranted and raved at him, she stood up to him. ‘Girl,’ he says, ‘Don’t rant and rave, it’s me, the bridegroom gave me the suit, he gave me the suit, he made me a bridegroom like himself. He gave me a suit from among his own’.

contents.textus: 016. ‘Hmmm...’ ʕAbər, ʕabər, šləḥle mədle li+qeməstayḏe, hiwole li+ḥurmayḏe. W yatiwi ann+arbʕo+naʕimayḏe ʕal i+ṣəṭlo du+baṣro, du+bərġəl, di+rezo w xəḷḷe, xəḷḷe. Ele w li+aṯto lo+fāšše. Lan+naʕime ntəšše u+muklo, xəḷḷe, kafínewayne ar+răbana.
contents.versio: 016. ‘Hmmm...’ He entered, he entered, he took off and held out his robe, he gave it to his wife. And his four children sat around the bucket of meat, burgul, and rice, and they ate, they ate. As for him and his wife, nothing remained for them. The children snatched the food away, they ate it, the poor things were hungry.

contents.textus: 017. Qām hánostene, məd hawxa hawi, i+ḥurmayḏe əmmo, ‘Mērⱪo! B Ăḷo fayišina ono w hat dlo muklo’. Omar, ‘De ḥurma, zax gdobəllax, kalé zaḥfyo, kito zaḥfyo, zax gdobəllax’. Azzayo, i+răbane mədla i+ṣəṭlayḏa, lwəšla u+fistānk̇ayḏa w azzá. Ḥəḷḷa li+kalo, kalkó kuṯyo i+aṯto du+ruʕyo, kuṯyo i+aṯto du+ruʕyo.
contents.versio: 017. After that, when it happened, his wife says, ‘Husband! By God, you and I have remained without food’. He says, ‘Go ahead, wife, they will give it to you, there’s plenty, there is plenty, go, they will give it to you’. She went, the poor thing, she took her bucket, she put on her little gown, and she went. The bride looked, the shepherd’s wife is just arriving, the shepherd’s wife is coming.

contents.textus: 018. Əmmo, ‘ʕAmmo!’ Omar, ‘Ha’. Əmmo, ‘ʕAmmo, mlay i+ṣəṭlayḏa bərġəl w baṣro, di+pirak̇ayo, w ṭro səlqo larke’.
contents.versio: 018. She says, ‘Uncle!’ He says, ‘Here’. She says, ‘Uncle, fill her bucket with burgul and meat, the one of that little lady, and let her come up here’.

contents.textus: 019. Saliqo saliqo, maʕəbrola li+oda, húlala badle ʕayni xud ruḥa, simola xud ruḥa, húlala badle.
contents.versio: 019. She came up, she came up, she brought her into the room, she gave her an outfit just like her own, she made her like herself, she gave her an outfit.

contents.textus: 020. Əmmo, ‘Dánnaqqa izáx’. Aṯyo, aṯyo, naḥito, mədla i+ṣəṭlayḏa du+baṣro, du+bərġəlayḏa mədla, w aṯyo lu+bayto, aṯyo lu+bayto. Lan+naʕime hǧəmme li+ṣəṭlayḏa, ela w lu+zlām tavda matimalle, xəḷḷe.
contents.versio: 020. She says, ‘Now then go’. She came, she came, she came down, she took the bucket of meat, and she took some of her burgul, and she came home, she came home. The children rushed to her bucket, she and her husband finished it up with them, they ate.

contents.textus: 021. W fayiši hawxa, fayiši hawxa. W gāh hiya gnəfqo larwal, w gāh hiye gnofaq larwal. Komar, ‘Dənya gáwrək̇a! Dəzzino gab i+ḥurmayḏi gmōṯno’. W i+žə́nk̇este kəmmo, ‘Doṯe gabi gmayṯono! Ma lo, latno ṭaw mine! ʕAṣəl híyeyo’. Konəfqi w kodəʕri, u+babo koqore me tamo, komar, ‘K̇urem, qay lo+kuzzúx li+odayḏux? Lawo, zux li+odayḏux, zux si+ḥurmayḏux, k̇urem’. Omar, ‘E, ba, baba, təmā́m, ṭrowe’.
contents.versio: 021. And they remained like so, they remained like so. Now she goes out, then he goes out. He says, ‘Oh, seductive world! If I go to my wife, I shall die’. And the wife also says, ‘If he comes to me, I shall die. Nay, I am no better than him! He is the one who is the real deal. They keep going out and returning, his father calls out from there, he says, ‘Son, why don’t you go to your room? Boy, go to your room, go to your wife, son’. He says, ‘Yes, dad, daddy, fine, let it go’.

contents.textus: 022. Axər, marke ltamhenik̇é, dʕalle lu+Alohaṯṯe la+tre. Əmmi, ‘D Aloho, šupḥo ləšme u+ḥalyo, d Aloho obelan ʕumro, hăma dhowina yašamíš ʕam+ḥḏoḏe kmo+əšne, kmo+əšne dhowina ʕam+ḥḏoḏe yašamíš’. Əmmi, ‘Təmā́m’.
contents.versio: 022. Finally, from then on, the two of them petitioned their God. They say, ‘If God, praise be to his most pleasant name, if God gives us a lifespan, if only we stay alive together for some years, may we stay for some years alive together’. They say, ‘Fine’.

contents.textus: 023. Dʕalle lu+Alohaṯṯe, li+žənk̇e məḷḷale lu+gawro, əmmo, ‘Mērk̇o!’ Omar, ‘Ha’. Əmmo, ‘Mērk̇o, gdəmmaḷḷux mede’. Omar, ‘Amár’. Əmmo, ‘Mērk̇o, dsaymat bdiḏi, gdobinanne falge+dʕəmrayna, gdobínanne falge+dʕəmrayna, lu+ḥaṯno w li+kalo’. Omar, ‘Ṭrowe, təmā́m, təmā́m’.
contents.versio: 023. They petitioned their God, the wife said to her husband, she says, ‘Husband!’ He says, ‘Here’. She says, ‘Husband, I am going to say something to you’. He says, ‘Say it’. She says, ‘Husband, if you do it my way, we shall give them half our life, we shall give them half our life, to the bridegroom and the bride’. He says, ‘Let it happen, fine, fine’.

contents.textus: 024. Hə́nəkste kodoʕən lu+Alohaṯṯe, kəmmi, ‘Hăma dhowina yašamíš ʕam+ḥḏoḏe a+kmo+əšne, tavda dmayṯina’. Hánostene, hawi dăráng du+lalyo, konofaq, komar u+babo, ‘K̇urem, qay lo+kuzzúx li+odayḏux?’ Komar, ‘Ba, təmā́m’.
contents.versio: 024. As for the other ones, they are petitioning their God, they say, ‘If only we stay alive together for some years, let us die together’. As for this one, it became late at night, he goes out, his father says, ‘My boy, why aren’t you going to your room?’ He says, ‘Dad, fine’.

contents.textus: 025. Azzeyo, azzé, ʕabər, azzé si+ḥurmayḏe. ‘Hak’, omar, ‘Yawo!’ Omar, ‘Ha’. Omar, ‘Yawo, kalé, kalé lo+māṯno, w hatste lo+mayiṯat!’ U+maloxo me taḥt i+qaryola nafəq, u+maloxo nafəq, omar, ‘Lo+məǧġolat’, omar, ‘Lo+məǧġolat’, omar. Lu+maloxo omar, ‘Lu+baqoro ... lu+ruʕyo w li+ḥurmayḏe húwallux falge+dʕəmrayye, húwallux falge+dʕəmrayye, tmoni+əšne kətte ʕəmro, arbʕi <elux...> də́ṯxune w arbʕi də́ṯṯene. Məd kamili a+tmoni+əšne a+tretayxu tavda gmayṯutu’. Couple, pair?
contents.versio: 025. He went in, he went, he entered, he went to his wife’s side. ‘Wow!’, he says, ‘Hey!’ She says, ‘Here!’. He says, ‘Hey, look, look, I did not die and you also did not die!’ An angel came out from under the bridal bed, an angel came out, he says, ‘Don’t speak’, he says, ‘Don’t speak’. The angel says, ‘The cowherd… the shepherd and his wife have given you half their life, they have given you half their life, they have eighty years of life, forty are yours, and forty are theirs. When the eighty years have finished, the two of you will die all together’.

contents.textus: 026. Hawxa omar, ‘E’. Əmmi, ‘Təmā́m’. Maqḏalle hawxa ʕam+ḥḏoḏe, hūl dkamili a+tmoni+əšnaṯṯe, hawəlle kul ḥa naʕímestene, kamili a+tmoni+əšnaṯṯe, w ann+arbʕo bəḥḏo naqqa mayiṯi, b̥ḥa lalyo, mayiṯi ann+arbʕo.
contents.versio: 026. He says accordingly, ‘Yes’. They say, ‘Fine’. They passed the time with each other like so, until their eighty years finished, each one of them had children as well, their eighty years finished, and the four died at once, in one night, the four died.

contents.textus: 027. W tə ṣāġ.
contents.versio: 027. The end of the story.

contents.textus: 001. Kәtwa Ṣәlṭā́n Ḥasan, Bani Hláliwa, ŭ kәtwa šēx daʕ+ʕarab. Latwa šēx, áġawa, aġa daʕ+ʕàrabwa, ánnaqqa әmmíwayle šēx. Ŭ kәtwa Xalī́l Bag, háwostene bәqríṯowa, bagwa.
contents.versio: 001. There once was a Sultan Hasan, he was a Hilalian, and there was an Arab sheikh. He was not a sheikh, he was an agha, he was an Arab agha, but they called him a sheikh. And there was Halil Bey, that one was in a village, he was a bey.

contents.textus: 002. Xalī́l Bag aṯi se Ṣәlṭā́n Ḥasan. Kə́twayle ḥoṯo, húleleyo, i+ḥoṯayḏe, hiwole l Xalī́l Bag. Ḥazna, әšma Ḥáznawa. Hiwole l Xalī́l Bag, hiwole l Xalī́l Bag. Xalī́l Bágstene blole ... i+ḥoṯo ... kogoraš, lo?
contents.versio: 002. Halil Bey came over to Sultan Hasan. He had a sister, he gave her to him, his sister, he gave her to Halil Bey. Hazna, her name was Hazna. He gave her to Halil Bey, he gave her to Halil Bey. Halil Bey also took her ... the sister... it’s recording, isn’t it?

contents.textus: 003. Xalī́l Bágstene mbele i+ḥoṯo, sәmle daʕwo, qrele lu+ʕulmo ġắlăbe (N: ‘Hánəste lә+gmoraxna aʕlayxu’, S: Morexa!). Hánəstene Ṣәlṭā́n Ḥasan mbele i+ḥoṯo, omar, ‘Ono lә+gmaqbanno saymat gәrgə́r, saymat daʕwe’, flān ŭ behvā́n, ‘Gdoṯeno gәmbanno ḥoṯi me tamo, gәmṭena lu+bayto.’
contents.versio: 003. Halil Bey also took his sister, he prepared a wedding, he called many people (N: ‘This one, I will not stretch it out for you’, S: ‘Stretch it out!’). This one, Sultan Hasan, he brought his sister, he says, ‘I don’t accept that you make a fuss, prepare a wedding’, and so on and so forth, ‘I’ll come to bring my sister from there, I’ll bring her back home.’

contents.textus: 004. Omar, ‘Lә+g̊sōmno.’ Blole, blole. Hawile tre+abne ǧewi, hawile tre+abne ǧewi l Xalī́l Bag. Hánəstene Ṣәlṭā́n... hano d̥komanno, Ṣәlṭā́n Ḥasan, mə́ḷḷele, omar, ‘Ḥūr, lukwe d̥saymat.’ Ele sәmle. Hawile tre+abne ǧewi, ḥa mәnne maḥatle әšme Xalaf, ŭ u+ḥrènostene, әšmo ḥreno maḥátwayle aʕle, háwostene... maḥatle әšme Fәnǧā́n Aġá. Tәmā́m? Maḥatle ‿šmé d̥ḥa Xalaf, ḥa‿š<me> Fәnǧā́n Aġá. Ann+abnayḏe ǧewi, hawile tre+abne.
contents.versio: 004. He says, ‘I won’t do it.’ He brought her back, he brought her back. He had two twin sons, he had two twin sons, Halil Bey. This one, the Sultan... this one that I’m talking about, Sultan Hasan, he said to him, he says, ‘Look, you shouldn’t do it.’ He did it. He had two twin sons, one of whom he called Halaf, and another one, he gave him another name, as for that one... he called him Finjan Agha. Okay? He named one Halaf, one Finjan Agha. His twin sons, he had two sons.

contents.textus: 005. Hánəstene, barbariye baynoṯayye. Šēx, šēx, hano... u+šēx daʕ+ʕarab d̥komaṇṇux, latyo šēx, áġayo hiye, aġa daʕ+ʕàrabyo. Mḥayṣele u+ruʕyo d̥ Ṣәlṭā́n Ḥasan, mḥayṣele u+ruʕyayḏe, mbele, mbele u+ruʕyayḏe.
contents.versio: 005. This one, there is a rivalry between them. The sheikh, the sheikh, this one, the Arab sheikh that I’m telling you, he is not a sheikh, he is an agha, he is an Arab agha. He captured Sultan Hasan’s shepherd, he captured his shepherd. He took him away, he took away his shepherd.

contents.textus: 006. Ṣәlṭā́n Ḥasan omar, ‘K̇uro, koyo u+ruʕyo? Qay laṯi?’ I+aṯto әmmo, ‘Ba may kuḏʕono? Kalkó laṯi, ono may kuḏʕono?’ K̇ačé! Ḥzawu, mšayelu aʕle.’ Mšayalle aʕle, ‘Nafәq se ... su+šēx, Šēx Muṣṭafá, šēx daʕ+ʕÀrabyo, aġa daʕ+ʕÀrabyo hiye’.
contents.versio: 006. Sultan Hasan says, ‘Boy, where is the shepherd? Why didn’t he come?’ His wife says, ‘How do I know? He hasn’t come back, how do I know? Girls! Look, inquire about him’. They inquired about him, (learning) ‘He appeared over by ... over by the sheikh, Sheikh Mustafa, it’s the Arab sheikh, it’s the Arab agha’.

contents.textus: 007. Mə́rrale l Ṣәlṭā́n Ḥasan, әmmi, ‘Haymén, kalé u+greʕayḏux, su+šēx daʕ+ʕArab’, ‘Hawxa?’ Әmmi, ‘E.’
contents.versio: 007. They said to Sultan Hasan, they say, ‘I swear, here’s your servant, over by the Arab sheikh’. ‘Like so?’ They say, ‘Yes’.

contents.textus: 008. Mšāʕle Xalī́l du+ḥaṯnayḏe, mšāʕle Xalī́l, omar... azzé, mṭele, ŭ šqile mine, bagwa, húleleyo, lu+šēx daʕ+ʕArab húleleyo. Mṭele u+ruʕyayḏe.
contents.versio: 008. He sent Halil, one of his son-in-laws, he sent Halil, he says... he went, brought him, and took him from him, he was (Halil) Bey, he gave him to him, the Arab sheikh gave him to him. He brought back his shepherd.

contents.textus: 009. Ṣәlṭā́n Ḥasan ṣulṭono da+Hlalìyeyo, omar, ‘Áydarbo g̊ṭoreno, g̊ṭoreno u+ḥaṯnay<ḏi>. u+greʕayḏi dәmbele lano, áydarbo g̊ṭoréneyo?’ Hánəstene, azzé dawr bi+<ḥolo> eba. Ṣәlṭā́n Ḥasan omar, ‘Lәkwe dlәzzoxu, dlә+mṭuṭu u+ṭarš ŭ talanayḏe. Kәbʕe mṭuṭu u+ṭarš ŭ talanayḏe, kule mṭūṭәle’, mәḷḷe la+greʕayḏe.
contents.versio: 009. Sultan Hasan, he is the Sultan of the Hilalians, he says, ‘How shall I let, shall I let, my son-in-… my servant whom that one took, how shall I let him do it?’ This one as well, a while passed for it in the meantime. Sultan Hasan says, ‘It isn’t right you don’t go, to bring back his livestock and his stolen cattle. It is a must that you bring back his livestock and his stolen cattle, bring back all of it’, he said to his servants.

contents.textus: 010. A+greʕayḏe azzehәn, mḥalaqqe ʕal i+qriṯo, mṭalle u+mede d̥kәtwa hno, mṭalle, la+greʕe d̥ Ṣәlṭā́n Ḥasan.
contents.versio: 010. His servants went, they attacked the village, they brought back the stuff that was there, they brought it back, the servants of Sultan Hasan.

contents.textus: 011. U+šēx daʕ+ʕArab ... Әmmi, ‘Ăḷa, mbele ŭ mbele l Ṣәlṭā́n Ḥasan u+medayḏux kule.’ Hánəste, u+šēx daʕ+ʕArab, híyeste áġayo, híyestene b̥k̇erhátiyo. Hǧəmle, hǧəmme ləḥḏoḏe, hǧəmme ləḥḏoḏe, qṭəlle tmanyo məḥḏoḏe, qṭəlle tmanyo+šaqṣat məḥḏoḏe, qṭilənne. Ṣәlṭā́n Ḥasan omar, ‘Diḏi aṯən kamile, laṯən kamile?’ Əmmi, ‘Haymén diḏux qṭīl tre, qṭīl tre mənne, qṭili’. Omar, ‘Looo’, omar, ‘Haymén, qṭili tre mənne?’
contents.versio: 011. The Arab sheikh … They say, ‘Gosh, Sultan Hasan took, he took all your belongings.’ As for this one, the Arab sheikh, he is also an Agha, he is also resourceful. He attacked, they attacked each other, they attacked each other, they killed eight of each other, they killed eight persons of each other, they killed them. Sultan Hasan says, ‘Did those of mine come back intact, did they not come back intact?’ They say, ‘I swear of yours, it was two killed, it was two of them killed, they were killed’. He says, ‘Nooo’, he says, ‘Really, two of them were killed?’

contents.textus: 012. ‘Du+šēx daʕ+ʕArab’, əmmi, ‘Ăḷa, du+šēx daʕ+ʕArab qṭīl əšto.’ ‘E’, omar, ‘Qṭīl əšto... mdiḏi tre, ġamo layto.’ Hánəstene, a+tre+abnè d̥še... d̥ Xalī́l Bag, a+tre+abne d̥ Xalī́l Bag hawən xortī́n, rabe, hawən xortī́n (čirók̇eyo), hawən rabe. Fənǧā́n Aġá omar, ‘Yabo’, omar, ‘Ha’. Omar, ‘Yabo, kəmmi qṭəlle tre məd̥ḥoli, ŭ qṭəlle əšto məd... du+šēx daʕ+ʕArab... du... daʕ+ʕarab, du+šēx qṭəlle əšto, ŭ tre məd̥ḥoli.’
contents.versio: 012. ‘Of the Arab sheikh’, they say, ‘Gosh, of the Arab sheikh. ‘Yes’, he says, ‘it was six killed, two of mine, no worries.’ This one as well, the two sons of sheikh... of Halil Bey, Halil Bey’s two sons became young lads, older, they became young lads (it is a story), they became older. Finjan Agha says, ‘Dad’, he says, ‘Here’. He says, ‘Dad, they say they killed two of my uncle’s (men), and they killed six of… of the Arab sheikh’s, of .. of the Arabs, they killed six of the sheikh’s, and two of my uncle’s.’

contents.textus: 013. Omar, ‘K̇urem, Fənǧā́n Aġá’, omar, ‘ʕəmrux əštaḥ... ḥamšaḥṣar, əštaḥṣar+əšneyo, rkad̥, rkad̥.’ Omar, ‘Ăḷa, yabo, gəzzino, gəzzino.’ ‘Gəzzúx layko?’ Omar, ‘Yabo, hăma gəzzino ónostene, growaxno ʕal u+səsyo, yabo, ŭ gəzzino gəmḥalaqno ʕal u+darbo. Hăma ónoste gəzzino bayn aš+šēx daʕ+ʕArab, ŭ támoda ŭ kibi fotalno ... dʔoṯeno bayn a+hlalìyeste, doṯeno gab ḥólistene tamo, hăma gmarfeno bəhn diḏi, yabo, gəzzino!’
contents.versio: 013. He says, ‘My boy, Finjan Agha’, he says, ‘You are six... fifteen, sixteen years old, stay back, stay back’. He says, ‘Gosh, Dad, I shall go, I shall go.’ ‘You will go there?’ He says, ‘Dad, please, I shall go, I shall ride a horse, Dad, and I shall go, I shall pounce on the way. Please, I too shall go to the Arab sheikh, and over there and I can also go around to come to the Hilalians, to come over to my uncle as well over there, please, I shall take my rest, Dad, I shall go!’

contents.textus: 014. Xalaf du+aḥunayḏe, omar, omar, ‘Lawo, lay gəzzúx? Fənǧā́n, lay gəzzúx?’ Omar, ‘Ašə́r gəzzí.’ Hánəstene mḥalaqle, mḥalaqle ʕal u+darbo. Qamayto azzeyo su+šēx daʕ+ʕarab. E, Ḥazna (Ḥazna i+barṯo du+šēx daʕ+ʕàrabyo), kalá bu+šəbbak̇yo, koḥayro kal kaṯi rawixo, xort šafiro, i+porik̇ayḏe maqlab̥to bayne ʕayne, xort šafiro.
contents.versio: 014. Halaf, one of his brothers, says, he says, ‘Boy, where will you go? Finjan, where will you go?’ He says, ‘I’ll surely go.’ This one even pounced, he pounced on the way. First he went over by the Arab sheikh. Yes, Ḥazna (Ḥazna is the daughter of the Arab sheikh), here she is at the window, she is looking and here he comes along riding, a handsome guy, his bangs are curled on his forehead, a handsome guy.

contents.textus: 015. Əmmo, ‘Ăla, hak̇a ónono, hano arbā́b díḏiyo, hano Ăla hano arbā́b díḏiyo.’ Aṯi, aṯi su šēx daʕ+ʕarab, a‘Salā́m ʕalayk!’ ‘ʕAlaykum salā́m’.a Yatu, yatu tamo. U+šēx daʕ+ʕarab omar, ‘Lawo, manhat, máykohat? Ya tgenč,t máykohat?’ Omar, ‘Ono u+abro d̥ Xalī́l Bagno.’ ‘U+abro d̥ Xalī́l Baghat?’ Omar, ‘E.’
contents.versio: 015. She says, ‘Gosh, as I live and breathe (lit. if I am I), this one is worthy of me, this one, gosh, he is worthy of me.’ He came, he came to the Arab sheikh, a‘Peace be upon you!’ ‘Peace be upon you as well!’a He sat, he sat there. The Arab sheikh says, ‘Boy, who are you, where are you from? tBoy,t where are you from?’ He says, ‘I am the son of Halil Bey’. ‘You are the son of Halil Bey?’ He says, ‘Yes’.

contents.textus: 016. Omar, ‘Xēryo daṯat?’ Omar, ‘Haymén ónostene ya, ya šēx daʕ+ʕarab, aṯino dmarfeno behn diḏi ŭ aṯino d̥koraxni k̇elik̇e. Omaṇṇo gəzzino tre+xabre gabayxu, tre+xabre gəzzí se ḥólistene, barbar-e dəḥḏoḏe hatu. Gəzzí gab ḥólistene, ḥoli gdomar, ‘Hə, azzé su+šēx daʕ+ʕarab ŭ laṯi, laṯi gabi u+xwarzayḏi’. Ašə́r gəzzino. Omar, ‘Klay, klay, xul muklooo, henú izúx.’ Omar, ‘Təmā́m.’
contents.versio: 016. He says, ‘Is it a good thing that you have come?’ He says, ‘I swear on my part, Arab sheikh, I came to take a rest and I came to take myself a stroll for a while. I say I will come for a couple of words with you, a couple of words at my uncle’s too, you are each other’s rivals. Were I to go to my uncle too, my uncle would say, “Hey, he went to the Arab sheikh, and he didn’t come, he didn’t come to my place, my nephew”. I shall surely go’. He says, ‘Stay, stay, eat some food, then go’. He says, ‘Okay’.

contents.textus: 017. Hánəstene komaḥti u+muklaṯṯe, maḥatte u+muklo, əmmi, ‘Mḥalaqle l Ṣәlṭā́n Ḥasan ʕal i+qriṯo, mḥalaqle ʕal i+qriṯo l Ṣәlṭā́n Ḥasan!’ ínaqqa dəmḥalaqle ʕal i+qriṯo l Ṣәlṭā́n Ḥasan, u+xwarzàyḏeyo, su+šēx daʕ+ʕàrabyo, ḥzele Ḥazna, kalá bu+šəbbak̇ koḥōr e... koḥōr eba, hne aʕla.
contents.versio: 017. As for these ones, they are putting out their food, they put out the food, they say, ‘Sultan Hasan attacked the village, Sultan Hasan attacked the village!’ When Sultan Hasan attacked the village, he is his nephew, and he is at the Arab sheikh’s, he saw Hazna, here she is at the window, he sees ... he sees her, he is whatsiting her.

contents.textus: 018. Omar, omar, ‘Mə́nyanano, mən hano, mən ʕúlmoyo, məg‿gərgəryano, mə́nyano?’ Fәnǧā́n Aġá, ‘Mən masáleyo haṯe, mə́nyaṯe?’ Əmmi, ‘Ăla, lu+šēx ... l Ṣәlṭā́n Ḥasan mḥalaqle ʕal u+šēx, kalkó mbele u+ṭarš ŭ talanayḏe!’ Hánoste, Fәnǧā́n Aġá komičək, komičək bu+šar ʕam u... ʕam a+greʕe du+ḥolo, ʕam u+ḥolo. Fәnǧā́n Aġaste, xəd u+, xəd u+čičak kuzzé, ko... mi+xaṣraṯe ŭ laṯe ŭ laṯe ŭ laṯe, mtaraqle kulle, kulle mahzamme. Kulle mahzamme, u+el daḥ+ḥolonayḏe.
contents.versio: 018. He says, he says, ‘What is this one, what is this one, what is the crowd, what is this noise, what is the matter?’ Finjan Agha, ‘What is the matter with this one, what is this?’ They say, ‘Gosh, the sheikh ... Sultan Hasan attacked the sheikh, he has taken his livestock and his stolen cattle!’ This one, Finjan Agha sneaks, he sneaks into the fight against his uncle’s servants, against his uncle. As for Finjan Agha, he goes like a ... like a flower, he is ... from this side and this, and this, and this, he drove them all off, they all fled. They all fled, his uncle’s clan.

contents.textus: 019. ‘Qṭīl, lo+qṭīl?’ Əmmi, ‘Qṭīl traḥṣar, qṭile l Fənǧā́n Aġa traḥṣar ma+greʕe daḥ+ḥolonayḏe.’ ‘Ohooo, lma qṭilile ŭ lma qṭilile?’ ‘L Fәnǧā́n Aġá, l Fәnǧā́n Aġá, l Fәnǧā́n Aġá!’ Azzehən daʕiri se Ṣәlṭā́n Ḥasan. Ṣәlṭā́n Ḥasan omar, ‘Kone?’ Omar, ‘Haymén qṭīl traḥṣar minan. Kito ḥa xort, aṣpah mine layto, ŭ noše layb‿aʕle, noše laybe qōm barbár diḏe... noše layb‿aʕle, ‘Looo?’ Əmmi, əmmi, ‘Haymén!’ ‘áydarbo g̊d̥owe hawxa?’
contents.versio: 019. ‘Was anyone killed or not?’ They say, ‘It was twelve killed, Finjan Agha killed twelve of his uncle’s servants.’ ‘Oooh, who killed them and who (else) killed them? ‘Finjan Agha, Finjan Agha, Finjan Agha!’ They went back to Sultan Hasan’s place. Sultan Hasan says, ‘Where are they?’ He says, ‘I swear it was twelve of us killed. There is one lad, no one is more handsome than him, and no one can defeat him, no one can stand up to him... no one can defeat him.’ ‘Nooo?’ They say, they say, ‘I swear!’ ‘How could it be so?’

contents.textus: 020. Ṣәlṭā́n Ḥasan mə́ḷḷela li+ḥurmayḏe, omar, ‘Ḥurma!’ Omar, omar, ‘Ha!’, omar, ‘Ḥurma, hak̇a ónono, hano u+xurtano u+xwarzàyḏiyo. Hak̇a ónono, Ṣəltan Ḥáṣanno, hano u+xwarzàyḏiyo, Fәnǧā́n Aġayo, Fәnǧā́n Bag.’ ‘Haaa, e, mə‿saymina, mə‿lo+saymina?’ Omar, ‘Haymén gəzzánole, gəzzánole. Ono gəzzínole, ya mínanyo, ya míneyo.’
contents.versio: 020. Sultan Hasan said to his wife, he says, ‘Wife!’ She says, she says, ‘Here!’, he says, ‘Wife, as I live and breathe (lit. if I am I), this very lad is my nephew. As I live and breathe, I Sultan Hasan, this is my nephew, he is Finjan Agha, Finjan Bey. ‘Oh, yes, what should we or shouldn’t we do?’ He says, ‘I swear, we shall go to him, we shall go to him. I myself shall go to him, either it’s (coming) from us or from him.’

contents.textus: 021. Mḥalaqle l Ṣәlṭā́n Ḥasan, mṭele kəppe zəd̥ me mo+šaqṣaṭ ʕam ruḥe. Ŭ aṯən, aṯən lu+šēx daʕ+ʕarab, u+šēx daʕ+ʕarab ánnaqqa mtaxaḷḷe, hawi u+šarkešaṯṯe Fәnǧā́n Aġá. Əmmi, ‘Hə hə hə hə, ăḷa mḥalaqqe ʕal i+qriṯo, mballe u+săwā̀l, ŭ kalkó kohəǧmi li+qrìṯostene, ŭ aṯən kəppe zəd̥̚ me mo+šaqṣaṭ’. ‘Hawxa?’ Omar, ‘E.’
contents.versio: 021. Sultan Hasan rushed him, he brought roughly more than a hundred people with him. And they came, they came to the Arab sheikh, then the Arab sheikh retreated, (so) Finjan Agha became their warlord. They say (to him), ‘Go, go, go, go!, gosh they have rushed towards the village, they have taken the cattle, and look they’re attacking even the village, and roughly more than a hundred men have come!’ ‘Is it so?’ He says, ‘Yes.’

contents.textus: 022. Fәnǧā́n Aġá omar, ‘Ḥazna!’, omar, ‘Ha’, omar, ‘Səmli qədáḥ d̥qaḥwa.’ Sə́mlale qədáḥ d̥qaḥwa. ínaqqa dəḥzela Fәnǧā́n Aġá koštele i+qaḥwa, maḥatle iḏoṯe ʕal ṣadra ŭ húlale i+qaḥwa, šətyole, mkamlole, omar, ‘Ḥazna, dayəm! Dayəm, Ḥazna! B̥xaṭə́r diḏax!’
contents.versio: 022. Finjan Agha says, ‘Hazna!’, she says, ‘Here’, he says, ‘Make me a cup of coffee.’ She made him a cup of coffee. When she saw Finjan Agha drinking the coffee, he had put his hands on her chest as she gave him the coffee, he drank it, he finished it, he says, ‘Hazna, thanks (lit. ‘always [may God multiply it]’)! Thanks, Hazna! By your leave!’

contents.textus: 023. Azzalle. Ha harke, ha harke, ha harke, falət, falət bəṯrayye, ḥa lo+ṭrele dlo+darbe, dlo+ḏarbe, hən brindarat, ŭ hən mahzamme, ŭ hə́nstene qṭilile l Fәnǧā́n Aġá. ‘K̇uro, lman səmle u+šar, lmas‿səmle i+gawruṯaṯe, lmas‿səmle haṯe, k̇uro, mánnani, hani?’ Əmmi, ‘K̇uro, kito ḥa, u+abro d̥ Xalī́l Bagyo, háwoyo, kəmmile Fәnǧā́n Aġá, háwoyo.’ Əmmi, ‘Eee, həəə!’
contents.versio: 023. He went to them. Over here, over here, over here, he pursued, he pursued after them, he didn’t leave anybody without blows, without blows, some were wounded, and some escaped, and Finjan Agha killed some too. ‘Boy, who did the battle, who did this feat, who did this, boy, who are they, these ones.’ They say, ‘Boy, there is someone, he is the son of Halil Bey, it’s that one, they call him Finjan Agha, it’s that one.’ They say, ‘Riiiight, ahah!’

contents.textus: 024. U+šēx daʕ+ʕarab omar, ‘Lawo, baṭilat? Dmaxlux k̇elik̇e!’ Omar, ‘Lo! Lo+baṭəlno. Sumli čik̇e d̥qaḥwa, Ḥazna!’
contents.versio: 024. The Arab sheikh says, ‘Boy, did you get tired? Take yourself a nap for a second!’ He says, ‘No! I didn’t get tired, make me a bit of coffee, Ḥazna!’

contents.textus: 025. E, Ḥáznastene, čičák̇eyo mu+šufrayḏa, mṭélale qədaḥ d̥qaḥwa. Košote i+qaḥwayḏe, naqla hǧəmme li+qriṯo disa. Hǧəmme li+qriṯo, u+ḥolo b̥qamuṯayye, u+ḥolayḏe b̥qamuṯayye. Aṯəlle l Fәnǧā́n Aġa, lu+ḥolo čīk qarši d̥ Fәnǧā́n Aġá. Omar, ‘Fәnǧā́n Aġá!’, omar, ‘Ha!’ Omar, ‘Fәnǧā́n Bag, lawo’, omar, ‘Ono ḥoluxno, u+aḥuno, u+aḥuno démuxno. Kobaʕno d̥kolat lawo hat. Ṭray mini ŭ mu+šēx daʕ+ʕarab’. Omar, ‘Ənkā́n layt’, omar, ‘Ənkā́n layt.’
contents.versio: 025. Right, now Hazna, she is a flower because of her beauty, she brought him a cup of coffee. He drinks his coffee, that moment they attacked the village again. They attacked the village, the uncle at their fore, his uncle at their fore. They came to Finjan Agha, his uncle got himself up against Finjan Agha. He says, ‘Finjan Agha!’, he says, ‘Here!’, he says, ‘Finjan Bey, boy’, he says, ‘I am your uncle, the brother, I am the brother of your mother. I want you to stay put, you are a boy. Leave me and the Arab sheikh be’. He says, ‘It’s impossible (lit. there isn’t any possibility)’, he says, ‘It’s impossible’.

contents.textus: 026. Čiki baynoṯayye, čīk u+ʕulmo baynoṯayye, čīk u+ʕulmo baynoṯayye, lə+ṭralle d̥quṭli ḥḏoḏe, lo, ʕulmo, ḥəngi čīk u+ʕulmo baynoṯayye. Lo+ṭrele, lo+ṭralle d̥quṭli ḥḏoḏe.
contents.versio: 026. They slipped between them, everybody (lit. the people) slipped between them, everybody slipped between them, they did not allow them to kill each other, no, people, since so many people slipped between them. He didn’t allow, they didn’t allow them to kill each other.

contents.textus: 027. Daʕər Ṣәlṭā́n Ḥasan, daʕər lu+baytayḏe. Daʕər lu+baytayḏe, hánəstene Fәnǧā́n Aġá koʕobar lu+bayto, koṯe, lo+kodoʕar, koṯe lu+bayto dísane, komar, ‘Ḥazna!’, komar, ‘Ha!’, komar, ‘Səmli čik̇e d̥qaḥwa.’ Sə́mlale čik̇e d̥qaḥwa, štele i+qaḥwayḏe, omar, ‘Šēx!’, omar, ‘Ha!’, omar, ‘Aġa, lo+kuḏʕat lmən aṯino?’ Omar, ‘Lo.’ Omar, ‘Haymén ono kobaʕno i+barṯayḏux, ŭ amaḷḷa li+barṯayḏux, dəmmo, “Lo”, lo’.
contents.versio: 027. Sultan Hasan returned, he returned to his house. He returned to his house, next (lit. ‘this one too’) Finjan Agha enters the house, he comes, he does not go back, he comes to the house (i.e., the Sheikh’s house) again, he says, ‘Ḥazna!’, she says, ‘Here!’, he says, ‘Make me a bit of coffee.’ She made him a bit of coffee, he drank his coffee, he says, ‘Sheikh!’, he says, ‘Here!’, he says, ‘Agha, don’t you know what I came for?’, he says, ‘No.’ He says, ‘I swear, I want your daughter, and tell your daughter, if she says, “No”, (then) no’.

contents.textus: 028. Mə́ḷḷela li+barṯo, əmmo, ‘Aʕli gawre ḥărā́m zowṫə́r me Fәnǧā́n Aġá. Ag+gawre dəbriṯo kulle babi ŭ aḥúnine’.
contents.versio: 028. He said to his daughter, she says, ‘Men other than (lit. ‘in excess of’) Finjan Agha are forbidden to me. All the men of Creation are my father and my brother’.

contents.textus: 029. U šēx daʕ+ʕàrabstene, kətle abre dʕammo, abre du+ʕammayḏe, ánnaqqa. Háwostene čīk b̥qamuṯa d̥ Ḥazna. Omar, ‘Lo, lə+gmaqbanno dobatla, dobatla l Fәnǧā́n Aġá.’ Omar, ‘Fәnǧā́n Aġá!’, omar, ‘Ha!’, omar, ‘Fәnǧā́n Aġá, i+Ǧanǧane, i+Ǧanǧane, i+səsto, i+ǧuwaniye di+səsto d̥ Ḥasan Aġayo, d̥ Ṣәlṭā́n Ḥáṣanyo, i+Ǧanǧane i+ǧuwaniye d̥ Ṣәlṭā́n Ḥáṣanyo.’ Omar, omar, ‘Dəzzúx mṭatli i+Ǧanǧane, dəmṭatla i+ǧuwaniye di+səsto d̥ḥolux, gdobénuxyo. Dlə+mṭatla, lə+gbènuxyo.’ (15.55)
contents.versio: 029. The Arab sheikh, he has a cousin, the son of his uncle, now. As for that one, he got himself in front of Hazna. He says, ‘No, I won’t accept your giving her, your giving her to Finjan Agha.’ He says, ‘Finjan Agha!’, he says, ‘Here!’, he says, ‘Finjan Agha, Janjane, Janjane the mare, Hasan Agha’s mare’s filly, of Sultan Hasan, Sultan Hasan’s filly Janjane.’ He says, he says, ‘If you go and bring me Janjane, if you bring me your uncle’s mare’s filly, I will give her to you. If you don’t bring her, I shan’t give her to you.’

contents.textus: 030. E, Fәnǧā́n Aġástene čīk lebe b̥ Ḥazna. Lo+blebo, bmo+lebe čīk lebe b̥ Ḥazna. Omar, ‘Təmā́m.’ Hawi ṣafro, qām mi+šamṯo, omar, ‘Ḥazna!’, omar, ‘Ha!’, omar, ‘Ḥazna, səmli čik̇e d̥qaḥwa.’ Sə́mlale čik̇e d̥qaḥwa, ŭ štele i+qaḥwayḏe, rawəx, azzé, rawəx, azzeyo, azzé, hǧəmle lu+ḥolo.
contents.versio: 030. Right, Finjan Agha, Ḥazna got into his heart, not just once (lit. ‘not the heart’), she got into his heart a hundred times (lit. ‘in a hundred hearts’). He says, ‘Okay.’ It was morning, he got up from his slumber, he says, ‘Ḥazna!’, she says, ‘Here!’, he says, ‘Hazna, make me a bit of coffee.’ She made him a bit of coffee, and he drank his coffee, he rode, he went, he rode, he went, he rushed to his uncle.

contents.textus: 031. U+ḥolòstene azzé se Xalī́l Bag rišo, su+ḥaṯnayḏe. Azzé rišo su+ḥaṯnayḏe, Ṣәlṭā́n Ḥasan. Hánəstene, koṯe u+abro, Fәnǧā́n Aġá koʕobar li+dərto koḥōr, kalá i+aṯto d̥ Ṣәlṭā́n Ḥasan bi+dərto. Ŭ hǧə́mlela, kalé u+abràyḏastene qəm ṣadra, u+zʕuràyḏaste kalé qəm ṣadra. Hǧəmle, omar, omar, ‘Taḥolo!’, omar, ‘Ha!’, omar, ‘Taḥolo, aṯino li+Ǧanǧane.’
contents.versio: 031. His uncle also went to Halil Bey’s place for a short visit, to his brother-in-law’s place. He went for a short visit to his brother-in-law’s place, Sultan Hasan did. Next (lit. ‘this one too’) the son comes, Finjan Agha, enters the courtyard to look, here’s Sultan Hasan’s wife, in the courtyard. And he rushed up to her, here’s her son at her breast too, her boy is here at her breast. He rushed up to her, he says, he says, ‘Aunt!’, she says, ‘Here!’, he says, ‘Aunt, I came for Janjane’.

contents.textus: 032. ‘I+Ǧanǧane,’ əmmo, ‘I+Ǧanǧane kalá, maḥtole lḥolux bi+šk̇afte, bu+axùr, ŭ maqlaḏle u+tarʕo, u+qliḏo ʕam ḥóluxyo. Klay hul doṯe ḥolux.’ Omar, ‘Laybi koleno doṯe ḥoli. Koməf<qatla>, komṭatla, kofətḥat u+tarʕo! Ftaḥe! Lo+g̊fətḥatle, qoṭaʕno qarʕe du+abrayḏax.’
contents.versio: 032. ‘Janjane’, she says, ‘Here’s Janjane, your uncle put her into the cave, into the stall, and he locked the door, the key is with you uncle. Wait until your uncle comes back’. He says, ‘I can’t wait for my uncle to come back. You should bring <her out>, you should bring her, you should open the door! Open it! If you won’t open it, I shall cut off your son’s head!’

contents.textus: 033. ‘K̇uro, l Ăloho šqile u+hawno minux!’ Omar, ‘Baḥ+ḥaye du+Alohano, dlo+mṭat... dlo+məfqatla, g̊ʶqoṭanne, g̊ʶqoṭanno u+abrayḏax’. Qām maǧbū́r, ǧbiro, məd əzzayo, ‘Ḥayra’, kəmmo, ‘Layko gəzzí, layt u+tarʕo, qliḏo layto!’ Mədle lu+zʕuro, mḥele u+šalfo, u+hno d̥qoṭele, u+sa<yfo> d̥qoṭaʕ qarʕe du+zʕuro. Əmmo, ‘Klay, klay, klay, brozo, klay, klay, klay!’, əmmo, ‘Klay, klay!’ Azzé, ftəḥle u+tarʕo, húlale i+Ǧanǧane. I+Ǧanǧane ǧewaníyeyo, di+sə̀stoyo, əšma Ǧanǧáneyo. Hánəstene, kəmṭe li+Ǧanǧane, komoṣaḷḷa bu+səsyayḏe ŭ koṯe. Kohoǧam, koṯe. (18:20).
contents.versio: 033. ‘Boy, God has taken your mind away (lit. ‘the mind from you’)!’ He says, ‘By the life of this God, if you do not bri..., if you do not bring her out, I will kill your son’. It became necessary, she was obliged, when she went, ‘Buddy’, she says, ‘Where shall I go, there is no door, there is no key!’ He took the little one, he struck him with the knife, the whatsit to kill him, the swo<rd> to cut off the little one’s head. She says, ‘Wait, wait, wait, you pig, wait, wait, wait’, she says, ‘Wait, wait!’ He went, he opened the door, she gave him Janjane. Janjane is the filly, she’s from the mare, her name is Janjane. As for this one, he brings Janjane, he hitches her to his horse and he comes back. He comes back in a rush.

contents.textus: 034. Maṭi u+xabro su+šēx daʕ+ʕarab, əmmi, ‘Haymén, kalkaṯi, kalkaṯi, mṭele, kalá ǧewaniye bəṯr u+səsyayḏe moṣarto’. Bu+durben koḥayri, Fәnǧā́n Aġá kalkaṯi. Aṯi, omar, omar, ‘Ba áydarbo sōmno?’ U+šēx daʕ+ʕarab omar, ‘Klay, ono mahzamno!’ ‘K̇uro, lay gəzzúx?’ ‘Omanno, toleno ruḥi, gəzzí toleno ruḥi, veg‿gdoṯe u+ḥolayḏe, g̊ʶqoṭal, g̊šolaḥ qarʕi, g̊ʶqoṭal, g̊ʶqoṭal ónostene, g̊ʶqoṭal, g̊ʶqoṭal u+xwarzàyḏestene.’ U+šēx daʕ+ʕarab tlele ruḥe, tlele ruḥe, maḥatle ruḥe bəškaftə́k̇e, tlele ruḥe u+šēx.
contents.versio: 034. The word reached the Arab sheikh’s place, they say, ‘I swear, he’s about to arrive, he’s about to arrive, he brought it, here’s a filly hitched behind his horse’. They are looking through binoculars, Finjan Agha is about to arrive. He came back, he says, he says, ‘How should I act?’ The Arab sheikh says, ‘Wait, let me escape!’ ‘Boy, where are you going?’ ‘I am saying, I should hide myself, I should go hide myself, now your uncle will come, he will kill, he will cut off my head, he will kill, he will kill me too, he will kill, he will kill my nephew too.’ The Arab sheikh hid himself, he hid himself, he put himself in a cave, the sheikh hid himself.

contents.textus: 035. ŭ Ṣәlṭā́n Ḥasan aṯi lu+bayto. ‘K̇ače, qay bemaʕd‿at?’ Əmmo, ‘Aḷḷá... aṯi ḥa, aṯi ḥa xortə́k̇ hawxa hno, aṯi. Bi+zoriye ... g̊ʶqoṭalwa u+abrayḏi, mədle u+abrayḏi d̥qo<ṭalle>, noḥaḷḷe lo+ṭreli, maǧbū́r hawyono, ftəḥli u+tarʕo, mbele i+Ǧanǧane, blole.’
contents.versio: 035. And Sultan Hasan came home. ‘Girl, why are you listless?’ She says, ‘By God... along came someone, along came one such guy, he came. Under duress, he would have killed my son, he took my son to ki<ll him>, I didn’t let him slaughter him, I was obliged, I opened the door, he took Janjane, he took her’.

contents.textus: 036. ‘Looo’, omar, omar, ‘ăḷa... mbele, blole, e, blole. Véǧare məs‿sōmno? Ḥa áydarbowa?’ Əmmo, ‘Ḥa hawxa bu+šəklànowa, bu+šəklànowa, i+porik̇ayḏe maqlabto, qḏole yarixo, šafiro, ʕayne kome, šafi<ro>, semoqo, ḥeworo, šafiro’. Omar, ‘ăḷa u+xwarzàyḏiyo, Fənǧā́n Aġayo!’  (19:55)
contents.versio: 036. ‘Nooo’, he says, he says, ‘Gosh, he took her away, he took her away, yes, he took her away. What shall I do this time? How was the one?’ She says, ‘He was one such, he was this type, he was this type, his hair was combed, his neck was long, a handsome one, his eyes were black, a handso<me> one, a ruddy one, a pale one, someone handsome’. He says, ‘Gosh, it is my nephew, it is Finjan Agha!’

contents.textus: 037. Mḥalaqle bəṯ<re>, məḷḷe la+greʕe, omar, ‘Malexu! Mən ḥa d̥kətwa bi+qriṯo’, omar, ‘malexu!’ Malaxxe, maṭən l Fənǧā́n Aġá qmi+qriṯo.
contents.versio: 037. He rushed after <him>, he said to his servants, he says, ‘Go! Whichever one is in the village’, he says, ‘go!’ They went, they reached Finjan Agha in front of the village.

contents.textus: 038. U+ḥolayḏe qrélele, omar, ‘Fənǧā́n Aġá!’, omar, ‘Ha!’, omar, omar, ‘Xwarzo, xāl ŭ xwarz dǝḥḏóḏena. U+aḥuno, u+aḥuno démuxno. Kobaʕno, lawo, lo+quṭlina ḥḏoḏe, ono ŭ hat. Kobaʕno dmarfat i+Ǧanǧane, ŭ izúx. Səmlux d̥quṭlat u+abràyḏistene lə+qṭilux, ŭ səmlux čazawús ʕal i+ḥurmayḏi.
contents.versio: 038. His uncle called him, he says, ‘Finjan Agha!’, he says, ‘Here!’, he says, he says, ‘Nephew, we are each other’s kuncle and nephewk. The brother, I am your mother’s brother. I want, boy, us not to kill each other, you and I. I want you to release Janjane, and go! You fixed to kill even my son, you didn’t kill him, and you raped my wife’.

contents.textus: 039. Kobaʕno, lawo, dmarfatla, dlo+qaṭlo, dlo hat quṭlatli ŭ lo ono qoṭannux. U+xwarzàyḏihat, ḥa ádmona. Səmle ŭ lo+səmle, omar, ‘Ənkā́n layto, ənkā́n layt dlə+mbanna lu+šēx.’
contents.versio: 039. ‘Boy, I want you to release her, without killing, without you killing me and me killing you. You are my nephew, we are one blood’. Whatever he did (lit. ‘he did and he didn’t’), he says, ‘It’s impossible, it’s impossible I wouldn’t bring her to the sheikh’.

contents.textus: 040. Tlaṯ+kore šqile u+darbo d Ăloho mine, mu+zolumano. Šqile u+darbo, u+darbo mine. Omar, ‘Lukwe dobena.’ Liwole, liwole. Mqadámlele l Ṣәlṭā́n Ḥasan hul dmaṭile l Fәnǧā́n Aġá. Qṭile, tloṯo+arbʕo qṭile mənne hul dmaṭi se Fənǧā́n Aġá, Ṣәlṭā́n Ḥasan.
contents.versio: 040. Three times he took the higher road (lit. ‘the road of God’) than him, than this offender. He took the road, the (higher) road than him. He says, ‘It isn’t right that I give her up’. He didn’t give her up, he didn’t give her up. Sultan Hasan approached him until he reached Finjan Agha. He killed, he killed three-four of them until he reached Finjan Agha, Sultan Hasan did.

contents.textus: 041. Maṭi se Fənǧā́n Aġá, omar, ‘Fənǧā́n Aġá!’ Omar, ‘Mənyo?’ Omar, ‘Lawo, kalkaṯinux. Komarfat i+Ǧanǧane, marfiya! Lo+k̬marfatla, kalkaṯinux, g̊šolaḥno qarʕux!’ Omar, ‘Bémənat hat, itúx, bémənat hat!’
contents.versio: 041. He reached Finjan Agha’s spot, he says, ‘Finjan Agha!’ He says, ‘What is it?’ He says, ‘Boy, I am about to come to you. If you’re going to release Janjane, release her! If you’re not going to release her, I am about to come to you, I will cut off your head!’ He says, ‘It’s up to you (lit. ‘you are without obligation’), come, it’s up to you!’

contents.textus: 042. Ḥazna kalá mqabə́l díḏeyo ŭ kəmmole, kəmmole, kodəryo hăwar ʕal u+ʕulmo, kəmmo, ‘Zoxu ʕam Fәnǧā́n Aġá, kalkomaṭi qmi+qriṯo, qṭile, qṭəlle hən tre+tloṯo mə́nnestene ŭ gəquṭli híyestene, zoxu affele.’
contents.versio: 042. Ḥazna is in front of him, and she says to him, she says to him, she cried for help (lit. ‘she cast hăwar, i.e., the call for help’) to the people, she says, ‘Go to Finjan Agha, he has just arrived in front of the village, he has killed, they have killed some two-three of them even and they will kill him too, go to him!’

contents.textus: 043. Noše lo+kuzzè, noše lazzeyo affele (mən makuno rišayxu, qarʕi čik̇e šmənto, mən makuno rišayxu), maṭi‿lbwar d̥ Fənǧā́n Aġá, mədle lu+sayfo, mḥalaqle lqarʕe d̥ Fənǧā́n Aġá. Lu+ḥolayḏe qṭile u+xwarzayḏe. Qṭile.
contents.versio: 043. People do not go, people did not go to him (for what am I giving you a headache, my head a little bit, for what am I giving you a headache), he arrived in front of Finjan Agha, he took his sword, he pounced at the head of Finjan Agha. His uncle killed his nephew. He killed him.

contents.textus: 044. E, u+aḥunayḏe, Xălaf, hánəstene mək‿kosṓm? Ṣәlṭā́n Ḥasan qṭile u+xwarzayḏe, qṭile. Qṭile ŭ mbele u+mede d̥kə́twaste. I+Ǧanǧàneste blole ŭ mede d̥kə́twastene bwar diḏe. Məḷḷe la+gre<ʕe>, omar, ‘Mḥawu, mbálŭle.’
contents.versio: 044. Right, his brother, Halaf, what does he do next (lit. ‘this one too’)? Sultan Hasan killed his nephew, he killed him. He killed him and took whatever there was too. Janjane too, he took her, and also whatever there was in front of him. He said to the serv<ants>, he says, ‘Beat them, take it’.

contents.textus: 045. Mballe. Omar, ‘Hǧamu l ṣəlṭā́n ... lu+šēx daʕ+ʕarab.’ Hǧámmule. Kohuǧmi lu+šēx daʕ+ʕarab, lə+k̬maḥwe. Koḥayri, kalé xalyo. ‘Layk‿azzeyo?’ Əmmi, ‘Lo+kuḏʕina áykoda azzeyo’. Karixi aʕle lo+karixi lə+ḥzalle.
contents.versio: 045. They took it. He says, ‘Attack the Sultan … the Arab sheikh’. They attacked him. They attack the Arab sheikh, he isn’t showing up. They look, here it’s empty (i.e., his house). ‘Where did he go?’ They say, ‘We do not know where he went’. Wherever they went (lit. ‘they went around, they didn’t go around’), they didn’t see him.

contents.textus: 046. Hánəstene Ṣәlṭā́n Ḥasan omar, ‘Mə‿səmxu?’ Omar, ‘Haymén, lə+k̬maḥwe. Be háykoda mahzamle, azzé, mahzamle. I+barṯayḏe kalá larġul, ŭ hiye ŭ i+aṯto lə+k̬maḥwən. Tə+noše lə+k̬maḥwe zowṫə́r mi+barṯo ṗeda’. ‘Hawxa?’ Omar, ‘E.’ Omar, ‘Mə‿kəmmutu, blina i+barṯo lo+blìnala? Mək‿kəmmutu?’ Hən mənne əmmi, ‘Mbala!’, ŭ hən mənne əmmi, ‘ʕÁyboyo, náməsyo, ʕáyboyo, náməsyo, lə+blatla.’ (Hēš əzzí bəṯra, heee?)
contents.versio: 046. As for this one, Sultan Hasan, he says, ‘What did you do?’ He says, ‘I swear, he isn’t showing up. Wherever did he escape to, he went away, he escaped. Here’s his daughter inside, but neither he nor his wife are showing up. Nobody would show up other than (lit. ‘in excess of’) the daughter’. ‘Is it so?’ He says, ‘Yes’. He says, ‘What do you say, shall we take the daughter, or not? What do you say?’ Some of them say, ‘Take her!’, and some of them say, ‘It’s a shame, she is honorable, it’s a shame, she is honorable, do not take her’. (Shall I go on after it, huh?)

contents.textus: 047. Qām hánəstene, daʕiri lu+bayto, lə+blalle, lə+blalle. Xălaf, du+aḥunayḏe d̥ Fənǧā́n Aġá, maṭile u+xabro, əmmi, ‘Haymén lḥolux qṭile Fənǧā́n Aġá.’ ‘Loo!’ Əmmi, ‘Haymén qṭile híyestene ŭ tloṯ+arbʕo+ḥrene.’
contents.versio: 047. Next (lit. ‘this one too’) he got up, they returned home, they didn’t take her, they didn’t take her. Halaf, one of Finjan Agha’s brothers, word reached him, they say, ‘I swear, your uncle killed Finjan Agha’. ‘Nooo!’ They say, ‘I swear, he killed him too and three-four others.’

contents.textus: 048. ‘Hawxa?’ Omar, ‘E.’ ‘Məm‿măsálewa?’ Əmmi, ‘I+măsale háwxawa, ŭ haymén aṯi, mbele i+ǧewaniye, i+Ǧanǧane, blole, ŭ səmle d̥qoṭal u+abro, u+abràyḏastene, lə+qṭile ḥəngi səmla k̇urk̇úr, lə+qṭile, lə+qṭile. Ŭ šqile bi+zoriye u+qliḏo mina, ftəḥle u+tarʕo, mbele i+Ǧanǧane, maṭi qmi+qriṯo. Qṭile l Fənǧā́n Aġástene tre mənne. L Ṣәlṭā́n Ḥasan ŭ alle qṭəlle əšto me Ṣəlṭā́n ... me du+šēx daʕ+ʕarab.’ Kəmmile i+măsàle kula, kəmmile l Xălaf du+aḥunayḏe. ‘Həəə hawxa?’ Əmmi, ‘E.’
contents.versio: 048. ‘Is it so?’ He says, ‘Yes’. ‘What was the issue?’ They say, ‘The issue was such, and I swear he came, he took the filly Janjane, he took her, and he fixed to kill the son, even her son, he didn’t kill him because she yelped, he didn’t kill him, he didn’t kill him. And he took the key from her by force, he opened the door, he took Janjane, he reached the front of the village. Finjan Agha also killed two of them. Ṣәlṭā́n Ḥasan and they killed six of Sultan ... of the Arab sheikh’s’. They tell him the whole issue, they tell to Halaf, one of his brothers. ‘Huh, it’s like so?’ They say, ‘Yes’.

contents.textus: 049. Omar, ‘Tlay!’ Mḥalaqle ʕal u+darbo, rawəx ʕal u+səsyo, hiye ŭ u+greʕayḏe Səllə́k. Səllə́k qaráčiwa, Səllə́k qaráčiwa, u+greʕay<ḏe>, u+greʕo d̥ Xắlafwa, ʕam Xắlafwa, u+greʕo d̥ Xalaf, du+aḥuno d̥ Fənǧā́n Aġá. Hánəstene, kəmḥalqi ʕal i+qriṯo du+šēx daʕ+ʕarab, komoṭən ḥeḏər i+qriṯo, komoṭən lətre+tloṯo+zlamat hawxa xətyark̇at. ‘K̇uro, məm‿măsáleyo, i+măsale?’ ‘Lma‿qṭile aḥuni, lmal‿lə+qṭile aḥuni, ameru di+raṣṭiye, dlo – lo! G̊šolaḥno qarʕe d̥kulxu, ameru di+raṣṭiye’.
contents.versio: 049. He says, ‘Scram!’ He pounced on the road, he rode on the horse, he and his servant Sillik. Sillik was a Garachi, Sillik was a Garachi, his servant, Halaf’s servant, with Halaf, Halaf’s servant, one of Finjan Agha’s brothers. Next (lit. ‘this one too’), they pounce upon the Arab sheikh’s village, they reach the village’s vicinity, they approach two-three men, such oldsters. ‘Boy, what’s the matter, the matter?’ ‘Whoever killed (lit. ‘who killed, who did not kill’) my brother, speak truthfully, if not, then no! I will cut off all of your heads, speak truthfully!’

contents.textus: 050. Əmmi, ‘Ḥayra, ăḷa, i+măsale, ḥāl ŭ măsale haṯe b̥áṯewa: haymén l Fənǧā́n Aġá mṣafele, mṣafele ḥolux ŭ qṭile tre mə́nnestene, ŭ mṭele i+Ǧanǧànestene. Ŭ haymén, u+šēx daʕ+ʕarab tlele ruḥe, mahzamle. Li+barṯo qrela, əmmo, “Toxu!” Əmmo, əmmo, “Toxu affele!” Noše lazzé affele. Haymén, aṯile. Ḥo<lo>, u+ḥolo, lu+ḥolo mə́ḷḷele lu+xwarzayḏe, omar, ‘Ḥayra, lo, lə+k̬baʕno d̥quṭlina ḥḏoḏe’. Səmle ŭ lo+səmle lo+qadər aʕle. Qām lu+ḥolo šləḥle, qṭile, šləḥle qarʕe.’ ‘Hawxa?’ Omar, ‘E.’
contents.versio: 050. They say, ‘Buddy, gosh, the matter, this was the long and the short of it (lit. ‘the state and the matter was this with this’): I swear, Finjan Agha wiped out (lit. ‘cleansed, purified’), he wiped out your uncle and also killed two of them, and he brought back Janjane as well. And I swear the Arab sheikh hid himself, he escaped. His daughter called him, she says, “Come!” She says, she says, “Come after him!” Nobody went after him. I swear, he came to him. Unc<le>, the uncle, the uncle said to his nephew, he says, “Buddy, no, I don’t want us to kill each other”. Whatever he did (lit. ‘he did and he didn’t’), he didn’t prevail upon him. The uncle up and cut him, he killed him, he cut off his head’. ‘Like so?’ He says, ‘Yes.’

contents.textus: 051. ‘U+šēx daʕ+ʕarab lazzé affele?’ Omar, ‘Lo.’ ‘Háykoyo u+bayto du+šēx daʕ+ʕarab, u+bayto du+šēx daʕ+ʕarab?’ ‘Hawheník̇eyo.’ Azzé kalé u+šēx daʕ+ʕarab raġlo ʕal raġlo yatiwo, ŭ kalé larġul.
contents.versio: 051. ‘The Arab sheikh did not go after him?’ He says, ‘No’. ‘Where is the Arab sheikh’s house, the Arab sheikh’s house?’ ‘It is over there’. He went, here’s the Arab sheikh, sitting with his legs crossed, and here he is, inside.

contents.textus: 052. Hánəstene, Xalaf, Xalaf Bag koʕobar komar, ‘Ya šēx!’ Komar, ‘Mənyo?’ Komar, komar, ‘Qay aṯi aḥuni, hawxa səmle, hawxa səmle, hawxa səmle, ŭ, ŭ maqṭelux aḥuni b̥ḥoli. Mən măsáleyo?’ Omar, ‘Lo+mede, lo+səmli mede, ono lo+məḷḷi mede.’ ‘Lo elux ṭləblux i+ǧa... i+ǧanǧane mine?’ Omar, ‘Lo’.
contents.versio: 052. Next, Halaf, Halaf Bey enters, he says, ‘Hey, sheikh!’ He says, ‘What is it?’ He says, he says, ‘Why did my brother come, he did such, he did such, he did such, and, and you made my brother murdered by my uncle. What’s the issue?’ He says, ‘Nothing, I did nothing, I said nothing’. ‘Didn’t you ask him for Janjane?’ He says, ‘No’.

contents.textus: 053. ‘K̇uro, mar! Lə+mdaglat, komaṇṇux, lə+mdaglat, amár elo g̊šolaḥno qarʕux, amár di+raṣṭiye.’ Omar, ‘Lo, lo eli, lo eli mə́ḷḷile.’ I+barṯo me tamo, Ḥazna me tamo əmmo, ‘Ăḷah elux mə́ḷḷuxle! Elux məḷḷux, əmmat, ‘Zux mṭay i+ǧanǧane, gdobenux Ḥazna. Qay ánnaqqa, qay kəmdaglat?’
contents.versio: 053. ‘Boy, speak! Don’t lie, I tell you, don’t lie, speak, else I’ll cut off your head, speak truthfully!’ He says, ‘No, no, it wasn’t me, not me who told him’. His daughter from there, Ḥazna from there says, ‘Gosh, it was you who told him! It was you who told him, saying, “Go, bring back Janjane, I’ll give you Hazna”. Why, now, why are you lying?’

contents.textus: 054. Naqqa ḥəḷḷe Xalaf, ḥəzyole, ínaqqa d̥ḥəzyole, qṭəʕle qarʕe, qṭəʕle qarʕe du+šēx daʕ+ʕarab, du+babayḏa, qṭile. ‘Noše zede, flān bəhvā́n, ǧġīl lə+ǧġīl?’ ‘Lo’, ‘Lə+ǧġīl noše?’ əmmi, ‘Lo.’ Xalaf Aġá malaxle. Malaxle, maṭi lu+ḥədud du+ḥolo. Maṭi lu+ḥədud du+ḥolo, qrele li+aṯto, kəmmo, ‘Koy...’, komar, ‘Koyo ḥoli?’ Əmmo, ‘Kalé larġul. Manhat?’ Omar, ‘Ono hawo dəqṭ<ile>, u+aḥuno tawo dlu+gawrayḏax qṭile. Aḥuni, ŭ aḥuni Fənǧā́n Aġá, ono Xalaf Aġá Bagno. Ono u+aḥuno d̥ Fənǧā́n Aġá dəqṭile’.
contents.versio: 054. Once Halaf saw, he saw her, the moment he saw her, he cut his head off, he cut off the Arab sheikh’s head, her father’s, he killed him. ‘Did anybody else, so and so, speak whatsoever (lit. ‘he spoke, he didn’t speak’)?’ ‘No!’ ‘Nobody spoke?’ They say, ‘No’. Halaf Agha went away. He went away, he reached his uncle’s border. He reached his uncle’s border, he called his wife. She says, ‘Where ...’ he says, ‘Where is my uncle?’ She says, ‘Here he is, inside. Who are you?’ ‘I am the one who kil<led>, the brother of the one whom your husband killed. My brother, and my brother is Finjan Agha, I am Halaf Agha Bey. I am the brother of Finjan Agha, whom he killed’. (27:44)

contents.textus: 055. ‘ṭro nofaq!’ Hánəste konofaq, Ṣәlṭā́n Ḥasan, ‘K̇uro, mə‿kəbʕat?’ Omar, ‘Tux, nfaq, nfaq <li+>m<a>ydane!’ Omar, ‘Xwarzo’. Omar, ‘Ha’, omar, ‘Xwarz, simoli naqqa, lə+g̊sōmna tarte. Lawo, tux, ʕbar, u+xwarzàyḏihat. U+abro d̥ḥóṯihat, lə+k̬baʕno d̥qoṭannux. Kibi qoṭannux’. Omar, ‘Ono komaṇṇux, tux, itúx.’ (28:15)
contents.versio: 055. ‘Let him come out!’ This one comes out, Sultan Hasan, ‘Boy, what do you want?’ He says, ‘Come, come out, come out to <the> squ<a>re!’ He says, ‘Nephew!’ He says, ‘Here!’ He says, ‘Nephew, I did it once, I shan’t do it twice. Boy, come, enter, you are my nephew. You are my sister’s son, I don’t want to kill you. I can kill you’. He says, ‘I am telling you, come, come’.

contents.textus: 056. Mḥalle qəm ḥḏoḏe tre+yawme, səmme ŭ lo+səmme, lḥa lə+qṭile ḥa. Tre+yawme lə+qṭile, ḥa lə+qṭile ḥa. A+tre gabòrene. U+yawmo da+tloṯo mṭele l Ṣәlṭā́n Ḥasan i+ḏarbo aʕ... aʕle dqoṭele. Omar, ‘Xalaf Bag!’. Omar, ‘Ha!’. Omar, ‘Ḥur, lawo, hə, ḥur, kibi qoṭaʕno qarʕux, qoṭannux’.
contents.versio: 056. They struck at each other for two days, whatever they did (lit. ‘they did and they didn’t), one didn’t kill the other. For two days, one didn’t kill the other. The two are champions. On the third day, Sultan Hasan got an opportunity (lit. ‘he reached a strike’) against, against him to kill him. He says, ‘Halaf Bey!’. He says, ‘Here!’. He says, ‘Look, boy, huh, look, I can cut off your head, I can kill you’.

contents.textus: 057.  ‘Lawo, lə+g̊ʶqoṭannux. Simoli naqla, lə+g̊sōmna tarte. Izúx, lawo, bdarbux.’ Omar, ‘Dobatli i+ǧanǧane, gəzzí bdarbi. Dlobátliyo, lo+kəzzì.’ Omar, ‘Xwarz, baḥs di+ǧanǧane lə+mṭat, izúx bdarbux, izúx bdarbux.’ (29:10)
contents.versio: 057. ‘Boy, I don’t want to kill you. I did it once, I’m not going to do it twice. Boy, go on your way.’ He says, ‘If you give me Janjane, I shall go on my way. If you don’t give her to me, I shall not go’. He says, ‘Nephew, don’t bring up the matter of Janjane, go on your way, go on your way’.

contents.textus: 058. Omar, ‘Qṭili u+šēx daʕ+ʕarab, ŭ haymén u+ḥa dməǧġə́lwaste, qoṭáʕwayno qarʕe. Lo+qṭile noše zede kulle, əmmi, “Latlan aḥna latlan suč, kule híyewa”.’ ‘Hawxa?’ Omar, ‘E.’ Omar, ‘Lawo’, omar, ‘Lawo, taw. Ḥur, ḥóluxno, u+greʕàyḏuxno, kobaʕno dyətwat.’
contents.versio: 058. He says, he says, ‘I killed the Arab sheikh, and I swear if someone else had spoken up, I would have cut off his head. I did not kill anybody else, they say, “We don’t have any, we have no fault, it was all him”.’ ‘Like so?’ He says, ‘Yes’. He says, ‘Boy’, he says, ‘Boy, sit down. Look, I am your uncle, I am your servant, I want you to sit down.’

contents.textus: 059. E, Xalaf Aġá kali, kali, kali. Lebo mdiḏe komar, ‘Mḥay ebe’, ŭ lebo mdiḏe komar, ‘Bavo, ḥóliyo, e, haymén lə+g̊ʶqoṭanne’. Omar, ‘Ḥolo!’, omar, ‘Ha!’, Omar, ‘Ḥolo, hawli u+səsyayḏux’. Omar, ‘Mədlux. Mə‿g̊saymat bu+səsyayḏi?’ Omar, ‘Gəzzino gəmṭeno Ḥazna’. Omar, ‘Lawo, taw. Xwarzo, taw. Ḥazna qolayïyo. Qṭi... qṭilux u+šēx daʕ+ʕarab. Rkad̥ ánnaqqa, tlelux ḥayf daḥ... ḥayf daḥunux, ṭray mini.’
contents.versio: 059. Halaf Agha held back, he held back, he held back. One mind (lit. ‘heart’) of his says, ‘Hit him!’, and one mind of his says, ‘My dear, he is my uncle, right, I swear I won’t kill him’. He says, ‘Uncle!’ He says, ‘Here!’ He says, ‘Uncle, give me your horse’. He says, ‘Take it. What are you going to do with my horse?’ He says, ‘I shall go and marry (lit. ‘bring’) Hazna’. He says, ‘Boy, sit down. Nephew, sit down. Hazna’s the least of your worries (lit. ‘she’s easy’). You kill... killed the Arab sheikh. Calm down now, you avenged your brother, leave me alone’.

contents.textus: 060. Omar, ‘U+ḥayf daḥuni, qṭili hawo məḥləf maḥuni. Elo, elo, ḥolo, hăma hawo latyo u+hno, u+hno daḥuni.’ ‘Ohooo’, kohṓz qarʕe Ṣәlṭā́n Ḥasan, kohṓz qarʕe. E, kibe qoṭal u+xwarzayḏe, kibe qoṭal háwostene, lə+g̊ʶqoṭele!
contents.versio: 060. He says, ‘My brother’s revenge, I killed that one in exchange for my brother. But, but, uncle, but that one is not the whatsit, my brother’s whatsit’. ‘Ohoooo’, Sultan Hasan shakes his head, he shakes his head. Yes, he can kill his nephew, he can kill that one too, he is not going to kill him!

contents.textus: 061. Mḥalle, ṭləble šar mine, lo? Ṭləble šar mine. I+aṯto d̥ Ṣәlṭā́n Ḥasan əmmo, ‘Ya Ṣәlṭā́n!’. əmmo, ‘Ha’. əmmo, ‘Ṣәlṭā́n Ḥasan, taw. Kəbʕono dyətwat, kalkazzino dmətwono híyestene’. Omar, ‘Izáx’.
contents.versio: 061. They fought, he asked him for a fight, no? He asked him for a fight. Sultan Hasan’s wife says, ‘Sultan!’ She (i.e. he) says, ‘Here!’ She says, ‘Sultan Hasan, sit down. I want you to sit down, I am about to make him sit down too’. He says, ‘Go’.

contents.textus: 062. Azzayo i+aṯto d̥ Ṣәlṭā́n Ḥasan, əmmo, ‘Xalaf, xwarzo!’ Omar, ‘Taḥolo, mtaxár!’ əmmo, ‘Mṭeli aḥunux, mṭeli b̥qamuṯi Fənǧā́n Aġá, ŭ kəbʕono dlo+moḥatle ḏarbo lḥolux, ŭ lo ḥolux moḥe ḏarbo elux, qoṭelux. Ṭroṯe Ṣәlṭā́n Ḥasan aʕmux, mṭawu Ḥazna. Mbalux Ḥazna’. Omar, ‘Hayde lə+g̊towaṇṇax, taḥolo.’ ‘Ṣәlṭā́n Ḥasan!’, əmmo. ‘Ha!’, əmmo. Omar, ‘Hawx...’. əmmo, ‘Hawxa mə́ḷḷile. Gəzzúx aʕme?’ Omar, ‘Gəzzí.’ Azzeyo.
contents.versio: 062. Sultan Hasan’s wife went out, she says, ‘Halaf, my nephew!’ He says, ‘Aunt, stay back!’ She says, ‘For the sake of (lit. ‘I have brought’) your brother, for the sake of your brother before me, I don’t want you to beat (lit. ‘hit a strike to’) your uncle, or your uncle to beat you, kill you. Let Sultan Hasan come with you, fetch Hazna! Bring back Hazna!’ He says, ‘I won’t break your heart (lit. ‘you’), aunt’. ‘Sultan Hasan!’, she says. ‘Here!’, she (i.e. ‘he’) says. He says, ‘So…’ She says, ‘Thus I said to him. Will you go with him?’ He says, ‘I shall go.’ He went.

contents.textus: 063. Azzé Ṣәlṭā́n Ḥasan aʕme. Omar, ‘Xalaf Bag’. Omar, ‘E, xwarz, e, ḥolo’. Omar, ‘Maláx b̥qamuṯi’. Omar, ‘Looo, áydarbo gmalaxno b̥qamuṯux?’ Omar, ‘Ənkā́n layto, maláx b̥qamuṯi, u+xwarzàyḏihat, maláx b̥qamuṯi.’
contents.versio: 063. Sultan Hasan went with him. He says, ‘Halaf Bey!’ He says, ‘Yes, nephew, yes, uncle!’ He says, ‘Go in front of me’. He says, ‘Nooo, how could I walk in front of you (i.e., due to etiquette)?’ He says, ‘It’s impossible, go in front of me, you are my nephew (i.e. so follow my order), go in front of me’.

contents.textus: 064. Malaxle b̥qamuṯe, maṭi li+qriṯo, u+ʕulmo d̥kətwa bi+qriṯo kulle qayimi me qumayye mi+zuʕ̥ṯo, rabbana. E, qayimi me qumayye, u+abro du+ʕammayḏe d̥ Ṣәlṭā́n Ḥasan, d̥šēx... šēx du+ʕarab. U+šēx kətle abre dʕammo, čīk b̥qamuṯa d̥ Ḥazna.
contents.versio: 064. He walked in front of him, he reached the village, the people that were in the village, all of them got up in front of him out of fear, the poor things. Yes, they got up in front of him,  Sultan Hasan’s (paternal) nephew, the sheikh’s, the Arab sheikh. The sheikh had a nephew, he got in front of Hazna.

contents.textus: 065. Kofəhmat, latyo hawxa? Čīk b̥qamuṯa, koḥōōōr, kalkó ha Ṣәlṭā́n Ḥasan aṯi, u+xwarzayḏe tavda, aṯən l Ḥazna. Omar, ‘Ənkā́n layto dlo qaṭlo, d̚lo qaṭlo ənkā́n layto, noše mofaq Ḥazna mu+baytano’. Hedik̇a l Xalaf, l Xalaf mḥele u+sayfo, u+sayfo ʕal qarʕe, qṭile qarʕe ŭ mbele, maḥatle su+qawro du+aḥuno.
contents.versio: 065. You understand, isn’t it so? He stuck himself in front of her, he sees, hey, here came Sultan Hasan, together with his nephew, they came to Hazna. He says, ‘It’s impossible apart from killing (lit. ‘there isn’t any possibility save murder’), apart from killing it’s impossible, someone ought to get Hazna out of this house!’ Then Halaf, Halaf struck the sword, the sword on his head, he cut off (lit. ‘killed’) his head and took him, he put him on his brother’s grave.

contents.textus: 066. Mbele, maḥatle su+aḥuno. ínaqqa dmaḥatle su+aḥuno, se Fənǧā́n Aġá, Səllə́k (qaráčiwa) omar, omar, ‘Xalaf!’ Omar, ‘Ha!’ Omar, ‘Ăḷá, u+qaputano, g̊šolaḥne maʕle, glowašne’. ‘k̇uro’, omar, ‘de məṯ hat ŭ babe dbabux lo’. Omar, ‘An+noše kuḏʕi d̥qaračhat, kwīš bayto, áydarbo g̥̊šəlḥat u+qaputayḏe mine gəblatle’. Omar, ‘Haymén, čīk lebi bu+qaputano’. Omar, ‘Skat!’, omar, ‘g̊šoqanno ḥa ṭaw mine’.
contents.versio: 066. He took him, he put him beside his brother. When he put him beside his brother, beside Finjan Agha, Sillik (he was a Garachi) says, he says, ‘Halaf!’ He says, ‘Here!’ He says, ‘Gosh, this coat, I shall take it off from him, I shall wear it’. ‘Boy’, he says, ‘screw you and the horse you rode in on (lit. ‘die, you and your father’s father’, i.e. the whole family), what!’ He says, ‘Everybody knows that you are a Garachi, damn you (lit. ‘may the house [of your father] be crushed’), how can you strip his coat off him and take it?’ He says, ‘I swear, I’ve got my heart set on this coat (lit. ‘my heart has stuck itself onto this coat’)’. He says, ‘Shut up!’, he says, ‘I will get you a better one’.

contents.textus: 067. Možadle qmu+aḥuno háwostene. Qṭile u+brazi du+šēx daʕ+ʕarab, hawo d̥čīk b̥qamuṯa d̥ Ḥazna. Qām mədde l Ḥazna, maruxalle ʕal u+səsyo bəṯre Xalaf, ŭ Ṣәlṭā́n Ḥasan komar, ‘Ánnaqqa malexu b̥qamuṯi’. Malaxxe, azzehən se Ṣәlṭā́n Ḥasan, tamo ... L Ṣәlṭā́n Ḥasan qrele lu+mallà ŭ mbaraxle l Ḥazna ʕal Xalaf. Ŭ ṫə sāġ.
contents.versio: 067. He laid that one too out before his brother. He had killed the Arab sheikh’s nephew, that one who got in front of Hazna. They up and took Hazna, they placed her on a horse behind Halaf, and Sultan Hasan says, ‘Now, go in front of me’. They went, they arrived at Sultan Hasan’s, over there ... Sultan Hasan invited the mulla and married Hazna to Halaf. The End (lit. ‘and you be well’ in Kurdish).

contents.textus: 001. Omaṇṇux? Hano u+qadišayḏan Mar Yuḥanǝn, Mar Yuḥánǝnwa. I+qaraqole maḥatla ak+kefayḏa ʕal qarʕe d Mar Yuḥanǝn. Maḥatla ak+kefe ʕal Mar Yuḥanǝn, zəbṭowa nawba.
contents.versio: 001. Shall I tell you? This was our saint Mar Yuhanən, Mar Yuhanən. The military outpost put its blocks upon the roof of Mar Yuhanən. It put the blocks upon Mar Yuhanən, it was keeping watch.

contents.textus: 002. Qām aṯi u+muxtā̀r, qréleli omar, ‘Nəʕman!’ Omaṇṇo, ‘Mənyo?’ Omar, ‘Tux! Kəmmi, maḥatte kefe ʕal u+qadišo, kozəbṭi nawba ʕal u+qadišo, kosaymi pisitiye ʕal u+qadišo. Itúx, zánanne’.
contents.versio: 002. The mayor up and came, he called me, he says, ‘Numan!’ I say, ‘What is it?’ He says, ‘Come! They say they have put blocks on top of the Saint, they are keeping watch on top of the Saint, they are fouling up the Saint on top. Come, let’s go to them’.

contents.textus: 003. Azzano – ono w ḥoli, ono w u+muxtā̀r, azzano lsu+baščawī̀š. Məḷḷan lu+baš, ǝmmina, ‘Qomutā́n, kǝbʕina d… maḥatlux ak+kefani, dǝmḥalqatte’. Omar, ‘Lo+gəmḥalaqnanne’. Lǝ+mḥalqile, lǝ+mḥalqile. Aṯina li+ʕito. Əmmina, ‘Kal kazzán l Asṭǝl, məǧġolina tre+xabre ʕam ḥḏoḏe, aḥna w hat’. W nafiqina.
contents.versio: 003. We went — my uncle and I, the mayor and I, we went to the sergeant-major’s. We said to the sergeant-major, we say, ‘Commander, we want that … you put these blocks, you throw them away’. He says, ‘I shall not throw them away’. He did not throw them away, he did not throw them away. We came to the church. We say, ‘Let’s go to Estel, we shall have words with each other, you and we’. And we went out.

contents.textus: 004. ʕAbirina li+dərto du+qadišo, u+muxtā̀r omar, ‘Kwīš bayto dbabux! Ma lmənhat? Ma míṯohat? Ma mənhat?’ Bdele ebe bi+dərto.
contents.versio: 004. We entered the saint’s courtyard, the mayor said, ‘God damn you! What are you up to? Are you a dead man? What are you?’ He went off on him in the courtyard.

contents.textus: 005. Qām hawi ʕam nhoroṯe. Naqqa lu+qadišawo Mar Yuḥanǝn mədle ʕaskar du+nobačì. Mədle lu+ʕaskarawo, mi+anišk̇e di+gorayo mḥalaqle, xud dǝmḥalqat ltāmhe. Mḥalaqle ltamhenik̇é u+ʕaskar, mḥalaqle ltamo.
contents.versio: 005. It started at dawn. All at once that saint, Mar Yuhanən, took a soldier of the watch. He took that soldier, he threw him from the corner of that roof, as you would throw something aside. Over there he threw the soldier, he threw him there.

contents.textus: 006. Noše bări mini lazzeyo, azzí ono qamayto aʕle. Ono siporčíwayno, roháṭwayno marke, mḥaláqwayno raġli ltamhenik̇é, roháṭwayno. Azzino ʕal riše, kal komigambal, twīr qarʕe, mpalpax qarʕe, w ʕayne tavda w druʕone. Maqlabli hawxa, hneli, w aṯi ḥreno, ṭayo mʕawalleli.
contents.versio: 006. No one went before me, I was the first to go to him. I was an athlete, I used to run from here, I would throw my leg over there, I used to run. I came up to him, here he is rolling around, his head was broken, his head was shattered, and his eyes, and his arms were altogether shattered. I turned him over like so, I whatsited, and another one came, a Muslim helped me.

contents.textus: 007. Ḥəḷḷan, kalé gmōṯ. Aṯyo i+ṭayara, i+ʕalikòptere, aṯyo, mədde, mḥalaqqe li+ʕalikòptere w māṯ. Māṯ, mballe lu+bayto du+babayḏe. U+qadišayḏan Mar Yuḥanǝn háwxayo. Hawxa bi+dùkṯoyo.
contents.versio: 007. We looked, here he is about to die. A plane, a helicopter came, it came, they took him, they threw him into the helicopter, and he died. He died, they took him to the house of his father. Our Saint Mor Yuhanən is like this! He is like so in his place!

contents.textus: 008. Šqilan sʕore, eli w Nadimo w lu+Galle d Be+Barṣo, Ăloho mḥasele. U+Galle d Be+Barṣo zlām ṭáwwowa, Ăloho mḥasele. Azzano, šqilan sʕore. Əmmina, ‘Gəblínanne l Mar Yuḥanǝn’. Kətwa … u+braxwàyḏiwa, ḥoṯi i+kalàyḏewa, u+Ḥanna, Muqsi Ḥanna d Be+Mado, əmmíwayle Muqsi Ḥanna, d Be+Mado. Omar, ‘Ḥayra, lǝ+blutu a+sʕoraṯxu l Mar Yuḥanǝn, lə+gmaqbal’.
contents.versio: 008. We bought barley, Nadimo and I, and Galle from the Barṣo family, may God rest his soul. Galle of the Barṣo family was a good man, may God rest his soul. We went, we bought barley. We say, ‘Let us bring it to Mar Yuhanən’. There was … he was my in-law, my sister was his daughter-in-law, Hanna, Hanna the Pilgrim from the Mado family, we called him Hanna the Pilgrim, from the Mado family. He said, ‘Buddies, do not take your barley to Mar Yuhanən, he won’t accept’.

contents.textus: 009. U+Nadimo omar, ‘waḷḷáh K_am ê bǝbǝn_K, Ălah gǝblinanne’. Qām mballe, qrelan ltre+ṭaye, ʕAzizo kəmmile, w Ṭáhǝro.
contents.versio: 009. Nadimo said, ‘By God, we will take, we will take it!’ They up and took it, we summoned two Muslims, they call him ʕAzizo, and Tahiro.

contents.textus: 010. Húlanne kallawat ḥaq dəṯṯe w maṭʕanne ak+kise, azzano. Ínaqqa dazzano su+qadišo, u+qadišo hǧə́mlelan. Ele w šawʕo+ḥrene, tmányowayne, baš+šurat, bas+sayfe, hǧə́mmallan.
contents.versio: 010. We gave them the money, their wages, and they loaded up the sacks, we went. When we came to the Saint, the Saint attacked us. He and seven others, there were eight of them, with sabres, with swords, they attacked us.

contents.textus: 011. Hǧə́mmallan, mahzamlan. Mḥalaqqe ak+kise, l Ṭáhəro w l ʕAzizo mḥalaqqe ak+kise, w l Nadimo mahzamle. Nadímoste ṭáyowa, mahzamle háwostene. Mahzamle l Nadimo, ono hedi hedi aṯino, omaṇṇo, ‘Ḥayra, Ăḷah, lə+gmaǧrina’. As+sayfaṯṯe, kul sayfo kə́pwayle haqqask̇e biḏoṯayye, xurxur dəṯṯe. W mahzamlan’.
contents.versio: 011. They attacked us, we ran away. They threw the sacks away, Tahəro and Azizo threw the sacks away, and Nadimo ran away. Nadimo was also a Muslim, he also ran away. Nadimo ran away, and I came back slowly. I say, ‘Buddies, by God, we will not dare. Their swords, every sword was this big in their hands, their snarl. And we ran away’.

contents.textus: 012. Aṯina lu+bayto. Qām u+Ḥaǧi, u+šuferàyḏanwa, u+Ḥaǧi omar, ‘K_Lawo waki wǝlo ya,_K waki háwxayo, lawo, lǝ+blutǝnne ltamo, ḥētne harke, bi+odaṯe’. Qām u+Muqsi, omar, ‘Ma lo+məḷḷǝlxu?’ Muqsi Ḥanna, ‘Lo+məḷḷǝlxu? Məḷḷi, lǝ+blūtne, lo+gmaqbal Mar Yuḥanǝn. Mar Yuḥanǝn lǝ+gmaqbal ṫaʕada. Ḥētne bi+odaṯe’. Qām maḥtilan bi+odayo. Hawxa səmle Mar Yuḥanǝn eban, lo+ṭrele dmaḥtina a+sʕorayḏan ebe.
contents.versio: 012. We came home. The Hajji, he was our driver, the Hajji up and says, ‘Guys, if it is like this, in case the matter is like so, guys, do not take them there, put them here, in this room’. The Pilgrim says, ‘Haven’t I told you?’ Ḥanna the Pilgrim, ‘Haven’t I told you? I told you, do not take them, Mar Yuhanən will not accept it. Mar Yuhanən will not accept transgression. Put them in this room’. We up and put them in this room. Mar Yuhanən did so to us, he did not allow us to put our barley in it.

contents.textus: 001. Kətwa šulṭono. Măsale omáṇṇanxu?
contents.versio: 001. There was a sultan. Shall I tell you a story?

contents.textus: 002. Kətwa šulṭono. Hiye w u+wazirayḏe azzehən li+šuqo. (B̥ ṣurayt omaṇṇo, lo?) Azzehən li+šuqo darwešī́n. Lwəšše ǧule qṭiʕe, maḥ+ḥuṭe qṭiʕe aǧ+ǧulaṯṯe. W azzehən li+šuqo.
contents.versio: 002. There was a sultan. He and his vizier went to the market (I shall tell it in Surayt, no?). They went to the market as dervishes. They put on torn clothes, their clothes were made out of torn threads. And they went to the market.

contents.textus: 003. Konuḥti. Dukkano, kalá dukkano xliṯo, mede layt eba. W kalé manqlo qume yatiwo ʕal u+kursiyayḏe.
contents.versio: 003. They went down. A shop, here is an empty shop, there is nothing in it. And here is a brazier in front of someone seated on his chair.

contents.textus: 004. Komar u+šulṭono … xud darwešī́n … hǝnnǝk lo+kuḏʕi dkətyo šulṭono w u+waziro, lo+kuḏʕi. Kǝmmi, ‘Darwēšne, faqírene. Ǧule qṭíʕene aʕlayye’.
contents.versio: 004. The sultan says … like dervishes … they did not know that it was a sultan and his vizier, they did not know. They say, ‘These are dervishes, beggars. There are torn clothes upon them’.

contents.textus: 005. Qām hánostene koʕubri, kəmmi, ‘Qayyo layt mede bi+dukkano, i+dukkano xlíṯoyo?’ ‘E, — komar, — kəmzabanno ʕaql, kəmzabanno ʕaql’. — ‘E, u+ʕaql áydarboyo?’ — Omar, ‘U+xabro blira. U+xabro blira’.
contents.versio: 005. Thereupon they enter, they say, ‘Why is it there is nothing in the shop, the shop is empty?’ ‘Yes, — he says, — I am selling advice, I am selling advice’ – ‘Yes, advice … how?’ He says, ‘One lira per piece of advice. One lira per advice’.

contents.textus: 006. Omar, ‘U+xabro blira?’ Omar, ‘E’. Omar, ‘Amár!’ Omar, ‘Mōṯ u+issā̀n dsōm i+qamayto lo+mətfakar bi+ḥarayto. Mōṯ. Ṭro mōṯ hawo!’
contents.versio: 006. He says, ‘One lira per saying?’ – He says, ‘Yes!’ – He says, ‘Speak!’ He says, ‘The man who does not consider the end when he does the beginning shall die. He shall die. Let that one die!’

contents.textus: 007. U+waziro omar, ‘Qəm, qəm, qəm! Omaṇṇo be mən ʕaql gdobelan’. U+šulṭono omar, ‘Maláx, lawo, ono fahəmno. Maláx!’ Malaxxe, malaxxe. Azzehən.
contents.versio: 007. The vizier says, ‘Come on, come on, come on. I shall say what kind of wisdom he is giving us!’ The sultan says, ‘Go, boy, I have understood, go!’ They went, they went, they left.

contents.textus: 008. Omar, ‘Zux, amaḷḷe lu+barbar’ — u+šulṭono komaḷḷe lu+waziro, omar, ‘Amaḷḷe lu+barbar, ṭroṯe ḥolaqli!’
contents.versio: 008. He says, ‘Go, tell the barber’ — the sultan says to the vizier, he says, ‘Tell the barber, he ought to come shave me’.

contents.textus: 009. Azzé u+waziro, komaḷḷe lu+barbar, komar, ‘Barbar!’ Komar, ‘Ha!’ Komar, ‘Itúx w ḥlaq u+šulṭono’. Omar, ‘Msamám i+muse, msamema w ḥlaqe! Hiye gmōṯ, ono ktoweno bdukṯe šulṭono w ksōmno hat waziro bdukṯi!’
contents.versio: 009. The vizier went, he says to the barber, ‘Barber!’ He says, ‘Here!’ He says, ‘Go and shave the sultan’. He says, ‘Poison the razor, poison it and shave him! He will die, I will become sultan in his place and make you vizier in my place!’

contents.textus: 010. Omar, ‘Mu+lebo?’ Omar, ‘E!’ Omar, ‘Təmā́m’.
contents.versio: 010. He says, ‘Sincerely?’ He says, ‘Yes!’ He says, ‘Fine!’

contents.textus: 011. Qayəm, msamamle i+məssine, msammole. W mədle li+čalṭayḏe w malaxle.
contents.versio: 011. He up and poisoned the pitcher, he poisoned it. And he took his bag and he went.

contents.textus: 012. Malaxle, aṯi. Aṯi, koḥōr, kalkó lu+šulṭònoste məssəmle?! Kṯule lu+šulṭono, kṯule b̥feme du+tarʕo, ‘Mōṯ u+issā̀n dsōm i+qamayto, lo+mətfakar bi+ḥarayto. Mōṯ u+issā̀n dsōm i+qamayto, lo+mətfakar bi+ḥarayto’. Kṯule larġul kuuule, kṯule.
contents.versio: 012. He went, he came. He came, he sees: what has the sultan just done?! The sultan wrote, he wrote on the doorframe, ‘The man who does not consider the end when he does the beginning shall die. The man who does not consider the end when he does the beginning shall die’. He wrote it everywhere inside, he wrote it.

contents.textus: 013. U+barbar koḥōr… (ánnaqqa maṣiṯu, hátustene maṣiṯu w hatste maṣə́ṯ). Koḥōr: kal kṯuuule kuuule.
contents.versio: 013. The barber looks (now listen carefully, you (pl.) too listen and you (sg.) listen as well!). He looks: he has just written it everywhere!

contents.textus: 014. U+barbar, u+barbar omar, ‘Aḷḷa laybi msamamne. Yawo, qoṭeli, laybi’.
contents.versio: 014. The barber says, ‘By God, I cannot poison him. For goodness’ sake, he would kill me, I cannot’.

contents.textus: 015. Qām ḥləqle. Ḥləqle, mədle li+muse, maḥtole, məḷḷe, ‘Laybi, quṭlili’. Maḥtole.
contents.versio: 015. He up and shaved him. He shaved him, he took the razor, he put it back. He said, ‘I cannot, they would kill me’. He put it back.

contents.textus: 016. Hiya … ʕáynayo bəṯra, bəṯra ʕáynayo. Koḥozela bi+ʕayna, koḥoze, omar, ‘Qay lə+ mədlux... lə+gmaydat li+musayo? Muda, ḥlaqli payo. Qay lo+kḥulqatli payo?’
contents.versio: 016. It … it is a mirror behind it. Behind it, it is a mirror. He sees it in the mirror, he sees, he says, ‘Why did not you take .. why don’t you take that razor? Take it, shave me with that one! Why don’t you shave me with that one?’

contents.textus: 017. Omar, ‘Lə+gʕawdo hayo, ḥarútoyo. Haṯe ṭawtəryo. Haṯe ʕawədtəryo’. ‘Hawxa?’ Omar, ‘E’.
contents.versio: 017. He says, ‘That one doesn’t work, it is broken. This one is better. This is sharper’. ‘Is that so?’ He says, ‘Yes’.

contents.textus: 018. Omar, ‘Ḥlaq!’ Ḥləqle. Omar, ‘Barbar!’ Omar, ‘Ha!’ Omar, ‘Lawo, gdomaṇṇux xabro, amár di+raṣṭiye’. Omar, ‘Mənyo?’ Omar, ‘Amár, qay mədlux li+musayo, maḥtolux w mədlux li+ḥreto? Amaḷḷi’.
contents.versio: 018. He says: ‘Shave me!’ He shaved him. He says, ‘Barber!’ He says, ‘Here!’ He says, ‘Boy, I will say something to you, speak truthfully’. He says: ‘What is it?’ He says, ‘Say, why did you take that razor, put it back and take the other one? Tell me!’

contents.textus: 019. Omar, ‘Ya u+šulṭonayḏi, Aḷḷah, mə́ḷḷeli lu+waziro, omar, omar, ‘Ḥlaqli … ḥlaqe w msamema. Hiye gmōṯ, ono ktoweno bdukṯe šulṭono, w ksōmnux hat waziro bdukṯi’.
contents.versio: 019. He says, ‘Oh my sultan, by God, the vizier told me, he says, he says, “Shave me … shave him and poison it. He will die, I will become sultan in his place and make you vizier in my place”’.

contents.textus: 020. ‘Hawxa mə́ḷḷelux?’ Omar, ‘E’. Omar, ‘Zux qrayle!’ Aḥmad w ʕAli, ʕAli w Aḥmad azzehən bəṯre. Aḥmad w ʕAli a+greʕàyḏene.
contents.versio: 020. ‘He said so to you?’ He says, ‘Yes’. He says, ‘Go call him!’ Aḥmad and ʕAli, ʕAli and Aḥmad went after him. Aḥmad and ʕAli are his servants.

contents.textus: 021. Azzə́n bəṯre, mṭalle u+barbar … Aḷḷah … u+waziro. ‘Waziro!’ Omar, ‘Ha!’ Omar, ‘Lawo, qayyo məḷḷux, “Msamám i+muse, kḥolaqne … ḥlaqe, hiye gmōṯ, ono ktoweno bdukṯe šulṭono w ksōmno hat waziro?”’
contents.versio: 021. They went for him, they brought the barber … by God … the vizier. ‘Vizier!’ He says, ‘Here!’ He says, ‘Boy, why did you say, “Poison the razor, I will shave him … shave him, he will die, I will become sultan in his place and make you vizier”?’

contents.textus: 022. ‘Qay gdəmmatle, lawo? Məssəmli ebux? Ṭreli lebux yawmo?’ Omar, ‘Lo’. ‘Mḥélilux?’ ‘Lo’. ‘Məssəmli ebux, dkəzzúx kəmmatle hawxa?’ Omar, ‘Lo+məḷḷi’. U+barbar omar, ‘Aḷḷah məḷḷux!’
contents.versio: 022. ‘Why would you have told him, boy? What have I done to you? Did I upset you some day?’ He says, ‘No’. ‘Have I beaten you?’ ‘No’. ‘What have I done to you that you would go tell him so?’ He says, ‘I didn’t say it’. The barber says, ‘By God, you said it’.

contents.textus: 023. U+barbar omar, ‘Aḷḷa məḷḷux, lo+kəmdagalno, Aḷḷa məḷḷux’. ‘Ema mǝḷḷi?’ Omar, ‘Aḷḷa, məḷḷux’.
contents.versio: 023. The barber says, ‘By God, you said it, I am not lying, by God, you said it’. ‘When did I say it?’ He says, ‘By God, you said it!’

contents.textus: 024. U+šulṭono omar, ‘Məḷḷux. Dləmmatwa, lə+gmarwa. Məḷḷux’.
contents.versio: 024. The sultan says, ‘You said it. If you had not said it, he would not have spoken. You said it’.

contents.textus: 025. ‘Aḥmad w ʕAli’, omar, ‘Zoxu, ftaḥu i+qalto’. Ftəḥḥe i+qalto w maḥatte u+waziro bi+qalto, zrəʕʕe.
contents.versio: 025. ‘Aḥmad and ʕAli’, he says, ‘Go, make an opening in the dunghill’. They made an opening in the dunghill and put the vizier in the dunghill, they planted him.

contents.textus: 026. Maḥatte bi+qalto u+waziro w mṭele, qrele lu ... kətle kalbo məṣro. Kətle kalbo məṣro daywono. Omar, ‘Zoxu, marféwule!’ Marfalle u+kalbo w šlǝḥle, xile aḏne, qṭile.
contents.versio: 026. They put the vizier into the dunghill, and he brought, he called the… he has a dog tied up. He has a mad dog tied up. He says, ‘Go, release him!’ They released the dog and he ripped off (and) ate his ears, he killed him.

contents.textus: 027. Qṭile u+waziro, lu+kalbo qṭile. Ínaqqa dəqṭile, lu+šulṭono omar, ‘Barbar!’ Omar, ‘Ha!’ Omar, ‘Lawo, ḥaláq as+sefoqe, hat hway u+wazirayḏi’.
contents.versio: 027. He killed the vizier, the dog killed him. Once he had killed him, the sultan says, ‘Barber!’ He says, ‘Here!’ He says, ‘Boy, toss the instruments and become my vizier’.

contents.textus: 028. Omar, ‘Hat hway waziro bdukṯe, hat hway waziro’. Qṭile hawo, səmle u+barbar waziro rruḥe. Omar, ‘Təmā́m’.
contents.versio: 028. He said, ‘You become vizier in his place, you become vizier’. He killed that one, he made the barber vizier for himself. He says, ‘Fine’.

contents.textus: 029. Omar, ‘Barbar!’ Omar, ‘Ha!’ Omar, ‘Maláx, zano li+šuqo, ḥozina be məkkit bi+šuqo, be məllayt bi+šuqo. Zan ḥozina, ḥozina bi+šuqo, məkkit, məllayt’.
contents.versio: 029. He said, ‘Barber!’ He says, ‘Here!’ He says, ‘Go, let us go to the market, let’s see what’s in the market, what’s not in the market. Let’s go see, let’s see in the market, what there is, what there isn’t’.

contents.textus: 030. Omar, ‘Maláx’. Omar, ‘Šlaḥ aǧ+ǧulani, šlaḥ aǧ+ǧulani, lwaš ǧule ʕatiqe. W ónoste glowašno ǧule ʕatiqe, w gnuḥtina gəzzano’.
contents.versio: 030. He says, ‘Go’. He says, ‘Take off these clothes, take off these clothes, put on old clothes. And I too will put on old clothes, and we will go down, we will go’.

contents.textus: 031. Azzehən, naḥiti li+šuqo. Koḥayri bi+šuqo: kalá i+šuqo sakná, kalá noše me noše lǝ+gmǝǧġǝl w noše baḥs dnoše lo+kǝmṭe, kosaymi kul ḥa u+bēʕ w u+bazaraṯṯe.
contents.versio: 031. They went, they went down to the market. They view the market: hey, the market is peaceful. Hey, people are not chatting about people, people are not bringing people’s gossip, everyone is doing their selling and bargaining.

contents.textus: 032. U+šulṭono omar, ‘Waziro!’ Omar, ‘Ha!’ Məḷḷe, komaḷḷe lu+barbar, omar, ‘Waziro!’ Omar, ‘Ha!’ Omar, ‘Waziro, haymén, i+šuqo naḏ̣ə́ftoyo, mede layt bi+šuqo. U+teḥriwo di+šuqaṯe kula u+waziràwowa, hawo dəqṭilan. Kulle hawo sōmwa aḥ+ḥarḥašunatani’.
contents.versio: 032.
