The sultan says, ‘Vizier!’ He says, ‘Here!’ He said, he says to the barber, he says, ‘Vizier!’ He says, ‘Here!’ He says, ‘Vizier, believe it, the market is clean, there is nothing to do in the market. The whole of this market’s corruption was that vizier, that one whom we killed. These provocations, that one was doing all of them’.

contents.textus: 033. Omar, ‘Ya u+waziro!’ Omar, ‘Ha!’ Omar, ‘Hul dkətno sāġ gmaqweno aq+qawetiyayḏi ʕal ann+abnàyḏistene, tark didux lǝgbǝn. Towat hat waziro, hul dkətna sāġ, towat waziro hat’. Səmle hawo waziro rruḥe.
contents.versio: 033. He says, ‘Oh vizier!’ He says, ‘Here!’ He says, ‘As long as I am alive I shall enforce my orders upon my sons as well, they will not give you your dismissal. You shall be vizier, as long as we are alive, you shall be vizier’. He made that one vizier for himself.

contents.textus: 001. Kətwa … kətwa təǧǧā́r, kətwa təǧǧā́r. U+təǧǧarano kul+naqla mbalwa arbʕi+baġle. Gamle, gamle hawxa, gamle, ḥaṣayye ha háwxayo, gámlene.
contents.versio: 001. There once was a merchant, there once was a merchant. This merchant would always take forty mules. Camels, camels like so, camels, their back is like this, they are camels.

contents.textus: 002. Kǝmballe me Diyā́r+Bakər, kǝmballe lǝ Gziro, kəmballe lǝGziro. Komaṭʕan aṭ+ṭaʕnayḏe me Diyā́r+Bakər, kəzzé lǝ Gziro … ann+arbʕi+ṭaʕnayḏe … hul dkomoṭe lǝ Gziro. Kobe laf+faqire, kobe lu+ʕulmo. U+ḥa dkoloqele, kobele parčaye.
contents.versio: 002. He brings them from Diyabakər, he brings them to Gziro, he brings them to Gziro. He loads up the loads from Diyarbakər, he goes to Gziro … his forty loads … until he reaches Gziro. He gives to the poor, he gives to people. Everyone who meets him, he gives him a portion.

contents.textus: 003. Kobe kul+naqla, kobe gāh təšʕo+ṭaʕne, gāh tmanyo, gāh təšʕo, gāh ʕaṣro kobe.
contents.versio: 003. Every time he gives, sometimes nine loads, sometimes eight, sometimes he gives ten.

contents.textus: 004. U+zlamano masule. Masule, azzé bann+əšne. Qām u+abro ḥəḷḷe ebe, hawxa ḥəḷḷe lu+abro ebe. Omar, ‘Yabo!’ Omar, ‘Ha?’ Omar, ‘Yabo, aǧ+ǧenik̇atayḏux ḥawiri. Yabo, ʕaršux hánostene šlīḥ ḥa mənne. Yabo, kobaʕno dyətwat, ono ksōmno məḥlofux i+taǧǧaraṯe. Ono ksōmna məḥlofux’.
contents.versio: 004. The merchant grew old. He grew old, he advanced in years. His son up and looked at him, the son looked at him like so. He says, ‘Daddy!’ He says, ‘Huh?’ He says, ‘Daddy, your temples have turned white! Daddy, your tooth, this one, one of them has gone away. Daddy, I want you to settle down, I shall handle the business in your place. I shall do it in your place’.

contents.textus: 005. Omar, ‘Lawo, ma gdəḏʕat saymat xoṯi?’ Omar, ‘E, yabo, e’. Omar, ‘Dəḏʕat, gdobenux. Lo – lo, lə+gbenux, lawo. Ono dkəzzino lǝ Gziro, kobeno kul+naqla təšʕo+ʕaṣro+ṭaʕne lan+noše faqire, xēr diḏi, kobenanne laf+faqire’. Omar, ‘Tǝmā́m, yabo, ahla w sahla’.
contents.versio: 005. He says, ‘Boy, will you know to do it like me?’ He says, ‘Yes, Daddy, yes’. He says, ‘If you know, I will give it to you. If not — then no, I will not give it to you, boy. When I go to Gziro, every time I give nineten loads to the poor, my good deed, I give them to the poor. He says, ‘Fine, Daddy, you are welcome’.

contents.textus: 006. Qām hánostene, u+təǧǧarànostene, maslamle u+qliḏo lu+abro. Lu+abro mədle lu+qliḏo w qrele la+greʕayḏe, maṭʕanne arbʕi+ṭaʕne, maṭəʕnənne. U+zʕurano maṭi lǝ Gziro, hule traḥṣar+ṭaʕne, hule traḥṣar. Fāšle tmanyo w ʕəsri+ṭaʕne.
contents.versio: 006. So this one, the merchant, up and handed over the key to his son. The son took the key and called his servants, they loaded forty loads, they loaded them. The young man came to Gziro, he gave away twelve loads, he gave away twelve. Twenty eight loads were left for him.

contents.textus: 007. Omar, ‘Ḥetu aṭ+ṭaʕnaṯxu harke. Gəzzino ḥōrno, gəzzino ḥōrno bi … kalá baxča basəmto, be haṯe mǝn báxčayo? Kal kazzí li+baxčaṯe, ḥozina, mək kīt eba, bi+baxčaṯe’.
contents.versio: 007. He says, ‘Put down your loads here. I shall go and look, I shall go and look in the … here’s a pleasant garden, what kind of garden is this? I am going to go to this garden, we shall see what is in it, in this garden’.

contents.textus: 008. U+zʕurànoste koʕobar, komaḥti a+greʕe aṭ+ṭaʕne, w hiye kəzzé li+baxča. Koḥōr, kalá biro dmaye, kalá biro dmaye. I+biràyostene, koḥōr bam+maye ḥewore, basime.
contents.versio: 008. The young man enters, his servants place the loads, and he goes to the garden. He sees, here’s a water well, here’s a water well. So this well, he is looking into clear and pleasant water.

contents.textus: 009. Omar, ‘Haymén kšoteno maye mi+biraṯe’. Híyestene, u+rabban, koṭowe qarʕe hawxa, dšote, – e, i+lappe ʕul me qarʕe komaḥwo. Komaḥwo lappe ʕul me qarʕe, iḏo ʕul me qarʕe, dmaḥtile, dmaḥti qarʕe bi+birayo.
contents.versio: 009. He says, ‘I shall surely drink water from this well’. So this one, poor fellow, bends his head down like so to drink, – yeah, a paw appears above his head. A paw appears above his head, a hand above his head, to put it, to put his head into the well.

contents.textus: 010. Koḥōr hawxa ḥeḏǝr ruḥe, koḥōr, noše lə+kḥoze. Pāk hano məʕ ʕaǧóboyo! Naqqa+ḥreto ṭwele qarʕe. Ṭwele naqqa+ḥreto disa, disa mḥele i+lappe dmoḥela. Maʕlele qarʕe, koḥōr, noše lə+kḥoze. Omar, ‘Ala lə+kšoteno’.
contents.versio: 010. He looks around himself like so, he looks around, he does not see anyone. Wow, this is so strange! He bent his head down once more. He bent his head down once more again, again he hit him with the paw that strikes him. He raised his head, he looks, he does not see anyone. He says, ‘By God, I shall not drink’.

contents.textus: 011. Nafəq qǝm feme du+tarʕo, koḥōr: kalé sofi bfeme du+tarʕo. Hiye bḥəšbone du+kurko ǧǝnnániyo, ‘Ǧǝnnániyo’, u+kurrəkano, ‘ǧənnániyo’. Komar, ‘Qay lə+štelux maye?’ Omar, ‘Haymén lə+šteli maye, w ṭweli qarʕi tarte+kore, ṭweli qarʕi dšoteno, da+tlaṯ lo+maǧreli. Lo+maǧreli dsōmnanne tlaṯ+kore. Nafəqno’.
contents.versio: 011. He went out through the doorway, he sees: here’s a derwish in the doorway. He is, in the opinion of the boy, a gardener. ‘It’s a gardener’, this boy (thinks), ‘it’s a gardener’. He says, ‘Why didn’t you drink some water?’ He says, ‘I surely did not drink any water, and I bent my head down two times, I bent my head down to drink, for the third time I did not dare. I did not dare to do it three times. I went out’.

contents.textus: 012. Omar, ‘Ono u+mšadro d Alóhono, malóxono. Ono u+mšadro d Alóhono, malóxono’. ‘Ánnaqqa kšuqlat ruḥi?’ Omar, ‘Lo’. Omar, ‘Lǝ+kšoqalno ruḥux’. Omar, ‘Zux, štay, amár əšme dǝṣlibo w štay. Dray u+ṣlibayḏux ʕal foṯux w štay’.
contents.versio: 012. He says, ‘I am God’s messenger, I am an angel, I am God’s messenger, I am an angel’. ‘Now then, are you going to take my soul?’ He says, ‘No’. He says, ‘I am not going to take your soul’. He says, ‘Go drink! Say “the name of the Cross” and drink. Make a cross on your face and drink’.

contents.textus: 013. W drele u+ṣlibayḏe ʕal foṯe w štele. Štele. Omar, ‘Maṭʕenu aṭ+ṭaʕnaṯxu’. Maṭʕanne aṭ+ṭaʕnaṯṯe, blile lǝ Gziro. (Lu+sofiyawo kə́twayle daqno hawxa, hno sófiyo.) Azzehən lǝ Gziro, naḥiti, azzehən gab u+xānči. Məḷḷe lu+xānči, omar, ‘Xānči!’ Omar, ‘Ha?’ Omar, ‘U+zʕurano u+abro dəflānkasyo. Lu+babo mšāʕle u+zʕurano. Kobaʕno, ʕayni xǝd u+babo, dhowatle moro, dhowatle moro lu+malayḏe w i+dukṯo, u+babayḏe dǝmḥalafwa u+māl. Be ayko mḥalafwayle kobaʕno dmaḥwatle ad+dukkananək, w dəzzeyo lad+dukkananək mḥalaf u+malayḏe. Omar, ‘Tǝmā́m’.
contents.versio: 013. So he made a cross on his face and drank. He says, ‘Load up your loads’. They loaded their loads, he brought them to Gziro. (The dervish, he had a beard like so, it is a dervish whatsit). They went to Gziro, they went down, they went to an innkeeper. He said to the innkeeper, he says, ‘Innkeeper!’ He says, ‘Huh?’ He says, ‘This young man is the son of so and so. His father has sent the young man. I want you to take charge of him, just like his father, to take charge of his property and the place, his father who used to exchange property. Wherever he used to exchange, I want you to show him those shops, so that he goes to those shops to exchange his property. He says, ‘Fine’.

contents.textus: 014. Qām məḷḷele, omar, ‘Ono kal kazzino. Šamiʕat?’ Komaḷḷe lu+zʕuro, komar, ‘Ono kal kazzino. I+numro ḥṣar, i+numro ḥṣar. Itúx lu+baytawo. Li+numro dkətyo ḥṣar.’ Omar, ‘Tǝmā́m’.
contents.versio: 014. He up and said, he says, ‘I am going to go. You heard it?’ He says to the young man, he says, ‘I am going to go. Number 10, Number 10. Go to that house. To Number 10’. He says, ‘Fine’.

contents.textus: 015. Hawyo i+saʕa ḥṣar, azzé li+numro da+ḥṣar, koḥōr, kalá ḥurma w zlām. U+zlām, i+daḥṯo kǝmḥalqo b̥foṯe, kodoʕaṯ. U+kurk̇o koʕobar, ‘Šlomo’. Komar, ‘Ahla w sahla!’ Komar li+ḥurma, komar, ‘Qǝm hawle fako dlaḥmo w mofeqe. Ṭro nofaq’.
contents.versio: 015. It was ten o’clock, he went to Number 10, he looks, here’s a woman and a man. The man, his sweat is pouring down his face, he is sweating. The boy enters, ‘Hello!’ He says, ‘Welcome!’ He says to his wife, he says, ‘Go give him a piece of bread and send him away. He should go away’.

contents.textus: 016. Kəmmo, ‘Kwīš bayto dbabux. Kalúx miṯo! Áydarbo gdoballe fako dmuklo, gməfqalle? Hăma ḏayfo ḏayfo d Alóhoyo, ṭro yotaw larġul’. Omar, ‘Lǝkwe’ – omar, ‘D̥fōš harke, gmōṯno’. Hawxa omar, e. Qām u+zʕurano, nafəq. Mofaqla li+žənk̇e, mabramla hawxa … oda … maḥatla tamo bi+odayo, ǝmmo, ‘De dmax harke, dmax harke. Məs saymono?’ Daməx tamo.
contents.versio: 016. She says, ‘Damn you! Here you are, a dead man walking! How am I going to give him a bit to eat and send him away? A guest is a guest from God, after all, let him stay inside’. He says, ‘No way!’ He says, ‘If he stays here, I will die’. He says like so, yes. The boy up and left. The woman brought him out, she brought him around like so … a room… she placed him there in the room, she says, ‘Sleep here, sleep here. What shall I do?’ He slept there.

contents.textus: 017. Aṯi u+malaxo, omar, ‘Qǝm!’ Məḷḷe lu+kurk̇o omar, ‘Qǝm!’ Qām aṯi, fatili, aṯən su+zlamawo u+naxwaš, dkətwa kayiwo. Omar, ‘Ḥur, mə ksōmno bi+ruḥayḏe!’ Mḥele bam+maḏrabat, šqile i+ruḥayḏe, šqile i+ruḥayḏe. Mḥalaqqe li+bemresaye, li+pisitiye, mḥalaqla b̥feme w bǝnḥire mi+bemresayayḏe. Omar, ‘Lawo, u+ḏayfo – u+ḏayfo d Alóhowa. Hawxa səmlux bu+zʕurano’.
contents.versio: 017. The angel came, he says, ‘Get up!’ He said to the boy, he says, ‘Get up!’ He up and came, they went around, they came to that sick man who was ill. He says, ‘See, what I will do with his soul!’ He struck him with mallets, he took out his soul, he took out his soul. The foulness, the filthiness lept, it lept through his mouth and his nose, because of his foulness. He says, ‘Boy, the guest was a guest from God. You treated this young man like so’.

contents.textus: 018. Axər šqile i+ruḥayḏe, nafiqi tre+ǧewǝrk̇at dak+kalbe bǝnḥire. Tre+ǧewǝrk̇at dkalbe nafiqi bǝnḥire, kome bemrés. Omar, ‘Tǝmā́m’.
contents.versio: 018. Finally he took out his soul, two dogs’ whelps came through his nose. Two dogs’ whelps came through his nose, black, dirty. He says, ‘Fine’.

contents.textus: 019. Omar, ‘Ramḥəl i+numro ḥḏaḥṣar i+saʕa ba+ḥḏaḥṣar tux ltamo’. Omar, ‘Tǝmā́m’. Azzé i+numro ḥḏaḥṣar, hawi dēr du+lalyo, i+saʕa hawyo ḥḏaḥṣar, azzé li+numro ḥḏaḥṣar, koḥōr, kalayo žənk̇e kal komkafro i+daḥṯo du+merk̇o. W komarle lu+merk̇o, komar, ‘Šlomo’. Komar, ‘Ahla w sahla! Ḥurma!’ ‘Ha?’ — Omar, ‘Qǝm hawle fako dmuklo. Hawle fako dmuklo w hawle nvine, ṭro domax bi+odayhenik̇é’. Əmmo, ‘Merk̇o, kalé … harke i+oda, kalá xliṯo, ṭro domax tamhenik̇é’. Omar, ‘Lo, hawle nvine w ṭro domax bi+odayo, w tǝmā́m’. Əmmo, ‘Ḥayra, tǝmā́m!’
contents.versio: 019. He says, ‘Tomorrow Number 11, at 11 o’clock, come there’. He says, ‘Fine’. He went to Number 11, it became the next night, it turned 11 o’clock. He went to Number 11, he sees, here’s a woman, she is wiping off the sweat of her husband. He says to the man, ‘Hello!’ He says, ‘Welcome! Wife!’ — ‘Huh?’ — He says, ‘Go and bring him a bit to eat. Give him a bit to eat and give him a bed, let him sleep in that room over there’. She says, ‘Husband, here’s … here is a room, here’s an empty one, let him sleep over there’. He says, ‘No! Give him a bed and let him sleep in that room, and that’s it’ She says, ‘My dear, fine!’

contents.textus: 020. Mbela, azzé u+kurk̇o. Mbela li+žənk̇e, əmmo, ‘De dmax harke, lawo!’ Daməx tamo. Daməx tamo, hawyo i+saʕa ḥḏaḥṣar. Aṯi, aṯi u+maloxo. Aṯi u+maloxo, omar, ‘Qǝm’.
contents.versio: 020. She took him, the boy went. The wife took him, she says, ‘Sleep here, boy!’ He slept there. He slept there, it turned 11 o’clock. There came, there came the angel. The angel came, he says, ‘Get up!’

contents.textus: 021. Mərle lu+merk̇o, omar, ‘Tux, ḥur!’ Aṯi. Hulele dabbūz, nṣəfle me ḥḏoḏe, lu+maloxo mtaḥte raġle šqile i+ruḥayḏe. Nafiqo ḥḏo k̇avok̇e, ḥḏo, ḥḏo. Nafǝq ǧewǝrk̇o dkalbo. (Háṯeste i+maʕnáyoste, gdomáṇṇanxuyo. Gdomaṇṇux háyostene.)
contents.versio: 021. He says to the husband, ‘Come, take a look!’ He came. He hit him with a mace, he shook him altogether, out from under his feet the angel took his soul. A dove came out, a single one. A dog’s whelp came out. (This is the meaning, I will tell it to you. I will tell you this too.)

contents.textus: 022. Qām omar, ‘De tux, i+saʕa ba+traḥṣar, itúx li+numro traḥṣar, tux ltamo!’ Omar, ‘Tǝmā́m’. (Heš əzzí bəṯra? Omaṇṇo? - E, e. Mdawám, amár!)
contents.versio: 022. He up and says, ‘Come, at twelve o’clock go to Number 12, go there! He says, ‘Fine!’(Shall I still go after it? Shall I tell it? - Yes, yes, continue, tell!)

contents.textus: 023. Qām hánostene … kuyo i+numro traḥṣar … koṯe. Komar, ‘Qǝm!’ Aṯi, yatu gabe, yatu gabe. I+naqqa dyatu gabe, omar, ‘Ḥur áydarbo kšoqaṇṇo i+ruḥo du+zlamano’. Omar, ‘Ahla ahla ahla bu+mšadro d Aloho, ahla. Tux tux tux tux’. — komaḷḷe lu+maloxo.
contents.versio: 023. This one up and … it turns Number 12 … comes. He says, ‘Get up!’ He came, he sat beside him, he sat beside him. When he sat beside him, he says, ‘Look how I will take out the soul of this man’. He says, ‘Welcome, welcome, welcome to the messenger of God, welcome! Come, come, come, come!’ — he tells the angel.

contents.textus: 024. Hánoste, u+maloxo, koyotaw qǝm raġle du+zlamawo, u+kùrk̇oste kalé tamo yatiwo. Košṓf raġle, košṓf raġle, kogoraš i+ruḥayḏe lbarke. Maṭyo lbarke, košṓf barke, u+maloxawo košōf barke, hul dmaṭyo lṣadre, larke diḏe. Maṭyo hul ṣadre.
contents.versio: 024. As for that one, the angel, he is sitting in front of that man’s feet, and as for the boy, here he is, sitting there. He massages his feet, massages his feet, he pulls his soul to his knees. Having reached his knees, he massages his knees, that angel massages his knees, until it reached his chest, to his ‘over here’. It reached up to his chest.

contents.textus: 025. Maṭyo lṣadre, omar, ‘Ḥur áydarbo košoqanno i+ruḥayḏe, košoqanno’ …’Ahla …’ … Maṭyo i+ruḥo larke. Disa komar, ‘Ahla, ahla bu+mšadro d Aloho’.
contents.versio: 025. It reached his chest, he says, ‘Look how I am taking his soul, I am taking …’ – ‘Welcome…’ The soul reached up to here. Once again he says, ‘Welcome, welcome to the messenger of God!’

contents.textus: 026. Qām hedik̇a, maṭyo llarke diḏe, šqile i+ruḥayḏe. Nafiqi tarte+k̇avok̇at ḥewore əmmi pərrr... Azzə́n, yatiwi se Mšiḥo. Maġalle lat+tarte+k̇avok̇atanǝk se Mšiḥo, s Aloho. Azzə́n s Aloho at+tarte+k̇avok̇atanǝk.
contents.versio: 026. Then it up and reached to his over here, he took out his soul. Two white doves came out, cooing. They went away, they sat beside Christ. The two doves penned beside Christ, beside God. Those two doves went up to God.

contents.textus: 027. Omar gdomannanxu, ḥuru komar, ‘U+issā́n, dhowe ṭawwo, dhowe mʕadlo, dhowe … w dḥowe aḏ+ḏayfe, dobe xēr w xeratat, – hawo, i+ruḥayḏe hawxa gməšqolo, basəmto gməšqolo.
contents.versio: 027. He says, ‘I will tell you, look.’ He says, ‘The man who is good, who is proper, who is… who hosts guests and gives charity and alms, – that one, his soul is taken out like so, it is taken out in a pleasant way.

contents.textus: 028. U+ issā́n, dhowe qasī́s, dhowe pīs, dlo+ḥowe aḏ+ḏayfe, – hawo, háwoste, kowele čike idara.
contents.versio: 028. And a man who is stingy, who is wicked, who does not host guests, that one, as for that one, he will have to manage a bit.

contents.textus: 029. Hăma u+ḥreno, dḏayfe dlo+ḥowe, dlobe xēr w xeratat, dhowe ganowo, dhowe ṭalǝb ḥărā́m, dhowe ṭalǝb ḥărā́m, dhowe pīs, dhowe pīs bi+briṯaṯe, dhowe hawxa pīs, hawo malkuṯo lukwe dḥoze. Gmiḥalaq li+koraye di+gihano. Koraye di+gihano gmiḥalaq.
contents.versio: 029. But the other one, who does not host guests, who does not give charity and alms, who is a thief, who is a crime seeker, who is a crime seeker, who is wicked, who is bad in this world, who is wicked like so, it is not for that one to see the Kingdom. He will be cast into the depths of Gehenna. Into the depths of Gehenna will he be cast.

contents.textus: 030. W hun sāġ!
contents.versio: 030. And you be well!

contents.textus: 001. YT. Əšmi Yusuf Turker, Maqsi Alyas. I+familayḏan kəmmila Maqsi Alyas. Bu+suryoyo Maqsi Alyas kəmmila. ʕUmri əno ḥamšaḥsar dat+təšʕo alfo ŭ čaʕmo arbaʕ ŭ əšti. Mawladno b Məḏyaḏ, e.  Əno hawino b Məḏyaḏ, e.
contents.versio: 001. My name is Yusef Turker, Maqsi Alyas. Our family name is Maqsi Alyas. In Syriac they call it Maqsi Alyas. My age is September 15, 1964. I was engendered in Midyat, right. I was born in Midyat, right.

contents.textus: 002. SL. Ayko koʕayšat aġlab?
contents.versio: 002. Where do you live mostly?

contents.textus: 003. YT. Əno harke b Məḏyaḏ kʕāšno.
contents.versio: 003. I live here in Midyat.

contents.textus: 004. SL. Ayko ʕayišat?
contents.versio: 004. Where have you lived?

contents.textus: 005. YT. Harke ʕayəšno, b Məḏyaḏ. Dáyima hárkeno, hárkeno, b Mə́ḏyaḏno, b Mə́ḏyaḏno.  U+baytayḏi bi+walàyeyo. E, mínaqqa dhawino hárkeno, bas azzino naqqawoṯo l Awrupa ŭ daʕəṇṇo, hayo rišo, kul+naqqa yarḥo, tre, bas harke b Mə́ḏyaḏno.
contents.versio: 005. I lived here, in Midyat. I’m always here, I’m here, in Midyat, in Midyat. My house is in the city. Right, since I was born, I’m here, but I went a few times to Europe and came back, that time was a visit, each time a month, two, but I am here in Midyat.

contents.textus: 006. I+ṣənʕayḏi meqəm ḥalóqowi, ḥaloqo du+sawko, e, qyoṣo du+sawko, e, ḥaloqo. Kə́twoli dəkkano bi+šuqo, bi+šuqo d Məḏyaḏ. Uʕdo haw kḥəlaqno, aḥuni támoyo. Molafli aḥuni, ŭ aḥúniste uʕdo bi+dəkkano kḥoləq, ḥalóqoyo.
contents.versio: 006. My profession formerly, I was a barber, a hair barber, hair cutting, right, a barber. I had a shop in the market, in the market of Midyat. Now I don’t cut hair anymore, my brother is there. I taught my brother, and my brother too does the hair-cutting now in the shop, he is a barber.

contents.textus: 007. Əno ʕumri tmone+əšnè bdeli biya, ʕawodo, yaʕni ʕawodo bdəkkano xəd̥‿ṣanəʕ̥, kəmmínale bu+məḏyoyo ṣanəʕ̥. ʕWədli, ŭ bəṯr edi, bat+tarte ŭ tmoni ftə́ḥlili dəkkano lruḥi,  ŭ hōōōl la+tralfo ŭ tloṯ, i+dəkkano, əno maʕwádnowola. Mat+tarte ŭ tmoni hol, disa, hol la+tralfo ŭ tloṯ əno maʕwádnowola, bəṯr ma+tralfo ŭ tloṯ əno ṭreli mena, molafli aḥuni. Kle aḥuni uʕdo bi+dəkkano kʕowəd̥, hēš ḥaloqo b Məḏyaḏ, e.
contents.versio: 007. When I was eight years old, I began with it, working, that is to say, working in the shop as an apprentice, we call him a ṣanəʕ̥ (‘apprentice’) in Midyatian. I worked, and after then, in 1982, I opened a shop for myself, and until 2003, the shop, I was managing it. Since 1982 until, once more, until 2003 I was managing it, after 2003 I left it, I taught my brother. See, my brother now works in the shop, he is still a barber in Midyat, right.

contents.textus: 008. Yaʕni kibux dəmmət tleṯi ḥḏo+tleṯi+əšne ʕwədli bi+ḥleqa, ḥaloqo, ḥaloqo. Bu+suryoyo kṯobonoyo kmalle garoʕo. B Məḏyaḏ, i+ǧġaliyayḏan, kəmmínale ḥaloqo. Ḥaloqo yaʕni kʶqoyəṣ u+sawko, qayoṣo du+sawko, qayoṣo du+sawko.
contents.versio: 008. That is, you can say 31, 30 years I worked in hair cutting, a barber, a barber. In Classical Syriac they call it garoʕo. In Midyat, our dialect, we call it a ḥaloqo. A ḥaloqo, meaning he cuts the hair, hair-cutting, hair-cutting.

contents.textus: 009. SL. Azzúx li+ʕaskariye?
contents.versio: 009. Did you go to the military?

contents.textus: 010. YT. Azzí li+ʕaskariye, e. Azzí tmonaḥṣar+yarḥe li+ʕaskariye. Bann+arbaʕ ŭ tmoni bu+yarḥo da+tloṯo azzano li+ʕaskariye, azzano qamayto l Amaṣya  ŭ tamo səmlan ʕaǧamtiye kəmmínala, tloṯo+yarḥe molúffallan. Tloṯo+yarḥe u+šəkl du+eʔitī̀m,  d̥kəmmile. Yaʕni, durošo, áydarbo u+sˤlaḥ, yaʕni, tfənge kmimodo, di+nawbe, ŭ kul+mede. Tloṯo+yarḥe səmlan ʕaǧamtiye kəmmínala.
contents.versio: 010. I went to the military, yes. I went for eighteen months to the military. In the year 1984, in the third month we went to the military, first we went to Amasya and there we did what we call ‘boot camp’, they taught us for three months. Three months is a kind of basic training, as they call it. That is, the instruction, how the weapon, like, the rifle is handled, about guard duty, and everything. Three months we did what we call ‘boot camp’.

contents.textus: 011. Bəṯr ma+tloṯo+yarḥè azzino l Ṭaṭwan, e, Ṭaṭwan Bitlis, fayəšno tamo ḥamšaḥsar+yarḥe. Bas tamo ḥalóqowi, naqqa+ḥreto, ḥaloqo, dar+rabe, di+ʕaskariye, dar+rabe, yaʕni, kəmmila sidayna daḏ+ḏəbbā̀ṭ, yaʕni, d̥kətne bi+rutbe, ʕloye, day+yuzbašiye ŭ dab+binbiyašiye, əno ḥaloqo d̥ánəkwi, latwi di+ʕaskar.
contents.versio: 011. After three months I went to Tatwan, right, Tatwan Bitlis, I stayed there fifteen months.  But there I was a barber, once again, a barber, of the senior officers, of the military, of the senior officers, like, they call this among us ‘of the officers’, like, of those who are at the rank, the high ones, of the captains and of the majors, I was the barber of those ones, not the soldiers.

contents.textus: 012. Ḥaloqo. Kə́twoli, huwánwoli odaye naʕəmto, huwánwoli odaye, qlayto naʕəmto, kíbowa kul+mede. Fayəšno tamo ḥamšaḥsar+yarḥe ḥaloqo dar+rabe di+ʕaskariye, ŭ hol daṯino, e.
contents.versio: 012. A barber. I had, they had given me a small room, they had given me a room, a little cell, everything was in it. I stayed a senior officers barber there for fifteen months, and even until I came back, right.

contents.textus: 013. Ŭ bəṯr edi aṯino mi+ʕaskariye naqqa+ḥreto, edi gawərno bann+alfo ŭ čaʕmo ḥamməš ŭ tmoni … baš+šeṯ ŭ tmoni bu+yarḥo da+tre gawərno, ŭ ftəḥli naqqa+ḥreto i+dəkkanayḏi di+ḥleqa, ŭ hol la+tralfo tloṯ ŭno ʕəwádnowo biya, ŭ uʕdo həwoli laḥuni, kle tamo huwe kḥoləq.
contents.versio: 013. And after then I came back from the military once again, then I married in 1985 …  in 1986 in the second month I got married, and once again I opened my barber shop, and until 2003 I had been working in it, and now I have given it to my brother, see, he does the hair-cutting there.

contents.textus: 014. Ŭ bəṯr ma+tralfo ŭ tloṯ edi hawino kəmmínala bi+hayye di+ʕito, bu+mawətbo  daʕ+ʕitawoṯo d Məḏyaḏ, ŭ səmli rišoyuṯo baʕ+ʕitawoṯo ba+tralfo ŭ tloṯ, la+tralfo ŭ tmone ŭno rišo di+hayye d Mə́ḏyaḏwi, ŭ uʕdo da+treno, mʕadrono,  da+treno. Naqqa+ḥreto uʕdo kḥanno laʕ+ʕitawoṯo ŭ lad+dayre d Məḏyaḏ.
contents.versio: 014. And after 2003, then I started in the Church Council, as we call it, in the Midyat churches session, and I made the first rank in the churches in 2003, until 2008 I was the president of the Council of Midyat, now I am the deputy, Helper, the deputy. Now once more I supervise the churches and the monasteries of Midyat.

contents.textus: 015. GD: Li ʕaskariyē byuzbašiyan=ra an binbašiyan=ra, b̥qomutanan=ra, yani čawa darbas bû, zaḥmat bū an hasanī bû?  (Bi+ʕaskariye, ʕam ay+yuzbašiye aw ʕam a+binbašiye aw ʕam aq+qomutane, yaʕni, aydarbo fayito? Zaḥmewa aw basəmtowa?)
contents.versio: 015. In the military, with Captains, Majors, or Commanders, like, how did it go (lit. ‘pass’)? Was it difficult or was it easy?

contents.textus: 016. YT: Lo, əno lăǧăni latwa zaḥme, əno məd̥‿kətwi ḥaloqo, əno məd̥‿kətwi ḥaloqo day+yuzbašiye ŭ dab+binbašiye. Latwa zaḥme, yaʕni, latwa awqask̇e yaqərto aʕli, latwa yaquro, ánnaqqa dəmmina yaquro. Hawxa lawi, hawxa hno aʕli. Əno, məd̥‿kətwi tamo ḥaloqo, bas əno, dukṯi ġắlăbe basə́mtowa,  ŭ mede lə+sàmnowa bas mi+ḥleqa.
contents.versio: 016. No, for me it wasn’t difficult, for me since I was a barber, for me since I was a barber to Captains and Majors. It wasn’t difficult, like, it was not so hard for me, it was not hard, so to speak hard. It wasn’t so, such a whatsit for me. For me, since I was a barber there, only me, my place was very pleasant, and I didn’t do anything except hair-cutting.

contents.textus: 017. B̥ṣafro bi+saʕa ba+tmone əzzínowo li+dəkkanayḏi, tamo ʕayni bgawe di … du+bənyono, bgawe du+bənyònowe, lə+nfàqnowo larwal. Hənne uṯanwo, maydiwo meni saʕa, ayna saʕa gdoṯən. Lu+goranawo dəweno xalyo, əmmánowolən, əṯanwo ŭ ḥəláqnowolən bu+šəklano. Əno dukṯi ġalabe basə́mtowa bi+ʕaskariye.
contents.versio: 017. At 8AM I would go to my shop, there inside the same … building, it was inside the building, I didn’t go outside. They would come, they would take from me a time, what time they would come. Depending on whether I were free then (lit. ‘according to that [time], if I were free’), I would tell them, they would come back and I would cut their hair in this way.  For me, my place was very pleasant in the military.

contents.textus: 018. SL. Azzúx li+madrašto?
contents.versio: 018. Did you go to school (lit. ‘parochial school’)?

contents.textus: 019. YT. Azzino li+madrašto, e, du+tərki, du+tərki. Harke kito madrašto. Ínaqqa daṯitu ḥəzyulxu kmalle Mehmetçik, e, tMehmetçik İlkokult ínaqlayo, uʕdo hawi, hawi <ortaokul>, e.
contents.versio: 019. I went to school, yes, the Turkish one, the Turkish one. There’s a school here. When you came, you saw it, they call it Mehmetçik, right, the Mehmetçik Primary School at that time, now it has become, it has become <a secondary school>, yeah.

contents.textus: 020. AL. I+madrašto di+ḥkume?
contents.versio: 020. Is it a public school?

contents.textus: 021. YT. Di+ḥkume, azzino ḥamməš+əšne. Bas azzino …  əzzánowo li+madràštoste du+suryoyo. Aḥna baʕ+ʕitawoṯo, kul+yàwmoste əzzánowo laʕ+ʕitawoṯo yulfínawo suryoyo, úʕdoste hēš kito hawxa. Ŭ azzí li+dayro du+Zaḥfarā̀n, qreli bi+dayro du+Zaḥfarā̀nstene. Tloṯ+əšne tamo bi+dayro du+Zaḥfarā̀nstene, bu+qayṭo‿zzánowo, yalfina suryoyo, kṯawto, qraye, kul+mede támostene.
contents.versio: 021. Yes, public, I went for five years. But I went … we also used to go to the Syriac parochial school. Those of us in the churches, every day we would go to the churches to learn Syriac, even now it is still like so. And I went to Deyrüzzaferân, I studied at Deyrüzzaferân as well. Three years there at Deyrüzzaferân monastery as well, we would go in the summer, we learned Syriac, writing, reading, everything there as well.

contents.textus: 022. AL. Azzúx lat+tarte+madrăsā̀t?
contents.versio: 022. Did you go to both schools (lit. ‘both church schools’)?

contents.textus: 023. YT. E, du+suryoyo maǧbū́r kəzzánola. Úʕdoste, madrašto du+suryoyo dyəlfina i+qraye, i+kṯawto du+suryoyo, ŭ a+ṣlawoṯo ŭ aʕ+ʕadat di+mšiḥuṯayḏan, ŭ aʕ+ʕadat di+suryoyuṯayḏan, dyəlfinala. Úʕdostene kətlan tarte+madrašyoṯo, tarte+madrăsā̀t. Bu+suryoyo, bu+məḏyoyo kəmmínalle madrăsā́t. Kətlan uʕdo tarte, hēš kʕūdi bu+šəklano. At+tarte+ʕitawoṯo, kətlan ḥḏo b̰‿ Mor Bar Ṣawmo, ŭ kətlan ḥḏo b̰‿ Mor Šarbel, madrašto.
contents.versio: 023. Yes, the Syriac one, we have to go to it. Now too, the Syriac school is for us to learn to read, Syriac writing, and the prayers and rites of our Christianity, and rites of our Syriac tradition, for us to learn it. Now as well we have two schools, two parochial schools. In Syriac, in Midyatian, we call them madrasas. Now we have two, they still work in this way. The two churches, we have one in [the Church of] Mor Barsawmo, and we have one in Mor Sharbel [Monastery].

contents.textus: 024. SL. Əšmo dbabux mənyo?
contents.versio: 024. What is your father’s name?

contents.textus: 025. YT. Əšme dbabi Šabo. Babi sāmwo farmo, fə́rnači, farmo, sāmwo laḥmo. Sāmwo laḥmo babi, e. ʕAmawo, áḥnaste ʕawdínawo aʕme blalyo. Kə́twolan farmo. Huwe naʕimo, ʕumre traḥsar+əšne, bdele bu+farmo. Bəṯr, e, b Məḏyaḏ, laḥmo, farmo du+laḥmo.  Sāmwo laḥmo, kə́twolan farmo, blalyo ŭ́noste‿zzánowo, mʕawnínawole, ŭno ŭ emi, kullayna, áḥnoni, mʕawnínawole.
contents.versio: 025. My father’s name is Shabo. My father ran a bakery (lit., bread oven), a baker, a bakery, he would make bread. My father would make bread, yeah. Moreover (lit. ‘with that’), we also would labor with him at night. We had a bakery. He, a little boy, twelve years old, he started with the bakery Later, yeah, in Midyat, bread, bakery. He would make bread, we had a bakery, at night I also would go, we would help him, my mother and I, all of us, my brothers, we would help him.

contents.textus: 026. Ínaqlayo latwo makinā́t du+lyošo, kul+mede bi+iḏowe, kul+mede bi+iḏowe. Ŭ kətwo … sāmwo u+laḥmo, saymínawo muklone bgawe du+farmo, saymínawo múkloste, mzabnínawo bgawe du+farmo. Meqəm harke latwo loqanṭā́ṭ ġắlăbe duxalwo u+ʕamo. Uṯanwo maq+qəryawoṯo, maq+qəryawoṯo, ham daṣ+ṣuroye, ham daṭ+ṭaye, ham da+mḥalmoye, da+mḥalmoye, hani dəkməǧġoli bʕárabi. Uṯanwo l Məḏyaḏ ŭ uxliwo bu+farmo, ŭ šuqliwo laḥmo, ŭ uxliwo múkloste bgawe du+farmo. E, səmle farmo babi, ʕəwadwo bu+farmo.
contents.versio: 026. At that time there were no kneading machines, everything was by hand, everything was by hand. And there was … He would make the bread, we also made food inside the bakery, we would also make food, we would sell it inside the bakery. Formerly, there weren’t many restaurants here for people to eat. They would come from the villages, from the villages, both the Christian ones, and the Muslim ones, and also the Mhallami ones, the Mhallami ones, those who speak Arabic. They would come to Midyat and eat at the bakery, and they they would buy bread, and they would eat food as well inside the bakery. Yeah, my father ran a bakery, he labored in a bakery.

contents.textus: 027. AL. Ayna lišone oḏaʕwa babux?
contents.versio: 027. Which languages did your father know?

contents.textus: 028. YT. Babi əḏaʕwo húweste arbʕo+lišone, məǧġalwo tərki, ʕárabi, k̇urmanǧí, ŭ suryoyo. Uʕdo áḥnaste ʕayni mede <hē>š kməǧġlina. Aḥna, lišonayna suryóyoyo, məd̥‿kito bgawe di+wălaye, yaʕni d̥kito bgawə‿d Məḏyaḏ, kito k̇urmā́nǧ, kito suryoye, ŭ kito mḥalmoye dəkməǧġoli bʕárabi, ŭ kito tərk, am+mamū̀r d̥kətne tərk, hənne latne <m>harke, bas harke d̥kətne xəd‿əmmina xəd‿ap+puweləṣ, xd‿a+hno, kməǧġəlina u+lišonàwostene. Yaʕni, kito uʕdo harke b Məḏyaḏ kmitəǧġəl arbʕo+lišone, arbʕo+lišone kmitəǧġəl b Məḏyaḏ.
contents.versio: 028. My father, he also knew four languages, he spoke Turkish, Arabic, Kurdish, and Turoyo. Now we also still speak in the same way. We, our language is Turoyo, since there are inside the city, like, there are inside Midyat, there are Kurds, there are Syriacs, and there are Mhallami who speak Arabic, and there are Turks, the government employees who are Turks, they are not (from) here, but here the ones who are, let’s say, like the police, like the whatsits, we speak that language as well. Like, there’s now here in Midyat, people speak four languages, people speak four languages in Midyat.

contents.textus: 029. AL. Əšme demux mənyo?
contents.versio: 029. What is your mother’s name?

contents.textus: 030. YT. Əšme demi Sṫire, Sṫire. Híyastene məǧġəlowa bas tloṯo+lišone, tərki ləḏʕowa, elo lo+qralle madrăsā́t du+tərki, mketəb du+tərki lə+qrèwola, ləḏʕowa tərki. Bas məǧġəlowa ʕárabi, suryoyo, ŭ kurmanǧí, e, ʕam aǧ+ǧiranayḏa.
contents.versio: 030. My mother’s name is Stire. She spoke only three languages, she did not know Turkish, since they did not study in the Turkish (church) schools, she had not studied in the Turkish (public) schools, she did not know Turkish. But she spoke Arabic, Turoyo, and Kurmaji, yes, with her neighbours.

contents.textus: 031. Elo harke aṭ+ṭayayḏan aʕ+ʕatiqe d Məḏyaḏ kməǧġoli hə́nneste suryoyo, məd yalifi mənayna suryoyo, elo aḥna harke meqəm áḥnawan zyude b Məḏyaḏ, yaʕni, bam+mo ḥamšo+ŭ təšʕi, təšʕo+ŭ təšʕi, aḥna am+məḏyoye d Mə́ḏyaḏwan, as+suryoye b Məḏyaḏ, zyúdewan, zəd̥ṫə́r maṭ+ṭàyewan.
contents.versio: 031. But here our elderly Midyatian Muslims, they also speak Turoyo, since they learned Turoyo from us, but earlier we were the majority here, in Midyat, like, 95-99 percent, we were the inhabitants of Midyat, the Syriacs of Midyat, we were the majority, we were more numerous than the Muslims.

contents.textus: 032. Maǧbū́r aṭ+ṭayyàyḏanste yalifiwo suryoyo, məǧġəliwo aʕmayna suryoyo. Elo ínaqqa dəzzánowo la+mketəb du+tərki, yani li+madrăse du+tərki, ínaqqa dəzzánowo, kətwo tkul+ṣənəft kəmmínale, yaʕni ckul+ṣədro,c tṣənəf,t kətwo ḥa+tre+ṭaye, a+ḥrene kulle suryóyewən.
contents.versio: 032. Our Muslims also would have to learn Turoyo, they would speak Turoyo with us. But when we went to Turkish schools, like, to the Turkish schools, when we went, every tclassroomt we call it, like, each cstudy hall,c tclassroom,t had one or two Muslims, the others were all Syriacs.

contents.textus: 033. Mawxa aṭ+ṭayàyḏanste yalifiwo suryoyo mənayna ġắlăbe ǧġaliye. E, uʕdo an+naʕimayḏan, ánnaqqa barimo, yaʕni, fayišo diḏan kul+tṣənəft ḥa+suryoyo, ŭ a+ḥrene ṭaye. Ánnaqqa an+naʕimàyḏanste klən kyəlfi k̇urmanǧí mənayye.
contents.versio: 033. For this reason, our Muslims also used to learn to speak Turoyo from us a lot. Right, now our children, now it’s flipped, like, of ours it stayed one Syriac every classroom, and the others are Muslims. Now then, our children too, here they are, learning Kurdish from them.

contents.textus: 034. AL. Ayko hawi babux?
contents.versio: 034. Where was your father born?

contents.textus: 035. YT. Babi b Məḏyaḏ hawi.
contents.versio: 035. My father was born in Midyat.

contents.textus: 036. AL. Ayko hawyo emux?
contents.versio: 036. Where was your mother born?

contents.textus: 037. YT. Harke b Məḏyaḏ, e.
contents.versio: 037. Here, in Midyat, right.

contents.textus: 038. AL. Əšme dǧəddux mənyo?
contents.versio: 038. What is your (paternal) grandfather’s name?

contents.textus: 039. Əšmə‿dǧəddi Sléymanyo, Sleyman, əšmə‿d̥qašti Sə́ṫṫowa, Səṫṫo. Əšmə‿d̥qašti, i+emo dbabi, əšma Sə́ṫṫowa. Əšmə‿demi Sṫire, bas əšmə‿d̥qašti, di+emo dbabi, Sə́ṫṫowa, əšmə‿dǧə́ddistene Sléymanwe.
contents.versio: 039. My grandfather’s name is Sleyman, Sleyman, my grandmother’s name was Sitte, Sitte. My grandmother’s name, my father’s mother, her name was Sitto. My mother’s name is Stire, but my grandmother’s name, my father’s mother’s, was Sitto, as for my grandfather’s name, it was Sleyman.

contents.textus: 040. AL. Ayko hawi ǧəddux?
contents.versio: 040. Where was your grandfather born?

contents.textus: 041. Ǧəddi b Məḏyaḏ hawi, aḥna məḏyóyena, məḏyóyena, kulle b Məḏyaḏ hawən. Ǧə́ddiste, ǧə́ddistene b Məḏyaḏ. Ayna ǧəddi, u+ḥreno, u+babo demi?  U+babo demi, ǧəddi u+ḥreno, əšme Ályasyo, u+babo demi. Əšme di+emo Zérowa, Zérowa. Hani b Bote hawən. Kətlan qriṯo diḏan das+suryoye, harke bu+darbo d K̇árboranyo, bu+darbo d̥ K̇árboran, marke ḥamšaḥsar+kilometər mə‿Məḏyaḏ raḥə́qtoyo.
contents.versio: 041. My grandfather was born in Midyat, we are Midyatians, we are Midyatians, all were born in Midyat.  My grandfather too, my grandfather also in Midyat. Which grandfather, the other one, my mother’s father?  My mother’s father, my other grandfather, his name was Alyas,  my mother’s father. His mother’s name was Zero, it was Zero.  They were born in Bote. There is a village of ours, of Syriacs, here on the Kerboran road, on the Kerboran road, from here it is fifteen kilometres distant from Midyat.

contents.textus: 042. AL. Qaštux, emo demux me Bótewa?
contents.versio: 042. Your grandmother, your mother’s mother was from Bote?

contents.textus: 043. YT. E, mi+qriṯo d Bóteyo, e, híyaste mi+qriṯo d Bóteyo. Ǧəddi ŭ qašti, i+emo dbab… demi, ŭ i+emo demi, hani m Bótene, latne məḏyoye, bətoye. Kəmmínalən, qriṯo d Bote, bətoye, e. Bi+qriṯayo d Bote saymiwo dəgəšyoṯo, dəgəšyoṯo.
contents.versio: 043. Yes, she is from the village of Bote, yes, she is also from the village of Bote. My grandfather and my grandmother, the mother of my fath… of my mother, and my mother’s mother, these are from Bote, they are not Midyadians, Boteans. We call them, Bote Village, Boteans, right. In that village of Bote they used to make clay jugs, clay jugs.

contents.textus: 044. AL. Ayna lišone məǧġoliwa?
contents.versio: 044. Which languages did they speak?

contents.textus: 045. YT. B Bote kməǧġoli k̇urmanǧiste ŭ suryoyo; ʕárabi – lo. Bi+qriṯayo ʕárabi lə+kməǧġoli. Elo qriṯo kiba k̇urmánǧ, yaʕni ṭaye, k̇urmánǧ, ŭ kíbowa suryoye bas. I… u+babo demi məǧġalwo ʕárabi húweste. Harke fúrnačiwe. Húweste harke kə́twole farmo b Məḏyaḏ, yaʕni, ġắlăbe raḥuqo, meqəm mo+əšne aṯən l Məḏyaḏ. Ŭ kə́twole ṣənʕa xəd babi, farmo, babi u+ṣanəʕ̥ dǧə́ddiwe. Ǧə́ddiste kə́twole farmo, ŭ yaləfwo harke ʕárabistene ŭ tə́rkistene, məǧġalwo.
contents.versio: 045. In Bote they speak Kurdish and Turoyo; Arabic, no. In that village they do not speak Arabic. But such a village has Kurds, that is, Muslims, Kurds, and it used to have Syriacs, that’s all. She … my mother’s father also spoke Arabic. He was a baker here. He too owned a bakery in Midyat, like, very long ago, a hundred years ago they came to Midyat. And he had a trade like my father, a bakery, my father was my grandfather’s apprentice. My grandfather also had a bakery, and here he had learned both Arabic and Turkish, he used to speak them.

contents.textus: 046. AL. U+əšmo di+ḥurmayḏux mənyo?
contents.versio: 046. What is your wife’s name?

contents.textus: 047. YT. Yəldəz. Bməḏyoyo komar ‘aṯtux’. ‘Ṗire’ bu+k̇urmanǧiyo.  Aḥna b Məḏyaḏ kəmmina aṯto, i+aṯto.
contents.versio: 047. Her name is Yildiz. In Midyatian one says ‘your spouse’. ‘Old woman’ in Kurdish. We in Midyat say ‘spouse’, the ‘spouse’.

contents.textus: 048. AL.  Əšme di+ʕayle di+aṯtayḏux mənyo?
contents.versio: 048. What is your wife’s family name?

contents.textus: 049. YT. Hiya m ʕƏ́rnəsyo. Kətlan qriṯo ʕƏrnəs, ʕƏrnəs. Híyaste marke ʕayni ḥamšaḥṣar+kilometər, mqabəl d Bótene. Hiya bas harke yariwo. Hiya ʕəmra šato, u+babo aṯi l Məḏyaḏ, sāmwo qweləb di+ʕmara, taxtayā́t, maʕmarwo bote, u+qaləb, hawo sāmwo. Hiya harke b Məḏyaḏ yariwo. ʕƏmra šato, aṯyo m ʕƏrnəs larke, ŭ harke yariwo. Uʕdo ʕəmra čaʕ ŭ tleṯi ə́šneyo.
contents.versio: 049. She is from ʕƏrnǝs. We have a village ʕƏrnǝs, ʕƏrnəs. This one too is the same fifteen kilometres from here, facing Bote. She just grew up here. She’s one year old, her father came to Midyat, he would make construction scaffolding, planks, he would build houses, the scaffolding, that one he would make. She grew up here in Midyat. She’s one year old, she came from ʕƏrnǝs to here, and she grew up here. Now he she is 39 years old.

contents.textus: 050. AL. Ayna lišone kməǧġolo i+<ḥurmayḏux>?
contents.versio: 050. Which languages does your <wife> speak?

contents.textus: 051. YT. Aṯti. Məǧġolo híyaste arbʕo+lišone: suryoyo, ʕárabi, tərki, ŭ k̇urmanǧí, e. U+ʕamo d Məḏyaḏ, u+ʕamo d Məḏyaḏ, kule, yaʕni, aġlab mede, ġắlăbe mənayye, kməǧġoli arbʕo+lišone. Uʕdo an+naʕimayḏan kməǧġoli tloṯo+lišone, kibux dəmmat hən mnayye kməǧġoli arbʕo, kfəhmi u+ʕàrabi, bas lə+kˠqudri mádəʕri, elo məd lə+kməǧġoli, ha hawxa. Aḥna məd məǧġəlínawo, hawxa yalifina ġắlăbe.
contents.versio: 051. My ‘spouse’. She too speaks four languages: Turoyo, Arabic, Turkish, and Kurdish, yeah. The people of Midyat, the people of Midyat, all of them, that is, most like, many of them, speak four languages. Now our children speak three languages, you can say some of them speak four, they understand Arabic but they are unable to respond, but since they do not speak it, it’s like so. As for us, since we would speak it, we learned a lot that way.

contents.textus: 052. AL. Ayna lišone koməǧġolat bi+dukṯo du+šuġlayḏux?
contents.versio: 052. Which languages do you speak at your workplace?

contents.textus: 053. YT. E, lgorā́n … ínaqqa dəḥulqínawo, be mən lišono məǧġalwo, məǧġəlínawo u+lišonawo aʕmayye. Yaʕni ʕam u+k̇urmanǧì k̇urmanǧí, ʕam u+ʕarabi ʕárabi, ʕam u+tərki tərki, ʕam dəṯewo d̥ḥəlaqwo, lu+gorā̀n du+lišonawo məǧġəlínawo aʕme. Dlo, məǧġálnowo suryoyo bayn ḥḏoḏe aḥna.
contents.versio: 053. Right, depending on… when we would do the hair cutting, whatever language someone would speak, we would speak that language with them. That is, with a Kurd Kurdish, with an Arab Arabic, with a Turk Turkish, with whoever would come to get his hair cut, depending on that language we would speak with him. Otherwise, I would speak Turoyo among us ourselves.

contents.textus: 054. AL. Kito suryoye dməǧġoli ʕárabi?
contents.versio: 054. Are there Syriacs who speak Arabic?

contents.textus: 055. YT. Kətwo suryoye məǧġəliwo ʕárabi, hani di+xaṣra d̥ Karǧóz̥, d̥ Karǧóz̥, e, Karǧóz̥, bu+darbo d Baṭmán. Hanək kə́twolan tamo suryoye kaldoye, e, katolík, e. Uṯanwo, aṯənwo l Məḏyaḏ larke, aṯənwo l Məḏyaḏ, fayišiwo b Məḏyaḏ. Ab+botaṯṯe aṯənwo m Karǧóz̥, aṯənwo l Məḏyaḏ. Hani məǧġəliwo bayn ḥḏoḏe ʕárabi tamo b̥ Karǧóz̥. Ŭ bəṯr, harke bab+botaṯṯe məǧġəliwo ʕárabi, bas aʕmayna məǧġəliwo suryoyo.
contents.versio: 055. There were Christians who used to speak Arabic, those around Kercoz (lit. ‘of the Kercoz side’), of Kercoz, right, Kercoz, on the Batman road. Those we used to have there are Chaldean Christians, right, Catholics, right. They were coming, they came (a long time ago) here to Midyat, they came to Midyat, they stayed in Midyat. Their families (lit. ‘their homes’) came here from Kercoz, they came to Midyat. These used to speak Arabic among themselves there in Kercoz. And later, in their homes here they would speak Arabic, only with us would they speak Turoyo.

contents.textus: 056. AL. Ema aṯən larke?
contents.versio: 056. When did they come here?

contents.textus: 057. YT. Hənne, hawilən bu+zabnayḏa taqriban hul tloṯmo+əšne dʔaṯən larke, hən mnayye. Ŭ hən mnayye, hawilən mo+əšne daṯən, ŭ hən mnayye əšti+šawʕi+əšne. Yaʕni hul meqəm ḥamši+əšne kə́twolan ʕamo kaldoyo b Karǧóz̥, edi uʕdo lə+fayəš nošo, azzə́n kulle.
contents.versio: 057. They, at the time (lit. ‘at its time’) it has been for them approximately as many as three hundred years that they came here, some of them. And some of them, it has been a hundred years that they came, and some of them sixty-seventy years. That is, up to fifty years ago we had Chaldean people in Kercoz, but now nobody has remained, everybody went away.

contents.textus: 058. U+mede ḥreno aṯənwo kulle larke l Məḏyaḏ. Hən mnayye hawilən tloṯmo+əšne bgawə‿d Məḏyaḏ. Ŭ kətte ʕito harke, dak+kaldòyeste, ŭ kətte da+prūṭste. Kətwo məǧġəliwo u+ʕamo ǧġēr mak+kaldoye, kətwo a+prūṭ, kəmmina protesṭā́n, a+protesṭā̀n, e, prūṭ, kəmmínalən prūṭ, bu+məḏyoyo. (26:35)
contents.versio: 058. Something else, they all came here to Midyat. Some of them it has been three hundred years for them within Midyat. And they also have a church here, both a Chaldean one, and they also have a Prot one. There were people that would speak it other than Chaldeans, there were Prots, we say ‘Protestants’, the Protestants, right, Prots, we call them ‘Prots’, in Midyatian.

contents.textus: 059. Hani, hániste aṯənwo bu+zabnayḏa mə‿hno, mə‿Mawṣal, mu+ʕIraq. Aṯən meqəm hul arbaʕmo+əšne mede, hawilən tloṯmo ŭ ḥamši, arbaʕmo+əšne aṯən larke. Əmmíwolən b̰<e> Musa b̥<e> šamošo, ah+hərməziye. Hani aṯənwo larke, ŭ kətte, bann+alfo ŭ tmonemo ŭ təšʕi maʕmáranne ʕito harke la+prūṭ. Kətte ʕítoste harke bas uʕdo ǧămaʕa lə+fayəš, uʕdo ʕamo prūṭ lə+fayəš, azzə́n kulle l Awrupa.
contents.versio: 059. These, these ones too, came at the time from whatsit, from Mosul, from Iraq. They came here up to some four hundred years ago, it has been three hundred fifty years for them, four hundred years they came here. They would call them the Musa family, the family of the deacon, the Hormizians. They came here and they have, in 1890 the Prots built themselves a church here. They still have a church here but now a community hasn’t remained, now the Prot people haven’t remained, all of them went to Europe.

contents.textus: 060. AL. Kəḏʕat suryoyo madənḥoyo?
contents.versio: 060. Do you know Eastern Syriac?

contents.textus: 061. YT. Suryoyo madənḥoyo kiban məǧġəlina, e, koḏaʕno. Elo yaləfina mqariwi Yawsef Beġtáš, aḏiʕat? Mu+babo ŭ mani. Əzzánowo li+qriṯo, l Ḥassana, hənne me támone. E, kməǧġəlina aʕmayye, e. Kšobah, lə … ʕayni xud u+suryòyoyo, xud u+suryòyoyo, húwestene, yaʕni u+lišono d̥kəmmina madənḥoyo.
contents.versio: 061. We can speak Eastern Syriac, yes, I know it. But we learned it from my children’s godfather Yusuf Beğtaş, you know? From his father and from these ones. We used to go to the village, to Ḥassana, they are from there. Yes, we speak with them, yes. It resembles, no… it is like Turoyo, like Turoyo, it too, that is, the language we call Eastern.

contents.textus: 062. Aḏiʕat? Yaʕni ṫox – ṫəxla, zəlla, laxma, əšme du+laḥmo laxma. Aḥna kəmmínale bu+suryoyo laḥmo, e. Də́xiya ‘áydarbo hat?’ Sfáhila, e, sfáhila, e. Məǧġəlina, kə́twolan harke, aṯíwolan mu+ʕIràq, i+šato da+t … alfo ŭ čaʕmo ŭ ḥḏo ŭ təšʕi, ínaqqa d̥ Ṣaddā́m. Ínaqlayo aṯíwolan ʕəraqiye larke ġắlăbe, kə́twolan hul mo+ḥamši+ʕaylā̀t, kəmmínalən bu+hno aḥna, aṯi larke eqaryoṯo, aṯi l Məḏyaḏ, mu+ʕIraq aṯənwo, yaʕni aṯən m Karkuk, aṯən mi+Sleymaniyye, aṯən mə Dəhók, ŭ aṯən mə hno, mu+ʕIràq kule. Aṯən diḏan da+mšiḥoyye daṯənwo.
contents.versio: 062. You know? Like, ‘come!’ is ṫǝxla, zǝlla, laxma, they call bread laxma. In Turoyo we call it laḥmo, right. Dǝxya ‘how are you?’ Sfáhila [‘she is good’], right, sfáhila, right. We speak it, we had them here, they came to us from Iraq in the year 2… 1991, when it was Saddam. That time many Iraqis came here to us, we had up to one hundred fifty families, we call them in the whatsit, their folks came here, they came to Midyat, they came from Iraq, like, they came from Kirkuk, they came from Sulaymaniyah, they came from Duhok, they came from whatsit, from the whole of Iraq. Ours came, some of the Christians that came.

contents.textus: 063. AL. Uʕdo koʕayši harke?
contents.versio: 063. Do they live here now?

contents.textus: 064. YT. Lo, aṯənwo larke, uʕdo kito harke tarte+ʕaylā̀t, kito tarte+eqaryoṯo mu+ʕIràq, e. Ánnaqqa aṯən, e, kətwo mo+ḥamši+ʕaylā̀t harke, məd̥ kətwo yaləfínawo mnayye, e, yaləfínawo mnayye. Bəṯr hənne azzə́n, aṯən d Ḥassana, di+qriṯo du+Yawsef. Hə́nneste bann+alfo ŭ čaʕmo ŭ tlaṯ ŭ təšʕi maxléwolən i+qriṯo, aṯən larke hul ʕəṣri+eqaryoṯo, ʕaylā́t, fayiši harke, aḥna húwalwolən bote, kəmmínale bi+šawṯo, yaʕni sidayna.
contents.versio: 064. No, they came here, now here there are two families, two folks from Iraq, yes. When they came, right, there were one hundred fifty families here, when they were [here] we learned from them, yes, we learned from them. After they left, some from Hassana came, from Yusuf’s village. They too in the year 1993 cleared out the village, up to twenty folks came here, families, they stayed here, we gave them houses, let’s say, in the vicinity, that is by us.

contents.textus: 065. Suryoyo... B̰ Məḏyaḏ kətlan ʕaylā́t, kətlan mo+ŭ+tleṯi, kətlan šeṯ+ʕitawoṯo das+suryoye, šeṯ+ʕitawoṯo, ŭ kito ḥḏo dak+kaldoye, ŭ kito ḥḏo da+prūṭ, hano b̰məḏyóyoyo, ha. Da+prūṭ, kəmmina protesṭā́n.
contents.versio: 065. Syriac… In Midyat we have families, we have a hundred and thirty, we have six Syriac churches, six churches, and there is one of Chaldeans, and there is one of the ‘Prots’, this is in Midyatian, here. Of the ‘Prots’, we say [for] ‘Protestants’.

contents.textus: 066. G: Kmo+bote dak+kaldoye kito?
contents.versio: 066. How many Chaldean households are there?

contents.textus: 067. YT: Uʕdo kito harke b̰ Məḏyaḏ tloṯ+ʕaylat, tloṯo+bote, tloṯo+bote kaldoye kito. E, lə+fayəš, azzənyo.
contents.versio: 067. Now there is here in Midyat three families, three households, there are three Chaldean households. Yes, it (i.e., the community) didn’t survive, they left.

contents.textus: 068. G: U+lišonaṯxu kuḏʕi?
contents.versio: 068. Do they know your language?

contents.textus: 069. YT: Suryoyo kməǧġoli, suryoyo kməǧġoli, suryoyo, kməǧġoli ʕárabistene, məǧġoli ʕárabi bu+bàytostene, bas kməǧġoli suryoyo, suryoyo, aḏiʕat? Yaʕni, farqiye layto, farqiye layto. Suryoyo, e, suryoyo d Məḏyaḏ, kməǧġoli, e,  suryoyo d Məḏyaḏ. <...> Bas kətlan… xəd məḷḷan kətlan šeṯ+ʕitawoṯo, kətlan tarte+madrăsā̀t, tarte+madrăsā̀t. An+naʕime kəzzə́n ltamo.
contents.versio: 069. They speak Syriac, they speak Syriac, Syriac, they speak Arabic too, they speak Arabic at home too, but they speak Syriac, Syriac, you know? Like, there is no difference (i.e., between Syriacs and Chaldeans in this regard), there is no difference. Syriac, yes, Midyatian Syriac, they speak it, yes,  Midyatian Syriac. <...> But we have… as we said, we have six churches, we have two church schools, two church schools. The children go there.

contents.textus: 070. Harke b Məḏyaḏ, baq+qərywoṯayḏa, hawirdṓr d Məḏyaḏ kito šeṯ+qəryawoṯo dač+čalkoye. Əšme daq+qəryawoṯaṯṯe, ḥḏo mnayye Baǧənne, ḥḏo mnayye K̇avnā́s, ḥḏo Daywank̇e, ŭ ḥḏo mnayye Ṫaqa,  ḥḏo mnayye Xarabya, hawxa, ŭ K̇očane. E, hani ʕayəd d Mə́ḏyaḏne, d̥kətne ʕayəd d Məḏyaḏ.
contents.versio: 070. Here in Midyat, in its villages, around Midyat there are six Yezidi villages. As for the names of their villages, one of them is Bacin, one of them is Kefnas, one is Denwan, and one of them is Taka,  one of them is Harapya, like so, and Koçan. Yes, these pertain to (lit. ‘are the property of’) Midyat, they pertain to Midyat.

contents.textus: 071. Ŭ kito ʕayəd d Házaxstene, kəmmila i+qriṯo, hayo kəmmila Kiwax, ʕayəd d Házaxyo. Meqəm ʕayəd d Mə́ḏyaḏwa, háyostene. Bəṯr Šərnax dawyo walaye, azzá ltamo. Yaʕni uʕdo b Məḏyaḏ šeṯ+qəryawoṯo kətlan ʕayəd d Məḏyaḏ, xəd məḷḷan aq+qəryawoṯani.
contents.versio: 071. And one pertains to Azəx, they call the village, that one they call Kiwex, it pertains to Azəx. Earlier it belonged to Midyat, that one as well. After Şırnak became a province, it went there. Like, now in Midyat we have six villages pertaining to Midyat, like we said, these villages.

contents.textus: 072. Ač+čalkoye kulle meqəm ʕūdi<wo>,  ŭ i+hnaṯṯe, i+mdăbăra dəmdabriwo ruḥayye mənwe? Kulle ba+ḥyewən, bu+săwā̀l, yaʕni tamo săwā́l kətte, ŭ kətte ə́šmoste darʕoṯo, duriwo ḥeṭe, sʕore, ṭlawḥe, ŭ masāyəl. Maftiwo ʕəmrayye bu+šəklano, ŭ ʕūdiwo‿xliwo. Akṯariye məd̥ kə́twolən săwā́l, u+săwā̀l d Məḏyaḏ, darke, kule msidayye oṯewo, a+ḥyewən.
contents.versio: 072. All Yezidis back then <would> work, and their whatsit, the occupation with which they would occupy themselves, what was it? All of them are with animals, with livestock, like, they have livestock there, and they also have a little bit of (farm)lands, they would cultivate wheat, barley, lentils, etc. They would spend their lives in this way, and they would work, eat. Mostly, since they had livestock, Midyat’s livestock, all of it would come from their place, the animals.

contents.textus: 073. Ŭ bəṯr edi ač+čalkoye hə́nnestene bat+təšʕiyā̀t, azzənyo, bdalle dəzzənyo l Awrupa, ŭ xalən aq+qəryawoṯaṯṯe. Ínaqqa d̥xalən aq+qəryawoṯaṯṯe, hə́nnestene, ḥáqqatan u+săwā̀l naqəṣ barke, b Məḏyaḏ ġắlăbe. Qayyo? Noše edi haw sāmwo săwā́l, ŭ azzə́n l Awrupa. Bas uʕdo ač+čalkòyestene, hedi-hedi, xəd diḏan das+suryoye, klən koṯən komáʕəmri aq+qəryawoṯaṯṯe, koṯən bu+qayṭo.
contents.versio: 073. And afterwards Yazidis, they too left in the nineties, they started going to Europe, and their villages emptied out. When their villages emptied out, they too, the livestock really declined in here, in Midyat, a lot. Why? Then people no longer tended livestock, and they went to Europe. But now the Yazidis too, bit by bit, like our folks among the Syriacs, here they are, coming to build their villages, they come during the summer.

contents.textus: 074. Uʕdo laq+qəryawoṯani dəbneli kulle xəd Baǧənne, xəd K̇avnā́s, xəd K̇očane, xəd Daywank̇e, xəd Ṫaqá ŭ Xarabya, aṯən kul+ḥa, kmaʕmarle bote. Kul+qriṯo kiba šawʕo+tmanyo+bote. Aṯən, maʕmárranne bote ḥaṯe, ŭ mḥaṯḥaṯṯe ab+botaṯṯe.
contents.versio: 074. Now these villages that I counted, all of them, like Bacin, like Kefnas, like Koçan, like Denwan, like Taqa and Harapya, everyone came back, (everyone) was building houses. In each village there are seven-eight households. They came back, they built themselves new houses, and they renovated their houses.

contents.textus: 075. Kəzzə́n ŭ oṯən bu+qayṭo. Hən mnáyyeste kfayši, ḥḏo+ʕayla knuṭro i+qriṯo. Uʕdo hawxa bu+šəklano. Ŭ hən mnáyyestene uʕdo šqə́llanne bote bgawə‿d Məḏyaḏ. Ínaqqa d̥koṯən bu+qayṭo lăǧan lu+hno, lu+əzən l Məḏyaḏ, kfayši harke b Məḏyaḏ. (9:10)
contents.versio: 075. They go and they come back in summer. Some of them stay, one family looks after the village. So now it’s this way. And some of them have already bought houses within Midyat. When they come back in summer for the whatsit, for the vacation to Midyat, they stay here in Midyat.

contents.textus: 076. Ač+čalkoye ṭabi‿ə́nnestene, aṯməl u+ʕeḏàṯṯewe, kmárwole... aṯməl bume ḥreno Kčaršambá ṣorK. Yawme darbʕo, yawme d̥ḥamšo kə́twolən ʕeḏo, aṯməl, kito harke čalkoye bu+qamp, aṯməl u+qaymaqā̀m d Məḏyaḏ, azzé mʕayaḏle ač+čalkoye bu+ʕeḏaṯṯe.
contents.versio: 076. Yazidis naturally they too, yesterday was their holiday, someone would call it … the day before yesterday KScarlet WednesdayK. On Wednesday, on Thursday they had a holiday, yesterday, there are Yezidis here in the camp, yesterday the district governor of Midyat, he went to congratulate the Yazidis on their holiday.

contents.textus: 077. Ŭ kətte i+šato tre+ʕeḏe. Áḥnaste ínaqqa d̥kətwən harke hən mnayye b Məḏyaḏ, mʕayḏínawo u+ʕeḏaṯṯe. Ha, lmə‿kmətyaqni? Kmətyaqni, l… kəmmile Ṭartavṓz, Kmalaké tavṓzK. Hənne lawo kʕəbdi, ŭ bu+šəklano, kətte ṣáwmoste, ŭ kətte ʕebádeste, ŭ kətte ʕéḏeste.
contents.versio: 077. And they have two holidays a year. We too, when there were some of them here in Midyat, we congratulated them on their holday. So, what do they believe? They believe in… they call it Ṭartavṓz, ‘the peacock angel’. They worship that one, and so, they have a fast too, and they have prayers too, and they have holidays too.

contents.textus: 078. Ŭ kətlan ʕalaqā́t ʕam ḥḏoḏe kayise. Ač+čalkoye ʕamo latyo ḥarbo, ʕamo kayísoyo. Aḏiʕat? Bu+šəklano kʕayiši uʕdo akṯariye b Awrupa.
contents.versio: 078. And we have good relations with each other. Yazidis are not a bad people, they are a good people. You know? So they live nowadays mostly in Europe.

contents.textus: 0001. U kṯowano d kətyo b iḏayxu, frəsla l Beṯ-Froso Nsibin, səyomo d Ǧan Beṯ-Ṣawoʕe. Hano kowe i ḥaləqto dat tarte maḥ ḥaləqyoṯo d “Beṯ-Nahrin Dasto, Uno Maġrafto“.
0002. Bi qamayto, bu froso du kṯowano, u Ǧan amṭele u "soz" diḏe l dukṯe w ḥatta mazədle aʕle. Aydarbo? D umarno ḥa b ḥa: bi qamayto marwaḥle i ḥəyərto ʕal u ṭuro, xaṣaṭan ʕal Məḏyaḏ.
0003. Da tre maʕmaqle hən maš šəwole d dəqwo bənne bu kṯowayḏe u qamoyo “Əno Mərli, Xori Brahim Haǧǧo Madʕarle“.
0004. Da tloṯ mawḏaʕlelan ʕal šaxṣiye, d hawila dawro rabo, baḥ ḥaye du ʕamayḏan bann əšne ḥaroye: ʕAmmo Išoʕ d be Qašo Malke.
0005. Ġer man nuqṭe, d kətne kayise, ʕal Məḏyaḏ w ʕal u Ṭuro lu maḏʕo, kḥuzeno ḥa maš šəyole ulṣoye (muhim), d kmənṭər ǧawab aʕle mas sowe d kətne xəd u ʕAmmo Išoʕ i qaḏiye du "Sayfo" yo.

0006. Bale xəd kḥuzena bu kṯowano, u medano lə fayəš hawxa sahəl. Mu sabab — xəd u Ǧan ste d kḏokər — bi Maʕəlṯo du kṯowo qamoyo w komər: “... aš šaxṣat d ʕayiši aq qaḏiyat du waxtawo... aw d kəḏʕənne ma ḥkeyat d šamiʕi, man noše d ʕayiši aq qaḏiyat bi šaxṣiyaṯṯe, qayṣ d koṯe knəqṣi m baynoṯayna...“.
0007. ʕAl hawxa əno ste kḥuzeno u šəwolano šəwolo əmṯonoyo w ġalabe muhim w klozəm d nəfqinale moro. W d maltmina u mede d kətyo mbarbzo harke w tamo.
0008. Šuġlo mu šəklano, yaʕni bu šəkəl da tre kṯowe d frəsla l Nsibin, b fəlḥono yaquro yo w kəbʕele šaġole d qədri ʕəwdi mnaḏmo w b ṣabər.
0009. Ḥawro Ǧan mnaḏmo həwle ruḥe lu fəlḥonano. Kətle ḥiyərto rwəḥto w kəmḥawəl d ubelan ṣərto ʕal nəqṭoṯe mšakle. Baynoṯayye maktab zabnoye (tarixiye), knušyoye w marduṯonoye.
0010. Bi badaye, kubaʕ d kuleno ʕal mədone d kətne mʕalqe bi šaxṣiye du maḥkəyono d mnaqele lu Ǧan. U maqṣad diḏi, latyo mahwo d zəbdo ʕal u kṯowo. Kubaʕno b karyuṯo d midaqno l nuqṭe mene.
0011. Am mədone d kmaḥke u ʕAmmo Išoʕ — ṭabʕan ʕal aš šəwole d mšayele u Ǧan — kiban fəlġinalle l nuqṭe dilonoye (xaṣ), mʕalqe bi šaxṣiye du maḥkəyono, w mədone gawonoye.
0012. Ad dilonoye kubaʕ d maṣərnən b karyo b ḥḏoḏe, mu sabab aḥ ḥaye du maḥkəyono mbarbze ne bu mede, d kito harke. Bəṯr gədubeno əšmo d ṣərto ʕal u Sayfo.
0013. Ġer man nuqṭani, kito ġalabe mədone gawonoye, akit hən mənayye šaməʕinalle (xaṣaṭan aḥna an noše d hawina b Məḏyaḏ), ṭabiʕi d kətwolle rəġgo, hawəlle fərṣa d yəlfi m noše ġalabe.
0014. Mawxa, an noše d latne m Məḏyaḏ, u mede d kmitaḥke harke balki ḥaṯo gədoṯe aʕlayye. Ṭabiʕi ste laǧan aǧ ǧilat d gədoṯe w xaṣaṭan hani d qayimi b Awruppa ak kṯowani du Ǧan gədhowən ġalabe muhim.
0015. U ʕAmmo Išoʕ hawi 25 b oḏər bi šato dan 1913 b Məḏyaḏ. Ṭaqriban šato w falge meqəm mu Sayfo. I iqarṯo (ʕayle) d be Ǧərǧo (d be Qašo Malke) rabṯowa.
0016. B Məḏyaḏ hawəlle asiruṯo (ʕalaqa) ʕam ġalabe iqaryoṯo. I naqqa d ṭiq u Sayfo b Məḏyaḏ, u babo qadər d maxləṣ huwwe w i ḥoṯo mə Məḏyaḏ.
0017. I emo kməqṭolo. Aṭ ṭaye d məskənne, mbelənne lə Mzizaḥ. U ǧəddo (Ǧərǧo d be Qašo Malke) šqəlile maṭ ṭaye huwwe w i ḥoṯo, b šawʕo w tleṯi (37) maǧidiye w zənǧər d semo.
0018. Xəd ġer iqaryoṯo hənne ste mahzamwolən l ʕIwardo. Bəṯr kfayši zabno b Anḥəl. U ǧəddo bəṯr mu Sayfo kməqṭəl ʕal iḏe d Šex Xalaf.
0019. U babo du ʕAmmo Išoʕ, kmaḥwe aʕle d kətwe ḥa ǧaṣur. Bu čaġ du Sayfo hənne heš b Anḥəl, ʕam kmo ḥawrone məḏyoye koṯən b gnowo lab botaṯṯe b Məḏyaḏ.
0020. Aṯən mədde hən mu mede d tlewolle bab bote. Ḥzalle b ʕaynayye i ʕaskar w aṭ ṭaye d msəkke w d yatiwi bi aġlabiye dab bote b Məḏyaḏ.
0021. I naqqa qamayto d kmaydi u babo du ʕAmmo Išoʕ li ʕaskariye kmahzəm.
0022. Maʕwədiwonne bu səyomo dad darbone b Šexane. Bəṯr mə d daʕiri mə Anḥəl, u babo kfotəḥ ḥḏo mad dukkane qamoye - bəṯr mu Sayfo - w mzabanwo biyya šuqo.
0023. Kumarno u ʕAmmo Išoʕ hawile šanṣ kayiso, qrele b madrašyoṯe mšakle. Tamo yaləf lišone w ftiḥ lašane əmkanat bu məstaqbəl.
0024. Bu zabnawo ġalabe noše, lə qadiri d mšayʕi an naʕimaṯṯe lam madrašyoṯo. U sabab ste, an noše kulle, lbike wən bu ḥəyṣolo du fako yawmonoyo.
0025. Huwwe qrele bi madrašto das səryoye, dak katolik w dap proṭəstan. Harke yaləf ʕarabi, tərki w lišone nəxroye xu ingilizi w əšmo faransawi.
0026. Lan noše du waxtano hano asas ġalabe kayiso we. Bu zabno d kətwe ṭalaba kmitaqləb u lišono du tərki mu ʕatiqo lu ḥaṯo.
0027. I šato dan 1940, u ʕAmmo Išoʕ kgowər w bəṯr lo b mede kəzze li ʕaskariye.

0028. M harke w azolo kbode aʕme u zawno d koḏəʕ mən hawi. ʕAl d kətwe mšiḥoyo, huwwe w tloṯo w tmoni (83) məḏyoye ḥrene ʕam ḥḏoḏe bi ʕaskariye ləwanne ṣəlaḥ. Maʕwədənne bad darbone w b səyomo d maydan d ṭiyara bə Traqya.
0029. Mu sabab u ʕAmmo Išoʕ d uḏaʕwo qraye w kṯawto səmme čawiš w bəṯr ste mtarǧmono bi qaṣṭaxana ʕal d uḏaʕwo ʕarabi, kurmanǧi w tərki.
0030. Hawile əmkan bəṯr d zoyər an noše d maltəmiwonne bu ḥtiyat b Maniṣa, b Aqḥiṣar bi šato dan 1941/42 (taqriban mede 600-700 nafšoṯo mə Məḏyaḏ w mə hawir diḏa).
0031. Səmme u ʕAmmo Išoʕ ‘səḥya čawiši‘ bi ʕaskariye. Yaləf əšme dad darmone w l goran d komər samwo ḥatta tadawi w kuraxwo baq qəryawoṯo du Ṭuro lu mḥoyo da mḥaṭe. Huwwe komər: “səmli ṭaxtoriye“.

0032. Kmaḥwe aʕle, bəṯr mə d daʕər mi ʕaskariye b kmo əšne, ʕabər bi siyase di mənṭəqa. Ap partiye dat tərk, bu asas diḏa ste bdewolən d ʕəbri li mənṭəqayḏan bann arbʕiyat (40). U Xalq (Halk Partisi) rakəwwo.
0033. W ḥa man noše iḏiʕe du Xalq ste u ʕAmmo Brahim d be Šabo we. U ʕAmmo Išoʕ, bəṯr hawi ḥa mam mʔassəsone du Damoqrat (Demokrat Partisi) b Məḏyaḏ.
0034. W bi muʕawanayḏe ṭrele d mḥayṣəl bi mənṭəqa bar rayat da mšiḥoye. Bəṯr mə qaḏiyat d kšuraḥlan u ʕAmmo Išoʕ mbadele u gabo w riz ʕam u Xalq.
0035. Ba tre partiye ste ḥuḏarwo bak qonġərat mənṭəqiye w b ʕAnqara ste baq qonġərat d kətwayye b darġo d Tərkiya.

0036. Kətle ṣərto ʕam Adnan Mandaras w Ǧalal Bayar. Bəṯr mə d mbadele lu Xalq grəšle i dəqqa d Ismat Paša w ḥatta ʕzəmle u ʕAmmo Išoʕ lu baytayḏe. Ṭaqriban hawi 4 əšne hadomo bu Məǧləs-idari d kətwe bi walaye d Mərde.
0037. An noše ḥrene d ʕabiri lu məǧləsano ste: u Brahim d be Šabo, Karmo Sṭayfan w Tuma Qəlič wayye.
0038. Ṭabiʕi fayəš šəwolo muhim, mən qadər d mqadəm bag gabani laǧan u ʕamayḏan?
0039. Mən fayde hawile lu ʕamayḏan? Kmətyaqanno u ṭalab dayəm ‘d lowe taʕaddayiye‘ ʕal u ʕamo we.

0040. Goya məkṯawwo egaryoṯo m ʕAnqara law waliye laǧan hawxa. Bale i naqqa d məftakrina bu xloyo du Ṭuro, baʕ ʕəsri əšne ḥaroyani mas səryoye, kiban d əmmina aṭ ṭalabani d hawi map partiye, lə manfaʕʕe ġalabe. Balki ste aṭ ṭalabe lə muṭanwo l ʕAnqara w li ḥkume.

0041. U šuġlo qamoyo d səmle lu ʕAmmo Išoʕ, hawi i ‘daʕwa wakiliye'. ʕAl asas du qanun di madde da tmone (8), bu qanun madani. Səmle ṭapowat dan noše. Laʔan u məlk meqəm latwe mqaydo ʕal əšme dam morayḏe.

0042. Heš bəṯr kul nošo mḥawele d soyəm u məlk diḏe ṭapo. Ḥḏo mad daʕwat muhim diḏe, d mwafəq biyya, hawyo i daʕwa d Mor Gabriyel i naqqa ban 1962/63 i ḥkume d abiʕo d maḥto iḏo ʕal u waqəf w əbʕiwo d saymola qəžla.
0043. Markawwolən hayye w u sakratar diḏa ste hawiwo ḥoli Gabro d be Ḥadodo. U ʕAmmo Išoʕ səmle tmonaḥṣar (18) əšne muxtariye bi šawṯo di ǧəmhuriye b Məḏyaḏ.
0044. Kuṯawwo stədʕat, kətwole ‘yazixana‘ b Astəl. L goran d kmaḥke manfaqle bann alfowat (!) pasaportat lan noše. W səmle xəd huwwe d kmaṯkər, “... mu šuġlano səmlili ġalabe kallat kayise...“.
0045. B šroro aḥ ḥaye du ʕAmmo Išoʕ, xəd kmaḥkelən, hənne falqo mu tarix d Məḏyaḏ w du Ṭuro ne. Hul l uʕdo ste kəzze w koṯe l Məḏyaḏ.
0046. Kmaḥwe aʕle d kətwe iḏiʕo w kətwole dukṯe. Ṭabiʕi ste klozəm d əmmina, kətwo ġalabe noše ġer mene ste iḏiʕe.

0047. Hani ste hawilən taʕab qəm u ʕamayḏan. Harke lə kməṯkər əšmayye. An nošani balki bann əšne ḥaroye latwən iḏiʕe xəd u ʕAmmo Išoʕ, bas kətwo šaxṣiyat d nufaqwo šuġlone m iḏayye. W qəm du ʕamayḏan ste b ġira maḥwanwo.

0048. Əno laǧani d kətyo muhim aq qaḏiyat d hawi bu Sayfo ne. Kḥuzeno əšmo muhim d ubeno ṣərto mu waxtawo. Harke u ḥa d latle mawḏaʕto kayəsto, balki zaḥme yo, d fohəm aš šəwole w aǧ ǧawabe d kito bu kṯowano.
0049. Hani kubəʕ əšmo d marwaḥnən w bəṯr b karyo ste kubəʕ d midaqno ʕal bəṯr mu Sayfo ste.
0050. U ʕAmmo Išoʕ bəṯr maḥ ḥamšiyat (50) w laf harke kubelan maʕlumat kayise.
0051. Hani kulle ʕayəšše. Bas naqla ḥreto ste klozəm mə ġer xawaṣər d mikaməl aʕlayye. Xaṣaṭan i həǧra d hawi l Awruppa, kul ḥa mənayna kumarno b šəkəl ʕayəšla, mawxa lə kubəʕ d kuleno aʕla.

0052. Meqəm mu Sayfo bu Ṭuro kətwo ġalabe səryoye. Xaṣaṭan b Məḏyaḏ w bi walaye d Mərde. Kətwo bu nəquṣo mo w ḥamši (150) qəryawoṯo du ʕamayḏan. Ġer mani kətwo səryoye bə Diyarbakər, b Alʕaziz, b ʕƏntab, b Urfa, b Xarput kətwo səryoye w armənoye.
0053. Bu zabnano kətwo ʕitawoṯo dak kaldoye w dap pərut rakiwe. W kətwo ǧamaʕat b manaṭəq manaṭəq. I naqqa d mḥe u Sayfo bas səryoye, gab ann armənoye bdewole meqəm bə tre-tloṯo (2-3) yarḥe.
0054. Ġalabe mənayye, bu zabnawo qṭəliwo. W as səryoye b dəkoṯo dəkoṯo šəmʕiwo aʕlayye.
0055. Bu kṯowo u yuqro kmitahwe ʕal i mdiṯo d Məḏyaḏ. Harke u Sayfo bdele b ḥzirən 1915. Qamayto mḥe baq qəryawoṯo w bəṯr b Məḏyaḏ.
0056. U qaymaqam d Məḏyaḏ məštaʕele dawro ġalabe pis. Hǧim ʕal Məḏyaḏ w mḥaṣro w hawi ḥərobo rabo w qawyo b Məḏyaḏ. B bote mʕayne layəm ġalabe w mdafaʕʕe ʕal ruḥayye hul d qadiri.
0057. Koṯe l boli ǧəddi (Barṣawmo d be Abrahəm) maḥkewo aydarbo mi məḏḏarayḏan muḥanwo bani d həǧmiwo mann adroṯo w mə ġer dəkoṯo aʕlayye.
0058. U bayto[1] d be qarəwoni, kəmmənne bə ʕAdoka, ḥa mab bote d hawiwo quṣro di mudafaʕa. Ad dəžmən harke mawballe u zor das səryoye w qṭil ġalabe noše.
0059. Lad dəžmən dlo raḥme nḥərre šaxṣat rabe w naʕime. U suhḏayḏan u ʕAmmo Išoʕ, bu zabnano kmaxləṣ huwwe w i ḥoṯo naʕime ʕam u babo mə tamo. I emo tamo kməqṭolo.
0060. Taqriban b mədde d šabṯo aw d ʕaṣro yawme u ʕamo mahzamle. U ḥa d maxlaṣle maṭi l ʕIwardo, l Anḥəl w l ġer qəryawoṯo.
0061. Xaṣaṭan ʕIwardo, hawyo xalaṣ du ʕamayḏan bu Ṭuro. 7000 rəḥwoṯo maʕṣalle ruḥayye tamo. W qadiri d saymi muqawame mqabəl dak kurmanǧ w di ʕaskar dat tərk aʕmayye.
0062. Bəṯr məd hawi šayno, an noše daʕiri l Məḏyaḏ. Ḥzalle b ʕaynayye aydarbo Məḏyaḏ simo falge d xərbe.

0063. Lak kurd ṭaye mašəġwolən ab bote. Ġalabe mab bote ste laṭ ṭaye maḥətwolən iḏo aʕlayye. B hən ste i ʕaskar čiko. Bəṯr mu maṯyo bdele lu kafno w aʕme kewe pəsin. Ġalabe noše d maxlaṣṣe mu Sayfo bəṯr mayiṯi.
0064. Bu zabnawo kšəmʕina d ʕabərwo muhaǧər m dəkoṯe du Anadol w du garbyo d Tərkiya l Məḏyaḏ.

0065. Xəd d kmaḥke u ʕAmmo Išoʕ ste əšmo əšmo an noše bdelən kfətḥənne šuġlone, dukkane w kəzzən w koṯən bi mənṭəqa. Bəṯr mu Sayfo, kəzze zawno yarixo ste bi ḥolo, heš an noše latwən mʔamne bu nfoqo w bu ʕboraṯṯe. Ġalabe noše qṭili bad darbone ʕal iḏe daṭ ṭaye.
0066. Baʕ ʕəsriyat (1920-1930), li ḥkume bdela hedi hedi kʕəbro li mənṭəqa.
0067. Bu zabno du ʕAmmo Išoʕ d əzzewo li madrašto, li ḥkume ṣxərwola am madrašyoṯo das səryoye. Ṭaqriban bu zabnawo bdela li ʕmara di qəžla m lišone d Kənʕan Paša b Məḏyaḏ.
0068. Tam bi dəkṯo d kətwa i ʕito d Mor Šarbel. U ʕAmmo Išoʕ kmaḥkelan aʕla. Koṯe l bole d kətwa dayro rabṯo, hawir diḏa kule bəstone, kətwola diwanxana rabṯo w ḥatta madrašto d mitaqrewo biyya.
0069. Kšəmʕina ste ʕal noše, bi badaye du doro d azzən mə Məḏyaḏ l Amarika w bəṯr daʕiri. U ʕAmmo Išoʕ kbone ḥa b ḥa ann əšmone dani d azzən.

0070. Bəṯr kḏokər ʕal u ‘Bəšoro dap proṭəstan‘ ste. Kətwolən kunaġ - Amarikan Qolleži - b Mərde w kərxiwo baq qəryawoṯo. Heš bu zabnawo mšayaʕwolən noše d qorən b Amarika. Kyəlfina ʕal noše d azzən hawən ʕaskar du Ingiliz w d Faransa.
0071. Goya mi fəqriye əzzənwo. B ʕayni zabno ste kətwo tahlika aʕlayye b Tərkiya. W ḥatta šawʕo (7) mənayye bəṯr məd daʕiri šniqi b Adiyaman.
0072. I naqqa ak kurd d qayimi li raġlo baʕ ʕəsriyat (20) msarganwolən noše mu ʕamayḏan ste.
0073. W šnəqwolən ʕam Šex Saʕid səryoye ste. U mede d kətyo ḥaṯo w d gorəš i dəqqa u ʕəsyan d hawi man aḥunonayḏan am madənḥoye b Hakkari ban 1924 yo.
0074. U ʕAmmo Išoʕ koṯe l bole əšme d Aġa Bəṭrəs d kətwe u mdabrono dan oṯuroye. W ḥatta komər: “Noše m Bsorino, m Hazax w m Ḥapsəs mʕawnənne!“

0075. I qaḏiye di ṭaqqa du ‘Dabbo‘ u Ǧan kəmšayela mu ʕAmmo Išoʕ. Ḥzeli, xəd Xori Brahim maḏʕo latle bi qəṣṣaṯe. U sabab ste huwwe latwe b gawe di qaḏiye. Kmaḥwe, asas u mede d meqəm mi ʕaskariyayḏe kayiso lə koṯən l bole. Bale kmaḥkelan b šəkəl rwiḥo ʕal u kafno w ak kewe dawiwo bəṯr mu ḥtiyat (1941) bu Ṭuro kule.
0076. Bu zabnano aydarbo u ʕamo bdele kmibarbəz w baq qaflat azzən l Suriya. Kətle iḏaʕto kayəsto ʕal “Varlik Vergisi“ d maḥətwola li ḥkume ʕal as səryoye.

0077. I aṯto du ʕAmmo Išoʕ ahəl d Šamʕune Ḥanne yo. Kmaḥkallan aʕle zəd mu mede d kəḏʕina. I ḥawruṯayḏe ʕam ʕAlike Baṭṭe. Əno šaxṣan knuṭarno mədone zəd mawxa man noše d kətwayye ġalabe qariwe l Šamʕune Ḥanne.
0078. U kṯowano kubelan ṣərtoṯo ʕal nuqṭe knušyoye w marduṯonoye ġalabe mšakle. Kumarno u Ǧan lə ṭrele ṭaqriban mede maḥ ḥaye yawmonoye d lə diq bənne.

0079. Aḥ ḥaye di renǧbariye, daṣ ṣanayəʕ b Məḏyaḏ, maʕ ʕitawoṯo, lad dayre hul lam məštawoṯo w heš ġer mədone dlə kubaʕno harke d bunenən. B šroro ftəḥlelan tarʕo rwiḥo w bu zabnano xaṣaṭan ḥa lḥuḏe d lə kqodər d ubele.
0080. Harke kḥuzeno u maṯlo d kobe u Ǧan b dukṯeyo. Yaʕni u Ṭuro w aḥ ḥaye du Ṭuro, kmašbahhe l dasto rabo w kul nošo ste, anǧax bi maġrafto kibe d moyəd mene!

0081. Haka kəbʕina d əḏʕina man masəmle ag gəbone d hawir Məḏyaḏ, aḥ ḥaṯnawoṯo baʕ ʕəsriyat (1920-1930) mən šəkəl lušiwo, ak kefe daʕ ʕmarat mayko uṯanwo, meqəm b Astəl mən səryoye kətwo? U ǧaryan qamoyo ema aṯi l Məḏyaḏ w ġalabe mədone ġer.
0082. Haka ʕal hawxa kməkrəx u kṯowano ġalabe muhim kfoyəš.
0083. Əno, šaxṣan awwəl naqqa kšumaʕno ʕal “aḥ ḥaləqyoṯo du saqəf“, ṭabi əno naʕimo nafəqno mu Ṭuro, balki mawxa.
0084. U ʕAmmo Išoʕ xəd maḥkəyono, heš, hawne kayiso yo w b dukṯe yo; kmətʕaǧabno asas aydarbo bnele am məštawoṯo du zabnayḏe ḥḏo b ḥḏo, ʕam kalo w ḥaṯno.

0085. Bnele zəd mə ʕəsri (20) əšmone. Kmaḥkelan ʕal u lwošo du zawnawo w kubelan ṣərto šafərto ʕal aš šawṯawoṯo d Məḏyaḏ, ʕatiqe w ḥaṯe. B šroro kito ġalabe nuqṭe, klozəm ḥḏo b ḥḏo d məqroyi. W bi maʕəlṯaṯe ste layban midəqina b kulle.
0086. Laǧani u Ǧan mwafəq, xaṣaṭan bu qəbolano d səmle ʕam u ʕAmmo Išoʕ. U sabab ste, qadər d maḥke mədone ḥaṯe w marwaḥle i ṣərto du maḏʕayḏan. W b šroro kətle iḏaʕto kayəsto.

0087. ʕAmuqo ʕabər baq qaḏiyat dan əšne ḥaroyani du ʕamayḏan, d kətwayye ġalabe ḥassas. Maṯlo u təhzimo dan niše w daʕ ʕlaymoṯo səryoye, kulan d kšəmʕina harke bi həǧra. Bu əmkan diḏe kṯəwle stədʕat w səyomo daš šuġlone du ʕamo bat tarʕe di ḥkume w bad dawayər w bam maḥkamat, mʕawanle ġalabe.
0088. Bale naqqa ḥreto ste klozəm d mišayewole šəwole, əšmo d kətne ḥassas ste.
0089. Aš šəwolani u Ǧan kəmšayelene, hal lawile bayn ele w l nafše šəwolo, “Əno hawino sabab d xole u Ṭuro?“ ʕAǧaba mən we d tfəkle d soyəm hawxa?
0090. U Ǧan ǧawab ftiḥo lə kmoyəd. Bale kumarno, kul ḥa d qore u kṯowano gəd huwele ṣərto ʕal am maqṣade d kətwayye bəṯre daq qaḏiyatani.
0091. Uno šaxṣi ḥzeli, b kul iqoro lu ʕAmmo Išoʕ, i maddiye, u kalla, ḥa mas sababe d samwo aš šuġlonani. Ṭabiʕi kətwo maqṣade ġer ste.

0092. Qay uno maṭino li qanaʕaṯe? B kmo dəkoṯo kḥuzeno u ʕAmmo Išoʕ d kətle ḥiyərto laḥ ḥaye mi ʕayno du mal w di zangane. Bu nəquṣo, ḥatta bi sobuṯaṯe diḏe (ʕəmre hawi 84 əšne), ak kallat luwwe heš kmaḥwən muhim.

0093. Ġer maṯe ste kmaṯkər b šəbhoro zangane d ġer noše. Mede ġer ste d gorəš i dəqqa u šəwolo dann əmkanat diḏe wayye. Aw xəd huwwe d kḥuzewolən: “... uno bi ḥkume qawyo wi, i ḥkume b iḏi wa... i ʕito b iḏi wa, kul mede b iḏi we...“ U medano tabʕan latwe ʕal asas qawyo, mawxa ʕabiri bəṯr aḥ ḥayayḏe bi tahlika.

0094. Nuqṭo ḥreto d gəršo i dəqqa, i ḥiyərto du ʕAmmo Išoʕ ʕal ann əmkanat d ġer noše yo. Lə mətyaqanwo d kətwo nošo ḥreno xədwoṯe: “... kul nošo l uḏaʕwo tərki; kul nošo ʕayne latwayye ftiḥe; kul nošo latwe hawxa našiṭ, ǧaṣur d əzzewo samwo šuġlone; l uṯewo mənayye...“!..

0095. U Ǧan baš šəwole, kəzze əšmo zəd aʕle w kmidəq ḥatta bu šəwolo di ǧasustiye (xəfyatiye). Kumarno mʕadlo səmle w d manṭele u šəwolano li ḥolo. Bu nəquṣo komər u ʕAmmo Išoʕ, bu medano, mu ṭaraf di ḥkume d mqadəmalle. Akit kətwo noše ġer d saymiwo ǧasusiye.
0096. Ṭabi aš šəwole ḥaroyani lə kmanqəṣi u taʕəb dawile u ʕAmmo Išoʕ ʕam u Ǧan bu ḥəḏoro du kṯowano. Kubaʕno d mqadamno tawədyoṯo lat tre.
0097. Kubilan mawḏəʕonuṯo ṭaqriban ʕal zabno d mo (100) əšne. Mədone mədone kmitahwe ṣərto aʕlayye ġalabe šrəḥto. Mi ḥiyərto marduṯonayto w knəšyayto ulṣoneye ne.

0098. Laǧani u Ǧan naqqa ḥreto mṯabətlelan d kətle iḏaʕto ġalabe kayəsto w ʕaməqto ʕal u Ṭuro, xaṣaṭan ʕal Məḏyaḏ. Xəzne kaməlto yo, kgorəš u maḥkəyono mə nuqṭo l nuqṭo. W lə kṭore mede muhim talyo, əlla kmanfaqle. Ḥatta, b ṣabro ġalabe rabo, kəzze hul lu ḥədud di iḏaʕto du maḥkəyono.
0099. Kuḏaʕno ʕasqo yo (zaḥme yo) l nošo sowo d maṯkər tuwerəx w əšne. Bale duwewo asiruṯo, ġalabe mam mədonani, bayna šato hawən aw bayna əšne maṣrene, kuwewo šṭaw.

0100. Lə kubaʕno d ṭuʕeno i aṯto du ʕAmmo Išoʕ, i ḥəlto Farida. Kmaḥwe, ġalabe b dəqqa mṣanṭowa ʕal kul mede. B dəkoṯo, kḥuzeno ʕabiro bi məlṯo. Kayiso səmle lu Ǧan d mšayelela liyya ste kmo šəwole w kobo i ṣərto daḥ ḥaye xəd koṯe l bola mu waxt ʕatiqo, heš hiyya ʕlaymṯo. Tawdi liyya.
0101. Bu təḥkiyayḏa, kmaḥwe laǧani Məḏyaḏ, məqqa naʕəmto wa aw u ʕamayḏa məqqa maṣro we bə ḥḏoḏe: I ḥəlto Fərdo yalifo naqəš si Xanəme, kəwyo taḥoli!

0102. Bu kṯowano, u Ǧan mwafəq w kmawḏaʕlan u dasto d kətyo malyo bat tašʕiyoṯo w bi marduṯo du Ṭuro. Marwaḥle w kmarwəḥ i ḥiyərtayḏan w kḥuzena, ġer mi maʕiquṯo, kətwo marduṯo šafərto ste baḥ ḥaye du ʕamayḏan.
0103. W haṯe gaban lḥuḏe wa. Bale kḥuzena, lu mede d kito b gawe du dastano, haw kmitahwe iqoro. Bu nəquṣo m laf i aġlabiye du ʕamo. U dasto kul məqqa d koṯe knošəf.

0104. Am maḥkəyonayḏe yawmo b yawmo knəqṣi. Ġer maṯe ste, maʕəl-asaf kmaydina, a qlofe d ġer ʕame. Xaṣaṭan d Awruppa. W kmankərina u ǧawhar d kətwolan. Tawdi naqla ḥreto lu Ǧan d maḥəslelan ʕal u medano.
0105. Ǧan: ʕAmmo Išoʕ, b ayna šato w ayko hawət?
0106. ʕAmmo Išoʕ: Uno 25 b Oḏər bi šato dan 1913 b Məḏyaḏ hawino.
0107. Ǧan: Əšme d babox mən yo?
0108. ʕAmmo Išoʕ: Əšme d babi Barṣawmo yo. Əšme d ǧəddi Ǧərǧo yo, u Ǧərǧo d be Qašo Malke yo. U muxtar das səryoye w zlam ġalabe mbayno we, ǧəddi.
0109. Ǧan: Əšme d emox mən yo?
0110. ʕAmmo Išoʕ: Əšme d emi Sətto yo. Emi m be Čalma yo.
0111. Ǧan: Əšme d qaštox mən yo?
0112. ʕAmmo Išoʕ: Əšme d qašti Sayde yo. Məb Malke Mire yo. Kəwyo pəsmam dani d be Kəno. I ʕamṯaṯṯe yo, d ʕAziz Kəno w hani.
0113. Ǧan: Kmo ʕammone kətlox, əšmonayye mən ne?

0114. ʕAmmo Išoʕ: ʕAmmone latwoli, bas kətwoli ʕammoṯo. Kətwoli ʕamṯi Sətto, i aṯto du ʕIsa be Awrohəm wa. I emo du Yaḥqub, du Yusəf w du ʕAtto w dani. W kətwoli ʕamṯi Zahre, i emo du Yawse d be Pəṭune, i emo du ʕAdo, u babo du ʕAdo, du ʕAbdo, du Saʕdo w du Malak. W kətwoli ʕamṯo stene i aṯto du Malak be Karkənni wa, i emo di Šəno wa. I Šəno i aṯto du Karmo d be Bašše wa. W kətwoli ʕamṯo əšma Wado wa. I kalo d be Use wa. U mede d emi w babi d maḥkəlalli. E d maḥkəlalli. W kətwoli ʕamṯo i Basse, i kalo d be Šamʕun Baḥḥo wa, i emo du Išoʕ d be Šamʕun Baḥḥo wa. W kətwoli ʕamṯo, Səkke wa əšma, smiṯo mat tarte ʕayne wa. Qṭəlulle i šato du Fərman (Sayfo) ʕam qašti w ʕam ǧəddi.
0115. Ǧan: Kmo aḥunone w ahwoṯo kətlox?
0116. ʕAmmo Išoʕ: Uʕdo ḥali-ḥaḏər kətli tloṯo aḥunone w kətli mawǧud saġ arbaʕ aḥwoṯo.
0117. Ǧan: Əšmonayye mən ne?

0118. ʕAmmo Išoʕ: Əšme d aḥuni u rabo Faridun yo. Faridun Aqqaya yo. Kowe harke b Gnetta. W aḥuni Fəkri Aqqaya kowe b Almanya. W aḥuni u Brahim ste harke yo. Bas baq qampat yo. Baq qampat yo. W ḥoṯi i Basse kəwyo harke b Rinkabi, i aṯto du Dawud d be Qašo Šamʕən yo. W ḥoṯi i Zaho i aṯto du Sḥaqo d be Ḥaydari yo. W ḥoṯi i Sade i aṯto du Nayəl d be Šabo Šaxxo yo. Mayəṯ u gawro. Kəlla b Ṣṭanbul yo. W ḥoṯi i Stire kəlla b Almanya, i kalo d Qašo ʕAdo yo.
0119. Ǧan: Əšme di ʕaylaṯxu d meqəm mən yo?

0120. ʕAmmo Išoʕ: Me meqəm əmmiwolan “be Qašo Ǧərǧo.“ Aḥna asas diḏan “be Qašo Malke“ kəmmilan. Aḥna u mede d kəḏʕina mab babayḏan w maǧ ǧəddayḏan me l ḥḏor d Diyarbakər aṯina l Məḏyaḏ. Qaše b Məḏyaḏ latwo, ǧəddayna qašo we. Ab babayḏan w aǧ ǧəddayḏan qaše wayye. Ṭləbənne mu Faṭəryarxo.

0121. U Faṭəryarxo hulelən musaʕada w aṯina m ḥḏor d Diyarbakər l Məḏyaḏ. Ǧəddayna l Məḏyaḏ qašo aṯi. W həwanwolan u qawro d kətyo b gawe di ʕito di Mart Šmuni. Taḥt u nəqušo, hadiye lab babayḏan. Hul d kətna saġ, u qawrano gəd howe lab babayḏan w laǧ ǧəddayḏan mawǧud. Ḥalan kəlle tamo mawǧud yo.
0122. Ǧan: Ayna šato ṭralxun i dukṯaṯxu d l ḥḏor d Diyarbakər w aṯitu? Nošo mərlelxu?

0123. ʕAmmo Išoʕ: U mede d ksamno taxmin, aḥna hawilan mo w tmoni (180), mo w tloṯ w tmoni (183) əšne. Čənki, mar qayo? Meqəm mu Fərman b tarte tloṯ əšne, aṯiwo u baladiya rayyəsi d Arġani, əšme du qaza Arġani yo.

0124. Aṯiwo l Məḏyaḏ mərle: “Kətxu baxčat w kətxu amlak, kəmmənne "Dəb Qašo Malke ne" w səmlan taḥqiqat aʕlayxu w hatu b Məḏyaḏ hatu. Kəbʕeno d mzabnitulline d samnolle ḥalal." Babi mərlele mərle: “Yabo aḥna lo ḥzelan u malano w lo šaməʕina. Alfo ḥalalat aʕlox, xəd u ḥalwo d emox.“
0125. Kumarnox, taxmini kumarno, u mede d šaməʕina, w d aṯina m Arġani l Məḏyaḏ hawilan mo w tmoni (180) əšne.
0126. Ǧan: Yaʕni hatu m Arġani aṯitu l Məḏyaḏ?

0127. ʕAmmo Išoʕ: M Arġani aṯina l Məḏyaḏ, e. Hawxa u mede d kəḏʕina. Tloṯ ʕaylat wayna. ʕAyla aṯyo w fayišo b Ḥəlwan, u qaḏa d Urfa w ʕayla fayišo b Mərde w ʕayla aṯyo l Məḏyaḏ. Tloṯ ʕaylat wayna. Hani aǧ ǧəddayḏan hawxa. Tloṯ ʕaylat wayye. Annaqqa kətwolan u kṯowano, ġalabe qimatli.

0128. Uʕdo kəlle b Almanya su Yaḥqo, abre d ʕammi. Mḥalaqlan pəšk, aḥna əmmina: "Yabo aḥna hawullan u kṯowano m darbe d kul mede. Fayitina bu məlk w ṭrelan lanək aḥ ḥrene." I ʕayle d Ḥəlwan stene hul meqəm b ḥṣar (10) əšne kətwo mənayye, heš ṣəroye w qəsəm mənayye hawən ṭaye. W qəsəm b Məḏyaḏ na w u qəsəm d Mərde ste qšiʕi. Hanək lə kuḏaʕnolle. U mede d kuḏaʕno hano yo.
0129. Ǧan: Hat naʕimo, man kətwolxu qarəwone?

0130. ʕAmmo Išoʕ: Aq qarəwonayḏan, aḥna tloṯ ʕaylat wayna, be Qašo Malke...w be Qašo Malke w be Šabo Baḥdo. Hani a tloṯ ʕaylat abre d ʕammone na. Ḥḏo ʕayla wa. Yaʕni frəqina me ḥḏoḏe. Kətwolan stene be Ḥawšo w be Mayya w u Yusəf be ʕAdde, hanək tloṯ ʕaylat abre d ʕammone wayye. M be Čalma wayye.

0131. Hani aq qarəwone d kulayna wayye. Qayəm ḥərlan, aḥna yarəwina, hawina ʕayla ġalabe qarabaləġ w be Qašo hawən ʕayla, be Qašo Ḥanna hawən ʕayle qarabaləġ ġalabe w be ʕammo Šabo Baḥdo hawən ʕayla qarabaləġ. W hanək ste hawən ġalabe.

0132. Annaqqa əmmina: “Yabo toxu mḥalqina pəšk aʕlayye“. Qayəm mḥalaqlan pəšk ʕal aq qarəwone. Azzano l ruḥayna yatəwina aʕ ʕaylat. Aḥna qayəṯlan be Mayya w be Qašo qayəṯṯe be Ḥawšo w be ʕammi Šabo Baḥdo qayəṯṯe be Yusəf d be ʕAdde. W frəqina me ḥḏoḏe. Aq qarəwonayḏan hani wayye. E.
0133. Ǧan: Me meqəm lə koṯe l boli haka mšayəlilox, hat l man mʕaməḏlelox?

0134. ʕAmmo Išoʕ: Lə kuḏaʕno, ksamno taxmini... ənkan latno ġalṭo, l Qašo Ḥanne mʕaməḏleli, uno lə koṯe l boli, bas hawxa əmmiwo: “L Qašo Ḥanne". U ǧəddo d Qašo Šamʕun mʕaməḏleli. U babo du Dawud d be Qašo Ḥanne. Hawxa əmmiwo. W uno bi šato dan 1913, hawino 25 bu yarḥo d oḏər.
0135. Ǧan: Bəṯr mu Sayfo, man kətwo ǧiran l ḥḏore du baytaṯxun?

0136. ʕAmmo Išoʕ: Kətwo ǧiran l ḥḏorayna ṣəroye be Fərmano wayye, be Maqsi Ǧərǧo wayye... Afandəma söyleyim be Šaxxo wayye, bəṯr mzabni ab bote d be Fərmano, maṭən l ʕAbdəlkarim u dišči. W d be Ḥasnəka fayiši dlo more w aḥ ḥrene d be Šaxxo, maṭənwo laṭ ṭaye. Hən ṭaye, bə ʕAbde Dalale, mzabniwonne ləb Brahim čawiš, hawo Brahim čawiš di baladiye, Brahim Šen. W d be Maqsi Ǧərǧo ste bəṯər maṭən laṣ ṣalḥoye. Fayiši diḏan bəlḥuḏe bi nave daṭ ṭaye. Kulle hawən ṭaye w diḏan fayiši dlo more, kəllən tamo xalye.
0137. Ǧan: Bu Sayfo man man nošaṯxu qṭil aw mḏayəʕ?

0138. ʕAmmo Išoʕ: Afandəm, uno i šato du Sayfo ʕəmri šato w falge we. Ǧəddi u Ǧərǧo d be Qašo Malke qṭəlle bi Saʕle. Šex Xalaf maqṭele. w qašti i Sayde qṭəlulle bab bote d Malke Karkənni ʕam ʕamṯi i Šmuni, hala i Səkke i smiṯo. W ʕamṯi i Maǧo. Hani qṭili bu Fərman. W ʕammi Išoʕ, ʕammi Šəbo qṭil. Abre d ʕammi we. W ʕammi Išoʕ, u ʕIsa azze li ʕaskariye w lu Safarbarlək w lə daʕər. Bu Safarbarlək azze laf Rusya w lə daʕər.
0139. Ǧan: Əšme mən we?

0140. ʕAmmo Išoʕ: ʕIsa we. Azze w lə daʕər. U Šəbo qṭəlle bu Sayfo. Kətwolle kačke, əšma Ziyo, i kalo, i aṯto du ʕIsa d be ʕIwarnayto wa. Kətwola abro əšme ʕAbdəlmasiḥ we, i šato du Fərman mawballe laṭ ṭaye w fayəš, hawi əšme Mḥammad Amin w hawi malla bi Qaməšlo w səmlan lə səmlan, ḥṣar kore amṭelan l Məḏyaḏ d doʕər w lə daʕər w mayəṯ bi mallatiye.

0141. Uʕdo kətle tre abne, tloṯo abne kəllən bi Qaməšlo. Ḥa əšme ʕAbdəllatif yo w u puləs du qaymaqam di Qaməšlo yo. U mede d kuḏaʕno kətle tloṯo arbʕo ḥrene. W kətle ḥa abro əšme Ǧano yo, fərnači yo. Hani u mede d kuḏaʕno, hawxa yo.
0142. Ǧan: Mənayxu l azze noše w ʕaṣi b ʕIwardo?

0143. ʕAmmo Išoʕ: Afandəm, bəṯr ǧəddi u Ǧərǧo d be Qašo Malke d mahzamle l ʕIwardo. Babi w emi w uno w ḥoṯi ʕaṣina, mahzamlan meqəm u qaṭlo, u mede d mawḏəʕallan. Azzano l be ʕAdoka, bax xərbat d be ʕAdoka.

0144. Tamo u ʕamo kule ʕaṣənwo, bax xərab d be ʕAdoka. ʕAṣənwo bax xərab d be ʕAdoka w qayəm mu kafno w mu ṣahwo... ḥəngi d ftəḥḥe u syoġo, babi nafəq bu šəbbak bi xərbayo w mnawəlalle emi, uno w ḥoṯi w səmme lə səmme emi d qədro nəfqo...

0145. Qayəm mahzamlelan. Azzano hul Mor Axəsnoyo, uno ʕal katfo, u mede d kuḏaʕno. Uno ʕal katfo w ḥoṯi ʕal katfo. Bəṯr mə Mor Axəsnoyo d əzzeyo d mawbelan l ʕIwardo. Qayəm ḥḏo žənnəke mhawarla aʕle əmmo: "Qariwo! Qariwo! Kaṯən gəd qəṭlilox!"

0146. Qayəm maḥətle əno w ḥoṯi taḥt i sato w mḥele bənne tfənge w mahzamle. W aḥna fayišina tamo taḥt i sato. Daməxinawo, lə kuḏaʕno b lalyo we.
